member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.KeyReceiver._States.EJECTING
member.summary: Declared state value that the examined KeyReceiver ejection routine does not select.

remarks.para: Release starts the ejection coroutine, a movement sequence that continues over several frames. It moves the key outward and later performs removal cleanup. That routine does not use EJECTING as its receiver state. Assigning this value does not start Release or its coroutine. This conclusion covers the examined KeyReceiver methods and generated routines; other code or mods may use it.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.KeyReceiver._States.EMPTY
member.summary: Records that the receiver has no fully inserted key and may begin accepting a matching entering key.

remarks.para: When the receiver is active, an entering Key that passes the code check moves it from EMPTY to HOVERING. Grabbing a seated key also sets EMPTY before the removal cleanup runs. This state alone does not guarantee the stored Key and host references have already been cleared.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.KeyReceiver._States.HOVERING
member.summary: Tracks a matching key approaching or aligning with the start of the receiver’s insertion path.

remarks.para: The receiver enters this state after a compatible Key’s host enters its interaction region. Realtime updates can guide the key toward startInsertTarget and adjust the holding hand’s desired pose. It is not a guarantee that the key has yet to touch any collider.

Once the insertion conditions pass, the receiver selects SLIDING and starts its seating coroutine. If the tracked host leaves the receiver while still HOVERING, it returns to EMPTY and clears the tracked key and host references.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.KeyReceiver._States.SLIDING
member.summary: Marks the insertion stage while the seating coroutine, a sequence that continues over several frames, moves the key toward endInsertTarget.

remarks.para: The coroutine updates the key’s position and rotation relative to the receiver, then runs the insertion-completion routine and selects INSERTED. Realtime hand updates in this state can keep a holding hand’s fingers closed.

The ejection coroutine also assigns SLIDING briefly while running the removal routine, which removes the key and notifies listeners, before returning to HOVERING. Reading this state alone therefore does not prove the key is currently traveling inward.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.KeyReceiver._States.SWITCHING
member.summary: Declared state value with no verified key-swapping behavior in the examined KeyReceiver implementation.

remarks.para: None of the examined KeyReceiver methods or its generated insertion, ejection, and update routines selects or specially handles SWITCHING. Assigning this value is not a verified way to exchange keys; normal approach updates handle HOVERING and SLIDING instead. Other code or mods were not covered by this conclusion.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.KeycardReceiver._States.EJECTING
member.summary: A declared state label that the inspected ejection routine does not use.

remarks.para: The ejection coroutine, a sequence that continues over several frames, moves the card back toward the insertion start. After it reaches that start and waits for the next physics update, it briefly selects SLIDING while running removal handling, then selects HOVERING. Neither the receiver’s class methods nor its three coroutine bodies assigns EJECTING.
Setting this value alone does not launch ejection. The Release methods start the ejection coroutine when a tracked card exists. Other or custom code was not exhaustively searched.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.KeycardReceiver._States.EMPTY
member.summary: Allows the receiver to acquire a keycard entering its detection area.

remarks.para: When the receiver is active and the card is not excluded by inventory handling, OnInteractableHostEnter stores the entering card and its object, calculates the holding hand’s alignment data, and changes to HOVERING. The later seating sequence reserves the card for this receiver. Removing a hovering card returns the receiver to EMPTY.
The receiver also selects EMPTY when an inserted card is grabbed. This value alone therefore does not prove that every stored card reference has already been cleared; it marks the acquisition phase.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.KeycardReceiver._States.HOVERING
member.summary: Guides an associated card and the holding hand toward the slot’s insertion start.

remarks.para: The pre-rig update runs MoveTowardsStartInsertTarget in this state and applies the calculated hand pose override when a hand is holding the card. Once insertion conditions are met, the receiver changes to SLIDING and starts its insertion coroutine.

This state is also used by the ejection coroutine, so it does not mean the card is only arriving for the first time. If the hovering card leaves the detection area, the receiver destroys its alignment joint and clears its tracked card.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.KeycardReceiver._States.INSERTED
member.summary: Marks an associated card as fully seated after the receiver’s lock/read handling has run.

remarks.para: OnMagazineLocked selects this state and the hasCartridge property requires it, together with a tracked Keycard reference. The state does not by itself prove that the card’s access code was accepted; the code result and unlock callback are handled separately.

The entry handler has an INSERTED branch that starts ejecting the seated card when another keycard enters, but that branch only runs while the receiver is active and the entering object passes the inventory exclusion. Normal seating disables the receiver, so INSERTED alone does not guarantee that another card’s entry will start ejection. Grabbing the seated card selects EMPTY and runs card-removal handling.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.KeycardReceiver._States.SLIDING
member.summary: Marks the card’s sliding phase while the insertion coroutine moves it toward the seated position.

remarks.para: The transition from HOVERING starts CoWaitLockMagazine, a coroutine that continues over several frames. It moves the associated card between the insertion targets and calls OnMagazineLocked when it finishes. During this state, the pre-rig update applies a closed-finger pose to a hand still holding the card.

After the ejection movement finishes, its coroutine briefly selects SLIDING during removal handling before changing to HOVERING. Assigning this enum value by itself does not start either movement sequence or provide the stored card references and insertion targets it uses.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.KeycardReceiver._States.SWITCHING
member.summary: A declared state label that the inspected receiver methods do not select or give a dedicated update branch.

remarks.para: The receiver’s class methods and its three coroutine bodies do not assign this value. Card replacement starts the ordinary ejection coroutine from INSERTED instead of entering SWITCHING.
Setting this value alone does not swap keycards. No separate switching behavior was established outside the inspected receiver code.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.MobileEncounter.SpawnOrder.PARALLEL
member.summary: Starts a timed spawn routine for every configured NPC group without waiting for earlier groups to finish.

remarks.para: A group is a configured set of NPC spawns with its own timing and count settings. Each routine uses that group's initial delay, maximum number of living NPCs, configured NPC spawn total, and seconds between permitted spawns. These routines can overlap, but this does not make every NPC appear at once.

When a group's recorded death count reaches its configured spawn total, the encounter marks that group complete. In PARALLEL mode, the same completion check also marks each unfinished group whose hostileGroup setting is false (the group is not marked hostile) complete. After every configured group is marked complete, the encounter sets its complete flag before firing the OnComplete event.

member.name: F:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.MobileEncounter.SpawnOrder.SERIES
member.summary: Runs configured NPC groups in order, starting the next group only after the current group is marked complete.

remarks.para: Group indexes start at 0. With three groups and none already recorded complete, StartEncounter starts group 0. The normal group loop marks it complete when its recorded deaths reach that group's configured NPC spawn total, then starts group 1 and group 2 in turn. Reaching the final spawn by itself does not complete the group; its recorded death count must reach the configured total. After the final group is marked complete, the encounter sets its complete flag before firing the OnComplete event.

StartEncounter does not clear the number of groups already recorded complete; TerminateEncounter clears that count and resets the groups. CheckCompletion changes encounter state rather than simply answering yes or no: calling it directly with an unfinished group marks that group complete and can advance the series before the normal death-count condition is met.

member.name: M:Il2CppPuppetMasta.BehaviourPowerLegs.SwitchMentalState(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourBaseNav.MentalState)
member.summary: Applies the chosen mood to this NPC, changing its decision timing, movement settings and state-specific animation setup.

remarks.para: An NPC is a character controlled by the game. This method does more than store a mood. It first cleans up the previous mood, then applies the requested mood, then stores mentalState and requests a fresh AI decision. AI means the rules that choose the character’s next action. Passing the current mood again repeats this setup; it can repeat a greeting or gesture too.

Rest sets a 2-second decision interval, relaxed hand poses, roamSpeed for movement, a turning speed of 90 degrees per second, acceleration of 2 metres per second squared and a stopping distance of 1 metre. Roam uses a 1-second interval and the same relaxed hands, movement speed, acceleration and stopping distance, but uses roamAngSpeed for turning. These speeds are settings for the NavMeshAgent, Unity’s component that follows a path through walkable space; changing them does not teleport the character or make it reach that speed immediately.

Investigate sets a 0.2-second decision interval, loose fist poses, roamSpeed and roamAngSpeed, acceleration of 2 metres per second squared and a stopping distance of 1 metre. The movement-speed settings are in metres per second, and the turning-speed settings are in degrees per second. Rest, Roam and Investigate resize the sphere that gathers possible visible targets using that mood’s configured range. Its radius is (range + 1) / 2, where range is restingRange, activeRange or investigateRange, respectively, in the sphere’s local Unity distance units; the added 1 is one such unit. At normal scene scale these units are metres. The sphere is shifted forward by radius minus 1 unit. A radius of 0.5 or less disables it. For example, a configured range of 5 gives a radius of 3 and a forward shift of 2. This target-gathering area is separate from whether a target passes the other sight checks.

Agroed sets a 0.1-second decision interval, prepares the current combat style, uses agroedSpeed and agroedAngSpeed, raises acceleration to 3 metres per second squared and reduces stopping distance to 0.5 metre. It sets a sight-gathering sphere radius of 2 local distance units, enables the angry animation flag and requests a greeting face animation when the supported face setup is enabled, or an aggression sound otherwise. Rest and Roam apply baseColor to the glowing material parts; Agroed applies agroColor. Investigate does not change that colour during this call.

Engaged sets a 0.05-second decision interval, relaxed hands, engagedSpeed and agroedAngSpeed, acceleration of 2 metres per second squared and a stopping distance of 1 metre. It sets both arm strength multipliers to 2, making the physics arms follow their intended poses more strongly, subject to health and other strength settings. It also requests the supported greeting or aggression sound. Mirror mode requests its gesture; Friendly mode can request a random gesture when the gesture cooldown has expired. Engaged does not resize the sight sphere or set the glowing colour during this call. MindControlled has no special entry setup here: after the old mood’s cleanup, it stores that mood and requests a decision while retaining the previous movement, sight and decision-interval settings.

Leaving Agroed clears its angry and blocking animation flags, restores both arm strength multipliers to 1 and restores the normal foot stance. Leaving Engaged also restores both arm multipliers to 1, and leaving its Mirror mode requests a gesture. Clearing the blocking animation flag in this cleanup does not also clear the stored BlockActive value. These are separate pieces of state.

The decision intervals are minimum gaps measured with Unity’s unscaled clock, which is not slowed by the game’s time scale. The requested fresh decision bypasses that gap on the next eligible AI tick; this method does not run the decision immediately. Frame scheduling and the character being frozen or inactive can delay it. For example, switching from Rest to Agroed changes the regular gap from 2 seconds to 0.1 second and asks for a fresh decision on the next eligible tick. It does not itself select a new target, deal damage or start a punch.

member.param: The mood to apply. Rest, Roam, Investigate, Agroed and Engaged each apply the setup described above; MindControlled has no special entry setup in this override.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Achievements.AWARDACHIEVEMENT(System.String)
member.summary: Requests a Steam achievement for an ID listed in AchievementsDict, through a component attached to a scene object that a Unity event can call.
member.param: An exact key from AchievementsDict, such as ACH_DESCENT.

remarks.para: A component is a piece of code attached to a Unity scene object. An event is a signal that tells selected routines to run. For example, in the Inspector, Unity’s configuration panel, select AWARDACHIEVEMENT on the attached Achievements component as a routine for an event to call, and enter ACH_DESCENT as its string argument.

Pass the dictionary key, such as ACH_DESCENT, rather than its readable value, such as Descent. The method validates the key, sends that same key to Steam, and writes a log message containing the key and readable name. It does not use note as the achievement ID; calling it with the default empty string fails the built-in key check.

An unknown ID writes an error and makes no Steam achievement request. For a known ID, the method requests Steam’s achievement update and requests storing stats if that update reports success. It discards the result and logs the award even if Steam rejected the update, so the log is not proof that the account received the achievement.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Achievements.Unlock(System.String)
member.summary: Requests a Steam achievement for a known ID, without requiring an Achievements component instance.
member.param: An exact achievement key accepted by AchievementsDict.

remarks.para: Use an AchievementsDict key, such as ACH_DESCENT. The dictionary’s readable value, Descent in that example, is used only in the log; it is not substituted for the ID sent to Steam.

Unknown IDs log an error without sending a request. Known IDs are passed to Steam’s SetAchievement operation, with StoreStats requested if that operation succeeds. This method returns no success result and its award log does not confirm platform acceptance. The audited implementation calls Steam, rather than dispatching to every installed platform service.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.ARENA_CancelMatch
member.summary: Clears the flag saying the player is ready for the arena match.

remarks.para: Only changes isPlayerReady to false. It does not stop enemy spawning, reset the arena state, move geometry or clear the score. Use the challenge-cancellation or quit flow when those actions are needed.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.ARENA_ChallengeResume(System.Int32,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Selects a survival profile and records the supplied round number for later play.
member.param: One-based round number to store.
True selects survivalProfileProjected; false selects survivalProfile.

remarks.para: projectedProfile false selects survivalProfile; true selects the already prepared survivalProfileProjected. This method does not generate that projected profile. It stores resumeRound directly, refreshes arena displays, resets the friendly AI-target reference list and clears score and updates scoreText when assigned, then sets the arena ACTIVE.

Round numbers are one-based when later used to look up rounds: 1 means the first round. Supply a round that exists in the selected profile. This method does not mark the player ready, ring the bell or begin enemy spawning.

When playerProxy exists, the target-list reset clears friendlyProxyList and adds only the player proxy, a reference identifying the player to AI, while setting its teamNumber to 1. It does not reset currFriendlyTarg, the separate index used to choose ally home positions.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.ARENA_ChallengeSelect(System.Int32)
member.summary: Selects a configured arena challenge or the survival profile and resets selection-related state.
member.param: Zero-based configured group index, or any negative value for survivalProfile.

remarks.para: A nonnegative sel is a zero-based index in roundProfileGroupList: 0 chooses its first group. Any negative sel chooses survivalProfile. The list must still be assigned for the initial bounds check, even for survival. An index beyond the list logs an error and returns.

Valid selection refreshes arena displays, resets the friendly AI-target reference list, clears score and updates scoreText when assigned, and sets ACTIVE. Nonnegative selection also enables the arena difficulty text components. It does not call ARENA_StartMatch or start spawning enemies.

When playerProxy exists, the target-list reset clears friendlyProxyList and adds only the player proxy, a reference identifying the player to AI, while setting its teamNumber to 1. It does not reset currFriendlyTarg, the separate index used to choose ally home positions.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.ARENA_CustomChallengeSelect(Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.RoundProfileGroup)
member.summary: Assigns the supplied custom group and prepares its selected arena layout when the player is not already ready.
member.param: Prepared group to assign, including its rounds, waves and game-mode settings.

remarks.para: Stores the same group in assignedRoundProfile, resets the friendly AI-target reference list, sets ACTIVE and refreshes arena displays. It does not build or copy the group; prepare its rounds and waves before calling.

If isPlayerReady is false, sets it true, invokes playerReady if assigned and asks geoManager to show its current selected layout. If already ready, skips those preparation actions. This does not immediately spawn the custom wave.

When playerProxy exists, the target-list reset clears friendlyProxyList and adds only the player proxy, a reference identifying the player to AI, while setting its teamNumber to 1. It does not reset currFriendlyTarg, the separate index used to choose ally home positions.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.ARENA_ObjectiveProfileCompleted
member.summary: Sets the arena to WIN, plays the win sound and starts the wave-reset sequence.

remarks.para: The method trusts the caller: it does not inspect objective completion or choose the next profile itself. The reset coroutine, a sequence Unity runs across frames with waits between cleanup steps, stops spawning and cleans up the wave, then calls EndOfMode for WIN; stacked groups can advance from that later mode-end flow.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.ARENA_PlayerEnter
member.summary: Applies the selected challenge settings when a ready player enters the arena.

remarks.para: If isPlayerReady is false, logs an error and returns. Otherwise invokes playerEnter, plays playerEnterClip, records the current light, medium and heavy reserve total, and loads currentRound and currentWave using the one-based round and wave counters.

ON_TRIGGER starts a countdown using arenaStartDelay, a duration in seconds of scaled game time; slow motion makes the same countdown take longer on a real-world clock. ON_TRIGGER_BELL invokes readyUpBell except in PROTECT mode; it waits for the bell to start that countdown. CUSTOM starts the wave's friendly-target spawn routine. PROTECT also resets the bell latch and requests the king after five real-time seconds. INSTA_DEATH turns on instant-death player health.

HARDER and HARDEST enable the configured slow-time limiter; HARDEST also enables instant-death health. Non-EASY, unstacked CHALLENGE, PROTECT, WEAPON, INSTA_DEATH and KING_OF_THE_HILL selections request IncreaseChallengeDifficulty, whose profile increase only handles MEDIUM and HARD. The method also refreshes scoreText and focuses the group's explicit leaderboard when configured.

This is entry setup, not a one-time latch: calling it again can repeat events, restart timers or request more allies. Configure the selected profile, valid round/wave indices, player rig and ammo references first.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.ARENA_QuitChallenge
member.summary: Begins quitting an ACTIVE arena challenge through its cleanup sequence.

remarks.para: Does nothing unless arenaState is ACTIVE. Plays playerEnterClip, invokes modeQuit if assigned, re-enables weaponSpawner when present, sets QUIT and starts CoResetOnWaveCompleteOrFail.

Cleanup runs as a coroutine: a sequence Unity continues across frames, with waits separating later cleanup steps. This method does not immediately reset all counters or return to WAITING; EndOfMode performs later mode cleanup.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.ARENA_ResetTheBell
member.summary: Allows the bell-start action to run again by clearing isRung.

remarks.para: Only clears the bell latch. It does not stop an existing countdown, reset arena state or play a sound. A later ARENA_RingTheBell call still requires ON_TRIGGER_BELL start mode.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.ARENA_RingTheBell
member.summary: Starts the bell-triggered countdown once per bell-latch reset and requests the current wave's loot.

remarks.para: Requires arenaStartMode ON_TRIGGER_BELL and isRung false. Sets isRung true, invokes ringBell if assigned and starts Co_TimerDown_Arena with arenaStartDelay, the countdown duration in seconds of scaled game time. Slow motion makes this delay take longer on a real-world clock. Later calls are ignored until ARENA_ResetTheBell or protect setup clears the latch.

It requests SpawnWaveLoot for currentWave unless arenaState is QUIT, finding a child loot spawner if needed. QUIT skips the loot request but does not prevent the countdown branch. The method does not check isPlayerReady.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.ARENA_SetDifficulty(System.Int32)
member.summary: Stores the requested difficulty and refreshes arena difficulty displays.
member.param: ArenaDifficulty value: 0 EASY through 4 HARDEST.

remarks.para: Defined values are 0 EASY, 1 MEDIUM, 2 HARD, 3 HARDER and 4 HARDEST. The method stores the integer without clamping it or rebuilding the selected profile.

Difficulty changes affect later entry, wave and score logic. Survival's normal wave-start flow chooses EASY below round 5, MEDIUM for rounds 5 through 9 and HARD from round 10, so it can overwrite a manual selection.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.ARENA_StartMatch
member.summary: Marks the player ready and requests the next arena layout for the selected challenge.

remarks.para: Returns immediately if isPlayerReady is already true. Otherwise sets it true, invokes playerReady when assigned and calls geoManager.IncrementAndToggleGeo when present.

WEAPON and PROTECT modes also disable weaponSpawner and despawn its tracked weapons when that spawner exists. This prepares the arena; entering and the configured start trigger or bell control when the wave begins. Supply assignedRoundProfile before calling.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.ARENA_SubmitScoreByType
member.summary: Requests leaderboard submission when the arena score is positive and the selected mode is not CUSTOM.

remarks.para: Uses the score already stored; it does not recalculate it. The base submission method requires a leaderboard manager and skips submission when the development-tool spawn flag is set.

The active leaderboard's score type chooses the submitted value: score, the base session timer in whole seconds, or that timer converted to milliseconds. A zero converted value is skipped. The arena score must still be positive to reach this request, even for a time leaderboard.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.ARENA_SwapSpawnerList(System.Int32)
member.summary: Replaces the active enemy-spawner list with the spawners from one configured zone group.
member.param: Zero-based index of the zone group in triggeredSpawnerList.

remarks.para: id is a zero-based index in triggeredSpawnerList. When that group is present, clears profileSpawnerList and copies every entry from its spawners array. It does not spawn an enemy or remove existing NPCs.
Supply a valid index and initialized lists. This method changes the active list directly; it does not synchronize spawnerHash or process pending removeSpawnerList entries.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.ARENA_ToggleDifficulty
member.summary: Cycles EASY → MEDIUM → HARD → HARDER → HARDEST → EASY and refreshes arena displays.

remarks.para: An undefined difficulty value is logged and left unchanged. Cycling stores the setting; it does not regenerate enemy profiles or immediately apply player-health and slow-time settings. Those are handled by later arena setup.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.AddZoneSpawners(Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_TriggeredSpawners)
member.summary: Adds the supplied zone's enemy spawners, first processing the spawner removals queued by previous zone exits.
member.param: Zone group whose spawners should become available.

remarks.para: Processes removeSpawnerList one queued spawner at a time. Only when spawnerHash still contains that spawner does it remove it from both spawnerHash and profileSpawnerList. It then clears the whole removal queue, including entries that failed that test. A stale profileSpawnerList entry can survive when the hash no longer contains it. Next adds each supplied spawner only if it is not already in spawnerHash.

This edits the available spawn locations; it does not move or create NPCs. Keep the hash and active list synchronized. RemovedZoneSpawners queues removal, so a spawner can remain usable until this method next processes that queue.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.AgroAllOnObjective(Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.NPC_Objective)
member.summary: Makes the registered NPCs target the supplied objective for aggression.
member.param: Objective whose proxy becomes the aggression target.

remarks.para: For every entry in NPC_Data_List, adds its data to the objective's npcHash and npcList, copies objective.proxy into its targetProxy, and calls its navigation behavior's SetAgro with that target. A proxy identifies the object the AI should focus on.

The list insertion is unconditional, so repeated calls can duplicate entries in npcList even though npcHash prevents duplicates. The method does not filter the controller's data list by friendly, dead or despawned flags; pass initialized data and objective references.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.AgroAllOnPlayer(Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.NPC_Objective)
member.summary: Redirects the NPCs enrolled in the supplied objective's npcHash toward the player.
member.param: Objective whose enrolled NPCs should now target the player.

remarks.para: For each enrolled data entry, copies this controller's playerProxy, the object reference identifying the player as an AI target, into the NPC record's targetProxy, its stored AI-target reference, and calls its navigation behavior's SetAgro. It does not walk every NPC in the arena or clear the objective's enrollment collections.
The method does not filter dead, despawned or friendly entries. The objective's hash and each NPC's AI behavior must be initialized.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.AssignFriendlyTargetPosition(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.AIBrain)
member.summary: Assigns an ally's navigation home to the next configured friendly target and starts its delayed greeting.
member.param: Ally AI brain receiving the home position and greeting routine.

remarks.para: Uses each friendlyTargetObjs position in world space, advancing currFriendlyTarg and wrapping after the last target. These are navigation destinations, not teleport positions. With an empty target array, assigns world position (0, 0, 0), the world origin, as the home position.

Also starts a greeting routine that waits five real-time seconds. On resuming, it first casts the brain's behavior to BehaviourPowerLegs, the NPC behavior type used for that greeting. An incompatible behavior throws a type-cast error rather than being safely skipped. With a valid behavior, it requests the face greeting animation and plays greetingClip at the NPC. A nonempty array needs valid target objects; the AI brain and its navigation behavior must exist.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.CalcScoreAndSubmitLeader
member.summary: Applies the arena's score adjustments, then requests eligible leaderboard submission.

remarks.para: Calls CalculatePlayerScore first. A successful calculation consumes the player's accumulated damage-score and death-save counters and clears this arena's recorded headshots, projectile shots and sampled movement after using them. Repeated successful calls therefore do not award those same recorded bonuses again, but can still multiply the existing score and add the remaining-ammo bonus again.

Submission requires a positive score and a selected mode other than CUSTOM. The base submission flow chooses score or time from the active leaderboard's score type and can skip the request when the manager or a usable value is missing.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.CalculatePlayerScore
member.summary: Adds end-of-run bonuses and penalties to the existing arena score and refreshes its display.

remarks.para: Returns while WAITING. Otherwise first asks lootSpawner to collect its remaining ammo pickups, then reads and clears Player_Health.playerDamageScore, accumulated damage points with each recorded damage amount truncated to a whole number, and playerDeathSaves, the count increased by the player's life-saving recovery routine. It counts the current light, medium and heavy ammo reserve.

Adds 2,000 points per positive recorded headshot, 100 per whole unit of positive totalPlayerDist, truncating away its fractional part, and 1,500 per positive recorded projectile. totalPlayerDist adds the squared changes of the player's world X, Y and Z position between samples. Those positions use Unity world units, so this total uses squared world units rather than ordinary distance traveled. Then multiplies the accumulated score by 1, 2, 3, 4 or 5 for EASY through HARDEST; undefined difficulty uses 1.

After that multiplier, adds 10 per remaining reserve round, adds 2 per positive death-save count and subtracts a positive playerDamageScore. For example, an existing score of 1,000 at MEDIUM with 20 reserve rounds and no other bonuses becomes 2,200.

This mutates the existing score rather than recomputing from zero. After completing the calculation and its display/log updates, it clears totalHeadShots, projectilesShot and totalPlayerDist. A second successful call therefore does not award those same recorded bonuses again, but can still multiply the existing score and add the remaining-ammo bonus again. It does not submit the score itself. Configure player health, ammo and the selected profile before use.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.CancelCurrentChallenge
member.summary: Clears player readiness and returns the controller to WAITING while resetting score and requesting geometry cleanup.

remarks.para: A coroutine is a sequence that Unity runs across frames, with waits between some steps.

Clears isPlayerReady, calls geoManager.ClearCurrentGeo when present, enables weaponSpawner, clears score and sets WAITING. weaponSpawner must be assigned; its call is not protected by an optional-reference check.

This method does not run the wave-reset coroutine, stop all spawn routines or refresh scoreText. It is the selection/menu cancellation path, while ARENA_QuitChallenge starts the staged cleanup of an ACTIVE challenge.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.CheckForWaveEnd
member.summary: Starts the end-of-wave sequence once the kill count reaches the current wave's scheduled enemy count.

remarks.para: A coroutine is a sequence that Unity runs across frames, with waits between some steps. Separate scheduled copies can overlap while an earlier copy is waiting; this check has no already-running guard.

Compares enemiesKilled with currentWave.enemyProfilesList.Count and starts CoEndOfWave when the count is reached or exceeded. FAILED skips that completion test. It does not compare activeEnemyCount with zero.

The method has no guard against starting a second end-of-wave coroutine. Avoid calling it repeatedly after the same wave has already met its kill condition. currentWave and its enemy list must be configured.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.CheckProfileForNextWave
member.summary: Advances the wave counter and prepares the next wave, round or end-of-mode decision.
member.returns: True when a next wave or round was prepared; false when the finite profile is complete or cannot continue.

remarks.para: This is an action with side effects, despite its name. It increments the one-based wave counter first. If a wave remains in the current round, stops the current arena timer and starts a new inter-wave countdown.

After the last wave, an existing next round is entered through EndOfRound. If there are no more rounds, the first round's LIMITED setting marks WIN, plays the win sound and stops the timer. An UNLIMITED setting creates another wave when the group has one round, or another round when it has multiple rounds, then starts the countdown.

A continuation within a round uses waveDelayTime from the first round in the group, including a newly generated wave. A continuation to another round uses that same first round's roundDelayTime, including a newly generated round. Both are countdown durations in seconds of scaled game time; slow motion makes them take longer in real time. This does not automatically use the current or next round's own delay setting.

It returns true for a continuation that was prepared, and false for completion or an unsupported exhausted round mode. Supply valid current round/wave counters and profile lists. Calling it merely to ask a question can advance the match again.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.ClearNPCDataAndZoneLists
member.summary: Removes dead NPC records from selected arena tracking collections while leaving living records intact.

remarks.para: Builds a temporary list of NPC_Data_List entries whose isDead flag is true. Removes their AI GameObjects from NPC_Data_Dict when present, removes those data entries from NPC_Data_List and removes their brains from NPC_List.
The complete method does not clear every zone list or despawn NPC objects. It is bookkeeping cleanup for dead records, so use the wave-reset sequence when physical cleanup is also needed.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.ClearScore
member.summary: Resets the stored arena score to zero.

remarks.para: Only changes score. The score label and the headshot, projectile, movement, combo and player-health counters are left as they were. Later score calculation can therefore add bonuses again.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.ClearSpawnerList
member.summary: Empties the active enemy-spawner list, preserving a fallback spawn location when needed.

remarks.para: If safetyZoneSpawner is missing and profileSpawnerList is nonempty, saves its first entry as the fallback before clearing the list. Existing safetyZoneSpawner is preserved.
This removes available list entries without destroying their objects, stopping active NPCs or clearing spawnerHash. Keep the hash synchronized when changing available spawners through multiple APIs.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.CoDelayedObjectiveStart
member.summary: Creates a coroutine that waits ten game-time seconds, then initializes objective mode.
member.returns: The prepared delayed-start sequence; pass it to StartCoroutine to run it.

remarks.para: The returned iterator is a prepared sequence of steps. StartCoroutine asks Unity to run it as a coroutine, a sequence that can continue across frames and waits.
Run the returned iterator with StartCoroutine to begin the wait. Calling this method alone only prepares the sequence. The wait follows game time, so pausing or slowing time also pauses or slows it.

After the wait, InitObjectiveMode prepares the first active objective and starts the arena start-delay countdown. This ten-second wait is an extra delay before that countdown; it does not directly spawn the first enemy. DelayedObjectiveStart starts this coroutine for you.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.CoEndOfWave
member.summary: Creates the sequence that checks what follows the finished wave, starts cleanup, and prepares loot for the next wave.
member.returns: The prepared end-of-wave sequence; pass it to StartCoroutine to run it.

remarks.para: The returned iterator is a prepared sequence of steps. StartCoroutine asks Unity to run it as a coroutine, a sequence that can continue across frames and waits.

Run the returned iterator with StartCoroutine. It clears nextWaveExists and, in WEAPON mode, removes the player inventory weapons and tracked loot weapons, including attached ones. It then waits one game-time second and plays the wave-end audio.

After the one-second wait and wave-end sound, HARDEST difficulty restores the player to full health only if the player is currently using instant-death health mode. This health restoration happens before CheckProfileForNextWave advances the wave/round counters and may replace the arena countdown or mark the mode finished. It saves that result in nextWaveExists and then starts CoResetOnWaveCompleteOrFail for staged NPC cleanup. Health restoration does not require the saved next-wave result to be true.

When another wave exists, it selects currentWave from the updated counters and asks SpawnLoot to prepare that wave's loot. WEAPON mode waits another two game-time seconds before this step. It does not wait for the cleanup coroutine to finish; cleanup and preparation can overlap. Required profiles, lists and mode-specific spawners must already be configured.

The full-health path also stops the player health component's coroutines, clears imminent-death state and resets its damage appearance. These are health-component effects, separate from this arena controller's spawn and timer coroutines.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.CoKillCombo
member.summary: Creates a timer that keeps the current kill combo alive until its time runs out.
member.returns: The prepared combo countdown; pass it to StartCoroutine to run it.

remarks.para: The returned iterator is a prepared sequence of steps. StartCoroutine asks Unity to run it as a coroutine, a sequence that can continue across frames and waits.

Start the returned iterator with StartCoroutine. When it first runs, it copies comboTimeVal into comboTimer. Each positive-countdown step, including its first step before yielding to the next frame, subtracts unscaledDeltaTime, the real-time seconds elapsed since the preceding frame; slow motion does not give the combo more time.

While counting down, it updates the optional comboTimerText using whole seconds. When the timer is no longer positive, StopAndResetKillCombo restores comboMult to 1 and updates or clears the combo labels. For example, a comboTimeVal of 3 allows about three real-time seconds before this reset; that is an example setting, not a default.

This routine controls the combo timer and multiplier, not a new award of kill points. Starting several copies can make them subtract from the same comboTimer. Normal controller code tracks one copy in killComboRoutine.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.CoPlayerDist
member.summary: Creates a movement check that records squared position changes and asks the launcher to target a nearly stationary player above world height 3.
member.returns: The prepared movement-check sequence; pass it to StartCoroutine to run it.

remarks.para: The returned iterator is a prepared sequence of steps. StartCoroutine asks Unity to run it as a coroutine, a sequence that can continue across frames and waits.

Run the returned iterator with StartCoroutine. On both the first step and later frame resumptions, it first tests isWaveOngoing. While that flag is true, it samples only when scaled game time is strictly greater than lastPlayerCheck plus playerDistTick, then yields to the next frame. There is no unconditional yield before its first sampling test. playerDistTick is the sampling interval in seconds of scaled game time. It reads playerProxy's world position, not a position relative to the arena.

Each sample adds dx*dx + dy*dy + dz*dz to totalPlayerDist, where dx, dy and dz are the changes in world X, Y and Z position since lastPlayerPos, each measured in Unity world units. The result uses squared Unity world units: each squared position change is added to the running total rather than converted to an ordinary distance. For example, one position change of 2 world units adds 4; two changes of 1 world unit add only 2. Sample spacing therefore changes what the total means.

If that squared change is strictly below thresh*thresh, where thresh is the movement threshold in Unity world units, and the player's world Y coordinate is strictly above 3 Unity world units, it calls launcher.LaunchProjectile with the current player position. Equality at either threshold does not pass. The check uses height above the world origin, not height above the floor; a valid launcher is needed when this condition is met.

It then makes the current position the next lastPlayerPos and stops when isWaveOngoing becomes false. StartPlayerDist normally initializes the previous position, sampling time and total before scheduling this routine. Starting the iterator directly does not perform those initial resets.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.CoResetOnWaveCompleteOrFail
member.summary: Creates the cleanup sequence that stops wave spawning, removes dead NPCs, and either prepares another wave or ends the mode.
member.returns: The prepared cleanup sequence; pass it to StartCoroutine to run it.

remarks.para: The returned iterator is a prepared sequence of steps. StartCoroutine asks Unity to run it as a coroutine, a sequence that can continue across frames and waits. A cancellation token lets work check whether it has been asked to stop. A callback is a routine registered to run when an action or notification occurs.

Start the returned iterator with StartCoroutine. Its first step invokes the wave-end event (a configured list of actions), clears isSpawning, stops the tracked enemy spawn coroutine, cancels the enemy spawn token, and stops the tracked friendly spawn coroutine, in that order. Only then does it clear isWaveOngoing and reset the kill combo. Living enemies are put into the puppet's Dead state, which requests death for their physics-controlled bodies.

The current arenaState controls friendly cleanup. For WAITING, FAILED and QUIT it also puts living friendlies into Dead state. WIN removes their NPC death callback and starts the friendly sublimation sequence instead. ACTIVE preserves friendlies so they can carry into another wave.

After one game-time second, it gathers distinct NPC records from NPC_List and NPC_Data_Dict. Dead records that have not already despawned receive despawn effects and a despawn request. It waits 0.1 game-time seconds after each record and another 0.5 seconds after the pass, so more records take longer to process.

It clears the living/dead enemy lists and resets activeEnemyCount, totalEnemyCount and enemiesKilled. ACTIVE calls ClearNPCDataAndZoneLists to remove dead records from the NPC dictionary, NPC data list and brain list; despite that method's name, its complete body does not remove dead entries from the zone-display lists. It may request replacement friendlies using the next wave's friendly count. A non-active valid state clears NPC bookkeeping and living friendlies instead.

After a further 0.25 game-time seconds it clears the dead-friendly and per-wave despawn records and refreshes NPC counters. ACTIVE finishes there. WAITING, FAILED, QUIT and WIN call EndOfMode to reset the mode and apply its ending behavior. This is a multi-frame cleanup; calling the factory alone does none of it, and cancellation before completion can leave later cleanup steps unfinished.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.CoSpawnObjectiveEnemies
member.summary: Creates a single pass of delayed enemy spawn requests for the current objective wave.
member.returns: The prepared objective spawn sequence; pass it to StartCoroutine to run it.

remarks.para: The returned iterator is a prepared sequence of steps. StartCoroutine asks Unity to run it as a coroutine, a sequence that can continue across frames and waits.

Start the returned iterator with StartCoroutine. It exits immediately if the base session is not ongoing when it first runs. Otherwise it reads enemySpawnDelay from the group currently referenced by assignedRoundProfile and waits that many seconds of game time before the first request. After every request, it reads that setting again for the next wait. Game time is the game clock affected by slow motion and pause: slow motion stretches these waits in real time, and paused game time stops their progress. Each loop test also reads the current wave’s maxConcurrent again, so changing the assigned profile, delay or wave limit while this sequence runs can affect later waits or the running pass limit.

It makes one request for each index from 0 up to currentWave.maxConcurrent minus one, choosing a random entry from profileSpawnerList each time. That index selects currentWave.enemyProfilesList when available; extra indices use StaticProfiles.enemyProfileList entry 3. The spawner list must be non-empty and the fallback list needs that entry when it is used.

Each request calls ExplicitArenaSpawn as an enemy and increments totalEnemyCount. This counts requests, not confirmed spawn success. Despite the maxConcurrent name, the loop does not check activeEnemyCount or continuously replace enemies after deaths; it is one pass whose number of iterations is set by that wave field.

For example, if these settings stay unchanged, maxConcurrent = 4 and two wave enemy profiles requests those two profiles and then two copies of the fallback profile. With enemySpawnDelay = 2, the first request follows a two-second game-time wait, with another two-second wait between requests. These are illustrative settings.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.Co_TimerDown_Arena(System.Single)
member.summary: Creates a game-time countdown that starts the next wave when it reaches zero.
member.param: Countdown length in game-time seconds; negative values use 10 and zero starts the next wave without a wait.
member.returns: The prepared countdown; pass it to StartCoroutine to run it.

remarks.para: The returned iterator is a prepared sequence of steps. StartCoroutine asks Unity to run it as a coroutine, a sequence that can continue across frames and waits.

Start the returned iterator with StartCoroutine. Its first step replaces arenaTimerValue with seconds. Negative values use a ten-second fallback; zero starts the next wave immediately when the iterator first runs. For a positive countdown, the first step also subtracts Time.deltaTime before its first yield; later steps do the same while the value remains positive. Time.deltaTime is the number of scaled game-time seconds since the preceding frame, so slow motion stretches the wait in real time and a paused game does not advance it.

On a later coroutine step after the value is no longer positive, it calls StartNextWave and ends. It does not check isWaveOngoing to decide whether to keep counting down; callers must stop an unwanted countdown. Starting several copies makes them write the same timer and can cause overlapping wave-start requests.

The native display condition compares the decreasing value with the last displayed value plus one. Under ordinary positive countdown progression this updates the label only on the first frame when at least one second remains, then leaves it stale; a countdown below one second may not refresh it at all. The underlying countdown still advances. Other code can refresh the arena timer label separately.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.Co_TimerUp_Arena
member.summary: Creates a timer that adds elapsed game time while a wave is ongoing.
member.returns: The prepared elapsed-time sequence; pass it to StartCoroutine to run it.

remarks.para: The returned iterator is a prepared sequence of steps. StartCoroutine asks Unity to run it as a coroutine, a sequence that can continue across frames and waits.

Start the returned iterator with StartCoroutine. While isWaveOngoing is true, each step adds Time.deltaTime, the scaled game-time seconds elapsed since the preceding frame, to arenaTimerValue and yields to the next frame. The total is in game-time seconds: slow motion makes it grow more slowly than a real-world clock.

It starts from the existing arenaTimerValue rather than resetting it. For example, a value of 12 followed by three seconds of game time becomes about 15. Set the timer to zero before starting if a fresh elapsed-time total is needed.

Its stored last-refresh value starts at zero. After adding frame time, it refreshes the display when arenaTimerValue is at least one game-time second above that stored value, then stores the current value as the new checkpoint. A preexisting timer at or above one second can therefore refresh on the very first step. When the wave flag becomes false it simply ends, keeping the recorded value; it does not itself finish the wave, award points or start the next one. Multiple running copies add time to the same total more than once per frame.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.DelayedObjectiveStart
member.summary: Schedules objective-mode initialization after ten game-time seconds.

remarks.para: StartCoroutine asks Unity to run a coroutine, a sequence that continues across frames and waits. A callback is a routine registered to run when an action or notification occurs.

This starts CoDelayedObjectiveStart immediately; no separate StartCoroutine call is needed. After the ten-second wait, InitObjectiveMode prepares the first objective and starts the separate arenaStartDelay countdown, measured in seconds of scaled game time, before wave startup.

The wait follows game time, so slow motion extends it in real time. This method does not cancel or replace an earlier delayed start. Calling it twice schedules two initialization attempts, which can add duplicate active-objective entries and connections to the same callback, so one later notification can call that routine multiple times.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.DespawnLootWeapons(System.Boolean)
member.summary: Asks the arena loot spawner to remove its tracked weapons, optionally including weapons attached to something.
member.param: Whether to detach and remove attached tracked weapons as well as unattached ones.

remarks.para: With despawnAll false, the spawner leaves attached weapons in place and attempts to despawn only unattached tracked weapons. With true, it first detaches attached weapons and then attempts to despawn them too. EndOfRound uses false; weapon-wave cleanup uses true.

This applies to the loot spawner's recorded weapon list, not every weapon in the scene. It needs the cached interaction component and Poolee, the component connecting an object to the game's spawning and despawning system. Once an entry passes the attachment and component tests, it queues that weapon for removal from tracking before requesting its despawn effects and calling Poolee.Despawn. After the pass it removes the queued entries from the tracking list without checking whether despawning succeeded. For example, Poolee.Despawn can return without despawning an object when the asset-spawner service is not ready. Entries skipped by the attachment or required-component tests remain tracked.
If this controller has no valid lootSpawner, this method returns without doing anything. It does not search for a missing spawner here.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.EndOfMode
member.summary: Finishes arena mode cleanup, returns the controller to WAITING, and can advance a stacked set of challenges.

remarks.para: A coroutine is a sequence that Unity runs across frames, with waits between some steps. A callback is a routine registered to run when an action or notification occurs.

The ending state controls score handling. FAILED skips score calculation and completion updates. SURVIVAL performs them for every other state, including QUIT; other modes skip them for QUIT. When that handling runs, it also invokes modeWin. Calling this method therefore does not require the state to already be WIN.

It resets the friendly AI-target reference list, clears despawnedDataList, resets totalEnemiesKilled, returns the round and wave counters to 1, and invokes modeEnd. Then it clears arenaTimerValue, refreshes the arena and NPC displays, clears player readiness, and sets WAITING.

If the group has clearAmmoOnModeEnd enabled, it first asks the loot spawner to despawn all tracked weapons and later clears the ammo reserve. It requests a five-second music fade-out when loop music clips are configured and asks the optional geometry manager to clear the current layout. Instant-death player health is turned off and restored to full health when that mode is active; the optional slow-time limiter is turned off too.

Finally, an isStacked group calls ProgressToNextProfile. ProgressToNextProfile directly selects another challenge during this same call when a next group exists, so WAITING need not remain the final state. This direct advance is separate from the earlier modeEnd event and the callbacks that event may invoke. This method expects the controller's profile, tracking lists, audio setup and player health to be initialized; it is the final stage of wave-reset cleanup, not a replacement for stopping spawn routines and removing NPCs.

When playerProxy exists, the target-list reset clears friendlyProxyList and adds only the player proxy, a reference identifying the player to AI, while setting its teamNumber to 1. It does not reset currFriendlyTarg, the separate index used to choose ally home positions.

The full-health path also stops the player health component's coroutines, clears imminent-death state and resets its damage appearance. These are health-component effects, separate from this arena controller's spawn and timer coroutines.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.EndOfRound
member.summary: Moves the round counter to the next round and requests its next arena layout.

remarks.para: Increments currRoundIndex and resets currWaveIndex to 1, meaning the first wave of that next round. It invokes the roundEnd event (a configured list of actions) when assigned, removes unattached tracked loot weapons, and asks the optional geoManager to increment and show its next layout.

The counters are one-based: if the current round is 2, this makes the round counter 3 and the wave counter 1. It does not check that round 3 exists or start enemies itself. CheckProfileForNextWave normally checks continuation and starts the separate countdown.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.FailEscapeMode
member.summary: Reports escape-mode failure and ends the base game session.

remarks.para: Calls the base EndSession flow: it runs the configured session-end event, clears the ongoing-session flag, stops the base session timer and requests the configured delayed ending action when that action calls for one.

This method does not set arenaState to FAILED or start the arena wave-reset sequence. Ending the base session and changing the arena match state are separate actions; code needing both must arrange both.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.FailObjectiveMode
member.summary: Stops this controller's coroutines, plays the failure sound, invokes ObjectiveFailed, and ends the base session.

remarks.para: A coroutine is a sequence that Unity runs across frames, with waits between some steps. StopAllCoroutines stops the sequences owned by this controller. A cancellation token separately lets asynchronous spawn work check whether it has been asked to stop; this method does not signal that token.

StopAllCoroutines runs first, so pending wave timers, objective waits and other coroutines owned by this controller stop before the failure event. It plays failModeClip as a two-dimensional one-shot sound, then invokes the ObjectiveFailed event (a configured list of actions) if assigned and calls base EndSession.

A selected profile is required for the failure flow. This does not itself set arenaState to FAILED, cancel the enemy spawn cancellation token, or run staged NPC cleanup. Base EndSession clears its ongoing-session flag and applies the configured session ending action.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.FailProtectMode
member.summary: Marks the arena FAILED, plays the failure sound, and starts staged cleanup unless it has already reached WIN.

remarks.para: StartCoroutine asks Unity to run a coroutine, a sequence that continues across frames and waits.

WIN returns without changes. Every other arena state is changed to FAILED, followed by failModeClip and StartCoroutine(CoResetOnWaveCompleteOrFail). It does not test whether the protected NPC is actually dead; the caller supplies that decision.

Cleanup stops spawning, removes NPCs over later coroutine steps and eventually calls EndOfMode. Because this sets FAILED first, that ending skips score/completion handling. This method does not immediately end the base session by calling EndSession.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.FailStateFX
member.summary: Plays the configured arena failure sound.

remarks.para: Calls PlayArenaAudio with failModeClip. This audio helper handles the sound; FailStateFX does not change arenaState, invoke the failure event, stop spawning or create a separate visual effect. Use the appropriate failure flow to change the match as well as play its sound.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.ForceStartMatchForTesting
member.summary: Runs arena preparation, moves playerObject to the world origin, and attempts the bell-start action.

remarks.para: Calls ARENA_StartMatch, then ARENA_PlayerEnter, then sets ACTIVE. It sets playerObject's Transform.position to (0, 0, 0), the world origin, before calling ARENA_RingTheBell. The move is absolute world position, not a position relative to this controller or a chosen arena spawn point.

Normal method conditions still apply. ARENA_StartMatch skips preparation when already ready; the bell only starts its countdown in ON_TRIGGER_BELL mode with isRung false. Entry setup can also start a countdown for ON_TRIGGER, so this is not a universal bypass of all start rules.
Configure the selected profile, player references and counters first. The method does not reset a previous run's score, wave/round counters or bell latch before these calls.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.FriendlyRegistration(Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.NPC_Data)
member.summary: Requests a king NPC's crown at this controller's position, or assigns a non-king friendly its target position.
member.param: Existing NPC record containing its brain and friendly/king flags.

remarks.para: If data.isKing is true, it requests the configured crown asset using this controller's world position and rotation and captures the NPC record as setup context for the spawn callback, a routine called when the spawn reports its object. That callback receives the newly spawned crown GameObject, the scene object containing the crown, and uses the separately captured record to configure it. The initial crown request is at the controller, not directly at the NPC's head.

If data.isFriendly is true and isKing is false, it calls AssignFriendlyTargetPosition with data.aiBrain. That assigns one of the configured friendly targets and starts the delayed greeting behavior. A king takes the crown branch even if the friendly flag is false.

This is extra setup for a supplied NPC record. Its complete body does not add that record to the base NPC tracking collections or increment friendly counts; normal registration must establish that bookkeeping separately.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.IncreaseChallengeDifficulty
member.summary: Builds a harder copy of the selected group for MEDIUM or HARD difficulty and assigns that copy to the controller.

remarks.para: EASY returns without making a copy. MEDIUM and HARD call CopyGroupProfile, adjust that copy's waves, and replace assignedRoundProfile. HARDER, HARDEST and unsupported values do not perform this profile increase. The difficulty field itself is not incremented.

Through this call, MEDIUM adds two enemy-profile entries per wave and HARD adds four, choosing from the wave's existing profiles. Each wave's simultaneous-enemy allowance increases by one only if the proposed value is at most maxConcurrentLimit. A value already beyond that limit is left unchanged rather than clamped down. Each wave's light, medium and heavy ammo amount is raised to at least 40.
For example, a wave with five scheduled enemies becomes seven at MEDIUM or nine at HARD. A simultaneous limit of 3 becomes 4 if maxConcurrentLimit allows 4. These are examples, not default settings.

The copy operation also marks the original group's round profiles isProceduralRound, so the original data is not completely untouched. Prepare non-empty enemy-profile choices before increasing difficulty. Repeated calls copy and increase the already assigned group again.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.InitObjectiveContainer
member.summary: Connects objective-key callbacks and configures each objective's player guide line for objective profile index 1.

remarks.para: A callback is a routine registered to run when an action or notification occurs. Each keyed-notification connection calls OnObjectiveKeyed with the objective that sent the notification. CODE_A is the key-code value assigned to the receiver's configuration; setting it here does not insert a key or unlock an objective.

Runs only when currProfile is 1 and the selected group has isObjectiveMode enabled. It connects every entry in allNPCObjectives to OnObjectiveKeyed, sets each objective's key receiver to CODE_A, and sets its DrawLine2Points.Point2 to a body object in the player's physics rig. That point supplies the player end of the objective's guide line.

After configuring the objectives it invokes the ObjectiveInitiated event (a configured list of actions) when assigned. Other profile indices skip this setup; the index is zero-based, so 1 means the second configured profile.

The objective list, key receivers, line components and player physics-body references must be initialized. Calling again adds the same callbacks again rather than replacing the existing connections, which can repeat notification handling.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.InitObjectiveMode
member.summary: Prepares the first active objective and starts its arena start-delay countdown.

remarks.para: A coroutine is a sequence that Unity runs across frames, with waits between some steps. StartCoroutine schedules that prepared sequence to run. A callback is a routine registered to run when an action or notification occurs. The destruction connection calls OnObjectiveDestruction with the objective that sent the destruction notification.

Sets currProfile to 0 and isPlayerReady true, then runs ARENA_PlayerEnter to apply entry settings. It adds allNPCObjectives entry 0 to activeNPCObjectives, connects OnObjectiveDestruction to every active objective, and requests each objective's lightning effect.

It clears the selected group's limitReached flag and starts Co_TimerDown_Arena using arenaStartDelay in game-time seconds, storing the resulting coroutine in arenaTimerRoutine. This delay precedes StartNextWave; no enemies are directly spawned by this method.

The first objective and all required entry references must exist. This does not clear activeNPCObjectives first or disconnect earlier callbacks; calling it again can duplicate entries, notifications and countdowns.

The ready-preparation block runs only if an entry event has cleared isPlayerReady again. Normally the flag set at the start stays true, so that block skips its playerReady event and geometry increment. Entry events can affect which branch is taken.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.InvertNavMeshArea(System.String)
member.summary: Requests navigation cost 100 for a named area whose current cost is zero or lower, or cost 0 when its current cost is positive.
member.param: Configured navigation-area name to look up.

remarks.para: A navigation area labels parts of the walkable surface used to plan NPC routes. Its cost is a relative pathfinding weight, not a distance, delay or on/off switch. Raising a cost makes routes through that area more expensive; it does not remove the surface or disable the area.

Any positive current cost takes the cost-0 branch, including values other than 100. For example, a current cost of 5 requests 0; a current cost of 0 requests 100. These are the values passed to Unity's navigation API, not a toggle of an area-enabled flag.

The name must match a configured navigation area. If GetAreaFromName returns an invalid index, the method does nothing. It uses the global NavMesh area-cost API; it does not edit a particular NPC's allowed-area mask.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.LOCK_NAVMESH_AREA(System.String)
member.summary: Requests a pathfinding cost of 100 for the named navigation area.
member.param: Configured navigation-area name whose global cost should be changed.

remarks.para: A navigation area marks part of the walkable surface for NPC route planning. The cost is a relative weight: routes crossing a high-cost area are more expensive than cheaper alternatives. It has no meter or second unit.

Despite LOCK in the name, this does not remove the surface, set an NPC's allowed-area mask or guarantee that NPCs cannot cross it. It calls the global NavMesh.SetAreaCost API with 100 after looking up the area. An unknown name is ignored.
UNLOCK_NAVMESH_AREA requests cost 0 for the same kind of lookup. InvertNavMeshArea chooses between those cost requests based on whether the current cost is positive.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.NPC_Registration(Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.NPC_Data)
member.summary: Applies arena entrance, friendly and objective-target setup to an NPC record that has been registered.
member.param: The existing NPC record whose entrance and arena target behavior should be configured.

remarks.para: The normal controller connects this handler to the base NPC registration notification while enabled. If NPCEntranceTrigger is assigned, it starts the brain's entrance timer using data.enemyProfile.entranceTimeVal in real-time seconds. That timer requests the puppet's Dead state, asking the NPC's physics-controlled body collection to die when time expires; it is a time limit on entrance, not a delay before spawning. The normal NPC_Enter callback, a routine registered to respond when an NPC enters the trigger, stops that timer when the NPC reaches the configured entrance trigger.

Friendly records also run FriendlyRegistration to request a king crown or an ordinary friendly target. If the selected group uses objectives, AssignObjectiveAgro chooses an active objective for the record and sets its AI attack target. With no active objective it targets the player instead; a full objective also sends attacks toward the player.

An unfilled objective is normally the attack target, with a random 2-in-11 branch targeting the player for that assignment. The NPC record can still record the objective proxy, the object reference identifying the objective as an AI target, in that branch. This configures what the AI should attack; it does not guarantee immediate movement or a hit.

The supplied record, brain, selected group and relevant profiles/targets must already exist. This handler does not itself add the NPC to the base tracking lists or increment their counts. Calling it again repeats setup and can start another entrance timer or add another objective-list entry.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.OnArenaSessionBegin
member.summary: Automatically prepares arena entry and starts the countdown when the start mode is ON_START.

remarks.para: Entry callbacks are routines registered to run in response to player entry. They run during ARENA_PlayerEnter and can change isPlayerReady before this method checks it afterward.

Returns for every other arenaStartMode and when assignedRoundProfile is missing. For ON_START with a valid profile, sets isPlayerReady true and calls ARENA_PlayerEnter, then starts Co_TimerDown_Arena with arenaStartDelay in game-time seconds and stores it in arenaTimerRoutine.
The normal enabled controller connects this method to the base session-begin event. Calling it manually runs the same setup without checking whether a new base session actually began.

Ready preparation is checked after entry callbacks. Normally readiness stays true and the playerReady event/geometry-increment block is skipped; an entry callback that clears readiness can make that block run. The countdown still follows entry setup. Repeated calls do not first stop the previous countdown, so they can schedule overlapping starts.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.OnPlayerDeath
member.summary: Calculates the arena score and requests an eligible leaderboard submission when notified of player death.

remarks.para: The normal enabled controller connects this method to the player-health death event. It calls CalculatePlayerScore, which can collect remaining ammo and consume the player's damage-score and death-save counters while adding bonuses to the existing score.

A submission is requested only when the selected mode is not CUSTOM and the stored score is positive. The base submission flow then checks the leaderboard manager and development-tool spawn flag, and chooses score or the base session timer according to the active leaderboard's score type. That timer is separate from arenaTimerValue; this call does not guarantee a successful upload.

This handler does not set FAILED, stop enemy spawning or begin the wave-reset sequence. Those failure/cleanup actions must come from the relevant match flow. Calling this yourself can repeat score calculation and its side effects even when the player has not died.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.OnPlayerSpawn
member.summary: Connects the loot spawner to this controller and adds the configured starting ammunition to the player's reserve.

remarks.para: If lootSpawner exists, calls its Initialize with this controller. Then each positive initLightAmmo, initMedAmmo and initHeavyAmmo is added to the corresponding light, medium or heavy reserve. Zero and negative configured counts are skipped.

These are counts of individual rounds, not magazines or physical pickup objects. The method adds to the existing reserve without clearing it first. For example, a light count of 20 adds twenty light rounds; another call can add twenty more.

The enabled controller connects this to the base player-spawn notification. A valid AmmoInventory and the static cartridge references are required when awarding ammo. The complete handler does not select a challenge, start a wave or physically spawn a new player avatar.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.PassEscapeMode
member.summary: Reports escape-mode success, plays the first round-end clip when available, and ends the base session.

remarks.para: The roundEndClips array must be assigned; an empty array skips the sound, while a non-empty array supplies its first clip to a two-dimensional one-shot. It then calls base EndSession to invoke the session-end event, clear the ongoing-session flag, stop the base timer and apply the configured ending action.
This method does not set arenaState to WIN, mark the selected challenge complete or run the wave-reset sequence. It trusts the caller's decision that the escape objective was passed.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.ProgressToNextObjectiveProfile
member.summary: Marks the current objective defense finished, requests enemy death, and schedules the next objective profile after ten game-time seconds.

remarks.para: Calls DefenseComplete on every active objective. That marks its objective empty and starts its emission-fade sequence, fading the lit appearance. It also sets every living enemy's puppet, its collection of physics-controlled body parts, to Dead to request that NPC's death.

It then starts CoObjectiveWait. That sequence resumes on a later frame after its ten-second game-time wait and calls StartNextObjectiveProfile to clear selected tracking data, advance currProfile and prepare the next objective, or end the stack. currProfile is not incremented until that later call.

This does not check whether the active objectives were actually completed before proceeding. The active-objective and living-enemy lists and their entries must be initialized. Repeated calls can schedule several delayed advances, each of which can move to another profile.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.ProgressToNextProfile
member.summary: Advances to the next configured challenge group, or ends the base session when the stack has no more groups.

remarks.para: Increments the zero-based currProfile index first. If it reaches roundProfileGroupList.Count, invokes StackCompletion and calls base EndSession. Otherwise, when the previous group was an objective group, it clears activeNPCObjectives and invokes ObjectiveCompleted. Next, if the new index is 2, it connects every objective's keyed notification to OnObjectiveKeyed. Only after those connections does it select the next group with ARENA_ChallengeSelect.

The new group is marked player-ready. If it is an objective group, every configured objective key receiver is set to CODE_A, the key-code value in that receiver's configuration; this assignment does not insert a key or unlock the objective. ObjectiveInitiated is then invoked, and the controller connects ObjectiveBatteryGrab to the shared battery-grab notification. A callback is a routine registered to respond to an action or notification: the keyed callback receives the notifying objective, while the battery-grab callback has no argument. Repeating setup can add duplicate connections and repeat calls to those routines.

A non-objective next group runs ARENA_PlayerEnter to apply entry settings. Its ready-preparation block normally skips because readiness is already true, although an entry callback can clear that flag. An objective next group waits for its battery/start flow rather than running player entry in this method.

The group list, previous selected group and required objective references must be configured. This call actually advances the index and clears or reconnects data; do not use it merely to inspect what the next challenge would be.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.ProjectileShot
member.summary: Adds one to the arena's recorded projectile-shot count.

remarks.para: While enabled, the controller connects this handler to RigidbodyProjectile.OnProjectileShot; disabling disconnects it. The notification has no shooter argument, and this handler does not check who fired, whether a wave is ongoing or what weapon was used.

Calling it directly adds one without firing a projectile. CalculatePlayerScore awards 1,500 points per positive recorded count before the difficulty multiplier; a successful calculation then clears projectilesShot together with totalHeadShots, so it consumes those recorded counts. This is a count of notifications received, not proof that every entry was a player hit or one trigger pull.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.RemovedZoneSpawners(Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_TriggeredSpawners)
member.summary: Queues the listed zone spawners for later removal from the arena's available spawn locations.
member.param: Zone object containing the spawner references to queue for removal.

remarks.para: Checks each trigSpawners.spawners entry against spawnerHash. Entries currently in that set are added to removeSpawnerList. Spawners absent from the set are skipped.

This does not immediately remove entries from profileSpawnerList or spawnerHash and does not destroy their objects. Repeating the call can queue the same spawner more than once. The supplied zone array, membership set and removal list must be initialized.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.RewardAmmo(System.Int32,System.Int32)
member.summary: Adds the requested number of light, medium or heavy rounds directly to the player's ammo reserve.
member.param: 0 for light, 1 for medium, or 2 for heavy ammunition.
Individual rounds to add; this path also passes through negative counts, which subtract from the reserve.

remarks.para: cartridge is a selector: 0 uses the configured light cartridge, 1 medium and 2 heavy. Other values return without changing inventory. These numbers are this method's selection values, not an arbitrary cartridge asset identifier.

amount counts individual rounds, not magazines or boxes. For example, RewardAmmo(1, 30) adds thirty medium rounds to the existing reserve. It creates no pickup object and does not load a held weapon's magazine.

The controller forwards amount without a positivity check. The checked AmmoInventory consumer adds it to the stored count, so a negative value subtracts and is not clamped to zero on this path.
