Configure AmmoInventory and the relevant static cartridge reference first; absent required references are not safely skipped.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.SetArenaState(Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.ArenaState)
member.summary: Stores the arena state and plays failure or win audio for those states.
member.param: State to store: ACTIVE, WAITING, FAILED, QUIT or WIN.

remarks.para: A coroutine is a sequence that Unity runs across frames, with waits between some steps.

ACTIVE, WAITING and QUIT only store the state. FAILED also plays failModeClip; WIN plays winModeClip. Repeating FAILED or WIN repeats the audio request because this method does not test whether the value changed.

An undefined enum value is still stored, then logged as an error. The method does not stop coroutines, remove NPCs, reset score or invoke mode-end events. Use the relevant transition flow when a state change also needs those actions.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.SetupCustomMode
member.summary: Starts friendly spawn requests toward the current wave's configured friendly count.

remarks.para: A coroutine is a sequence that Unity runs across frames, with waits between some steps.

Uses currentWave.friendlyProfileList.Count as the target count and stores the started CoSpawnFriendlyList coroutine in friendlySpawnRoutine. Existing activeFriendlyCount contributes toward that target; if it already meets the count, the routine ends without requesting another friendly.

The friendly list provides a count here, not individual profile choices. The checked spawn routine requests StaticProfiles.friendlyProfileList entry 0, cycling through profileSpawnerList locations, and waits after every request. Each wait reads the current assignedRoundProfile.friendlySpawnDelay, an integer duration in seconds of scaled game time. This is the configured delay of the currently assigned group, read again for each wait; slow motion makes it take longer on a real-world clock. Those lists and their required entries must be configured.

It does not prepare enemy waves, rebuild a custom challenge or clear previous friendlies. Starting it again does not first stop the earlier routine; both can request allies while waiting for the active count to update.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.SetupProtectMode
member.summary: Resets the bell latch, starts ordinary friendly spawning, and schedules the king after five real-time seconds.

remarks.para: A coroutine is a sequence that Unity runs across frames, with waits between some steps.

Clears isRung and starts CoSpawnFriendlyList using currentWave.friendlyProfileList.Count as the target active-friendly count, storing its coroutine. This uses the ordinary static friendly profile rather than each wave-list entry as a different spawn choice. After every ordinary-friendly request, the sequence reads the current assignedRoundProfile.friendlySpawnDelay, an integer duration in seconds of scaled game time, and waits that long. The delay is read again for each wait, and slow motion makes it take longer in real time.

It also starts CoKingEntrance with a five-second real-time wait, unaffected by slow motion. After the wait, a later frame resumes the sequence and calls SpawnKing, which requests the king and attempts the bell-start flow. The delay does not prove the king has finished spawning before the bell is rung.

Prepare the current wave, friendly profiles, spawn locations and kingSpawner before use. Calling this again resets the bell and schedules another king arrival without first canceling earlier arrivals or ordinary-friendly routines.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.SpawnKing
member.summary: Requests a friendly king from the configured king spawner, then attempts to ring the arena bell.

remarks.para: Uses entry 1, the second profile, in StaticProfiles.friendlyProfileList and sets that profile's isKing flag true. It changes the shared profile object rather than making a private copy. The static list must contain that entry and kingSpawner must exist.

Calls kingSpawner.ExplicitArenaSpawn with the friendly flag true, then ARENA_RingTheBell immediately after the request. It does not wait for a completed spawn. Bell conditions still apply: ON_TRIGGER_BELL and a clear isRung latch are required to start that countdown.
The registered king's FriendlyRegistration hook requests the crown. Calling SpawnKing again can request another king, even when the bell has already rung and skips a second countdown.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.SpawnLoot
member.summary: Requests the current wave's configured loot from .

remarks.para: Spawning coroutines are sequences the loot spawner continues across frames and waits. They schedule spawn requests whose completion may occur later.

Returns when arenaState is QUIT. Otherwise, if lootSpawner is missing, it searches this controller's children for GenGameControl_Spawner and caches the result. When a valid spawner exists, calls SpawnWaveLoot(currentWave); if none is found, returns without a request.

The request uses the already selected currentWave. It does not choose the next wave, mark a reward earned or directly add score. Other states, including FAILED and WAITING, do not block the request in this method.

The spawner's wave-loot flow starts its own spawning coroutines and uses a separate weapon-mode loot path when configured for WEAPON. Loot amounts and entries come from the wave profile, so a request is not a guarantee that every possible item appears. Repeated calls can schedule the same wave's loot again.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.StartNextObjectiveProfile
member.summary: Clears selected NPC tracking data and prepares the next objective profile, or ends the session after the last group.

remarks.para: A callback is a routine registered to run when an action or notification occurs. The objective-destruction callback receives the objective that sent the destruction notification. Entry callbacks are routines run in response to player entry during ARENA_PlayerEnter; they can change readiness before the later check.

Immediately resets enemiesKilled and activeFriendlyCount, clears the living-friendly list, NPC_List, NPC_Data_List and NPC_Data_Dict, and empties the NPC record list for every zone display. It refreshes the displays, then increments the zero-based currProfile index.

If that index reaches roundProfileGroupList.Count, invokes StackCompletion, plays winModeClip and calls base EndSession. Otherwise selects that group with ARENA_ChallengeSelect, marks the player ready and runs ARENA_PlayerEnter to load entry settings.

It replaces activeNPCObjectives with allNPCObjectives[currProfile]. If the new group is an objective group, clears its limitReached flag, connects the objective destruction callback and requests the lightning effect. Then it stops the tracked arena timer, if present, and starts a fresh arenaStartDelay countdown in game-time seconds.

The objective list must contain an entry matching the new group index. These tracking-list clears do not themselves despawn every physical NPC; the normal ProgressToNextObjectiveProfile flow requested enemy death before its ten-second wait. Calling this directly skips that wait and advances immediately, and repeating it can skip another profile.

The ready-preparation block after player entry normally skips because readiness is already true. An entry callback can clear it and make its playerReady/geometry actions run. Configure all lists, profiles and player references before using this transition.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_SpawnCapsule.OnLaunchedArena(Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController,Il2CppSLZ.Data.EnemyProfile)
member.summary: Enables the capsule’s trail and starts its timed arena enemy-spawn sequence.
member.param: Controller providing the ACTIVE-state check, normal-spawner fallback and spawned-enemy registration.
Profile supplying the enemy spawnable and optional AI configuration for success or fallback spawning.

remarks.para: A coroutine is a sequence that continues over frames. This one waits 0.25 game-time seconds, requests 10 positional beeps with delays starting at 0.25 seconds and multiplied by the unitless factor 0.99 after each cycle, then waits another 0.25 seconds before checking the capsule’s world position. These numbers are requested waits on the scaled game clock, which slows during slow motion. The coroutine resumes on a later frame after each wait, so actual elapsed time can be longer. It does not wait for a collision or test whether the capsule has landed.

The position check requires world Y from 0 through 4, inclusive, and full three-dimensional distance from the world origin no greater than the magnitude of maxDistFromCenter, its value without a minus sign, measured in world units. It checks once at this stage, not continuously while the capsule moves. The sequence then enables expandCollider, waits 0.1 game-time seconds and grows its spherical physics shape over a 0.5-game-second interval before disabling it and restoring startRadius.

After growth, an acceptable earlier position and an ACTIVE arena select the success path: it requests the explosion sound, waits 0.1 game-time seconds, then requests the supplied profile’s spawnable at the capsule’s current world position with identity rotation, the world’s unrotated orientation. ACTIVE is checked before that sound/wait, not again immediately before the later spawn request.

The spawn callback, a routine called to report the spawned object, passes the profile’s optional AI configuration to an AIBrain only when the profile has that configuration and an AIBrain is found on the object. AIBrain is the component that manages an enemy’s behavior; SetBaseConfig stores the supplied configuration on its existing behavior component. The callback then activates the object even without an AIBrain. A found AIBrain must also have its behaviour component, the code controlling its actions, for death/reactivation wiring and registration; a missing behaviour causes an error at that step. If an AIBrain with that component is found, it connects death/reactivation handling through profileSpawnerList[0] and registers it with the arena as an enemy; without an AIBrain it skips that wiring and registration. The list must contain that first normal spawner; the capsule is not itself a ProfileSpawner.

The capsule invokes its no-argument OnSpawn UnityEvent, a list of routines that run when the event fires, after issuing the success request. The request can complete later, so this event is not proof that the callback or registration has finished. The event runs after the expanding collider has been disabled and reset, but before the later 0.5-game-second cleanup wait, trail disable and pooled-despawn request.

If the earlier position check failed or the arena was not ACTIVE at the success test, it calls SpawnFailedHoiPoi and requests its own pooled despawn. Its Poolee component manages spawned objects kept for reuse; despawning removes the capsule from active play through that component. A capsule outside a pool is deactivated rather than guaranteed to return to a pool. That fallback requests the same profile through a random normal arena spawner only if the arena is still ACTIVE. Required setup includes the trail, expand collider, event, supplied controller/profile and a valid normal-spawner list. A firing impulse is a brief push that changes motion. This method does not apply the launcher’s firing impulse, and repeated calls start additional sequences without stopping a previous one.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ArmFinale.BuildJoints
member.summary: Creates the ceiling tiles’ physics connections from the configured tile list and joint settings.

remarks.para: A joint is a physics connection that controls how a body can move. Unity’s Start callback, the routine called when this component begins running, executes the same setup. For each _ceilingTiles entry, it adds a new MarrowJoint to that body’s GameObject, supplies _jointInfo with that tile as body A and no body B, then stores the available ConfigurableJoint at the matching _tileJoints index. A missing connected body makes the connection use the world rather than another moving body.

Provide valid tile bodies and joint settings before startup. MarrowJoint creates its underlying ConfigurableJoint only when the tile body is active and enabled. If it is inactive during this pass, the cached slot can be null; the later creation of that body’s joint does not itself refresh ArmFinale’s cached slot.

The constructor creates a 16-slot _tileJoints array, and this pass does not resize it. The array must have at least as many slots as the tile list. Calling this again adds another MarrowJoint per tile and overwrites the cached references without first removing the previously added components. It is setup, not a safe way to refresh an existing set of tile connections.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ArmFinale.GongHit
member.summary: Enables offscreen arm-mesh updates and starts the descent timeline, recording the finale’s Decent stage first.

remarks.para: If armMesh is assigned, updateWhenOffscreen is set to true so the skinned arm can continue updating while outside the camera’s view. It then sets _armStage to Decent and calls Play on decent, the PlayableDirector for the descent timeline. A PlayableDirector plays a prepared sequence of animation and other scene actions.

The stage changes before the director’s Play call. There is no current-stage guard, gong-collision test or _timer reset in this routine: another call requests playback again. The gong or timeline must be connected to call this method; the method does not detect a hit by itself. decent is required, while armMesh is optional.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ArmFinale.JointDestroyEvent(System.Int32)
member.summary: Locks a cached ceiling tile’s movement and rotation settings, then sets its joint’s break-force threshold to zero.
member.param: Index of the tile’s already-created joint in _tileJoints, matching its position in _ceilingTiles.

remarks.para: It sets all three linear motion settings and all three angular motion settings to Locked, preventing motion allowed by those settings while the joint remains intact, then sets breakForce to zero. breakForce is the force threshold for breaking, rather than a force applied to the tile. This assigns a zero threshold; it does not guarantee a completed break or its exact physics step. It does not directly call Destroy or erase the _tileJoints reference.

The index selects the cached joint at the same position used when BuildJoints processes _ceilingTiles. Use a valid array index whose joint has been created. Negative indices, indices outside the array and missing joints are not treated as harmless requests.

The method does not check the finale stage, a collision or whether the tile was smashed. A scene action or other caller chooses when to invoke it. Do not use its name as a promise that the component disappears immediately or that every other joint setting, such as drives or collision settings, is cleared.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ArmFinale.ReadyForAscent
member.summary: Enters the Hold stage so the ascent starts on an Update with at least one reported attached hand.

remarks.para: Update is Unity’s routine called each rendered frame. The angular drive is the joint’s physics motor, which requests rotation. This call only sets _armStage to Hold. On a later Update, a positive _attachedHandCount changes the stage to Ascent before stopping decent, playing ascent and changing the windmill joint’s angular drive. Existing reported attachments can satisfy this immediately on the next Update; a new grab is not required.

Calling it does not itself play the ascent timeline, stop the descent timeline or reset _timer. It has no current-stage guard. Calling it while another stage is active returns the component to this waiting rule, so it is not equivalent to simply assigning the Ascent stage.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ArmFinale.ReadyForVoid
member.summary: Enters the Void stage, activates the assigned hole stopper and starts the later seat/grip release timing.

remarks.para: The order is _armStage = Void, holeStopper.SetActive(true), then _timer = Time.time. Time.time is the scaled game-time clock in seconds, so pauses and changes to the game’s time scale affect the elapsed timing. holeStopper is required; activation can run that GameObject’s enable callbacks, routines Unity calls to respond to becoming active, before this method records the new timestamp.

Update is Unity’s routine called each rendered frame. A Rigidbody is Unity’s component for physics motion; the seat-body check tests its assigned physics body, separately from whether a player occupies the seat. In the Void stage, Update disables offscreen updates on an assigned armMesh. After more than 0.75 game-time seconds, it requests immediate exit from palmSeat when that seat has a valid seat Rigidbody; Seat itself performs the exit only if a player rig is registered. After more than one game-time second, a positive _attachedHandCount makes it call hostManager.ForceDetachAll.

The Update checks force-detach before requesting seat exit when both conditions pass on the same frame. These are repeated checks, not one-shot completion flags. Calling ReadyForVoid again records a new timestamp after activating the stopper, delaying the release checks from that new time. It does not immediately eject or detach the player.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ArmFinale.WindmillProjectRotation(System.Single)
member.summary: Chooses a windmill joint rotation using the blades’ predicted orientation, then adjusts its drive over the supplied time.
member.param: Positive lookahead and adjustment duration in scaled game-time seconds; the same value is used for prediction and the frame sequence.

remarks.para: A Rigidbody is Unity’s component for physics motion. The joint drive acts like a motor: its spring pulls toward the target angle, and damping resists relative rotational motion. It reads windmillBlades.rotation and angularVelocity in world space. The prediction assumes the current angular velocity stays constant: predicted turn in degrees = angular speed × secondsFromNow × 180/π. Angular speed is the velocity vector’s length in radians per second; secondsFromNow is the lookahead in game-time seconds; 180/π is the unitless radians-to-degrees conversion factor. For example, an illustrative speed of 1 radian per second over 2 seconds predicts about 114.6 degrees of additional turn. Zero angular speed uses the current rotation.

Among the blades’ predicted local up, down, right and left directions, it chooses the one most nearly pointing toward world up. It assigns the corresponding one of four prepared rotations to windmillJoint.targetRotation immediately. The remaining signed angle is measured from that predicted direction to world up, with its sign determined around the blades’ current world-space forward direction. This is a drive target, not a direct rotation assignment to the Rigidbody.

It then starts a coroutine, a sequence that continues over frames, using the same secondsFromNow as its duration. The requested total change in target angular velocity is 2 × signed angle × π/180 ÷ duration. Here signed angle is in degrees, π/180 converts degrees to radians, and duration is seconds, giving a change in radians per second. Each frame adds deltaTime × requested change ÷ duration to the joint target’s X component; deltaTime is that frame’s scaled game-time duration in seconds. The duration is the loop’s configured threshold. Each pass tests elapsed time before adding a whole frame’s deltaTime and yielding to a later frame. The last increment can take elapsed time beyond the duration; the final drive and zero-velocity writes occur on the next coroutine resume. The formula’s requested change therefore does not guarantee an exactly achieved total change.

During the sequence, angular-X spring strength is 1000 × progress², where progress is elapsed game-time seconds divided by duration seconds, clamped from 0 to 1. For example, progress 0.5 gives spring strength 250. The captured drive’s damping and maximum-force settings are retained during this ramp. At completion it instead writes spring strength 1000000, damping 100000 and targetAngularVelocity = zero; these are explicit drive settings, not a restoration of the original drive.

Assign both windmillBlades and windmillJoint before calling it, and use a positive duration. There is no input clamp or zero-duration protection, and the angle calculation divides by the supplied duration. A nonpositive duration skips the frame loop but still reaches the final drive writes. Repeated calls start additional sequences without stopping earlier ones, so their writes can compete. This method returns no projected angle and does not check _armStage.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ArticulatedArmController.Awake
member.summary: Measures the starting arm lengths and records the starting rotations needed to drive the finger joints.

remarks.para: Awake is Unity's initialization callback: a routine Unity calls when this component is first initialized. It measures shoulder-to-elbow and elbow-to-wrist distances in the world, and stores half the wrist-to-hand distance for each of the two small wrist/hand segments. BONELAB uses meters for these distances.

For each of the 15 finger joints, it records the finger segment's rotation relative to the body connected to that joint. A physics joint is a connection between two objects in the physics simulation. These starting rotations let later finger poses become joint targets. Assign the arm references, all finger joints, and their connected bodies before initialization; missing references interrupt setup.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ArticulatedArmController.CalibrateArmStretch
member.summary: Requests stretch-curve adjustments at current point indices 0 and 1, then remembers the stretch settings.

remarks.para: A key is a point on the curve. Desired wrist reach is the world-space distance from the shoulder to the target hand position shifted by the current wrist-minus-hand displacement. The starting arm length is the shoulder-to-elbow length plus the elbow-to-wrist length measured during initialization. stretchThreshold is the unitless reach input above which the curve is sampled; maxStretchFactor is the unitless setting for the generated upper multiplier of both starting segment lengths; stretchRatio controls how much extra requested wrist reach, relative to the starting arm length, is needed to arrive at that multiplier. Update is Unity's routine that runs once per rendered frame.

The horizontal axis of ArmStretchCurve is desired wrist reach divided by the starting shoulder-to-elbow plus elbow-to-wrist lengths. The vertical axis is the multiplier applied to both lengths. For the normal ordered two-point setup, this routine requests key 0 at (stretchThreshold, 1) and key 1 at (1 + (maxStretchFactor - 1) × stretchRatio, maxStretchFactor + 0.0001). All three settings and both curve axes are unitless.

For maxStretchFactor = 1.05, stretchThreshold = 0.8, and stretchRatio = 2, the requested points are (0.8, 1) and (1.10, 1.0501). It also sets the tangents, which control how the curve bends between keys. It does not remeasure the arm. Update performs this same adjustment when a setting differs from its remembered value.

A key is a point on the curve; its index is its position in the list ordered by horizontal input, starting at 0. Calibration requests adjustments to the points currently at index 0, then index 1. Moving the first point can change the list order, so a custom curve's extra points are not guaranteed to keep their original values.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ArticulatedArmController.SolveArm
member.summary: Positions and turns the arm bones toward , stretching the upper arm and forearm when the requested reach passes the stretch threshold.

remarks.para: The target is a Transform, an object holding a position, rotation, and scale. Its position is a world-space hand goal. The solver offsets that goal by the current wrist-to-hand displacement to find the desired wrist position. It divides shoulder-to-desired-wrist distance by the two starting arm lengths to obtain the unitless stretch-curve input.

It places the elbow and wrist along their parents' local blue Z axes, turns the shoulder and elbow to bend toward that wrist goal, relaxes arm twist, and positions the small carpal/hand segments. The final hand rotation matches targetHand's world rotation. The hand may fall short of an unreachable position: the solve limits reach and keeps a 0.004-meter (4 mm) margin below the current upper-arm plus forearm length.
This routine changes transforms directly. The finger physics-joint targets are handled separately by SolveHandPose. Required arm and target references must be assigned.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ArticulatedArmController.SolveHandPose
member.summary: Builds the finger pose from the five curl inputs and makes the finger physics joints aim for that pose.

remarks.para: It sends thumb, index, middle, ring, and pinky to handAnimator, asks it to calculate and apply its pose, then reads each posed finger segment's rotation relative to its parent. It converts that rotation, together with the joint's cached starting rotation, into the target for the matching physics joint. A physics joint connects two objects in the physics simulation; its target is the rotation it tries to reach, not a guarantee that the finger has already reached it.

Set up handAnimator and all 15 finger joints before use. The starting rotations are recorded during Awake, a routine Unity calls when this component is first initialized. The animator smooths the curl inputs over successive frames and can replace an input with a queued finger override.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ArticulatedArmController.Update
member.summary: Each rendered frame, refreshes changed stretch settings, solves the arm, then updates the finger pose and physics-joint targets.

remarks.para: maxStretchFactor sets the unitless generated upper multiplier of both starting arm lengths. stretchThreshold sets the unitless reach input above which ArmStretchCurve is sampled. stretchRatio controls the extra requested reach needed for the generated upper key. A key is a point on the curve. Its input is shoulder-to-desired-wrist distance divided by the starting shoulder-to-elbow plus elbow-to-wrist lengths, and its output multiplies both starting lengths. The desired wrist position is the target hand's world position shifted by the current wrist-minus-hand displacement. The two starting lengths are measured during initialization.

Unity calls Update once per rendered frame while the component is enabled. If maxStretchFactor, stretchThreshold, or stretchRatio differs from its remembered value, the curve is adjusted at current index 0, then current index 1, before solving. SolveArm includes WristRelax and the carpal/hand positioning pass; SolveHandPose runs afterward.
A physics joint connects objects in the physics simulation. Its rotation target is the orientation it tries to reach; setting the target does not guarantee that the finger has already reached it.

A key is a point on the curve; its index is its position in the list ordered by horizontal input, starting at 0. Calibration requests adjustments to the points currently at index 0, then index 1. Moving the first point can change the list order, so a custom curve's extra points are not guaranteed to keep their original values.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ArticulatedArmController.WristRelax
member.summary: Gradually rolls the upper arm around its reach direction to ease wrist twist, then realigns the wrist with the hand target.

remarks.para: The roll axis is the world-space direction from shoulderLf toward the desired wrist, including the current wrist-to-hand offset. ElbowIsNot computes the requested roll from wrist twist, arm posture, and WristElbowIsNotCurve. The stored roll angle moves partway toward that request each call.

The fraction moved is the smaller of 0.12 and 0.0025 × the absolute angle difference in degrees. For a stored angle of 0 degrees and a requested angle of 40 degrees, the fraction is 0.1, so the new stored angle is 4 degrees. This smoothing is per call and has no elapsed-time multiplier; its speed can therefore change with frame rate. It turns shoulderLf, then adjusts wristLf so the wrist still points along the forearm while following the target's roll.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BalloonGun.Fire
member.summary: Advances the preview-color queue and requests a balloon and muzzle effect at the firing point.

remarks.para: A spawn callback is a routine called with the object when a spawn succeeds; the request can finish after the requesting routine returns and does not itself guarantee success. A raycast checks a straight line through the scene for an allowed collision shape.

SetBalloonColor runs first, moving the old balloonColor3 into nextBalloonColor and choosing a new random preview color. The balloon spawn callback applies the current nextBalloonColor and assigns firePointTransform as its aiming reference.

The spawned ProjectileBalloon performs the aiming raycast and attachment using its own range and collision layers. This method does not raycast using BalloonGun.effectiveRange or collisionLayers. The callback reads the current color and muzzle pose when the object becomes available, so those are not immutable snapshots for overlapping spawn requests.
Calling this method directly does not play gunSFX.GunShot; the normal held-trigger update includes that sound after requesting the spawns.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BalloonGun.OnDisable
member.summary: Removes the trigger-grip event routines registered by when this component stops being active.

remarks.para: Unity calls OnDisable when the component stops being active. It removes OnTriggerGripAttached, OnTriggerGripDetached and OnTriggerGripUpdate from the assigned trigger grip's grab, release and held-update events. Callbacks are routines called to perform or report an action; removing these registrations stops those events from calling this gun through those subscriptions.

The checked path requires an assigned triggerGrip. It removes the routines from the reference currently stored there; replacing triggerGrip while enabled does not automatically move the old registrations to the new grip.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BalloonGun.OnEnable
member.summary: Registers trigger-grip event routines when this component becomes active.

remarks.para: Unity calls OnEnable when the component becomes active. It registers OnTriggerGripAttached for a grab, OnTriggerGripDetached for a release and OnTriggerGripUpdate for updates while held. A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action; registering it lets the grip event call that routine with the reporting Hand.

The grab and release routines show and hide the preview-balloon root. Held updates animate the previews and process trigger-down firing. The assigned triggerGrip must be valid; OnDisable removes these registrations when the component stops being active.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BalloonGun.OnTriggerGripAttached(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand)
member.summary: Shows the gun's preview-balloon root when the trigger grip is grabbed.

remarks.para: It activates balloonRoot. It does not physically attach the reporting hand or reset the color queue; the hand argument is not read by this preview toggle. balloonRoot must be assigned.

member.param: The hand reported by the grip; the preview toggle does not use it.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BalloonGun.OnTriggerGripDetached(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand)
member.summary: Hides the gun's preview-balloon root when the trigger grip is released.

remarks.para: It deactivates balloonRoot without clearing preview colors or cached motion state. It does not physically detach the reporting hand; the hand argument is not read by this toggle.

member.param: The hand reported by the grip; the preview toggle does not use it.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BalloonGun.OnTriggerGripUpdate(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand)
member.summary: Animates the held gun's preview balloons and fires when the reporting hand has a trigger-down event.

remarks.para: A renderer draws the visible preview shape; moving its Transform changes that shape’s position.

The grip calls this routine while a hand holds it. A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action. Local positions are measured along each preview object's parent axes, in scene-distance units corresponding to meters when parent scale is 1. The motion gradually approaches each chosen target rather than jumping to it.

Every call rotates balloonRoot locally, periodically chooses new local target positions and smoothly moves each preview renderer toward its target. It checks the hand's index-button-down flag after that visual update; holding the trigger without another down event does not provide continuous fire here.

On a down event it advances the color queue, requests the balloon and muzzle effect, then plays GunShot. There is no separate input for cycling colors in this method: the color shift belongs to the shot.
The preview arrays and renderer references must be valid and long enough. The callback is an attached-grip update, not an unconditional update for guns left lying in the world.

member.param: The held grip's hand; its trigger-down flag requests the shot.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BalloonGun.SetBalloonColor
member.summary: Moves the last preview color into the shot-color slot, shifts the other preview colors forward, and chooses a new random first color.

remarks.para: A renderer draws a visible preview shape; its material controls the color of that shape’s surface.
Start is Unity's one-time setup routine before this enabled component's first normal update.

The shift is nextBalloonColor = old balloonColor3, then color3 = old color2, color2 = old color1, color1 = old color0, and color0 = a random color. It updates the materials of balloonMesh elements 0 through 3 to show the resulting queue.

For example, a queue labeled A, B, C, D becomes random, A, B, C and the shot color becomes D. Start runs this after initializing the four preview colors, and every Fire runs it before requesting a balloon.
The method expects at least four valid renderers with materials. Setting a color field alone does not refresh these displayed materials.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BaseGameController.BeginSession
member.summary: Fires the session-begin event, marks the session running, and starts the timer selected by timerMode.

remarks.para: sessionBegin fires before isSessionOngoing becomes true and before the timer starts. A listener therefore sees the previous session state. The older onSessionBegin Unity event is not invoked by this base implementation.

The timer is a coroutine: a routine that continues in steps over several frames. COUNT_UP and COUNT_UP_REALTIME add to the existing timerValue; this method does not reset it, the score, or the NPC lists. COUNT_DOWN initializes its own countdown, while REALTIME reads seconds since the application started.
There is no already-running check. Calling this repeatedly starts additional timer sequences and replaces the stored timerRoutine reference.
sessionBegin is invoked with no arguments. An event listener is a routine called when that event fires. timerValue is the shared stored timer in seconds.

A frame is one game update. timeScale is the unitless game-speed multiplier: scaled frame seconds follow that multiplier, while unscaled frame seconds measure real elapsed time. At timeScale 0.5, a frame lasting 0.02 real seconds normally contributes 0.01 game seconds.

Replacing timerRoutine does not stop the earlier sequence. Each active COUNT_UP sequence adds the frame's game time to the same timerValue; for example, two such sequences can advance it roughly twice as fast. COUNT_UP_REALTIME sequences also share the stored value, adding real frame seconds when timeScale is nonzero.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BaseGameController.CheckForProxyTarget(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.TriggerRefProxy)
member.summary: Gives each living registered NPC targeting the supplied proxy a replacement target from .

remarks.para: A target proxy is a small component that identifies an object the NPC can aim at. This walks NPC_Data_List, skips records marked dead, and checks each record's targetProxy. For a match, it changes the NPC's behavior target and stores the replacement in that record.
This changes existing target assignments; it does not add or remove the supplied proxy from friendlyProxyList.

member.param: The target identifier to replace on matching living NPC records.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BaseGameController.CoDelayedEnd
member.summary: Creates the countdown that can reload or change levels after the session has ended.

remarks.para: A coroutine is a routine that continues across frames; calling this only creates its sequence. EndSession starts it for LOAD_NEXT, RELOAD_CURRENT, and EXPLICIT. The session flag is already false when this sequence begins.

A positive delayedEndMaxTime becomes timerValue, in seconds, and decreases by scaled frame time. Slow motion stretches the wall-clock wait and a paused game stops it. A negative value copies defaultEndDelayedMaxTime into both values. Exactly zero exits without performing a level transition.

Once the countdown is no longer positive, RELOAD_CURRENT requests a reload and EXPLICIT requests the configured level through the fade effect. LOAD_NEXT and NONE perform no loading in this base implementation. It reads endMode at that time. The shared timerValue can pass slightly below zero on the final frame.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BaseGameController.CoDelayedStart
member.summary: Creates a countdown that displays the remaining wait before calling .

remarks.para: A coroutine is a routine that continues across frames. Calling this only creates its sequence; it must be started with StartCoroutine to run. BeginSession itself does not start this delay.

Positive delayedMaxTime supplies the starting timerValue in seconds. Negative delayedMaxTime restores defaultDelayedMaxTime into both fields. Each frame subtracts scaled frame time and refreshes the display, so slow motion lengthens the wall-clock wait and pausing stops it.

When the countdown finishes, the known timer modes reset timerValue to zero before BeginSession; COUNT_DOWN then initializes its own remaining time. An exactly zero delayedMaxTime calls BeginSession immediately and skips that reset. A configured 3-second wait ends on a frame after the countdown reaches zero, rather than at a guaranteed wall-clock instant.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BaseGameController.CoTimerDown
member.summary: Creates the session countdown that calls when time runs out.

remarks.para: A coroutine is a routine that continues across frames. BeginSession starts this sequence for COUNT_DOWN. It copies a positive maxTime into timerValue, both measured in seconds; otherwise it copies defaultMaxTime into maxTime and timerValue.

Each running frame subtracts scaled frame time. At half time scale, 10 countdown seconds take about 20 real seconds. The value is not clamped to zero; after a subtraction crosses zero, EndSession is called on the next continuation. It also calls EndSession if continued after the session flag becomes false.

The compiled display-refresh test asks whether remaining time has increased by at least one second since the last refresh. A normally decreasing countdown can therefore leave its label unchanged until the end-session refresh. The stored timer still decreases.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BaseGameController.CoTimerRealtime
member.summary: Creates a timer that displays seconds since the application started while the session is running.

remarks.para: A coroutine is a routine that continues across frames. BeginSession starts this sequence for REALTIME. Each continuation replaces timerValue with Unity's realtimeSinceStartup and refreshes the timer labels.

This clock ignores game time scale. If the application has been running for 120 seconds when the session begins, the value starts near 120, rather than zero. It continues sampling while the session flag is true, including during a time-scale pause.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BaseGameController.CoTimerUp
member.summary: Creates a timer that adds game-time seconds to timerValue while the session is running.

remarks.para: A coroutine is a routine that continues across frames. BeginSession starts this sequence for COUNT_UP. It adds scaled frame time to the existing timerValue without resetting it or stopping at maxTime.

At half time scale, about 2 real seconds add 1 timer second. At time scale zero the value stops growing. Timer labels refresh when the value is at least one second above the last value sent; EndSession provides the final fractional display.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BaseGameController.CoTimerUpRealtime
member.summary: Creates a timer that adds real-time frame durations while the session is running and the game is not paused.

remarks.para: A coroutine is a routine that continues across frames. BeginSession starts this sequence for COUNT_UP_REALTIME. It adds unscaledDeltaTime, the real duration of the last frame in seconds, to the existing timerValue.

Slow motion does not reduce the amount added, but timeScale equal to zero skips the addition. It therefore pauses during a game-time pause. For example, at half time scale, about 2 real seconds add 2 timer seconds. It does not reset timerValue or stop at maxTime.
Labels are checked for a refresh before that frame's addition, when the value is at least one second above the last value sent.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BaseGameController.CreateZoneSeeker(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.AIBrain)

After spawning succeeds, a callback—a routine called to report the result—assigns the player rig and the NPC target to its SuperSeeker component. Returning from this method does not guarantee the marker has finished spawning. The player rig is the set of objects that controls the player's body.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BaseGameController.DespawnAllNPCs

It does not clear the tracking lists or count these removals as kills. The base despawn callback only marks records already recorded as dead, so this method is not a general cleanup of all bookkeeping for living NPCs.
