member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BaseGameController.EndSession
member.summary: Fires the session-end event, stops the stored timer, and starts any configured end countdown.

remarks.para: sessionEnd fires before isSessionOngoing is cleared and before timerRoutine is stopped. A listener can still see the running-session flag and the final session timer value. The older onSessionEnd Unity event is not invoked by this base implementation.

LOAD_NEXT, RELOAD_CURRENT, and EXPLICIT start CoDelayedEnd, a coroutine—a routine that continues across frames. NONE starts no end countdown. A positive end delay can immediately replace timerValue with remaining transition time before the final display refresh.
The method refreshes timer labels with hundredths of a second. It does not itself mark progress complete or submit a score, and repeated calls can fire the event and start end sequences again.
sessionEnd is invoked with no arguments. An event listener is a routine called when that event fires. During an end countdown, timerValue is the shared remaining transition time in seconds.

A frame is one game update. timeScale is the unitless game-speed multiplier: scaled frame seconds follow that multiplier, while unscaled frame seconds measure real elapsed time. At timeScale 0.5, a frame lasting 0.02 real seconds normally contributes 0.01 game seconds.

Repeated calls can start multiple end countdowns sharing timerValue. A newly started countdown can reset that remaining value, and each active countdown subtracts the frame's game time from it. A coroutine handle is the reference Unity uses to identify a running sequence. This method does not retain or stop the end-countdown handles; stopping timerRoutine affects the stored session timer.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BaseGameController.GetAllLinkData
member.summary: Clears the link data list and repopulates it with the loaded objects returned by Unity's no-argument FindObjectsOfType call. Components on inactive GameObjects are omitted.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BaseGameController.GetFriendlyProxy
member.summary: Chooses a player or eligible friendly-NPC for hostile NPCs from .

remarks.para: A target proxy identifies an object the NPC can aim at. The search begins at currFriendlyProxy, resetting that starting index to zero when it is at or beyond the list count. A Player entry returns playerProxy. Another entry needs an AgentLinkControl whose puppet's requested state is Alive; it returns that component's triggerProxy. A puppet is the system controlling an NPC's simulated body. This tests its state setting, so a physical state transition can still be in progress.

If no eligible entry is found, it returns playerProxy, which can itself be null. Selecting a target increments currFriendlyProxy once. Skipping entries only advances the local search index, so this is not a guarantee of strict round-robin selection.
Keep the list and its entries valid. A null list, null entry, missing root object, or missing puppet reference can fail rather than cleanly returning null.

member.returns: The selected target proxy, or the cached playerProxy fallback; that fallback can be null.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BaseGameController.KillAll
member.summary: Requests the Dead state for every NPC in .

remarks.para: Each NPC's physical puppet—the system that controls its simulated body—gets a Dead state request. This does not directly subtract health, update kill counters, or despawn bodies; those effects depend on the NPC's later state/death handling.
It only visits the controller's living-enemy list. Friendly NPCs and unregistered enemies are not included.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BaseGameController.LOADEXPLICITLEVEL
member.summary: Requests a fade transition to the level stored in .

remarks.para: With no explicitSceneCrate reference, this returns without starting a load. Otherwise it passes that destination and the game's default loading-screen level to LoadFXAndLevel. Loading is requested after the spawned fade effect reports completion, so the destination need not be ready when this method returns.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BaseGameController.LOADNEXTLEVEL
member.summary: Performs no action in the compiled base controller.

remarks.para: Calling this does not request the next level. The base CoDelayedEnd sequence also performs no load for LOAD_NEXT. A game-specific controller or mod must provide any next-level transition it needs.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BaseGameController.LOAD_HUB
member.summary: Requests a fade transition to the hub level configured in .

remarks.para: The destination is StaticProfiles.hubLevelCrate, with the game's default loading-screen level. LoadFXAndLevel requests the load after its fade effect completes; returning from LOAD_HUB does not mean the hub has finished loading.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BaseGameController.LoadFXAndLevel(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.LevelCrateReference,Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.LevelCrateReference)
member.summary: Requests the game's fade-out effect and arranges to load the destination after the fade completes.

remarks.para: This first asks the asset pool to spawn the configured fade effect. A callback—a routine called to report a completed action—finds its FadeVolume component and assigns an onComplete handler. That handler then calls the scene-loading system with level and loadLevel.
The fade and level load continue after this method returns. The effect must successfully spawn and have a FadeVolume component before this path can request the load.

member.param: The destination level crate to request after the fade finishes.
The loading-screen level crate passed to the scene-loading system.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BaseGameController.OnLevelLoadGetPlayer
member.summary: Caches the player's and , attempts to seed friendly targets, and reports the end of that setup attempt.

remarks.para: Awake, Unity's initialization callback, registers this routine with the level-loading system. It reads PlayerRefs.Instance.PlayerRigManager, stores the rig's GameObject and child TriggerRefProxy, and, only when that proxy is valid, assigns it team number 1. A rig is the set of objects that controls the player's body; the proxy identifies that body to NPC targeting.

Only when the player proxy is valid does it clear friendlyProxyList and add that proxy. With a missing or destroyed proxy, the old target list is kept. It then sets each configured ProfileSpawner's private cached playerProxy to the found reference, even when that reference is missing. OnPlayerFound fires afterward with no arguments. There is no one-shot latch here: another successful invocation can notify listeners again.

Awake is the initialization routine Unity calls before normal component startup. A GameObject is a Unity scene object that holds components. The player-target setup notification reports the completion of this attempt; it does not guarantee that a valid targeting proxy was found.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BaseGameController.OnNPC_DeathBase(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.AIBrain)
member.summary: Records a registered NPC's death, updates faction counts and lists, then invokes .

remarks.para: The record is found by the brain's GameObject. The method marks it dead and captures its puppet's targetRoot position in world coordinates, measured in meters along the scene's axes. targetRoot is the puppet's stored root Transform, the component holding an object's position and rotation. Hostile deaths decrement activeEnemyCount and increment enemiesKilled and totalEnemiesKilled; friendly deaths decrement activeFriendlyCount without adding an enemy kill.

Before the event, the brain moves from the matching alive list into the matching dead list and its controller death handler is removed. A friendly also leaves the target-proxy pool and friendly_Data_List, and its behavior team is changed to 0.

The event receives that same NPC_Data record. It fires before optional delayed despawning, before the UI refresh, and before ARENA records deathTime and appends to dead_NPC_Data_List. An unknown brain logs an error and does not fire the death event. Calling this manually again is not protected by an already-dead check.
A brain is the NPC's behavior component; its puppet is the system controlling its simulated body. A GameObject is the Unity scene object holding those components.

member.param: The behavior component of the NPC whose death should be recorded.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BaseGameController.OnSlowTime(System.Single)
member.summary: Updates isSlowTime from the reported slow-motion step number.

remarks.para: The TimeManager callback—a routine called when the time controls report a change—passes a step number as a float. Step 0 is the normal-time setting; steps 1 and above select slow motion. This stores true when slowStep is at least 1, and false otherwise.

It does not itself change time scale or timer pacing. Timer sequences choose scaled or unscaled frame durations separately. For example, passing 0 clears the flag and passing 1 sets it. The argument is a step index, not a duration in seconds or a speed multiplier.

member.param: The slow-motion step number reported as a float; 0 is normal time and values at least 1 set the flag.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BaseGameController.RELOADCURRENTLEVEL
member.summary: Requests that the scene-loading system reload the current level.

remarks.para: This forwards directly to SceneStreamer.Reload. The level transition is handled by that system; returning from this method does not mean a fresh level is already ready. For a delayed request, use WAITANDRELOADCURRENTLEVEL.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BaseGameController.RegisterNPCBase(Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ProfileSpawner,Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.AIBrain,Il2CppSLZ.Data.EnemyProfile,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Registers a spawned NPC's , connects its death/despawn notifications, and reports its data to registration listeners.

remarks.para: For a GameObject not yet in NPC_Data_Dict, this creates an NPC_Data record holding the brain, spawner, zone, profile and available target-proxy references. It adds the brain to NPC_List and the appropriate alive list and increments that faction's active count. A friendly gets behavior team 1 and contributes its target proxy to friendlyProxyList.

The NPC death notification is connected to OnNPC_DeathBase. If the object has a cached pool component, its despawn notification is connected to OnDespawn. These notifications are callbacks: routines called when the corresponding action is reported. In ARENA, a hostile NPC can also be assigned a target from GetFriendlyProxy.

onNPCRegistration fires with the record after its main list/dictionary insertions. Registering the same GameObject again reuses its existing record, still fires this notification, and can reassign an ARENA hostile target; it does not repeat the new-record count increments. The spawner and required NPC references must be valid.

member.param: The spawner whose zone and identity are stored in the NPC record.
The spawned NPC's behavior component.
The profile stored with the record; friendly king status is copied from its king flag.
True adds the NPC as a friendly with behavior team 1; false tracks it as a hostile.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BaseGameController.ResetFriendlyProxyList
member.summary: Replaces the NPC target pool with the cached player proxy and assigns that proxy team number 1.

remarks.para: A proxy identifies an object that NPCs can aim at. If playerProxy is missing or destroyed, this returns without clearing the existing list. With a valid player proxy, it clears friendlyProxyList and adds only that proxy.
It does not reset currFriendlyProxy, change the NPC alive lists, or immediately change existing NPC target assignments.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BaseGameController.SubmitScoreByType
member.summary: Requests leaderboard submission of points or the stored timer, according to the selected leaderboard's score type.

remarks.para: boneLeaderManager.currData.scoreType selects the value: POINT uses score, TIME_IN_SECONDS converts timerValue seconds to a whole number, and TIME multiplies timerValue by 1000 before converting, producing milliseconds. Other score types do not submit through this method.

For a nonnegative timerValue of 12.345 seconds, TIME_IN_SECONDS produces 12 and TIME produces 12345. Fractions are discarded. A zero result is skipped. Because this reads the current timerValue, a transition countdown or REALTIME application clock can change what is submitted; it does not calculate elapsed session duration for you.
Submission is also skipped when the manager is missing or DevToolSpawn has marked developer-tool use. A request to the manager is not proof that the online leaderboard accepted it.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BaseGameController.UpdateNPCDisplay
member.summary: Copies enemy-kill totals and living faction counts into the configured text labels.

remarks.para: killsTexts receives enemiesKilled; totalKillsTexts receives totalEnemiesKilled; aliveTexts receives activeEnemyCount; aliveFriendsTexts receives activeFriendlyCount when that optional list is nonempty.
These are stored counters converted to number strings. This does not count dead bodies or recount the tracking lists. Registration and death handling call it after their count changes.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BaseGameController.UpdateTimeDisplay(System.Boolean)
member.summary: Formats the current timerValue and copies it to active timer text objects.

remarks.para: timerValue is measured in seconds. The meaning comes from the active timer sequence: it can be elapsed game time, remaining countdown time, or seconds since the application started.

When showMilliscond is false, the value is converted to a whole number of seconds before formatting as a TimeSpan, a value representing a duration. When true, it uses hours:minutes:seconds.hundredths. For example, 12.345 seconds displays as 00:00:12.34 in that format; this is two fractional digits, despite the parameter's name.

The method updates tsTimerValue and tsTimerString, then writes tsTimerString to timerTexts entries whose GameObjects are active in the scene. Inactive objects are skipped. It does not advance the timer.

member.param: True keeps fractional time and shows hundredths of a second; false formats whole seconds.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BaseGameController.WAITANDRELOADCURRENTLEVEL(System.Single)
member.summary: Starts a countdown that requests a reload of the current level after the delay.

remarks.para: This starts a coroutine, a routine that continues across frames. It subtracts scaled frame time from a private countdown in seconds, so slow motion lengthens the real wait and time-scale pausing stops it.

The reload is requested on the next continuation after the countdown is no longer positive. A zero or negative delay requests the reload immediately when the sequence starts. This countdown does not overwrite the session's timerValue.

member.param: Game-time seconds to wait before requesting the reload.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BehaviourCrablet.DetachFromFace
member.summary: Releases the face-attachment connection and cleans up its player-facing effects.

remarks.para: The method hides the visor, removes the registered player-death callback, fades down the attachment sound loop, and asks Unity to destroy the face joint if one exists. A physics joint is a connection that constrains how two simulated bodies move; removing this one lets the crablet stop following the attached head.

A callback is a function registered to run when an event occurs. Removing the player-death callback stops this attachment cleanup from remaining subscribed after detachment. This method does not itself change the mental or movement mode, clear every mount flag, or move the crablet to a new position.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BehaviourCrablet.DoCrumbleDeath
member.summary: When crumbleDeath is enabled, loosens selected body joints and pushes the parts outward for the crumble effect.

remarks.para: A muscle is a simulated body part, and its physics joint limits how that part moves relative to neighboring parts. Starting after the root muscle, this routine skips parts labeled Spine. For other parts with the required joint and physics body, it frees all three position axes and all three rotation axes, applies an outward explosion force, then sets their muscle-strength and damping multipliers to zero. These factors scale the part’s controlled movement and its resistance to motion; zero removes those contributions.
The force is centered on this behavior object’s world position and has an 8-meter radius. Damping means resistance to motion. The parts are loosened for simulation rather than deleted immediately.

After processing the muscles, the method starts a coroutine, a routine that pauses and resumes over later frames, with a configured 3-second wait before returning the enemy to its object pool. A pool stores inactive objects for reuse. A frame is one game update. This wait uses scaled game time and resumes on an eligible later frame, so it is not an exact three seconds of wall-clock time. If crumbleDeath is false, the method returns without these changes.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BehaviourCrablet.Jump(Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BehaviourCrablet.JumpType)
member.summary: Launches the crablet by setting its body parts’ velocities for the requested jump mode.
member.param: The launch mode: Dash follows the navigation steering point, Attack aims at the target, FaceMount attempts a head latch, and OffmeshLink uses the saved navigation-link destination.

remarks.para: A muscle is one simulated body part. A Rigidbody is a Unity component that lets a body part move in the physics simulation. This routine calculates a launch velocity and writes it to the available muscle bodies, with stun-related scaling. The velocity uses world directions and meters per second. It clears the navigation path and jump-charge flag, plays jump audio, records jump timing, and switches the movement mode to Jumping.

Dash aims toward the navigation steering point, the next point on the planned movement path. Attack predicts a leap toward the moving target’s head. FaceMount aims near the target head and begins a preliminary face-attachment attempt. OffmeshLink aims at the saved link destination, such as the far side of a navigation gap. The target-following modes account for gravity and limited target motion; a launch does not guarantee a hit or completed face attachment.

This method does not test enableJumpAttack or jumpCooldown before launching. Those settings gate the normal AI’s choice to begin an automatic attack. For example, disabling automatic jump attacks does not make a direct Jump call a no-op. If the root’s physics body cannot be obtained, the routine returns before launching.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BehaviourCrablet.KillEnd
member.summary: Finishes death cleanup by releasing any face attachment and shutting down navigation and target tracking.

remarks.para: The crablet first runs DetachFromFace and changes its emissive color to black, removing its colored glow. The base cleanup then clears its navigation path, disables the navigation agent, clears saved roaming and target data, and finally invokes OnDeath, the death event with no arguments.

A navigation agent is the component that plans movement over the level’s walkable routes. The event marks this cleanup stage; this method does not itself perform the crumble effect or guarantee that the pooled enemy has already disappeared.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BehaviourCrablet.KillStart
member.summary: Begins death cleanup by releasing the face attachment, resetting animation, and disabling perception.

remarks.para: The method detaches from the face, sets the emissive color to black, switches the movement mode to InAir, and resets the animator. An animator is the component that chooses and plays the character’s animation poses. The base death-start step then disables the vision sphere, the sphere-shaped area used to detect visible targets, clears active melee state, and invokes OnDeathStart, the death-start event with no arguments.

The death sound plays after that event only if the scaled game clock has already reached the stored collision-block deadline at this call, the end of a period during which collision processing was temporarily blocked. The scaled clock is affected by slow motion. Otherwise this call skips the sound; it does not wait to play it later. Beginning this cleanup does not itself run DoCrumbleDeath or wait for the final death stage.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BehaviourCrablet.MountAttack(System.Single)
member.summary: Sends a damage attack to the currently tracked target’s head object.
member.param: The damage amount to put in the attack message, in the game’s damage units. It is not a force or a distance; the receiver determines the health effect.

remarks.para: The method builds an Attack message with the supplied damage value and the Slicing attack category, then delivers it to attack receivers on the target head’s object. An attack receiver is code that handles the message and decides the resulting damage; sending it is not proof that a particular amount of health was removed.

A Transform is the reference that stores an object’s position, rotation, and size (scale). The attack uses the tracked target’s reference Transform: its world forward direction becomes the attack normal, the direction reported for the hit’s surface orientation, and the reported origin, the message’s hit-position reference, is 0.1 meter in front of that transform’s world position. The Attack.direction vector is deliberately (0, 0, 0), so the message reports no travel direction. Its collider, the Unity collision shape for a hit, is unset. Its proxy, a reference identifying the target, is also unset. The message has backFacing set to false, so it is not marked as hitting the back of a surface. This method uses the current sensor target rather than checking the stored face joint, and it does not apply its own attack cooldown.

The normal mounted-update code calls this only when its scheduled damage time has passed and its mount calculation produces positive damage. Calling it directly bypasses those timing and mount checks.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BehaviourCrablet.ResetAnimator
member.summary: Restores animation defaults and chooses the crablet’s resting or awake animation setup from its current mental mode.

remarks.para: An animator is the component that chooses and plays animation poses. The animation target root is the root of the animated body. This routine resets it to world identity rotation, meaning it aligns with the world axes. It then rebinds the animator, rebuilding its animation connections to the current object properties and bones, and writes their default values.

Rest mode uses the resting setup and stops animation playback; other mental modes use the awake setup at 0.6 times normal playback speed. Both clear the standing flag. The base reset also restores the eye transform’s local rotation relative to its parent.
This resets animation and target orientation, rather than respawning the enemy, moving it to a checkpoint, or resetting its health.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BehaviourCrablet.RestoreFromCrumbleDeath
member.summary: When crumbleDeath is enabled, relocks linear movement on the first fifteen non-root muscle joints and stops this component’s coroutines.

remarks.para: A muscle is one simulated body part, and its physics joint limits how connected body parts move. This routine visits muscle indexes 1 through 15, after the root at index 0, and locks the joint’s X, Y, and Z position movement when the underlying joint is available. It expects the crablet’s usual layout with at least sixteen muscle entries.

It does not restore every change made by DoCrumbleDeath: this routine does not relock the rotation axes or restore the muscle-strength and damping multipliers. Broader reactivation code must handle the remaining state.

A coroutine is a routine that pauses and resumes over later frames; a frame is one game update. After the joint pass, this method stops all coroutines running on this component, including a pending crumble-despawn wait. It does not itself resurrect or recreate the enemy. If crumbleDeath is false, it does nothing.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BehaviourCrablet.SwitchMentalState(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourBaseNav.MentalState)
member.summary: Applies the requested awareness or combat mode and configures its AI timing, movement, perception, and presentation.
member.param: The awareness or combat mode to apply, such as Rest, Roam, Investigate, Agroed for alert combat, or Engaged for the face-grappling mode.

remarks.para: First, Rest chooses the resting animation; other modes choose the awake animation. Next, if the previous mental mode is Engaged, the routine switches movement to InAir, triggers dismount, and resets the face-hug trigger before setting up the requested mode. If the old movement mode is Grappling, switching to InAir calls DetachFromFace, which requests destruction of the face joint, the connection that keeps simulated bodies attached. This cleanup also runs when Engaged is requested again.

Engaged sets the Grappling movement mode, records the current target, and starts face-hug animation and sound. For a player target it also shows the visor, registers detachment on player death, and updates the equipped position. Registering a callback means saving a function to run when that event occurs. Entering this mode does not itself create the face joint.

Rest uses the configured roaming movement speed with turning speed set to zero. Roam and Investigate use the configured roaming movement and turning speeds; Agroed uses the configured combat speeds. Movement speed is in meters per second, and turning speed is in degrees per second. The resting, active, and investigation vision ranges are configured distances in meters, selected for Rest, Roam, and Investigate respectively. The routine adds 1 meter to the selected range and halves the result to choose the detection sphere’s radius, the distance from its center to its surface. A zero or negative range disables this sphere and resets its radius and center to zero. The actual test uses the computed float radius: at 0.5 meter or less, including a very small positive range rounded to that value, it disables and clears the sphere. Above that threshold, it enables, resizes, and shifts the sphere-shaped vision area. Agroed applies its combat vision area, angry animation, sound, and glow. If Engaged is requested again after detachment, its setup restores Grappling presentation but does not create a replacement face joint; the repeated call is not a harmless assignment.

The nominal AI-check intervals are 2 seconds in Rest, 1 in Roam, 0.2 in Investigate, 0.08 in Agroed, and 0.1 in Engaged. These checks use the clock unaffected by slow motion. The routine stores the new mental state after its setup and marks the next AI check to bypass its normal interval wait; it does not run that entire check immediately.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BehaviourOmniwheel.SwitchMentalState(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourBaseNav.MentalState)
member.summary: Sets this computer-controlled character's mental state and applies that state's navigation, sensing and combat setup.

remarks.para: An AI tick is one decision update for the computer-controlled character. A navigation agent is the component that plans movement over the navigation mesh, the surface map used to plan movement, and follows its path. Rest sets the AI tick interval to 2 seconds. Roam sets it to 1 second. Investigate sets it to 0.2 seconds. All three apply roamSpeed as the navigation travel speed in meters per second, roamAngSpeed as the turning limit in degrees per second, acceleration of 2 meters per second squared, and a stopping distance of 1 meter. These are navigation-agent settings, not a guarantee that the physical character instantly moves at that speed.

These three states also set the vision sphere radius to (R + 1) / 2, where R is the numeric restingRange, activeRange or investigateRange value for the chosen state, used directly as a local-distance value. The added 1 is one local length unit, and dividing by the unitless 2 halves the result. A collider is a shape used to detect contacts; this sphere defines the sensing region. The radius is measured in the sphere collider's local length units, meters at scale 1. For example, R = 9 gives a radius of 5 local units. The sphere center is offset forward by radius minus 1 in the collider's own axes, subtracting that same one local length unit. A resulting radius of 0.5 or less disables the sphere instead.

Agroed sets the tick interval to 0.1 seconds and applies agroedSpeed in meters per second, agroedAngSpeed in degrees per second, acceleration of 3 meters per second squared, and stopping distance of 0.5 meters. Its vision sphere is enabled with radius 2 local units and a forward center offset of 1 local unit. It also asks the sound component to play its configured aggression sound.

When agroState is exactly Charge, entering Agroed resets the charge phase to Windup. The method briefly assigns chargePrepSpeed, the configured preparation travel speed in meters per second, to the navigation agent, but then overwrites that speed with agroedSpeed through the common Agroed setup. When agroState is exactly GunFight, it resets the gun phase to Aim; if hasCombatProjection is true, it also resets the saved unitless aim-animation value and the projection animator's accuracy parameter to zero. An animator is the component that controls animated poses. These resets do not themselves complete an attack.

Engaged sets the tick interval to 0.1 seconds. With engagedMode Follow, it applies followSpeed in meters per second; with Hide, it applies hideSpeed. Both use a turning limit of 180 degrees per second, acceleration of 2 meters per second squared and stopping distance of 1 meter. Stay leaves the existing navigation settings in place. Engaged also asks for the aggression sound, but does not resize the vision sphere through this method.

MindControlled sets the tick interval to 0.1 seconds, clears the navigation path through ClearPath, and clears the sensor's current target. ClearPath can try to place an off-mesh agent back onto the navigation mesh, the surface map used to plan movement, and requests Standing when the character is currently Walking. This does not set a new destination for the controlling player.

After this setup succeeds, the method stores mState and marks the next AI tick to bypass its normal interval wait. The tick intervals use unscaled seconds, which do not slow down with the game's time scale; updates still depend on when the AI tick routine is called. Switching to the already selected state runs its setup again. The navigation agent, sensors and sound or projection components required by the chosen path must be initialized.

member.param: The mental state to enter: Rest, Roam, Investigate, Agroed, Engaged or MindControlled.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Blip.CallDespawnEffect
member.summary: Writes a warning that the old despawn-effect call is deprecated; it does not remove the object.

remarks.para: The message is “Deprecated despawn Call!”. This method does not create the fizzlerSpawnable effect, play a sound, hide a renderer, or return an object to its pool. A pool keeps objects available for later reuse.

A Poolee is the component that manages an object’s return to a reusable pool. If Poolee.Cache exists, ItemDropper’s TryGet lookup checks a table of previously registered Poolee references; it does not search the object for that component. When this lookup fails, ItemDropper searches the object for a Blip. If it finds one, it calls this method and then disables the object itself. A failed lookup does not prove the object lacks a Poolee component. AvatarPedestal calls it before a later step hides its dome. Calling CallDespawnEffect by itself produces the warning, without those separate actions.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Blip.CallSpawnEffect
member.summary: Writes a warning that the old spawn-effect call is deprecated; it does not spawn or reveal an object.

remarks.para: The message is “Deprecated spawn Call!”. The method does not read spawnSpawnable, create a visual effect, play sound, enable renderers, or reset the stored flags. For example, calling it after assigning a different spawnSpawnable still only produces the warning.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BoardGenerator.BoardSpawnerAsync
member.summary: Starts spawning a randomly chosen board between the saved firstPoint and EndPoint, then connects its first physics body at both ends.

remarks.para: A prefab is the object template used to create a board. A MarrowEntity groups an object’s physical pieces; a MarrowBody is one physical piece.

The gap is measured in world-space meters. A gap shorter than 0.1 m, or 10 cm, plays misfireSFX at the generator and produces no board. If isUsingAmmo is true, ammoDistance must be strictly greater than the gap: an exactly equal budget fails too. Insufficient budget stops this operation without the misfire sound.

For an allowed placement, the board is requested at the midpoint, pointing its forward direction from the first point to the end point and using upDir for its up direction. Its requested scale is (min(d, 1), min(d, 1), d), where d is the numeric gap length measured in meters and all three scale factors have no units. For example, a 2 m gap requests scale (1, 1, 2); a 0.5 m gap requests (0.5, 0.5, 0.5). The visible dimensions also depend on how the chosen prefab was authored.

Spawning may wait for the asset/pool operation to complete and then continue in a later frame. The result needs a MarrowEntity with at least one MarrowBody. Two joints, physics connections between objects, are added to its first body using FirstRb and EndRb; a missing connected body anchors that end to the world.

With ammo enabled, the gap is deducted before requesting the spawn. After the joints are created, an available ObjectDestructible is subscribed to OnBoardDestruction and added to destBoardHash. The free-placement branch instead requests the board’s spawn effect and does not add that refund subscription. Both successful branches play endSFX at EndPoint afterward.

The routine rereads firstPoint, EndPoint, FirstRb and EndRb after the spawn wait when creating joints; those values are not saved as a private snapshot. Starting another placement while one is waiting can change its eventual anchors. This routine does not verify Valid or make a fresh endpoint raycast on release.

Here, d is the gap length’s numeric value in world-space meters. In min(d, 1), min means the smaller of d and 1; 1 is a unitless cap used as a scale factor. upDir is a unitless world-space direction pointing straight out from the first hit surface, saved on the first successful shot. FirstRb and EndRb hold the MarrowBody (one physical piece) hit at the first and latest successful endpoints, respectively, when one is present.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BoardGenerator.CeaseFire
member.summary: Clears the held-button flag and hides the placement line.

remarks.para: ButtonDown becomes false first, then line is disabled. A running lineloop stops when it next checks the flag. This does not perform the release action that starts BoardSpawnerAsync.

The saved anchor points and bodies remain stored, and laserPointer is not changed here. A board-spawn operation already waiting for its asset is not canceled by this routine. A configured line renderer is required.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BoardGenerator.OnBoardDestruction(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.ObjectDestructible)
member.summary: Credits a board in back to ammoDistance when its destruction callback runs.
member.param: The destructible object whose membership and current Z scale determine the refund.

remarks.para: A callback is a routine called to report an action; ammo-enabled spawning subscribes this routine to the board’s ObjectDestructible.OnDestruction. The board must be in destBoardHash. If it is absent from that set, the routine returns without a refund.

The amount added is the destructible object’s transform.localScale.z, not a fresh distance measurement. The spawner uses the numeric gap length in meters for the requested Z scale, so an unchanged matching board can refund that amount. Changing the scale or placing the destructible on a differently scaled transform changes the credit.

The board is not removed from destBoardHash and its callback is not unsubscribed here. Calling this repeatedly for the same tracked board credits it repeatedly. Membership, rather than the current isUsingAmmo flag, controls whether this routine refunds it.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BoardGenerator.OnDisable
member.summary: Unsubscribes this generator’s attached-update, hand-attached and hand-detached routines from its configured grip.

remarks.para: A coroutine is a sequence that can pause and resume over several frames.

Unity calls this when the component becomes disabled. Each callback, a routine called to report or handle a grip action, is removed from _grip. The same grip reference used by OnEnable is needed for matching removal.

This routine does not hide line or laserPointer, stop its audio player, clear the button flag, or explicitly cancel its coroutine or pending board spawn. Use CeaseFire when you specifically need to clear the held state and hide the line.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BoardGenerator.OnEnable
member.summary: Subscribes this generator to its grip’s hand attachment, detachment and attached-hand update actions.

remarks.para: Unity calls this when the component becomes enabled. The callbacks are routines the grip calls to report an action: attachment shows laserPointer, detachment hides it, and attached-hand updates handle the hand’s primary-button press and release.

Configure _grip before enabling the component. Enabling itself does not mean a hand is holding it and does not immediately show the pointer. OnDisable removes these three subscriptions; repeatedly calling OnEnable manually can add duplicate listeners.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BoardGenerator.PrimaryButtonDown
member.summary: Marks the primary button held, takes the first anchor raycast, and starts updating the placement line.

remarks.para: A coroutine is a sequence that can pause and resume over several frames. A MarrowBody is one physical piece. RaycastDistance is the ray’s maximum length in meters, and layerMask selects which physics layers, groups used to filter objects, the ray can hit.

ButtonDown becomes true before the first-shot routine runs. That routine enables line and casts from FirePoint’s world position along its forward direction using RaycastDistance and layerMask. A hit saves firstPoint, its surface normal in upDir, and the hit MarrowBody in FirstRb when available, then plays startSFX at that point.

The initial line runs from the saved hit point to FirePoint; lineloop then updates its far end while the flag stays true. Even if the first ray misses, the coroutine is started and the previous firstPoint, FirstRb and upDir are left unchanged. A failed first ray does not itself play misfireSFX.
A surface normal is the direction pointing straight out from the hit surface.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BoardGenerator.PrimaryButtonUp
member.summary: Ends the held-button state, hides the placement line, and starts spawning a board from the saved anchor values.

remarks.para: The order is ButtonDown=false, then line disabled, then BoardSpawnerAsync started. It does not make a final raycast or test Valid. The last successful coroutine hit supplies EndPoint and EndRb; a recent miss can leave older values in place.

The attached-hand input routine performs the same release sequence. Configure the line renderer before calling this. Releasing is different from CeaseFire, which clears the held state and hides the line without starting a spawn.

A coroutine is a sequence that can pause and resume over several frames. The last successful aim hit in that sequence stores EndPoint as a world position in meters and EndRb as the MarrowBody (one physical piece) hit there, when present.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BoardGenerator.lineloop
member.summary: Creates the coroutine that repeatedly raycasts the current aim and redraws the line from the saved first point to the latest successful hit.

remarks.para: A physics update is a step of the physics simulation, separate from the frame that draws the view. A MarrowBody is one physical piece. RaycastDistance is the ray’s maximum length in meters, and layerMask selects which physics layers, groups used to filter objects, the ray can hit.

A coroutine is a sequence that can pause and continue over several frames. This method creates that sequence; the first-shot routine starts it through StartCoroutine. Creating the iterator alone does not update the line.

It first waits for a physics update. Each subsequent cycle checks ButtonDown, then casts from FirePoint’s current world position along its forward direction with RaycastDistance and layerMask. A successful hit stores EndPoint and EndRb and redraws both line positions. A hit without a matching MarrowBody stores a null EndRb for a world anchor.

Both hit and miss branches then pause for two ordinary frame resumptions before testing the flag and casting again. They do not keep waiting for physics updates on every cycle. A miss leaves the previous endpoint, body and line positions unchanged. This routine neither calculates distance nor updates Valid.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BodyVitals.ApplyUILayoutSettings
member.summary: Sizes the player’s UI from the active avatar and reapplies inventory-side settings.

remarks.para: The menu scale is activeArmLength / standardArmLength × uiScale. activeArmLength is the current avatar’s arm length in meters; standardArmLength is the UI rig’s reference arm length in meters; uiScale is the UI rig’s own size multiplier. The result has no units and is assigned equally to X, Y, and Z local scale, relative to each configured UI object’s parent. For example, an arm-length ratio of 1.2 and a UI-rig multiplier of 1 produce a scale of 1.2. BodyVitals.uiScaling is not read by this method.

With an active avatar, UI rig, and tutorial rig, it temporarily returns the slots of an open inventory panel to their body locations, resizes the configured UI objects, updates the popup menu’s starting position, and scales the tutorial rig, the controller-instruction display, uniformly from avatar eye height divided by its reference height and multiplied by its separate size factor. Both heights are in meters; the factor and resulting scale have no units. It then calls rescaleEvent listeners, each with no arguments and no return value, and moves those slots back to the panel targets. A listener is a function called by an event. Inventory flips are applied afterward, using beltFlipped and bodyLogFlipped.

The required player references must already exist. A missing avatar or UI/tutorial rig skips the sizing and notification block; inventory-side application is a separate later step. Changing stored preferences does not automatically call this method.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BodyVitals.CalibratePlayerBodyScale
member.summary: Adjusts tracked-player scale and torso shape using the stored real-world measurements.

remarks.para: The player template is the body description used to relate real tracked movement to the active avatar. This method stores realWorldHeight in that template and adjusts the VR tracking root, the object whose scale controls how tracked headset and controller motion fits the avatar. It applies uniform scale, meaning the same multiplier on all three axes. It compensates the last recorded headset position relative to its parent, saved by the controller rig’s input update, for the scale change. The root’s local scale is activeEyeHeight / estimatedPlayerEyeHeight: activeEyeHeight is the active avatar’s eye height in meters, and estimatedPlayerEyeHeight is realWorldHeight in meters divided by the template’s cached height-to-eye-height ratio. That full-height/eye-height ratio is already stored on the template before this call; calibration reuses it rather than rebuilding it. The ratio and resulting scale have no units. For example, a real height of 1.80 meters and a ratio of 1.125 give estimatedPlayerEyeHeight = 1.80 / 1.125 = 1.60 meters. An active avatar eye height of 1.80 meters then gives a scale of 1.80 / 1.60 = 1.125.

Each stored torso circumference, in meters, is divided by estimatedPlayerEyeHeight in meters before being passed to the template’s torso-shape routine. This turns the measurement into a size relative to eye height. The routine rebuilds torso widths and depths; when a calibration avatar is present, the template copies the relevant torso dimensions to it and refreshes its own derived body measurements.

The method also passes wingspan and realWorldHeight to SetPlayerWingspan, then inseam and realWorldHeight to SetPlayerInseam. Both setters are empty on the built-in RealHeptaAvatar template in this build, so this call does not change its limb proportions through those setters. It does not itself refresh menus or fire rescaleEvent; PROPEGATE calls the separate UI/settings pass afterward. A live player template and valid positive height measurements are needed for the scale ratios. If the active avatar is missing, the method logs and returns.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BodyVitals.PROPEGATE
member.summary: Applies body calibration, then copies the stored layout and controller settings to the live player.

remarks.para: Calls CalibratePlayerBodyScale first and PROPEGATE_SOFT second. The tracking root is the object whose scale adjusts how headset and controller motion fits the avatar. Calibration adjusts that object’s scale and the torso description; the second pass updates menus, inventory slots, the Body Log device, movement controls, handedness, and controller vibration. Required live player systems must already be set up.

For example, after changing realWorldHeight and a torso circumference in meters, call this method to apply both the body changes and the related UI layout. It does not save the values to disk. The “PROPEGATE” spelling is original to the game.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BodyVitals.PROPEGATE_SOFT
member.summary: Applies layout, Body Log, movement-input, handedness, and vibration preferences without recalibrating body measurements. The full calibration pass is .

remarks.para: Applies UI layout first, rebuilds avatar-based body-slot placement, and, when the expected special-slot child has a PullCordDevice, updates its active state, enabled state, side, and orientation. It then applies UI layout a second time before copying the movement curve, movement direction reference, turning settings, quick-menu permission, handedness, and both controller vibration multipliers.

The two layout passes can each call rescaleEvent, so a listener can run twice during one call; each notification supplies no arguments and returns no value. A listener is a function called by the event. Both calls happen before the later controller-setting copies. Movement direction is selected using the controller rig’s existing handedness, before the new isRightHanded value is copied.

For example, after changing beltFlipped or mod_globalHaptic, call this method to apply the preference without changing the tracking-root scale. The tracking root is the object whose scale adjusts how headset and controller motion fits the avatar; this soft pass leaves that scale alone. BodyVitals.uiScaling, turnEnabled, and slowTimeEnabled are not read by this method. Required live player references, UI, tutorial, inventory, and controllers must already exist; missing controller vibration components can end the pass before the multiplier is copied.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BodyVitals.add_rescaleEvent(Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BodyVitals.RescaleUI)
member.summary: Adds a function to the UI-layout notification list.
member.param: The no-argument function to add to the notification list.

remarks.para: The function takes no arguments and returns no value. It is called by ApplyUILayoutSettings after popup-position and tutorial-scale updates, before inventory flips. Subscribing does not recalibrate or resize anything immediately. PROPEGATE_SOFT can call the notification twice because it applies the layout twice.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BodyVitals.remove_rescaleEvent(Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BodyVitals.RescaleUI)
member.summary: Removes a function from the UI-layout notification list.
member.param: The previously added function to remove from the notification list.

remarks.para: Removes the matching function from rescaleEvent using delegate removal. A delegate is a reference to a function or a list of functions. Removing the function does not undo a previous UI resize or body calibration.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BonelabGameControl.Awake
member.summary: Reads saved checkpoint progress and sets up resuming, or clears this level’s saved object state for a fresh visit.

remarks.para: Awake is Unity’s initialization call, which runs before Start. A null, empty, or whitespace-only LevelKey stops initialization with an ArgumentNullException, an error reporting that a required identifier is missing.

With PartialProgress enabled in SaveFeatures, this reads the active save’s checkpoint index into Progress. A missing or unusable saved number becomes 0. Resuming is selected only when that number is nonzero and TemporaryLoadData.ResumeFromSave is true. IsResuming becomes true, TeleportToProgress is registered for persistent-scene loading, and ResumeProgress is registered for level loading.

A callback is a function saved to run at another operation’s stage. If the loader has already reached the requested stage, registration can run the function immediately. Otherwise, the teleport and checkpoint changes happen later; calling Awake alone does not mean they are finished.

When resuming is not selected, this deletes the level’s saved object-specific values while preserving the save system’s reserved values. For example, a saved checkpoint index of 2 resumes only when the temporary resume request is also true; an ordinary fresh visit takes the cleanup path.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BonelabGameControl.FinalizeInventory
member.summary: Prepares the current ammunition and carried-item data for leaving this level.

remarks.para: This does work only when SaveFeatures includes Inventory, which covers both items and ammunition. For each ammunition type, it calculates a new change as the current number of rounds minus the starting number calculated from earlier levels’ saved ammunition changes in PriorLevels. Positive means more rounds than that starting amount; negative means fewer. If a usable older final-change record exists, it keeps the larger of the older and new changes for each type, treating a missing older type as 0. With no usable older record, it stores the new changes directly. It then deletes this level’s temporary in-progress ammunition record. Ammunition values count rounds, separately for each ammunition type. For example, 50 current rounds minus 60 starting rounds gives -10 rounds; if that type already has -5 saved, the merged record keeps -5.

When NextLevel is nonblank, it gathers the player’s carried-item identifiers and stores them as starting inventory for both that next level key and the BONELAB Hub key, "Hub". A level key is the text identifier in saved progression data; it is not a level asset reference. With no next key, that transfer is skipped.

It then records the carried inventory under the older final-inventory format for this level and removes the temporary in-progress inventory record. The gathered item data associates inventory slots with item asset identifiers, rather than copying entire scene objects. An unavailable player inventory can prevent item gathering from succeeding.

This prepares the active save data in memory and does not request a file write or load another level. For example, finish the level’s objective, call FinalizeInventory to prepare carryover, then JustSave to request saving. PriorLevels must be supplied as a list, even when empty.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BonelabGameControl.JustSave
member.summary: Asks the data manager to save the active save with progression data included.

remarks.para: This calls the data manager’s save attempt using the Progression save flag. It does not first mark completion, advance a checkpoint, or gather inventory. Prepare those changes before calling it if they should be included.

The method returns no success result, so returning from this call does not confirm that a save was successfully written. For example, call SetCompleted followed by JustSave to request saving an objective’s completion.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BonelabGameControl.ResumeProgress
member.summary: Applies the current checkpoint’s death checkpoint and switches its scene objects off and on.

remarks.para: Progress chooses an entry in ProgressionPoint by list index: 0 is the first entry, 1 the second, and so on. This first looks up that entry and, when its checkpoint is assigned, calls SetCheckpoint so the player can use that death checkpoint.

Next, it disables every object in disableObjects, then enables every object in enableObjects, in each array’s order. An object in both arrays ends enabled. Disabled objects stop being active in the scene; enabled objects become active, subject to their parent objects also being active.

Provide a valid nonnegative index and a nonnull ProgressionPoint list. The first lookup happens before the later bounds checks, so those checks do not make an invalid index safe. Use empty object arrays when no objects need switching, and avoid null entries.

The resume setup calls this at the loader’s level-load stage. This method does not teleport the player or invoke OnReachedResumePoint; advancing progress through SetProgress handles that event separately. For example, a resumed checkpoint can disable earlier enemy spawners and enable the next door.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BonelabGameControl.SetCompleted
member.summary: Records level completion and resets the saved checkpoint number according to the enabled save features.

remarks.para: With Completion enabled in SaveFeatures, this sets the active save’s completed value for LevelKey to true. With PartialProgress enabled, it then writes 0 as that level’s saved checkpoint index. The two feature checks are independent: either change can happen without the other.

These changes affect save data in memory. The controller’s live Progress property is not reset, no inventory is finalized, and no file write is requested here. For example, call SetCompleted when a level objective is finished, then JustSave when that completion should be written by the data manager.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BonelabGameControl.Start
member.summary: Sets up the level-load work that restores inventory and ammunition and optionally records completion.

remarks.para: Start is Unity’s startup call after the component’s initialization. It captures the active save’s progression data, clears TemporaryLoadData.ResumeFromSave, and registers a callback with the current scene-loading session. A callback is a function saved to run when loading reaches a stage; it can run immediately if the level-load stage has already finished.

When that callback runs with the Inventory save feature enabled, it chooses the current checkpoint’s left- and right-hand item locations when the checkpoint index is valid, passes InventorySaveFilter’s replacement rules when a filter is assigned, and asks the progression helper to restore inventory and ammunition. PriorLevels provides earlier levels to consult when selecting starting items and ammunition.

The callback then clears IsResuming. If CompleteOnLoad is true, it records this level as completed even when the Completion save feature is off. It does not reset the saved checkpoint number as SetCompleted does.

Item restoration can continue asynchronously, meaning its spawning work finishes later while the game keeps running. Neither this method returning nor IsResuming becoming false proves every item has appeared. For example, use CompleteOnLoad for a level that should count as complete upon loading, and keep the checkpoint list and inventory setup valid so the callback can reach that step.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BonelabGameControl.TeleportToProgress
member.summary: Queues the player’s feet and facing direction to move to the current saved checkpoint.

remarks.para: This requires the PartialProgress save feature and a player found through the runtime player tag, the identifier used to locate the player’s rig. A rig is the collection of objects that controls the player’s body. It selects ProgressionPoint[Progress], so Progress is a whole-number list index, with 0 meaning the first point.

The destination is the selected spawnLocation’s world position, in Unity world units, measured from the scene’s origin. This native path does not convert the position or establish how many Unity world units equal a metre. Facing comes from that location’s forward direction, its blue Z axis expressed in world coordinates; this direction has no distance unit. The player’s feet use the destination, rather than the head.

This stores a teleport request in the player’s rig manager, which applies it during EarlyUpdate, its early per-frame update stage. It also requests that the body’s movement velocity be cleared. It does not move the player immediately inside this call, and another teleport queued before that update can replace the destination.

An unusable player-tag value, no entity found with that tag, an unusable rig manager after a Rig has been found, or an index at or beyond the end of the list makes this return without queueing a teleport. Missing runtime settings, the tag reference, the entity manager that finds tagged scene objects, a null returned entity, or the found entity’s Rig component can instead cause an error. A negative index, a missing list, or a missing spawnLocation can cause an error instead. For example, Progress = 2 selects the third point; place that point’s spawnLocation at floor level and turn its forward axis toward the desired facing.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ButtonHoverClick.CLICK
member.summary: Requests click vibration and a click sound, or a confirmation sound when is true.

remarks.para: It first requests the active controller's configured press-click vibration. It then selects the sound category: false confirmer uses clips_Click and clip_override_click; true confirmer uses clips_Confirm and clip_override_confirmer. The confirmation flag changes the audio category, not the vibration pattern.

Vibration is sent to the controller currently recorded as active by the in-game UI, rather than to a controller argument from the pointer event. If that controller or its vibration driver is missing, the request has no controller to reach.

The matching default clip list on feedback_audio must contain at least one entry. The sound-selection mode first chooses and checks a list index, then substitutes the override if one is assigned. An override does not bypass an empty list or an invalid index. In single mode, clipToPlay must be a valid zero-based index: 0 is the first entry, 1 the second, and so on.

Sound is requested at this button object's world position when the method runs. That position is captured for playback; the sound does not follow the button afterward. The audio provider's settings control loudness and whether the listener's position affects the sound.

These direct feedback methods use the references already stored on the component. They do not look up missing providers themselves. A missing tactile reference skips vibration, and a missing audio reference skips sound. Assign the references before a manual call, or let the component's level-load or pointer-enter setup fill them from the main UI rig.

This method supplies feedback. Calling it does not invoke a button's gameplay action or check whether that action succeeded. For example, a confirm button can set confirmer to true and call CLICK to use the confirmation sound category.

These direct feedback methods use the references already stored on the component. They do not look up missing providers themselves. A missing tactile reference skips vibration, and a missing audio reference skips sound. Assign the references before a manual call, or let the component's level-load or pointer-enter setup fill them from the main UI rig.

The pointer-enter handler normally calls this after checking its entered target. You can also call it manually. HIGHLIGHT supplies feedback; it does not change button color, select a button, or create a hover animation.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ChallengeSelectMenu.CancelCurrentChallenge
member.summary: Invokes the menu's cancellation event if one is assigned.

remarks.para: A UnityEvent is a list of actions that a scene author can connect in Unity's Inspector. These events take no arguments, so listeners receive no challenge number or enemy-count value directly.

The method calls OnChallengeCanceled and returns. It does not itself clear challengeID, choose another challenge, or stop the arena controller. Connected actions must provide any gameplay cancellation or menu changes. If no event is assigned, the method does nothing.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ChallengeSelectMenu.ChallengeStarted
member.summary: Invokes the start event at the menu's current challenge index.

remarks.para: A UnityEvent is a list of actions that a scene author can connect in Unity's Inspector. These events take no arguments, so listeners receive no challenge number or enemy-count value directly.

The method looks up OnChallengeStarted[challengeID] and calls that one event. An index is a numbered position starting at zero: challengeID = 2 selects the third event. The array and that event must exist, and the index must be within the array.
This method does not directly start the arena controller or select a new challenge. It provides the event call; connected actions decide what starting that challenge actually does.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ChallengeSelectMenu.OnChallengeSelect
member.summary: Refreshes the active title, calls the selection event, then optionally applies the menu's enemy-count goal.

remarks.para: If activeChallengeText is assigned, the method copies the controller's assigned challenge profile title into it. A profile is stored challenge settings. With this label present, both the controller and its assigned profile must be valid; a missing required reference fails before listeners run. It then invokes OnChallengeSelected if that event is assigned. A UnityEvent is a list of actions connected in the scene; this event passes no arguments.

After listeners return, an available controller and updateEnemyCount = true make the method pass enemyCountValue to UpdateProfileEnemyCount with immediateIncrease = false and increaseRate = 3. The count is the goal for enemies present at the same time, measured in whole enemies; it is not a count of currently spawned enemies. The controller stores a custom progression setting rather than immediately changing the current wave's limit. A wave is a planned batch of enemies. For later custom extra-wave generation, the new wave's concurrent-enemy limit is min(oldLimit + 3, goal), meaning the smaller of those two numbers. oldLimit is the preceding wave's configured maximum number of enemies present at the same time, and goal is the menu count copied when this confirmation runs; both are measured in whole enemies. The same rate also adds six planned enemy entries to the new wave, rather than guaranteeing six successful spawns or six enemies alive at once. For example, oldLimit = 4 and goal = 10 give a new limit of 7. If the goal is below the old limit, this formula can lower the new limit.

Listeners run before that enemy-count setting is applied. The method reads the controller reference, flag, and count after the event, so changes made by a listener can affect that following step. This method does not call SelectChallenge; choose the controller's profile separately before confirming it here.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ChallengeSelectMenu.SelectChallenge(System.Int32)
member.summary: Stores a challenge index, asks the arena controller to select that profile, and refreshes the menu's description labels.

remarks.para: idx is a zero-based position in the controller's roundProfileGroupList: 0 means the first profile and 2 means the third. With a controller assigned, the method saves idx in challengeID and calls ARENA_ChallengeSelect(idx). A text component is a piece attached to a scene object that draws a label. For a valid nonnegative challenge index, the controller's difficulty-label list must be assigned and every listed entry must be valid for this selection path to complete. The controller enables those text components before assigning the profile; enabling one lets Unity display its label. It then puts that profile's descriptionText into every element of chalDescriptionTexts. All those labels receive the same selected description.

A profile holds stored challenge settings, including rounds, which group waves; a wave is a planned batch of enemies. A successful controller selection also resets its stored score to zero points and updates the score label if that label exists. When the controller's cached player targeting proxy (the object enemies can target) is valid, it clears the friendly targeting pool, the list of possible targets for enemies, and puts only that saved player proxy back in the list. The controller saved that reference during level-load setup, so the reset reuses it instead of searching for the player again. With an invalid cached proxy, the reset leaves the existing list alone. It stores arenaState = ACTIVE, the controller's status value for an active arena. This state write alone does not begin a session, start its timer, or spawn waves.

This method does not invoke OnChallengeSelected or update activeChallengeText; OnChallengeSelect handles those separate confirmation actions. If no controller is available, it returns without changing challengeID.

Use an index within the profile list. The menu does not clamp it, and it stores the value before the controller and description lookups finish. An invalid index can leave challengeID changed and cause a later list or event-array lookup to fail. chalDescriptionTexts must be assigned; an empty array skips description updates, while entries in a nonempty array must be valid text objects.

member.param: Zero-based index of the desired profile in the arena controller's roundProfileGroupList.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ChallengeSelectMenu.SelectLoadout(System.Int32)
member.summary: Stores the menu's selected loadout index for a later notification.

remarks.para: An index is a numbered position starting at zero; idx = 2 records the third loadout choice. This method only writes loadID. It does not equip items, check whether that loadout exists, or call OnLoadoutSelected.

OnLoadoutSelect is the separate method that sends the saved loadID to the static OnLoadoutSelected callback. A callback is a method called to react to a notification. For example, SelectLoadout(2) followed by OnLoadoutSelect sends 2 to subscribed listeners.

member.param: Loadout choice number to save; this method does not validate it.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ChallengeSelectMenu.Start
member.summary: Selects the first controller challenge and, when the count label exists, initializes the menu count from its first wave.

remarks.para: Start is a callback: a routine Unity calls when an enabled component begins running. With an arena controller assigned, this method chooses challenge index 0 and fills every challenge-description label with that profile's description. A text component is a piece attached to a scene object that draws a label. When the assigned controller selects profile 0, its difficulty-label list must be assigned and each listed entry valid for the selection to complete. The controller enables those text components before assigning the profile, letting Unity display their labels. A successful controller selection also resets its stored score to zero points and sets the score label to zero if that label exists. When the controller's cached player targeting proxy (the object enemies can target) is valid, it clears the friendly targeting pool, the list of possible targets for enemies, and puts only that saved player proxy back in the list. The controller saved that reference during level-load setup, so the reset reuses it instead of searching for the player again. With an invalid cached proxy, the reset leaves the existing list alone. It stores arenaState = ACTIVE, the controller's status value for an active arena. This state write alone does not begin a session, start its timer, or spawn waves. It does not call the menu's OnChallengeSelect confirmation method.

A profile holds stored challenge settings; a round groups waves, and a wave is a planned batch of enemies. If enemyCountText is assigned, Start requires an assigned controller and profile with an existing first round and first wave for its initial count read. It reads maxConcurrent from that first wave, saves it in enemyCountValue, and displays the number. maxConcurrent means the configured maximum number of enemies present at the same time, not the total enemies across the challenge. Those first round and wave entries must exist.

The constructor is setup code that runs when this component is created. It initializes the minimum and maximum adjuster values to 3 and 30 enemies and supplies the difficulty-description array. Start does not set those bounds or refresh the difficulty label. Without enemyCountText, it skips the initial count read and keeps the previously stored count.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ChallengeSelectMenu.ToggleEnemyCount(System.Boolean)

remarks.para: With up = true, the method adds one only if enemyCountValue is below maxEnemyCount. With up = false, it subtracts one only if the value is above minEnemyCount. These are counts of whole enemies. For example, with bounds 3 and 30 and a value of 4, an increase displays 5; decreasing at 3 leaves 3.
It rewrites enemyCountText even when the number does not change, so that label must be assigned. It does not check updateEnemyCount and does not immediately send the value to the arena controller.
The checks limit each requested step; they do not clamp an arbitrary existing value into the whole allowed range. For example, a stored value of 40 with maximum 30 stays 40 when asked to increase.

member.param: True to request one more concurrent enemy; false to request one fewer.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ChallengeSelectMenu.UpdateDiffText

remarks.para: The method reads the controller's difficulty number and uses it to choose diffDescriptions[number]. The normal order is EASY = 0, MEDIUM = 1, HARD = 2, HARDER = 3, and HARDEST = 4. This is the controller's difficulty, not challengeID.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Control_UI_BodyMeasurements.BUTTON_CONFIRM
member.summary: Attempts to save the current measurements, applies them to the player and signals completion.

remarks.para: It first resolves the player reference, then attempts to save settings and the active save. It applies the active settings through controlPlayer.SEND_VITALS, hides the change reminder, and finally invokes completionEvent with no arguments, calling its registered actions without passing a value. The save methods’ success results are not checked here; the event means this call reached its completion step, not that disk saving was verified.
This confirms the values already in the active PlayerSettings object. For example, after changing a dimension, confirmation clears the reminder and lets completion listeners move to the next screen.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Control_UI_BodyMeasurements.BUTTON_GUESS
member.summary: Estimates height from the controller rig, replaces the body dimensions, then saves, applies and signals completion.

remarks.para: The controller rig is the group of scene objects representing the tracked player. It first calls CheckApprovals, then calls CalculateMeasurements with guessHeight = true. That computes a new height from the rig’s current head, chest and tracking-root positions, then derives wingspan (fingertip-to-fingertip reach with arms spread), inseam (inside-leg length), and the chest, underbust, waist and hip circumferences (distances all the way around those body parts; underbust is just below the chest).

After CalculateMeasurements returns, it calls CheckApprovals a second time, then attempts to save settings and the active save. It applies the active settings through controlPlayer.SEND_VITALS, hides the change reminder, and finally invokes completionEvent with no arguments, calling its registered actions without passing a value. The save methods’ success results are not checked here; the event means this call reached its completion step, not that disk saving was verified.

Guess therefore also invokes completionEvent with no arguments; its effect includes the same completion sequence as Confirm. The guessed height is limited to 90–228 centimetres and rounded to a whole centimetre.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Control_UI_BodyMeasurements.BUTTON_HEIGHT(System.Boolean)

remarks.para: With up = true, it adds 1 cm only when the current height is below 244 cm. With up = false, it subtracts 1 cm only when the current height is above 90 cm. These are tests before the step, not a clamp of the result: for example, 243.5 cm can become 244.5 cm.

The six estimates are stored in metres: wingspan (fingertip-to-fingertip reach with arms spread), inseam (inside-leg length), and chest, underbust, waist and hip circumferences (distances all the way around those body parts; underbust is just below the chest). Height is used for wingspan and inseam; the four circumferences use the selected shirt-size factor and are not multiplied by height.

After the change, it recalculates all six estimated dimensions, attempts to save settings and the active save, applies the settings through controlPlayer.SEND_VITALS, shows the change reminder, and refreshes the measurement labels.
The recalculation and later save/application/display steps still run if the height test prevents a step. Recalculation also replaces earlier manual dimension edits with the calculated estimates.

member.param: True adds 1 cm when below the upper test boundary; false subtracts 1 cm when above the lower test boundary.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Control_UI_BodyMeasurements.BUTTON_MEASUREMENTS(System.Int32)
member.summary: Selects Custom and changes one saved body dimension by one centimetre.

remarks.para: The button numbers select a dimension and direction: 1/2 increase/decrease wingspan; 3/4 chest circumference; 5/6 underbust circumference; 7/8 waist circumference; 9/10 hip circumference; 11/12 inseam length. Circumference means the distance all the way around that part of the body; wingspan is fingertip-to-fingertip reach with arms out, and inseam is inside-leg length.

Each step is 0.01 metres, which is 1 cm. An increase requires the current dimension to be below 2.8 m. A decrease requires it to be above 0.9 m, except inseam uses 0.5 m. These strict tests happen before the step and do not clamp the result. For example, a wingspan of 2.795 m can increase to 2.805 m.

It sets the preset to Custom before checking the number. It then attempts both saves, copies the active body measurements into the current player body data through the player controller, shows the change reminder and refreshes labels. member.param: A number from 1 to 12 selecting one of the six increase/decrease pairs described above.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Control_UI_BodyMeasurements.BUTTON_SHIRT(System.Boolean)
