remarks.para: Normal shirt presets run from 1 through 7: XSmall, Small, Medium, Large, XLarge, XXLarge and XXXLarge. With left = true, it subtracts one and wraps 1 to 7. With left = false, it adds one and wraps 7 to 1. Preset 0 is Custom.

The six estimates are stored in metres: wingspan (fingertip-to-fingertip reach with arms spread), inseam (inside-leg length), and chest, underbust, waist and hip circumferences (distances all the way around those body parts; underbust is just below the chest). The selected shirt-size factor scales only the four circumference estimates; wingspan and inseam use saved height and their own unitless proportions.

After the change, it recalculates all six estimated dimensions, attempts to save settings and the active save, applies the settings through controlPlayer.SEND_VITALS, shows the change reminder, and refreshes the measurement labels.

From Custom, a right step selects XSmall. A left step from Custom produces -1 instead of wrapping to the largest preset; the subsequent preset-array lookup is invalid. Use a normal shirt preset before stepping left. Arrays for shirt labels and size multipliers must have entries for the enum values they use.

member.param: True steps toward smaller preset numbers; false steps toward larger ones.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Control_UI_BodyMeasurements.CalculateMeasurements(System.Boolean)
member.summary: Replaces the active settings’ six body dimensions with estimates, optionally replacing height first.

remarks.para: Wingspan is fingertip-to-fingertip reach with the arms spread. Inseam is inside-leg length. A torso circumference is the distance all the way around a body part: chest, underbust just below the chest, waist or hips.

Without guessing height, it uses PlayerHeight already in the active settings, measured in centimetres. Wingspan in metres = height × 0.01 × wingspanModifier. Inseam in metres = height × 0.01 × inseamModifier. The factor 0.01 metres per centimetre converts height to metres. Both modifiers are unitless proportions of total height; wingspanModifier sets the arm-reach proportion and inseamModifier sets the inside-leg proportion.

For each torso circumference, the estimate in metres = its medium base circumference in metres × the selected shirt-size multiplier. The four base values are mediumChest, mediumUnderbust, mediumWaist and mediumHips; the unitless multiplier comes from shirtSizeModifier at the saved MeasurementState preset number: Custom 0, XSmall 1, Small 2, Medium 3, Large 4, XLarge 5, XXLarge 6 or XXXLarge 7. That number selects the multiplier-array entry for the chosen body-size preset. These circumferences are not scaled by height in this calculation. For example, a 1.054 m chest base with multiplier 1.1 gives a 1.1594 m circumference.

When guessHeight is true, it reads the current OpenControllerRig through PlayerRefs. A rig is the group of objects representing the tracked player. World Y is the scene’s up/down coordinate. Let h be the head’s world Y position, r the tracking root’s world Y position, k the root’s local Y scale (its scale in that direction relative to its parent object), u the unitless world direction of length one pointing up from the rig, d the world vector from chest to head, and H the old saved height in centimetres. The estimated height in metres is (h − r) / k + (0.27 m − dot(u, d)) × H / 176 cm. The dot product measures chest-to-head separation along the rig’s up direction. Positions and d use metres; k and H / 176 cm are unitless.

It limits that estimate to 0.9–2.28 m, converts it to centimetres, and rounds to the nearest whole centimetre; exact halfway values choose the even integer. The rounded height then supplies the wingspan and inseam estimates. The first part of the height formula uses world Y, while the chest-to-head correction uses the rig’s own up direction.

This overwrites all six dimensions even when the selected preset is Custom. It changes the active settings object in memory; callers perform saving, player application and label refresh as separate steps.

member.param: True first estimates height from the current tracked rig; false keeps the saved height while recalculating the six dimensions.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Control_UI_BodyMeasurements.CheckApprovals

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Control_UI_BodyMeasurements.DISPLAY_MEASUREMENTS

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Control_UI_BodyMeasurements.SendVitals

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.DrawBezierCurve.UpdateLines
member.summary: Rebuilds the line vertices from the four point objects’ current positions and the current sampling settings.

remarks.para: A LineRenderer is Unity’s component for drawing connected line segments through supplied positions. It sets the LineRenderer vertex count to lineSteps, then reads the point objects again while computing every sample. Assign the renderer and all four points before calling; this method has no missing-reference fallback.

The component reads the four point objects’ Transform.position values, which are world coordinates in Unity length units, normally meters. It writes those coordinates directly to the LineRenderer. Use a renderer configured for world-space positions; this method does not change useWorldSpace or convert them to the renderer’s local coordinates.

Let N be lineSteps, the requested vertex count; i be a vertex’s zero-based index, from 0 through N - 1; and F be linePercentageFill, a unitless curve-parameter multiplier. Each vertex samples t = (i / N) * F. Here t = 0 is Point1 and t = 1 is Point4. Mathematically the last sample is F * (N - 1) / N. For ordinary vertex counts, F = 1 therefore stops short of Point4; native floating-point rounding can affect the result with very large counts.

For example, N = 6 and F = 1 sample t values 0, 1/6, 2/6, 3/6, 4/6 and 5/6, making six vertices joined by five segments. The curve parameter is not a distance percentage: evenly spaced t values can produce uneven distances along a bent curve.

OnWillRenderObject calls this method before each camera renders a visible, enabled component. That is a Unity callback, a method Unity calls when that rendering event occurs, so updates can happen more than once in a frame. A direct call can redraw after setup even when the component was disabled by OnlySetOnStart.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Feedback_Tactile.CLICK(System.Boolean,Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.BaseController)
member.summary: Requests the controller vibration configured for pressing or releasing a UI button.
member.param: True selects press feedback; false selects release feedback. The default is true.
Controller whose Haptor supplies the vibration settings. Pass null to use the active UI controller.

remarks.para: A Haptor is the controller's vibration helper. If the supplied controller is missing or has been destroyed, this method tries the active controller stored by Control_UI_InGameData. It returns without sending feedback if that controller is also missing, or if the selected controller has no Haptor.

For a press, the Haptor reads hap_click_down_t, hap_click_down_frequency and hap_click_down_amplitude. For a release, it reads the corresponding hap_click_up values. These are the requested duration in seconds, vibration frequency in hertz (cycles per second), and strength with no physical unit. Strength is clamped to 0 through 1, then multiplied by the Haptor's mod_globalPer strength scale. The values are read when called, and the requested delay is zero. The duration describes the request; the controller and its hardware determine the feedback actually felt.

For example, call feedback.CLICK(true, leftController) when a button is pressed, then feedback.CLICK(false, leftController) when it is released. The false call sends the release settings; it does not cancel the press request. The caller decides when a press or release happened.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Feedback_Tactile.HOVER(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.BaseController)
member.summary: Requests the controller's subtle vibration to give feedback when a pointer reaches a UI item.
member.param: Controller whose Haptor supplies the vibration settings. Pass null to use the active UI controller.

remarks.para: A Haptor is the controller's vibration helper. If the supplied controller is missing or has been destroyed, this method tries the active controller stored by Control_UI_InGameData. It sends nothing if that controller is also missing or if the selected controller has no Haptor.

The Haptor reads its stored subtle settings at the time of the call: hap_subtle_t is the requested duration in seconds, hap_subtle_frequency is vibration frequency in hertz (cycles per second), and hap_subtle_amplitude is strength with no physical unit. Strength is clamped to 0 through 1, then multiplied by mod_globalPer, the Haptor's overall strength scale. The requested delay is zero. These settings describe a request; the controller and its hardware determine the feedback actually felt.

For example, call feedback.HOVER(rightController) when the right-hand pointer first enters a button. Each call requests feedback again, so the caller should choose when to call it. Passing null uses the active UI controller instead of choosing a hand explicitly.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GachaPlacer.OnPersistentLoad
member.summary: Requests a capsule spawn if its represented crate passes the active save’s unlock and optional campaign-completion checks.

remarks.para: This callback, a routine called to perform a loading action, is registered during Awake, Unity’s initialization callback. The streaming session calls it during persistent-scene loading, or immediately when registered if that loading action has already happened.

It first resolves unlockCrate to a crate definition. If resolution fails, it returns. A resolved crate must have an unlock count below one in the active save and have Redacted false, the crate flag used to hide it from menus. If onlyPlaceIfBeatGame is true, the save’s BeatGame flag must also be true. It does not additionally test the crate’s Unlockable flag.

When all checks pass, it calls the configured CrateSpawner’s SpawnSpawnable. This begins a spawn request without waiting for the spawned object to be ready; it does not itself award an unlock. Configure the spawner in Manual Mode, since its own automatic loading path otherwise requests a spawn independently of these checks. This routine expects assigned crate/spawner references and loaded active-save records.

Changing completion or unlock data later does not continuously rerun this callback. Each call checks the current data and can request another spawn when eligible; this routine does not record a once-only placement flag.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GachaPlacer.ShouldSpawn
member.summary: Reports whether the represented crate passes the current save’s capsule-placement checks.

remarks.para: The represented crate is the stored item definition selected for the capsule’s contents. It returns false if unlockCrate cannot resolve, if the save records at least one unlock for its barcode, or if the resolved crate is Redacted, the flag used to hide it from menus. Otherwise it returns true when onlyPlaceIfBeatGame is false; when that option is true, it returns the active progression record’s BeatGame flag. A barcode identifies the particular crate in the unlock records.

For example, a resolved, non-redacted crate with zero recorded unlocks can pass before campaign completion when onlyPlaceIfBeatGame is false. Turning that option on makes the same check fail until BeatGame is true. A permission callback is a routine the CrateSpawner calls for a yes/no answer before spawning. The spawner calls its optional shouldSpawn field when that field is assigned; this type does not assign ShouldSpawn to it. This query only reports eligibility; it does not spawn or award an unlock. An assigned unlockCrate reference that does not resolve returns false. A null reference or absent active-save record follows the native failure path; when completion checking is enabled, an absent progression record does too.

member.returns: True when the crate resolves, its saved unlock count is below one, it is not redacted, and the optional BeatGame requirement passes.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Descent.CONFIRMFORCEGRAB
member.summary: Cancels the delayed force-grab hint and hides its tutorial object.

remarks.para: First it stops forceGrabRoutine, the saved sequence that waits before showing the hint. It then deactivates module_ForceGrab and clears canForceGrab. It does not set gate_d6 or another sequence gate. DescentIntroSequenceCtrl calls this when the avatar die breaks free of its physics connection.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Descent.CoroutineSequence
member.summary: Creates the sequence that reveals the height and mirror areas, waits for player milestones, and runs the gallows and lightning effects.

remarks.para: A coroutine is a sequence that pauses and continues over several frames. Pass the returned sequence to Unity StartCoroutine to run it; calling CoroutineSequence alone only creates it. Normal level startup starts it after loading when the player is not resuming a save. Its scene references and the cached mirror Renderer must already be prepared. A Renderer is the component that draws an object; its material holds appearance settings.

It waits for gate_mirror, gate_d6, gate_noose, gate_drop and gate_cut in that order, plus dynamicGallows' world Y rotation becoming at most 232 degrees. World rotation means orientation relative to the level, not relative to the object's parent. Setting a later flag early lets that later wait pass when reached; it does not jump over earlier animation or waits. gate_height is not read by this sequence.

After gate_noose, it requests music cue 1 and field ambience/reverb, copies the avatar's barcode (its saved asset identifier) into CurrentAvatar and FallbackAvatar, requests saving, and releases the player through RigManager.UnleashPlayer. These happen before it hides the opening void and enables the gallows pin and drop gate. Finishing the final gate_cut wait ends this coroutine; it does not itself call DoLevelComplete.

Animation uses deltaTime, the game-time seconds since the previous frame. The height effect grows in local X, then Y, then Z, each using a 0.5-second timer. Local axes turn with the object and its parent; scale is a size multiplier, not a distance in meters. Each opening curve blends from scale 0.001 to the corresponding local scale of module_HeightInTarget. Closing changes Z first for 0.1 seconds, then X and Y together for 0.1 seconds, blending module_HeightInTarget to module_HeightOutTarget. Each timer resets between those stages. The effect's direct children receive world scale (0.03, 0.03, 0.03) through SetGlobalScale.SetScale so their size does not simply follow the changing parent scale.

Mirror spawn particles grow in local X, then Z, then Y, each using a 1-second timer and curve_Mirror to blend scale 0.001 to 2. MirrorInProgress begins when Y growth begins. Curve input is elapsed seconds divided by that stage's configured seconds, and curve output is a dimensionless blend limited to 0 through 1. The loops sample while elapsed time is below the duration; they do not guarantee a final sample at input 1. Frame timing and changes to game speed affect elapsed real time.

Lightning uses two separate material values. Each progress value is dimensionless, meaning it has no physical units: each frame adds deltaTime divided by its configured duration to progress. deltaTime is the game-time seconds since the previous frame, and duration is the configured game-time seconds for that value: 0.2 seconds for the first and 1 second for the second. Each value is set to exactly 1 after its loop. The material decides how those values change the bolt's appearance. Gate checks and animations yield null, meaning continue next frame; timed pauses use WaitForSeconds, which waits in game-time seconds.

For patches, GameControl_Descent._CoroutineSequence_d__69.MoveNext resumes the saved sequence. Its __1__state identifies the next resume point, not the SEQUENCE gate index. The table retains those resume points; a frame-loop state can be entered many times before its timer finishes. _lerpInSpeed_5__3 and _lerpOutSpeed_5__5 hold durations in seconds despite their names.

item.description: Running or done. Unhandled states return false.
First entry. It waits 1 s.

Resumes after the initial 1-second wait. Enables module_MirrorPedestalParticles, module_DaggerParticles and module_HeightSpawnEffect. Sets the opening duration to 0.5 seconds, prepares child world scale (0.03, 0.03, 0.03), plays clip_HeightParticleWoop, and begins X growth.
Resumes the X growth loop using curve_HeightOpenX. Once its 0.5-second timer finishes, resets elapsed time, plays clip_HeightParticleWoop again and begins Y growth.
Resumes the Y growth loop using curve_HeightOpenY. Once its timer finishes, resets elapsed time, enables module_Height and begins Z growth.
Resumes the Z growth loop using curve_HeightOpenZ. Once its timer finishes, waits 0.5 seconds.
Continues after 0.5 s. It deactivates module_HeightSpawnEffect and waits for gate_mirror.
Repeats the gate_mirror check. When true, enables module_HeightSpawnEffect, sets the closing duration to 0.1 seconds, resets elapsed time and begins Z closing.
Resumes Z closing with curve_HeightCloseZ. Once its timer finishes, hides module_Height, resets elapsed time and begins simultaneous X/Y closing.
Resumes simultaneous X/Y closing with curve_HeightCloseX and curve_HeightCloseY. Once its timer finishes, waits 0.1 seconds.
Continues after 0.1 s. It deactivates module_HeightSpawnEffect and waits 1 s.
Resumes after a 1-second wait. Enables module_Mirror and module_MirrorSpawnParticles, plays sfx_MirrorVoidParticles if present, sets each mirror axis duration to 1 second and begins X growth.
Resumes mirror-particle X growth using curve_Mirror. Once its timer finishes, resets elapsed time and begins Z growth.
Resumes mirror-particle Z growth using curve_Mirror. Once its timer finishes, starts MirrorInProgress, resets elapsed time and begins Y growth.
Resumes mirror-particle Y growth using curve_Mirror. Once its timer finishes, enables module_MirrorReflectVol and module_MirrorVoidParticles, stops the spawn particle system, and waits 3 seconds.

Resumes after 3 seconds. Enables module_MirrorPedestal and requests showing module_AvatarDie. If canForceGrab is true, saves and starts ForceGrabCoroutine, which clears canForceGrab when it begins. Then sets gate_forceGrab true and waits for gate_d6.

Repeats the gate_d6 check. When true, first clears gate_forceGrab, disables module_MirrorPedestal, requests hiding module_MirrorButton, requests hiding module_AvatarDie, disables module_MirrorSpawnParticles, stops the void particle system, starts MirrorOutProgress and waits 2.5 game-time seconds.

Resumes after 2.5 seconds. Disables module_Mirror and module_GallowPin, requests the noose reveal sound, disables module_DropGate, selects music cue 0 and waits for dynamicGallows world Y rotation to become at most 232 degrees.
Repeats the gallows rotation check. When Y is at most 232 degrees, enables module_GallowLockPin and waits for gate_noose.

Continues after 5 s. It deactivates module_MirrorVoidParticles and waits for gate_drop.
Continues after the gate_drop wait. When set, it waits 1.5 s.
Continues after 1.5 s. It plays sfx_radioIntro and waits 0.5 s.
Continues after 0.5 s. It plays module_LightningAudioClip at module_LightningAudioTransform and waits 1.4 s.
Resumes after 1.4 seconds. Gets the lightning bolt material, enables the bolt, resets progress and configures the first material-progress duration as 0.2 seconds.

Resumes the first lightning material-progress loop. After it finishes, sets that value to 1, requests showing daggerEntity, enables hit/path particles and plays the dagger hit sound at module_DaggerHitPoint. Resets progress and sets the second material-progress duration to 1 second.
Resumes the second lightning material-progress loop. After it finishes, sets its value to 1 and waits 4 seconds.
Continues after 4 s. It deactivates module_LightingBolt and module_LightingHitParticles, then waits 2 s.
Continues after 2 s. It completes if gate_cut is set, otherwise it yields null.
Continues after the gate_cut wait. It repeats state 27's check.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Descent.MirrorInProgress
member.summary: Creates the mirror-frame reveal animation.

remarks.para: A coroutine is a sequence that pauses and continues over several frames. Run the returned sequence with StartCoroutine. It starts its dimensionless material progress at -0.2 and adds 0.5 times deltaTime each frame, where deltaTime is the game-time seconds since the previous frame. It writes the new progress to the cached mirror renderer's material, then waits until the next frame. A Renderer is Unity's drawing component, and its material holds the appearance settings.

The sequence stops once its saved progress reaches 1. A change of 1.2 at 0.5 per second takes about 2.4 game-time seconds; frame timing can carry the final value past the boundary because there is no final clamp. For example, a 0.02-second frame changes progress by 0.01. This method does not itself activate or deactivate the mirror object.

The renderer was cached from module_MirrorVoidFrame during level startup. Assigning a different frame afterward does not replace that cached renderer. For patches, GameControl_Descent._MirrorInProgress_d__72.MoveNext runs the loop; __1__state 0 starts it and 1 resumes after the frame wait.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Descent.PlayIntroMusic(System.Int32)

If the intro or main clip is already selected, the manager can adjust its volume instead of starting a new intro; when the volume also matches, that branch leaves playback alone. Audio override is a mode that temporarily gives other music priority and holds ordinary cue requests. An active override can defer this request. Fade times use real-time seconds, unaffected by game slow motion. Volume is a dimensionless source-level setting: 0 is silent and 1 is the ordinary full source level.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Descent.SEQUENCE(System.Int32)

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Descent.SetupFieldReverbAndAmbience
member.summary: Requests the field's echo preset and background ambience through the global audio manager.

remarks.para: First it requests a transition to fieldReverbObj, then it cues fieldAmbClipMain at amb_volume with amb_fadeInTime and amb_fadeOutTime. amb_volume is a dimensionless source-volume target: 0 is silent and 1 is the ordinary full source level. amb_fadeInTime controls the incoming clip, or the volume adjustment if that clip is already selected; amb_fadeOutTime controls the old clip when switching. Both volume fades use real-time seconds, unaffected by game slow motion. Reverb means the room-like echo added to sound; its transition timing is separate from the ambience fade settings.

These values are read when the request is made. Editing the fields afterward does not automatically update a playing sound; call this method again to request the new settings. The main intro sequence makes the same requests after gate_noose. Audio continues changing over later frames.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Holodeck.CYCLEMATERIAL
member.summary: Selects the next wall material and starts the fast panel-update routine.

remarks.para: It increments materialIndex and wraps to 0 after the final wallMaterials entry. Index 0 is the first entry. It stops the previously saved routine, replaces matCycle with a new CycleMatOverTimeEditor iterator, and starts it. An iterator is the object holding a paused routine's progress.

The editor routine first waits until its next coroutine step, then changes all panels in that step and applies the selected reflection and ambient-light data. It also changes the door-cover object and room-light objects. It does not use the timed routine's ambience and reverb changes.

A coroutine is a routine that can pause and resume on later frames. A frame is one game-update step. The index changes before the panels and lighting, so the saved selection can briefly differ from what is visible. For a three-entry material list, cycling from index 2 selects index 0.

Use a valid index in both wallMaterials and cubemaps, and provide valid panel references and at least two reflection-probe references. The selection methods do not clamp an invalid index into range. Missing required references or out-of-range indices can fail partway through a change.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Holodeck.CycleMatOverTime
member.summary: Creates the routine that changes panel materials one at a time and applies lighting after the final panel.

remarks.para: A coroutine is a routine Unity runs in steps that can pause and resume on later frames. A frame is one game-update step. An iterator is the object holding a paused routine's progress. Calling this iterator method only creates the routine; its scene changes happen when the routine is started or advanced.

When it first runs, it requests an achievement unlock, adjusts light objects, and prepares the preset's audio settings. Index 0 enables the room lights; other indices disable them and set the door-cover renderer's material. For index 0, hiding the door-cover object and disabling the check image happen inside the light loop, so an empty light list skips those two updates.

Ambience is background sound. Reverb is sound's lingering reflections. For indices 0 through 7, it copies the chosen ambience clip and reverb settings into both zoneAmbience objects, requests the global reverb change, and cues ambience at a volume factor of 0.1 with configured 1-second fade-in and fade-out times. These are requests; they do not mean the fades have already finished.

The fixed audio routing is 0: ship, 1: space, 2: desert, 3: beach, 4: city, 5: stadium, 6: meadow, and 7: void. The visual materials can be replaced, but these audio meanings remain tied to the numbers. Valid visual indices above 7 still update panels and lighting but do not select new ambience or reverb in this routine.

It shuffles the wallPanels array itself, so its stored order changes. Before each panel it waits for a random duration from 0 to maxPanelTicTime seconds of scaled game time, then updates that panel. Scaled game time follows the game clock: slowing that clock makes the same requested wait take longer in real time. Coroutine frame scheduling can also make the elapsed wait longer. A material controls a surface's appearance. A renderer is the component that draws it, and a material slot is one surface-material entry on that renderer. Panels with two or four slots receive the selected material in every slot. Other slot counts use the single-material setter, which changes the first slot.

At initial setup, the two- and four-slot replacement arrays capture the selected wallMaterials entry before the first wait. Other slot counts read the current wallMaterials array and materialIndex after that panel's wait, then set the first slot. For example, replacing the selected array entry between waits can change a later first-slot update while a later two- or four-slot update still uses its earlier captured material.

After all panels, it applies the selected cubemap pair and ambient-light data with SetSky, clears matCycle, and finishes. An empty panel array goes straight to that final lighting step. Stopping it early leaves any material, light, door-cover, and audio changes already made in place.

member.returns: An iterator for the paused routine. Creating it does not start the transition; Unity must run it as a coroutine or the caller must advance it.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Holodeck.CycleMatOverTimeEditor
member.summary: Creates the fast routine that updates every panel in one step after its initial paused step.

remarks.para: A coroutine is a routine Unity runs in steps that can pause and resume on later frames. An iterator is the object holding a paused routine's progress. Calling this iterator method only creates the routine; its scene changes happen when the routine is started or advanced.

Its first step yields without changing the scene. When Unity runs it as a coroutine, execution resumes on a later frame, meaning a later game-update step. Manually advancing the iterator only moves to its next step and does not itself wait for another frame. On the next step, index 0 hides doorHide, disables doorCheckImage, and enables the room-light objects. A nonzero index sets the door-cover renderer's material, activates doorHide, and disables the lights. The nonzero branch leaves the check image's enabled state as it was.

It shuffles the wallPanels array itself, then updates every panel without per-panel waits. A material controls a surface's appearance. A renderer is the component that draws it, and a material slot is one surface-material entry on that renderer. Panels with two or four slots receive the selected material in every slot. Other slot counts use the single-material setter, which changes the first slot. It finishes by applying the selected reflection textures and ambient-light data.
Unlike the timed routine, it does not select the eight ambience/reverb presets or clear the saved matCycle field on completion. Its name does not prevent CYCLEMATERIAL from using it at runtime.

member.returns: An iterator for the fast routine. Its scene changes begin after its first paused step when the iterator is run.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Holodeck.GenerateSHs
member.summary: Rebuilds the saved directional ambient-light numbers from the first cubemap of every preset pair.

remarks.para: The lighting data is a pair of cubemaps plus saved spherical-harmonic numbers. A cubemap is a six-sided image of the surroundings, used here for reflections. Spherical harmonics are a small set of numbers describing the color and brightness of light arriving from different directions.

For each cubemaps entry, it reads cubemap0's six image faces and samples 4096 random directions across the whole cubemap. It converts their colors into SphericalHarmonicsL2: 27 numbers, consisting of 9 directional coefficients for each of red, green, and blue. The sample count is a number of directions, not a duration or 4096 samples per face.

It replaces that pair's saved harmonics. It does not render new cubemap images, bake reflection probes, change wall materials, or immediately apply the new numbers to the live ambient-light setting. SetSky copies those saved numbers into the live setting when that preset is applied.

Provide a nonnull pair and readable cubemap0 pixel data for each entry. Changing a source cubemap afterward does not automatically regenerate the saved harmonics. For example, after replacing a beach cubemap, run this calculation again and then apply that preset's lighting. Random sampling can produce small differences between runs.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Holodeck.OnLevelLoad
member.summary: Applies reflection and ambient-light data from preset 0 when the level-load callback runs.

remarks.para: This calls SetSky with index 0. A reflection probe is a Unity component supplying an environment image for reflective surfaces. Here, the controller assigns already stored images. It assigns the first preset pair's cubemaps to the first two reflection probes, copies its saved directional-light numbers into the global ambient-light setting, and requests an environment-lighting refresh.

It does not select or change wall materials, reset the saved materialIndex, or choose new ambience audio. Start hides the UI and registers this callback. A callback is a method saved for another system to run when an event occurs; if the load session is already done, registration invokes it immediately.

The lighting data is a pair of cubemaps plus saved spherical-harmonic numbers. A cubemap is a six-sided image of the surroundings, used here for reflections. Spherical harmonics are a small set of numbers describing the color and brightness of light arriving from different directions.

member.summary: Selects a wall-material index and starts the timed panel transition to that selection.

remarks.para: A coroutine is a routine Unity can pause and resume on later frames. A frame is one game-update step. An iterator is the object holding a paused routine's progress. The method saves i as materialIndex immediately, stops the previous saved transition if present, creates a new CycleMatOverTime iterator, and starts it. It does not wait for all panels to finish before returning.

The timed routine prepares lights, the door-cover material, and the fixed ambience/reverb routing, then changes wall panels in shuffled order. It requests a random wait before each panel. The reflection and ambient-light settings change only after the final panel.

A renderer draws a surface, and a material slot is one entry in its surface-appearance settings. At initial setup, the two- and four-slot replacement arrays capture the selected wallMaterials entry before the first wait. Other slot counts read the current wallMaterials array and materialIndex after that panel's wait, then set the first slot. For example, replacing the selected array entry between waits can change a later first-slot update while a later two- or four-slot update still uses its earlier captured material.

Selecting another index during a transition stops that routine and starts a new one. Already changed panels are not rolled back; they can show a mixture until the new routine reaches them. The new routine reads current controller fields as it progresses.

The fixed audio routing is 0: ship, 1: space, 2: desert, 3: beach, 4: city, 5: stadium, 6: meadow, and 7: void. The visual materials can be replaced, but these audio meanings remain tied to the numbers. Valid visual indices above 7 still update panels and lighting but do not select new ambience or reverb in this routine.

Use a valid index in both wallMaterials and cubemaps, and provide valid panel references and at least two reflection-probe references. The selection methods do not clamp an invalid index into range. Missing required references or out-of-range indices can fail partway through a change.

member.param: Zero-based selection index: 0 is the first entry. It must exist in wallMaterials and cubemaps. Indices 0 through 7 also select the fixed audio categories described above.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Holodeck.SetSky(System.Int32)
member.summary: Applies one preset pair's reflection textures and saved ambient-light data, then requests an environment refresh.

remarks.para: The lighting data is a pair of cubemaps plus saved spherical-harmonic numbers. A cubemap is a six-sided image of the surroundings, used here for reflections. Spherical harmonics are a small set of numbers describing the color and brightness of light arriving from different directions.

A reflection probe is a Unity component supplying an environment image for reflective surfaces. Here, the controller assigns already stored images. probes[0] receives that pair's cubemap0 as its custom baked texture, and probes[1] receives cubemap1. Additional probes in the array are untouched. The pair's harmonics are copied into RenderSettings.ambientProbe, the global ambient-light data, and the ambient mode is set to Custom.

It also assigns cubemap0 as the global custom reflection texture, updates the sky manager, and asks Unity to refresh environment lighting. The method does not render new probe images or set the probes' modes. The sky manager's choice of texture still depends on the already configured default reflection mode; assigning a custom texture does not itself switch that mode.

This method does not change wall materials, audio, or the controller's saved materialIndex. For example, applying lighting for index 0 while materialIndex remains 3 can temporarily combine index-0 lighting with index-3 walls.

The cubemaps index must be valid, its pair must exist, and probes must contain at least two valid probe references. The saved harmonics are copied now; editing them later requires another application to replace the live ambient-light data.

member.param: Zero-based index into this controller's cubemaps preset-pair array. This parameter selects lighting without changing the saved selection field.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Holodeck.TOGGLEDOOR
member.summary: Switches the door-cover object and its check image on or off for a nonzero material selection.

remarks.para: With materialIndex equal to 0, the method does nothing. Otherwise it reads doorHide's own active flag, flips it, and sets doorCheckImage.enabled to the same on/off state.

The object's own active flag is its local choice, independent of whether a disabled parent keeps it invisible. The check image's flag enables or disables drawing that UI image; it does not change its sprite or color.
This toggles the configured cover object. It does not send a physical door-opening command or run an opening/closing animation. Assign doorHide and doorCheckImage before using it.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.AIRLOCKCYCLE

The inspected AirlockEnter routine waits on doorCycle and a stop request tied to this component’s destruction; replacing airlockCoroutine alone does not cancel that door-opening wait. member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.AIRLOCKOCCUPIED(System.Boolean)

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.AirlockEnter(System.Int32)
member.summary: Loads the required airlock area and attempts to open the entry-side door over later frames.

remarks.para: Scene chunks are separately loaded parts of the level. Side 0 attempts to open the large south doors, which requires recorded lab power and at least three inserted module keys in either Hub mode; side 1 starts opening the small north door. Other values run the loading and cancellation-source setup but do not select a door. It loads airlockChunk together with the currently loaded labFloorChunk or funicularChunk when needed, then replaces the doorCycle stop-request source and waits for the chosen opening task.

The entry wrappers create airlockCoroutine before calling this routine. That reference is cleared after normal completion, allowing another entry request. Door-opening tasks can finish because of cancellation as well as because their position threshold was reached.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.AirlockExitCycle
member.summary: Switches the airlock between the lab floor and funicular areas, waiting for one side’s closing attempt before loading and requesting opening on the other.

remarks.para: The routine starts a fresh middle-lamp blink loop and marks airLockExitCycle true. With labFloorChunk loaded and funicularChunk unloaded, it closes the large doors, loads airlockChunk and funicularChunk, then opens the small door. With the opposite chunks loaded, it closes the small door, loads airlockChunk and labFloorChunk, then attempts to open the large doors.

Scene chunks are separately loaded parts of the level. It waits for the closing task before loading the other area. That task can end when cancellation is observed during its position checks, so continuing the cycle does not prove the physical door reached its closed position. This work continues over later frames. After normal completion it stops blinking, restores mat_Lamp[3] on the two middle lamps, clears airLockExitCycle, and clears airlockCoroutine. Large-door opening still checks lab power and at least three inserted module keys.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.BWBoxSequence
member.summary: Creates the timed steam, warning-sound and lock-bar sequence that releases the Big Walk door.

remarks.para: Start is Unity’s setup routine called before this component’s first frame update. The generated state machine stores which numbered step resumes next; MoveNext runs that step until the next pause. In the table, _barInterval_5__2 is the requested game-time wait between bars, in seconds, and _i_5__3 is the zero-based bar index, a count with no distance units.

A coroutine is a sequence that pauses and continues across later frames. This method returns that sequence; run it with StartCoroutine to produce the effects. OPENBWDOOR normally starts it after checking the keys.

The requested waits are 2, 2, 14 and 2.5 seconds before retracting the bars, 1 second after each bar, then 0.25 and 0.6 seconds before disabling doorStopper. These are waits in game time, not a promise of exact wall-clock timestamps; continuation occurs on a later frame.

A physics joint connects objects and limits their motion. Making each bar joint’s X motion Limited allows the bar to move within its configured travel. A Rigidbody is the object’s physics body; WakeUp lets the simulation move it again. The joint and body arrays are cached from lockBar during Start, so replacing a lockBar object later does not rebuild those cached references.

Audio plays at bwDoorPismatic, except barRetraction at each lockBar. Each bar's lockBarJoints.xMotion becomes Limited, and lockBarRB wakes. It waits _barInterval_5__2 between bars until _i_5__3 reaches lockBarJoints.Length. Other states end iteration.
To change its behavior, patch its state machine's MoveNext method, GameControl_Hub._BWBoxSequence_d__161.MoveNext. The values of __1__state are:

item.description: Running or done.
First entry. It disables backUpBWBoxCollider, starts the first two steamParticles, and plays bwClunk. It waits 2 s.
Continues after the 2 s wait. It stops those particles, plays bwWarning, and waits 2 s.
Continues after the 2 s wait. It plays radiation and waits 14 s.
Continues after the 14 s wait. It starts KlaxonLight, plays klaxon, and waits 2.5 s.
Continues after the 2.5 s wait. It sets _barInterval_5__2 to 1 s and _i_5__3 to 0, then starts retracting bars.
Continues after the bar-interval wait. It increments _i_5__3 and repeats. It waits 0.25 s after the last bar.
Continues after the 0.25 s wait. It plays doorSeal and waits 0.6 s.
Continues after the 0.6 s wait. It disables doorStopper and completes.

member.returns: The sequence to run as a coroutine.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.BackUpYoinkLoad
member.summary: Creates a fallback sequence that waits 10 seconds of game time, then requests the Ascent transition through GOTOSCENE(2).

remarks.para: A coroutine is a sequence that continues across frames. Calling this method only returns the sequence; the box-volume and destruction handlers start it with StartCoroutine. After the wait, it calls GOTOSCENE(2) without rechecking whether the player remains in the box. The wait resumes on a later frame, so it is not an exact 10-second wall-clock deadline.

member.returns: The fallback sequence to run as a coroutine.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.BlinkAirLockCycleLight
member.summary: Creates a repeating blink sequence for the first two middle airlock cycle lamps.

remarks.para: A coroutine is a sequence that pauses and continues across frames. When run, this sequence applies mat_Lamp[4], waits 0.75 seconds of game time, applies mat_Lamp[3], waits another 0.75 seconds, and repeats. It changes materials in steps rather than smoothly fading them.
The sequence does not check occupancy itself. AirlockExitCycle stores and starts it; the exit-cycle cleanup or AIRLOCKOCCUPIED(false) stops it and restores mat_Lamp[3].

member.returns: The repeating sequence to run as a coroutine.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.CANCELCYCLE
member.summary: Requests cancellation of the airlock and door waits, clears the entry reference, and resets all door-motion and exit-cycle flags.

remarks.para: A coroutine is a sequence that pauses and continues on later frames. The middle-lamp blink coroutine can therefore continue after this method’s stop requests unless another routine stops it.

It cancels airlockCoroutine if present, then clears that reference. It also cancels doorCycle if present, but leaves that reference stored. It clears airLockExitCycle, bigDoorsOpening, bigDoorsClosing, smallDoorsOpening and smallDoorsClosing.

Cancellation is a stop request for routines waiting across frames. This method does not restore door power, move a door back, or directly stop the middle-lamp blink coroutine. Reset flags alone do not prove that the physical doors have stopped.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.CheckAirLockOpenAnimStatus
member.summary: Updates the lab strip lights and airlock lock lamp when the player is in the proxy volume and lab power permits access.

remarks.para: Requires inAirLockProxy, isLabPowered and hasPlayedAirlockProxy false. Old Hub mode additionally requires the cached keyCount to be at least 3. It applies mat_StripLight[1] to the strips and mat_Lamp[3] to the lock lamp.

If the save has no readable LongRun completion record, it first sets hasPlayedAirlockProxy true, then invokes quarantineDoorUnlocked with no arguments, then requests south entry. An event invokes its registered listener routines; those listeners see the flag already true. This test checks whether the completion record can be read, not whether its stored value is true. A readable false record also skips that event branch.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.CheckGeneratorStatus(System.Boolean)
member.summary: Starts or cancels the staged generator startup when both battery insertion flags are true and the lab is not yet powered.

remarks.para: Passing true starts GeneratorStartSequence only if no sequence is stored. Passing false stops the stored coroutine, clears its reference and restores mat_Lamp[4] on the three generator lamps only while blockGeneratorDisable is false.

A coroutine is a sequence that continues over several frames. Its third startup event occurs before blockGeneratorDisable becomes true; after that change, a false request cannot cancel through this method. Once isLabPowered is true, this method does nothing, so false is not a general power-off command.

member.param: True to request startup; false to cancel startup before its cancellation lock is set.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.CheckTotal
member.summary: Recomputes whether every module insertion flag is true and checks the Hub achievement condition.

remarks.para: For the normal six-key array, isAllInserted becomes false at the first missing key and true when all six are inserted. An empty array leaves its previous value unchanged. Jimmy’s key and the batteries are checked separately by other routines.

The achievement check only requires isLabPowered in normal mode, or cached keyCount at least 3 in old Hub mode; it does not require isAllInserted. This method does not refresh keyCount. CountKeys or DisplayKeys can refresh that count before an old-mode check.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.CloseBigDoors(Il2CppSystem.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Commands the large airlock doors closed and waits until the first door reaches its closing threshold or cancellation is requested.

remarks.para: A physics joint connects objects and controls their movement. Each door’s Powerable_Joint control translates the opening, neutral or closing command into its configured joint targets and drive forces when its relevant controls are enabled. Sending a command does not prove the door reached its destination.

If they are already closing, it returns without starting another close. If they are opening, it clears the opening flag, sends the neutral power command, waits 2 seconds of game time, then sends the closing command. Otherwise it sends the closing command immediately.

It watches the first door’s local Z position, measured along its parent’s blue axis, until that coordinate is at most 4.05. These are the built-in Hub coordinates, approximately meters when parent scale is 1, rather than a general closed-position setting. It also starts a 13-second doorway-clearing timer; during position polling, reaching the threshold or observing cancellation cancels that timer, sets the two south lamps to mat_Lamp[4], and clears bigDoorsClosing.

A cancellation token is a stop request shared with the waiting routine. Cancellation observed during position polling ends that wait and runs the timer, lamp and closing-flag cleanup described above. The earlier 2-second reversal delay also uses the caller’s token; cancellation or failure during that delay is not covered by those polling-exit cleanup branches. A stop request does not reverse the door command or guarantee that the physical door has stopped.

member.param: Stop request for the asynchronous closing wait.
member.returns: A task representing this closing attempt; completion may also result from cancellation or an already-closing guard.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.CloseSmallDoor(Il2CppSystem.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Applies the small door’s closing joint settings and waits for its local Y coordinate to reach the closing threshold or for cancellation.

remarks.para: The X drive is a motor-like force control along the physics joint’s own X axis, as chosen by its axis setting; this is separate from the parent-coordinate Y threshold below. smallDoorOffSettings.x sets spring strength, .y sets damping that resists the difference between wanted and actual speed, and .z caps the force. These three values are copied when this call starts. Under ordinary meter, second and kilogram conventions, spring strength is in newtons per meter of position error (N/m), damping is in newtons per meter-per-second of speed error (N·s/m), and the force cap is in newtons (N), a unit of push or pull. These settings affect the simulated force rather than specifying an exact travel time.

A physics joint connects objects and controls their movement. This call first marks smallDoorsClosing true, then copies smallDoorOffSettings into the joint’s X drive and wakes the door’s Rigidbody, its simulated physics body. It then starts a 1-second doorway-clearing timer.

The wait watches the door’s local Y coordinate, along its parent’s green axis, until it is at most 5.15. These are built-in Hub coordinates, approximately meters when parent scale is 1. It then cancels the clearing timer, applies mat_Lamp[4] to the two north lamps and clears smallDoorsClosing. The timer clears overlapping objects; it does not initiate door motion.
A cancellation token is a stop request shared with the waiting routine. Canceling ends its wait; it does not reverse the door command or guarantee that the physical door has stopped.

member.param: Stop request for the asynchronous closing wait.
member.returns: A task for this closing wait; cancellation can end it before the physical door is closed.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.CountKeys

member.returns: The number of true entries in isKeyInserted.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.DataRead

remarks.para: Reads the integer HubSpawnLocation, the six module unlock and placed flags, Jimmy’s unlock and placed flags, both battery placed flags, and LabPoweredOn from the shared Hub save section. The module order is Tactical Trial, Arena, Sandbox, Parkour, Experimental, then Mods.

A missing respawn value starts at index 0, but a missing or false ElevatorBroken flag overrides the loaded index with 9. Lab power also becomes true in normal Hub mode when a readable LongRun completion record exists, even if that record contains false. The routine does not show keys or teleport the player itself; those actions occur during later Hub setup.
Awake, a setup routine Unity calls when this component initializes, normally calls this routine before the level-load setup. Calling DataRead again replaces these runtime values with saved ones.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.DataWrite

remarks.para: Writes the cached respawn index, six module unlock flags, six module placed flags, Jimmy’s placed flag, both battery placed flags and lab-powered flag into the shared Hub section. It does not write JimmyKeyUnlocked or ElevatorBroken here; Jimmy’s unlock is read during restore, and the elevator breakout handler writes its own flag.

Writing flags does not insert physical keys or batteries, teleport the player, or apply electrical power. For immediate game changes, the corresponding Hub action methods also refresh displays and the progress board.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.DisplayKeys

Insertion lamps use mat_Lamp[0] when absent, mat_Lamp[1] for inserted even-numbered indices and mat_Lamp[2] for inserted odd-numbered indices.

Lock-lamp materials are based on the player’s unlock count for each corresponding avatar crate, a separate check from the module key’s unlock flag. The routine also recounts inserted modules into keyCount and fills the big-door progress lamps in count order.

With useOldHubMode true and at least three inserted modules, it sets isLabPowered true and updates the airlock lamp. It sets generator lamp materials and module-menu activity from the lab-powered flag, then calls CheckAirLockOpenAnimStatus. These are display and progression changes; it does not directly apply generator electrical output.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.DoorCloseTimer(Il2CppSystem.Threading.CancellationToken,System.Single,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Waits for the requested game-time delay, then removes objects overlapping the selected doorway.

remarks.para: After a successful delay it calls DoorEmancipator(bigDoor). It does not close a door. The closing routines use it to clear obstructions: 13 seconds for large doors and 1 second for the small door, canceling the timer if the door reaches its threshold first.

The delay continues over later frames, so timerLength is a requested game-time duration rather than an exact elapsed frame timestamp. Canceling its token during the delay prevents the doorway-clearing call.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.DoorEmancipator(System.Boolean)
member.summary: Plays despawn effects and removes distinct Marrow entities overlapping the chosen doorway’s clearing box.

remarks.para: A collider is an object’s shape used for collision checks. A Rigidbody is its simulated physics body. The MarrowBody cache is a stored lookup connecting a physics body’s scene object to the Marrow entity that owns it, so the scan can remove a complete game object rather than treating every collision shape as a separate item.

The box is centered at emancipatorPointBig or emancipatorPointSmall in world space and rotated with that transform. emancipatorBoundsBig/Small supplies its full width, height and depth in meters; the overlap query halves each dimension to obtain center-to-side distances. For example, bounds (2, 1, 1) gives a box extending 1 meter sideways and 0.5 meter along its other two axes.

layerMask selects which colliders are considered. The routine finds each collider’s attached Rigidbody, the object’s physics body, and uses the MarrowBody cache to identify its owning entity. It collects distinct entities so several colliders on one object do not cause repeated despawns. bigDoorEntity and smallDoorEntity are both excluded. This performs a scan immediately; it is not a trigger callback for objects merely crossing a boundary.

member.param: True to scan the large doorway box; false to scan the small doorway box.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.ELEVATORBREAKOUT

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.ENTERBWBOXVOL
member.summary: Records that the player entered the Big Walk box volume and requests the seat’s pull-in sequence when the broken-box and key requirements are met.

A repeat request can be ignored while that sequence reference is already stored. Returning from this method does not mean the player has finished moving into the seat.

It first sets isInBWBoxVolume true. If isAllInserted, isJimmyKeyInserted and isBWBoxBroken are all true, it starts BackUpYoinkLoad, disables flooring and calls seatTrigger.Yoink. The backup sequence requests GOTOSCENE(2) after a 10-second game-time wait.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.EXITBWBOXVOL

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.GOTOSCENE(System.Int32)
member.summary: Captures the player’s current inventory and requests the stage-1 Long Run or stage-2 Ascent level transition.

remarks.para: The final ammo delta is the change in round count for each ammo type: the current ammo count minus the computed starting count for that type. The starting count comes from earlier progression entries. If a readable saved delta already exists, a larger saved change for a type is retained. For example, 120 current rounds minus 100 starting rounds gives a new change of 20 rounds; an existing change of 30 remains 30. MenuResume is the saved menu resume-progress marker, not a count of inventory items.
Stage 1 uses the configured longRun reference and raises saved MenuResume to at least 2. Stage 2 uses ascent and raises MenuResume to at least 6. Stage 0, the default, and other values do nothing.

For the selected Hub stage, it updates the final ammo delta, removes obsolete inventory entries, captures the player’s current inventory from their body and hand slots for the destination and shared Hub save sections, updates CurrentCampaignLevel from the selected crate, and requests LoadFXAndLevel. The transition waits for the spawned fade effect’s completion callback, a routine called when the fade finishes; this method returning does not mean the next level has loaded. It requests a save after updating the resume stage.

member.param: 1 selects longRun; 2 selects ascent; 0 and other values do nothing.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.GeneratorStartSequence
member.summary: Creates the timed generator lamp-and-event sequence that records lab power after the third startup event.

remarks.para: A coroutine is a sequence that pauses and continues across frames. This method returns that sequence; CheckGeneratorStatus normally starts it. It waits 0.2 seconds of game time, sets generator_Lamp[0] to mat_Lamp[3] and invokes generatorStart1 without arguments. One second later it does the same for lamp 1 and generatorStart2; after another second, for lamp 2 and generatorStart3.

The third event fires before blockGeneratorDisable becomes true. After that event returns, the flag becomes true; after a further 0.3-second wait, isLabPowered becomes true. An event calls its registered listener routines without arguments. blockGeneratorDisable prevents CheckGeneratorStatus(false) from stopping startup through its cancellation branch. With isLabPowered and blockGeneratorDisable initially false and listeners leaving those values unchanged, all three events run before this sequence sets lab power, and the third runs before this sequence sets the cancellation-block flag. Listeners can change these writable flags themselves or call Hub methods again, so the proven order is this routine’s own writes rather than an unconditional promise about every listener’s observations.

The sequence refreshes the progress board and saves lab power. Old Hub mode requests the battery achievement and finishes there. Normal mode also updates the airlock lamp and access sequence, waits another 0.3 seconds, then sets slzSign output to 1. The event listeners can have their own effects; this routine does not directly set generatorPower output. Requested waits can resume on a later frame rather than at exact elapsed timestamps.

member.returns: The startup sequence to run as a coroutine.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.InAirLockProxyVolume(System.Boolean)

member.param: True on entry to the proxy volume; false on exit.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.KEYINSERTED(System.Int32)
member.summary: Marks a module key inserted, saves Hub progress, checks the combined key requirement and refreshes the displays and progress board.

This reports insertion by setting isKeyInserted[keyInt] true; it does not validate a key code or physically move a key into a socket. DisplayKeys then hides the loose module object and shows the seated object.

member.param: Module index from 0 through 5 in the matching key arrays.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.KlaxonLight
member.summary: Creates the warning-light sequence that spins its physics mount, fades in its brightness and later fades it out.

remarks.para: _velRef_5__4 stores the current rate of brightness change between smoothing updates, in intensity units per game-time second. deltaTime is the game-time seconds since the previous frame; adding it to _alarmTime_5__5 updates the elapsed-time counter. A per-frame null yield pauses until a later frame. _smoothTime_5__3 is the smoothing response setting in seconds, not a promise to arrive at the target in exactly that time. The generated state machine stores which numbered step resumes next; MoveNext advances that step until its next pause.

A coroutine is a sequence that continues across frames. This method returns it; BWBoxSequence starts it. A physics joint controls the light mount’s motion, and klaxonRB is its Rigidbody, the simulated physics body. The initial angular-velocity target is (2, 0, 0) radians per second about the joint’s X axis, approximately 115 degrees per second; this is a target, not guaranteed actual speed.

The sequence caches the light’s starting intensity once, enables it at zero brightness, and smooths toward that cached value with a 0.3-second smoothing setting. Changing the initial intensity later does not replace that saved target. After the accumulated game-time counter is strictly greater than 22 seconds, it requests zero rotation and smooths toward zero brightness. At the first update with the counter at least 25 seconds, it disables the light. These checks happen on frames, so they are not exact wall-clock times.

The light uses SmoothDamp each frame with _smoothTime_5__3 and _velRef_5__4. Its target is _orginalIntensity_5__2 until _alarmTime_5__5 exceeds 22 s. Then klaxonJoint.targetAngularVelocity becomes Vector3.zero, and the target intensity becomes 0. The frame loop starts with _alarmTime_5__5 at 0. At 25 s, the coroutine disables klaxonLight. States other than 0 and 1 end iteration.
To change its behavior, patch its state machine's MoveNext method, GameControl_Hub._KlaxonLight_d__162.MoveNext. The values of __1__state are:

item.description: Running or done.

First entry. It sets klaxonJoint.targetAngularVelocity to (2, 0, 0) and wakes klaxonRB. It stores klaxonLight.intensity in _orginalIntensity_5__2, enables the light at intensity 0, and sets _smoothTime_5__3 to 0.3 s.
Continues after the per-frame null yield. It repeats the intensity update and adds deltaTime to _alarmTime_5__5.

member.returns: The light sequence to run as a coroutine.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.OnLevelLoad
