member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.Teleport
member.summary: Moves the player rig to the Hub resume point selected by the cached respawn index.

remarks.para: The player rig is the group of body objects and controllers representing the player. A transform stores an object’s position and facing. World position is measured in the level’s shared coordinate system, normally in meters, and its forward direction chooses which way the player faces.

Uses hubSpawnPoints[_loadedTeleportSpot].spawnLocation’s world position and forward direction, so turning that spawn transform changes the player’s facing. DataRead normally fills the cached index during initialization; changing the saved HubSpawnLocation alone does not update an already-running controller’s choice.
The selected list entry and spawn transform must exist. The method does not clamp an invalid index or choose another point if the selected entry is missing.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.UNLOCKJIMMYKEY(System.Boolean)
member.summary: Marks Jimmy’s key unlocked, saves and refreshes Hub progress, and requests its unlock achievement.

remarks.para: isJimmyKeyUnlocked becomes true first. With fromSave true and the key not inserted, it also shows the loose jimmyKey object. With fromSave false it does not directly show that loose object.

This records unlock state in memory, but DataWrite does not write JimmyKeyUnlocked. Restoring that flag later therefore depends on a saved flag supplied elsewhere; this method’s save call alone does not establish that persistence.

member.param: True to show an unlocked, uninserted loose key while restoring progress.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.UNLOCKKEY(System.Int32)
member.summary: Marks a module key unlocked, activates its progress-board ball, saves and refreshes Hub progress.

remarks.para: The module indices are 0 = Tactical Trial, 1 = Arena, 2 = Sandbox, 3 = Parkour, 4 = Experimental, and 5 = Mods. For example, index 1 selects the Arena key. The matching arrays must contain that index.

It sets isKeyUnlock[keyInt] before calling progressBoard.BALLSACTIVE. DisplayKeys removes the matching stopper lock and updates the visible keys. Unlocking does not mark the module key inserted; KEYINSERTED reports that separately.

member.param: Module index from 0 through 5 in the matching key arrays.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.UpgradeHubInventoryToPush
member.summary: Copies a legacy saved final inventory into the shared Hub initial-inventory entry when that entry is missing.

remarks.para: An existing readable SLZ.Bonelab.initial_inventory entry in Hub makes the method return. Otherwise it first tries the SLZ.Bonelab.final_inventory entry in Hub_C. If present, it copies that value into SLZ.Bonelab.initial_inventory in Hub and deletes the old Hub_C entry.

If Hub_C has no readable final inventory, it searches PriorLevelsC in reverse order and copies the first readable final inventory it finds. Those earlier-level entries are retained. This changes the active save’s data; it does not spawn inventory objects or request a disk save itself. Awake, a setup routine Unity calls when this component initializes, normally calls it before reading Hub data and later requests a save.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_KartRace.DoLevelComplete
member.summary: Runs the inherited level-completion and transition setup, then records that the hub’s mod key is unlocked.

remarks.para: This is separate from ending the timed race. ENDRACE handles the race result and objective; this method calls the inherited level-completion path. That path records completion and inventory according to the level’s save settings, applies configured rewards and campaign progress, and requests the fade object that will lead to the next configured level.

A callback, a routine run later when another operation reaches a step, connects the created fade object to the later level-load request. Calling this method therefore starts transition setup; it does not mean the destination has already loaded. After the inherited call returns, this override attempts to set the hub’s mod-key-unlocked flag to true and requests a progression save. It needs an active save. The save request is not a guarantee of a successful write to disk.
This override does not call ENDRACE or stop the race timer. Finish the race separately if its statistics should be recorded before level completion.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_KartRace.ENDRACE
member.summary: Stops the race clock and music, records the final total, updates best times and requests the finish rewards and celebrations.

remarks.para: Stops the stored timer coroutine, a sequence that pauses and continues on later frames, and clears timerRoutine. It then stops the override music and runs the inherited objective-completion action. That action requests the configured avatar reward spawn if it is still locked; otherwise it requests showing the configured progression buttons. A spawn request does not prove the reward object has already appeared.

Hides aff_Finish, copies _elapsedSumOfLapTimesTotal, the running race clock in seconds, into _sumOfLaps_Current, the final-result snapshot, and sets finishedRace true. It does not recalculate the result by adding lapTimes, and it does not set raceStarted false. Changing the lap array alone therefore does not change the final total recorded here.

The session best becomes the final result if the old session best is approximately zero or the new result is strictly smaller. It then reads the saved personal best for this level. If that value is missing, or the session best is strictly faster, it copies the session best into _sumOfLaps_PersonalBest, attempts to store it and requests a progression save. Equal times do not replace an existing best. For example, a 125-second result beats a 130-second best; 130 does not beat 130. Save success is not checked by this method.

Refreshes the lap label, best-time labels and lap-time labels. It requests the motorway completion achievement, then extra achievements for a session best strictly below 120 seconds and, within that branch, strictly below 110 seconds. Exactly 120 or 110 does not pass the corresponding threshold. These checks use the session best, so a slower current result can still qualify after an earlier fast race in this session.

Finally requests all three particle celebrations in the order confettiLap, confettiStart, confettiFinish, then their three sound players in the same order. NEWLAP already requests the lap celebration before calling this method on a final lap, so that final crossing can issue another lap celebration request here.

This method has no check that a race was started, that all checkpoints were visited, or that the final lap was reached. Calling it directly can record an incomplete clock value and request objective rewards. The normal FinishLineTrigger-to-NEWLAP path applies checkpoint and lap-count checks first. A full retry should call RESETRACE before STARTRACE, because the started flag remains true after a finish.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_KartRace.FinishLineTrigger
member.summary: Starts the race on the first call, then tries to complete a lap on later calls until the race is marked finished.

remarks.para: If raceStarted is false, calls STARTRACE. Otherwise, if finishedRace is false, calls NEWLAP, which checks the lap’s checkpoint flags. If both flags are true, does nothing. For example, the first line crossing starts timing; the next one records a lap only after every configured checkpoint has been marked.

This is a callable scene action. It does not inspect a kart, a collider, crossing direction or position. Connect the appropriate scene trigger event to this method; a trigger volume is an invisible shape that can report when something enters it. Assigning trigger_StartRace or trigger_NewLap alone does not create that event connection. After ENDRACE, raceStarted stays true and finishedRace is true, so another call is ignored until those flags are reset.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_KartRace.NEWLAP
member.summary: Records the current lap and advances its index when every configured checkpoint flag is true, ending the race at the configured lap count.

remarks.para: First checks whether any trackCheckPoint entry is false. If so, returns without recording a lap or changing its index. The flags are a checklist, not an ordered route: checkpoint 2 can be marked before checkpoint 0. An empty, non-null checkpoint array has no false entries, so it passes this check. A null array is invalid.

After passing, clears all checkpoint flags for the next lap, requests the lap particles and sound, writes the current _elapsedLapTime in seconds into lapTimes[_lapIndex], resets the lap clock to zero and increments _lapIndex. Supply a non-null lapTimes array with a valid slot at that index. If a required celebration object or array entry fails, later steps are not guaranteed to run.

If the new index is exactly totalLaps, calls ENDRACE. Otherwise, if it is exactly totalLaps minus 1, shows aff_Finish as a hint for the final lap. With totalLaps set to 3, index 0 records the first lap; advancing to index 2 shows the final-lap hint, and advancing to index 3 ends the race. The comparison is equality, not “at least”: advancing an already excessive index does not automatically finish.

Refreshes the lap-count display afterward. This method itself does not check raceStarted or finishedRace, so direct calls must respect the race’s state. It does not reset the running race-total clock or recompute that total from lap splits.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_KartRace.RESETRACE
member.summary: Stops the race clock and music, clears lap timing and checkpoint progress, and returns the race displays to the starting state.

remarks.para: Stops and clears timerRoutine, the stored coroutine handle; a coroutine is a sequence that can resume on later frames. Stops the override music, clears both raceStarted and finishedRace, shows aff_Start and hides aff_Finish. It clears lapTimes and writes zero-time strings to every txt_lapTimes entry, including entries that are currently disabled.

Sets _lapIndex, _elapsedLapTime and _elapsedSumOfLapTimesTotal to zero, clears every checkpoint flag, then refreshes the lap label, best times and timing labels. The ready lap label is start. The next STARTRACE can therefore begin a new run from lap index 0 with both clocks at zero.

Preserves the session best, saved personal best and _sumOfLaps_Current, the previous final-result snapshot. It does not rewind or move the kart, restore track objects, or clear the displayed best records. Use WIPE_PB separately to request deleting the saved best. All required scene references and arrays must be configured before this reset can finish.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_KartRace.STARTRACE
member.summary: Starts the race’s music and clock, clears lap and checkpoint arrays, and requests the lap celebration when the race has not started.

remarks.para: Returns immediately if raceStarted is already true. Otherwise, requests override playback of raceMusic, hides aff_Start, clears lapTimes and trackCheckPoint, and resets the split-time labels to zero. It sets _elapsedLapTime to zero, then plays confettiLap and its cached sound player. It does not play confettiStart in this path.

Stops an old timerRoutine if one is stored, starts a new StartTimer coroutine, saves its handle, refreshes the lap-count display and finally sets raceStarted true. A coroutine is a sequence that can pause and continue on later frames. The saved handle is what later lets RESETRACE and ENDRACE stop this clock. Music and sound calls request playback; they do not prove a sound is already audible.

This method does not reset _lapIndex, _elapsedSumOfLapTimesTotal or finishedRace. Use RESETRACE before starting a full retry. For example, clearing raceStarted by itself after a finish can start timing with the previous lap index and total still stored, which can also make the timer access a lap slot beyond the array.

The clock adds unscaled frame seconds: the real elapsed time between Unity frames, without multiplying by the game’s slow-motion setting. It skips the addition when Time.timeScale, the game’s speed setting, is exactly zero. For example, a frame lasting 0.02 second adds 0.02 to both lap and race clocks at a time scale of 1 or 0.5, but adds nothing at a time scale of 0. The clock is updated frame by frame, so a line crossing records the latest stored frame value, not a separately measured instant of crossing.

Provide non-null arrays and non-null required objects before starting. Empty display arrays are allowed if that display is not needed. lapTimes must have a slot for every driven lap, and each enabled txt_lapTimes entry needs a matching slot at the same index. The controller does not create those arrays or scene objects for you.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_KartRace.StartTimer
member.summary: Creates the frame-by-frame sequence that advances the lap and race clocks and refreshes their displays.

remarks.para: Returning this sequence does not start it. STARTRACE passes it to Unity’s coroutine runner, which starts and resumes sequences across frames, and stores the resulting handle in timerRoutine. Each running step either waits while Time.timeScale is exactly zero, or adds the current unscaled frame duration to both clocks.

The clock adds unscaled frame seconds: the real elapsed time between Unity frames, without multiplying by the game’s slow-motion setting. It skips the addition when Time.timeScale, the game’s speed setting, is exactly zero. For example, a frame lasting 0.02 second adds 0.02 to both lap and race clocks at a time scale of 1 or 0.5, but adds nothing at a time scale of 0. The clock is updated frame by frame, so a line crossing records the latest stored frame value, not a separately measured instant of crossing.

After adding time, writes _elapsedLapTime into lapTimes[_lapIndex] and calls UI_DisplayLapTime, then waits until another frame. The array therefore contains the active lap’s running time as well as completed splits. For example, while driving lap index 1, entry 0 can hold the finished first lap and entry 1 is repeatedly updated with the second lap’s current duration.

The sequence has no stopping condition based on raceStarted or finishedRace. Changing those flags alone does not stop it. ENDRACE or RESETRACE stops it through the stored handle. Starting another copy separately can advance the clocks more than once per frame; keep one running sequence and configure a valid lap array and index.

member.returns: A sequence that updates the two clocks when run as a Unity coroutine. It does not begin timing merely because it was returned.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_KartRace.TRACKCHECKPOINT(System.Int32)
member.summary: Marks one checkpoint as visited so the next accepted lap can pass its checkpoint checklist.

remarks.para: Sets trackCheckPoint[checkpoint] to true. The index starts at zero: checkpoint 0 is the first entry, and an array of three checkpoints accepts indices 0, 1 and 2. Negative indices and an index equal to or greater than the array length are invalid and cause an out-of-range failure; a null array is invalid too.

Does not require an active race or enforce a crossing order. Repeating the same checkpoint simply leaves its flag true. NEWLAP requires every entry to be true, then clears them all for the next lap. STARTRACE and RESETRACE also clear the checklist, so marks made before starting are lost.

member.param: Zero-based checkpoint index to mark true. It must be at least 0 and smaller than trackCheckPoint.Length.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_KartRace.UI_DisplayBests
member.summary: Copies the stored session and personal best times into their configured text arrays.

remarks.para: Times are stored as seconds and displayed as minutes:seconds:hundredths of a second. For example, 65.25 seconds displays as 01:05:25. This is a time display format, not three separate saved values.

Writes _sumOfLaps_SessionBest to every txt_totalTime_SessionBest entry and _sumOfLaps_PersonalBest to every txt_totalTime_PersonalBest entry. Both source values are seconds. This helper writes even to disabled text components; it does not check whether each one is currently visible.

It only refreshes text. It does not read or write the save, find a new best, or calculate a total from lapTimes. Start loads the saved personal best, ENDRACE updates the best values, and WIPE_PB clears both values before calling this helper. Configure non-null arrays with non-null entries; empty arrays are allowed.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_KartRace.UI_DisplayLapTime
member.summary: Refreshes the running race total, current lap clock and indexed lap-time labels from their stored second values.

remarks.para: Times are stored as seconds and displayed as minutes:seconds:hundredths of a second. For example, 65.25 seconds displays as 01:05:25. This is a time display format, not three separate saved values.

Writes _elapsedSumOfLapTimesTotal to each active and enabled txt_totalTime entry, then _elapsedLapTime to each active and enabled txt_CurrentLapTime entry. The race total includes the current lap, not just completed laps. Finally, active and enabled txt_lapTimes[i] receives lapTimes[i], so index 0 displays the first lap slot, index 1 the second, and so on.

An active and enabled text component is one whose object is active and whose text component is enabled. Disabled entries keep their old text during this helper. Provide non-null arrays and entries; every lap-time display that will be enabled needs a matching lapTimes slot. This helper only formats stored values: it does not advance the clock or add split times together. The running timer calls it once per advancing frame.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_KartRace.UI_DisplayLaps
member.summary: Shows the current lap number, start, or finished according to the stored timer handle and finish flag.

remarks.para: If timerRoutine is non-null, active and enabled txt_CurrentLap entries display (_lapIndex + 1)/totalLaps. _lapIndex is the zero-based slot being driven, and totalLaps is the configured lap count; the added 1 converts the slot to a human lap number. For example, index 1 with totalLaps 3 displays 2/3.

If timerRoutine is null, those entries display finished when finishedRace is true, or start when it is false. The choice uses the stored handle, not raceStarted, and a non-null handle does not itself prove that its coroutine—a sequence that pauses and resumes over later frames—is still running. Disabled text entries are skipped. This method only refreshes labels and does not change the lap index or start or stop timing.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_KartRace.WIPE_PB
member.summary: Requests deletion of this level’s saved best time, clears both in-memory best times and refreshes the best-time labels.

remarks.para: Attempts to delete the sum-of-laps personal-best entry from the active save for this controller’s level, requests a progression save, sets _sumOfLaps_SessionBest and _sumOfLaps_PersonalBest to zero, then refreshes both displays. The method does not check the delete or save result, so zero in the display alone is not proof that a disk write succeeded.

It leaves the running timer, lap index, lap array, current final-result snapshot and race flags unchanged. A later ENDRACE can establish a new best from its result. For example, wiping a 125-second personal best also clears the session best, even if the current race clock is still running.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_MagmaGate.DoLevelComplete
member.summary: Runs the shared level-completion code from its parent controllers and the next-level transition request, then records the arena key as unlocked in hub progress and requests a save.

remarks.para: The shared completion code from this controller's parent classes first marks this level complete when completion saving is enabled. When partial-progress saving is enabled, it resets this level's saved progress number to 0. It finalizes saved inventory when that option is enabled, and grants the configured item unlocks. It updates campaign progress as needed and starts the transition to the configured next campaign level through a fade effect. A transition request does not mean the next scene has already finished loading when this method returns.

The shared avatar-level completion code from the parent controller then sets the hub progress flag SLZ.Bonelab.ParkourKeyUnlocked to true and requests a progression save. After that returns, this override sets SLZ.Bonelab.ArenaKeyUnlocked to true on the current active save and requests another progression save. These flags are saved yes-or-no values; they are not physical key objects spawned into the scene.

The flag-setting and save-request results are not checked here. The active save, progression data, and campaign references required by the parent controllers must be set up before calling this method. For example, call it when a configured Magma Gate objective is complete; do not treat its return as confirmation that saving or scene loading succeeded.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_MagmaGate.DoorDissolve
member.summary: Immediately calls the listeners currently assigned to the loss event.

remarks.para: The loss event is a UnityEvent: a list of methods configured to run when it is invoked. Each listener is a callback, meaning a method called in response to the event. This invocation passes no arguments. If loseEvent is null, the method returns without invoking anything.

Door changes come from the assigned listeners. For example, a scene can connect a listener that starts a door animation or removes a barrier. This method itself only invokes the event; it performs no door animation and makes no player-health or failure check.

LoseSequence requests this call after activating its laser objects and waiting for a configured delay of 1.25 seconds. Calling DoorDissolve directly invokes the event immediately, without that laser activation or delay. A delayed call uses whichever event is assigned when DoorDissolve actually runs.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_MagmaGate.LoseSequence
member.summary: Sets each assigned laser object active, then asks Unity to call the loss-event method after a delay of 1.25 seconds.

remarks.para: Objects in laserBeams are processed in array order. The method calls SetActive(true) on each one, which sets that object's active setting. Its visible beam and damage behavior depend on the components and scene setup attached to the object.

Only after every entry has been processed does the method schedule DoorDissolve with a delay value of 1.25 seconds. It returns after scheduling; loseEvent is invoked later when Unity runs the delayed call. The delay is a scheduling value, not a guarantee that the call occurs at an exact elapsed frame time.

Assign the array and every object in it before calling. A null array or null entry stops the method with an error before the delayed call is scheduled; earlier entries may already have been activated. An assigned empty array still schedules the call. The method makes no player-failure check and does not cancel an earlier delayed call.

For example, with three assigned beam objects and a door-animation listener on loseEvent, this call sets the three objects active now and requests the listener invocation after the delay. Merely changing laserBeams or loseEvent does not start the sequence.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GenGameControl_Display.ChangeAllTextColor
member.summary: Requests the configured default text color on matching text components in this object’s hierarchy.

remarks.para: It searches for TMP_Text components on the same GameObject and on active child GameObjects, then assigns textColor to each result’s color property. TMP_Text is a TextMeshPro component that draws a string. Inactive children are excluded by this search.

The search uses the hierarchy, not the named title, timer or statistic reference fields. An unlisted child text component can be recolored, while a named reference on an unrelated object is not reached. For example, a new active child label receives the color without needing a statistic slot.

This is a one-time operation when called, also available from the component’s ChangeAllTextColor context-menu command. Changing textColor later does not repeat it automatically. It changes the default letter color, not the text strings, counts or timer values; formatting tags inside a string may still override that default.
A GameObject is an object in a Unity scene. The hierarchy is Unity’s tree of scene objects. A child is an object nested under another object; the search includes active descendants at any depth.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GenGameControl_Spawner.DespawnLootWeapons(System.Boolean)
member.summary: Returns eligible tracked loot weapons to their object pools, optionally detaching held or attached weapons first.
member.param: True also detaches tracked attached weapons before attempting to despawn them; false leaves attached weapons alone. Both choices still require the interaction and pool components.

remarks.para: An object pool keeps an object ready for later reuse instead of permanently destroying it. This method examines the weapons recorded by this spawner, rather than searching every object in the arena. It requires a recognized interaction component and a recognized pool component on each weapon it removes.

With despawnAll false, attached weapons are skipped. With despawnAll true, an attached weapon is forcibly detached before the pool lookup. A recognized weapon with no pool component can therefore be detached without being removed.

For each weapon it can return to a pool, the method records it in a temporary removal list, requests its despawn visual effect when available, and then despawns it. After that pass, it removes those objects from the tracked weapon list and clears the temporary list. Ammo pickups are handled separately.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GenGameControl_Spawner.ForceCollectAllAmmo
member.summary: Collects active ammo pickups recorded in this spawner's collection list, then clears that list.

remarks.para: For each recorded pickup whose object and parents are active, its collection routine adds the pickup's ammoCount rounds of its ammoGroup to the current ammo inventory. That routine then marks the pickup collected, invokes its collection event, and requests its effects and sound. It needs an available ammo inventory.
The method clears the entire list after processing it, including inactive entries that it skipped. It does not clear the saved light, medium and heavy pickup references or reset the ammo counters.

This covers newly created pickups recorded by the ordinary wave path and heavy pickups recorded by the weapon-mode path. The weapon-mode light and medium callbacks do not add their pickups to this list. For example, a visible weapon-mode light ammo box can remain uncollected by this call unless something else has added it to the list.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GenGameControl_Spawner.Initialize(Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController)
member.summary: Connects this spawner to an , caches its player rig, and prepares the ammo and player-relative drop locations.
member.param: The arena controller to store and obtain the current player rig from; it must be supplied.

remarks.para: The controller reference is stored, and its current rig manager is copied into this spawner. If both that rig and the player-relative helper prefab exist, the method creates the helper used for weapon-mode drops.

If no ammo spawn transform is assigned, it creates a child object of this spawner at local position (0, 0, 0.25). Local coordinates are measured along the parent's axes: zero sideways, zero upward and 0.25 units forward. At normal BONELAB scale this is 25 centimetres forward; parent scaling can change the world distance.

Supply a controller before starting waves. This is setup work: changing the controller's rig later does not automatically refresh this cached rig or move the existing helper. Calling initialization again can create another helper; it does not first reuse or remove the previous one, and it does not reset the ammo counters or tracking lists.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GenGameControl_Spawner.SetupPlayerRelativeGunSpawns
member.summary: Creates and connects the location helper that places weapon-mode loot relative to the player.

remarks.para: This instantiates playerRelSpawnPrefab as a helper object. It parents the helper to the cached player rig's center-of-pressure transform, a moving reference point in the rig. It then sets the helper's position relative to that parent to zero and its rotation relative to the parent to no extra turn.

The method saves the helper's PlayerRelativeGunSpawns component and gives it the player's pelvis Rigidbody. A Rigidbody is the Unity component that represents a body with mass and movement for physics. The rig, its reference point and the prefab must be ready; the prefab needs the helper component for later weapon-mode drops.

This call creates the helper, not a weapon. The wave-spawning routine later updates its drop point, shows its marker and requests loot there. Each setup call creates a new helper rather than checking whether the previous helper can be reused.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GenGameControl_Spawner.SpawnWaveLoot(Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.WaveProfile)
member.summary: Starts the selected arena mode's sequence of weapon and ammo spawn requests for a .
member.param: The wave's loot entries and light, medium and heavy ammo amounts, measured in rounds. Positive ammo amounts are processed. Loot percentages are tested by the weapon-mode path, but not by the ordinary path.

remarks.para: The arena controller and its assigned round profile choose the path. If the controller is missing, the method logs a message and returns. Otherwise it requests the spawn sound at this spawner's world position before starting a coroutine: a routine that pauses and continues on later Unity frames. Returning from this method does not mean the requested objects have finished spawning. A callback is code run later with the object returned by a spawn request; those callbacks record the pickups and weapons.

Outside weapon mode, positive heavy, medium and light ammo amounts are processed in that order. An existing saved pickup that is still active receives the wave's amount as extra rounds; otherwise a new pickup is requested at ammoSpawnTrans's world position. Each positive ammo step is followed by a wait of 0.5 game-time seconds. The routine then requests each valid loot entry at this spawner's world position, with a 0.5 game-time-second wait per entry. This path does not test the entries' loot percentages.

In weapon mode, the routine updates the player-relative drop point, shows its marker and waits 1 real-time second. It filters a nonempty loot list using one shared random integer from 0 through 99: an entry passes when that number is greater than zero and no higher than the entry's percentage. Thus even a percentage of 100 fails on a roll of zero. If no entry passes, the returned list is missing and this routine cannot continue to its ammo and marker-hiding steps.

When that selection succeeds, selected valid weapons are requested at the player-relative drop point. New light, medium and heavy pickups are then requested there for positive wave amounts, rather than topping up the saved pickups. Weapon requests and the light and medium ammo steps wait 0.5 real-time seconds each; the heavy ammo step waits 0.5 game-time seconds. The marker is hidden after the sequence resumes from its last wait.

Game-time waits follow the game's time scale, so slow motion lengthens their real-world duration. Real-time waits ignore that scale. These are configured waits followed by a later-frame continuation, not exact measured elapsed times or a check that a previous spawn has completed. The player-relative helper and ammo location must have been prepared before their respective paths run.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GeoManager.Awake
member.summary: Builds the preset-name lookups from the configured geometry mover list.

remarks.para: Awake is Unity's initialization callback, a routine called while setting up the component. For each geoMoverList entry, it adds the mover's name and zero-based list position to geoDict, and the same name and mover reference to geoMoverDict. For [Bridge, Towers], the positions are Bridge = 0 and Towers = 1.

The dictionaries are created during construction. Awake adds entries without clearing them, so names must be unique and the list must have no missing movers. Renaming, adding or reordering movers later does not automatically rebuild these lookups; calling Awake again can encounter duplicate keys.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GeoManager.CleanupDecalsAndFragments
member.summary: Requests removal of active pooled fragments and projected marks across the loaded scene.

remarks.para: A fragment is a broken piece of an object. A DecalProjector draws a mark on a surface, such as a bullet hole or blood splatter. This searches for SpawnFragment and DecalProjector components rather than only children of the active geometry mover.

A GameObject is a Unity scene object that contains components. Active in the hierarchy means that the object and its parent objects are active. For each such object, it looks for a cached Poolee on that same GameObject and asks it to despawn, removing it from play so its pool can reuse it. A Poolee represents an object managed by a pool, a supply of objects kept for reuse. An object without that matching pool entry is left alone. This can affect matching active effects elsewhere in the scene; it is not a deletion of every mark or piece of debris.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GeoManager.ClearCurrentGeo
member.summary: Hides non-death-pit presets, restores an inactive pit-cover floor, and cleans the recorded active mover's temporary objects and joint.

remarks.para: A GameObject is a Unity scene object that contains components. It first disables the GameObjects of every geoMoverList entry whose isDeathPit flag is false. Those objects are hidden immediately rather than lowered through their movement sequence. If deathPitFloorMover is inactive, it activates that object and starts raising its floor, restarting an earlier floor movement if needed, with the higher-pitch movement sound.

If activeGeoMover is dynamic, it asks that mover to despawn its recorded pooled destructibles and clears their lists. Pooled objects are kept for reuse; despawning removes them from play so the pool can reuse them. If its timberJoint exists, it makes the Rigidbody on that joint's GameObject kinematic and schedules the joint for destruction. A Rigidbody gives an object simulated mass and motion; kinematic means physics forces no longer move it. A joint connects simulated bodies.

It then runs the scene-wide fragment and decal cleanup. The active mover and configured floor must exist. This method does not clear activeGeoMover, reset either index, or write geoState = CLEARED. A raised floor can later become activeGeoMover and send a move-up notification when its own sequence finishes.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GeoManager.IncrementAndToggleGeo
member.summary: Clears the current setup, advances currGeoIndex, and starts deploying that list entry.

remarks.para: It runs ClearCurrentGeo first, then adds 1 to currGeoIndex and wraps to 0 when the result is beyond the last geoMoverList entry. It passes the resulting index to ToggleGeo. With three presets and currGeoIndex = 2, the next request uses entry 0.

This uses the saved selection counter, not the position of activeGeoMover in the list. Clearing and any delayed deployment still follow their normal separate paths. Configure a nonempty mover list and the active/floor references needed by ClearCurrentGeo; an empty list cannot supply the requested entry.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GeoManager.IncrementGeoIndex
member.summary: Advances the saved preset-selection counter without moving any geometry.

remarks.para: It adds 1 to currGeoIndex and resets it to 0 if it is greater than the last geoMoverList position. Positions are zero-based: a three-entry list uses 0, 1 and 2, and advancing from 2 gives 0.
It does not call ToggleGeo, change activeGeoMover, or update moverIndex. The list must exist. With an empty list it sets the counter to 0, but that still is not a valid preset to deploy.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GeoManager.MoveDownComplete(Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GeoMover)

It does not change geoState or clear activeGeoMover. Calling it directly performs this bookkeeping; it does not move the object through its downward path.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GeoManager.MoveUpComplete(Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GeoMover)

remarks.para: A callback is a routine used to report completion. If the supplied mover is a floor, this first disables deathPitGeoMover. It then sets activeGeoMover to the supplied mover, stops the audio player, sets geoState = UP, and invokes OnMoveUpComplete with no arguments. Listeners see that new reference and state.

If the supplied mover is a death pit, only after that notification does it start lowering deathPitFloorMover and restart the sound at the higher pitch. The notification therefore does not mean the pit is already uncovered. The normal mover sequence also sends this manager notification before its own onMoveUpComplete event and before calling SpawnDestructables for dynamic props.

This routine does not calculate the mover's position or update either index. Calling it directly can report completion without carrying out a movement sequence; normally the GeoMover coroutine, a sequence that pauses across frames, reaches it after raising.

member.param: The mover reporting a completed raise; its floor and death-pit flags control the follow-up actions.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GeoManager.SelectGeo(System.String)

remarks.para: It looks up geoTitle in geoDict. If the name is found, it calls ClearCurrentGeo and then ToggleGeo with that saved list index. A missing name leaves the setup unchanged. Use the exact stored mover name, including its capitalization.

Awake is Unity's initialization callback, a routine Unity calls while setting up the component; it builds the names from geoMoverList during setup. Renaming or reordering the list later does not automatically update that mapping. SelectGeo does not copy its selected index into currGeoIndex or moverIndex, and a request can finish later across several frames.

member.param: The exact mover name stored in geoDict during initialization.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GeoManager.ToggleAudio(System.Boolean,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Starts or retunes the geometry movement loop, or stops its managed audio player.

remarks.para: With startPlaying true, the supplied pitch factor P is 1 for the normal setting or 1.2 when pitchShift is true. P is unitless: 1 means the clip's usual playback speed and pitch, and 1.2 means a faster, higher setting before any new-loop adjustment. If the player reports it is already playing, only its pitch is changed. Otherwise it requests a loop of moveGeoClip at local position (0, 0, 0) on this manager's Transform, so the source follows the manager. A Transform stores an object's position, rotation and size.

For a new loop, the audio helper uses P × (0.75 × S + 0.25), where P is the supplied unitless playback-speed/pitch factor and S is Time.timeScale, Unity's unitless game-speed multiplier: 1 means normal game speed and 0.5 means half speed. The constants 0.75 and 0.25 are unitless weights. For S = 0.5 and P = 1.2, the result is 1.2 × 0.625 = 0.75. This adjustment happens when the loop is requested; this call does not recalculate it every frame. When the player already reports playing, ToggleAudio sets P directly instead.

A new loop uses volume setting 0.5, a unitless sound level where 0 is silent and 1 is the full setting. Its minimum distance is 4 meters: within that distance, distance fading has not yet reduced the volume. Its spatialBlend is 0.8, a unitless blend toward 3D positioning where 0 is fully 2D and 1 fully 3D. With startPlaying false it stops the player and ignores pitchShift. The player is created during manager construction; this call requests audio rather than guaranteeing that a sound is audible.

member.param: True to start or retune the movement loop; false to stop it.
When starting or retuning, true supplies pitch factor P = 1.2 and false supplies P = 1. A new loop applies the game-speed adjustment explained above. The default is false.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GeoManager.ToggleGeo(System.Int32)
member.summary: Activates a preset at its starting position and requests its movement toward the deployed position.

remarks.para: A GameObject is a Unity scene object that contains components; its Transform stores position, rotation and size. The index is a zero-based position in geoMoverList. For three entries, use 0, 1 or 2. The chosen mover's Transform.localPosition is first set to its startPos, then its GameObject is activated, geoState is set to MOVING, its upward movement is started, and normal-pitch movement audio is requested.

startPos and the mover's endPos are positions relative to its parent's axes, in local length units, meters at parent scale 1. The movement interpolates between them across frames using the mover's configured moveUpDuration in game-time seconds; it does not promise an exact number of frames. Game-time seconds advance with the game-speed setting, so movement and waits can take a different number of real-time seconds.

If the recorded activeGeoMover is a death pit, deployment is delayed by deathPitFloorMover.moveUpDuration + 0.1 game-time seconds. A coroutine, a sequence that pauses across frames, handles that wait before the same activation steps. This is a duration-based delay, not a check that the floor reported completion.

ToggleGeo does not itself clear or lower the old preset, assign activeGeoMover, or update currGeoIndex or moverIndex. SelectGeo and IncrementAndToggleGeo call ClearCurrentGeo separately. The active reference changes on the later move-up report. A missing mover or an index outside the list is not clamped to a valid entry.

member.param: A valid zero-based position in geoMoverList for the preset to deploy.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.HighlightUI.DisableMesh
member.summary: Hides the surface drawn by the cached highlight Renderer.

remarks.para: A GameObject is the Unity scene object that holds components such as HighlightUI and Renderer. Sets m_Renderer.enabled to false. This hides that renderer without disabling the GameObject or changing its two stored colors. It does not stop a color fade that is already running, so the colors can continue changing while the surface is hidden.

Start applies the saved color pair through SetColors. SetColors finds the Renderer on this same GameObject when the cached reference is missing. A Renderer is the Unity component that draws the visible surface. DisableMesh itself does not search for the component, so the renderer reference must already be available. EnableMesh shows that cached renderer again.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.HighlightUI.EnableMesh
member.summary: Shows the surface drawn by the cached highlight Renderer.

remarks.para: A GameObject is the Unity scene object that holds components such as HighlightUI and Renderer. Sets m_Renderer.enabled to true. It does not reset color1 or color2, start a fade, or activate an inactive GameObject. For example, hiding the renderer, changing its colors through SetColors, and showing it again keeps the newly applied colors.

Start applies the saved color pair through SetColors. SetColors finds the Renderer on this same GameObject when the cached reference is missing. A Renderer is the Unity component that draws the visible surface. EnableMesh itself does not look up the component; it needs the cached reference to be available first.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.HighlightUI.Start
member.summary: Applies color1 and color2 to the highlight Renderer as the initial visible color settings.

remarks.para: A Renderer is the Unity component that draws a surface. A GameObject is the scene object that holds it and this HighlightUI component. Unity calls Start during component startup. It passes the two current fields to SetColors, which writes them into the shared MaterialPropertyBlock and applies that block to this component’s renderer. A MaterialPropertyBlock is a container of shader settings applied for one renderer; a shader is the drawing program that turns those settings into the visible surface.

Awake, Unity’s initialization callback (a routine called to perform or report an action), prepares the shared block and color-property IDs when the block is missing. SetColors obtains the Renderer from this same GameObject if its cached reference is missing. Start does not search children for a renderer or create a missing one.

This routine uses the fields’ current values rather than resetting them to constructor colors. Changing a color field later only changes the stored value; call SetColors to apply the pair again. Start does not enable a hidden renderer or stop a running fade.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LaserCursor.AUDIOSEND(System.Int32)
member.summary: Plays one laser cue: 0 selects pulse sounds, 1 appearance sounds, and 2 disappearance sounds.

remarks.para: The selected array must be assigned. An empty array skips playback; another action number selects no cue. It uses the cached prismaticSFX Transform’s current world position, acquiring that Transform when first needed. Audio is played through Audio3dManager using three settings: _sourceVolume, a unitless numeric volume level where 0 requests silence; _sourceRadius, passed as AudioSource.minDistance in meters; and spatialBlend, a unitless 2D/3D mix where 0 is fully 2D and 1 fully 3D. For a 3D sound, moving closer than _sourceRadius no longer makes it louder; farther away, the AudioSource settings start making it quieter. This is not the farthest distance at which the sound can be heard or the laser’s reach.

Each array has its own stored counter. The routine increments it before selecting counter modulo the array length, and resets it to zero only when it exceeds that length. For an illustrative three-clip array and an initial counter of zero, selections are indices 1, 2, 0, 0, 1, 2. This repeats the first clip at the wrap boundary rather than producing a clean 0, 1, 2 cycle.

member.param: 0 for pulseSound, 1 for raySpawn, or 2 for rayDespawn.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LaserCursor.Activate
member.summary: Marks the cursor active and activates its whole GameObject, the Unity scene object that holds components such as this cursor and may have child objects.

remarks.para: The internal active flag is set before GameObject activation, so initialization or activation callbacks, routines called to perform or report an action, observe that flag already true. This allows later pointer updates and Trigger to operate.
It does not directly call ShowCursor, calculate a new region intersection, or play the appearance cue. The normal Update path handles showing when its region and display conditions pass.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LaserCursor.CalcCursor
member.summary: Calculates the focused controller’s ray and selects the first region that passes its plane and bounds tests.

remarks.para: It runs only after controllerFocused is true. It copies the shared active controller, obtains that controller’s initialized UI cursorTarget Transform, then examines regions in array order. Each region supplies a plane through its center using its forward direction, plus bounds in that center’s rotating coordinate frame. Translation and rotation are used; Transform scale is not applied to the bounds conversion.

The calculated plane-ray distance must be below 10 meters, the intersection point rotated into the region’s frame must lie inside its bounds, and the ray direction must have a positive dot product with the region’s forward direction. A positive dot product means the directions point partly the same way. This uses the returned distance rather than the Plane.Raycast success flag and does not test scene colliders for obstruction.

It writes world-space startPosition and endPosition, isOnPlane and whether the candidate region’s GameObject (its Unity scene object, which can hold components and child objects) is active, stored in isRegionActive. It stops at the first geometric match even if that region is inactive; the caller then requires the active result to display. An empty region list or lack of controller focus leaves previous cached results in place. This calculation does not itself show the visuals or dispatch a UI press.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LaserCursor.Deactivate
member.summary: Marks the cursor inactive and deactivates its whole GameObject, the Unity scene object that holds this cursor’s behavior and may have other components and child objects.

remarks.para: The internal active flag is cleared before GameObject deactivation. This stops this object’s normal Unity updates and also affects other components and children on that object.

It does not call HideCursor or play the disappearance cue. It does not explicitly clear the queued press, cursorHidden or pulse bookkeeping; those stored values are separate from whether the GameObject is active.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LaserCursor.FireRayPulse
member.summary: Creates the animation sequence that moves a pulse marker along the configured curved beam.

remarks.para: A coroutine is a sequence that continues over several frames. Creating this returned iterator does not run the animation; Unity must advance it, normally through StartCoroutine. The normal Update path starts one only when no pulse is recorded as firing and canShowCursor is true.

On its first advance it sets isFireingPulse true, resets pulseProgress and curentPulseTime to zero, starts a cursorEnd blip, plays the pulse cue, places rayPulse at the curve’s start and shows it. During travel, the curve input is curentPulseTime / pulseLength: both are seconds, so this ratio is unitless. pulseAceleration returns the unitless position parameter, not a speed. That parameter is clamped to 0–1 only for drawing the marker; the stored pulseProgress retains the curve result.

For example, with pulseLength 0.5 seconds and elapsed time 0.25 seconds, the curve is evaluated at 0.5. A linear curve returning 0.5 places the marker halfway through the Bezier parameter, which need not be halfway through its physical travel distance. Each travel step adds Unity’s deltaTime, so this uses game time rather than unscaled real time.

The sequence ends when elapsed time reaches pulseLength or stored pulseProgress reaches 1. It starts one blip on each middle marker when progress first exceeds 0.35. On normal completion it blips cursorStart, hides rayPulse, then clears isFireingPulse. A nonpositive duration completes without entering the travel calculation. Stopping the sequence early does not run a separate cleanup routine here.

member.returns: An iterator for the pulse sequence; advance it as a Unity coroutine to perform the animation.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LaserCursor.HideCursor
member.summary: Plays the disappearance cue, marks the visuals hidden, and hides the normal laser markers and line.

remarks.para: In order, it sends the disappearance audio action, sets cursorHidden true, requests 0.05-second hides for cursorStart, cursorMid, cursorMid2, cursorEnd and lineEnd, disables cursorLine, then disables prismaticSFX. cursorBez and rayPulse are not directly hidden by this routine.

It leaves the component’s active flag and plane calculation enabled. A later valid Update can show the cursor again when canShowCursor allows it. Calling HideCursor repeatedly can repeat the cue; cursorHidden alone is not a permanent visibility lock.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LaserCursor.Initialize
member.summary: Connects discovered controllers to the UI rig’s cursor targets, activates the cursor, and releases its startup pause.

remarks.para: Awake is Unity’s initialization callback, a routine called to prepare a component. It registers this initialization routine with the streaming session’s level-load callback; a callback is a routine called to perform or report an action. Registration may invoke it immediately when that session is already at its level-loaded state.

Initialize finds active BaseController components and replaces controllers. It adds left-handed controllers to the UI rig’s left cursorTarget and right-handed ones to its right cursorTarget in the internal mapping. It then calls Activate, disables the assigned prismaticSFX component, and finally sets holdForStart false.

The UI rig, cursor targets and sound reference must exist. This is setup rather than continuous discovery: the mapping is not cleared before entries are added, so repeating initialization with the same controllers can fail on duplicate dictionary keys. Replacing controllers later does not build a matching cursor-target mapping.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LaserCursor.ShowCursor
member.summary: Positions the laser markers, plays the appearance cue, and shows the normal cursor visuals when display is allowed.

remarks.para: It returns immediately when canShowCursor is false. Otherwise it recalculates the region data and, while the component is active and an input module exists, sends that ray and the queued press to the module before clearing the queued press. Its own display path expects usable cached region data and assigned visual references; it does not independently require a successful active-region result.

It resets the marker smoothing velocities, places the start and intermediate markers along the start-to-end segment, and puts cursorEnd and lineEnd 0.025 meters, or 2.5 centimeters, behind the endpoint along the region’s forward direction. The appearance cue is sent before cursorHidden is cleared and before prismaticSFX is moved to this endpoint.

After positioning, it sets cursorHidden false, requests 0.05-second shows for cursorStart, cursorMid, cursorMid2, cursorEnd and lineEnd, enables cursorLine, then moves and enables prismaticSFX. cursorBez is positioned but is not directly shown by this routine; the pulse marker has its own sequence.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LaserCursor.Trigger
member.summary: Queues a UI press when the cursor is active and returns false.

remarks.para: The stored m_IsActiveThisFrame flag is set only when the internal active flag is true. The name does not guarantee it expires at the end of that frame: it clears only after a later successful ray update sends it to the input module.

The normal Update sends any previously queued press before it checks the current controller button and calls Trigger. That newly queued press therefore waits for a later dispatch, unless ShowCursor also dispatches during the same update. Calling Trigger does not itself raycast UI, unlock an item or start the pulse sequence.

member.returns: False, including when the press flag was successfully queued.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LevelsPanelView.CalculateSceneList
member.summary: Rebuilds the sorted list of levels that this panel currently allows the player to select.

remarks.para: The AssetWarehouse is the game’s catalog of installed content. A level crate is a catalog record for a level; its barcode is its unique identifier. This scan removes crates marked Redacted, meaning hidden from menus, then sorts the remaining candidates by their titles using string comparison.

Normally a candidate must pass two checks: its barcode must be in the panel’s completed-story list, and its source must be allowed. The completed-story list comes from the configured barcode-to-save-key mapping and the active save’s ammo-delta records. Ammo deltas are saved changes in ammunition counts. The gathered map is a lookup table indexed by saved level keys, with an entry for each key that passes this saved-data test. A valid saved final-ammo-delta entry counts even when the saved completion flag is false; a true completion flag also counts when the final-ammo-delta key is absent.

For source filtering, internal means the crate’s pallet, or content package, is recognized as belonging to the current game. With only includeInternalLevels true, internal candidates pass. With only includeExternalLevels true, external candidates pass. With both flags true, or both false, candidates from both sources pass. These source choices still require the completed-story check.

When the active save’s BeatGame flag and the settings’ DeveloperMode flag are both true, every non-redacted candidate passes, including ones excluded by the source flags or missing from the completed-story list.

The scan first clears _levelCrates and resets _totalScenes. If the warehouse exists but InitialLoaded is false, it logs an error and leaves the level list empty; it does not wait. In that early return, the old completed-story list remains. A successful loaded scan rebuilds that list and stores the final number of selectable levels in _totalScenes. Page count, current page, row objects, and labels are updated separately by PopulateMenu.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LevelsPanelView.GetLevelCompletion(Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SaveData.PlayerProgression,System.String)
member.summary: Tests whether the supplied save produces an ammo-delta entry for the requested level key.
member.param: Save progression whose LevelState records are inspected.
Save-data key of the level to test.
member.returns: True when the gathered final-ammo-delta map contains level; otherwise false.

remarks.para: The level argument is a save-data key string, not the displayed title or a crate barcode. This method gathers final ammo deltas from progression.LevelState, then tests whether the gathered map contains that key. Ammo deltas are saved changes in ammunition counts; their numeric values are not tested here.

A dictionary, also called a map, is a lookup table. Here an ammunition-count dictionary pairs ammunition names with whole-number count changes. A JSON object is saved data containing named values, which the helper converts into that lookup table. A saved SLZ.Bonelab.final_ammo_delta value that is an ammunition-count dictionary, or a JSON object converted to one, produces an entry even when SLZ.Marrow.completed is false or absent. If the ammo-delta key is absent, a saved boolean true for SLZ.Marrow.completed produces an empty entry and also returns true. With neither of those cases, the method returns false.

For example, a level with a valid saved ammo-delta dictionary and a false completion flag still returns true. A present but null or unsupported ammo-delta value is not the same as an absent key: it can prevent the empty-entry fallback even when the completion flag is true. Supply a valid progression object and its initialized LevelState map.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LevelsPanelView.LoadFirstLevel
member.summary: Activates and refreshes the panel, then requests loading the first level on its current page.

remarks.para: It activates this component’s GameObject, meaning its scene object, and calls the panel’s Activate routine to rebuild the menu before selecting a level. It keeps _currentPage. Thus “first” means row zero of the current page, rather than always the first level in the entire list.

The selected list index is page × rows, where page is the zero-based _currentPage value and rows is items.Length, the number of row slots per page. For example, page 2 with four rows selects list index 8, the ninth selectable level. The current page must contain a level; an empty list or out-of-range page is not safely skipped.

The method starts a SceneStreamer loading request. A level whose pallet, or content package, is marked Internal or recognized as belonging to the current game uses the direct barcode request without a loading-scene choice. Other levels pass modLoadScreen as the loading-scene choice. Returning from this method does not mean the target scene has finished loading.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LevelsPanelView.NextPage
member.summary: Shows the next cached page when another page remains, then stores its index.

remarks.para: Both _currentPage and _numberOfPages describe the menu’s last refresh. The page index starts at zero: page 0 is the first page. If current page + 1 is less than the cached page count, the method updates the page label and row objects, then stores the new index. At the last page it leaves the display and index alone.

It uses items.Length as the number of rows per page and does not rescan installed levels or saved progress. For example, with three pages, page 1 advances to page 2; another call at page 2 has no effect. Labels and rows are updated before _currentPage changes, so a failed UI update can leave the old index stored.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LevelsPanelView.PopulateMenu
member.summary: Rescans selectable levels, recalculates the page count, and redraws the current page.

remarks.para: First CalculateSceneList rebuilds the eligible, title-sorted level list and its count. The page count is ceil(levels / rows): levels is the number of selectable levels, rows is items.Length, the row capacity of one page, and ceil means round upward to the next whole number. The division is performed with floating-point numbers, which can contain fractions: nine divided by four gives 2.25 before rounding upward to three. For example, nine levels and four rows make three pages; zero levels with four rows make zero pages.

It stores that count, updates the page label and navigation objects, then updates the row objects and their title labels. It preserves _currentPage rather than returning to page zero. If a rescan shrinks the list, the stored page can end up beyond the new page count and show no rows until the page is adjusted.

This routine does not wait for AssetWarehouse.InitialLoaded. That property means the content catalog has finished its initial load; call PopulateMenuAsync when that wait is needed. Configure at least one non-null row object, matching row labels, both navigation objects, and pageText. An empty items array causes division by zero before the UI is redrawn.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LevelsPanelView.PopulateMenuAsync
member.summary: Starts a wait for the initial content-catalog load, then rebuilds the level menu.
member.returns: UniTaskVoid is a fire-and-forget async return type; callers cannot await the menu refresh's completion.

remarks.para: AssetWarehouse is the catalog of installed game content. This method waits until AssetWarehouse.Instance.InitialLoaded is true, then calls PopulateMenu to scan selectable levels, calculate the page count, and refresh the current page. The wait resumes through Unity’s Update loop, the repeating part of each rendered frame. It has no fixed number of seconds or frames.

This call gives its caller no awaitable completion value for the menu refresh. Calling it is not evidence that the menu has already refreshed. The warehouse instance and UI references must exist. This method does not reset _currentPage when it eventually refreshes.

An async state machine is the generated helper that remembers where a method paused and continues it later. The preserved patching guide and state-value table below describe that helper’s waiting and completed states.
It waits until AssetWarehouse.Instance.InitialLoaded is true.
To change its behavior, patch its state machine's MoveNext method, LevelsPanelView._PopulateMenuAsync_d__25.MoveNext. The values of __1__state are:

item.description: First entry. It awaits UniTask.WaitUntil.
Continues after UniTask.WaitUntil. It calls LevelsPanelView.PopulateMenu() and finishes.
Done.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LevelsPanelView.PrevPage

It does not rescan levels or compare the previous index against _numberOfPages. If a refresh shrank the list while retaining an out-of-range current page, repeated calls can move back toward a valid page. The index changes only after both UI updates succeed.

Number of row slots to update and the row capacity used to calculate full-list indices; normally items.Length.

remarks.para: For each row slot from 0 through maxItems − 1, it first deactivates items[slot], then reactivates it if the corresponding level index is below _totalScenes. That index is pageIdx × maxItems + slot: pageIdx is the zero-based requested page, maxItems is the number of row slots per page, and slot is the zero-based position inside that page. An occupied row receives the matching level crate’s Title; a level crate is the catalog record holding a level’s title. The title is written in text[slot].

For example, pageIdx 2 and maxItems 4 display list indices 8 through 11. If there are only ten selectable levels, the first two row objects are active and the last two are inactive. Labels on hidden rows are not cleared. Slots at or above maxItems are left untouched.

Provide a non-negative pageIdx and a maxItems value that fits the items array, with non-null row objects and matching text labels for occupied rows. Negative full-list indices and mismatched arrays are not safely handled. Normal calls use items.Length for maxItems; SelectItem also uses items.Length, so a different row capacity can make displayed rows and selected levels disagree. This routine does not store the requested page as _currentPage.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LevelsPanelView.UpdatePageText(System.Int32,System.Int32)

Total page count used in the label and the forward-navigation bound.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.ApplySettingsToAllLedgeLinks

Copies linkDepth (start-to-end spacing along local Z), edgeWidth (sideways hand spacing), edgeDepth (front/back edge offset), chestHeight (vertical chest offset) and chestDepth (forward chest placement). member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.CreateClimbBarObjects
member.summary: Rebuilds alternating hand-grab markers from the existing bar array and prepares a movable chest joint.

remarks.para: Uses barObjs in array order; it does not create the bars from climbingBarsPrefab. Replaces grabObjs with one empty marker per bar. Each marker starts at that bar’s origin, is reparented to rotaterParentObj while retaining its world position, then moves 0.1 local units up. Even array indices move right by edgeWidth; odd indices move left by edgeWidth.

Creates primary and secondary chest targets near edgeTarget: the first is chestHeight below and edgeDepth forward; the second is half chestHeight below and edgeDepth backward. chestHeight is a local vertical distance and edgeDepth is a local forward/back distance. Local X, Y and Z mean right, up and forward relative to rotaterParentObj, the parent of the generated markers. Distances are local Unity units, normally metres when the parent and link have scale 1. These markers tell traversal where to aim; creating them does not move an agent.
Existing marker GameObjects are destroyed immediately and replaced. Save any hand-edited positions before rebuilding, and use the new references afterward.
A physics joint is a connection that constrains or pulls bodies. This mover uses springs to pull the agent’s chest toward its target during bar traversal.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.CreateEdgeObjectsByType
member.summary: Rebuilds this link’s target hierarchy and chooses marker placement for its .

remarks.para: Refreshes allNavLinks from navigation-link components on this same GameObject, a scene object that holds components. A component is an attached part that supplies behavior or data. Checks only the first cached link against legAgentID, the navigation-agent type identifier. Only if it matches does the method record that first entry as the leg link and, when present, the second as the crab link. Destroys the old rotaterParentObj hierarchy, creates a new child with zero local position and rotation, and puts edgeTarget at local (0, edgeHeight, 0). edgeHeight is the edge’s height above the link origin in local units, normally metres at scale 1. Calls the marker builder for linkType; ESCALATOR only produces a diagnostic message here. This method does not run the ground raycasts or refresh start/end coordinates; run endpoint setup separately when needed. Rebuilding discards manual changes to generated children.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.CreateLaunchObjects
member.summary: Rebuilds launch aiming and chest markers from the leg navigation link’s endpoints.

remarks.para: Places launchTarget above edgeTarget by launchHeight, or restores its previously saved local position when ignoreLaunchTarget is enabled. Places primary and secondary chest targets at the leg navigation link’s local start and end, each raised by chestHeight. launchHeight and chestHeight are local vertical distances, normally metres at scale 1.

Also creates or repositions simLaunchObj at the navigation start for trajectory calculations, and overwrites crabJumpForce with twice edgeHeight, the edge’s local height. The crablet later treats that number as an aiming speed, so set your desired speed after rebuilding if necessary. Requires a leg navigation link; this method prepares markers and does not launch the player.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.CreateMoverJoint(System.Single,System.Single)
member.summary: Adds a physics body and a to the primary chest target so bar traversal can pull an agent along its route.

remarks.para: A Rigidbody is the component that gives an object a body in the physics simulation. This new body is kinematic, meaning the game controls its motion rather than letting forces move it freely. A ConfigurableJoint is a physics connection with adjustable movement rules. This joint locks turning and uses the same spring drive on all three movement axes.

A positive driveSForce is the spring strength in newtons per metre; a positive driveMForce is the maximum drive force in newtons. Each input that is zero or negative is replaced with 2500. Damping, which resists relative speed, is set to 100 newton-seconds per metre. For example, (500, 1000) creates a gentler spring with a 1000-newton force cap; (-1, -1) selects both defaults.
The joint initially has no connected body. The bar-climbing routine connects it to the agent’s chest later. This method adds new components each time; it does not update an existing joint.

member.param: Spring strength in newtons per metre. Zero or any negative value selects 2500.
Maximum drive force in newtons. Zero or any negative value selects 2500.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.CreateSlideObjects
member.summary: Rebuilds hand and chest markers for the two stages of an agent’s slide.

The primary chest target has local Y 0.5 and is 0.25 backward from the edge’s Z; the secondary chest target has local Y 0.5 and local Z 1.5.
