member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.CreateStartEndPoints
member.summary: Replaces the two markers from which endpoint setup casts downward to find the floor.

remarks.para: Creates startRayTarget and endRayTarget under rotaterParentObj. Their local positions are (0, edgeHeight + 1, linkDepth / 2) and (0, edgeHeight + 1, -linkDepth / 2). edgeHeight is the edge’s height above the link origin, and linkDepth is the spacing between the markers along local Z. At scale 1, these distances are metres.

For example, edgeHeight 4 and linkDepth 6 place both markers 5 units high, with Z coordinates +3 and -3. These are ray origins, not the final grounded start and end. This method creates the markers; SetStartEndPoints performs the floor checks. Previous marker objects are destroyed immediately.
Local X, Y and Z mean right, up and forward relative to rotaterParentObj, the parent of the generated markers.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.CreateZipObjects
member.summary: Rebuilds zipline chest markers and finds the zip manager and trigger when their references are missing.

remarks.para: The primary chest target is local (0, chestHeight, 0). A ZIPLINE_DOWN link also gets a secondary target at local (0, chestHeight, 1). chestHeight is a local vertical distance; one local unit forward normally means one metre at scale 1. Existing targets being rebuilt are destroyed immediately.

Looks for a ZipLinkManager in this object’s parent hierarchy and a GenGameControl_Trigger in its children if those cached references are absent. It prepares references and chest positions; it does not spawn a zip stick or attach a rider.

Local X, Y and Z mean right, up and forward relative to rotaterParentObj, the parent of the generated markers. The GenGameControl_Trigger component reports objects entering its volume. ZipLinkManager coordinates the group of zipline links; a component is an attached part that supplies behavior or data.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.DisplayMaxHeight
member.summary: Draws a debug height line for the last rising sample in the stored drag trajectory and logs launch timing estimates.

remarks.para: Initializes the selected index and height to Vector2.zero, or (0, 0), then scans the existing dragPositions starting with the pair at indices 1 and 2. Every strict increase in world Y replaces both values, so the result is the last rise found, which need not be the highest point. If no rise is found, the index remains 0 and height remains 0; the pelvis estimate therefore uses H = 0 rather than sample 0’s Y. Requires a nonempty sample array; it does not create new drag samples.

For a found rise, draws a debug line for 10 seconds from that sample to world Y = 0 at the same X/Z. With no rise, the selected sample is sample 0 but H = 0, so the line ends where it starts and has zero length. Logs the selected zero-based index and selected height in metres. Logs one flight-time estimate from simLaunchObj toward reverseObj, with arc-height input edgeHeight + launchHeight minus forwardObj’s local Y. Here edgeHeight is the configured edge height, launchHeight is extra launch height, and local Y is height relative to forwardObj’s parent; these local distances normally mean metres at scale 1. Logs another estimate from the player pelvis toward reverseObj, using the selected height (zero if no rise is found) as its H input. Both estimates are seconds calculated from positions and gravity, rather than measured flight durations; they do not prove the player will reach that height in the live physics simulation.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.DrawEditorPath
member.summary: Fills the ideal trajectory samples for a preview starting at simLaunchObj.

remarks.para: Calculates an ideal no-air-resistance launch from simLaunchObj’s world position toward reverseObj, using edgeHeight + launchHeight as the arc-height input. edgeHeight is the edge’s local height, launchHeight is extra height above it, and both are normally metres at scale 1.

Stores the calculated initial velocity and flight time, then fills positions with splineResolution + 1 world-position samples along the gravity curve. For example, resolution 10 produces 11 samples from the launch origin to the end of the estimated flight. This prepares the sample array; it does not itself launch the player or draw line segments.

The stored initial velocity is in metres per second and the estimated flight time is seconds. Each world-position sample is a point in the scene’s shared X/Y/Z coordinates, normally measured in metres, rather than a position relative to the launch object.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.DrawEditorPathWithPlayerBody
member.summary: Fills the ideal trajectory samples using the position of the player entity’s ninth stored body as the launch origin.

remarks.para: Uses body-list index 8, counting from zero, then calculates a no-air-resistance arc toward reverseObj. Requires the player entity and at least nine body entries. It uses that body’s position, not its dimensions or mass.

The arc-height input is edgeHeight + launchHeight: the edge’s local height plus extra height above it, normally metres at scale 1. Stores the initial velocity and flight time and creates splineResolution + 1 world-position samples in positions. It prepares preview data without launching the player.

The player entity is the container holding the player’s physics body parts. The stored initial velocity is metres per second and the flight-time estimate is seconds. The world-position samples use the scene’s shared X/Y/Z coordinates, normally in metres.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.FindMaxHeight
member.summary: Finds the last stored drag-trajectory sample whose world height is strictly above the preceding sample.

remarks.para: The first comparison is sample 1 to sample 2, so the rise from sample 0 to sample 1 is ignored. Each later strict rise replaces the result. A flat or descending pair does not. This is a last-rising-sample search, not a search for the greatest height.

The returned X is a zero-based array index stored as a float. Y is the selected sample’s world Y coordinate in metres. For heights [0, 1, 2, 1, 3], returns (4, 3). For [0, 5, 4], returns (0, 0), because the only rise is the ignored first pair. A non-null array with fewer than three entries also returns zero.

member.returns: A Vector2 containing (sample index, world height in metres), or (0, 0) when no checked pair rises. The dragPositions array must be assigned.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.FixedUpdate
member.summary: Adds a small forward impulse to the player’s physics bodies while corrective thrust is active.

remarks.para: FixedUpdate is Unity’s physics-step update. When applyCorrectiveThrust is false, this method does nothing. Otherwise it aims from the player pelvis toward the path sample two indices beyond lerpValInt, or the last positions sample if that look-ahead exceeds the array.

For each player Rigidbody, meaning a body in the physics simulation, applies an impulse of mass × thrustFactor × fixedDeltaTime along that world-space direction. Mass is in kilograms, thrustFactor acts as acceleration in metres per second squared, and fixedDeltaTime is the physics step in seconds. The impulse is in newton-seconds; the resulting velocity change is thrustFactor × fixedDeltaTime metres per second. For example, 0.1 with a 0.02-second step adds 0.002 m/s.

Uses the player bodies cached by LinkDataManager, not currLinkAgent. Requires valid player references and a populated positions array. The correction coroutine normally turns this flag on or off according to trajectory error; a coroutine is a routine that resumes its work over later frames.
lerpValInt is the zero-based index of the lower sample of the current path segment. The launch-monitoring coroutine selects it from elapsed flight progress; the look-ahead uses that index plus two.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.LaunchAudio(System.Boolean)
member.summary: Plays the shared launch clip at the forward or reverse launch object.

remarks.para: Both directions use LinkDataManager’s launchClip. isForw chooses the world position where the sound plays; it does not choose a different clip. Requires the manager and the selected launch object.

member.param: True plays at forwardObj; false plays at reverseObj.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.LaunchPlayer
member.summary: Requests a computed launch velocity change for the player, then notifies launch listeners and starts optional path correction.

remarks.para: Returns immediately while the stored cooldown deadline is still in the future, when this link’s GameObject is inactive in its hierarchy, or when the player entity is missing. For an accepted launch, sets the next deadline to current game time plus coolDownDuration, measured in seconds, before applying forces.

Chooses a direction from the player pelvis’s signed position along the link’s forward axis. With applyDragForce enabled, a positive side value selects forwardObj and a zero or negative value selects reverseObj; scene placement determines the actual travel direction. The method calculates a target-aware velocity toward the selected object and multiplies its vertical and horizontal parts by the player drag-compensation settings. With it disabled, calculates an arc toward launchTarget, adds a forward/back velocity whose speed numerically equals one third of linkDepth in m/s, and multiplies by launchForceMult. linkDepth is the local start/end spacing, normally metres at scale 1; launchForceMult is a unitless velocity multiplier.

Subtracts the rig’s tracked current velocity to form the world-space velocity change, in metres per second. The drag-compensation branch requests each body’s mass times that change as an impulse; mass is kilograms and impulse is newton-seconds, meaning a one-off push. The other branch requests the change directly using Unity’s VelocityChange force mode, which applies a speed change independently of body mass. These calls request a physics change; their effects are processed during a later physics simulation, so they do not establish that motion has already changed when listeners run. A body without an attached physics Rigidbody can skip the request; a Rigidbody is the component that gives an object a body in the physics simulation.

After all initial body-force calls, invokes OnLaunchAction with that velocity change. A callback is a function registered to run at this point. The cooldown has already been set; restarting the optional correction coroutine and final launch audio happen afterward. Path-order reversal, when required, has already happened before the callback. Skipped launches do not invoke it. A coroutine is a routine that resumes over later frames; this one compares the player with stored ideal path samples and controls corrective thrust. It does not guarantee a successful landing.

The player rig groups the controllers for movement and body parts. Its player entity is the container holding those physics bodies. The world velocity change uses the scene’s shared X/Y/Z directions, with Y upward.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.OffsetBarGrabObjects
member.summary: Moves existing bar-grab markers sideways, alternating right and left in array order.

remarks.para: Adds edgeWidth to local X at even zero-based indices and subtracts it at odd indices. Leaves local Y/Z unchanged. edgeWidth is a local distance, normally metres with scale 1; X is measured relative to each marker’s parent.

This adds to each marker’s current position. For example, two calls with edgeWidth 0.5 move an even-index marker 1 unit farther right. Use rebuilding when you need fresh positions rather than repeated accumulated offsets.
Local X, Y and Z mean right, up and forward relative to each marker’s current parent. The builder normally puts these markers under rotaterParentObj.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.OnZipOccupied

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.PlayerAttack

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.ReleaseLink

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.RotateLinkTargets(System.Boolean)
member.summary: Sets the generated target parent to the forward or reverse orientation of a bidirectional link.

remarks.para: Requires an assigned leg navigation link. With an existing one-way link, logs an error and leaves the targets unchanged; a missing reference instead fails. bidirectional means the navigation shortcut can be crossed in both directions. Sets rotaterParentObj’s local rotation to zero for forward, or 180 degrees around local Y for reverse. Local Y is the parent’s up axis.
This is an absolute choice of orientation: calling reverse twice still gives 180 degrees. It rotates child markers but does not exchange navigation endpoints.

member.param: True sets zero local rotation; false sets a 180-degree turn around the parent’s up axis.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.SetExplicitStartAndEndLaunchPoints
member.summary: Uses the placed launch objects as navigation endpoints and moves the link origin between them.

remarks.para: Reads forwardObj and reverseObj in world space. Sets linkDepth to their horizontal X/Z distance, ignoring height difference. Temporarily detaches forwardObj’s parent scene object, moves this link’s origin to the horizontal midpoint at forwardObj’s height, then reparents that parent object under this link. This can change the positions of other children of the moved link.

Places simLaunchObj at the forward object and updates every cached navigation link with the launch objects’ positions converted into this link’s local coordinates. Positions and horizontal distance normally use metres at scale 1.

It does not refresh startPoint, endPoint, startPosLocal or endPosLocal. Those separate cached coordinates come from SetStartEndPoints and can remain from an earlier setup. Requires both launch objects and the cached navigation-link array.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.SetStartEndPoints
member.summary: Finds ground below the endpoint markers and copies the resulting positions into the cached navigation links.

remarks.para: Creates ray markers if the start marker is missing. From each marker’s world position casts a ray, an imaginary line used to test collisions, straight down along world Y for up to 100 metres. startEndLayermask chooses which collision layers count as floor. A collision layer groups scene objects; this mask selects the groups the ray can hit.

A successful hit stores the world position in startPoint or endPoint and its link-local equivalent in startPosLocal or endPosLocal. A missed ray leaves that endpoint’s previous cached coordinates intact. Copies those local coordinates to every entry in allNavLinks, so missed rays can preserve an old endpoint.

For a LAUNCH link, also places each existing launch object at its cached local endpoint and an existing simLaunchObj at the start. Each assigned automatic trigger object gets local position (0, 1, 0), meaning one unit above its own parent, normally one metre at scale 1.

A navigation link is an AI route shortcut between two positions. Its local endpoints are measured relative to this link’s position, rotation and scale; the grounded world endpoints use the scene’s shared coordinates.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.SubToPlayerJump(System.Boolean)
member.summary: Adds or removes LaunchPlayer as a listener for the player’s jump event.

remarks.para: An event listener is a function called when the event happens. Enabling registers LaunchPlayer with RemapRig.onPlayerJump through RigManager.remapHeptaRig; disabling removes it. RigManager groups the player’s controllers, and RemapRig translates movement input into player movement. This event passes no arguments. When jumping is enabled, RemapRig.Jump sends the notification before setting its jump-in-progress state and stage, so the notification does not prove the player is already airborne or has finished jumping. The isSubbedToJump flag prevents repeated enable calls from adding duplicate registrations and repeated disable calls from removing again.

Changes the subscription, not the pad’s lamps or objects. Each later jump still goes through LaunchPlayer’s cooldown and active-object checks. Turning a pad on with ToggleLaunchPadLink does not automatically make this subscription.

member.param: True subscribes LaunchPlayer to jumps; false removes that subscription.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.TelePlayerToLinkEnd
member.summary: Moves the player rig and all stored body-part transforms to reverseObj’s world position.

remarks.para: Debug helper that uses the placed reverseObj, rather than the cached startPoint/endPoint. Returns when the rig manager is absent.

Sets the physics rig transform and every body-part transform to the same point. It does not preserve their relative body offsets or clear their velocities in this method, so it can initially bunch the body parts together. Requires the target object and a valid player entity/body list.

The player rig groups the controllers for movement and body parts. A transform stores an object’s position, rotation and scale. These world positions use the scene’s shared X/Y/Z coordinates, normally in metres; the player entity is the container holding the physics body parts.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.TelePlayerToLinkStart
member.summary: Moves the player rig and all stored body-part transforms to forwardObj’s world position.

remarks.para: Debug helper that uses the placed forwardObj, rather than the cached startPoint/endPoint. Returns when the rig manager is absent.

Sets the physics rig transform and every body-part transform to the same point. It does not preserve their relative body offsets or clear their velocities in this method, so it can initially bunch the body parts together. Requires the target object and a valid player entity/body list.

The player rig groups the controllers for movement and body parts. A transform stores an object’s position, rotation and scale. These world positions use the scene’s shared X/Y/Z coordinates, normally in metres; the player entity is the container holding the physics body parts.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.ToggleBiDirectional
member.summary: Switches every cached navigation link between one-way and two-way traversal and shows or hides the reverse object.

remarks.para: Uses the leg navigation link’s current bidirectional value to choose the opposite value for allNavLinks. When switching to two-way, activates reverseObj if present; when switching to one-way, deactivates it. A navigation link is an AI route shortcut; two-way allows crossing it in either direction.
Does not rotate target markers or change endpoint coordinates. Requires the leg navigation link and cached array.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.ToggleLaunchPadLink(System.Boolean)
member.summary: Changes the pad’s lamps, configured objects, trigger colliders and power sounds to the requested state.

remarks.para: Assigns brightLampMat when enabled or darkLampMat when disabled to both lamp-ring renderers. Enables/disables the configured forward objects and trigger colliders, and plays forward power sounds. Updates the reverse-side objects, colliders and sounds only when the leg navigation link is bidirectional. A collider is a shape the physics system uses to detect contact.

Disabling first removes the player-jump subscription, after changing the lamp materials. Enabling does not subscribe to player jumps; use SubToPlayerJump for that. This call does not launch a player or enable/disable the navigation links themselves. LaunchPlayer called directly still uses its own active-object and cooldown checks.

A material defines a surface’s appearance; a renderer draws that surface. bidirectional means a two-way navigation shortcut. Both lamp-ring renderers and the leg navigation link must be assigned. member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.TogglePlayerTarget(System.Boolean)
member.summary: Shows or hides the player-target marker chosen by which side of the link the player’s pelvis is on, plus the launch-direction guide.

remarks.para: Tests the player pelvis against the link’s forward axis. A negative side value chooses playerTargForwObj; zero or positive chooses playerTargRevObj. Only that selected marker is toggled. The side comparison does not establish where either marker is placed in the scene. It does not change both markers together.

Positions the shared launch helper at the cached startPoint or endPoint, raised 0.01 metre in world Y, and sets its line from that endpoint toward launchTarget. Toggles the helper and plays the manager’s enable/disable target clip at the pelvis. Requires the player/manager, chosen marker and helper references. These are launch-direction guides; this method does not calculate a new landing point.

The side value subtracts the link’s world position from the pelvis’s world position, then takes the amount along the link’s forward direction. With a unit forward direction, it is signed distance in metres: negative is behind the link origin, positive is in front, and zero is on the dividing plane. It measures position, rather than which way the player is facing.

member.param: True shows the selected side’s marker and launch helper; false hides them.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.ToggleReversePositionArray
member.summary: Reverses the positions trajectory array in place and flips its reversed-state flag.

remarks.para: For samples [A, B, C], the same array becomes [C, B, A], so users of this array read the opposite order. Sets isPosArrayReversed to the opposite of its previous value. Requires positions to be assigned.
Only positions is reversed. dragPositions and the navigation endpoints are unchanged. The player launch routine uses this to orient the ideal samples for corrective thrust.

positions contains the ideal no-air-resistance trajectory samples used by correction. Each sample is a point in the scene’s shared world X/Y/Z coordinates, normally in metres. Reversing changes sample order without changing the coordinates of any sample.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.UpdateMoverJointDrive(System.Single,System.Single)
member.summary: Replaces the existing mover joint’s spring strength and force cap on all three movement axes.

remarks.para: A physics joint is a connection that constrains or pulls bodies. driveSForce is its spring strength in newtons per metre, and driveMForce is its maximum force in newtons. Keeps the stored damping value, which resists relative speed and is measured in newton-seconds per metre, and reapplies the updated drive to X, Y and Z.

Both arguments are written directly. There is no keep-current or default sentinel: passing -1 stores -1. For example, (500, 1000) sets a 500-newton-per-metre spring and 1000-newton force cap. Requires linkJoint to have been created.

member.param: Replacement spring strength in newtons per metre; the value is stored directly.
Replacement maximum force in newtons; the value is stored directly.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.MineCartControl.UpdateSpeed(System.Int32)
member.summary: Selects a ride preset and sends its target velocity, damping and force limit to splineBody.
member.param: Preset index, using the RideSpeed values 0 through 8.

remarks.para: The target is signed meters per second (m/s) along the contact joint’s track-oriented X direction, so its sign follows that joint’s orientation rather than a fixed direction in the scene. Damping sets how much motor force responds to each m/s of difference between target and actual speed, in newton-seconds per meter (N·s/m). The force setting caps each contact motor in newtons (N).

The preset indexes are 0 Off, 1 Station, 2 Lift, 3 Coast, 4 Brake, 5 Boost, 6 SuperBoost, 7 MatchSpeed1 and 8 MatchSpeed2. rideSpeed is stored first; a recognized index then copies its three preset fields into velocity_current, damper_current and force_current. The spline body’s velocity setter runs next, followed by its damping setter and finally its maximum-force setter.

Each spline setter stores the input, marks its drive settings changed and wakes its Rigidbody, the object’s simulated physical body. SplineJoint applies those settings to the contact joints on an eligible physics update. A joint is a physics connection; its motor tries to reach the target velocity rather than instantly setting the cart’s actual speed.

Changing a preset field or rideSpeed directly does not run this application. Call UpdateSpeed again, even with the same valid index, to copy edited preset values. Configure splineBody and its Rigidbody before applying a preset.

An index outside 0 through 8 is still stored in rideSpeed, but leaves the three current caches unchanged and sends those old cached settings to splineBody. It does not reject or clamp the index. Use a declared preset index to select new settings.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.MineCartControl.UpdateSpeedOneShot(System.Int32)
member.summary: Applies the requested ride preset once while hasShot is false, then locks this trigger until that flag is cleared.
member.param: Preset index to apply, rather than a target speed in meters per second.

remarks.para: If hasShot is already true, the routine returns without changing the ride. Otherwise it calls UpdateSpeed with the supplied preset index and sets hasShot true only after that call returns. A failed application that throws before returning does not reach the flag write.

The index mapping is 0 Off, 1 Station, 2 Lift, 3 Coast, 4 Brake, 5 Boost, 6 SuperBoost, 7 MatchSpeed1 and 8 MatchSpeed2. This trigger can choose any of those presets; its name does not restrict it to a MatchSpeed preset. An out-of-range index still reapplies the old current caches through UpdateSpeed and consumes this trigger if the call returns.

The two trigger flags are independent: hasShot2 does not block this routine. Clear hasShot to allow another use. Calling ordinary UpdateSpeed does not reset either flag, and clearing the flag alone does not change the current drive settings.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.MineCartLapBar.LockBar
member.summary: With cj.swapBodies disabled, this method makes the lap bar’s joint motor strongly hold its current rotation, then runs OnBarLocked; when enabled, the helper exchanges the target and reference rotations.

remarks.para: The physics joint is the connection that controls how the bar can move. This method reads the joint object’s current local rotation, meaning its orientation relative to its parent object. With cj.swapBodies disabled, it sets that rotation as the motor target and uses the local rotation saved during Start, Unity’s setup call before the first update, as the reference. When cj.swapBodies is enabled, the helper exchanges those target and reference inputs before writing the joint target.

It replaces the joint’s angular X drive with spring strength 100,000,000, damping 1,000 and maximum torque 10,000,000 N·m. Angular X means twisting around the joint’s configured primary axis; that axis need not point along the scene’s X direction. Spring strength means how strongly the motor corrects an angle error, and damping means how strongly it resists turning away from the desired motion. For an angular force drive, spring units are N·m per radian, damping units are N·m per (radian per second), and the torque cap is in N·m. Torque is turning force; one radian is about 57.3 degrees.

OnBarLocked runs after the target and drive settings have been written. It passes no arguments and does not wait for physics to settle. Calling LockBar twice reads the rotation twice and fires the event twice. The method does not check lockAngle; for example, with cj.swapBodies disabled, an explicit call while the bar is partly raised holds that partly raised orientation.

Assign a valid cj and let Start save its initial rotation before calling this method. The joint must be configured to use its local target and angular X drive. Joint limits and the available torque still affect movement; this motor hold does not change the joint’s motion setting to Locked.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.MineCartLapBar.UnlockBar
member.summary: Changes the lap bar to a gentler joint motor drive and runs OnBarUnlocked.

remarks.para: This method changes the motor target with two rotations: it supplies the local rotation saved during Start, Unity’s setup call before the first update, first and the joint object’s current local rotation second. With cj.swapBodies disabled, these are the requested orientation and reference, respectively; when enabled, the helper exchanges those roles. Local means relative to the object’s parent. The target and reference roles are reversed from LockBar when cj.swapBodies is disabled. The joint helper converts them into the joint’s own target frame; this does not directly set the bar’s visible rotation or guarantee an exact final open angle.

It replaces the angular X drive, the motor for twisting around the joint’s configured primary axis, with spring strength 100,000, damping 100 and maximum torque 50 N·m. Spring strength means how strongly the motor corrects an angle error, and damping means how strongly it resists turning away from the desired motion. For an angular force drive, spring units are N·m per radian, damping units are N·m per (radian per second), and the torque cap is in N·m. Torque is turning force; one radian is about 57.3 degrees.

OnBarUnlocked runs after these settings are written, with no arguments. It announces the unlock command; it does not report that the bar has finished moving. Repeated calls fire the event again. The lower torque cap lets outside forces oppose this drive more easily than the locked drive.

This method does not stop an angle-checking routine that is still running. If the player is still registered with the seat and the next sampled twist meets lockAngle, that routine can call LockBar again. Unseating stops the routine, but does not itself call UnlockBar. A valid cj and the startup rotation cache are required.

A physics joint is the simulated connection that controls how the bar can move. The checker compares the Servo’s signed turning angle in degrees around its joint’s configured primary axis, the direction around which twist is measured, with lockAngle, the threshold in degrees. The angle is measured against the reference set during Servo initialization, relative to the connected physics body when present, otherwise fixed in the world. A physics body is an object whose motion Unity simulates.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.NooseBonelabIntro.AttachNeck
member.summary: Connects the player’s physical chest to the noose knot, disables three noose grab points, and starts the Reeling stage.

remarks.para: Creates a ConfigurableJoint, a physics connection that limits how far two objects can move apart and pulls them toward a target. It is added to the chest body and connected to knotRb. The chest anchor is at its center; the knot anchor is 11.6 cm along the knot’s negative local X axis and 0.4 cm along its negative local Z axis. These directions turn with the knot.

Sets a 20 cm movement limit, installs spring and movement drives, chooses a left or right target, and plays noosePutOn. It forcibly releases and disables interaction on grab points 6, 7, and 8 in the host manager’s list. The scene therefore needs those nine grab points in the expected order.

After setup it changes _nooseStage to Reeling and sets _nooseTimer to the current game time plus one second. Update normally calls this when its initial head-position check passes. This method itself does not check the current stage or prevent an additional joint from being created if called again.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.NooseBonelabIntro.CheckAndSetTargetSide
member.summary: Moves the chest-to-knot joint’s target to the left or right as the knot crosses the chest.

remarks.para: Measures the knot’s anchor position relative to the physical chest, then expresses that displacement in the virtual chest’s orientation. X is sideways: negative X selects the left target and positive X selects the right target. The knot anchor is its position plus its rotated local offset of (-0.116, 0, -0.004) meters.

Switches from right to left only below -0.02 meters, and from left to right only above +0.02 meters. Within that 4 cm band it keeps the previous side, preventing rapid switching near the center. It sets the joint target to (-0.2, 0, 0.2) meters for left or (0.2, 0, 0.2) meters for right. These are the physics joint’s target coordinates, not absolute world positions; it does not exchange the rope-body references.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.NooseBonelabIntro.CheckReel
member.summary: Measures the distance from the physical chest to the middle of the noose’s two side points.

remarks.para: For each side body, the measured point is its world position plus an 8 cm offset along that body’s negative local X direction. It averages those two points and measures the full three-dimensional distance to the chest, in meters. This measures separation, not pulling force or speed.
The Reeling stage finishes when this distance is strictly below 0.1 meters, or when its one-second deadline has passed. A result of 0.08 therefore means an 8 cm separation.

member.returns: Distance in meters between the side-point midpoint and the player’s physical chest.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.NooseBonelabIntro.CheckRelativeToHead
member.summary: Checks whether the noose’s position and tilt are suitable for attaching it to the player’s chest.

remarks.para: Builds a plane through fixed anchor points on the knot and the two side bodies. A plane is an imaginary flat surface; here it describes the noose’s orientation. The points use offsets of (-0.116, 0, -0.004) meters on the knot and (-0.08, 0, 0) meters on each side body, rotated with their bodies.

The combined sideways-and-forward distance from the physical chest to the midpoint of the two side anchors must be at most 8 cm. The midpoint must also be between 10 cm below and 12 cm above the chest. These distances use the physical head’s orientation: X is sideways, Z is forward/backward, and Y is up/down. The noose plane’s normal, its perpendicular direction, must have an absolute dot product of at least 0.707 with the head’s up direction. This accepts normals within roughly 45 degrees of either the head’s up or down direction.
This is a geometric proximity test. It does not detect whether the rope mesh truly surrounds the head or whether a collision occurred. Update uses a successful check to call AttachNeck.

member.returns: True when the side-anchor midpoint and noose plane pass the attachment position and tilt checks.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.NooseBonelabIntro.HangingSequence
member.summary: Releases the platform joints one at a time, then enables hanging damage and invokes the dagger cue.

remarks.para: At each reached _nooseTimer deadline, sets the next armPlatformJoints entry’s X-axis angular movement to Free, letting that connection rotate without an X-angle limit. It processes entries 0 through 6, one per call, and schedules the next deadline as the current game time plus plankDropTimer seconds. Even a zero delay does not release all seven entries in one call.

On the following call at step 7, increments _stageInt to 8, sets _isHanging to true, and then invokes daggerSpawnEvent with no arguments. Listeners therefore observe the new step and hanging flag. The event is a cue; this method does not spawn or reveal the dagger itself.

Requires seven non-null platform joints and does not check that _nooseStage is Hanging. Update normally performs this sequence within that stage, then separately applies choking damage when its force and time conditions pass. This method alone does not deal damage.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.NooseBonelabIntro.LoadFXAndLevel
member.summary: Creates the delayed death sequence that invokes nooseDeath, requests a fade effect, and arranges to reload the current scene after the fade.

remarks.para: Returns a coroutine: a sequence that pauses and continues over several frames. Creating it does not run the sequence; Unity must start it. Update starts it once when hanging health is at or below zero, setting _skipUpdate first to prevent duplicate starts.

First waits pH.deathTimeAmount seconds, the health component’s configured delay for the player’s last chance before death. Then invokes nooseDeath with no arguments and waits another three seconds. These are waits in game time, so the actual resume occurs on a later frame rather than at an exact instant.

After both waits, requests the game’s default fadeout effect only if pH.curr_Health is exactly zero. Positive or negative health both end this sequence without that spawn request. When the effect’s object arrives, a callback, a routine run to report completion, adds LoadLevel to FadeVolume.onComplete. That later completion requests SceneStreamer.Reload for the current scene. The level field is not used to select another destination in this path.

member.returns: The coroutine to start for the delayed death event and fade/reload request.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.NooseBonelabIntro.LockedNeck
member.summary: Keeps the knot’s left/right target current, then starts the cutscene and platform-release stage after the reveal delay.

remarks.para: When game time is strictly later than _nooseTimer, sets _nooseStage to Hanging, resets _stageInt to 0, and sets the first platform-release deadline to the current time plus sceneRevealToPlankDrop seconds. It then invokes nooseOnAndHeldEvent with no arguments before starting and enabling introCutscene.

The event’s listeners see the new Hanging stage and deadline while _isHanging has not yet been set by the release sequence. No held-hand check occurs here despite the event’s name. The normal Update loop performs the same handling while Locked; this helper itself does not check the current stage.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.NooseBonelabIntro.ManualHideDagger
member.summary: Requests that daggerEntity be hidden.

remarks.para: Uses the entity’s normal hide request, without forcing its GameObject inactive immediately. The entity manager applies the request through its normal update path, so calling this is not proof that the dagger has already disappeared. It does not cut a joint, reset the dagger’s pose, or change the noose stage.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.NooseBonelabIntro.NooseChoke
member.summary: Starts the choking audio loop on the first call, and requests that it stop on later calls.

remarks.para: The first call passes nooseChoke to nooseChokePlayer, using nooseChokePoint as the parent transform and that point’s localPosition as the audio offset. A local position is measured in a parent’s axes; here that value is reused as an offset relative to the point itself.

Sets hasChokePlayed to true after issuing the loop request. Subsequent calls stop the managed audio player but leave that flag true, so another call does not restart the loop unless the flag is cleared separately. ResetNoose and re-enabling this component do not clear the flag in the inspected class.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.NooseBonelabIntro.NooseCut
member.summary: Releases the chest from the noose during the Hanging stage, disables noose grabs and collisions, and invokes nooseCutEvent.

remarks.para: Does nothing unless _nooseStage is Hanging; it does not require _isHanging to be true. Plays nooseCut at this component’s world position, releases all held noose grab points, disables their interaction and collisions, and requests destruction of the chest-to-knot joint before clearing its reference.

Sets a deadline five game seconds ahead, changes the knot’s mass to 2 kilograms, and sets the stage to Cut. It then calls the dagger joint’s cut helper, requests the falling-wind sound, and invokes nooseCutEvent with no arguments. Listeners see Cut and a cleared chest-joint reference, but _isHanging is not cleared until later Update cleanup.

Recovery runs on a later eligible Update in Cut, after scene streaming reports DONE and a player rig is available. If _skipUpdate is true, that Update first stops this component’s coroutines, sequences that can pause and continue on later frames, requests full health, and clears _skipUpdate. When game time is strictly beyond the five-second deadline and _nooseBool is false, it then stops and disables the cutscene, clears _isHanging, sets _nooseBool true, and requests hiding of the dagger followed by the gallows. NooseCut itself does not perform this later recovery or clear the retained _nooseBool latch.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.NooseBonelabIntro.ReelingNeck
member.summary: Pulls the chest and knot together during Reeling, then switches to Locked when they are close enough or the deadline passes.

remarks.para: Updates the knot’s left/right target. While the side-anchor midpoint is at least 10 cm from the physical chest and game time has not passed _nooseTimer, increases the connection’s spring strength each frame and sets its damping, resistance to motion, to one tenth of that strength.

When the separation is strictly below 10 cm or the deadline has passed, clears that limit spring’s strength and damping, sets _nooseStage to Locked, changes the knot’s mass to 30 kilograms, and schedules _nooseTimer for the current time plus nooseOnToSceneReveal seconds. It invokes nooseOnEvent afterward with no arguments. The installed movement drives remain separate from the limit spring being cleared.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.NooseBonelabIntro.ResetNoose
member.summary: Attempts to release the hanging noose and restore the cached platform and dagger poses; it only runs from the Hanging stage.

remarks.para: Plays the cut sound, detaches noose grabs, requests destruction of the chest connection, cuts the dagger connection, then switches to Initial and re-enables noose collisions and interaction. Restores world rotations for platform joints 0 through 4 and returns those five X-axis angular limits to Limited. It does not restore entries 5 and 6 that HangingSequence can release.

Restores the dagger’s cached world position and rotation, clears its movement and spinning velocity, and requests hiding it. The pose caches are recorded in OnEnable, Unity’s callback when this component becomes enabled, after any reset attempted there. The final cutscene command would stop playback while leaving its object enabled.

This is not a complete reset of the sequence: it does not clear _isHanging, _nooseBool, _skipUpdate, _stageInt, the damage-time accumulator, hasChokePlayed, or torchSpawned. It also calls the dagger cut helper twice. If the first call successfully clears that helper’s joint reference, the second can fail on the now-missing reference before the final cutscene command. Do not rely on this method alone to make the entire intro ready to repeat.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.NooseBonelabIntro.Update
member.summary: Advances the noose intro through attachment, reeling, reveal, platform release, choking damage, and cut cleanup. Hanging damage requests health points per qualifying tick using the time threshold.

remarks.para: Unity calls this once per rendered frame. It waits for scene streaming to report DONE and for a player rig to be available. If rM is missing, it obtains the current player rig and its Player_Health component. Initial checks attachment geometry; Reeling tightens the chest connection; Locked waits for reveal; Hanging releases the platform joints and handles damage; Cut handles recovery and hiding.

Once _isHanging is true in the Hanging stage, adds this frame’s game-time duration to _timeSinceLastDamageTick. A tick requires the chest joint’s upward world-space force to exceed half the avatar’s calculated weight and the timer to be strictly greater than damageTickRate. Weight here is massTotal kilograms multiplied by 9.81 meters per second squared, giving newtons; massTotal is the avatar’s cached total mass. It passes damagePerTick health points to pH.TAKEDAMAGE and resets the timer after that call.

After the possible tick, resets the timer whenever upward joint force is 500 newtons or less. A force below half the avatar’s weight does not itself reset the timer if it remains above 500 newtons. At most one tick occurs per frame; excess elapsed time is discarded instead of producing missed ticks.

Health at or below zero starts the delayed death/fade sequence once, with _skipUpdate set before it starts. _skipUpdate does not stop this Update method. If the rope enters Cut while that sequence is pending, Update stops this component’s coroutines, sequences that continue across frames, restores full health, and clears _skipUpdate before its delayed cut cleanup.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PageItem.#ctor(System.String,Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PageItem.Directions,Il2CppSystem.Action)
member.summary: Creates the data for a radial-menu choice, storing its label, menu slot, and action to run when triggered.

remarks.para: A radial menu arranges choices around a circle. n is the text shown for this choice, and d selects one of the eight named menu slots. c is a callback: a function saved so the item can call it later, without passing any arguments. Constructing the item stores these values; add it to a Page and render that page to display it.

The constructor does not run c. Invoke or a menu view's trigger runs the stored action later. Passing null for c creates an item that does nothing when invoked. For example, an item named "Inventory" in the NORTH slot can save a function that opens your inventory; that function determines the actual result.

member.param: Label text copied into the menu button when the page is rendered, such as "Inventory".
Named slot in the radial menu, such as NORTH or EAST; PageView uses it to choose the matching button.
Saved function to call when triggered, with no arguments. null means there is no action to run.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PageItem.Invoke
member.summary: Calls the item's currently stored action immediately, if one is assigned.

remarks.para: The action is a callback: a function saved in m_Callback for later use. It receives no arguments. If m_Callback is null, Invoke returns without doing anything. This call does not check whether the item is visible or selected, so calling it yourself runs the action directly.

Each call can run the action again; Invoke does not clear it or mark the item as already used. The callback runs during this call. Any delayed work that the callback starts follows that work's own timing. For example, invoking a choice whose callback opens a menu runs that opening function now.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PageView.Activate
member.summary: Opens an inactive page view, or invokes the selected item when the view is already marked active.

remarks.para: First it calls onActivated, passing this view, then enables its GameObject, the Unity scene object holding the component. The callback runs before those changes and runs on every Activate call. A callback is a function supplied by other code to run at this point; it is not a signal that the opening animation has finished.

When m_IsActivated is false, it renders the saved home page if one exists, sets that flag true, stops this component's coroutines and starts the summon animation, then enables TextCanvas. A coroutine is work that can continue over later frames. The opening sound and subtle controller vibration are requested by the summon routine.

When the flag is already true, this method invokes the selected item's action if available. If there is no selected button, it calls ShutOff instead. That branch does not perform Trigger's selection-sound and click-vibration step. Configure the buttons, audio placement, cancelButton and TextCanvas before using the view.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PageView.ChangePage(Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Page)
member.summary: Starts a sequence that closes the existing buttons before attempting to render and summon another page.

remarks.para: A coroutine is work that continues over later frames. ChangePage first stops every coroutine running on this component, then starts its page-change routine. The routine starts and waits for the close animation; its next step renders the supplied page and starts the summon animation.

This does not change the stored home page or set m_IsActivated. It also does not immediately display the new page. The close animation disables this view's GameObject before calling onDeactivated, so the page-change routine can be interrupted by that object becoming inactive. Do not treat a returned ChangePage call as proof that the new page has opened.

For example, use SetHomePage to replace the saved default page and render it immediately. Use the normal activation flow to reopen a view that has been disabled. The supplied page and its items list must be valid when the rendering step runs.

member.param: The page data to render, with a valid items list and directions supported by the configured buttons.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PageView.Clear
member.summary: Starts closing and removing the button data currently displayed by this view.

remarks.para: It stops all coroutines on this component and starts CoCloseAnimation, a routine whose work continues over later frames. Closing removes each button's stored PageItem, fades its visuals toward transparent and shrinks its local scale toward zero. When closing completes, it disables the view's GameObject and calls onDeactivated with this view.

Clear does not change the home-page reference, m_IsActivated or m_SelectedButton directly, and does not run Deactivate's cancel-indicator and text-clearing steps. It requests visual closing rather than making all of the view's logical state inactive at once. For example, a caller can still read the old activation flag while the closing routine runs.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PageView.CoCloseAnimation
member.summary: Creates a coroutine that fades and shrinks the buttons, then disables the view and signals that closing has finished.

remarks.para: A coroutine is work that advances over later frames. Calling this method returns the routine; run it with StartCoroutine to perform the animation. At its first step, it clears every button's PageItem data and makes its segment colors alpha 0, meaning transparent. Active and enabled segment visuals are asked to fade; inactive or disabled visuals have transparent colors set immediately.

Each button receives a randomly chosen smoothing time from 0.02 to 0.1 seconds. Scale progress is unitless, starts at 0 and smoothly approaches 1 using elapsed frame time unaffected by game-speed changes; that progress blends local scale from (1, 1, 1) toward (0, 0, 0). Local scale is a unitless size multiplier relative to the object's parent, so 0.5 means half size along each axis. For active and enabled segment visuals, the color fade is requested with that smoothing time plus 0.01 seconds.

Closing waits until every button's progress reaches the stored 0.99 threshold, then explicitly sets every local scale to zero. These smoothing times are not exact total animation durations. It then disables the view's GameObject and invokes onDeactivated, passing this view. The routine does not set m_IsActivated or clear the cached selected-button reference.
This routine does not request the closing sound. ShutOff handles that sound and its vibration separately. The buttons array and its entries must be valid while the routine runs.

member.returns: A routine to run with StartCoroutine; creating it alone does not advance the animation.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PageView.CoSummonAnimation
member.summary: Creates a coroutine that requests opening feedback and grows the buttons to normal local scale.

remarks.para: A coroutine is work that advances over later frames. Calling this method returns the routine; run it with StartCoroutine to animate. Its first step requests clip_summon at audioPlacementOverride's world position and a subtle vibration through feedback_tactile and controller.

Each button receives a random smoothing time from 0.02 to 0.1 seconds. Scale progress smoothly approaches 1 using elapsed frame time unaffected by game-speed changes; that progress blends local scale from (0, 0, 0) to (1, 1, 1). Local scale is a unitless size multiplier relative to the object's parent. The button's own normal colors are restored, with a requested color-fade time equal to the smoothing time plus 0.01 seconds for active visual elements.

The routine keeps yielding another frame after the buttons approach full size. It has no normal finished-opening signal or completion threshold in this implementation. Activate, Deactivate, Clear and ChangePage can stop it through their coroutine management. Creating or running it alone does not set m_IsActivated or enable TextCanvas.

member.returns: A routine to run with StartCoroutine; creating it alone does not advance the animation.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PageView.Deactivate
member.summary: Marks the view inactive, clears selection and text, and starts closing if it was marked active.

remarks.para: When m_IsActivated is true, it stops this component's coroutines and starts CoCloseAnimation, work that can continue over later frames. It then requests a 0.15-second hide of the cancel indicator, sets m_IsActivated false, fades the selected button's cursor highlight over a requested 0.05 seconds if needed, clears m_SelectedButton and clears/hides the text canvas.

The view's GameObject can remain enabled while its buttons shrink. When the close animation completes, it disables the object and calls onDeactivated with this view. Deactivate does not request a closing sound; ShutOff supplies that feedback. If the flag was already false, it performs the selection/text cleanup without starting a new close routine.
The fade times are requested durations in seconds, not guarantees that everything finishes on a particular rendered frame. A valid cancelButton and TextCanvas are needed for this cleanup.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PageView.GetHomePage
member.summary: Returns the saved default page assigned by .

remarks.para: This reads the stored page reference without rendering or opening anything. It can return null if no home page has been assigned. Render and ChangePage can show another page without changing this reference, so it does not necessarily identify the content currently visible.

member.returns: The saved home-page reference, or null when none is assigned.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PageView.Render(Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Page)
member.summary: Replaces the button data and visible directional items using the supplied .

remarks.para: It first makes every configured button's segment colors transparent, clears its stored PageItem and disables that button object. It then walks page.items and fills the button slot matching each item's direction, assigns its name to the text label, shows the matching segment visuals and enables the button object.

Slots are indexed from 0: NORTH uses 0, NORTHEAST 1, EAST 2, SOUTHEAST 3, SOUTH 4, SOUTHWEST 5, WEST 6 and NORTHWEST 7. For example, an EAST item fills buttons[2]. Provide enough non-null slots for all directions the page uses, along with each button's required text and visual references. The page and its items list must be valid.

This renders data without changing the saved home page, m_IsActivated or m_SelectedButton, and without starting a summon animation. It also does not enable this view's GameObject or TextCanvas. Because selection is cached separately, an old selected reference can remain after its PageItem data has been cleared; update the cursor or deactivate the view before relying on that selection.

member.param: The page data to render, with a valid items list and directions supported by the configured buttons.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PageView.SetHomePage(Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Page)
member.summary: Stores the page to use when reopening the view and immediately renders that page's buttons.

remarks.para: The page reference is saved in m_HomePage, then passed to Render. It is not cloned: later rendering uses the same Page object and its items list. When Activate opens a view whose activation flag is false, it renders this saved page again if one exists.

This call does not activate the view, show TextCanvas or start an opening animation. Provide a valid page with an items list and configured button slots before calling it. For example, assigning a settings page replaces the buttons immediately while also making it the page used on the next normal opening.

member.param: The page data to render, with a valid items list and directions supported by the configured buttons.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PageView.ShutOff
member.summary: Requests closing feedback when allowed, then performs .

remarks.para: clip_closeDownFirstPlay starts true. When that flag is true, ShutOff changes it to false and skips both the closing sound and click vibration. When it is false, the method requests clip_closeDown at audioPlacementOverride's world position, requests a strong click vibration if feedback_tactile exists, and leaves the flag false.

It then calls Deactivate, which clears the activation flag, selection and text and can start closing over later frames. For example, the first ShutOff after construction is silent, while later calls can request closing feedback again; this is not a permanent play-once latch. The sound request uses feedback_audio and may not begin before this method returns.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PageView.Trigger
member.summary: Invokes the selected item's action if one exists, then requests selection sound and click vibration.

remarks.para: If m_SelectedButton is missing, it returns false without requesting feedback. Otherwise it calls the selected button's stored PageItem action when that action exists, then requests clip_select at audioPlacementOverride's world position and a strong click vibration through feedback_tactile if available.

A true result means that a selected button reference was present and the method reached its feedback-request path. This can be true even if that button has no PageItem data or action function. Audio can be skipped when feedback_audio or its required click array is unavailable, or it may still be waiting for an audio player; tactile feedback may be unavailable. True therefore does not prove that an item action, sound or vibration occurred. This method does not check m_IsActivated or whether the selected object is currently enabled, and does not itself close the page. For example, a rendered button without an action can still produce feedback and a true result.

member.returns: True when a selected button reference is present and the method reaches its feedback-request path; false when no selected button exists. True does not prove that an item action ran or that sound or vibration occurred.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PanelView.Activate
member.summary: Marks the panel active and turns on the Unity object that contains it.

remarks.para: This base implementation first sets the panel’s active flag to true, then enables its GameObject, the Unity object that holds the panel and its components. An inactive parent can still keep the panel from appearing on screen.

Active panels can record a trigger press and forward cursor input. For example, call Activate when opening a preferences page. Setting the active flag directly does not turn on the GameObject; this method performs both steps. Derived panel classes can add their own opening behavior.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PanelView.CloseMenu
member.summary: Asks the assigned to close its popup menu.

remarks.para: The popup menu clears its open state and calls the closing methods of its linked panels. Closing can include an animation, so each panel need not disappear at exactly the same moment. If no usable popup menu is assigned, this base method does nothing.
For example, a Close button on a preferences panel can call CloseMenu to close the surrounding menu. Assign popUpMenu to that menu first; the method does not search the panel’s parents to find one.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PanelView.Deactivate
member.summary: Marks the panel inactive and turns off the Unity object that contains it.

remarks.para: This base implementation first sets the panel’s active flag to false, then disables its GameObject, the Unity object that holds the panel and its components. The panel stops accepting new trigger presses and forwarding cursor input through the base methods.

For example, call Deactivate when switching away from a page. It does not clear a previously recorded trigger press or close the whole popup menu. Derived panels can add closing behavior, such as an animation before they call this base method.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PanelView.Trigger
member.summary: Records a pending cursor press when the panel is active, then returns false.

remarks.para: The base implementation sets a true-or-false pending-press flag only when the panel’s active flag is true. It does not click a button immediately. The next cursor update that finds a usable input module forwards the flag to that module and then clears it. The input module is the component that turns pointing and pressing into menu input.

Repeated Trigger calls before that forwarding step still record just one pending press. If the panel is inactive or no input module is available, cursor forwarding does not clear an already recorded press. Activating or deactivating the base panel does not clear it either.

For example, activate a page, call Trigger when its controller button is pressed, and keep updating the cursor. A false return does not mean that the press was rejected: the base method also returns false after recording it. Derived panels can replace this behavior.

member.returns: Always in the base implementation.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PlayerAvatarDecorator.Awake
member.summary: Registers the avatar override attempt with the current level-loading session during Unity initialization.

remarks.para: Awake is Unity’s initialization callback: a routine Unity calls while setting up this component. It registers OnLevelLoad with the current StreamSession, the object tracking this level’s loading. That notification is delivered when the session marks itself finished, after its player-spawning work.

If the session already reports finished, registration calls OnLevelLoad immediately instead of waiting for a future load. That routine still requires _hasSpawned to be true and preventSwap to be false. Awake does not populate _playerMarker, subscribe to its spawn notifications, or swap on its own without that check.
This registration requires an existing current loading session. OnDisable only removes the separate player-marker listener; it does not remove this level-load registration.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PlayerAvatarDecorator.OnDisable
member.summary: Stops this decorator from receiving spawn and despawn notifications from its configured player marker.

remarks.para: OnDisable is a Unity callback, a routine called when this component becomes disabled or its scene object becomes inactive. It unregisters this decorator from _playerMarker’s spawn-listener list. The marker must already be assigned.

It does not clear _hasSpawned or unregister the level-load routine added by Awake, Unity’s initialization callback. A later level-load notification can therefore still attempt an override using the retained readiness flag; preventSwap is the explicit check that blocks that attempt.
The marker removes one matching listener entry. If OnEnable was manually called repeatedly and added duplicate registrations, one call here leaves the other entries in place.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PlayerAvatarDecorator.OnEnable
member.summary: Registers for player-marker notifications and records whether that marker already has a spawned player.

remarks.para: OnEnable is a Unity callback, a routine called when this component becomes enabled on an active scene object. It first registers this decorator with _playerMarker so its OnSpawn and OnDespawn routines can update _hasSpawned.

If _hasSpawned is currently false, it then asks the marker whether a player has already spawned and sets the flag true when that lookup succeeds. A flag already true is left unchanged without another lookup. This is stored readiness, rather than a fresh check on every enable.

This routine does not change the avatar. OnSpawn only sets the readiness flag too; the automatic override attempt happens separately in OnLevelLoad. The marker reference must be assigned before enabling. The marker appends listeners without a duplicate check, so manually calling OnEnable repeatedly adds repeated registrations.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PlayerAvatarDecorator.OnLevelLoad
member.summary: Requests the configured avatar when the level-load notification arrives and the player is marked spawned.

remarks.para: This callback is a routine registered by Awake, Unity’s initialization routine, with the current level-loading session. It returns immediately when _hasSpawned is false or preventSwap is true.

Otherwise it reads overrideAvatar’s barcode, the identifier of the avatar asset package, and passes it to the current PlayerAvatarManager with avatar caching enabled. Caching lets the rig, the system that controls the player’s body, retain and reuse an avatar instance for that identifier. The manager checks whether the identifier is valid before starting its swap request.

The override reference and the current player references/avatar manager must exist. The swap can finish later while its assets load and the player rig processes the change; this routine does not wait for completion or check the returned result.
A later spawn notification only changes _hasSpawned. It does not repeat an override that was skipped because this level-load notification arrived before readiness.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PlayerAvatarDecorator.Reset
member.summary: Finds a PlayerMarker on this scene object or its parent hierarchy and stores it for later spawn notifications.

remarks.para: Reset is Unity’s editor setup callback: a routine called when first adding the component or choosing Reset in its Inspector menu. This implementation searches the component’s own GameObject, the scene object containing it, and then its parents for a PlayerMarker. It includes inactive parent objects.

The result replaces _playerMarker, including a missing result if no marker is found. It does not reset _hasSpawned, change overrideAvatar or preventSwap, or register any listeners. The stored marker is used later by OnEnable and OnDisable.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PlayerAvatarDecorator.SwapAvatar
member.summary: Requests a swap to overrideAvatar unless preventSwap is set.

remarks.para: Unlike OnLevelLoad, this helper does not check _hasSpawned. With preventSwap = false, it reads the configured avatar package’s barcode, its asset identifier, and asks the current PlayerAvatarManager to override the player’s avatar with caching enabled. Caching retains an avatar instance for reuse on a later request for the same identifier.

The manager rejects an invalid identifier before starting the swap. A valid identifier still needs its avatar package available to the asset system. The reference and current player references/avatar manager must exist; this helper does not treat missing references as a harmless skipped swap.

The request can continue while the asset loads and the player rig, the system that controls the player’s body, applies it. This helper does not wait for completion, inspect its success result, or modify _hasSpawned. Changing a field alone does not call this helper.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PlayerHealthDecorator.OnDestroy
member.summary: Removes one registration of this decorator's callback from the player's global death event.

remarks.para: OnSpawn connects PlayerDeath to that event. A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action; this one runs the configured OnPlayerDeath actions. Unity calls OnDestroy for destruction cleanup. A normal paired spawn and destruction removes its matching subscription, but repeated spawns can add duplicate callbacks. This cleanup removes only one matching subscription, so duplicates can remain after destruction. OnDisable does not perform this death-event cleanup.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PlayerHealthDecorator.OnDisable
member.summary: Removes one spawn-listener registration from the assigned marker when Unity disables this component.

remarks.para: In the normal paired enable/disable lifecycle, this removes the marker registration added on enable. Repeated manual OnEnable calls add duplicate registrations, and OnDisable removes only one, so duplicates can remain and still report spawns while the decorator is disabled. This does not restore the player's previous health settings or disconnect an existing death callback, a routine called to report the player's death. If this decorator has already handled a spawn, its OnPlayerDeath actions can still run while the component is disabled. The player marker must be assigned.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PlayerHealthDecorator.OnEnable
member.summary: Registers this decorator to configure the player when its marker reports a spawn.

remarks.para: Assign the player marker before enabling the component. Registration adds a listener; it does not immediately configure a player that already spawned. The settings are applied by OnSpawn when a later spawn notification arrives. Calling OnEnable repeatedly adds repeated registrations.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PlayerHealthDecorator.PlayerDeath
member.summary: Runs the actions configured in .

remarks.para: The decorator connects this method to the player's final-death event during OnSpawn. Calling it yourself runs those actions immediately; the method does not reduce health, kill the player, or reload the level by itself. The configured event must exist.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PlayerHealthDecorator.Reset
member.summary: Finds a player marker on this object or a parent and assigns it to the decorator.

remarks.para: The search includes inactive objects. Unity uses this when resetting the component in the editor. It only fills the marker reference; it does not apply health settings or connect spawn and death callbacks, routines registered to respond to spawning or dying.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PreferencesPanelView.PAGESELECT(System.Int32)
member.summary: Hides all configured page objects, then activates the page at the supplied valid index.

remarks.para: The pages array is the ordered list of Unity scene objects that hold the settings pages. Indices count from zero: 0 selects the first entry, 1 the second, and so on. For three pages, PAGESELECT(1) turns all three off first, then turns the second page object on.

The default argument is -1. Calling PAGESELECT() or PAGESELECT(-1) leaves every page off; this method does not substitute defaultPage. To select the configured opening page explicitly, pass defaultPage, provided it contains a valid index.

Use an index from 0 through pages.Length - 1, where pages.Length is the number of entries. Any negative index, or an index greater than pages.Length, simply leaves all pages off. An index exactly equal to pages.Length passes the first check and then fails the array bounds check, after the pages have already been turned off. For three entries, 3 is this failing boundary.

The array and every entry must exist. A missing entry stops the operation, so earlier pages may already be off. Activating a page object also requires its parent objects to be active for that page to appear in the scene.

member.param: Zero-based page index to activate; -1, including the omitted argument, hides all pages. A valid index is less than the number of entries.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PullCordDevice.AvatarTransformationSequence(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.AvatarCrateReference,System.Int32)
member.summary: Creates the timed sound, glyph-light, and particle sequence that requests a change to the supplied avatar.
member.param: Avatar crate to request after the animation.
Intended zero-based ending glyph choice, from 0 through 5; the default -1 is treated as 0.
member.returns: An unstarted animation sequence.

remarks.para: This returns a coroutine: a sequence that continues over several frames. Run the returned sequence with StartCoroutine, or use ForceAvatarChange, which starts and tracks it for you.

The sequence starts the core particles and activation sound, waits 0.2 seconds, advances the six glyph lights for a configured 2-second phase, plays the lock sound, then waits 0.5 seconds. It then hides the glyphs, plays the blast particles, stops the core particles, and calls SwapAvatar. Frame timing and asset loading can make the completed change take longer than these configured waits.

stopIndex only affects the glyph-light animation. avatarRef chooses the avatar independently. Values outside 0 through 5 are replaced with 0. The saved avatarTransformationSequence is cleared after the swap request, without waiting for the avatar-loading operation to finish.

The glyph choice is an intended ending choice. The timed loop changes glyphs only on its updates and does not assign a final glyph after that phase. If one update skips the last part of the phase, the previously selected glyph can remain until the later hide step.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PullCordDevice.BodyVitalsUpdateEvent
member.summary: Sets the device’s rotation relative to its parent to face the appropriate way for left- or right-handed use.

remarks.para: leftHanded selects local Euler angles (0, 180, 0) when true and (0, 0, 0) when false. These are degrees around the parent’s axes. The method replaces the entire local rotation, including any previous X or Z tilt; it does not add another 180-degree turn each time.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PullCordDevice.BreakWorldJoint
member.summary: Undocks the ball from its world anchor, refreshes the favorite-avatar previews, and starts returning the ball to the device.

remarks.para: A physics joint is a connection that limits an object’s movement. This destroys the extra worldJoint, restores ballJoint’s connected anchor to ballStartTrans expressed in the connected body’s local coordinates, and sets isBallInReceiver to false. It starts a normal, audible RetractBall sequence only if ballRetraction is null.
The preview refresh requests asset loads; it does not wait for every preview mesh to finish loading.

ballStartTrans is the transform marking the ball’s rest point. A transform stores an object’s position, rotation and size. The connected anchor is the joint’s attachment point on the connected physics body. InverseTransformPoint converts the rest point’s world position to a position relative to that body’s origin and axes, in meters, before that point is assigned.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PullCordDevice.BreakWorldJointHand
member.summary: Undocks the ball from its world anchor and refreshes favorite-avatar previews without starting a retraction.

remarks.para: It destroys worldJoint when one exists and sets isBallInReceiver to false. Unlike BreakWorldJoint, it does not restore ballJoint’s connected anchor or start RetractBall. The method itself does not check whether a hand is holding the ball. Preview mesh loads may finish later.

worldJoint is the extra physics connection that holds the ball at a fixed world position when docked. A physics connection limits the movement of the objects it joins; this one attaches to the world itself.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PullCordDevice.DisableBall
member.summary: Removes the ball’s cord joint, freezes and releases its grip, and hides the ball and cord visuals.

remarks.para: The method immediately destroys ballJoint, freezes ballHost, forces attached hands to detach, disables the grip, stops the core particles, and hides ballArt and ballLine. It then restores the host’s saved initial position and rotation relative to its parent.
It does not write ballShown itself. Normal callers update that bookkeeping flag separately; setting the flag alone also does not perform these changes.

ballJoint is the physics connection between the ball and the body slot: it limits how far the cord can extend and supplies the pull toward its target. Removing it removes those cord forces and limits. The grip is the component that lets a hand hold the ball.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PullCordDevice.EnableBall
member.summary: Recreates the ball’s cord joint and shows the ball, its colliders, and the cord so the player can grab it.

remarks.para: A joint connects objects in the physics simulation. This creates a new ballJoint on the grip object, applies the hand-joint configuration saved during Awake (Unity’s initialization callback), and connects it to the body Rigidbody in the cached slot. A Rigidbody is the component that lets physics move an object.

The ball is placed at ballStartTrans and given the connected body’s velocity at that point, so it begins moving with the player. The method starts the core particles, applies the minimum drive settings scaled by the current avatar’s upper-body strength multiplier, enables both grip colliders, and shows ballArt and ballLine.
The method does not set ballShown itself, and calling it repeatedly creates another joint each time. Normal Update calls it only when transitioning from hidden to shown.

A drive supplies a spring-like pulling force. Its three settings are spring strength in newtons per meter of position error, damping in newton-seconds per meter of velocity error, and maximum force in newtons. These settings are applied to each of the joint’s X, Y and Z movement axes. The avatar’s upper-body strength multiplier is unitless and multiplies all three settings. Grip colliders are the two contact shapes that let physics detect contact with the ball. Enabling them makes those shapes participate in contact detection; ballArt supplies the visible object.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PullCordDevice.ForceAvatarChange(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.AvatarCrateReference,System.Int32)
member.summary: Starts the animated Body Log change to a supplied avatar without requiring the player to pull and release the cord.
member.param: Avatar crate to request after the effect sequence.
Zero-based cosmetic glyph choice, 0 through 5; -1 uses 0.

remarks.para: The method starts a coroutine, meaning an animation sequence spread across several frames. The avatar request comes after a 0.2-second wait, a configured 2-second glyph phase, and a 0.5-second wait. It is not a promise of a completed avatar change when this call returns.
Calls are ignored while avatarTransformationSequence is non-null. The sequence clears that field after asking SwapAvatar to change the avatar; the asynchronous loading may still be unfinished then.

stopIndex controls only which of six glyphs the animation aims to end on. It does not choose an avatar from avatarCrateRefs: avatarRef supplies the actual target. Values outside 0 through 5, including the default -1, are treated as 0.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PullCordDevice.HapticEvent(System.Single)
member.summary: Requests a vibration from every controller whose hand is attached to ballHost.
member.param: Amount for blending each minimum vibration setting toward its maximum.

remarks.para: driver is a blend amount, limited to 0 through 1.
