Zero selects the configured minimum amplitude, frequency and duration; one selects their maximums; 0.5 selects the midpoint of each pair. Duration is in seconds, frequency is in hertz (vibrations per second), and amplitude is a unitless strength request. The controller’s global vibration setting can further scale amplitude.

During a pull, OnBallGripUpdate calls this when its smaller haptic-step index changes. It supplies the detent-curve resistance, except that resistance below 0.0001 is replaced with 1 for this call. driver is therefore not simply the overall percentage of cord extension.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PullCordDevice.HologramAnimation
member.summary: Creates the brief scale-and-shader animation that changes the avatar hologram during a pull.
member.returns: An unstarted hologram animation sequence.

remarks.para: The returned coroutine is a sequence that continues over several frames; run it with StartCoroutine. Its horizontal curve input is elapsed animation time divided by hologramAnimLength, a duration in seconds, limited to 0 through 1.

Each frame, the scale becomes (1, 1, 1) plus hologramAnimDisplacement multiplied by hologramScaleCurve’s value. hologramAnimDisplacement contains the three configured additions to local X, Y and Z scale; both it and the curve output are unitless scale quantities. hologramShaderCurve’s value, limited to 0 through 1, blends scanline size from its saved baseline to three times that baseline, depth fading to five times its baseline, and tint toward the saved tint with alpha 0.5.

While the sequence is still within its configured duration, the mesh changes once on the first update strictly after halfway. A large frame step that skips the rest of the phase can skip that mesh change. When the sequence finishes, it restores the saved shader values and clears hologramCoroutine. It does not explicitly restore the scale at the end, so the scale curve should provide the desired ending scale.

A shader is the drawing program that gives the hologram its appearance; a material stores the settings given to that program. Awake, Unity’s initialization callback, reads and saves the assigned material’s scanline-size, depth-fade and tint values once. The animations blend from these saved values rather than recapturing the material each frame. Tint alpha is its opacity component, conventionally 0 for transparent and 1 for opaque; the drawing program determines the visible result.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PullCordDevice.JointToWorld
member.summary: Places the ball at receiverTransform and locks it there with an extra physics joint.

remarks.para: A physics joint is a connection that limits movement. worldJoint has no connected Rigidbody, so it anchors to the world. All three movement axes and all three rotation axes are locked. Its break force is positive infinity, and joint collision is disabled. isBallInReceiver becomes true after the joint has been configured.

A Rigidbody is the component that gives an object physics motion, including its mass and velocity. With no connected Rigidbody, this extra joint’s other end is the fixed world. Positive-infinity break force means no finite pulling force can exceed its configured force threshold.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PullCordDevice.LerpAnchor(System.Single)
member.summary: Creates a gradual move of the cord’s body anchor toward the body’s forward centerline.
member.param: Configured anchor-adjustment duration in seconds; actual completion follows frame timing.
member.returns: An unstarted anchor-adjustment sequence.

remarks.para: A coroutine is a sequence that continues over several frames; run this returned sequence with StartCoroutine. lerpTime is its configured duration in seconds. The target is recalculated from the slot Rigidbody’s world position and forward direction: the nearest point on that infinite line to this device’s world position.

The sequence blends from the ball’s current world position toward that point, then converts the result to the connected body’s local coordinates before setting ballJoint’s connected anchor. It also ramps the joint drive from zero toward jointDriver scaled by the current avatar’s upper-body strength multiplier. The changing target means this is not a fixed straight-line trip between two saved positions.

anchorLerp is set true when the sequence starts and false on normal completion; anchorCoroutine is cleared on completion. OnBallGripDetached stops the sequence early without clearing those two values itself. The normal grab starts it with a configured 0.4-second duration.

The slot Rigidbody is the component that lets physics move the player’s body slot. The connected anchor is the cord joint’s attachment point on that body, measured in meters from its origin along its local axes. jointDriver stores the current three drive settings; the ramp blends each setting from 0 toward its strength-scaled value as elapsed seconds divided by lerpTime advances. A drive supplies a spring-like pulling force. Its three settings are spring strength in newtons per meter of position error, damping in newton-seconds per meter of velocity error, and maximum force in newtons. These settings are applied to each of the joint’s X, Y and Z movement axes. The avatar’s upper-body strength multiplier is unitless and multiplies all three settings.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PullCordDevice.LoadFavoriteAvatars
member.summary: Rebuilds the cord’s avatar choices from favorite barcodes in the active save, using the default list when needed.

remarks.para: A barcode is the identifier of an avatar crate, not an image. A null saved favorites list uses defaultFavoriteAvatarsBarcodes. For each barcode the warehouse cannot resolve as an AvatarCrate, the method substitutes the default barcode at that same list index.

If the resulting list is shorter than the default list, the method returns before replacing avatarCrateRefs. Otherwise it replaces each array slot whose list entry is a valid barcode string. It does not load the hologram meshes; BodyMallUpdate follows this call with UpdateAllPreviewMeshes.
The configured arrays and lists must have compatible sizes: this method indexes the default list and saved list directly rather than padding a short list automatically.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PullCordDevice.OnBallGripAttached(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand)
member.summary: Prepares the cord and preview when a hand grabs the ball, and undocks the ball if it was in a receiver.
member.param: Hand reported by the grip attachment event.

remarks.para: This is a callback: a routine the grip calls when a hand attaches. OnEnable subscribes it to the grip’s attachment event, and OnDisable unsubscribes it.

After the grab sound, a docked ball refreshes favorite-avatar previews, destroys its world joint, clears isBallInReceiver, and tells the connected Body Mall panel to disconnect. ballHeld then becomes true. If anchorCoroutine is null, the callback starts the 0.4-second anchor-adjustment coroutine, a sequence spread across frames.

It shows the cord line, restores saved hologram shader settings, clears the preview mesh, and activates the preview’s spin object. The hand argument is part of the event signature; this implementation does not choose its state from that argument.

A shader is the drawing program that gives the hologram its appearance; a material stores the settings given to that program. Awake, Unity’s initialization callback, reads and saves the assigned material’s scanline-size, depth-fade and tint values once. The animations blend from these saved values rather than recapturing the material each frame. Tint alpha is its opacity component, conventionally 0 for transparent and 1 for opaque; the drawing program determines the visible result. Restoring these values removes the temporary scanline, depth-fade and tint changes from the pull animation.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PullCordDevice.OnBallGripDetached(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand)
member.summary: On release, requests the selected avatar and retracts the cord, or docks the ball when the handle is in a receiver.
member.param: Hand reported by the grip release event.

remarks.para: This callback is a routine called by the grip’s release event. It plays the release sound and stops a saved anchor-adjustment sequence. If isHandleInReceiver is true, it locks the ball to the world and asks the Body Mall panel to accept the Body Log.

Otherwise, with an existing ballJoint, it restores the connected anchor to ballStartTrans. avatarIndex greater than 0 chooses avatarCrateRefs[avatarIndex - 1]; a different barcode from the current avatar starts the asynchronous SwapAvatar operation and plays blast particles. Index 0 requests no change. It starts RetractBall only when ballRetraction is null.
It then hides the tick lines, glyphs and preview spin object, and only afterwards clears ballHeld. The avatar may still be loading when the release callback ends.

ballJoint is the physics connection that supplies the cord’s movement limit and pulling force. ballStartTrans is the transform marking the ball’s rest point. A transform stores an object’s position, rotation and size. The connected anchor is the joint’s attachment point on the connected physics body. InverseTransformPoint converts the rest point’s world position to a position relative to that body’s origin and axes, in meters, before that point is assigned. A barcode is the unique identifier for an avatar crate, so matching barcodes mean the same avatar choice.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PullCordDevice.OnBallGripUpdate(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand)
member.summary: While the ball is held, turns cord extension into avatar selection, pull resistance, tick sounds, vibrations, and hologram motion.
member.param: Hand reported by the attached-update event.

remarks.para: This callback is a routine called during the grip’s attached-hand updates. It measures the world distance in meters from fxLineGroup to the ball. The full selection distance is (2 × sidewaysShoulderOffset + upperArmLength + armSum) × armLengthMultiplier, in meters. sidewaysShoulderOffset is the signed sideways offset from the chest to the right upper-arm bone along the avatar’s rightward axis, measured during setup; it is not the straight-line distance between those points. upperArmLength is the right shoulder-to-elbow measurement. armSum is upperArmLength + lowerArmLength + 0.5 × wristToHandLength. lowerArmLength is elbow-to-wrist when an optional wrist point is configured, otherwise elbow-to-hand. wristToHandLength is that optional wrist-to-hand distance, or 0 without the wrist point. All these measurements are cached meters, and armLengthMultiplier is unitless.

The distance is mapped from zero to that full distance into zero through the number of avatarCrateRefs. The floored result is avatarIndex: 0 selects no avatar, 1 selects array entry 0, and so on. Changing slots restarts the hologram animation, chooses the matching glyph and plays the appropriate inward or outward tick sound.

The fractional part of the mapped pull samples jointDetentCurve for resistance. Outward motion blends between the minimum and maximum drive settings; inward motion uses the return drive. Drives are smoothed and scaled by the avatar’s upper-body strength multiplier, except that the anchor-adjustment sequence handles the live drives while anchorLerp is true. Smaller steps within a slot trigger HapticEvent. The method also turns the preview spin and rock objects around their local axes.

The avatar’s setup precomputation measures its skeleton and saves proportions and palm dimensions. RefreshBodyMeasurements converts the arm proportions into cached lengths in meters using the avatar’s eye height. The upper arm runs from the right upper-arm bone to the right lower-arm bone; the lower arm runs from there to the optional wrist point, or to the hand bone when no wrist point is configured. Palm dimensions come from the finger positions. The device reads these saved measurements; moving the hand does not recalculate them. Floor rounds a number down: for example, a mapped pull of 2.7 gives avatarIndex 2. A detent is the resistance bump between choices; jointDetentCurve uses the unitless fractional progress within one choice interval to set that resistance. A drive supplies a spring-like pulling force. Its three settings are spring strength in newtons per meter of position error, damping in newton-seconds per meter of velocity error, and maximum force in newtons. These settings are applied to each of the joint’s X, Y and Z movement axes. The avatar’s upper-body strength multiplier is unitless and multiplies all three settings.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PullCordDevice.PlayAvatarParticleEffects
member.summary: Requests an avatar-blaster effect for each non-null renderer in the current avatar’s bodyMeshes array.

remarks.para: bodyMeshes contains the body’s skinned mesh renderers: meshes that bend with the avatar’s bones. This method does not iterate the separate headMeshes or hairMeshes arrays. Each spawn request uses that renderer’s world position and rotation. When spawning completes, a callback—a routine called with the spawned object—looks for ParticleTint and asks it to emit particles from the captured renderer, with white tint, scale (1, 1, 1), and zero emitter velocity.

The particle burst multiplier is 2 × (x × y + x × z + y × z), where x, y and z are the renderer’s world-axis bounding-box widths in meters. This has square-meter units and is the box’s surface area, even though the receiving parameter is named volumeSize. For a 1-meter cube the multiplier is 6. It changes the burst amount rather than resizing the effect object to the bounds.
This method makes spawn requests; effects have not necessarily finished spawning when it returns. A spawned object without ParticleTint receives no mesh-particle setup from this callback.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PullCordDevice.ResetBall
member.summary: Moves the ball to ballStartTrans and restores the avatar-scaled minimum joint drives.

remarks.para: Only the ball’s world position is replaced; the method does not restore its rotation or reset receiver, visibility, or selection flags. A joint drive supplies the spring-like force pulling connected physics objects toward their target. The three jointMinDrive settings are multiplied by the current avatar’s upper-body strength multiplier before they are applied to all movement axes.

A drive supplies a spring-like pulling force. Its three settings are spring strength in newtons per meter of position error, damping in newton-seconds per meter of velocity error, and maximum force in newtons. These settings are applied to each of the joint’s X, Y and Z movement axes. The avatar’s upper-body strength multiplier is unitless and multiplies all three settings. ballStartTrans marks the resting point, and its world position is measured in meters along the world axes.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PullCordDevice.RetractBall(System.Boolean)
member.summary: Creates the sequence that pulls the released ball back to ballStartTrans by shrinking the joint’s movement limit.
member.param: Suppresses only the short/long retraction sound; the return and final state changes still happen.
member.returns: An unstarted ball-return sequence.

remarks.para: The returned coroutine is a sequence that continues over several frames; run it with StartCoroutine. It disables the grip, applies jointReturnDrive, and restores the body-relative anchor to ballStartTrans. When quiet is false, a starting distance below 0.8 meters uses retractShort; 0.8 meters or more uses retractLong.

The configured return duration is retractSpeed multiplied by the starting distance in meters. Thus retractSpeed acts as seconds per meter: for example, 0.5 and a 0.6-meter starting distance give a configured 0.3-second return phase. Frame timing and the physics response determine the actual motion. The limit shrinks toward zero and never exceeds the ball’s currently measured distance from its rest point.

The return phase ends when that distance is below 0.01 meters or its configured duration has elapsed. The sequence then applies the minimum limit settings, yields a zero-second wait to a later update, restores the avatar-scaled minimum drives and maximum limit settings, reenables the grip, then conditionally hides the ball. If ballShown is true and the saved armLength threshold is less than or equal to saved handDist, it calls DisableBall and clears ballShown. Only after that conditional hide does it clear ballRetraction.

handDist is the last saved world distance in meters from the appropriate physical hand to ballStartTrans. armLength is the last saved reveal threshold: (upperArmLength + lowerArmLength + max(palmSizeX, palmSizeY)) × handShowDist. The four arm and palm numbers are the avatar’s cached measurements in meters; max chooses the larger palm dimension, and handShowDist is a unitless fraction. The return’s hide test reads these saved values without measuring a fresh hand pose. The avatar’s setup precomputation measures its skeleton and saves proportions and palm dimensions. RefreshBodyMeasurements converts the arm proportions into cached lengths in meters using the avatar’s eye height. The upper arm runs from the right upper-arm bone to the right lower-arm bone; the lower arm runs from there to the optional wrist point, or to the hand bone when no wrist point is configured. Palm dimensions come from the finger positions. The device reads these saved measurements; moving the hand does not recalculate them.

ballStartTrans is the transform marking the ball’s rest point. A transform stores an object’s position, rotation and size. The connected anchor is the joint’s attachment point on the connected physics body. InverseTransformPoint converts the rest point’s world position to a position relative to that body’s origin and axes, in meters, before that point is assigned. The return initially applies the three jointReturnDrive numbers without the avatar-strength multiplication; the minimum drive restored at completion is multiplied by that unitless strength factor. A drive supplies a spring-like pulling force. Its three settings are spring strength in newtons per meter of position error, damping in newton-seconds per meter of velocity error, and maximum force in newtons. These settings are applied to each of the joint’s X, Y and Z movement axes. The avatar’s upper-body strength multiplier is unitless and multiplies all three settings.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PullCordDevice.SetBodySegment
member.summary: Reconnects the cord joint to the body Rigidbody stored in the cached slot container.

remarks.para: A Rigidbody is the component that lets physics move an object; a joint connects it to another object. This changes ballJoint.connectedBody to _slotContainer.rootRb. It does not move the ball or recalculate the connected anchor. Awake, Unity’s initialization callback, finds the slot container on the device’s parent and performs the same initial connection.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PullCordDevice.SetPreviewMesh(System.Int32)
member.summary: Clears the hologram at index 0, or displays and fits the loaded avatar preview selected by a positive one-based index.
member.param: 0 to clear the mesh; 1 through the cached crate count to select a preview.

remarks.para: Index 1 uses previewMeshCrates[0], index 2 uses entry 1, and so on. A missing crate or unloaded mesh leaves the existing preview unchanged. Negative or out-of-range positive indices are not safely ignored; array indexing can throw.

For a usable mesh, the method sizes previewPoint using the reference previewBounds mesh, the selected mesh’s bounding-box size, and the unitless previewMeshScaleTune multiplier. It offsets previewMeshPosition relative to its parent to center the mesh, then assigns the mesh to previewMesh. It does not request asset loading itself.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PullCordDevice.SwapAvatar(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.AvatarCrateReference)
member.summary: Requests a different avatar through RigManager, then updates save data, sound, particles, and player settings after a successful change.
member.param: Reference whose barcode identifies the target avatar.

remarks.para: This operation can continue after the call returns while the avatar loads. A reference with the current avatar’s barcode is skipped. For a different barcode, bodyLogFirstUse is cleared before the swap request; that flag can therefore change even if loading fails.

Only a successful returned result with a non-null barcode writes the saved CurrentAvatar, plays switchAvatar, schedules PlayAvatarParticleEffects with a configured 0.1-second delay, and attempts to save. If the resolved crate’s pallet is marked Internal, it also updates the saved FallbackAvatar. It then refreshes the player’s menu layout, body-slot placement, Body Log availability and handed orientation, and controller preferences such as turning and vibration strength.
The delayed particle invocation follows Unity’s update timing, so 0.1 seconds is a configured delay rather than an exact frame timestamp. This method returns no success result to its caller.
A barcode is the unique identifier for an avatar crate. A pallet is the package containing that crate; its Internal flag identifies it as built in for this fallback-save condition.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PullCordDevice.Update
member.summary: Each frame, decides whether to show the enabled Body Log ball, follows a docked receiver, and updates the cord’s two visible endpoints.

remarks.para: It returns immediately when _bodyLogEnabled is false. In lookMode, the ball appears only when the camera-to-device direction has a dot product with camera forward strictly greater than lookDot; a larger dot product means the device is closer to the center of the view. Otherwise, it compares the appropriate physical hand’s world distance from ballStartTrans with armLength, the avatar-scaled hand-show threshold.

Normal hiding waits until the ball is unheld and no retraction is saved. The hand-distance branch additionally preserves a first-use or docked ball. A docked ball is moved to receiverTransform’s world position. A shown, loose, undocked ball more than 0.05 meters from fxLineGroup starts a quiet return if no return is already saved.

The line renderer receives the world positions of ballLine and ballGrip as endpoints. Avatar selection, resistance drives and preview spinning happen in OnBallGripUpdate, the grip’s attached-hand callback, rather than in this per-frame method.

The two look directions are normalized, meaning reduced to length 1 without changing their direction. Their dot product is unitless: 1 means the same direction, 0 means sideways, and -1 means opposite directions. lookDot is the unitless comparison threshold. In hand-distance mode, armLength is recalculated as (upperArmLength + lowerArmLength + max(palmSizeX, palmSizeY)) × handShowDist, in meters. The arm and palm quantities are the current avatar’s cached measurements in meters; max selects the larger palm dimension. handShowDist is a unitless distance fraction. The avatar’s setup precomputation measures its skeleton and saves proportions and palm dimensions. RefreshBodyMeasurements converts the arm proportions into cached lengths in meters using the avatar’s eye height. The upper arm runs from the right upper-arm bone to the right lower-arm bone; the lower arm runs from there to the optional wrist point, or to the hand bone when no wrist point is configured. Palm dimensions come from the finger positions. The device reads these saved measurements; moving the hand does not recalculate them. An attached-hand callback is a routine the grip calls while a hand remains attached.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PullCordDevice.UpdateAllPreviewMeshes
member.summary: Replaces cached dial crates and requests their hologram mesh assets, unloading each previous cached mesh asset first.

remarks.para: For every avatarCrateRefs entry, it unloads the old cached crate’s preview asset when present, resolves the new crate, stores it in previewMeshCrates at the same array index, and requests the preview mesh asset when the resolved crate exists.

The method does not wait for those asset requests to finish. Its load callback—a routine called when the load reports its result—has an empty body, and SetPreviewMesh later checks whether an asset is actually available. Calling this is therefore not a guarantee that all holograms can immediately be displayed.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PullCordForceChange.SwapAvatar(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.AvatarCrateReference)
member.summary: Starts an avatar-swap request through the stored player rig and updates player settings when the rig reports success.
member.param: Reference to a registered avatar asset. Its barcode, the asset's unique identifier, is sent to the player rig.
member.returns: A UniTaskVoid handle for work that may finish later. It provides no success result to the caller.

remarks.para: This method resolves the supplied reference to an avatar crate and asks rigManager to swap to its barcode with avatar caching enabled. Caching lets the rig keep a loaded avatar instance for later reuse. rigManager must already have been stored by the trigger's ForceChange path; the method does not find it itself. A missing reference, unresolved crate or missing rig causes an error.

The request runs asynchronously: it can pause while the rig loads and applies the avatar, then continue later. Returning from this call does not prove the avatar has changed. The rig's completion result controls the following settings update.

When the rig reports success and the requested crate has a barcode, this method writes that requested identifier to the active save's PlayerSettings.CurrentAvatar. If the crate belongs to a pallet whose Internal flag is true, it also updates FallbackAvatar, the identifier saved for fallback use. A pallet is a package that groups game assets. These are changes to the active save data in memory; this method does not call the save-to-disk operation.

After those settings updates, it calls BodyVitals.PROPEGATE_SOFT to refresh the player's body-slot, pull-cord, UI and control settings. For example, the disabled-pull-cord branch requests a change this way. The trigger may already be marked used while the request is still waiting; used is not a successful-completion flag.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.RandomObject.Flipper
member.summary: Reapplies the current local scale to this component’s object, keeping the same X, Y and Z values.

remarks.para: A Transform stores an object’s position, rotation and size. This method reads that object’s local scale, its size multipliers relative to its parent, and writes those same three values back. Scale has no physical units: 1 keeps the original axis size and 2 doubles it.
For example, scale (2, 3, 1) stays (2, 3, 1). This method does not swap axes or mirror the object. The inspected enable and random-pick routines do not call it.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.RandomObject.Method
member.summary: Asks Randomizer to pick from Objects when the list has at least one entry, then disables this RandomObject component.

remarks.para: The Unity editor’s Static Pick command is available from this component’s menu. It runs the same candidate-selection routine as normal enabling, then sets this component’s enabled setting to false. Disabling the component leaves the chosen object’s activation setting as the pick routine set it.

For a list of three different objects, one list position is chosen and the other two objects are turned off. Re-enabling this component later runs its enable routine and chooses again, so Static Pick does not permanently remember a choice. The selection requires an assigned list of at least one non-null entry. With an assigned empty list, Randomizer changes no objects’ activation settings, but Static Pick still disables this component.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.RandomObject.Randomizer
member.summary: Chooses a random position in Objects, turns that entry on and turns the other entries off.

remarks.para: It calls Unity’s integer random picker with 0 as the first allowed index and the list count as the excluded upper limit. For three entries, the possible indices are 0, 1 and 2. It then visits entries from first to last and calls SetActive(true) on the chosen position and SetActive(false) on every other position. These calls change the objects’ activation settings; an inactive parent can still keep a chosen child inactive in the level.

Keep each object in the list once. If Objects is [A, A, B] and index 0 is chosen, the later visit to index 1 turns A off again. The result therefore need not leave one object on when entries repeat. The list must be assigned and entries must be non-null; a missing entry is not skipped. An empty list gives the activation loop no objects to change.

The enable routine calls this immediately whenever this component becomes enabled on an active object. It can pick the same position again on a later call. Editing the list alone does not make another pick; changes affect the next selection.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.RigScreenOptions.EnableFisheye
member.summary: Switches the spectator screen to the separate Fisheye camera, using the right-eye viewpoint.

remarks.para: This is a shortcut for SetSpectatorCamera with Fisheye and Right. It activates cam, positions its follow target half the headset camera's eye separation to the right, and applies tiltAngle, the follow target’s up-or-down tilt in degrees around its local X axis: positive values tilt downward and negative values tilt upward. This target tilt is applied only in Fisheye mode. It does not preserve the previously selected eye or change the saved spectator settings.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.RigScreenOptions.RenderOverlay
member.summary: Activates OverlayCam's object, renders one image immediately, and schedules the object to be hidden 0.2 seconds later.

remarks.para: Hiding is done by TurnOffOverlayCam. This method does not itself select an eye, change the spectator mode, or keep calling Render every frame. OverlayCam must already be assigned.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.RigScreenOptions.SetCameraLocation(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.SaveData.EyeTarget)
member.summary: Moves the spectator camera's follow target to the left eye, right eye, or midpoint between the eyes.
member.param: Left or Right chooses that eye's sideways offset; Center removes the offset.

remarks.para: The offset is along TargetTransform's parent's local X axis. Setup makes that parent the headset's main camera, so turning your head turns the offset direction too. Left uses minus half Camera.main.stereoSeparation, Right uses plus half, and Center uses zero; local Y and Z are zero. With an illustrative eye separation of 0.064 meters and parent scale 1, Left is (-0.032, 0, 0), or 3.2 cm to the left.

The method writes both SpecCamLocalpos and TargetTransform.localPosition. It needs Camera.main and TargetTransform to exist, and does not update the eyeTarget field, saved settings, or the headset mirror's eye selection. Use SetSpectatorCamera to apply a complete spectator mode.
For diagnosing the eye offset, it also logs the target’s lossyScale (its scale including parent scaling), the calculated X offset, and the headset camera’s eye separation.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.RigScreenOptions.SetPassthroughLocation(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.SaveData.EyeTarget)
member.summary: Chooses which headset eye images Unity copies to the spectator screen.
member.param: Left shows the left eye; Right shows the right eye; Center selects Unity's BothEyes output.

remarks.para: Center here means both rendered eyes, not a new camera placed halfway between them. This method changes Unity's XR game-view output only. It does not activate or deactivate cam, move TargetTransform, or update eyeTarget or saved settings. SetSpectatorCamera with Passthrough also turns off the separate spectator camera.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.RigScreenOptions.SetSpectatorCamera(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.SaveData.SpectatorCameraMode,Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.SaveData.EyeTarget)
member.summary: Applies a spectator screen mode and its eye viewpoint immediately.
member.param: Passthrough mirrors headset eye images; Fisheye enables the separate spectator camera; Void disables both outputs and renders the overlay once.
Left, Right, or Center. Passthrough treats Center as both eyes; Fisheye places its target at the midpoint between the eyes.

remarks.para: Passthrough deactivates cam's GameObject and disables its Camera component, then selects the headset mirror output. Fisheye disables that mirror output, activates cam's object, sets the target's eye offset, applies tiltAngle, the follow target’s up-or-down angle in degrees, around the target's local X axis (positive values tilt downward and negative values tilt upward), and enables the Camera. The existing camera setup supplies the Fisheye appearance; this method does not set lens or projection properties.

Void turns off cam and the headset mirror output, then activates OverlayCam, renders it immediately, and schedules its object to be hidden after 0.2 seconds. It requires the overlay camera reference as well as cam. Fisheye also requires the initialized TargetTransform and Camera.main.

The arguments control this call; cameraMode and eyeTarget are not updated. No settings are saved by this method. A later settings refresh can apply the saved mode and eye again, replacing a temporary change made here.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.RigScreenOptions.TurnOffOverlayCam
member.summary: Hides the entire GameObject containing OverlayCam.

remarks.para: RenderOverlay schedules this after 0.2 seconds, including when the Void mode renders its overlay. Other components on the same object are also made inactive. This does not change the Camera component's enabled setting or the main spectator mode.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.RoundProfileGroup.CalcRoundBPE(Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.RoundProfile)
member.summary: Returns an integer ammo-budget value per enemy from the round’s saved totals.

remarks.para: The calculation is (L + 2 × H) / N. L is totalRoundLightCount, the saved light-ammo total in rounds of ammunition; H is totalRoundHeavyCount, the saved heavy-ammo total in rounds of ammunition; N is totalRoundEnemyCount, the saved number of enemy entries. Medium ammo is left out. These totals are read as they stand; this method does not count the wave lists again.

For positive counts, any fractional remainder is discarded: 40 light rounds, 10 heavy rounds and 4 enemies produce 15; 5 light rounds and 2 enemies produce 2. This measures an ammo budget, not the number of hits needed to kill an enemy. An enemy total of zero logs an error and returns zero. The method returns the result without updating the round’s bullets-per-enemy field.

member.param: The non-null round whose stored ammo and enemy totals are read.
member.returns: The calculated whole-number budget, or zero when the saved enemy total is zero.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.RoundProfileGroup.CalcWaveBPE(Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.WaveProfile)
member.summary: Returns an integer ammo-budget value per enemy entry in the wave.

remarks.para: The calculation is (L + 2 × H) / N. L is wave.lightBulletAmount in rounds of light ammunition; H is wave.heavyBulletAmount in rounds of heavy ammunition; N is wave.enemyProfilesList.Count, the number of entries in the enemy list. Medium ammo is left out. Repeated references to the same enemy profile still count as separate entries.

For positive counts, the fraction is discarded: 40 light rounds, 10 heavy rounds and 4 enemy entries produce 15. This is not a health or damage calculation. An empty enemy list logs an error and returns zero. The method does not write wave.bulletsPerEnemy.

member.param: The non-null wave with a non-null enemy list.
member.returns: The calculated whole-number budget, or zero for an empty enemy list.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.RoundProfileGroup.CopyGroupProfile(Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.RoundProfileGroup)
member.summary: Creates new round and wave containers for a group, while sharing several referenced assets and lists.

remarks.para: This is a partial copy. It creates a new group, round list, rounds, waves, enemy lists and loot lists. Enemy profiles and loot items are still the same referenced objects. Each copied wave also shares its entire friendlyProfileList with its source, so changing that list affects both waves.

There is a source-side effect: before copying each source round, the method sets that source round’s isProceduralRound flag to true. This flag marks a round generated by code rather than authored by hand. The copied round’s flag starts false because CopyRoundProfile does not copy it.

The new group keeps the mode, display title, objective and stacked flags, kill limit, ammo-clearing and reward settings, custom-count flag, teleport values, saved light/medium/heavy/enemy/bullets-per-enemy statistics, and the same trialProfile and boneLeaderData references.

Other settings start at new-group defaults. These include descriptionText, friendlyCount, spawn delays, sublimateOnDeath, increaseEnemyRate, maxConcGoal, limitReached, the group display flags showGroupInfo and showGroupGraph, currRound/currWave/currEnemy and totalGroupBulletCount. For example, a source enemySpawnDelay of 4 becomes the new-group default of 1, and a source maxConcGoal of 20 becomes 10. If those settings matter, assign them explicitly after copying.

member.param: The non-null source group, containing valid rounds and waves.
member.returns: A new group with new round and wave containers, but shared referenced assets and friendly lists.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.RoundProfileGroup.CopyRoundProfile(Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.RoundProfile,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Creates a new round and copies its waves, delays, mode and saved totals.

remarks.para: Each wave is copied through CopyWaveProfile, using the same randLoot choice. The round and wave containers are new; enemy profiles and loot items remain shared references unless a loot item is replaced. Each copied wave’s friendly list is the source’s same list.

The saved light, medium, heavy, enemy and bullets-per-enemy totals are copied without recalculation. showRound and showRoundInfo control round visibility in the menu. isProceduralRound marks a round generated by code rather than authored by hand. These settings, along with isSlowHealthRegen and customHealthRegenDuration, are not copied. They start at new-round defaults rather than keeping the source’s custom choices. If the source has special health-regeneration settings, restore them explicitly on the copy.

member.param: The non-null source round with a valid wave list.
Whether each copied wave replaces supported loot items with random items of the same broad weapon category. Defaults to false.
member.returns: A new round containing copied waves.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.RoundProfileGroup.CopyWaveProfile(Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.WaveProfile,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Creates new enemy and loot lists for a wave, optionally replacing its loot by weapon category.

remarks.para: The copied wave keeps maxConcurrent, light/medium/heavy ammo amounts, bulletsPerEnemy and hoiPoiChance. Its enemy list has the same entries in the same order, referring to the same enemy profiles. Its friendlyProfileList is the source’s entire same list. Editing an enemy list changes only that wave’s list; editing a shared profile or the shared friendly list can affect both waves.

With randLoot false, the new loot list contains the source’s same loot objects. With true, each LIGHTGUN item becomes a random pistol or submachine gun with equal category chance; MEDGUN becomes a rifle; MELEE becomes a blade or blunt weapon with equal category chance; HEAVYGUN becomes a shotgun. An unsupported loot type is logged and omitted. The replacement is a table item, so the original item’s individual spawnable, title and percentage are not preserved.

The menu-visibility settings showWave, showEnemies, showFriendlies and showWaveLootItems start false. isProceduralWave also starts false and marks a wave generated by code rather than authored by hand. Ammo and bullets-per-enemy values are copied as saved; this method does not check whether the budget still matches the copied enemy list. Random replacement needs the matching nonempty loot tables in StaticProfiles, the game’s shared arena profile registry.

member.param: The non-null source wave with valid enemy and loot lists.
Whether to randomize supported loot categories in the copy. Defaults to false.
member.returns: A new wave with new enemy and loot lists and a shared friendly list.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.RoundProfileGroup.CreateDefaultRound(System.Boolean)
member.summary: Builds a round with four waves, each containing four entries for the first registered enemy profile.

remarks.para: Every wave gets 40 light, 40 medium and 40 heavy rounds of ammunition. Each enemy entry refers to StaticProfiles.enemyProfileList[0]; this does not randomly choose four enemy types or spawn four actors. The wave’s concurrent enemy limit starts at 3, meaning the spawning loop allows up to three living enemies at a time.

With addRandomLoot true, the first wave gets a random blade and pistol, and the second gets a random rifle. The last two loot lists stay empty. With false, all four loot lists are empty. The registry and its first enemy must exist; the optional loot also needs nonempty matching loot tables.

Each wave’s bulletsPerEnemy becomes 30: (40 light rounds + 2 × 40 heavy rounds) / 4 enemy entries. Medium ammo is ignored in this ratio. Round-wide saved totals are left at their initial zero values; they are not summed from the waves here. The new round otherwise starts with LIMITED mode, a 5-second wave delay and a 10-second round delay.

member.param: Whether to add random blade/pistol loot to wave one and rifle loot to wave two. Defaults to false.
member.returns: The new configured round; no enemies or loot are spawned by this method.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.RoundProfileGroup.CreateSurvivalProfileAtRound(Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.RoundProfileGroup,Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.RoundProfileGroup,System.Int32,System.Int32,System.Int32)
member.summary: Rebuilds the supplied destination group’s rounds to support resuming survival at a requested round.

remarks.para: This edits the destination profile in place and clears its old round list first. It adds a default round with random loot and UNLIMITED mode, then copies the source’s rounds except its last two. It repeatedly copies the source’s final round to fill the gap. The final appended copy has random loot, UNLIMITED mode and difficulty scaled with the requested round number.

For each gap-filling copy, the difficulty factor is the destination round count minus one before that copy is added. Filling stops when this factor reaches round minus two. For example, a source with 5 rounds and a request for round 8 produces a default round, copies of source rounds 1–3, three final-round copies with factors 3, 4 and 5, and a final copy with factor 8. A small requested number does not trim the fixed prefix.

The difficulty changes use IncreaseRoundDifficulty: medium adds twice the factor in enemy entries per wave, while hard and higher add four times the factor. A proposed concurrent limit above maxEnemy leaves that wave’s old limit unchanged. The method rebuilds the rounds only; other destination metadata and saved group totals stay as they were.

Use distinct source and destination groups with non-null lists and a nonempty source round list. Loot randomization also needs the shared arena loot registry. Clearing the destination makes using the same object as source unsafe.

member.param: The source survival profile. Its final round is the template for extra rounds.
The existing destination profile whose round list is cleared and rebuilt.
The requested survival round number; also the difficulty multiplier for the final copy.
The concurrent-enemy limit passed to the difficulty helper, measured in living enemies.
Difficulty code: 0 easy, 1 medium, 2 hard, 3 harder or 4 hardest.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.RoundProfileGroup.IncreaseConcurrentEnemyCount(Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.RoundProfileGroup,System.Int32,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Sets every wave’s concurrent enemy limit to the supplied count, optionally adding enough enemy entries to fill it.

remarks.para: maxConcurrent counts living enemies allowed at the same time. It is assigned exactly, so this method can lower a limit despite its name. It edits the supplied group and returns that same group; it does not set group.maxConcGoal or immediately create or remove actors.

With updateEnemyProfiles true, a wave with fewer enemy-list entries than its new limit gets extra entries selected from its existing list. Each existing list position has equal chance, so duplicate entries make a profile more likely. A wave with 2 entries and a limit of 5 gets 3 additions. Existing excess entries are never removed. A wave needing additions must already have a nonempty seed list.
Ammo budgets and saved round/group/bullets-per-enemy statistics are not refreshed. Without updateEnemyProfiles, only the concurrent limits change.

member.param: The non-null group to edit, with valid round and wave lists.
The new limit in living enemies per wave; the supplied integer is stored unchanged, including negative values.
Whether to append enemy entries to waves whose lists are shorter than the new limit.
member.returns: The same group object after editing.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.RoundProfileGroup.IncreaseGroupDifficulty(Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.RoundProfileGroup,System.Int32,System.Int32)
member.summary: Applies one difficulty increase to every round in the supplied group.

remarks.para: The group is edited in place. Each round calls the round-difficulty helper with a factor of 1. For every wave, medium difficulty proposes one extra concurrent enemy and adds two enemy entries; hard, harder and hardest propose one extra concurrent enemy and add four entries. Easy adds none. A proposal above maxConcurrentLimit leaves the old concurrent limit unchanged.

Every wave’s light, medium and heavy ammo amounts are raised to at least 40 rounds. Added entries choose among that wave’s existing distinct enemy profiles. The helper refreshes each round’s enemy total and bullets-per-enemy value from its existing saved ammo totals, but it does not refresh wave bulletsPerEnemy or any group totals. No actors are spawned here.

member.param: The non-null group to edit, with valid rounds, waves and seed enemy lists.
0 easy, 1 medium, 2 hard, 3 harder or 4 hardest.
The maximum allowed proposed wave concurrency, in living enemies.
member.returns: The same group after its rounds are edited.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.RoundProfileGroup.IncreaseRoundDifficulty(Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.RoundProfile,System.Int32,System.Int32,System.Int32)
member.summary: Edits each wave’s difficulty, then refreshes the round’s enemy total and saved ammo-budget ratio.

remarks.para: The round parameter is an integer multiplier, defaulting to 1. Medium proposes round extra concurrent enemies and adds 2 × round enemy entries per wave. Hard, harder and hardest propose round extra concurrent enemies and add 4 × round entries. Easy adds none. Added entries are chosen from the wave’s existing distinct profile references; they are not spawned actors. When additions are needed, each wave must already have a nonempty list of valid enemy-profile references to seed that selection.

Each wave’s proposed concurrent limit is accepted only when it is no greater than maxConcurrentLimit; otherwise its old limit stays. All three wave ammo amounts become at least 40 rounds of ammunition. The wave’s cached bulletsPerEnemy is not refreshed.

After the changes, totalRoundEnemyCount becomes the sum of all wave enemy-list lengths, including repeated entries. totalRoundBulletsPerEnemy becomes (L + 2 × H) / N with the fraction discarded for positive values. L is the round’s existing saved light-ammo total in rounds of ammunition, H its existing heavy-ammo total in rounds of ammunition, and N the newly counted enemy entries. Medium is ignored and zero enemies give zero. The saved round ammo totals themselves are not re-summed, so they may still be stale.

member.param: The non-null round to edit.
0 easy, 1 medium, 2 hard, 3 harder or 4 hardest.
The ceiling for proposed wave concurrency, in living enemies.
The integer difficulty multiplier, normally positive; defaults to 1.
member.returns: The same round object after editing.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.RoundProfileGroup.IncreaseWaveDifficulty(Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.WaveProfile,System.Int32,System.Int32,System.Int32,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Adds enemy entries and proposes a larger concurrent limit according to the difficulty tier and multiplier.

remarks.para: round is an integer multiplier, defaulting to 1. Easy (0) adds no enemies and no concurrency. Medium (1) adds 2 × round enemy entries and proposes round extra concurrent enemies. Hard, harder and hardest (2, 3 and 4) add 4 × round entries and propose round extra concurrent enemies. Unsupported difficulty codes log a message and add none.

The proposed concurrent limit is applied only if it is no greater than maxConcurrentLimit. An over-limit proposal leaves the previous limit unchanged; it is not clipped down to the limit. For example, an old limit of 4, multiplier 2 and ceiling 5 keep concurrency at 4 even though medium still adds 4 enemy entries.

With randomEnemyType false, selection chooses equally among distinct enemy profile references already in the wave, ignoring duplicates when choosing types. With true, medium draws from the medium enemy table and hard or higher from the hard enemy table in StaticProfiles, the game’s shared profile registry. These selectors exclude their table’s final item when it contains more than one item. When additions are needed, false requires a nonempty wave enemy list of valid profile references; true requires a nonempty matching StaticProfiles difficulty table.

Every light, medium and heavy ammo amount becomes at least 40 rounds, even for easy or unsupported difficulty. The supplied wave is edited directly. Its saved bulletsPerEnemy is not recalculated, and this method does not spawn actors.

member.param: The non-null wave to edit.
0 easy, 1 medium, 2 hard, 3 harder or 4 hardest.
The largest proposed concurrent enemy limit that may be accepted, in living enemies.
The integer multiplier for additions; defaults to 1.
Whether to draw additions from the shared difficulty tables instead of this wave’s existing distinct profiles. Defaults to false.
member.returns: The same wave object after editing.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.RoundProfileGroup.IncreaseWaveDifficultyAtCustomRate(Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.RoundProfileGroup,Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.WaveProfile)
member.summary: Changes a wave’s concurrent limit and adds enemy entries using the group’s custom rate.

remarks.para: The new limit is min(C + r, G). C is the wave’s old maxConcurrent in living enemies, r is group.increaseEnemyRate in enemy entries per increase, and G is group.maxConcGoal in living enemies. For r > 0, the method adds 2 × r enemy-list entries. If r <= 0, it appends no entries; a negative r can still lower the proposed limit C + r, subject to the cap at G. For example, C=3, r=2 and G=4 produce a limit of 4 and four extra entries. An old limit already above G can be lowered.

Each addition chooses a position from the wave’s current enemy list with equal chance. Repeated profile references act as weights, and newly appended entries participate in later choices during this call. For positive-rate additions, the list must already contain valid enemy profiles as seeds.

The wave is edited in place; ammo amounts and saved bullets-per-enemy, round and group totals are not refreshed. No actors are created or removed. This helper does not clamp or correct a negative rate or goal.

member.param: The non-null group providing increaseEnemyRate and maxConcGoal.
The non-null wave to edit; positive-rate additions also need valid enemy profiles in its enemy list.
member.returns: The same wave object after editing.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ScrollButton.IncrementalScrollContent
member.summary: Starts an animated move from the current scrollbar value toward that value plus the cached signed step.

remarks.para: The scrollbar value normally measures position from 0 to 1 across its full travel, rather than pixels or meters. signedStepSize is the cached change in that value: Start, Unity's startup call before normal updates, copies stepSize and negates it for DOWN. For example, current value 0.4 and signedStepSize 0.1 give target 0.5.

It first stops every coroutine on this component. A coroutine is an animation routine that pauses and resumes across frames. It then starts RefactoredSmoothScrolling with the captured current value, the target, and scrollFrequency as the requested duration in seconds of game time. Unity's time-scale setting can make game time pass faster or slower than real time, or pause it at zero. The call starts movement; it does not wait until the target is reached.

The target is not clamped to 0 through 1. A current value of 0.95 and signed step 0.1 request 1.05, which this scrollbar setter can store. Use suitable steps or limit your targets yourself. The scrollbar must be assigned, and scrollFrequency should be positive. This method neither checks button press permission nor cancels scheduled ScrollContent repetitions.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ScrollButton.RefactoredSmoothScrolling(System.Single,System.Single,System.Single)
member.summary: Creates a frame-by-frame routine that moves the scrollbar between the supplied start and target values.

remarks.para: A coroutine is a routine Unity can pause and resume across frames. Calling this method creates its iterator, the object tracking that progress; it does not run the animation until Unity starts the iterator as a coroutine or a caller advances it. CurValue is the supplied starting scrollbar position, not an instruction to read the live position. TargetValue is the supplied end position. Positions normally use the scrollbar's 0-to-1 travel scale, not pixels or meters.

With a positive totalTime, each update adds deltaTime / totalTime to a progress fraction. deltaTime is elapsed game time for that frame, in seconds. Unity's time-scale setting can make game time pass faster or slower than real time, or pause it at zero. totalTime is the requested duration in seconds of game time. It clamps the progress fraction from 0 to 1, then writes CurValue + (TargetValue - CurValue) × progress. Thus progress 0 gives the start, progress 0.5 gives the halfway position, and progress 1 gives the target. For CurValue 0.2 and TargetValue 0.6, halfway is 0.4.

The first update advances progress before writing a value. Each write is followed by a wait until the end of a rendered frame. The update whose progress reaches or passes 1 writes the target, and the iterator finishes when resumed again. Actual completion depends on frame timing and Unity's time scale; totalTime is not an exact wall-clock completion promise. A paused time scale can stop progress.

Only progress is clamped: start and target values are not limited to 0 through 1, and this scrollbar setter can store values outside that range. Use a positive duration and valid assigned scrollbar. Zero can cause an immediate target write or invalid arithmetic when frame time is zero; a negative duration can keep the routine running without moving toward the target. Cancelling the coroutine leaves its last written value.

member.param: Starting scrollbar position on the usual 0-to-1 travel scale.
Ending scrollbar position on the same scale; this routine does not clamp it.
Positive requested duration measured in seconds of game time.
member.returns: Iterator for the animation; start it as a coroutine or advance it to make it run.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ScrollButton.SmoothScrolling(System.Single,System.Single,System.Single)
member.summary: Creates the older scrollbar animation routine, whose duration calculation does not produce the supplied duration.

remarks.para: A coroutine is a routine Unity can pause and resume across frames. This method returns an iterator, the object holding its progress; merely calling the method does not start movement. minValue is the starting scrollbar position and maxValue is the target, even when the target is smaller than the start. These positions normally use a 0-to-1 travel scale, not pixels or meters.

The implementation first multiplies totalTime by the absolute distance between the endpoints. It then multiplies each frame's deltaTime by that same result while updating elapsed progress, cancelling the intended duration scaling for positive duration and different endpoints. deltaTime is elapsed game time for each frame, measured in seconds; Unity's time-scale setting can make this clock pass faster or slower than real time, or pause it at zero. As a result, progress follows about one second of accumulated game time, regardless of the positive totalTime supplied. For example, 0.2 to 0.6 with totalTime 0.5 does not produce a half-second move.

It writes the start on its first update and waits until the end of each rendered frame between updates. If the next accumulated progress passes the end, it finishes without writing a final target value. It can therefore stop just short of the target; it reaches the target only if a sampled progress value lands on the end. Changing Unity's time scale, cancelling the routine, or the button reaching its stopping boundary can change the actual movement.

Equal endpoints or totalTime = 0 make the routine divide by zero and can repeatedly write an invalid value rather than complete. A negative totalTime with different endpoints finishes without a value write. Use the refactored routine when you need the supplied duration to control the animation. Neither routine clamps its supplied endpoint values to the usual 0-to-1 range.

member.param: Starting scrollbar position on the usual 0-to-1 travel scale; it need not be the smaller endpoint.
Target scrollbar position on the same scale; it need not be the larger endpoint.
Requested seconds used by the older calculation; positive values do not set the actual duration as intended.
member.returns: Iterator for the older animation; it must be started or advanced to run.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ScrollButton.stopScrolls
member.summary: Cancels scheduled ScrollContent repetitions and stops all coroutines on this component.

remarks.para: A coroutine is a routine that pauses and resumes across frames, including these scrollbar animations. Calling stopScrolls directly stops that work immediately and leaves the scrollbar at its last written value; it does not finish the move, restore the start, or change whether the button accepts presses.

The pointer-release handler schedules this method about 0.2 seconds later rather than stopping immediately. Work can continue during that delay. stopScrolls cancels the ScrollContent schedule, but does not cancel a pending delayed stopScrolls call, so an earlier release can still stop a new press made before that delay expires.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ScrollElementsContainer.OnTransformChildrenChanged
member.summary: Calls the registered listeners when Unity reports that this container’s child objects have changed.

remarks.para: A child is an object placed under another object in Unity’s hierarchy, the tree of scene objects. Unity sends this message when the container’s child list changes, such as adding an item or moving one to a different parent.

This method calls OnContainerChildrenChanged if a routine is registered there, passing no arguments. A callback is a routine called when a notification occurs. It runs directly during this call; this method does not schedule a later-frame refresh. With no registered callback, it returns without doing anything.

For example, a connected ScrollButton receives the notification and rechecks whether its button can still scroll. That listener can disable the button and stop its ongoing scrolling when there is no further movement available. The listener performs that work; this container method sends the notification.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SecurityCamera.IndicateSave
member.summary: Starts the camera’s save-indicator sound, particles, surface change and timed flash-cone display.

remarks.para: This requests the same asynchronous effect sequence as IndicateSaveAsync. Asynchronous means the sequence can wait and resume later without making the caller wait for the whole flash interval.

It provides feedback only; these camera routines do not write game progress. Each call starts a separate sequence, so repeated requests can overlap and an earlier sequence can hide the cone while a newer request is still waiting.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SecurityCamera.IndicateSaveAsync
member.summary: Starts save-indicator effects and hides the flash cone after a game-time delay.

remarks.para: An AudioClip is a recorded sound asset. It requests cameraFlashSFX at this camera object’s world position with volume 0.3, base pitch 1 and minDistance 2 metres. Volume is a unitless playback level, pitch is a unitless playback-rate multiplier, and minDistance is the near-distance setting within which moving closer no longer makes the source louder. The audio helper adjusts the requested pitch for slow motion: with Time.timeScale at 0.5, the requested base pitch 1 becomes 0.625. Time.timeScale is the unitless rate of game time relative to real time, with 1 meaning normal speed.

Next it activates flashCone, plays particles and assigns material to each renderer in renderers. flashCone, particles and renderers must be supplied. The renderer array may be empty, but any entries it contains must be valid. Afterward it samples flashActiveTime in seconds and starts a delay using the game clock. Slow motion makes this clock advance more slowly, so the same delay lasts longer in real time. Destroying the Unity scene object that holds this camera cancels the pending delay.

On normal completion it hides the current flashCone reference. It does not explicitly stop the particles or restore the previous renderer materials. Hiding the cone can also hide effects placed under that object; otherwise their separate settings or other code determine what remains visible. Editing flashActiveTime after a request has started its delay does not reschedule that delay.
Each call has its own wait; there is no “already flashing” gate in these camera methods. Repeated calls can overlap, and an earlier completion can hide the cone during a later request’s interval.

To change the sequence itself, patch the state machine’s MoveNext method, SecurityCamera._IndicateSaveAsync_d__24.MoveNext. A state machine is the compiler-generated routine that remembers where the sequence stopped and resumes it after a wait. Its __1__state values are:

item.description: Initial entry starts sound and visual effects and awaits UniTask.Delay for flashActiveTime game-time seconds.
Resumes after the delay; on normal completion it hides flashCone and finishes.
The sequence is complete.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SecurityCamera.OnEntityUncull
member.summary: Prepares the camera to choose a fresh aim after its entity’s culling inactivity is released.

remarks.para: This callback is a routine called to report the entity’s return from culling, the entity system’s temporary inactivity processing. Awake, Unity’s initialization callback, registers this camera with its assigned entity for these notifications.

It sets firstLoop true and, when Camera.main exists, stores a goalRot facing from cameraRb toward that main-view camera’s world position. Camera.main is Unity’s enabled camera marked MainCamera. This method does not immediately rotate the body; the next valid pass, Unity’s per-frame tracking method Update, refreshes the starting rotation and blend timer.

If there is no main-view camera, firstLoop stays true and the stored goal rotation is left unchanged. A valid cameraRb, the camera’s simulated physics body, is needed when a main-view camera is available.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SimpleGripEvents.OnAttachedDelegate(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand)
member.summary: Runs OnAttach for an incoming grab notification and, when two-hand suppression is enabled, records which hand grabbed.
member.param: The hand reported by the grip as attaching.

remarks.para: With doNotRetriggerOnMultiGirp off, every callback runs OnAttach and the hand flags are not updated. With it on, OnAttach runs only when both flags were false; the arriving hand’s flag is set after the event runs.
This method handles a notification. Calling it yourself changes event/state handling without attaching a physical hand. Use the real grab system to attach an object.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SimpleGripEvents.OnAttachedUpdateDelegate(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand)
member.summary: Checks a held hand’s trigger-press and menu-tap inputs and runs the corresponding actions.
member.param: The hand whose trigger and controller menu inputs are checked.

remarks.para: A trigger press runs OnIndexDown. A controller menu tap runs OnMenuTapDown. Both events receive no arguments. This is called through a monitored grip’s held-hand update, rather than from this component’s own Unity Update method.

The callback uses the supplied hand’s cached inputs and does not check Grips, the hand flags, or doNotRetriggerOnMultiGirp. Calling it yourself can run the events even if that hand is not actually holding a monitored grip. Repeated calls while an input flag remains true can repeat the event.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SimpleGripEvents.OnDetachedDelegate(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand)
member.summary: Records an incoming release notification and runs OnDetach when the configured hand condition is met.
member.param: The hand reported by the grip as detaching.

remarks.para: With doNotRetriggerOnMultiGirp off, every callback runs OnDetach and the hand flags are not updated. With it on, this clears the releasing hand’s flag first, then runs OnDetach only if both flags are false.
Calling this method yourself runs notification handling; it does not release the physical hand or remove its joint. A joint is the connection holding the hand to the object in the physics simulation.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SmoothFollower.MoveCameraUpdate
member.summary: Moves this object's world position toward the target, then turns its world rotation toward the target using remembered smoothing rates.

remarks.para: A transform stores an object's position, rotation and scale. This method reads targetTransform's current world position and rotation and writes this component's own transform. World coordinates describe placement in the whole level, rather than relative to a parent. It applies no separate follow offset and does not change scale.

Position uses a smooth-damping calculation that remembers its current movement rate in velocity. Rotation smooths the four numbers of a quaternion, Unity's rotation representation, and remembers their rates in quatVel. These are calculation state; this method changes transforms directly rather than applying force to a Rigidbody, Unity's physics-body component.

For position, the smoothing-response interval is TranslationSmoothTime multiplied by Time.deltaTime. For rotation, it is RotationalSmoothTime multiplied by Time.deltaTime. Both named fields are unitless multipliers here; Time.deltaTime is the current frame interval in scaled game-time seconds. For example, a multiplier of 0.15 and a frame interval of 0.02 seconds supply 0.003 seconds to that smoother. The interval is an approximate response setting, not a deadline for reaching the target.

The method returns without changing anything when the component is not active and enabled. While active, it requires a valid targetTransform. Enabling the component registers this method as a callback, a saved function called later, on the player controller's camera-update signal; disabling removes it. That signal is fired while the main camera begins rendering, after the controller's camera-related tracking work. Calling the method yourself performs another smoothing step.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SpawnGun.CoFireFlash
member.summary: Creates the animation that briefly changes the gun display materials when tool-action feedback is requested. See .

remarks.para: A material supplies an object's drawing settings; its shader is the drawing code that uses those settings. This is action feedback: starting the flash does not establish that a requested object has finished spawning.
FlashScreen starts this iterator as a Unity coroutine, allowing it to continue over later frames. Merely obtaining the iterator does not start that animation.

It uses a configured 0.5-second threshold in scaled game time: time measured by the game clock, affected by game speed and pausing. On each coroutine resume it first updates material slot 1, the second material, on every gunBodyRenderers entry, then checks the accumulated time against that threshold. While time is at most 0.5 seconds it adds this frame's game-time duration and yields; the next resume can make the final material write with time already above 0.5 seconds. Frame sampling therefore determines the stopping point rather than guaranteeing an exact 0.5-second elapsed animation. It writes the FlashCoroutine shader float to 1 minus a clamped curve result. The curve input is four times elapsed seconds: fireCurve is used through input 1, then returnCurve receives the continuing input above 1, rather than restarting at 0.
The renderers need at least two valid materials each, and the two inherited Gun curves must exist. The shader must use this property for a visible flash.

A coroutine is a sequence that can pause and continue over several frames. Each AnimationCurve here maps the numeric input to a flash-progress output; the output is clamped between 0 and 1 before subtraction from 1. The timing multiplier 4 is per second, making the curve input dimensionless.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SpawnGun.Fire
member.summary: Does nothing in this SpawnGun implementation.

remarks.para: The usual held-grip update waits for the hand's trigger-release event, checks the aim ray and UI restrictions, then explicitly calls the base Gun.Fire implementation. That base call can reach SpawnGun.OnFire after the gun's own readiness checks.
Calling this override directly therefore does not request a spawn or despawn. OnFire contains the tool action, but calling it directly also skips the normal release-input and base-gun checks.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SpawnGun.FlashScreen
member.summary: Starts a brief flash animation on the gun display materials.

remarks.para: CoFireFlash writes on each resume before checking its accumulated time. A frame that advances the time past 0.5 seconds allows a final write on the following resume, so the threshold is not an exact elapsed-duration promise. Material slot 1 is the second material, and the shader is the drawing code that consumes its flash setting.

It starts CoFireFlash as a coroutine. The animation uses a configured 0.5-second threshold in scaled game time, meaning the game clock affected by game speed and pausing, and writes the FlashCoroutine shader float on material slot 1 of each gunBodyRenderers entry.

It does not keep a coroutine handle or cancel an earlier flash in this method. Repeated calls can start overlapping animations that write the same materials. The shader and renderer materials must support the flash property.
A coroutine is a sequence that continues over several frames; starting it lets the animation resume on later frames without making this call wait for the whole duration.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SpawnGun.OnFire
member.summary: Performs the selected spawn or removal action after the base gun accepts a shot.

remarks.para: A pool keeps reusable game objects and supplies an instance for a spawn request. The ordinary spawn reads a cached world pose: position truePlacePosition in scene coordinates, conventionally meters, and orientation truePlaceRotation saved by an earlier placement update. An avatar crate instead asks currentHand's rig manager, the controller for the player's body/avatar, to swap the avatar when that hand is available. A Rigidbody is Unity's physics body for simulated movement and rotation. Display flashes and muzzle-effect requests report the action request; they do not confirm that a spawned object or an avatar swap has completed.

In Spawner mode it starts the asynchronous SpawnCrate operation using the selected crate and the cached truePlacePosition/truePlaceRotation. It also starts display feedback and muzzle visual requests. An ordinary object-spawn request can complete after this routine returns; the completion callback calls the optional caller callback, then requests the spawned entity's spawn effect.

In Remover mode it uses the cached _hitInfo collider's attached Rigidbody to find its Marrow entity. An entity is the group of game objects managed and despawned together. If any entity bone tag matches playerTag by barcode, it skips removal. Otherwise it requests the despawn effect, flashes the display, requests a muzzle effect and despawns that entity.

The normal held update refreshes _hitInfo with a raycast on trigger release before calling base Gun.Fire. Calling OnFire yourself does not refresh the aim or enforce those UI/base-gun gates. Neither this method nor the release path checks placerValid as a firing permission. A static collider without an attached Rigidbody is skipped by the normal removal input path.

A completion callback is a routine called when the spawned object is available. The optional caller callback runs before the entity spawn-effect request, so it can inspect or change the object at that point.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SpawnGun.OnModeSelect(Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.UtilityModes)
member.summary: Changes the operating mode and refreshes the selection UI label and image.

remarks.para: Spawner mode shows the selected crate title, or the selection prompt/image when no crate is selected. Remover mode shows its removal label and hides the selection image. It then renders the UI camera again.

This callback changes _selectedMode. It does not synchronize isDespawnMode, play modeSFX or start the body screen color transition. The normal held-input mode-switch path performs those sound/color steps separately. The global SpawnGunUI must be available.

A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action. The callbacks here respond to the grip, selection or asynchronous completion described above; assigning a related field does not invoke them automatically.

member.param: Spawner places the selected crate; Remover targets an entity for removal.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SpawnGun.OnPoolInitialize
member.summary: Runs the base gun pool setup and hides the laser pointer.

remarks.para: A pool keeps reusable objects for later requests. The inherited Gun pool setup runs first and force-detaches every additional grip in otherGrips; only after that base setup returns does this override hide the laser. The callback is a routine called for this initialization action.
The SpawnGun-specific step deactivates laserPointerGameObject, which must be assigned. It does not reset the selected crate, preview meshes or SpawnGun color-transition fields here.
The inherited Gun setup resets its firing/slide state and prepares grip/holster behavior. This callback is for an object being taken from the pool for use, not for opening the selection UI.

A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action. The callbacks here respond to the grip, selection or asynchronous completion described above; assigning a related field does not invoke them automatically.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SpawnGun.OnSpawnableSelected(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.SpawnableCrate)
member.summary: Stages a crate, shows its title in the gun UI and begins loading its preview mesh.

remarks.para: It stores the crate in _selectedCrate, disables the selection image, updates the title and renders the UI camera. SetPreviewMesh then unloads the previous preview asset and requests the new one asynchronously.
This is selection and preview setup; it does not place the crate in the world. A valid crate and the global SpawnGunUI are required. The new mesh may become available after the method returns.

member.param: The crate asset definition to select and preview; this callback expects a valid reference.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SpawnGun.OnTriggerGripAttached(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand)
member.summary: Connects the held spawn gun to the spawn-menu UI and shows its preview and laser.

remarks.para: An Animator is Unity's component for playing animations; speed 1 means its normal playback rate. The UI camera far clip distance is the farthest distance from that camera at which it draws the scene, here 10 scene units. These changes occur during a callback, a routine called to report the grip attachment.

After base Gun attachment setup, it adds the spawn menu, subscribes to crate/mode selection events and assigns this gun to the menu panel. It sets the assigned Animator speed to 1, its normal playback rate, refreshes an existing selection preview or the selection prompt, activates the preview spin group and laser, and stores currentHand.

It caches the UI RawImage image tint, the color applied to the UI element that displays an image, sets the UI camera far clip distance to 10 world units and renders the camera. The menu/UI singletons, Animator, grip and visual references must be available. This callback responds to a grip attachment; it does not itself grab the hand.

A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action. The callbacks here respond to the grip, selection or asynchronous completion described above; assigning a related field does not invoke them automatically.
The menu event subscriptions and visual/camera setup happen before currentHand is assigned. The field assignment does not itself send a grip-attachment event.

member.param: The attached grip's hand, saved as currentHand for later avatar-selection work.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SpawnGun.OnTriggerGripDetached(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand)
member.summary: Disconnects the spawn-menu callbacks and hides the gun preview spin group and laser.

remarks.para: After base Gun detachment setup, it removes the spawn menu and unsubscribes its crate/mode selection handlers. It hides the preview spin group and laser, disables the UI selection image, sets the UI camera far clip distance to 0.5 world units, renders the camera and clears currentHand.

This callback reports trigger-grip detachment. Its inherited Gun step first force-detaches every additional grip in otherGrips, before the SpawnGun menu and visual cleanup. This override does not clear the selected crate or explicitly deactivate placerPreview; those are separate from its menu and held-visual cleanup.

A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action. The callbacks here respond to the grip, selection or asynchronous completion described above; assigning a related field does not invoke them automatically.
