The menu handlers are unsubscribed before the preview/laser are hidden; currentHand is cleared after the UI camera refresh.

member.param: The detached hand reported by the grip; inherited detachment setup receives it.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SpawnGun.SetPreviewMesh
member.summary: Replaces the staged crate preview by unloading the old asset and asynchronously loading the selected crate's mesh.

remarks.para: It first hides previewMeshSpin's GameObject and placerPreview, clears previewMesh and placerPreviewMesh, and unloads the preview asset remembered by _lastSelectedCrate. It then remembers the current _selectedCrate and requests that crate's preview mesh.

When loading completes, the callback stores the mesh in loadedMesh[0]. Provided the squared bounds-size length is not below approximately 0.0000000001 in squared mesh-coordinate units, it sets the small display's scale from previewBounds and previewMeshScaleTune, centers it using previewMeshPosition, assigns the mesh to both previewMesh and placerPreviewMesh, then shows the spin group.

The selected crate and required visual references must exist. Returning from this method does not mean loading has finished. A near-zero-size mesh leaves the display hidden. The callback, a routine called when the mesh becomes available, has no saved selection-identity check. If an older load completes after a new selection, that older mesh can overwrite loadedMesh[0] and the current preview displays. The tiny-size test happens after loadedMesh[0] is written; a rejected mesh leaves the display hidden.
Here, the mesh-load callback is a routine called when the requested asset becomes available; that routine performs the preview updates described above.

For the scale/centering calculation, the loaded length is sqrt(width² + height² + depth²), using the loaded mesh bounds dimensions in mesh-coordinate units. The reference dimensions are the width, height and depth of previewBounds.mesh.bounds, also in mesh-coordinate units. previewMeshScaleTune is an extra dimensionless multiplier. Dividing each reference dimension or bounds-center coordinate by that loaded length normalizes the display; it is not the distance from the gun to the aimed surface.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SplineBody.SetMaximumForce(System.Single)
member.summary: Requests a new force ceiling for each contact joint's movement drive and wakes the physics body.

remarks.para: The method first stores the value, then sets isSpeedChanged to true, then wakes rb, the Rigidbody that Unity uses to simulate this object's motion. Waking a body makes it eligible for physics updates after it has gone to sleep. The assigned spline controller copies the settings to the contact joints during a later FixedUpdate, Unity's regularly spaced physics update. This method does not immediately change those joints.

force is measured in newtons. Each contact joint is a physics connection that keeps one body contact on the curved spline path. Its X drive is the motor that pushes along the path. For example, force = 100 limits that motor to 100 newtons per joint; it does not cap gravity, collision forces, or the combined force of every joint. A smaller ceiling can make the body take longer to reach its requested speed.

rb must be assigned. If it is missing, the value and refresh flag have already been stored when the attempt to wake the body fails. The method does not check whether the new value differs from the old value or clamp the number to a range.

member.param: Maximum force in newtons for each contact joint's X movement drive.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SplineBody.SetPositionDamper(System.Single)
member.summary: Requests a new strength for correcting the difference between the drive's requested speed and current speed.

remarks.para: The method first stores the value, then sets isSpeedChanged to true, then wakes rb, the Rigidbody that Unity uses to simulate this object's motion. Waking a body makes it eligible for physics updates after it has gone to sleep. The assigned spline controller copies the settings to the contact joints during a later FixedUpdate, Unity's regularly spaced physics update. This method does not immediately change those joints.

Despite the name, the spline controller configures the X movement drive with a position spring of zero, so this damper acts on the difference between requested and current speed along the joint's X direction. The value multiplies a speed error measured in Unity distance units per second to request force. When one Unity unit represents one metre, the coefficient's SI unit is newton-seconds per metre. For example, at that scale, a coefficient of 20 multiplied by a speed error of 2 metres per second requests 40 newtons before the joint's force ceiling. If a scene uses a different distance for one Unity unit, the metre-based unit and example change with that scale. Greater positive damping makes the motor correct a speed difference more strongly; with a zero requested speed it resists movement along the joint's X direction.

rb must be assigned. If it is missing, the value and refresh flag have already been stored when the attempt to wake the body fails. The method does not check whether the new value differs from the old value or clamp the number to a range.

member.param: Speed-error correction coefficient for each contact joint's X drive; its SI unit is N·s/m when one Unity unit represents one metre.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SplineBody.SetTargetVelocity(System.Single)
member.summary: Requests a signed speed along the spline contact joints' X direction and wakes the physics body.

remarks.para: The method first stores the value, then sets isSpeedChanged to true, then wakes rb, the Rigidbody that Unity uses to simulate this object's motion. Waking a body makes it eligible for physics updates after it has gone to sleep. The assigned spline controller copies the settings to the contact joints during a later FixedUpdate, Unity's regularly spaced physics update. This method does not immediately change those joints.

velocity is in Unity distance units per second, normally metres per second when one Unity unit represents one metre. The spline controller writes it into the X component of each contact joint's target velocity, with Y and Z set to zero. X is the joint direction defined by the body's axis setting and aligned with the path as the spline controller updates the contacts. It is not the scene's fixed world X direction.

For example, SetTargetVelocity(2) requests an X-drive speed of 2 metres per second at the usual scale. A negative value reverses the signed request. This is a motor target: the body's actual speed also depends on damping, the drive's force ceiling, and other forces. Calling the method again with the same speed still sets the refresh flag and wakes the body.

rb must be assigned. If it is missing, the value and refresh flag have already been stored when the attempt to wake the body fails. The method does not check whether the new value differs from the old value or clamp the number to a range.

member.param: Signed X-drive target speed in Unity distance units per second, normally metres per second.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.StaticProfiles.CreateStatProfile(Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.StaticProfiles)
member.summary: Sets the supplied profile as the shared source for later NPC, loot, ammunition and alliance lookups.

remarks.para: Assigns the supplied object itself. Later reads through instance return that same object, so changing one of its lists changes the data seen by later lookups. Existing NPCs, spawned objects and lists already copied into another controller are not rebuilt by this method.

This method only stores the reference. It does not load the profile from path or register its spawnable assets. BaseGameController normally calls it from Awake, Unity's setup call when a component starts, if no shared profile is assigned. Supply a configured profile before asking the game controllers for enemies or loot.

member.param: The static profiles to assign.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TaxiController.DisableTaxiGrips
member.summary: Releases every hand holding a grip in gripsToDisable, then prevents further interaction with those grips.

remarks.para: Each grip is force-detached before its interaction is disabled. This changes grabbing, rather than disabling the whole taxi object. The configured array and every grip in it must be present; missing entries are not skipped.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TaxiController.DriveComplete
member.summary: Begins braking the taxi and starts a stop-wait sequence that tests its shared motion cache.

remarks.para: First allows the rear seat to be exited and selects the brake velocity, damper, and maximum-force targets. OnStopingStart then fires, before the brake sound is requested. The engine changes toward interior idle over a requested 5-second fade.

A coroutine, meaning a sequence that continues over several frames, tests the saved currVelMag against stopThresh squared. stopThresh is a speed cutoff in meters per second, squared for this comparison. When the shared-cache test completes, it fires OnRideComplete before requesting the door-opening sound and showing toggleObjects. Calling this method does not mean the taxi has already stopped. Repeated calls start additional stop-wait sequences.

The sequence first puts the placeholder 20 into currVelMag before testing it. If stopThresh squared is at least 20, the sequence can complete before sampling the body at all; for example, stopThresh = 5 meters per second gives a squared cutoff of 25. When another sample is needed, it normally stores squared world speed in that same cache. A concurrent push checker can overwrite it with signed forward speed, so completion does not guarantee measured slowing or a stationary taxi.

The brake targets are velocity_brake, the requested path-drive speed in meters per second; damper_brake, force per speed difference in newton-seconds per meter; and force_brake, the force cap in newtons. throttleTime is the smoothing-response time in seconds for approaching those targets, not an exact deadline for reaching them.

The requested 5-second engine fade uses scaled game-time seconds. Slow motion stretches its real-world duration; for example, at a constant half-speed time scale, 5 game seconds take about 10 real seconds, with completion still limited to frame updates.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TaxiController.KillPushPromptCoroutine
member.summary: Stops the repeating push prompts and clears the saved sequence so prompts can be started again.

remarks.para: A coroutine is a sequence that continues over several frames. If no push prompt sequence is saved, this does nothing. It does not stop the separate speed check started by StartPushTaxiRoutine.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TaxiController.PlayerExitedCab
member.summary: Sets the exit signal that allows the waiting taxi to drive away once its departure delay has also passed.

remarks.para: This sets _exitedCab to true; it does not check where the player is or remove the player from a seat. Seat removal starts a separate sequence that waits until both this signal is true and at least 11 seconds have accumulated since that sequence began. The signal is not reset by the inspected TaxiController code.

The 11-second departure delay uses scaled game-time seconds accumulated from frame updates. Slow motion lengthens the real-world wait; at a constant half-speed time scale, 11 game seconds take about 22 real seconds. The exit signal and the delay must both be satisfied.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TaxiController.SplineLoopCounter
member.summary: Adds one completed loop and starts braking when the count reaches the ride's loop goal.

remarks.para: A spline is the curved path the taxi follows. The count increases before listeners are called. OnWhiteFlag fires only when the new count equals loopGoal minus one. For a goal of 3, that happens on the second call.

At or beyond loopGoal, this begins the DriveComplete braking sequence, then fires OnLoopComplete. OnLoopComplete is not called for earlier loops. There is no completed latch here: further calls at or beyond the goal can start braking again and invoke OnLoopComplete again.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TaxiController.StartCreditsCoroutine
member.summary: Displays the credits texture, scrolls it vertically, then clears the texture after the final pause.

remarks.para: A coroutine is a sequence that continues over several frames. It assigns creditsTexture to the material saved from creditsRenderer during Start, Unity's setup routine before normal updates, waits 2 seconds, scrolls for creditsLength seconds, then waits 4 seconds before clearing the texture.

The vertical texture offset is -0.01 minus elapsed scroll time divided by creditsLength; elapsed time and creditsLength are in seconds, and texture offsets are fractions of the image rather than meters. Longer positive creditsLength values make the same image scroll more slowly. Each frame uses its accumulated time, so the sequence is not guaranteed to last exactly creditsLength plus 6 seconds. Starting again does not cancel an earlier credits sequence.

The 2-second pause, creditsLength scrolling duration, 4-second pause, and elapsed scroll time all use scaled game-time seconds. Slow motion makes the sequence take longer in real time; at a constant half-speed time scale, the same configured times take about twice as long, subject to frame updates.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TaxiController.StartDuckMusicCoroutine(System.Single)
member.summary: Fades the taxi song toward duckVolumeLevel, holds it there, then fades back to cashedBaseVolume.

remarks.para: A coroutine is a sequence that continues over several frames. Each fade uses duckTime seconds; length is the separate hold after fading down. For duckTime = 1 and length = 3, the intended sequence is about 5 seconds, with completion rounded to frame updates.

The fades sample duckCurve using elapsed fade time divided by duckTime, then clamp the curve output to a 0-to-1 blend amount. A request is ignored while duckCoroutine is already saved; it neither restarts nor extends the existing hold. The final volume is explicitly restored and the saved sequence is cleared.

Both duckTime and length are in scaled game-time seconds, and elapsed fade time advances on that same game clock. Slow motion lengthens the real-world duration: the example with two 1-second fades and a 3-second hold takes about 10 real seconds at a constant half-speed time scale, with frame scheduling still affecting completion.

member.param: Seconds to hold at duckVolumeLevel between the two fades.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TaxiController.StartPushPromptsCoroutine
member.summary: Starts repeating Jimmy's push-prompt animation sequences at randomly spaced intervals.

remarks.para: A coroutine is a sequence that continues over several frames. It waits a random 12 to 24 seconds before each prompt, cycles jimmyController sequence indices 2, 3, and 4, then repeats. Calling again while pushCoroutine is saved does nothing. KillPushPromptCoroutine or registering the player in the rear seat stops it.

The random 12-to-24-second waits use scaled game-time seconds. Slow motion stretches the real-world intervals; at a constant half-speed time scale they take about 24 to 48 real seconds, and the next prompt still resumes on a frame update.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TaxiController.StartPushTaxiRoutine
member.summary: Starts checking forward taxi speed and runs the engine-start sequence once the push threshold is reached.

remarks.para: A coroutine is a sequence that continues over several frames. While below velThresh, it measures carBody's velocity along that body's local blue Z axis, in meters per second. Backward speed is negative; sideways or upward speed does not count toward this check.

When the saved speed reaches or exceeds velThresh, OnEngineStart fires first. Then it requests engine-start and door-opening sounds and an exterior-idle engine fade lasting 0.5 seconds. This sequence does not itself select a drive-speed preset. It compares the saved currVelMag before taking the next sample, so a preexisting cache value can satisfy the first check. Each call starts another checker.

velThresh is the signed forward-speed cutoff in meters per second, measured along carBody's local blue Z axis. For example, a cutoff of 1 accepts a saved forward value of 1 or more; a backward value of -1 does not reach that positive cutoff. The first test still uses the existing shared cache rather than forcing a fresh sample.

The requested 0.5-second engine fade uses scaled game-time seconds. Slow motion stretches its real-world duration; at a constant half-speed time scale it takes about 1 real second, subject to frame updates. This does not add a fixed wait before the push-speed comparison.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TaxiController.StartTaxiSong
member.summary: Requests the taxi song at cabMusicTransform using cashedBaseVolume, while fading out the existing background music.

remarks.para: The existing background music is asked to stop over 3 seconds. The taxi song uses fenceMusic through cabMusicSource. Its audio object follows cabMusicTransform and is placed at an additional local offset equal to that transform's localPosition, meaning its position relative to its own parent. A zero localPosition puts the sound at the transform's origin.
The audio system may need to obtain an audio object before playback begins, so returning from this method does not confirm audible playback has started.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TaxiController.SwapEngineSound(System.Int32,System.Single)
member.summary: Starts fading between engine loops, using alternating audio players to bring one loop up while fading the other down.

remarks.para: Choices 0 and 2 use engineVolume; choices 1 and 3 use engineVolumeInterior. The new loop follows engineTransform. Calling this stops the saved engineCoroutine and starts a new fade from the players' current volumes.

A coroutine is a sequence that continues over several frames. For a positive blendTime, the blend amount is elapsed seconds divided by blendTime, limited to 0 through 1. The sequence samples only while elapsed time is below blendTime and does not snap the final volumes to their endpoints; the last frame can leave a small difference. Zero or negative blendTime still requests the loop but skips the volume-fade samples. Values outside 0 through 3 fall back to the exterior-idle clip with the interior-volume target.

blendTime and the elapsed fade time are in scaled game-time seconds. Their ratio is a unitless blend amount. Slow motion stretches the real-world fade duration: a positive blendTime of 2 takes about 4 real seconds at a constant half-speed time scale, subject to the existing frame-sampling and endpoint behavior.

member.param: Engine loop: 0 exterior idle, 1 interior idle, 2 exterior moving, or 3 interior moving.
Requested fade duration in seconds; positive values allow per-frame volume blending.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TaxiController.SwapEngineSoundSimple(System.Int32)
member.summary: Starts a 2-second engine-loop fade and changes the global reverb preset.

remarks.para: Reverb is the echo-like sound of a space. Selection 1 requests cabReverbData; every other selection requests voidReverbData, including interior-moving selection 3. This calls SwapEngineSound, so it interrupts any saved engine fade and uses the same loop-selection rules.

The requested 2-second engine fade uses scaled game-time seconds. Slow motion lengthens its real-world duration; at a constant half-speed time scale it takes about 4 real seconds, subject to frame updates and the same unsnapped endpoint behavior as SwapEngineSound.

member.param: Engine loop: 0 exterior idle, 1 interior idle, 2 exterior moving, or 3 interior moving.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TaxiController.UpdateSpeed(System.Int32)
member.summary: Selects the target speed, damping, and force limit for the physics connection that pulls the taxi along its curved path.

remarks.para: A physics joint is a connection that guides or holds objects in the physics simulation. This copies the chosen velocity, damper, and force values into jointDriveTarget. The later physics updates gradually move the current settings toward that target using throttleTime, then apply them to splineJoint's drive along the path.

Changing a preset field after selection does not update this copied target; select the preset again. This does not set carBody's velocity directly or set the wheel motors. Values outside 0 through 4 leave the target unchanged.

The selected velocity_* field supplies requested path speed in meters per second. The damper_* field supplies force per speed difference in newton-seconds per meter, and force_* supplies the maximum drive force in newtons. These quantities refer to the path connection's linear drive, rather than wheel rotation.

throttleTime is the smoothing-response time in seconds for approaching the copied speed, damping, and force targets. Smaller positive values make the settings approach their targets more quickly; the value is an approximate response setting, not a guaranteed completion deadline. Physics can still prevent the taxi from achieving the requested speed.

member.param: Preset: 0 off, 1 idle, 2 fast, 3 slow, or 4 brake.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TimeTrial_GameController.CheckTimeTrialKills
member.summary: Checks the accumulated kill count, requests remaining-enemy indicators and completes a running kill trial when its quota is met.

remarks.para: First compares totalEnemiesKilled, the controller’s accumulated enemy-death count, with profileSpawnerList.Count - remainSeekCount. profileSpawnerList.Count is the number of registered profile spawners; remainSeekCount is an integer offset, initially 3. For example, 12 spawners and offset 3 request seeker indicators when the total reaches 9. This first check is not limited to a running session or KILLS mode.

If that threshold is reached and spawnedSeekers is false, requests seeker objects for the currently living enemies. Then, only in KILLS mode during an ongoing session, compares the accumulated enemy deaths with reqKillCount, the required integer quota.

On reaching or exceeding that quota, invokes OnKilledAll with no arguments, requests the end sound, optionally despawns registered NPCs and calls EndSession, in that order. A callback is a function registered to run when an event fires. OnKilledAll callbacks run while the session is still marked ongoing; EndSession changes that flag later. This method reads the existing count and does not add a kill itself.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TimeTrial_GameController.CreateActiveSpawnSeekers
member.summary: Requests a separate seeker indicator for each enemy in the living-enemy list.

remarks.para: Sets spawnedSeekers to true before visiting Alive_Enemy_List, the controller’s list of living enemy AI controllers. For each entry, asks the base controller to spawn the configured seeker object. The original enemy is kept; it is not converted into a different character.

Spawning may finish later. A callback, a function registered to run when the spawned object arrives, gets its SuperSeeker component, supplies the player rig and assigns that enemy as its target. The seeker then stays with the player and points toward the target. The flag records that the request pass started, not that every object appeared successfully. Calling this method directly again makes another request pass even when the flag is already true.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TimeTrial_GameController.OnPlayerSpawn
member.summary: Adds configured light ammunition and matching medium and heavy amounts to the player’s inventory.

remarks.para: For a positive initLightAmmo, adds that many default light cartridges. For a positive initMedAmmo, adds that many default medium cartridges and also that many default heavy cartridges. For example, light 20 and medium 8 add 20 light, 8 medium and 8 heavy rounds.

The inspected implementation does not read initHeavyAmmo. These are counts of cartridges added to the existing inventory, not target inventory totals; calling the method repeatedly adds ammunition repeatedly. Zero or negative configured counts are skipped. The player’s ammunition inventory and the default cartridge profiles must be available.
The controller registers this method with its player-spawn notification while enabled. It is not limited to the moment the trial timer starts.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TimeTrial_GameController.OnRegisteredNPC_Death(Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.NPC_Data)
member.summary: Checks trial thresholds after a registered NPC death notification.

remarks.para: First compares totalEnemiesKilled, the controller’s accumulated enemy-death count, with profileSpawnerList.Count - remainSeekCount. profileSpawnerList.Count is the number of registered profile spawners; remainSeekCount is an integer offset, initially 3. For example, 12 spawners and offset 3 request seeker indicators when the total reaches 9. This first check is not limited to a running session or KILLS mode.

If that threshold is reached and spawnedSeekers is false, requests seeker objects for the currently living enemies. Then, only in KILLS mode during an ongoing session, compares the accumulated enemy deaths with reqKillCount, the required integer quota.

On reaching or exceeding that quota, invokes OnKilledAll with no arguments, requests the end sound, optionally despawns registered NPCs and calls EndSession, in that order. A callback is a function registered to run when an event fires. OnKilledAll callbacks run while the session is still marked ongoing; EndSession changes that flag later. This method reads the existing count and does not add a kill itself.

The passed NPC record is not read by this implementation. In the normal base-controller path, an enemy death increments totalEnemiesKilled before this callback is notified; a friendly death does not add an enemy kill but can still send the notification. Calling this method directly therefore rechecks the current total rather than recording the supplied death.

member.param: The deceased NPC’s record supplied by the notification. This implementation does not inspect it or increment a kill count from it.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TimeTrial_GameController.ProgPointKillCount(System.Int32)
member.summary: Adds a supplied amount to the required kill quota and updates its displayed total.

remarks.para: Adds tCount to reqKillCount, the integer number of kills required, then logs the change and writes the new quota into each totalEnemiesTexts text element. For example, quota 10 plus tCount 4 becomes 14; passing -2 changes 10 to 8.

It does not increment the recorded enemy deaths or check whether the new quota is already satisfied. Unlike SetRequiredKillCount, it does not validate the result against the registered spawner count. The controller subscribes it to Trial_SpawnerEvents.OnTotalKillCalc, which can report the amount required for an additional spawner group.

member.param: An integer amount to add to the required quota. A negative amount lowers it; this method does not validate the resulting total.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TimeTrial_GameController.SetLeaderboardByDifficulty
member.summary: Selects and queries the leaderboard entry at the current difficulty index.

remarks.para: Uses ttDifficulty as a zero-based board index: EASY 0, MEDIUM 1 or HARD 2. If leaderManager is missing, searches the scene for a BoneLeaderManager and caches it. A manager and a matching board entry must be available.

The manager selects that entry as its current data, changes its display mode, updates the display state and queries the board data. This method selects a board to show; it does not submit a new score. UpdateDifficulty does not call this method automatically, so request it separately when the displayed board should change.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TimeTrial_GameController.SetRequiredKillCount(System.Int32)
member.summary: Sets the kill quota, falling back to the registered spawner count when the requested value is invalid.

remarks.para: A valid killCount is greater than 0 and no greater than profileSpawnerList.Count, the number of registered profile spawners. A valid value is saved as reqKillCount and written into each totalEnemiesTexts display. For 10 registered spawners, 6 is valid.

Zero, a negative number or a number above the registered count logs an error and replaces the quota with the registered count. For example, requesting 0 or 12 with 10 spawners leaves quota 10. That fallback branch does not refresh the quota text. If there are no registered spawners, the fallback is 0.
Requires the registered spawner list and, for the valid branch, the text list. Setting the quota does not immediately finish a session; CheckTimeTrialKills evaluates it later.

member.param: Requested integer kill quota. Values outside 1 through the registered spawner count are replaced with that spawner count.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TimeTrial_GameController.SpawnDifficultyCrates
member.summary: Requests spawning through every configured spawner-difficulty entry.

remarks.para: Visits spawnerDifficulties in array order and calls SpawnCrate on each entry. Each entry calls SpawnSpawnable on its cached CrateSpawner, the component responsible for creating its chosen asset. The array, entries and their crate-spawner references must be assigned; missing entries are not skipped.

This method does not choose a difficulty or apply its settings first. Use UpdateDifficulty beforehand when a different asset or AI setup should be selected. A spawn request is not proof that the requested object has completed spawning.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TimeTrial_GameController.TIMETRIAL_PlayerEndTrigger
member.summary: Ends an ongoing speed-run trial when called by the finish setup.

remarks.para: Runs only when timeTrialMode is SPEED_RUN and the session is ongoing. Requests timeTrialEndClip if assigned, then calls EndSession. It does not end a KILLS trial through this path.

EndSession invokes its end event first, then marks the session stopped, stops the stored timer coroutine and updates the time display. A callback is a registered function called by an event; end-event callbacks run before the flag and timer-stop changes. A coroutine is a routine that resumes over later frames.
This method does not inspect a trigger volume or identify the player. Configure the scene’s finish notification to call it at the intended time.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TimeTrial_GameController.TIMETRIAL_PlayerStartTrigger
member.summary: Begins a stopped trial when trigger-based starting is selected.

remarks.para: Runs only when timeTrialStartMode is ON_TRIGGER and isSessionOngoing is false. Requests timeTrialBeginClip when that clip is assigned, then calls the base BeginSession. Other start modes and an already ongoing session leave the state unchanged.

BeginSession invokes its start event before marking the session ongoing and starting the timer routine selected by timerMode. An event callback is a registered function that runs when notified; start-event callbacks therefore see the earlier session state. A coroutine is a routine that resumes work over later frames, as the timer does.

This method has no player or collider argument and does not verify who entered a volume. Wire the appropriate scene trigger to call it when the player should start; its name alone does not perform overlap detection.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TimeTrial_GameController.UpdateDifficulty(System.Int32)
member.summary: Selects a difficulty, applies its kill quota and updates every spawner-difficulty profile.

remarks.para: Use index 0 for EASY, 1 for MEDIUM or 2 for HARD. First saves the index as ttDifficulty and logs it, then reads diffReqKillCount at that zero-based index and passes the count to SetRequiredKillCount. It next calls ApplyDifficulty with the index on every spawnerDifficulties entry.

Profiles can change the chosen spawn asset, AI configuration, home behavior and placed spawn position/orientation. These are setup changes for later spawning; this method does not call SpawnDifficultyCrates or switch the displayed leaderboard.

The index must exist in diffReqKillCount, and all profile entries must be assigned. There is no bounds clamp. An invalid index can fail after ttDifficulty was already changed, so use a valid difficulty and an array with entries for all supported options.

member.param: Zero-based difficulty index: 0 EASY, 1 MEDIUM or 2 HARD. It must have a matching kill-quota array entry.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Trial_SpawnerEvents.GetTotalCountFromPerc
member.summary: Recalculates the local death quota and records the configured spawner-array length.

remarks.para: The quota is the configured array length multiplied by requiredPerc, then rounded upward to an integer. The array length is the number of crateSpawners entries, and requiredPerc is a unitless fraction: 0.5 means half, while 1 means all. For five entries and 0.5, the product is 2.5 and the quota becomes three deaths. Inactive entries still count toward the length; this does not count how many enemies have actually spawned.

The method stores the rounded result in totalCount and the array length in spawnerCount. It does not use useSpawnerTotal to select another quota formula. This explicit recalculation does not update either text display, invoke OnTotalKillCalc, reset the recorded deaths, or check for completion.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Trial_SpawnerEvents.OnDeath(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.AIBrain)
member.summary: Records one reported AI death, checks the quota and updates the displayed death count.
member.param: The AI brain supplied by the death event. This handler does not read it; each call records one death regardless of which brain is supplied.

remarks.para: A callback is a method another component calls when something happens. The spawn listener connects this callback to a spawned object's AIBrain death event when that object has both an AIBrain, the component controlling its AI, and a recognized pool component. Calling this method directly also adds one to deadCount; it does not check the brain argument or remember whether that enemy was already counted.

Completion is checked when the new deadCount is at least totalCount and sentKillEvent is false. totalCount is the stored local quota, which startup calculates from the configured array length and requiredPerc.

On a qualifying death, the method invokes OnKilledAll if assigned, requests the completion sound, sets sentKillEvent true, and finally updates deadText if assigned. The event has no arguments. Its listeners run before the flag is set and before the displayed count changes, so a listener that calls a death handler again can trigger completion again during that call.

This version requests the completion sound without first checking whether killAllClip is assigned. OnSpawnerDeath performs that clip check. Later calls still increment the count and refresh its text after completion, but normally skip the event while the flag remains true.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Trial_SpawnerEvents.OnDrawGizmosSelected
member.summary: Draws white editor guide lines from this component to its configured spawners when selected.

remarks.para: A gizmo is a guide drawing in Unity's scene editor. This method uses the world positions of this component and each crateSpawners entry as the line endpoints. The guides show which spawners are connected; they do not register listeners, change the death quota or affect gameplay. The configured array and its spawner references must be supplied.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Trial_SpawnerEvents.OnSpawnerDeath
member.summary: Records one death, updates its display and completes the local quota when eligible.

remarks.para: Each call increases deadCount by one. It checks whether that new count is at least totalCount and sentKillEvent is false. It trusts the call as a report of one death rather than checking an enemy or the number of live spawners.

When the test passes, it invokes OnKilledAll if assigned, requests killAllClip only if a valid clip is assigned, and then sets sentKillEvent true. Finally it writes the current count to deadText if assigned. A UnityEvent is a list of listener actions configured to run when the event is invoked; this event passes no arguments.

Listeners therefore see the previous displayed count and a false completion flag while they run. Calling a death handler again inside a listener can trigger completion again before the first call sets that flag. Later ordinary calls still count deaths and update text but skip completion while the flag is true.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TutorialElevator.CloseDoors
member.summary: Requests door closing, damages tracked doorway objects, and removes matching entities from the doorway cleanup box.

remarks.para: Sets isClosing to true before sending voltage 1, a unitless control signal, to every powerableJoints controller. Each controller stores the command even when unpowered, but applies its configured joint settings only when Powered is true. The door physics joints are connections that guide the panels in the physics simulation. Sending the command does not prove the panels have reached their closed positions.

Next, calls doorTrig.OnDoorClose when that trigger is assigned, then runs DoorEmancipator. It does not wait, play the closing sound, seal the panels, or start the ride; those later steps belong to CoDoorRoutine.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TutorialElevator.CoComplete
member.summary: Creates the sequence that briefly applies strong global gravity, restores the saved gravity, and completes the Descent level.

remarks.para: A coroutine is a sequence that can pause and continue on later frames. When Unity runs this one, it first sets Physics.gravity to spikeGravGoal, a world-axis acceleration vector in meters per second squared. It waits for the next fixed-update continuation, then restores startGrav and calls LevelComplete on a GameControl_Descent found in the scene, if one exists.

This changes gravity for the physics scene, including objects outside the elevator. The wait is a physics-update wait, not a configurable number of seconds. StartImpact runs this sequence; merely obtaining its returned sequence does not run it.

startGrav is the saved global gravity captured when CoFallRoutine begins. Its X, Y and Z components are accelerations along the world axes in meters per second squared. Before that capture, the constructor initializes this stored vector to (0, -9.81, 0); it is the stored value, rather than a fresh gravity measurement, that this sequence restores.

member.returns: Sequence for Unity to run with StartCoroutine.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TutorialElevator.CoDoorRoutine
member.summary: Creates the closing sequence that waits, seals the elevator doors, and starts the ride timeline.

remarks.para: A coroutine is a sequence that can pause and continue on later frames. This one first performs CloseDoors: marks closing requested, sends the door controllers voltage 1, handles tracked doorway objects, and removes entities in the cleanup box. It then waits doorWaitDuration seconds of game time, plays doorCloseClip at the elevator, runs SealDoors, and finally calls Play on director.

The delay begins after closing is requested; it is not a period for leaving the doors open. Unity resumes the wait on a later frame, so the actual elapsed time can exceed the requested delay. The sequence does not test whether the panels have arrived. StartElevator runs it only when doorRoutine is null, and natural completion does not clear that handle.

member.returns: Sequence for Unity to run with StartCoroutine.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TutorialElevator.CoFallRoutine
member.summary: Creates the fall transition that reverses the moving shaft scenery and blends the whole scene toward the fall gravity.

remarks.para: A coroutine is a sequence that can pause and continue on later frames. On entry, this one sets the elevator joint's X motion to Limited, changes every tutorial shaft to MOVING_DOWN, copies the current Physics.gravity into startGrav, and resets perc to 0. Limited motion means the physics connection can move within its configured limits.

Over a nominal two seconds of game time, progress p is elapsed game time divided by 2 seconds, limited to 0 through 1. Each update sets shaft speed to fallSpeed times p and global gravity to startGrav plus p times the difference between gravityGoal and startGrav. Both gravity vectors are world-axis accelerations in meters per second squared. fallSpeed is the shaft movement setting in meters per second before the movement-per-iteration calculation described below.

Once the shared progress reaches 1, the next continuation starts CoFallingZeroG. The cab is not directly translated down the shaft by this routine: the shaft scenery moves upward along each shaft's own Y axis to simulate falling.

Each shaft movement iteration multiplies its speed setting by Time.fixedDeltaTime, the configured physics-step duration in seconds, to obtain a movement distance in Unity length units, conventionally meters. The loop pauses and resumes across frames, so this timestep calculation does not guarantee the same distance per second of real elapsed time.

member.returns: Sequence for Unity to run with StartCoroutine.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TutorialElevator.CoFallingZeroG
member.summary: Creates the near-weightless fall sequence, turning on both spark objects and moving the elevator joint's Y target.

remarks.para: A coroutine is a sequence that can pause and continue on later frames. This one activates the GameObjects holding rightSparkler and leftSparkler, captures the current global gravity, and resets perc to 0. Over a nominal three seconds of game time it blends that gravity toward (0, -0.1, 0) meters per second squared in world axes. This is weak downward gravity, not exactly zero gravity.

The curve's horizontal input is progress p: elapsed game time divided by 3 seconds, limited to 0 through 1. The Y target is 5 times yCurve(p) meters; for example, a curve value of 0.4 requests 2 meters. Each update stores that result in yPos and writes (xPos, yPos, zPos) to vatorJoint.targetPosition. xPos and zPos are the stored X and Z target lengths in meters, carried through unchanged. These are target-position coordinates for the physics connection, not the cab's measured world position; the joint's configuration determines the axes and how closely the cab follows.
The loop ends after progress reaches 1. It does not turn the spark objects off or restore gravity at that point; StartImpact and CoComplete perform those later actions.

member.returns: Sequence for Unity to run with StartCoroutine.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TutorialElevator.CoInitialBreakRoutine
member.summary: Creates the two-second slowdown of the moving shaft scenery before the fall.

remarks.para: A coroutine is a sequence that can pause and continue on later frames. It maps elapsed game time over two seconds to progress p between 0 and 1, then writes stage1Speed times (1 - p) into every shaft's speed. stage1Speed is the initial ascent-scenery speed setting. With stage1Speed = 2, the setting is 1 halfway through and 0 at the end. These speed settings are in meters per second before each shaft loop multiplies by the physics-step duration.

This sequence shares perc with the other movement sequences and does not reset it on entry. If perc is already 1 or higher, it ends without slowing the shafts. SlowUpwardMovement runs the sequence and stores its handle in moveUpRoutine.

member.returns: Sequence for Unity to run with StartCoroutine.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TutorialElevator.CoSwing
member.summary: Creates a temporary change to the elevator's physics pivot that encourages the swinging motion.

remarks.para: A coroutine is a sequence that can pause and continue on later frames. This one sets vatorJoint.anchor to (0, -0.25, 0), waits one second of game time, then sets the anchor to (0, 0, 0). The anchor is the connection point on the joint's own object, expressed along that object's local axes. The distance values are Unity length units, conventionally meters when its scale is 1.

ReleaseJointRot starts this after changing the joint motion limits. This sequence itself changes the pivot, not the angular limits, and it does not guarantee a particular swing angle. SwingImpact can change the anchor again while the wait is in progress.

member.returns: Sequence for Unity to run with StartCoroutine.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TutorialElevator.DoorEmancipator
member.summary: Plays despawn effects and removes matching Marrow entities overlapping the doorway cleanup box.

remarks.para: The box is centered at emancipatorPoint's world position and turned to match its world rotation. emancipatorBounds gives the full side lengths in meters; the physics query uses half of each value. For example, (2, 1, 0.5) makes a box extending 1 meter, 0.5 meter, and 0.25 meter each way along the point's rotated axes. The point's scale does not resize this query.

Only solid colliders in layerMask are queried; trigger colliders are ignored. For each result, the routine looks up the attached Rigidbody's MarrowBody, then collects its owning entity. A Rigidbody is the component that lets an object participate as a moving body in physics. An entity found through several colliders is removed only once, and its despawn effect is called before Despawn.

The selected colliders must have attached Rigidbodies. The routine does not safely skip a collider without one. A failed MarrowBody cache lookup is skipped. CloseDoors calls this cleanup immediately after requesting closure.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TutorialElevator.EnterExitElevator(System.Boolean)
member.summary: Sets the player-inside flag that allows StartElevator to begin the door sequence.

remarks.para: This directly stores the supplied value in playerInElevator. It does not check the player's position, detect a trigger crossing, or start or stop an existing ride. With the flag false, StartElevator returns without beginning its sequence.

member.param: True when entering; false when leaving.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TutorialElevator.LimitJointRot
member.summary: Sets the elevator joint's Y and Z angular limits to 1 degree, reducing how far it can tilt on those axes.

remarks.para: A physics joint is a connection that constrains movement between objects. This changes the configured Y and Z angle limits and sets their bounce and contact-distance values to 0. It does not change their motion modes, change the X angle limits, or force the current cab rotation to a specific angle. These limits take effect when those axes use limited motion.

Bounce controls how much the body rebounds when it reaches an angle limit. Contact distance is the margin for starting to handle that limit as the body approaches it; for these angular limits the margin is measured in degrees. This method sets both values to 0 for the Y and Z limits.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TutorialElevator.OPENCLOSEDOOR(System.Boolean)
member.summary: Sends the optional door power source a signed command: -1 for open or +1 for close.

remarks.para: The output is a control signal with no distance or speed units. The connected power logic decides how that signal drives the doors. If doorPower is absent, this call does nothing. It does not update isClosing or run the doorway cleanup done by CloseDoors.

member.param: True sends the open command (-1); false sends the close command (+1). Defaults to true.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TutorialElevator.OnDrawGizmosSelected
member.summary: Draws a cyan wire box in Unity's editor to show the doorway cleanup area when this component is selected.

remarks.para: The preview uses emancipatorPoint's world position and rotation and emancipatorBounds as the full box size. It draws nothing when the point is unassigned. A gizmo is an editor drawing for setup; this call does not detect or remove objects.
The three emancipatorBounds components are the full side lengths in Unity length units, conventionally meters, along the point's rotated axes. The point's own scale is not multiplied into this size.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TutorialElevator.OpenDoors
member.summary: Requests open positions from every configured door joint controller and clears the closing-request flag.

remarks.para: Sets isClosing to false before sending voltage 0 to each powerableJoints controller. A physics joint is the connection guiding a door panel. The controller must be powered, and its own settings determine which position or drive it changes. The request does not prove the panel is already open.
This does not stop doorRoutine, reactivate doorway triggers, or undo the fixed panel placement made by SealDoors. Calling it alone during the closing sequence does not cancel the later sealing step.
A drive is the joint's force settings that try to make the panel follow a requested position or speed.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TutorialElevator.ReleaseJointRot
member.summary: Allows limited movement on all three rotation axes and the Y/Z sliding axes, then starts the temporary swinging-pivot sequence.

remarks.para: The physics joint is the connection that guides the elevator cab. This sets angular X, Y and Z and linear Y and Z to Limited, so movement remains constrained by the joint's configured limits. It leaves linear X unchanged.

It then starts CoSwing, a coroutine: a sequence that continues across frames. That sequence briefly shifts the local anchor down by 0.25 Unity length units, conventionally meters at scale 1, and restores it after a one-second game-time wait.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TutorialElevator.SealDoors
member.summary: Locks the door panels into their scripted closed positions and changes the surrounding objects for the ride.

remarks.para: First clears isClosing, disables doorTrigCol, and activates both ogShaftObj and otherShaftObj. It hides every outerDoorObjs object, makes every doorBodies Rigidbody kinematic, and sets every vatorColliders object to Unity layer 0. Kinematic means physics forces no longer move that Rigidbody; a script can still position it.

It then sets the first four door panels' parent-relative X positions to fixed values of about -1.60, -0.34, -1.60 and -0.33, preserving their Y/Z positions, and activates shaftColliderObj. The array must contain at least four valid panels in the expected order. These coordinates are local Unity length units, conventionally meters with parent scale 1.
This does not wait for physical closure. CoDoorRoutine calls it after its timed delay, before starting director.
A Rigidbody is the Unity component that simulates an object as a physics body.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TutorialElevator.SlowUpwardMovement
member.summary: Starts a nominal two-second slowdown of the shaft scenery from stage1Speed to zero.

remarks.para: Starts CoInitialBreakRoutine and stores its handle in moveUpRoutine. A coroutine is a sequence that continues across frames. The sequence writes each shaft's speed as stage1Speed times (1 - p), where p is elapsed game time divided by 2 seconds, limited to 0 through 1.

The sequence does not reset the shared perc value on entry; perc already at 1 or higher makes it finish without changing speeds. This call does not stop a previous slowdown before starting another, and it does not directly translate the cab.

stage1Speed is the initial shaft-scenery speed setting, in meters per second before the shaft loop's timestep calculation. Each movement iteration multiplies the current speed setting by Time.fixedDeltaTime, the physics-step duration in seconds, to get movement distance in Unity length units, conventionally meters. The shaft loop pauses across frames, so this is not a guarantee of the cab's actual speed.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TutorialElevator.StartElevator
member.summary: If the player-inside flag is true, begins the timed door-closing sequence and makes the cached player health invincible.

remarks.para: The check uses playerInElevator, a stored flag; this call does not measure where the player stands. It first requests an achievement unlock and sends +1 to doorPower when assigned. It starts CoDoorRoutine only when doorRoutine is null. A coroutine is a sequence that continues across frames; this one requests closing, waits doorWaitDuration seconds of game time, seals the doors, then starts director.

Next, it obtains the player's health component from PlayerRefs when the cached pHealth is missing and sets its health mode to Invincible if found. A non-null doorRoutine can remain after natural completion, so repeated calls need not start a fresh door sequence. They can still repeat the power and health setup.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TutorialElevator.StartImpact
member.summary: Stops the shaft scenery, turns off the sparks, freezes the cab's physics motion, and starts the gravity pulse and level completion.

remarks.para: Sets each tutorial shaft to STOPPED and cancels its loop, disables the GameObjects holding both spark particle systems, and makes elevatorBody kinematic. A Rigidbody is a moving physics body; kinematic mode prevents forces from moving it.

When pHealth is assigned, it calls that component's Dying routine with argument 8; this is not a normal 8-point damage call. In the Invincible health mode set by StartElevator, the inspected Player_Health implementation sets current health to 0 without calling Death. Other health modes have different behavior.

Finally starts CoComplete, a coroutine: a sequence that continues across updates. It applies spikeGravGoal globally until the next fixed-update continuation, restores startGrav, then completes the Descent level if its game controller is found. This method itself does not detect a collision or wait for the cab to hit the shaft bottom.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TutorialElevator.StartMoveDownward
member.summary: Stops the stored slowdown sequence and starts the shaft-speed and global-gravity transition into falling.

remarks.para: If moveUpRoutine is assigned, stops that coroutine without clearing its stored handle. A coroutine is a sequence that continues across frames. It then starts CoFallRoutine, which sets shafts to their downward-ride state, resets perc, saves the current gravity, and ramps shaft speed from 0 to fallSpeed over a nominal two seconds of game time while changing global gravity toward gravityGoal.
This call does not start the shaft loops itself or stop a previously started fall sequence. The usual upward phase starts those loops first.

fallSpeed is the target shaft-scenery speed setting in meters per second. Each shaft movement iteration uses its current speed setting times Time.fixedDeltaTime, the physics-step duration in seconds, as its movement distance in Unity length units, conventionally meters, even though the loop resumes across frames. gravityGoal is the target global gravity vector: its X, Y and Z components specify acceleration along the world axes in meters per second squared. This gravity affects the whole physics scene.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TutorialElevator.StartMoveUpward
member.summary: Starts the shaft scenery loops that simulate the elevator ascending and enables doorSeel when assigned.

remarks.para: First starts every tutShafts loop, then sets each shaft to MOVING_UP and copies stage1Speed into its speed. In that state, the scenery moves opposite each shaft's own Y axis; the elevator cab is not directly translated upward by this method.

Each shaft loop uses speed times Time.fixedDeltaTime as its movement per iteration. That is the physics-step duration in seconds, even though the loop continues through asynchronous frame waits. Repeating this call starts additional loops without first cancelling existing ones.

stage1Speed is the initial shaft-scenery speed setting in meters per second, copied into each shaft when this call runs. An asynchronous frame wait lets the work pause and resume on a later frame instead of completing the whole loop in this call.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TutorialElevator.StopDoorRoutine
member.summary: Stops the stored timed door sequence, plays the abort sound, and clears the handle so another sequence can start.

remarks.para: Stops doorRoutine if its handle is assigned, then plays abortDoorClip at the elevator's world position and finally sets doorRoutine to null. The sound is requested even when there was no assigned handle.

A coroutine is a sequence that continues across frames. Stopping this one prevents its later timed steps, but does not reopen doors, clear isClosing, undo already sealed panels, or stop a director timeline that has already started.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TutorialElevator.SwingImpact
member.summary: Moves the elevator joint's local connection point to (0, 0.5, 0), changing the pivot for the scripted impact.

remarks.para: The anchor is where the physics connection attaches to its own object. These coordinates are along that object's local axes in Unity length units, conventionally meters at scale 1. This changes the connection point immediately; it does not apply a force, detect a collision, or set a guaranteed swing angle.
If CoSwing is still waiting, its later continuation resets the anchor to (0, 0, 0).

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TutorialRig.DEACTIVETUTORIAL
member.summary: Ends the active controller tutorial, fades its art and tooltips out, and hides its direction arrows.

remarks.para: This cancels the scheduled DEACTIVETUTORIAL call first. If tutorialActive is false, it stops there. Otherwise it requests the controller and tooltip fade-out, deactivates every arrow object, sets tutorialActive to false, and clears cur_activeTutorial.

The visual fade can continue after the active flag is cleared. The controllerTitles object is hidden after the longer of the two tooltips' timeToHighlight values, measured in seconds. This method ends the display; it does not mark the trigger as completed or change its repeat count. Both tooltip references and the arrow arrays must be assigned.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TutorialRig.GrippedLeft(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandReciever)
member.summary: Marks the left tooltip as belonging to a hand that is holding an object.
member.param: The receiver from the hand event; this method does not inspect it.

remarks.para: The normal level-load setup connects this callback to the left hand's receiver-attached event. It sets toolTip_left.isHoldingObject to true. The receiver argument is ignored; this does not grab the object or complete a tutorial.

While the tooltip follows its controller art, this flag adds a 0.2-meter (20 cm) offset along the tooltip's own forward direction before the position is limited and smoothed. It changes the requested placement, so the final displayed movement need not be exactly 20 cm.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TutorialRig.GrippedRight(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandReciever)
member.summary: Marks the right tooltip as belonging to a hand that is holding an object.
member.param: The receiver from the hand event; this method does not inspect it.

remarks.para: The normal level-load setup connects this callback to the right hand's receiver-attached event. It sets toolTip_right.isHoldingObject to true. The receiver argument is ignored; this does not grab the object or complete a tutorial.

While the tooltip follows its controller art, this flag adds a 0.2-meter (20 cm) offset along the tooltip's own forward direction before the position is limited and smoothed. It changes the requested placement, so the final displayed movement need not be exactly 20 cm.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TutorialRig.TUTORIALSCALE(System.Single)
member.summary: Resizes the entire tutorial rig to suit the avatar's eye height.
member.param: Vertical distance from the avatar model's Animator-root position to its eye center, in meters; must be positive.

remarks.para: The model root is the Animator object's base position; the supplied height measures the eye center's vertical height above that position. The method sets all three components of this object's local scale to avatarEyeHeight / standardHeight multiplied by tutorialScale. Eye height and standardHeight are distances in meters; their ratio and tutorialScale are unitless multipliers. With illustrative values standardHeight = 1.6, avatarEyeHeight = 0.8, and tutorialScale = 1, the resulting local scale is (0.5, 0.5, 0.5).

This replaces the existing local scale instead of multiplying it, so repeating the same call does not keep shrinking the rig. A zero or negative eye height logs a message and leaves scale unchanged. standardHeight is not checked before division, so provide a positive reference height.

The normal BodyVitals UI-layout update passes the current avatar's calculated eye height. Changing the two scaling fields alone does not resize anything until this method runs. Neither field is overwritten with the resulting scale.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TutorialRig.UngrippedLeft(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandReciever)
member.summary: Returns the left tooltip to its placement for a hand that is not holding an object.
member.param: The receiver from the hand event; this method does not inspect it.

remarks.para: The normal level-load setup connects this callback to the left hand's receiver-detached event. It sets toolTip_left.isHoldingObject to false, removing the extra forward offset used by the following calculation.
The receiver argument is ignored. This does not release an object, hide the tooltip, or end a tutorial; the tooltip continues using its normal position limits and smoothing.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TutorialRig.UngrippedRight(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.HandReciever)
member.summary: Returns the right tooltip to its placement for a hand that is not holding an object.
member.param: The receiver from the hand event; this method does not inspect it.

remarks.para: The normal level-load setup connects this callback to the right hand's receiver-detached event. It sets toolTip_right.isHoldingObject to false, removing the extra forward offset used by the following calculation.
The receiver argument is ignored. This does not release an object, hide the tooltip, or end a tutorial; the tooltip continues using its normal position limits and smoothing.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.UIControllerInput.RemoveCursorTargetOverride
member.summary: Clears the override so later reads return cursorTarget instead.

remarks.para: A Transform holds a scene object's position, rotation and scale. This method clears _cursorTargetOverride without moving either Transform or changing the default cursorTarget. The fallback takes effect when a consumer next asks for CursorTarget.

It does not force an already-open menu to rebuild its position or alter consumers that read cursorTarget directly. For example, LaserCursor.Initialize caches the default cursorTarget reference without consulting the override.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.UIControllerInput.ResetLevel
member.summary: Requests the configured fadeout effect and arranges a scene reload when that effect reports completion.

remarks.para: It obtains the default fadeout spawnable from MarrowSettings, registers it with AssetSpawner and requests a spawn. A spawnable is an asset the game can create as an object in the scene. When the object arrives, a callback, a routine called to perform or report an action, obtains its FadeVolume component and assigns a completion callback. That completion callback calls SceneStreamer.Reload.

The FadeVolume sequence runs over frames and applies its final visual settings before invoking onComplete. ResetLevel returns after the spawn request; it does not directly reload in its own body, wait for the fade, or prove that the level has finished reloading. It requires working runtime settings, an available effect with FadeVolume and a successful completion path.

A coroutine is a sequence that continues across several frames. This public method does not check the held-button timer or m_canOpenMenu. The hold-to-reset coroutine calls it after its own threshold check; a direct call bypasses that wait. The spawn callback replaces the effect's onComplete callback list rather than adding to it.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.UIRig.UI_AVATARSCALE(System.Single)
member.summary: Resizes the listed UI transforms for the avatar's arm length and records the arm-length ratio.
member.param: The avatar's calculated arm length in meters; must be positive.

remarks.para: The ratio is armLength / standardArmLength. Here standardArmLength is the reference arm length in metres, and uiScale is the extra unitless size multiplier. Both lengths are distances in meters. Each transform in scaleOffset gets a new local scale of (ratio × uiScale, ratio × uiScale, ratio × uiScale). With illustrative lengths 0.8 and 0.4 meters and uiScale = 1, the result is (2, 2, 2). Raising uiScale to 1.5 makes it (3, 3, 3).

This replaces each transform's local scale, so repeated calls with the same input do not multiply the previous size again. cur_avatarArmScaleMult stores the ratio before uiScale is applied. Zero or negative armLength logs a message and leaves the old ratio and scales unchanged. standardArmLength is not checked before division; give it a positive value, and provide an assigned array with non-null transforms.

The normal BodyVitals UI-layout refresh also copies the ratio to the pop-up menu and updates its starting position. Calling this method alone does not perform those extra menu-distance steps. Changing scaling fields alone takes effect when scaling is next applied.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.UI_HUD.#ctor
member.summary: Sets initial HUD distances, ammo-warning thresholds, empty text and scaling times.

remarks.para: The initial head distance is 1 world unit, normally 1 metre. The empty-ammo text is "EMPTY". The light and medium low-ammo thresholds start at 30 rounds each; the heavy threshold starts at 6 rounds.

timeToScale starts at 1 second, while the separate internal _resetLevel_timeToScale starts at 0.5 seconds. The reset animation reads the internal value, so the public one is not its duration in the inspected HUD methods. Other component references still need scene setup. Unity may replace these constructor values with saved scene or prefab settings.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.UI_HUD.AmmoFollow_Coroutine
member.summary: Creates the routine that shows or hides ammo and copies its selected target’s world pose.
member.returns: An iterator for the ammo-placement routine; the routine runs only when the iterator is advanced or started as a coroutine.

remarks.para: A coroutine is a routine that can pause and continue later. Calling this method only creates its iterator, the object that remembers the routine’s next step; it does not start the routine by itself.

When run, the routine reads ammo_displayLocation on each step. Belt, Head and Inventory activate hud_AMMO and choose their target transform; Head reads lowAmmoPopupRight each time to choose a side. It copies world position and rotation, without smoothing, scaling or changing the target’s parent. It pauses between steps until Unity’s next physics update, the update where the game advances simulated motion. The timing follows game time and frame scheduling.

None deactivates hud_AMMO, uses this HUD component’s own transform as the placement, copies that pose once, waits for a physics update and then ends. Its stored _co_ammo_follow reference is not cleared when it ends. SHOWAMMO normally creates, stores and starts this routine.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.UI_HUD.Awake
member.summary: Registers OnLevelLoad with the current scene-loading session so the HUD can bind to the player.

remarks.para: Awake is Unity’s early component setup call. A callback is a function registered to run when another system reaches a particular stage. This method registers OnLevelLoad for the session’s DoLevelLoad stage.

The session calls the function immediately if the session is already marked done; otherwise it stores the function for later. Thus HUD setup can happen during this Awake call. The player references and ammo inventory must be ready when the callback runs. This method does not itself position the HUD or start an ammo-follow routine.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.UI_HUD.CheckAmmoForHeldGuns
member.summary: Checks the cached right and left guns’ stored-ammo groups, then hides ammo unless Inventory mode is selected.

remarks.para: For each non-null cached WeaponSlot, it tries to find a Gun on that slot’s object and looks up the group for the gun’s cartridge type. A WeaponSlot is the component that identifies an inventory-compatible held weapon.

The low-ammo test compares stored group rounds with that group’s threshold using less than or equal: with a threshold of 30, 30 rounds is low and 31 is not. This method discards that result; it does not set showLowAmmoPopup or open a warning popup. It checks inventory ammo, not the gun’s loaded magazine.

Outside Inventory mode, it calls SHOWAMMO(None) to hide the ammo module and turns head following off if _followingHead is true. Inventory mode keeps its current display. These effects also apply when a cached gun exists; they do not depend on the discarded low-ammo answer.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.UI_HUD.DisplayAmmo
member.summary: Writes stored light, medium and heavy ammo counts into the assigned text components.

remarks.para: It reads the ammo inventory’s group totals for "light", "medium" and "heavy". Each number counts stored rounds in that group. It does not read how many rounds remain in a held gun’s magazine.

A total exactly equal to zero is displayed as emptyNote, initially "EMPTY"; any other integer is converted to text. For example, a light count of 25 displays "25", and a count of zero displays the configured empty message. A missing text component is skipped independently.

This method changes text only. It does not activate hud_AMMO or choose a placement. UIHudSetup calls it during setup, and UpdateUI calls it when the subscribed ammo event runs. Direct field changes need a refresh before the displayed text changes.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.UI_HUD.HUD_SoftFollow
member.summary: Creates the routine that smoothly moves the head-follower target in front of the cached head.
member.returns: An iterator for head-following motion; creating it alone does not move the target.

remarks.para: A coroutine is a routine that can pause and continue later. Calling this method only creates its iterator, the object that remembers the routine’s next step; it does not start the routine by itself.

Each step reads the head’s world position and forward direction. The desired point is head position plus forward direction multiplied by offset_HeadDistance, measured in world units, normally metres. It smooths motion toward that point with a maximum positional lag of 0.2 metres, an offset-return rate of 5 per second and a smoothing time of 0.1 seconds.

It writes target_HEADFOLLOWER’s world position. Its forward direction points from the head toward that follower point, with the scene’s up direction as up; individual widget orientation depends on scene setup. It pauses between steps until Unity’s next physics update, the update where the game advances simulated motion. The timing follows game time and frame scheduling.

HEADHUDFOLLOW(true) initializes the smoothing history, activates the target object and starts this routine. A missing head makes a step skip its pose update; the routine still waits and tries again. The routine itself does not test _followingHead each step, so changing that bool alone does not stop it.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.UI_HUD.HeadFollowTimmer
member.summary: Creates the routine that follows the head until its remaining game-time countdown runs out.
member.returns: An iterator for the timed head-follow routine; HEADHUDFOLLOWTIMED normally stores and starts it.

remarks.para: A coroutine is a routine that can pause and continue later. Calling this method only creates its iterator, the object that remembers the routine’s next step; it does not start the routine by itself.

When run, it first tests _headFollowCountDown in seconds. If the value is positive, it enables head following when needed, subtracts Unity’s reported game-time step and waits for the next physics update. Game time follows slow motion and pause settings.

On a later step when the countdown is zero or negative, it calls HEADHUDFOLLOW(false), which resets and hides the follower target, clears _co_headFollowTimmer and ends. Subtraction happens after the test, so a step can make the countdown negative before the next step performs shutdown.
HEADHUDFOLLOWTIMED(seconds) stores the starting countdown and replaces the old timer iterator. The duration is a countdown input, not an exact real-time completion timestamp.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.UI_HUD.OnDisable
member.summary: Unsubscribes this HUD from ammo and hand-slot changes, then stops its coroutines.

remarks.para: OnDisable is Unity’s call when a component becomes inactive. It removes UpdateUI from the ammo inventory’s update event, then removes the left and right hand insertion and removal handlers from the player’s inventory. After those removals, it stops all coroutines, routines that can pause and resume later, on this component.

This cleanup requires the current ammo inventory and player inventory references. It does not clear the iterator fields, hide either module, or reset _followingHead and _resetting. Its complete native body does not remove the scene-session callback added in Awake. Re-enabling alone does not call UIHudSetup.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.UI_HUD.OnEnable
member.summary: Stops every coroutine currently running on this HUD component when it is enabled.

remarks.para: OnEnable is Unity’s call when a component becomes active. A coroutine is a routine that can pause and continue later. The complete native method calls StopAllCoroutines only, even though its shared native label names another class’s disable method.

It does not clear the stored iterator fields or reset _followingHead and _resetting. Those stored values can therefore remain after their routines have stopped. It also does not call UIHudSetup to restore subscriptions.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.UI_HUD.OnLevelLoad
member.summary: Replaces the cached head with the player physics rig’s head and runs UIHudSetup.

remarks.para: This is the function registered for the scene session’s DoLevelLoad stage. It reads the current player physics rig, the rig whose body movement the game simulates, and stores its head transform in _playerHead. A transform describes an object’s position, orientation and size.

It then calls UIHudSetup to subscribe to inventory changes and refresh the ammo text and held-gun checks. This refresh explicitly replaces the head cache. By comparison, UIHudSetup and UpdateUI use the controller rig’s head only when that cache is missing. The session stage is the trigger; this method does not prove that every part of scene loading has finished.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.UI_HUD.ProgressBar
member.summary: Creates the routine that decreases the reset bar’s material value over a two-game-second countdown.
member.returns: An iterator for the progress-material countdown; creating it alone does not change the bar.

remarks.para: A coroutine is a routine that can pause and continue later. Calling this method only creates its iterator, the object that remembers the routine’s next step; it does not start the routine by itself.

When run, it starts an elapsed counter at zero and uses a duration of 2 seconds. While elapsed time is below 2, it writes clamp(1 - elapsed / 2, 0, 1) to the bar material’s "_Float0" property. Here elapsed is accumulated game time in seconds; clamp limits the written unitless value to the range 0 through 1. For example, the value is 1 at the first sample and 0.5 at one accumulated second.

After each material write it adds Unity’s reported game-time step and waits for the next physics update. Game time follows slow motion and pause settings; completion occurs on a later step when the counter reaches or exceeds 2 seconds. It then clears _co_progressBar and ends. It does not explicitly write a final zero at completion.

The material must interpret "_Float0" to draw the intended bar. This routine only animates that material value: it does not reload the scene. Opening the reset popup starts it when no progress iterator is stored; closing stops it and clears the stored reference.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.UI_HUD.SHOWAMMO(Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.UI_HUD.AmmoDisplayLocation)
member.summary: Selects an ammo placement and replaces the routine that applies that placement.
member.param: Where to place the ammo module. None (the default) hides it; Belt, Head and Inventory choose their corresponding target transforms.

remarks.para: It stops the previous ammo-follow iterator when present, stores ammoLocation in ammo_displayLocation, creates and stores a new iterator, then starts it. A coroutine is a routine that pauses and resumes later; an iterator remembers its next step.

None hides hud_AMMO. Belt shows it at target_ammo_belt. Head shows it at target_ammo_head_right when lowAmmoPopupRight is true, otherwise at target_ammo_head_left. Inventory shows it at target_ammo_inventory. The visible modes copy the target’s world position and orientation immediately and after each physics update.

The method does not change the ammo text or start head following itself. Assign the relevant target and hud_AMMO before selecting a visible mode. Calling it again replaces the follower even if the location value is unchanged.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.UI_HUD.Start
member.summary: Routes reset-display audio through the game’s UI mixer and hides both HUD modules.

remarks.para: Start is Unity’s setup call before this component’s first update. It assigns sfx_resetLevel to Audio3dManager’s UI mixer group, then deactivates hud_AMMO, then deactivates hud_RESETLEVEL. Deactivated objects do not display their HUD graphics.
Assign the audio source and both HUD root objects before this call. This call does not subscribe to ammo changes or find the player head; UIHudSetup performs that separate work.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.UI_HUD.UIHudSetup
member.summary: Subscribes the HUD to ammo and hand-slot changes and immediately refreshes ammo information.

remarks.para: First it adds UpdateUI to AmmoInventory’s onAmmoUpdate event, a notification that runs listener functions when stored ammo changes. If _playerHead is missing, it takes the controller rig’s head from PlayerRefs; a transform records that head object’s position and orientation.

It calls DisplayAmmo and then CheckAmmoForHeldGuns. After that initial refresh, it subscribes the left/right hand insertion and removal handlers to the player inventory. Those handlers update the corresponding cached WeaponSlot when an inserted object has the required gun components.

The ammo inventory and player references must exist before this call. Repeated calls add the ammo-update listener again: the method does not remove that subscription first.
