OnDisable removes listeners separately. This method refreshes information; it does not directly begin head following or display a low-ammo popup.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.UI_HUD.UpdateUI
member.summary: Refreshes stored-ammo text and checks the cached guns, finding a head reference if needed.

remarks.para: If _playerHead is missing, this method caches the controller rig’s head from PlayerRefs. It then calls DisplayAmmo followed by CheckAmmoForHeldGuns.

DisplayAmmo uses the ammo inventory’s light, medium and heavy group counts, in rounds, rather than the cartridges inside a gun’s magazine. The held-gun check currently discards its low-ammo results and hides the ammo module outside Inventory mode. This method does not subscribe to future updates; UIHudSetup performs that step.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.VRInputModule.ClearSelection
member.summary: Clears cached pointer hover targets and removes the EventSystem’s selected scene object.

remarks.para: The EventSystem is Unity’s manager for menu input and selection. For every cached pointer, this method first tells it to leave its hovered objects. The hover handlers receive that pointer’s own PointerEventData, the record containing its target and input details. In this path Unity sends a pointer-move notification before a pointer-exit notification to each hovered object, then clears the hover list and target.

After handling all cached pointers, clears m_PointerData and asks the EventSystem to select no object. That last operation uses general event data from this module, rather than one of the pointer records. For example, a menu can clear its old hovered button and keyboard selection before another menu takes over.

This does not reset the stored origin, direction or press flag, and it does not replace m_MouseState. Its old button record can still reference a pointer object that was removed from the dictionary; the next mouse-data refresh reconnects it to the new or reused cached record. It is not a request to destroy UI objects or stop polling input.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.VRInputModule.GetMousePointerEventData
member.summary: Refreshes the primary simulated mouse pointer and returns its shared button state and first usable raycast result.

remarks.para: Gets or creates the cached pointer with ID -1, resets its general event-used state, sets its 2D position to (0, 0), sets its 2D movement delta to (1, 0), clears scroll movement, marks it as dragging and labels its button as Left. The delta is a fixed one-unit move in pointer coordinates, not the measured movement of a controller between frames.

Copies the latest m_RaycastOrigin and m_RaycastNormal into the pointer’s world-position and world-normal fields, then asks the EventSystem’s registered raycasters to find hits. A raycaster is a component that tests pointer data against objects. Saves the first result whose object is valid and updates m_MouseState.hasHitUIElement from that result. The temporary hit list is cleared afterward.

The registered raycaster decides which pointer fields to read. The inspected VRGraphicRaycaster uses the 2D position; this helper keeps that at zero. Supplying a 3D origin and direction alone therefore does not guarantee a hit test along that 3D direction, or a cursor moved to the matching spot on a menu.

Writes the left button state as Pressed when the latest supplied m_InputPressed is true, otherwise Released. It does not compare with a previous value to report only the moment a physical button changes. Supplying true on two refreshes produces Pressed on both; a caller that wants a one-update press must supply that pulse and then supply false. It refreshes only the left entry and does not create right- or middle-button events.

Returns the same stored MouseState object on successive calls. This helper collects data; VRStandaloneInputModule later uses it for press/release and hover handling. It does not itself send a click or update pointerEnter, the cached hover object checked by IsPointerOverGameObject. A fresh hit result and that older hover cache can therefore temporarily differ.

member.returns: The shared MouseState, refreshed with the left-button event record and whether the first usable raycast result contains a valid object. Later refreshes mutate this same object.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.VRInputModule.IsPointerOverGameObject(System.Int32)
member.summary: Reports whether the requested cached pointer currently has a valid hover target.

remarks.para: Looks up pointerId in m_PointerData without creating an entry. Returns false if no record exists; otherwise checks pointerEnter, the scene object last recorded by hover processing. A GameObject is an object in the Unity scene. This test uses Unity’s valid-object check, so a destroyed hover object does not count.

For the primary simulated mouse pointer use -1, the value of kMouseLeftId; a touch record uses its own supplied finger ID. The number 0 used for the Left button type is a different identifier and does not select the -1 mouse cache entry.

It does not perform a new raycast or test the currently selected object. For example, after ClearSelection it returns false until a pointer record and its hover target are established again. After only collecting a new hit with GetMousePointerEventData, the result can still reflect the previous hover target until movement/hover processing runs.

member.param: The pointer-cache ID to look up. Use -1 for the primary simulated mouse pointer, or the finger ID supplied for a touch record.
member.returns: True when an existing pointer record has a valid cached hover object; false when the record or its hover object is absent or the object was destroyed.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.VRInputModule.MouseButtonEventData.PressedThisFrame
member.summary: Reports whether the stored button state includes a press, including a press and release recorded together.

remarks.para: This checks buttonState: Pressed and PressedAndReleased return true; Released and NotChanged return false. For example, a PressedAndReleased record makes both this method and ReleasedThisFrame return true.

It reads the prepared record rather than polling the controller or checking the current frame’s clock. Calling it does not clear the state or send a UI event; updating the record determines what later queries see.

member.returns: True for Pressed or PressedAndReleased; otherwise false.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.VRInputModule.MouseButtonEventData.ReleasedThisFrame
member.summary: Reports whether the stored button state includes a release, including a press and release recorded together.

remarks.para: This checks buttonState: Released and PressedAndReleased return true; Pressed and NotChanged return false. For example, a PressedAndReleased record makes both this method and PressedThisFrame return true.

It reads the prepared record rather than polling the controller or checking the current frame’s clock. Calling it does not clear the state or send a UI event; updating the record determines what later queries see.

member.returns: True for Released or PressedAndReleased; otherwise false.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.VRInputModule.MouseState.AnyPressesThisFrame
member.summary: Reports whether any cached button event is marked Pressed or PressedAndReleased.

remarks.para: The method scans every record in m_TrackedButtons and returns as soon as it finds either label. PressedAndReleased means the record includes both a press and a release, so both this method and AnyReleasesThisFrame return true for that record. An empty list returns false.

This reads saved event data; it does not sample a controller, perform a raycast, or check a frame timestamp. Reading it does not clear the labels. For example, after storing Pressed for the left button, repeated calls return true until that record is changed.

Refresh the records before treating the answer as input for a new frame. The base VRInputModule producer writes Pressed for its stored pressed-input flag and Released for its false state on each sample; it does not compare that flag with its previous value here. A true answer from that path therefore does not by itself prove a newly started press.

member.returns: true if at least one tracked event record is Pressed or PressedAndReleased; otherwise false.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.VRInputModule.MouseState.AnyReleasesThisFrame
member.summary: Reports whether any cached button event is marked Released or PressedAndReleased.

remarks.para: The method scans every record in m_TrackedButtons and returns as soon as it finds either label. PressedAndReleased means the record includes both a press and a release, so both this method and AnyPressesThisFrame return true for that record. An empty list returns false.

This reads saved event data; it does not sample a controller, perform a raycast, or check a frame timestamp. It leaves the labels unchanged. For example, storing Released for the left button makes repeated calls return true until that record is changed.

Refresh the records before treating the answer as input for a new frame. The base VRInputModule producer writes Released whenever its stored pressed-input flag is false on a sample. It does not compare that flag with its previous value here, so this can report a release label even if the input was already unpressed.

member.returns: true if at least one tracked event record is Released or PressedAndReleased; otherwise false.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.WeaponPack.OnDespawnWeapon
member.summary: Removes the pack's current host registrations from reset handling and then marks the pack as not spawned.

remarks.para: It asks WeaponResetVolume to remove weaponHost and, when present, magHost from its shared host-to-pack lookup. The magazine removal is inside the branch that first finds the weapon-host entry.

After that call returns, it sets isSpawned to false. It does not itself return objects to the pool, destroy them, clear saved object/component references, or remove the grip-attachment callbacks added by OnSpawnWeapon.

The separate WeaponSpawner despawn path detaches the weapon host when needed, requests the weapon Poolee's despawn, clears spawnedWeaponObj, processes a secondary pack, and then performs this bookkeeping. Calling this method alone only changes registration and the flag.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.WeaponPack.OnSpawnWeapon
member.summary: Registers the existing weapon and optional magazine hosts for reset handling, marks the pack as spawned, and adds grip-attachment callbacks.

remarks.para: An InteractableHost is the component that groups an object's hand interactions and tracks attachments. It first asks WeaponResetVolume to associate the configured hosts with this pack. It then sets isSpawned to true and subscribes OnWeaponGrabbed to every entry in allGrips.

This method does not request a new weapon or magazine from the asset spawner, discover their components, or check that both objects were created. WeaponSpawner calls equivalent setup from its weapon spawn-completion callback after storing the weapon object and related references.

Provide a valid weaponHost and a nonnull allGrips array containing valid grips. The magazine host can be absent. An empty grip array adds no callbacks. Registration handles an already registered weapon host by skipping its whole registration branch, including a new magazine-host entry.
The spawned flag is written before grip subscriptions finish. Calling this repeatedly adds another callback subscription to each grip; it does not remove earlier subscriptions first.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.WeaponPack.OnWeaponGrabbed(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Hand)
member.summary: Invokes with this pack when a subscribed weapon grip reports an attachment by a .

remarks.para: OnSpawnWeapon subscribes this method to each grip in allGrips. A callback is a method saved for another system to invoke when something happens. The callback receives this WeaponPack, not the Hand argument.

The method does not inspect the supplied hand, verify isSpawned, or change object references. It also invokes the callback if called directly. With no OnPackGrabbed callback assigned, it does nothing. Multiple subscriptions or grip attachments can cause repeated notifications.

member.param: The hand reported by the grip attachment. This implementation does not inspect or forward it; the notification carries this pack instead.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.WeaponPack.ResetHostObj(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.InteractableHost)
member.summary: Returns a matching weapon or magazine to its configured world position and orientation, then clears that object's saved physics motion.

remarks.para: An InteractableHost is the component that groups an object's hand interactions and tracks attachments. If host matches weaponHost, it uses weaponSpawn and gunBody. Otherwise, if it matches magHost, it uses magazineSpawn and magBody. A host matching neither is left alone; the weapon comparison takes priority if both references identify the same host.

A Transform stores an object's position, orientation, and size. World position and orientation use the scene's shared coordinate system rather than its parent's coordinates. The method moves the host GameObject's Transform directly to the chosen spawn Transform's world position and world orientation. Positions are distances in metres. It does not copy scale, gradually animate the move, or rebind any pack references.

A Rigidbody is Unity's physics component for a movable object, including its motion and response to forces. If the matching saved body exists, it sets its linear velocity to zero metres per second and angular velocity to zero radians per second, stopping its stored sliding and spinning motion. Moving the host still happens when that body is absent.

WeaponResetVolume calls this for a registered host that should be reset. For example, moving weaponSpawn to a display stand changes where the next weapon-host reset sends the object. Provide the matching spawn Transform before resetting that host. This method does not release hand attachments, reload the gun, or insert a magazine.

member.param: The interaction host to return. It must match this pack's weaponHost or magHost to cause a move; each match uses its corresponding spawn point and saved physics body.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.WeaponSpawner.CoSpawnDefaultPack
member.summary: Creates a coroutine that waits 2 game-clock seconds before requesting the default loadout.

remarks.para: A coroutine is a routine that can pause and continue during later game updates. Calling this method creates the routine; start it with StartCoroutine to run it. After its fixed wait, it calls SpawnDefaultSpawnablePack, which requests default ammo first and then the configured crate selections.

The wait uses the game’s clock, so a slower game speed makes it take longer in real-world time. Unity starts this wait at the end of the current frame and resumes on a later frame after the wait has passed. A frame is one round of game updates; this is not a promise of exactly 2 seconds on a stopwatch.

For example, run StartCoroutine(CoSpawnDefaultPack()) to use this delayed path. It does not read initSpawnDelay or wait for a crate asset to load. Spawn requests can still finish later, or fail without producing a counted object.

member.returns: The routine to start as a coroutine; creating it does not itself request a spawn.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.WeaponSpawner.CreateSpawnDictionary
member.summary: Rebuilds the lookup that turns a selected crate barcode into a configured weapon pack.

remarks.para: A barcode is the identifier of a crate asset, rather than the name of a spawned object. This method clears the old map, replaces it with a new map, and fills it from each pack’s weapon crate in weaponPackList. If several packs use the same barcode, the first one in the list wins.
OnWeaponSelected uses this saved map to choose a preset pack with its own spawn point and optional secondary weapon. A crate absent from the map follows the general spawn path at defSpawn instead.

For example, rebuild the map after adding or rearranging packs if kiosk selections should use those changes. Editing weaponPackList alone does not refresh an existing map. Configure every listed pack and its weapon crate before rebuilding.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.WeaponSpawner.DespawnAllAmmo
member.summary: Removes the three cached ammo-box instances from active play and clears their references.

remarks.para: It processes light, medium and heavy ammo in that order. Each usable cached Poolee, the component that manages a reusable pooled object, has its object’s despawn effect requested when available, then is despawned and its cache is cleared. Despawning removes an object from active play so pooling can reuse it.

For example, call this to remove the last completed light, medium and heavy boxes held by this spawner. It does not search for every ammo box in the scene or cancel spawn requests whose completion callbacks have not yet filled those caches.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.WeaponSpawner.DespawnAllWeaponPacks
member.summary: Runs pack cleanup for each configured entry in .

remarks.para: Each entry is passed to DespawnPack. Packs marked spawned have their weapon removed and their optional secondary pack cleaned up. A pack not marked spawned is skipped.

For example, use this to clear the configured preset packs. This method does not itself clear the tracked-object dictionary or send a new total count. DespawnAllWeapons performs the broader inventory and tracked-object cleanup.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.WeaponSpawner.DespawnAllWeapons
member.summary: Clears cached inventory weapons, configured packs, and this spawner’s tracked pooled objects.

remarks.para: It first drops and removes weapons from the cached inventory slot receivers, the components that hold items in inventory slots. If that cache is empty or its first entry is missing, it searches the scene for active slot receivers. The inventory cleanup can therefore include items that this kiosk did not spawn.

It then cleans up weaponPackList and iterates the tracked pooled objects. For each tracked object it requests its own despawn effect when available, despawns it, requests spawnFXSpawnable at its position, and plays despawnClip there. Despawning removes an object from active play so it can be reused.

After that loop, it clears the tracked dictionary and notifies OnCountUpdated with (0, weaponLimit). The first number is the remaining tracked count; the second is the configured selection limit. Default ammo has separate cleanup through DespawnAllAmmo.

For example, use this for a full kiosk/inventory reset, rather than only removing preset packs. It does not cancel outstanding asynchronous spawn requests, which can complete afterward and add tracked objects again.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.WeaponSpawner.DespawnCountUpdate(UnityEngine.GameObject,Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Pool.Poolee)
member.summary: Removes a tracked object from the count and then reports the remaining count and limit.

remarks.para: If rootObj is a key in the tracked dictionary, this method removes it and invokes OnCountUpdated when a listener exists. The payload is (remaining tracked objects, weaponLimit), with both values expressed as object counts. An untracked object produces no change or notification.

The poolee argument is not read, and this method does not despawn the object. It is bookkeeping to call when an object has been removed. For example, removing one tracked object from a count of 3 with a limit of 5 produces the pair (2, 5).
The spawner’s own spawn requests do not attach this method as their despawn callback automatically. Calling it before the object is removed can free a counted slot while the object is still in play.

member.param: The spawned Unity object to remove from this spawner’s tracked dictionary.
The pooled-object component supplied by the caller; this implementation does not read it.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.WeaponSpawner.DespawnPack(Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.WeaponPack)
member.summary: Removes a pack’s weapon and recursively cleans up its optional secondary pack.

remarks.para: The pack must be configured and marked isSpawned. This method requests spawnFXSpawnable at the weapon’s current world position, plays spawnClip at defSpawn, detaches the weapon from any hand holding it, and despawns its pooled instance. Despawning removes it from active play for reuse.

It then clears spawnedWeaponObj, handles the optional secondary pack, unregisters the pack from weapon-reset handling, and sets isSpawned to false. Its explicit effect and sound use the spawn settings, even though this is a cleanup operation.

For example, clean up one preset and its secondary weapon without processing every pack. This method does not itself remove the pack’s entries from the tracked count or separately despawn a magazine object.

member.param: The configured weapon pack to remove; a pack not marked spawned is skipped.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.WeaponSpawner.GetWeaponSlots
member.summary: Finds active inventory slot receivers in the scene and replaces the cleanup cache with them.

remarks.para: An inventory slot receiver is a component that holds an item in an inventory slot. This method searches for those components across the loaded scene, rather than only under one player, and stores the resulting array in inventorySlotRecievers. Unity’s default search excludes inactive objects.

DespawnAllWeapons later uses that cache to drop and remove items. For example, refresh the cache after replacing the player rig or adding inventory slots. This is a snapshot, so newly added receivers are not included until another search.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.WeaponSpawner.OnDisable
member.summary: Disconnects this spawner from the kiosk and challenge-menu actions that OnEnable connected.

remarks.para: Unity calls OnDisable when this component becomes disabled or its object is turned off. It removes its handlers for crate selection, clearing all weapons, updating defSpawn, and selecting a challenge loadout index.
For example, disabling this spawner stops those static menu actions from calling it through these subscriptions. This method does not remove existing weapons or ammo, or change isSpawningAllowed.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.WeaponSpawner.OnEnable
member.summary: Connects kiosk selections, clear requests, spawn-point changes, and challenge loadout choices to this spawner.

remarks.para: Unity calls OnEnable when this component becomes enabled on an active object. It subscribes OnWeaponSelected to SpawnableDisplay.OnSpawnableSelected, DespawnAllWeapons to OnDespawnAll, and a spawn-point setter to OnTeleportDisplay. It also connects ChallengeSelectMenu.OnLoadoutSelected to SpawnPackByIndex.

A callback is a function called when an action happens. These subscriptions let the display or challenge menu call the matching spawner operation. For example, a display selection can request the selected crate while a challenge loadout index can request a preset pack.
The matching OnDisable method removes these subscriptions. OnEnable does not subscribe to WeaponPack grab events or automatically change the weapon count.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.WeaponSpawner.OnWeaponSelected(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Warehouse.SpawnableCrateReference)
member.summary: Requests a selected crate or its preset pack when the tracked count is below the limit and spawning is allowed.

remarks.para: Both conditions must pass: pooleeDict.Count must be less than weaponLimit, and isSpawningAllowed must be true. The count is the number of completed objects recorded in this spawner’s dictionary. With a count equal to the limit, or with spawning disabled, the method plays overLimitClip at defSpawn and returns.

An existing weaponPackMap chooses a preset by the selected crate’s barcode, its asset identifier. If the map is missing, it is rebuilt first. A matching pack uses its own weapon spawn point and may request a secondary pack after completion. An unmatched crate is registered for pooling and requested at defSpawn’s world position and orientation.

Spawn completion can happen later. The completion callback records an object only if its Poolee, the component that manages a reusable pooled object, is found. OnCountUpdated is sent after that bookkeeping. Requests reserve no counted slot, and secondary packs can add another object, so this check is not a guarantee that the eventual count stays below the limit.

For example, count 4 and limit 5 allows a request; count 5 and limit 5 rejects it. Several requests made before their callbacks finish can all see count 4. The general-crate path requests its visual effect and plays spawnClip after submitting the weapon request, without waiting for success. Its completed-spawn callback also plays spawnClip.

member.param: The crate reference to select; it identifies the asset to request, not an already spawned object.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.WeaponSpawner.SpawnAllWeaponPacks
member.summary: Requests every pack in when the first pack is not marked spawned.

remarks.para: weaponPackList must contain at least one configured entry. This method checks the first pack’s isSpawned flag. If that flag is true, it returns without trying the other packs. Otherwise it calls SpawnWeaponPack for every entry, using each pack’s own world spawn point.
It does not check isSpawningAllowed or weaponLimit, and it does not spawn default ammo by itself. Each pack request may finish later and may request a secondary pack on completion.

For example, use this to populate a preset display from all configured packs. If the first pack is already marked spawned while a later pack is missing, this method still skips the whole list; select that later pack separately instead.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.WeaponSpawner.SpawnDefaultAmmo
member.summary: Removes cached ammo boxes, then requests new light, medium, and heavy boxes at their targets.

remarks.para: It first calls DespawnAllAmmo, then requests the light, medium and heavy ammo assets from StaticProfiles. Each request uses the target object’s current world position and orientation. Positions are in Unity distance units, normally meters; orientation says which way the box faces.

The boxes may finish spawning later. Each completion callback resets its movement and spinning to zero, adds 40 to an AmmoPickup’s ammo count when that pickup is present, and stores the Poolee found for the completed box. A Poolee manages a reusable pooled object. The addition is 40 units of ammunition on top of the pickup’s existing count, rather than an exact total of 40.

For example, configure all three target objects before requesting replacement ammo. This method does not check the weapon count or isSpawningAllowed. Repeated calls while earlier requests are unfinished can leave extra boxes, because only the last completed reference for each size is cached.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.WeaponSpawner.SpawnDefaultSpawnablePack
member.summary: Requests default ammo first, then selects each crate in .

remarks.para: The default SpawnablePack contains a list of crate references, identifiers for assets to request. Each one is sent through OnWeaponSelected, which applies the spawning flag and current tracked-count limit and may use a matching preset pack.

Ammo is requested before this list is processed and is independent of the weapon-selection permission. For example, with isSpawningAllowed false, this method can still request the three ammo boxes while rejecting the weapon selections.

Configure the default pack and its list before using this method. Calling it starts the requests immediately; it does not itself wait initSpawnDelay. Returning does not mean that all requested objects have finished spawning.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.WeaponSpawner.SpawnPackByIndex(System.Int32)
member.summary: Requests the pack at a zero-based index in .

remarks.para: Index 0 selects the first pack, index 1 the second, and so on. The index must be at least 0 and less than the list’s current count; there is no clamping or fallback for an invalid index.
This method calls SpawnWeaponPack directly. It uses that pack’s own spawn point and bypasses the isSpawningAllowed and weaponLimit checks made by kiosk crate selection. Completion can happen later.
For example, with three configured packs, use index 2 for the third pack. A challenge loadout choice can reach this method through the subscription installed by OnEnable.

member.param: The pack’s zero-based list index: 0 for the first entry, up to Count minus 1.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.WeaponSpawner.SpawnRandSpecialWep
member.summary: Requests a random entry from at the special spawn point.

remarks.para: The list must contain at least one valid spawnable asset. An integer random choice selects one list index, including 0 and excluding the list count. The chosen entry is registered for pooling and requested at specialWepSpawnPoint’s world position and orientation.

This method bypasses isSpawningAllowed and weaponLimit. It supplies no callback to add the completed object to pooleeDict, so the special weapon is not included in this spawner’s tracked selection count or its dictionary cleanup.
For example, a list of three entries makes indices 0, 1 and 2 eligible. Assign the special spawn point before calling; moving it affects later requests and does not move previously spawned objects.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.WeaponSpawner.SpawnWeaponPack(Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.WeaponPack)
member.summary: Requests a preset pack’s weapon, then its optional secondary pack after the weapon completes.

remarks.para: A weapon pack combines a weapon asset with its spawn point and optional secondary pack. If spawnedWeaponObj already refers to a usable object, the method skips the request. With visDebug true, that skipped request writes a short message to Unity’s Console, the developer message log.

A new request uses the pack’s weaponSpawn world position and orientation. Positions are in Unity distance units, normally meters; orientation says which way the weapon faces. The method requests spawnFXSpawnable and plays spawnClip as part of making the request, so that feedback does not prove the weapon finished spawning.

The completion callback stores the weapon object, records its pooled-object component when found, and sends the tracked count and limit to listeners after the dictionary bookkeeping. It then caches interaction components and grips, the parts a player can hold, registers weapon-reset handling, marks the pack spawned, and connects its grips to pack-grab notifications before requesting a secondary pack.

This method directly bypasses the spawner’s permission and limit checks. It does not request the pack’s magazine asset. For example, two calls made before a first completion fills spawnedWeaponObj can both request weapons; a completed object reference is what prevents another request.

member.param: The configured pack whose weapon and optional secondary pack are requested.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.WeaponSpawner.Start
member.summary: Registers configured assets for pooling, builds the pack lookup, and schedules the optional default loadout.

remarks.para: Start is Unity’s setup call before this component’s first normal update. It registers the listed pack weapons, valid magazines for ranged packs, optional secondary weapons, the three default ammo assets, and both configured visual-effect assets. Registering prepares an asset for pooled reuse; it is not a completed spawn.

It then rebuilds weaponPackMap. If spawnDefAtStart is false, it stops there. If true and the current level session is loading, it registers SpawnDefaultSpawnablePack as a level-load callback, a function run when that load action happens. Otherwise it starts CoSpawnDefaultPack, which waits a fixed 2 game-clock seconds before requesting the default ammo and crate selections.

For example, enable spawnDefAtStart for automatic loadout requests and configure the default pack, ammo targets, pack references, and effects first. The loading-session callback path does not use the coroutine’s 2-second wait. initSpawnDelay is not read by either startup path.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.WeaponSpawner.ToggleWeaponSpawning(System.Boolean)
member.summary: Sets this kiosk’s selection permission, then sends the supplied value to the shared permission callback.

remarks.para: The stored isSpawningAllowed flag changes before IsSpawningAllowed is invoked. A callback is a function run when notified. The notification carries enable even when the flag already had that value; this is not limited to changes.

The callback is static, shared by all WeaponSpawner instances. An enabled SpawnableDisplay subscribes to update its permission message. This method expects at least one listener: without one, the flag is still changed before the invocation fails.

For example, call ToggleWeaponSpawning(false) to reject later OnWeaponSelected requests and update a subscribed display. Existing objects and pending requests are unaffected, and direct preset or special-weapon requests bypass this selection gate.

member.param: True to allow kiosk crate selections; false to reject them. The same value is sent to listeners.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Combat.RigidbodyProjectile.#ctor
member.summary: Initializes the projectile with all layers eligible for blast targeting and blocking, fire damage, and a radius and damage value of 1.

remarks.para: These are code initialization values: a Unity prefab or saved scene can provide different serialized settings. Constructing the component does not assign its Rigidbody, sounds, collider, or blast asset; Unity initialization and a configured object are still needed.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Combat.RigidbodyProjectile.Awake
member.summary: Prepares a six-collider blast query buffer, registers the blast asset, and finds a collider if col is missing.

remarks.para: Awake is Unity’s initialization callback, a routine called to initialize the component. The fallback collider comes from the same GameObject. An already assigned col is kept. The buffer is temporary storage for blast targets; it is not a list of colliders that belong to the projectile.

This setup does not find or assign _rb. Supply the Rigidbody and other prefab references separately. Registering blastSpawnable prepares it for the asset-spawning system; it does not create a blast during Awake.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Combat.RigidbodyProjectile.OnEnable
member.summary: Enables the collider and ignores collisions between colliders within a small sphere around the projectile; after the level's first two seconds, also resets movement and plays its throw sound.

remarks.para: Unity calls OnEnable when this component becomes enabled and active. The sphere is centered on the projectile transform's world position and has radius 0.06 world units, or 6 centimeters at the game's usual meter scale. The code takes every collider returned and requests IgnoreCollision for every pair in that collection. This can affect two nearby objects as well as pairs involving the projectile. It does not use attackLayerMask or blockLayerMask for this query.

When Time.timeSinceLevelLoad is at least 2 seconds, it sets _rb.velocity to zero, records Time.time in _initialTime, asks the audio manager to play one randomly selected throwClips entry at local position (0, 0, 0) under this transform, and clears throwerProxy. Set a new launch velocity and attacker reference after this reset if needed. It does not reset angular velocity in this method.

The two-second condition is measured from level loading, not from this projectile's activation. Collider enabling and collision-ignore requests still run earlier. The method needs valid col and _rb references for the operations that use them; it does not launch the projectile or invoke OnProjectileShot.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Combat.SpawnLauncher.Spawn
member.summary: Starts registration of and a repeating wait sequence that does not spawn an item.

remarks.para: This starts an asynchronous sequence: it can wait while the rest of the game continues. It reads the configured spawnable once, asks the shared asset spawner to register its crate, waits two seconds, then repeats a half-second wait. The repeated part contains no request to create an item, no movement, and no check of the fire-point transform.

Registration prepares a pool, a place where the shared spawner can keep reusable items, and can begin loading the crate's asset if its pool is missing. The launcher does not wait for registration to finish or check whether it succeeded. Waiting two seconds therefore does not prove that the asset is ready.

The waits count game time in seconds, using the time that passed since the previous game frame. A frame is one update of the game. Slow motion stretches these waits in real time, and pausing game time stops their progress. Each wait resumes on an update after its target has been reached, so its actual elapsed time can exceed the target.

Every call starts its own sequence. The loop supplies no cancellation signal and does not check whether the component is enabled. Changing the configured spawnable after a sequence starts does not make that sequence register the new value.
For example, calling this with a crate for a ball can prepare that crate for the shared spawner, but it does not produce a ball at the fire point, either immediately or after the waits.

member.returns: A UniTaskVoid value, representing work that continues without giving the caller a task to await for completion. It is not a spawned object or a success result.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Combat.SpawnLauncher.Start
member.summary: Automatically starts the same registration and repeating waits as when Unity starts this component.

remarks.para: Unity calls Start before this enabled component's first update. The launcher reads its configured spawnable and starts registration, then waits two seconds of game time before entering repeated half-second waits. The game continues running during each wait.

This startup sequence never requests an item spawn and never reads the fire-point transform. It also does not await the separate registration operation, so the first wait is not an asset-ready check. Calling Spawn yourself starts an additional sequence alongside the one started here.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.KeyReceiver.GetHost
member.summary: Returns the interaction component of the key currently being handled by this socket.
member.returns: The cached key host, or null when no host is assigned.

remarks.para: This is the stored _keyHost reference, which provides the key’s grips, held hand and physics body. It is assigned when an accepted key enters an empty receiver, so it can already be available while the key is approaching the slot. Use hasCartridge to test whether insertion has finished.
An empty receiver normally returns null. Removal can briefly leave this reference assigned until the host-exit cleanup runs.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.KeyReceiver.MakeDynamic
member.summary: Separates the key’s physics body from the receiver so it can move independently again.

remarks.para: Unpacks the key from the receiver’s MarrowEntity, enables a ForcePullGrip if its grip has one, removes the host transform’s parent and wakes its Rigidbody so physics resumes. Packing is the game’s way of combining bodies into one movable assembly; unpacking restores a separate object.
This helper expects _keyHost and marrowEntity to be assigned. It does not run the removal sound, onLock, OnKeyRemoved or OnRemoved callbacks; the normal removal path performs those steps separately.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.KeyReceiver.MakeStatic
member.summary: Combines the key’s physics body with the receiver’s body so the key stays with the socket.

remarks.para: Disables the host’s force-pull grip if present, forcibly detaches held hands, destroys every Joint component on the key entity’s primary-body GameObject, then packs that body into the receiver’s body. A Joint is a physics connection between objects; these connections are removed before the bodies are combined.

This operates on the assigned _keyHost and marrowEntity. It does not itself mark insertion complete or fire onUnlock. The insertion coroutine performs this preparation before moving the packed key to its seated position.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.KeyReceiver.MoveTowardsStartInsertTarget
member.summary: Guides the held hand toward the slot entrance and decides when automatic insertion can begin.

remarks.para: During HOVERING, the receiver measures the Key transform’s distance and facing relative to startInsertTarget. It calculates a smoothed blend between the hand’s tracked pose and an aligned entrance pose, then stores the resulting world-space hand pose in _HandTargetTransform. OnPreRealtimeRig applies that pose to the visible hand skeleton.

Once the key is sufficiently close and aligned, or has been released without being force-pulled, the receiver changes to SLIDING and starts CoWaitLockMagazine. That coroutine moves the key to endInsertTarget. Hosts held in inventory or claimed by another interaction are checked before starting insertion.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.KeyReceiver.Release
member.summary: Starts the key’s animated ejection when a valid Key is assigned.

remarks.para: The coroutine, a sequence that continues over several frames, moves the key from endInsertTarget back toward startInsertTarget, preserving the offset between the Key component’s transform and its interaction host. At the exit it unpacks the body, plays an ejection sound, fires onLock and OnKeyRemoved, gives the Rigidbody an outward velocity and restores interaction. It then performs host-exit cleanup and invokes OnRemoved.

The call returns before that animation finishes. It does nothing when _key is null or destroyed. This entry point checks neither hasCartridge nor isKeyConsumed, so isKeyConsumed does not prohibit a scripted Release call. OnRemoved is the completion notification for this path.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.KeyReceiver.SetHoverEject
member.summary: Marks the next ejection for a short pause before the same key can be accepted again.

remarks.para: This call only sets _IsHoverEject to true; it does not start ejection. At the end of CoEjectMagazine the flag is cleared and _WasMagazineGrabbed is set. OnInteractableHostStay then accumulates about half a second before re-running exit and entry handling, allowing the key to be considered again.
No hand-hover detection is performed by this method or by the audited ejection coroutine. Call Release separately to request ejection.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.KeyReceiver.SlideTowardsEndInsertTarget
member.summary: Closes all fingers of the hand holding the key during the insertion stage.

remarks.para: Gets the first hand attached to _keyHost and applies a curl override of 1 to every finger through its HandPoseAnimator. If no hand is holding the key, it returns without changing a hand pose.

Despite its name, this method does not move the key transform. CoWaitLockMagazine performs the movement toward endInsertTarget; OnPreRealtimeRig also applies the finger override while the receiver is in SLIDING.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.PowerPuncher.OnSignificantCollisionEnter(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.CollisionCollector.RelevantCollision)
member.summary: Discharges the charging puncher on a qualifying impact, adding knockback, sending an attack to the struck collider, and playing the blast feedback.
member.param: The collected hit, including its world-space contact point, relative velocity, struck collider, and struck rigidbody.

remarks.para: The puncher must have a nonzero charge-start timestamp, and at least 0.8 seconds of scaled game time must have passed since the previous discharge. The hit must have a valid rigidbody, meaning an object participating in Unity's physics simulation, and relative speed must be greater than 0.5 meters per second. A hit against a collider with no rigidbody is rejected.

The contact must also lie in front of the puncher: the normalized direction from triggerGrip.targetTransform's position to the contact point, expressed in the puncher component's orientation, must have a dot product greater than 0.76 with forward. For a forward vector of length 1, this means less than about 40.5 degrees away from that direction. It tests where the contact is, not whether the collision normal points forward.

Full charge is not required. The normalized charge factor is C = min(elapsed charge time / 1.6 seconds, 1), so 0.8 seconds gives C = 0.5. With relative speed measured in meters per second, the impact factor is S = min(speed × 0.5, 3), reaching its cap at 6 meters per second. The attack's damage value is 2 × C × S. For example, 0.8 seconds of charge and a 2-meter-per-second impact produce a damage value of 1 before the receiver handles it. Longer charging or a faster impact increases the shove too, within those caps.

A successful discharge plays blastParticles, starts PopAnim if it is not already running, plays the firing sound, and sets both timing fields to the current game time. Keeping the trigger held therefore starts building the next punch immediately, while the separate cooldown still prevents another discharge for 0.8 seconds. Normal use reaches this method through the collision collector; calling it directly skips the collector's own impact threshold.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.PowerPuncher.PopAnim
member.summary: Creates the coroutine that shows the icon's two discharge frames for 0.4 seconds each.
member.returns: The icon-animation coroutine to run with StartCoroutine.

remarks.para: Calling this method alone creates the sequence; StartCoroutine begins it. The sequence sets popAnimPlaying, selects icon frame 4, waits 0.4 seconds, selects frame 5, waits another 0.4 seconds, then clears the flag. These waits use scaled game time, so slowing or pausing the game changes their real-time duration.

While the flag is set, ordinary charging updates leave those icon frames alone. The collision handler avoids starting a second sequence while one is running. The sequence finishes on frame 5; later charging or trigger release supplies another icon frame.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.MLAgents.BehaviourArmWorm.SwitchMentalState(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourBaseNav.MentalState)
member.summary: Applies the armworm's settings for the requested mental state, stores that state, and requests a new decision check.

remarks.para: A mental state is the game-controlled character's current mode, such as resting, roaming, investigating, or being angry. A decision check, called an AI tick, is where the character checks its situation and decides what to do. This method changes settings first, then stores the requested state and sets forceAiTick. That flag makes the next AI tick skip its usual waiting interval; it does not run the tick inside this call.

Roam sets aiTickFreq, the minimum interval between ordinary decision checks, to 1 second. It also configures the NavMeshAgent, Unity's component for following paths over walkable ground: maximum movement speed becomes roamSpeed in metres per second, maximum turning speed becomes roamAngSpeed in degrees per second, maximum acceleration becomes 4 metres per second squared, and stopping distance becomes 1 metre from the destination. These are movement settings rather than a promise that the armworm is already moving at that speed.

Investigate sets the ordinary decision-check interval to 0.2 seconds. Agroed sets it to 0.08 seconds. These intervals use unscaled time, the clock that continues at its normal rate during slow motion. Checks still happen only when the character's update code calls its AI tick, so these numbers do not guarantee an exact frame or deadline. The forced next check can happen before the usual interval has passed.

Roam and Investigate also resize the vision SphereCollider, the round detection shape attached to the sensors. Its radius r is (range + 1) / 2: range means activeRange, the configured roaming distance, for Roam; it means investigateRange, the configured investigation distance, for Investigate. Here r, range, and the added 1 are distances in the collider object's own local coordinates. One local unit is one metre at the normal scale of (1, 1, 1); changing that object's scale changes the shape's size in the world.

When r is greater than 0.5 local units, the vision shape is enabled and its centre is moved by r - 1 local units along the object's local Z axis, its forward direction. A negative offset puts the centre behind the object's origin. For example, activeRange = 8 gives radius 4.5 and moves the centre 3.5 units forward. If the calculated radius is 0.5 or smaller, the helper instead disables the shape, sets its radius to zero, and resets its centre to the object's origin. Agroed requests radius 2, so its enabled shape has its centre 1 local unit forward.

Agroed requests the configured angry audio after changing the interval and vision shape, but before storing the new mental state and setting forceAiTick. Whether a sound plays depends on the sound component's configured clips. Calling this method with the same state again repeats that state's setup and audio request. Rest, Engaged, and MindControlled only store the state and request the next check here; they leave the previously configured interval, navigation settings, and vision shape in place. Later update and decision code can act on the new state.

Roam needs an assigned navigation agent and sensors with a vision collider. Investigate needs those sensors, and Agroed also needs the sound component. Missing required references can stop the call before the new state and forceAiTick are stored, even though some settings have already changed. The method itself does not select a new target or perform an attack.

member.param: The mental-state mode to apply. Roam, Investigate, and Agroed apply the settings described above before the state is stored.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.MLAgents.BehaviourBoid.SwitchMentalState(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourBaseNav.MentalState)
member.summary: Applies the boid's behavior-mode settings, stores the requested mental state, and requests another AI decision tick.

remarks.para: A mental state is a mode that guides this computer-controlled character's decisions. This method changes sensor and AI settings for Rest, Roam, Investigate and Agroed. It applies the mode's setup before storing the requested state, then sets a flag that lets the next eligible AI tick skip its usual waiting interval. An AI tick is one round of behavior decisions; requesting it does not immediately move the character or perform an attack.

Roam allows changes through the boid sensor's goal-radius and proximity-radius setters, marks agent.activelyManaged true, sets the behavior-decision interval to 1 second, and configures the vision sphere. Its requested radius is (R + 1) / 2, where R is activeRange, the configured roaming distance value in Unity distance units. For example, an activeRange of 9 produces a radius of 5 units. The boid inference agent, the component that supplies information to its learned AI, can collect observations while its activelyManaged flag is true, subject to its other checks.

Investigate also allows those radius setters and marks the agent actively managed. It sets the behavior-decision interval to 0.2 seconds and requests a vision-sphere radius of (R + 1) / 2, where R is investigateRange, the configured investigation distance value in Unity distance units.

Agroed, the aggressive mode, blocks those goal-radius and proximity-radius setters, marks the agent actively managed, and sets the decision interval to agroTickRate. Despite that field's name, it supplies an interval in seconds rather than a number of ticks per second. If the ordinary sensors already have a target, this method copies that target's head Rigidbody Transform to boidController.boidBall, the reference the boid controller follows. A Rigidbody is Unity's physics body, and its Transform supplies its scene position and rotation. If there is no sensor target, this reference is left as it was. The method requests a vision radius of 2 units and calls the aggression-sound routine, which can play a configured aggression clip and start a configured loop.

The vision sphere is a round sensor area. These radii are local Unity distance units on its object; one unit normally represents one metre before object scaling. For the radii requested here, the sensor routine enables the sphere only when its radius is greater than 0.5 units. A radius of 0.5 units or less disables it. The decision intervals above are checked using time unaffected by the game's time-scale setting. Actual decisions still depend on when the AI update runs; these are configured intervals, not guaranteed frame-to-frame times.

Rest has an unusual extra step. It first allows the boid sensor's radius setters, then calls SetAgentInactive. That helper reads start_state_list[start_state_ind], where the list contains candidate starting mental states and the index chooses one, stores the selected state, and runs its state setup. Only after the helper returns does this outer call store Rest. As a result, Rest can retain settings from the selected start state, including an actively managed agent. If the selected entry is Rest on an ordinary BehaviourBoid, the helper enters Rest again and can keep calling itself instead of completing. The list and index must be valid.

Engaged and MindControlled receive no special setup in this method: it stores the selected state and requests an AI tick while leaving the preceding settings in place. Calling the method with the same state still runs its setup again; for example, repeating Agroed calls the aggression-sound routine again. Required agent and sensor references must already be configured. If setup fails, earlier setting changes are not rolled back and the final requested-state write may not be reached.

member.param: Behavior mode to configure and store. Rest also runs the selected starting state's setup as described above.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.MLAgents.BehaviourBoidBall.SwitchMentalState(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourBaseNav.MentalState)
member.summary: Applies the boid ball’s settings for a mental state, records that state and requests a new AI decision pass.
member.param: The mental-state behavior mode to apply. Rest, Roam, Investigate and Agroed have preset setup; the other values are recorded without that preset setup.

remarks.para: A mental state is the ball’s behavior mode: Rest, Roam, Investigate or Agroed, meaning alerted to a target. A boid is one of the small creatures associated with the ball. These four modes select nbBoidsRest, nbBoidsRoam, nbBoidsInvestigate or nbBoidsAgro, respectively. The method applies that count to the first encounter group’s maximum-alive limit and calls encounter startup. Reducing the limit can also despawn surplus boids. This is configuration and a startup request, not proof that the requested creatures have finished spawning.

For each of those four modes, the matching rest_, roam_, investigate_ or agro_ settings are copied into the active minimum/maximum goal and proximity radii, the hover-height target and the radius transition rates. The goal and proximity radii are distance settings around the ball passed to connected boids’ sensing scripts, in world distance units, normally metres. The current goal radius is immediately set to its selected minimum, followed by the current proximity radius. If a value changes, its change event runs after the new number is stored and receives that number. An event calls registered methods, called callbacks. Goal-change callbacks run before proximity-change callbacks, and both run before the new mental state is recorded. A boid whose sensor blocks radius changes may ignore those updates.

The selected hover-height target, in distance units normally metres, is written to the fourth thruster, index 3, in ballMover.thrustMngr.thrusters. A thruster is a script that pushes the ball through physics. This changes its requested distance from the surface detected by its ground ray, not the ball’s position immediately. The selected radius rates become state_lerp_rate_min and state_lerp_rate_max: per-second blend factors for approaching the minimum and maximum radii. For example, rate 2 over a 0.02-second update gives a 0.04 blend step before clamping to 0–1. They are not exact travel speeds or fixed times to reach a radius. An already-running radius controller, a coroutine that resumes over several frames, can change the current radii again using these new settings; this method does not reset its existing blend value or direction.

Rest sets the thruster manager’s destination tolerance to 0. Roam and Investigate also set it to 0; Agroed sets it to 1 world distance unit, normally 1 metre. The manager considers destination pushing when the ball’s world distance from its destination is at least this tolerance and its movement flags allow it. These changes configure movement rather than guaranteeing the ball has arrived.

Roam copies ballConfig.roamFrequency, the roaming-choice setting used by the AI, sets aiTickFreq to 1 second between ordinary AI decision passes, and turns ballMover.active on. It applies roamSpeed, the requested path speed in metres per second, and roamAngSpeed, the requested turning speed in degrees per second, to the navigation agent, Unity’s path-following component. It also requests acceleration 4 metres per second squared and stopping distance 1 metre. Investigate sets aiTickFreq to 0.2 seconds. Agroed sets aiTickFreq = health.cur_hp × agroTickRate: cur_hp is the health fraction, normally 1 at full health and 0.5 at half health, and agroTickRate is the interval in seconds at full health. For example, half health times a 0.4-second full-health interval gives a 0.2-second interval. Lower health therefore shortens the ordinary wait. These intervals use time unaffected by game-time slowdown; their values are not exact elapsed times between rendered frames. Rest does not replace the existing AI interval here.

Roam, Investigate and Agroed reconfigure the vision sphere, a sphere-shaped collider used to sense targets. The game passes the current sensors.visionFov number as the radius; this call treats it as a distance in the collider’s own local units, normally metres at unit scale, despite the field’s name. At 0.5 or below the sphere is disabled; above 0.5 it is enabled and centered at its local origin, the zero point of its own coordinate system. Agroed also calls the aggression-sound routine. That routine can start the configured sounds, but missing or empty clip choices do not guarantee audible playback.

Finally, on the normal return path, mentalState is set to mState and _forceAiTick becomes true, asking the next eligible AI tick call to skip its usual interval wait. This does not run the whole AI decision pass inside this method or guarantee an exact rendered-frame delay. Engaged, MindControlled and other values receive those final two writes without the four modes’ preset setup. Assigning the current mode again still repeats its setup. For example, repeating Agroed can request the aggression sound again and reset changed radii back to their configured minima. The method expects initialized encounter, mover, thruster and other required references; an error or a throwing callback can interrupt setup after earlier changes and before the final state write.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.MLAgents.BehaviourQuadDrone.SwitchMentalState(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourBaseNav.MentalState)
member.summary: Applies the requested mental mode's flight and turret settings, saves that mode, and requests a new AI check for this drone.

remarks.para: A mental mode describes what the drone is trying to do, such as resting, wandering or attacking. Before making any change, this method asks the first body in its puppet setup for a Rigidbody, Unity's component that gives an object physical movement and rotation. If that body reports no Rigidbody, the method returns without changing the mode or requesting an AI check. The puppet setup must contain that first body, and the references needed by the selected mode must be assigned.

Rest copies restHeight into minHeight, clears the thrust manager's destination-distance threshold to 0, and allows physics rotation. If homeIsPost is true, it also asks for a path from the first body's current position to homePosition. Both positions are in metres in world coordinates, the shared scene coordinate system. Asking for the path does not mean the drone has already arrived home.

Roam copies roamHeight into minHeight and roam_speed into the thrust manager's configured speed limit, sets the AI-check interval to 1 second, and clears the destination-distance threshold to 0. It also configures the navigation agent, the component that plans movement routes, with roamSpeed in metres per second, roamAngSpeed in degrees per second, acceleration of 4 metres per second squared, and a stopping distance of 1 metre. Investigate instead copies investigateHeight into minHeight and investigateSpeed into the thrust manager's speed limit, sets the AI interval to 0.2 seconds, and clears the same distance threshold. This method does not reconfigure the navigation agent for Investigate.

Roam and Investigate both update the vision sphere, stop the turret's saved update routine if there is one, and allow physics rotation. For this sphere update, the implementation uses sensors.visionFov as the collider's radius despite that field's name: values above 0.5 enable a sphere centred on the sensor object, while values at or below 0.5 disable it. The radius is in the collider's local distance units, normally metres; object scaling changes its size in the scene. A collider is a shape Unity uses to detect contact or nearby objects.

Agroed copies agroHeight into minHeight, agroSpeed into the thrust manager's speed limit, and agroTickRate into the AI interval in seconds. It updates the vision sphere in the same way as Roam, copies the existing sensor target's head Transform into the turret's target, starts the turret update routine if one is not already saved, requests the aggression sound effects, and then allows physics rotation. A Transform stores an object's position and rotation. The turret routine is a coroutine, work that pauses and continues on later frames: it aims at that target and can start a firing sequence when its cooldown allows. This call needs an existing sensor target and head reference; choosing Agroed does not itself find a player.

MindControlled sets the fourth thruster's hoverHeight to 0.5 metres, stops the turret's saved update routine if present, and freezes rotation on the thrust manager's Rigidbody. The fourth thruster means array position 3, because positions start at 0. Switching from MindControlled first releases that physics rotation freeze, even when switching to Engaged. Engaged has no additional mode-specific setup in this method. Freezing rotation prevents physics from rotating the body; it does not by itself stop its position from moving.

The copied height settings are metres, but changing minHeight configures later movement rather than moving the drone immediately. Its minimum-height adjustment only runs when useMinHeight is enabled and path travel is not active. With player-height tracking off, the value is a minimum destination height on the world's vertical Y axis; in Agroed with tracking enabled, it is added above the sensor target's head height. The speed-limit settings likewise describe later speed control, not an immediate commanded velocity. For example, roam_speed of 2 configures a 2-metre-per-second limit when the thrust manager's activation and speed-governing settings allow that control.

After the selected setup completes, the method saves mentalState and sets a flag asking the next eligible AI update to bypass its usual interval. It does not run that AI check directly. The normal interval is measured in seconds using time unaffected by the game's time scale, and actual checks occur when updates run. Calling with the already selected mode repeats its setup; there is no same-mode early return here.

member.param: The mental mode to apply: Rest, Roam, Investigate, Agroed, Engaged or MindControlled.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.MLAgents.BehaviourSecurityCam.SwitchMentalState(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourBaseNav.MentalState)
member.summary: Changes the security camera's decision state and requests a decision update, with extra movement or sensing setup for Roam, Investigate and Agroed.

remarks.para: An AI tick is one decision update for this computer-controlled character. Roam sets the normal tick interval to 1 second. It also applies roamSpeed as the navigation travel speed in meters per second, roamAngSpeed as the turning limit in degrees per second, acceleration of 4 meters per second squared, and a stopping distance of 1 meter. A navigation agent is the component that plans and follows paths over the navigation mesh, the surface map used for movement. These settings guide its movement; they do not promise that the camera's physical body immediately reaches that speed.

Roam also sets the sensing sphere's radius to (R + 1) / 2, with R taken from activeRange. Investigate sets the tick interval to 0.2 seconds and uses the same sphere calculation with R taken from investigateRange; it keeps the existing navigation movement settings. In this calculation R is the configured numeric range used directly as a local-distance value, the added 1 is one local length unit, and dividing by the unitless 2 halves the result. A collider is a physics detection shape; this sphere defines the sensing region. Its radius and center offset use the collider's own axes and local length units, meters at object scale 1. For example, R = 9 gives a radius of 5 local units and a center 4 local units forward. The center offset is radius minus one local unit. A computed radius of 0.5 or less disables the sphere instead.

Agroed sets the tick interval to 0.08 seconds, enables the sensing sphere with radius 2 local units and center offset 1 local unit forward, and asks the sound component to play its configured aggression sound. An empty aggression-clip list produces no sound through that request. This branch keeps the existing navigation movement settings. Roam, Investigate and Agroed also write a debug log message when entered.

Rest, Engaged and MindControlled keep the previous tick interval, navigation settings and sensing sphere through this method. They still become the recorded mental state and request the next decision update. Selecting an already selected state runs its setup again.

After the chosen setup finishes, the method stores mState, then marks the next AI tick to bypass its interval wait. The intervals use unscaled seconds, which do not slow down with the game's time scale. The update still waits until the AI tick routine is actually called; this method does not run it immediately or promise an exact frame delay. The navigation agent, sensing component and sound component needed by the chosen branch must be initialized for that setup to finish.

member.param: The decision state to enter: Rest, Roam, Investigate, Agroed, Engaged or MindControlled.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.MLAgents.BehaviourStationaryTurret.SwitchMentalState(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.PuppetMasta.BehaviourBaseNav.MentalState)
member.summary: Changes the turret's mental state and prepares its laser, sounds, search pose, or attack timers for that state.
member.param: The requested state. Rest means sleeping; Investigate prepares searching; Agroed prepares attacking. Roam, Engaged, and MindControlled have no extra entry setup in this method.

remarks.para: The method first handles leaving the old state, then entering the requested state. After that work succeeds, it stores mState in mentalState and sets _forceAiTick, which asks the next AI tick—the next periodic decision check—to run without waiting for its usual interval. It does not run that tick immediately. Requesting the current state again still repeats the exit and entry work.

Leaving Rest activates laserPointer and enables laserCollider. If the cached aiBrain exists, its OnGroupDeregister event receives that same AIBrain object and false. Entering Rest stops the stored turret sound-loop player, deactivates the laser object, disables the laser collider, and sends the brain event that same object and true. The Boolean is false on waking and true on sleeping. Stopping the loop player does not promise that every separately played sound has stopped.

An event listener is a function attached to the event. These listeners run before this method stores the new mentalState, so a listener reading that field sees the old value unless listener code changes it itself. For example, a Rest-to-Rest call turns the laser on and sends false, then turns it off and sends true, before storing Rest again.

Leaving Investigate clears the accumulated search time, measured in scaled game-time seconds. Leaving Agroed also clears that time, sets an integer search-step counter from the body's current local turn, changes the first material on each glow renderer back to baseColor, and remembers the second muscle target's local yaw in degrees. Later search updates use the counter to choose their scan pose. A muscle target is the desired pose of a puppet body part. Local yaw means turning around its parent's up axis, measured relative to that parent.

Leaving Agroed also asks Unity to stop a newly created BurstFire routine. A coroutine is a routine that can pause and continue on later frames. This call supplies a new routine instead of the saved identity of a running burst, so it does not establish that an existing burst has stopped. A running BurstFire routine does not check mentalState before each shot.

Entering Investigate requests the idle sound loop when usable clips are available and resets the last muscle target's local rotation to zero turn relative to its parent. Entering Agroed requests that loop, applies agroColor to the first material of the inner and outer glow renderers, and prepares firing. It sets _lastBurstTime, the previous burst's completion-time stamp, to zero seconds. It sets burstWaitDuration, the configured attack-wait threshold, to 0.5 seconds and clears _agroTime, the attack-delay accumulator measured in seconds. It requests the alert sound when clips are available and sets _reloadTimer, the earliest allowed time for another burst, to the current scaled game time in seconds. _lastBurstTime and _reloadTimer use the scaled game clock, which follows the game's time scale.

The attack-delay accumulator follows a different rule: while it is at or below the wait threshold, each eligible attack check adds aiTickFreq, the configured AI-check interval in seconds, and returns. A later check with the accumulator above the threshold can proceed to the ammunition and firing checks. AI-tick eligibility normally uses unscaled time, which does not slow with the game's time scale. The accumulator counts configured intervals instead of measuring exact elapsed frame time, so the 0.5-second setting does not promise a shot exactly 0.5 seconds after this call.

Agroed also sets _calculatedBurst to A - B. A is the magazine's current number of rounds; B is burstCount, the configured number of shots in a burst. The result is a remaining-ammo threshold for the later AI checks. For example, 25 rounds and a burstCount of 10 produce a threshold of 15 rounds. This setup does not refill the magazine or immediately fire a shot. The later AI tick checks the target, delays, ammunition, and whether a burst is already running before starting one.

Roam, Engaged, and MindControlled still receive the state assignment and next-tick request, after any cleanup for the old state. Their names do not add extra entry actions here. Leg folding is started separately by routines such as those used by ToggleSleep.

The turret needs its sound, laser, puppet, target, and renderer references set up for the branches that use them. Missing required objects or material entries can stop the method partway through. Earlier changes or event calls can already have happened while mentalState still holds the old state.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.FilteredDespawn.OnEnter(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity)
member.summary: Requests the entering entity's despawn effect, then calls its Poolee despawn path.
member.param: The entering entity. Its MarrowEntity needs a non-null Poolee reference for this despawn path.

remarks.para: The inherited activatorTags field is a MarrowQuery: it checks the entity against configured tag queries and can also check its crate reference. Its all/any setting controls whether those checks combine with AND or OR. Normal ZoneItem entry runs this filter before calling this override, so a direct call skips it. For example, a zone configured to accept dropped props can remove those accepted props as they enter.

The effect request happens before despawning and does not wait for an effect to finish. A MarrowEntity needs a non-null Poolee reference for this despawn path; the Poolee component tracks this object's pool state. For an in-pool Poolee, a registered non-null SpawnPolicy is a per-object rule for handling despawn: it receives the request and its mapping is removed. When the policy map has no entry and the matching pool is available, it calls Pool.Despawn. If Pool.Despawn finds the Poolee in the spawned list, it removes that entry and adds it to the pool's despawned list, where a later spawn can reuse it. Otherwise Pool.Despawn returns before sending despawn events, running the Poolee's registered cleanup methods, changing either list, or deactivating the object. Poolee.IsInPool does not establish spawned-list membership: it checks a stored flag or crate reference. A separate fallback applies when the Poolee is not currently in a pool: it sends the despawn event, runs the Poolee's registered cleanup methods, deactivates its Unity GameObject (the object in the scene), then logs an error instead of returning it through the pool-list path.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.FizzleOnRecycleDecorator.Awake
member.summary: Registers this decorator with its assigned crateSpawner so it can receive OnRecycle callbacks when the spawner recycles an object.

remarks.para: Awake is Unity's initialization callback. The crateSpawner reference must already be assigned; Awake reads it directly and registers this component as an IRecycleListenable, the listener interface that lets the spawner call this component when it recycles an object. A GameObject is Unity's object in the scene, and a component is behavior or data attached to that object. The spawner passes the recycled GameObject to OnRecycle. A callback is a method another object calls to report an event; here OnRecycle reports the recycle. Reset is Unity's editor setup hook that finds a CrateSpawner on this same GameObject.

This is setup work. Calling Awake again does not switch an existing registration to a new spawner: it registers with the reference currently stored in crateSpawner. This class has no disable-time unsubscribe, and CrateSpawner dispatches its recycle-listener entries without checking whether each component is enabled, so disabling this component alone does not stop OnRecycle calls. To stop notifications, call CrateSpawner.UnregisterSpawnEventListener(IRecycleListenable) on the registered spawner. To move the subscription, unregister from the old spawner, update crateSpawner, then call CrateSpawner.RegisterSpawnEventListener(IRecycleListenable) on the new spawner.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.FizzleOnRecycleDecorator.Reset
member.summary: Finds the CrateSpawner on this GameObject and stores it as the source of recycling callbacks.

remarks.para: Reset is Unity's editor setup hook; Unity calls it when the component is added or reset in the Inspector. It fills the hidden crateSpawner reference from a CrateSpawner on the same GameObject. Awake, Unity's initialization callback, later uses that stored reference to register the recycle listener. If you call Reset after setup, it updates the reference but does not move the listener registration; unregister from the old spawner and register with the new one if you need to change it.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.MobileEncounter.Awake
member.summary: Unity calls Awake when it initializes this component. This method creates one empty storage slot per spawn group for a cancellation source (the handle that later asks that group's timed spawn loop to stop), connects group spawn notifications, and puts each configured spawner into manual mode.

remarks.para: The encounter controls when these spawners spawn, so Awake sets each CrateSpawner.manualMode to true. It also forwards each group's OnGroupSpawned notification through GroupMemberSpawned to OnGroupMemberSpawned.

Set up spawnGroups and every group's spawners before this runs. The cancellation array is sized here, but its sources are created individually when groups start. Replacing or resizing spawnGroups later does not resize that array or rebuild these subscriptions.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.MobileEncounter.CheckCompletion(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.SpawnGroup)
member.summary: Marks an unfinished group complete, counts it, and advances or completes the encounter according to spawnOrder.
member.param: The group being reported complete; this method does not first test whether its members are dead.

remarks.para: This changes state rather than merely asking a yes-or-no question. For an unfinished group it calls CompleteGroup, increments completeCount, invokes onGroupComplete when assigned, and requests dead-member cleanup if the group exceeds maxDead. The timed encounter loop normally calls it after the group's death count reaches totalSpawn.

In SERIES, it starts the group at completeCount while that index is in range; otherwise it completes the encounter. In PARALLEL, it also marks each unfinished nonhostile configured group complete by setting isComplete and increasing completeCount. This shortcut does not call that group's CompleteGroup method, so its group-level completion callbacks and cleanup do not run, and it does not invoke onGroupComplete for that extra group. The encounter completes when the count reaches the group-array length.

Calling it again for an already complete group does not increment that group's count, but the order-handling code still runs and can start the next series index again. Use it as a completion action, not for polling.

The supplied group is not checked against spawnGroups. Passing a different unfinished group still gives it completion credit and can advance SERIES progression or change whether the encounter completes.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.MobileEncounter.CompleteEncounter
member.summary: Stops coroutines running on this component (a coroutine is a routine Unity resumes over later frames), marks the encounter complete, and invokes OnComplete. It then asks each group's timed spawn loop to stop through its cancellation source, the handle that sends that stop request.
