remarks.para: It does nothing when _complete is already true. Otherwise it sets complete true, active false, and paused false before invoking OnComplete if assigned. The completion event runs before cancellation requests are sent, so callbacks should account for that ordering.

Cancellation expects every slot in _spawnCTSs to contain a source. Awake creates empty slots and StartGroupEncounter fills them. If a group has never started, cancellation can fail on its empty slot after this method has already changed the flags and fired the completion event. This method does not kill or directly despawn existing members, and a group spawn already being awaited does not receive this cancellation token.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.MobileEncounter.EncounterLoop(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.AI.SpawnGroup,Il2CppSystem.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Runs one group's timed spawn sequence and reports completion when its dead count is at least totalSpawn.
member.param: The group supplying spawners, counts, delays, and limits.
Cancels the loop's delays and is checked between iterations; it is not passed into the group's spawn task.

remarks.para: The timed sequence continues across later frames as its waits and any awaited spawn operation finish. The loop first waits initialGroupDelay, then waits 0.15 seconds before each check. If the group's dead count has reached totalSpawn, it calls CheckCompletion and then AllGroupsKilled before returning. This is a per-group check, even though the callback name says all groups. The IsAllDead test is deadCount >= totalSpawn; it does not test whether the alive set is empty or whether isComplete is set, and totalSpawn = 0 passes immediately.

When tracked dead members exceed maxDead or alive members exceed maxAlive, it waits another 0.5 seconds and requests cleanup of a dead member. If alive members still exceed maxAlive, it asks the group to kill one. When alive count is below maxAlive and spawn count below totalSpawn, it waits spawnInterval and awaits SpawnProfileAsync when an encounterProfile exists, otherwise SpawnAsync.

The configured delays are game seconds on Unity's scaled clock, so slow motion makes the same delay take longer in real time; the code converts them to whole milliseconds. For example, spawnInterval = 1 adds a one-second wait before a permitted spawn, alongside the loop's other waits and the spawn operation itself. This is not a guarantee of exactly one spawn per second. The checked loop does not use _isEncounterActive or _isEncounterPaused to suspend its work.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.MobileEncounter.KillAll
member.summary: For every currently tracked living NPC brain, sets its PuppetMaster.State to Dead; PuppetMaster controls the NPC's simulated body.

remarks.para: The PuppetMaster.State choices are Alive, Dead, and Frozen. This changes the state of tracked living brains; it does not remove the NPC from the pool, mark the encounter complete, or cancel future spawning. A running loop can keep spawning until its group limits, completion count, or cancellation stop it.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.MobileEncounter.MentalAllEncounter(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity)
member.summary: Uses the entity's TriggerRefProxy to request investigation of its position or aggression toward it from configured groups.
member.param: The entity supplying a child TriggerRefProxy as the groups' AI target.

remarks.para: A TriggerRefProxy is a component (data or behavior attached to a Unity object) that AI, the code controlling game characters, uses as a target reference for a character. It points to body parts such as the head, chest, and feet. Each group with mentalMode INVESTIGATE asks eligible living members to investigate the position of the proxy's feetTran Transform. A Transform is Unity's position-and-rotation reference for an object; this target is read in world space. The group uses investigateTimeout as a duration in scaled game seconds; slow motion makes the same number of game seconds take longer in real time. Existing AI state and an unexpired investigation can prevent that request from starting another investigation. AGRO targets the proxy for aggression. NONE leaves the group's mental targeting unchanged. Members in the group's ignored-brain set are skipped.

The group also stores the proxy, so later spawned members can receive the same configured targeting. A culled member, marked by the game's culling system to temporarily stop its physics or game behavior, can defer its mental-state change until reactivation. If no TriggerRefProxy is found, the method logs an error and does not update the groups' target. This method does not start the encounter.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.MobileEncounter.OnDestroy
member.summary: When Unity destroys this component, it removes the spawn-notification connection that forwards each group's event to OnGroupMemberSpawned, for the groups currently in spawnGroups.

remarks.para: This undoes the group subscription made by Awake. It iterates the current spawnGroups array, so if that array was replaced after Awake, the earlier groups are not retained here and may remain subscribed. It does not ask the groups' timed spawn loops to stop (that uses the cancellation sources in _spawnCTSs, the handles that send stop requests), and it does not perform CompleteEncounter's state changes. Removing the component therefore does not use this hook to explicitly cancel its pending group work.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.MobileEncounter.PauseEncounter
member.summary: Sets the paused flag used to skip group setup on a later StartGroupEncounter call.

remarks.para: The checked base implementation only sets _isEncounterPaused. Its async EncounterLoop never reads that flag, so calling PauseEncounter does not suspend an already running loop or its spawn delays. It also leaves _isEncounterActive true, which can make a later StartEncounter return immediately.
Derived implementations can provide different pause behavior. For the base behavior, use the loop's cancellation sources to control pending async work rather than assuming this flag freezes spawning.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.MobileEncounter.Start
member.summary: In Unity's Start callback, before this component's first Update, this method starts registration of encounter-profile spawnables and collects the groups' spawner settings and optional toggles.

remarks.para: For groups with an encounterProfile, this registers the profile's NPC spawnables and looks up SpawnAISettings on the configured spawner objects. For each group it also adds any SpawnerToggle found on a spawner object to spawnerToggles and enables useSpawnerToggle when the toggle count matches the spawner count.
This prepares configuration; it does not call StartEncounter or set isWarmed. Repeated calls add found toggles again because this method does not clear the toggle list first.
AssetSpawner.Register starts its RegisterAsync routine but does not wait for that task to finish, so Start begins profile-spawnable registration without confirming completion.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.MobileEncounter.StartEncounter
member.summary: Starts every group in PARALLEL, or the group at completeCount in SERIES, when the encounter is neither active nor complete.

remarks.para: It sets _isEncounterActive before starting groups and clears _isEncounterPaused after the start calls. It leaves completeCount unchanged, so a series start uses the existing count as its group index. Calls made while active or complete return without starting anything.
This overload supplies no AI target entity. Use the entity overload or MentalAllEncounter when the groups should investigate or attack a specific TriggerRefProxy.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.MobileEncounter.StartEncounter(Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Interaction.MarrowEntity)
member.summary: Starts the configured groups when allowed, then supplies the activator's TriggerRefProxy to groups with an investigate or aggression mode.
member.param: The entity supplying the AI target proxy, rather than an entity used for an activation-filter check.

remarks.para: A TriggerRefProxy is a component (data or behavior attached to a Unity object) that AI, the code controlling game characters, uses as a target reference for a character. It points to body parts such as the head, chest, and feet. The same active/complete guards and spawnOrder rules as the parameterless overload apply. After the group start calls, the method clears paused and searches the activator's children for TriggerRefProxy. Non-NONE mental groups then use that proxy for eligible current members and retain it for later spawns.

If the proxy is missing, it logs an error after starting the encounter; that failure does not undo the start. A call while already active or complete returns before updating the target. Use MentalAllEncounter to update targeting without starting.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.MobileEncounter.StartGroupEncounter(System.Int32)
member.summary: Replaces the indexed group's cancellation source and starts its timed encounter sequence, which continues over later frames as waits and spawning proceed.
member.param: A zero-based index valid in both spawnGroups and the cancellation array allocated by Awake.

remarks.para: It requests cancellation on an existing uncanceled source, calls the group's Setup unless _isEncounterPaused is true, creates a new source, and launches EncounterLoop with its token. Setup attaches the group's tracking to its spawners.

This method does not test _isEncounterActive or _complete itself. It relies on valid initialized arrays and a nonnull group; replacing spawnGroups after Awake can break the matching indices. Canceling the prior loop does not pass a cancellation token into a group spawn operation that is already in progress.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.MobileEncounter.StopEncounter
member.summary: Stops Unity coroutines attached to this component; a coroutine is a routine Unity resumes over later frames.

remarks.para: The checked base implementation does not cancel _spawnCTSs, change encounter flags, or kill members. It also does not stop the separate timed group loop: that sequence continues across later frames as its waits and spawning proceed, and the group's cancellation source is how the loop is asked to stop. Use CompleteEncounter when you need its completion event and group-loop cancellation, accounting for its initialized-source requirement.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.MobileEncounter.TerminateEncounter
member.summary: Runs CompleteEncounter, then clears the encounter flags and completion count and resets each group's tracking collections and counters.

remarks.para: If not already complete, CompleteEncounter first fires OnComplete and cancels the initialized sources. TerminateEncounter then sets active, paused, and complete false, resets completeCount to zero, and calls ResetVariables on every group.

The checked group reset clears its tracked brain sets and counters, not the physical NPCs, isComplete, or its setup flag. This is therefore not a complete despawn-and-rebuild operation or a guaranteed fresh replay. Completion must return successfully for the subsequent reset to run.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.SFX.TriggeredAudio.#ctor
member.summary: Initializes the default volume, minimum distance, and pitch to 1.0.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.SFX.TriggeredAudio.PlayAudio
member.summary: Requests one clip from at this component's current position, using , , and .

remarks.para: Call this method when your code or a trigger should make a sound. This component does not detect trigger collisions by itself. It reads its current world position and settings, then asks the 3D audio manager to play a non-looping sound there. The manager can finish that request later while it obtains a reusable audio player, so this void method does not wait for playback to start or finish.
The manager uses a spatial blend of 0.98 when this call supplies no blend value, so the sound is almost fully 3D. A blend of 0 is 2D audio and 1 is fully 3D audio.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.UI.SpawnablesPanelView.Activate
member.summary: Opens the spawnable browser, reloads favorites, and refreshes the category and item pages.

remarks.para: On its first activation, it prepares the category tree, collects pallet directory dates, cleans up crate tags, and selects the first tab. A pallet is a package of game or mod content; a spawnable crate is a catalog entry describing an object the spawn gun can create.
Later activations reuse that setup. Favorites are loaded again on every activation. firstActivation stays true during the first refresh and becomes false only after the refresh finishes.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.UI.SpawnablesPanelView.CleanupUserTags
member.summary: Repairs loaded crate tags and adds missing categories so the spawn browser can organize them.

remarks.para: This changes the Tags lists on loaded crates, rather than only changing button labels. It does nothing outside play mode. During the first activation it adds parent categories, recognizes several alternate tag spellings, supplies fallback categories, and adds unfamiliar tags beneath Other in the category tree.

For example, it converts Mag or Mags to Magazine and removes Ammo from entries identified as magazines. If a mod pallet outside the built-in pallet-title list has no tags on any of its crates after empty tags are removed, it gives those crates Untagged and the pallet title as tags. Calling it again can therefore affect shared catalog data seen by other code.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.UI.SpawnablesPanelView.CollectPalletDates
member.summary: Caches pallet folder dates for the browser’s newest-first pallet ordering.

remarks.para: For each loaded pallet it checks the folder formed from the runtime mods directory and the pallet barcode, which is its identifying string. The date is the folder’s last-write time, so it can change when folder contents change; it is not a recorded installation time.

A missing folder gets a fixed early fallback date. The BONELAB Content pallet is also remembered as dummyBonelabPallet, and its cached date is set to the earliest possible date so the combined BONELAB group sorts at the old end. First activation builds this cache; switching sort order reuses it.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.UI.SpawnablesPanelView.FavoriteItem
member.summary: Adds or removes the selected crate from favorites, updates its favorite marker, and saves the barcode list.

remarks.para: If selectedObject is missing, it does nothing. Otherwise it checks the crate barcode in favoriteCrates: an existing key is removed, and a missing key is added with the selected crate as its value.

The marker changes first, then the current pages refresh, then SaveFavorites runs. This refresh does not rebuild the category mapping, so removing a favorite does not by itself rebuild the Favorites tab’s item list.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.UI.SpawnablesPanelView.FilterTagTree
member.summary: Rebuilds the category rows for the current tree branch and updates the path and back button.

remarks.para: It keeps only child tags that also occur in _allTags, the tags found when the current tab’s item mapping was built. A leaf category uses its parent’s children so sibling categories remain available. All is inserted as the first row.

The back button is hidden at the root and shown inside a branch. The path text joins parent names with " / "; fallback tags such as Gun Other are displayed as Other. This prepares all rows for that branch, not just one visible page.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.UI.SpawnablesPanelView.GenerateCategoriesMapping
member.summary: Rebuilds the lists of spawnable crates that the selected browser tab can display.

remarks.para: It clears the existing category map and navigation rows, then gathers eligible crates from the loaded content catalog. Locked unlockable crates, hidden crates, and avatar crates are excluded. Developer Tools additionally requires the DevTool tag; Favorites requires a barcode in the active save’s favorite list.

The category tabs group crates by tag. The Pallets tab groups them by package title and combines the six built-in BONELAB package titles into BONELAB. The Authors tab groups by the pallet author after removing whitespace. It sorts each item list by crate title, while the Pallets navigation rows use alphabetical or newest-first package order.

It replaces the Ammo category with the entries listed in ammoBarcodes, in that list’s order, and copies the generated navigation tags into _allTags for later tree filtering. Rebuilding these lists does not itself represent a completed object spawn.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.UI.SpawnablesPanelView.HighlightProperSpawnItem
member.summary: Shows selection highlights only on the pages containing the remembered item and category indexes.

remarks.para: The remembered indexes count across their full lists, starting at 0. For each visible page it checks whether the remembered index lies on that page, then highlights the matching button slot. Changing pages can hide a highlight without changing selectedObject.
An item index of -1 means no item should be highlighted. This method updates the highlight images; it does not select a different crate or send selection notifications.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.UI.SpawnablesPanelView.LoadFavorites
member.summary: Replaces the panel’s favorites dictionary with the barcode entries from the active save.

remarks.para: It first asks the save manager to load the active save, then clears favoriteCrates. Valid barcode strings are looked up in the loaded content catalog and added to the dictionary; invalid barcode strings are skipped.

The catalog lookup’s success result is not checked before its output is stored. A key in this dictionary therefore does not guarantee that its crate value is available. Activate runs this again each time the panel opens, overwriting unsaved dictionary changes.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.UI.SpawnablesPanelView.MeowButton
member.summary: Requests meowClip as a 3D sound relative to the capsule button.

remarks.para: It does nothing if the clip is missing. With a clip assigned, capsuleButton and its Transform, Unity’s position-and-orientation component, are required. The sound request uses volume 0.3, meaning 30% of the usual level, and base pitch 1. At normal game speed this gives normal clip speed; the audio manager lowers pitch during slow motion.

The button Transform is supplied as the parent, with the button’s localPosition as the sound’s local offset. localPosition measures meters along the button’s parent axes; the audio request interprets the supplied offset relative to the button itself. It does not simply supply the button’s world position.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.UI.SpawnablesPanelView.NextPage
member.summary: Shows the next item page if one exists.

remarks.para: At the last page it does nothing; pages do not wrap around. It refreshes the page label and visible buttons, stores the new page index, then refreshes the selection highlights. It does not choose a different spawnable crate.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.UI.SpawnablesPanelView.NextTagPage
member.summary: Shows the next category page if one exists.

remarks.para: At the last page it does nothing; pages do not wrap around. It refreshes the page label and visible buttons, stores the new page index, then refreshes the selection highlights. It does not choose a different spawnable crate.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.UI.SpawnablesPanelView.PopulateMenu
member.summary: Refreshes the visible category and item buttons and their page controls from the current browser lists.

remarks.para: It filters the category tree on the first tab, then calculates page counts by rounding each list’s length divided by its button count upward. For example, 13 items with 6 item buttons need 3 pages. These are counts of entries and pages, not time or distance.

It updates item and category labels, hides unused button slots, and refreshes favorite markers. The content-writing routines require an assigned spawnGun. It does not rebuild the category mapping or update the selected item’s information text. An empty _activeTags list returns before refreshing the display.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.UI.SpawnablesPanelView.PrevPage
member.summary: Shows the previous item page if one exists.

remarks.para: At the first page it does nothing; pages do not wrap around. It refreshes the page label and visible buttons, stores the new page index, then refreshes the selection highlights. It does not choose a different spawnable crate.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.UI.SpawnablesPanelView.PrevTagPage
member.summary: Shows the previous category page if one exists.

remarks.para: At the first page it does nothing; pages do not wrap around. It refreshes the page label and visible buttons, stores the new page index, then refreshes the selection highlights. It does not choose a different spawnable crate.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.UI.SpawnablesPanelView.SaveFavorites
member.summary: Copies the current favorite barcode keys into the active save’s player settings and asks the save manager to save them.

remarks.para: It replaces the saved list with a new list of favoriteCrates keys. The dictionary values are not written, so this stores content identifiers rather than spawned objects. It does not reload the dictionary or rebuild the visible Favorites category.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.UI.SpawnablesPanelView.SwapSortButton
member.summary: Switches the Pallets tab between newest-first package order and alphabetical package order.

remarks.para: It flips sortSwap, then selects tab 3 and rebuilds that tab. false selects NEW, using cached directory last-write times with newer packages first; true selects ABC, using package titles alphabetically. The individual crate lists still sort by crate title.
Selecting the tab resets both page indexes to 0 and clears the remembered item highlight. The dates are not collected again by this method.

member.name: M:Il2CppSLZ.UI.SpawnablesPanelView.TreeBackButton
member.summary: Moves the category browser to its parent branch and refreshes the first pages there.

remarks.para: At the root, which has no parent, it does nothing. Otherwise it clears the remembered item highlight, resets both page indexes and the category highlight index to 0, and selects All at the root or the parent branch’s tag deeper in the tree.
It refreshes the highlights and pages without sending a crate-selection notification. The previously selected crate can remain selected even though its highlight was cleared.

member.name: P:Il2CppPuppetMasta.BehaviourAnimatedStagger.FallParamsGroup.groups
member.summary: Chooses which muscle groups receive this override's fall settings during the animated loss-of-balance sequence.

remarks.para: A Muscle is the controller for one simulated body part. At the beginning of LoseBalance, the first matching entry caps that muscle’s stored strength multiplier at startMuscleWeightMlp. Both values are unitless and control how strongly the body part tries to follow its intended animation. Current strength 0.8 and a chosen start value of 0.3 become 0.3; current strength 0.2 remains 0.2.

For example, including Head makes muscles whose own group is Head use this entry's fallParams when the settings are looked up. Matching uses exact enum values; this array does not create muscles or change their assigned groups.

BehaviourAnimatedStagger searches groupOverrides in order, so an earlier matching entry wins when a group appears in several entries. An empty groups array matches no muscles; an encountered null array can fail during the lookup. Set up this list before the fall sequence begins. The additional GetFallParams lookups occur before the first yield, a pause until a later game update. Their returned settings are not used by the following smoothing, and the sequence marks that lookup phase complete before yielding, so later resumes skip it. Editing groups after initialization does not recalculate the initial strength cap in this sequence.

member.name: P:Il2CppPuppetMasta.BehaviourFall.onEnd
member.summary: Runs the configured fall-ending actions once when the allowed fall has lasted long enough and the first physics body is moving slowly enough.

remarks.para: During physics updates, the end check requires canEnd to be true, the accumulated timer to be at least minTime seconds, and PuppetMaster to have finished switching its physical mode or alive/dead/frozen state. It also needs an available Rigidbody for the first entry in PuppetMaster.muscles. A Rigidbody is the Unity object that stores a physical body's motion; each muscle is one physical part of the character.

The speed check uses that body's full world-space velocity, including sideways and vertical motion, in meters per second. Its speed must be strictly less than maxEndVelocity. Equal speed does not pass. This check does not require a ground hit, even though the same update also checks ground height for animation blending.

The timer adds the current game-time step before checking the limit. For example, with minTime = 1.5 and maxEndVelocity = 0.5, the event can run on a physics update after at least 1.5 game seconds have accumulated, provided the body is moving below 0.5 meters per second and the other conditions pass. This is a threshold checked on updates, not an alarm guaranteed to fire at exactly 1.5 seconds.

The behavior marks the event as already triggered before running it, so later checks do not repeat it. Activation resets this mark and the timer at the start of its activation routine; OnReactivate resets them too. The event first runs its parameterless UnityEvent callbacks, meaning the routines connected to the event receive no speed, time or character argument. It then processes the configured animation actions and finally tries to enable the behavior named by switchToBehaviour. Merely meeting the end conditions does not independently disable this fall behavior; what happens next depends on those configured actions.

member.name: P:Il2CppPuppetMasta.BehaviourPowerLegs.Block
member.summary: Holds the blocking animation and arm-targeting settings activated by ContextBlock, and the arm and spine strength settings read by ContextBlockAnim.

remarks.para: This is a settings object, not an event notification or the current blocking status. Assigning it does not raise the hands or enable blocking. The ContextBlock command activates its animation, saves it as the active targeting setting, copies limbStrengthMultiplier into both arms and spineStrengthMultiplier into the spine, and clears the melee-active flag. ContextBlockAnim plays its own fixed blocking animation instead, but still reads these strength multipliers. These unitless strength multipliers control how strongly the physics body follows the intended pose, subject to health and other strength settings; they are not damage reduction percentages.

The regular fist-fight AI enables or disables BlockActive by changing a stored flag and an Animator blocking flag. An Animator is Unity’s animation player. That setter does not activate this Block object, and the inspected TriggerAttack blocking path calls that setter. Therefore changing Block.animationState does not change the animation requested by that regular blocking path.

For ContextBlock, the target is the world position of IKPunchGameObject, the configured object marking a test target. IK, or inverse kinematics, moves a limb toward a chosen point. The point is converted into the NavMeshAgent object’s local space: coordinates measured from that object using its directions and scale. The stored correction is that point minus localContactPoint, the configured point the animation would otherwise reach. Both use Unity distance units, normally metres at scale 1. The NavMeshAgent is Unity’s component that follows paths through walkable space. The correction is applied along the character root’s directions as an offset from the animated hand position. The root is the Transform, the position and rotation component that positions and turns the whole animated character. The normal movement update aligns the root’s rotation with the NavMeshAgent object’s rotation; these are still distinct references. Capturing the point uses the path-following object’s scale, while applying the offset along the root’s directions uses rotation without applying that scale. targetedLimb determines whether the correction is applied to the left or right arm; this updater does not apply both arms just because both strength multipliers were changed, and it does not apply the leg choices.

The setting contains the animationState name, layer number, crossfadeTime in seconds and clipLength, the configured targeting duration in scaled game seconds. Scaled game seconds are seconds on the game clock: they pass more slowly during slow motion and stop while that clock is paused. An Animator is Unity’s animation player; a positive crossfadeTime blends into the named animation, while zero or a negative value starts it directly. Targeting progress is elapsed scaled game seconds since activation divided by the cached clipLength. It is not the Animator’s live playback progress. startIkNormalTime and contactPointNormalTime are fractions of that configured duration: with a 1-second duration, values 0.3 and 0.6 start the correction at 0.3 second and reach its full amount at 0.6 second. The correction then falls back to zero at progress 1. Configure a positive duration and timing fractions satisfying 0 <= startIkNormalTime < contactPointNormalTime < 1 to avoid the timing divisions becoming invalid.

Configure this object before activation. Its first activation, unless Initialize was called earlier, caches the animation name and timing division factors; call Initialize again after changing those values. Replacing Block later does not replace the object already saved as the active setting. ContextBlock starts a coroutine, a sequence that pauses and resumes on later physics steps, to update that active correction. An update after configured progress becomes strictly greater than 1 clears the saved object, restores both arm multipliers to 2 and spine multiplier to 1, and clears the melee-active flag. At exactly 1 the correction is zero, but cleanup waits for a later update. For example, configuring a 1-second duration does not guarantee cleanup at exactly 1 second or that the regular BlockActive flag has become false.

member.name: P:Il2CppPuppetMasta.BehaviourPowerLegs.Fist1MidUppercutL
member.summary: Sets the animation, timing and arm-targeting correction for the left uppercut selected in FistFight combat.

remarks.para: This holds the animation and arm-targeting settings chosen for a left uppercut while agroState is FistFight. It is a settings object, rather than a notification that you subscribe to. Setting it does not immediately start a punch. The attack routine first checks conditions such as its cooldown, target distance and facing direction. It then chooses a side using the two arms’ remaining health plus a small random adjustment, and makes a separate random choice between the two attacks on that side. That second choice is between the straight punch and mid uppercut; a random value greater than 0.5 chooses the straight punch, while 0.5 or less chooses the uppercut.

The uppercut aims near the target’s chest: it takes chestTran’s world position and adds an offset of 0.08 unit along the chest’s right direction and -0.15 unit along its up direction, with no forward offset. At normal scene scale this is 8 centimetres to the chest’s right and 15 centimetres down. The directions come from the chest’s own rotation, not this NPC’s or the scene’s axes. chestTran is the target’s configured chest Transform, Unity’s object position, rotation and scale component.

The setting contains the animationState name, layer number, crossfadeTime in seconds and clipLength, the configured targeting duration in scaled game seconds. Scaled game seconds are seconds on the game clock: they pass more slowly during slow motion and stop while that clock is paused. An Animator is Unity’s animation player; a positive crossfadeTime blends into the named animation, while zero or a negative value starts it directly. Targeting progress is elapsed scaled game seconds since activation divided by the cached clipLength. It is not the Animator’s live playback progress. startIkNormalTime and contactPointNormalTime are fractions of that configured duration: with a 1-second duration, values 0.3 and 0.6 start the correction at 0.3 second and reach its full amount at 0.6 second. The correction then falls back to zero at progress 1. Configure a positive duration and timing fractions satisfying 0 <= startIkNormalTime < contactPointNormalTime < 1 to avoid the timing divisions becoming invalid.

IK, or inverse kinematics, moves a limb toward a chosen point. At attack activation the target point is converted from world space, the whole scene’s coordinates, into the NavMeshAgent object’s local space, coordinates measured from that object using its directions and scale. The stored correction is this local target point minus localContactPoint, the configured point the animation would otherwise reach. These are Unity distance units, normally metres at scale 1. The NavMeshAgent is Unity’s component that follows paths through walkable space. The correction is applied along the character root’s directions as an offset from the animated hand position. The root is the Transform, the position and rotation component that positions and turns the whole animated character. The normal movement update aligns the root’s rotation with the NavMeshAgent object’s rotation; these are still distinct references. Capturing the point uses the path-following object’s scale, while applying the offset along the root’s directions uses rotation without applying that scale. For example, with the path-following object’s scale at 1 and its directions aligned with the root’s, a target 0.2 metre farther forward than localContactPoint adds a 0.2-metre forward offset from the animated hand position at contact time. The target point is captured when the attack begins; it is not continuously recaptured from a moving target. Set targetedLimb to the matching LeftArm or RightArm: the property’s name selects an attack slot, but targetedLimb selects which arm receives this correction. This updater handles those two arm choices, not the leg choices.

Assign and configure this setting before starting an attack. On its first activation, unless Initialize was already called, it caches the animation name and the timing division factors. Changing animationState, clipLength or the timing fractions later requires Initialize again to refresh those cached values. The selected setting object is saved for the active attack, so replacing this property does not replace an attack already in progress. During a normal melee attack, limbStrengthMultiplier is copied into the chosen arm’s strength setting and spineStrengthMultiplier into the spine’s. These are unitless multipliers for following the intended pose, not damage amounts or new health. A value of 2 requests twice the contribution from that strength setting compared with 1, while health and other settings still affect the final force. On a later targeting update whose configured progress is strictly greater than 1, the active setting is cleared, both arm multipliers become 2, the spine multiplier becomes 1 and the melee-active flag is cleared. At exactly 1, the correction is zero but cleanup has not happened yet. Actual completion can therefore occur on a later frame.

That branch sets a separate throw-active flag and a release deadline 0.5 scaled game second after activation. It uses fixed right-arm and spine strength multipliers of 5 and 2.5 there, rather than copying the setting’s two strength multipliers as the normal melee branch does. After the 0.5-game-second deadline has passed, a later eligible update of the character’s AI, the game’s action-selection rules, calls Throw to request a projectile spawn. A spawn request asks the game to create or reuse an object and can finish later. Once a valid projectile is supplied, its spawn callback, a routine called when that spawn succeeds, applies the launch force. After submitting the request, Throw clears the throw-active flag; clearing that flag does not prove the spawn or launch has finished. Reaching the deadline or activating this animation is not proof that an object has already been thrown.

member.name: P:Il2CppPuppetMasta.BehaviourPowerLegs.WildPunchJabL
member.summary: Sets the animation, timing and arm-targeting correction for the left jab selected in WildPunch combat.

remarks.para: This holds the animation and arm-targeting settings chosen for a left jab while agroState is WildPunch. It is a settings object, rather than a notification that you subscribe to. Setting it does not immediately start a punch. The attack routine first checks conditions such as its cooldown, target distance and facing direction. It then chooses a side using the two arms’ remaining health plus a small random adjustment, and makes a separate random choice between the two attacks on that side. That second choice is between the jab and large punch; a random value greater than 0.5 chooses the jab, while 0.5 or less chooses the large punch.

The normal wild punch starts with the world position of the target’s targetHead Rigidbody. A Rigidbody is Unity’s component for a body moved by physics; here it supplies the configured target head’s current position. When the target is beyond meleeRange, the attack routine can instead choose a nearby eligible collider found along the attack direction; a collider is a shape used for contact checks. This means the captured point can belong to a nearer object rather than the intended target’s head.

The setting contains the animationState name, layer number, crossfadeTime in seconds and clipLength, the configured targeting duration in scaled game seconds. Scaled game seconds are seconds on the game clock: they pass more slowly during slow motion and stop while that clock is paused. An Animator is Unity’s animation player; a positive crossfadeTime blends into the named animation, while zero or a negative value starts it directly. Targeting progress is elapsed scaled game seconds since activation divided by the cached clipLength. It is not the Animator’s live playback progress. startIkNormalTime and contactPointNormalTime are fractions of that configured duration: with a 1-second duration, values 0.3 and 0.6 start the correction at 0.3 second and reach its full amount at 0.6 second. The correction then falls back to zero at progress 1. Configure a positive duration and timing fractions satisfying 0 <= startIkNormalTime < contactPointNormalTime < 1 to avoid the timing divisions becoming invalid.

IK, or inverse kinematics, moves a limb toward a chosen point. At attack activation the target point is converted from world space, the whole scene’s coordinates, into the NavMeshAgent object’s local space, coordinates measured from that object using its directions and scale. The stored correction is this local target point minus localContactPoint, the configured point the animation would otherwise reach. These are Unity distance units, normally metres at scale 1. The NavMeshAgent is Unity’s component that follows paths through walkable space. The correction is applied along the character root’s directions as an offset from the animated hand position. The root is the Transform, the position and rotation component that positions and turns the whole animated character. The normal movement update aligns the root’s rotation with the NavMeshAgent object’s rotation; these are still distinct references. Capturing the point uses the path-following object’s scale, while applying the offset along the root’s directions uses rotation without applying that scale. For example, with the path-following object’s scale at 1 and its directions aligned with the root’s, a target 0.2 metre farther forward than localContactPoint adds a 0.2-metre forward offset from the animated hand position at contact time. The target point is captured when the attack begins; it is not continuously recaptured from a moving target. Set targetedLimb to the matching LeftArm or RightArm: the property’s name selects an attack slot, but targetedLimb selects which arm receives this correction. This updater handles those two arm choices, not the leg choices.

Assign and configure this setting before starting an attack. On its first activation, unless Initialize was already called, it caches the animation name and the timing division factors. Changing animationState, clipLength or the timing fractions later requires Initialize again to refresh those cached values. The selected setting object is saved for the active attack, so replacing this property does not replace an attack already in progress. During a normal melee attack, limbStrengthMultiplier is copied into the chosen arm’s strength setting and spineStrengthMultiplier into the spine’s. These are unitless multipliers for following the intended pose, not damage amounts or new health. A value of 2 requests twice the contribution from that strength setting compared with 1, while health and other settings still affect the final force. On a later targeting update whose configured progress is strictly greater than 1, the active setting is cleared, both arm multipliers become 2, the spine multiplier becomes 1 and the melee-active flag is cleared. At exactly 1, the correction is zero but cleanup has not happened yet. Actual completion can therefore occur on a later frame.

member.name: P:Il2CppPuppetMasta.BehaviourPowerLegs.onGetUpProne
member.summary: Provides the first animation setting to activate when the character starts getting up from a face-down pose.

remarks.para: When SwitchLocoState enters GetUp, the body sensors choose the prone array when the hips’ forward direction is pointing below the character root’s up direction. In the usual upright setup this corresponds to lying face-down. The character root is the Transform, the position and rotation component that positions and turns the whole animated character. That test follows the root’s up direction, not a fixed scene-up direction. It does not require a perfectly flat pose. If the hips’ forward direction is exactly perpendicular to that up direction, as in a sideways pose, the supine array is selected.

This array contains AnimatorEvent settings that tell the Animator, Unity’s animation player, which animation to play. Despite the plural name, the inspected GetUp entry reads and activates only element 0. It does not play every entry or choose a random entry. Assign a non-null array with at least one non-null setting; a null array, empty array or null first setting causes the get-up setup to fail. For example, an array containing two get-up settings still activates only the first one here.

The first setting supplies animationState, the animation state name, layer, the animation layer number, and crossfadeTime, a blending duration in seconds. A positive duration blends into the state; zero or a negative duration plays it directly. resetNormalizedTime requests a start at animation progress 0 when true; when false, the call leaves that progress argument at Unity’s default. The state name is cached as a numeric animation lookup value on the first activation unless Initialize was already called. Changing the name after that needs Initialize again; merely replacing other array entries has no effect on this get-up activation.

GetUp entry disables foot targeting, sets the body’s strength settings and, for this face-down branch, sets a retry/state-switch deadline 2.6 scaled game seconds after entry. Scaled game seconds are seconds on the game clock: they pass more slowly during slow motion and stop while that clock is paused. A positive coolDown passed to SwitchLocoState overrides that deadline. This timer is separate from crossfadeTime and from the animation’s actual length; it does not prove the character is standing at exactly 2.6 seconds. After activating element 0, the method aligns the body for the get-up animation, samples the intended body rotations and starts smoothing the physics pose toward them with a 0.5-second smoothing setting. It stores locoState as GetUp after that setup. Later AI updates check grounding, support and balance before moving to another movement state.
