member.name: P:Il2CppPuppetMasta.Booster.groups
member.summary: Configures which body-part categories a targeted boost should affect, such as hands or legs.

remarks.para: A muscle here is a simulated body part connected by a physics joint, a connection that controls how body parts move relative to one another. Each muscle has a group label such as Hand, Arm, or Leg. This array selects those labels rather than naming individual joints.

A boost can temporarily increase resistance to collision damage and the impact strength delivered to another puppet. The booster stores those choices separately as immunity, a protection amount from 0 to 1, and impulseMlp, a multiplier for impact strength. For example, selecting Hand describes a boost aimed at hand muscles rather than the whole body.

The fullBody option takes priority: when it is true, the groups and individual muscles selections are ignored. This array starts empty. It is saved configuration; assigning a group does not itself apply a boost or schedule an update. The code that applies the booster must use the selection when choosing muscles.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Achievements.AchievementsDict
member.summary: The registry of accepted achievement IDs and the readable names used in award logs.

remarks.para: For example, the built-in entry ACH_DESCENT maps to Descent. Both award methods check for the key and send ACH_DESCENT itself to Steam; Descent is appended to their log message. Use the keys when selecting an achievement to award.

Changing a readable value changes the log’s name, not the ID requested from Steam. Removing a key makes the award methods reject that ID. Adding a key only changes this local validation registry; it does not define a new achievement in Steam.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Achievements.note
member.summary: Text stored with this component; the award methods do not read it.

remarks.para: You can keep a scene-design reminder here. To select the actual achievement, pass its dictionary key to AWARDACHIEVEMENT or Unlock. Editing note does not change the ID supplied to those methods. No runtime use of the text was found in the audited Achievements methods; code outside this class was not exhaustively checked.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ArenaLootItem.lootType
member.summary: Chooses which weapon list supplies a replacement when a wave is copied with randomized loot.

remarks.para: CopyWaveProfile with randLoot enabled uses LIGHTGUN for a pistol or SMG, MEDGUN for a rifle, MELEE for a blade or blunt weapon, and HEAVYGUN for a shotgun. The paired choices use an equal random choice, then select a random entry from the chosen list.

When randomized loot is disabled, the wave copy keeps the original item reference. Changing lootType does not turn the configured spawnable into a different kind of weapon when that entry is spawned directly.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ArenaLootItem.percentage
member.summary: Threshold used by the weapon-mode loot roll to decide whether this entry is included.

remarks.para: Looter.GetAllLootItems rolls one integer from 0 through 99 for the whole list. Each entry passes if that same number is greater than zero and no greater than its percentage. For example, 25 accepts rolls 1 through 25. A shared roll of 20 includes entries set to both 25 and 70; a roll of 50 includes only the 70 entry.

This is not a relative weight or a separate roll for each item, and the entries do not need to add up to 100. Zero never passes. Even 100 fails when the shared roll is zero, so it is not a guaranteed inclusion. Fractional settings only change which whole-number rolls pass: 25.5 still accepts 1 through 25.

The constructor starts this setting at 100. The Inspector, Unity’s configuration panel, shows a range of 0 to 100, but the loot routine does not clamp values written by code. The ordinary CoSpawnLoots path requests a spawn for each valid configured entry without consulting percentage, and the six random weapon-list selectors also ignore it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ArenaLootItem.spawnable
member.summary: Crate and pool-policy settings for the world object this loot entry asks the arena to spawn.

remarks.para: A Spawnable is an input description. Its crate reference identifies the packaged object asset to create; its pool policy gives the rules for creating new instances or reusing old ones. Changing it selects the actual loot object; the title and lootType fields do not alter that object’s contents.

Ordinary wave loot registers the configured entries and requests each valid one at the spawner’s world position with identity rotation, meaning no extra rotation. Weapon mode first filters the entries through Looter, then requests the selected objects at its player-relative gun drop location. Both requests supply no scale override or parent transform, the object to place the new object under in the scene hierarchy. Weapon requests also use identity rotation, meaning no extra rotation.

This field is an input description, not a reference to the instance already created in the scene. Ordinary wave loot reads this value when issuing the request. Weapon mode copies the value when Looter builds its selected list, before the spawn requests; later edits to the original entry do not change the descriptions already saved in that list.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ArenaLootItem.title
member.summary: Text label for identifying this loot entry while organizing its configuration.

remarks.para: The audited Looter, wave-copy routines, six random weapon selectors and both arena loot-spawning routines do not read title. Those routines choose the object through spawnable and the random replacement through lootType, so changing this text does not change their loot choices.
These consumers do not establish an on-screen display for this label. A separate editor or UI script would need to read it to show it to the player.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ArenaMenuController.selectedColor
member.summary: Color applied to an enemy button's image when its profile is added to the custom-game selection.

remarks.para: ToggleEnemyProfile copies this color to the matching buttonImages entry after adding the profile to enemyHash. Red, green, blue and alpha control the UI tint and opacity. Selection means the profile will be included in the next custom build; it does not mean the Button component is enabled or disabled.
Changing this color does not immediately recolor the buttons. It affects later selection tint writes. Editing enemyHash directly also does not refresh their colors.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ArenaMenuController.survivalDifficultyDescription
member.summary: Explanation displayed instead of a fixed difficulty name on the active survival page.

remarks.para: SetupActivePage copies this string into activeChallengeDiffText when the selected group's game mode is SURVIVAL. The constructor initializes it to Difficulty increases as rounds increase.
This is explanatory text, not a difficulty setting or calculation. Changing it affects the next SetupActivePage refresh. Other game modes display the controller's ArenaDifficulty name instead.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ArenaMenuController.timeAchievedText
member.summary: Text component showing the survival time stored in supplied player save data.

remarks.para: When playerStats.survivalRoundReached is positive, OnLoadSaveFile reads survivalTimeReached as seconds, discards its fractional part, and displays the resulting TimeSpan after Time Elapsed: . For example, 125.8 seconds displays a duration of 00:02:05.

A zero or negative saved round produces Time Elapsed 00:00:00 instead. This is a refreshed save-data label, not a running timer or a comparison that chooses the best time. Supply updated player data through OnLoadSaveFile to refresh it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ArenaMenuController.trialDescriptionText
member.summary: Text component that TrialSelect fills with the selected arena group's title and description.

remarks.para: TrialSelect uses a valid zero-based index in arenaGameController.roundProfileGroupList and joins that group's displayTitle and descriptionText with a colon and space. ChallengeSelect fills challengeDescriptionText separately.

The label refreshes when TrialSelect runs. Editing its text changes the display, without selecting a profile or starting a match. Later changes to the group's title or description require another refresh.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ArenaMenuController.waveCount
member.summary: Number of waves generated inside the single custom round when the menu builds its custom group.

remarks.para: A wave is one scheduled set of enemies within a round. UpdateCustomGroup clears customProfileGroup's old rounds, creates one LIMITED round, and adds waveCount waves to it. This setting counts waves, not survival rounds or enemies.

For example, waveCount = 3 generates three waves. With three selected profiles and enemyCount = 4, their scheduled enemy totals are 12, 15 and 18: each later wave adds one repetition of every selected profile. concurrentEnemyCount separately limits the normal spawn loop's enemies at once.

The builder adds no waves when the count is zero or negative; it still creates the round. It does not clamp this setting. Changes affect the next custom build, without resizing already generated wave lists or changing a running wave.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ArenaMenuController.waveEnemyCountText
member.summary: Label showing the cached first-wave enemy total calculated by the custom selection controls.

remarks.para: ToggleEnemyProfile and ToggleEnemyCount write enemyHash.Count times enemyCount to enemiesPerWave and this label while at least one profile is selected. Three profiles with count 4 display 12. Later generated waves contain extra repetitions per profile, so this label does not describe every wave.

Removing the last selected profile leaves the previous total and label unchanged. Direct field edits do not refresh the label, and the custom builder calculates its own enemy lists without reading this display cache.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.healthPackCount
member.summary: Tally of health pickups successfully configured by this controller, checked against before random pack-drop requests.

remarks.para: The large- and small-pack spawn callbacks increase this count after finding the pickup components, connecting their despawn notification, initializing the pickup timer and assigning this arena controller. A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action; a spawn request that has not reached its callback is not yet counted.

HealthPickup.OnDespawn calls HealthPackCollected, which subtracts 1. Despawn removes a pickup from active play, including when its timer expires. This happens when a tracked pickup despawns, not only when the player collects it. The subtraction has no zero clamp. For example, a count of 3 and healthPackLimit of 3 blocks another chance-based request until the count falls.

This is bookkeeping, not an automatic search for every live health pack. Direct large/small spawn requests bypass the limit check, and several pending requests can pass it before their callbacks increase the count. Changing the count affects later checks without creating or removing packs.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.healthPackLimit
member.summary: Count threshold that blocks new chance-based health-pack requests when healthPackCount reaches it.

remarks.para: SpawnHealthPackOnChance returns when healthPackCount is greater than or equal to this value. Passing the check only allows the later health-mode and random-drop tests; it does not guarantee a pack. For example, limit 2 allows a chance check at count 1 and blocks it at count 2.

This does not remove existing packs or limit direct calls to SpawnLargeHealthPack and SpawnSmallHealthPack. Packs are counted when their spawn callbacks, routines called to report spawn completion, finish their setup, so overlapping pending requests can exceed the threshold. Lowering the limit only changes future chance checks. There is no runtime clamp or automatic repair of a manually changed count.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.initHeavyAmmo
member.summary: Additional heavy reserve cartridges granted when the controller handles a player spawn.

remarks.para: OnPlayerSpawn passes this amount to RewardAmmo for the heavy cartridge type only when it is greater than zero. The unit is a cartridge count: for example, 20 adds 20 cartridges to the existing reserve. Zero and negative values are skipped in this starting-ammunition path.

This adds to AmmoInventory; it does not set the total to this value, load a weapon’s magazine, or create a physical ammunition pickup. The callback is a routine called to report the player-spawn action, so another reported player spawn can add the amount again. Changing the field does not immediately grant ammunition and is separate from merely starting an arena match.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.initLightAmmo
member.summary: Additional light reserve cartridges granted when the controller handles a player spawn.

remarks.para: OnPlayerSpawn passes this amount to RewardAmmo for the light cartridge type only when it is greater than zero. The unit is a cartridge count: for example, 20 adds 20 cartridges to the existing reserve. Zero and negative values are skipped in this starting-ammunition path.

This adds to AmmoInventory; it does not set the total to this value, load a weapon’s magazine, or create a physical ammunition pickup. The callback is a routine called to report the player-spawn action, so another reported player spawn can add the amount again. Changing the field does not immediately grant ammunition and is separate from merely starting an arena match.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.initMedAmmo
member.summary: Additional medium reserve cartridges granted when the controller handles a player spawn.

remarks.para: OnPlayerSpawn passes this amount to RewardAmmo for the medium cartridge type only when it is greater than zero. The unit is a cartridge count: for example, 20 adds 20 cartridges to the existing reserve. Zero and negative values are skipped in this starting-ammunition path.

This adds to AmmoInventory; it does not set the total to this value, load a weapon’s magazine, or create a physical ammunition pickup. The callback is a routine called to report the player-spawn action, so another reported player spawn can add the amount again. Changing the field does not immediately grant ammunition and is separate from merely starting an arena match.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.initPlayerAmmoVal
member.summary: Snapshot of the player’s total light, medium and heavy reserve cartridges taken by ARENA_PlayerEnter.

remarks.para: The entry flow adds the three default cartridge counts and stores their sum here. For example, reserves of 10 light, 5 medium and 2 heavy produce a snapshot of 17 cartridges. This is a measured baseline; it is not an amount applied to the player’s weapons or ammunition inventory.

CalculatePlayerScore combines this snapshot with the profile’s total group ammunition, or the loot spawner’s granted ammunition on QUIT, to calculate its reported ammunition-used value. In the checked score arithmetic, that baseline cancels out of the separate remaining-ammunition bonus, which uses the currently counted reserves. Editing the snapshot can change that bookkeeping but does not award ammunition.
Each successful entry call takes a new snapshot after its entry event and sound/start handling. It does not continuously follow the player’s reserve changes.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.isPlayerReady
member.summary: Readiness gate required by ARENA_PlayerEnter and used to avoid repeating ARENA_StartMatch setup.

remarks.para: ARENA_StartMatch returns if this is already true. Otherwise it sets the flag to true before invoking playerReady, so that event’s callbacks, routines called to report an action, see the player already marked ready. ARENA_PlayerEnter rejects entry while the flag is false.

The ON_START and objective progression paths can set the flag directly before calling entry; those assignments do not by themselves invoke playerReady. ARENA_CancelMatch, CancelCurrentChallenge and EndOfMode clear it. This is the controller’s stored permission to run entry setup, not a check of the player’s position or a guarantee that combat has begun.
Manually setting true can cause a later ARENA_StartMatch call to skip its event and geometry setup. Clearing it does not stop enemy producers, end an ongoing wave or perform full match cleanup.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.isRung
member.summary: Bell latch that prevents ARENA_RingTheBell from scheduling another opening countdown until reset.

remarks.para: The bell method acts only in ON_TRIGGER_BELL mode and while this flag is false. It sets isRung to true first, then invokes ringBell, then starts a countdown using arenaStartDelay, the configured delay in game-time seconds, and immediately requests current-wave loot if the arena is not QUIT and a valid loot spawner is found. Event callbacks, routines called to report an action, therefore see the bell already latched before the countdown is started.

ARENA_ResetTheBell clears the flag. PROTECT entry/setup also clears it before staging the king. Setting true manually suppresses the bell method; setting false makes it eligible again but does not ring the bell or stop an earlier countdown. This records the controller’s accepted bell action, not whether a particular bell sound is audible.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.isSpawning
member.summary: Control flag required by the ordinary enemy loop before it can request another enemy.

remarks.para: StartSpawning sets this true before choosing the ordinary async loop or initial objective coroutine, a sequence that continues over frames. Async work can finish later while its caller continues. NPC means a non-player character. The ordinary loop also requires arenaState to be ACTIVE. A true flag does not mean an NPC is appearing on every frame: the producer can be waiting for a spawn, a delay or an available slot in the current wave.

Wave reset clears the flag and cancels enemySpawnCTS or stops enemySpawnRoutine. That reset invokes waveEnd before clearing isSpawning, so listeners can still observe its previous value. StopSpawningAndCureAll clears the flag too, but does not cancel or stop those producers.

Setting false alone does not safely terminate the ordinary async loop: its invalid-state branch repeatedly logs without pausing for another frame until cancellation is observed. enemySpawnCTS is the cancellation source that tells the ordinary loop to stop when it checks that request. Use that source to request cancellation of the loop. The initial objective producer does not use this flag as its per-request stop condition; changing the field is not a substitute for stopping its saved coroutine.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.isWaveOngoing
member.summary: Flag that keeps the arena’s elapsed-time and player-movement routines continuing across frames.

remarks.para: StartNextWave sets this true after refreshing the arena display and before invoking waveBegin. Its callbacks, routines called to report an action, therefore see the flag already true. Co_TimerUp_Arena and CoPlayerDist are coroutines, sequences that continue over frames, and finish when their next step sees the flag false.

The wave-reset sequence invokes waveEnd before it clears this flag. Listeners can therefore still see true during that event. Setting the field false does not itself invoke waveEnd, remove non-player characters (NPCs) from active play, or cancel enemy spawning; those actions belong to the reset flow. Removing a character from active play is called despawning.
This is a stored control flag, not a live count of remaining enemies. It can stay true briefly while end-of-wave handling is waiting to start cleanup.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.killComboRoutine
member.summary: Saved handle for the coroutine that counts down the kill-combo window.

remarks.para: A coroutine is a sequence that continues over several frames. An eligible non-objective enemy death starts CoKillCombo and saves its handle here. That sequence copies comboTimeVal, the new window’s duration in real-time seconds, into comboTimer and subtracts unscaled frame time until it resets comboMult to 1. comboTimer is the remaining window in real-time seconds; unscaled frame time is the real time between frame steps, unaffected by slow motion. comboMult is the unitless factor multiplying eligible kill points.

If a handle is already stored when another enemy dies, the death handler stops it and increases comboMult before starting a fresh countdown. StopAndResetKillCombo stops this saved handle when present but does not set it to null. A retained handle therefore does not prove that the window is still active.
Replacing the handle or assigning null does not stop an existing coroutine. Use the reset operation for its intended stop and label updates; it keeps previously awarded score.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.killScore
member.summary: Cached profile contribution to the most recent eligible enemy-death score, before combo multiplication.

remarks.para: The non-objective enemy-death handler overwrites this with that enemy profile’s deathMult, its unitless profile multiplier for death points, multiplied by 10. It then adds the enemy’s accumulated score contribution to killScore and multiplies the sum by comboMult, the unitless kill-combo multiplier, before adding it to the total score.

For example, deathMult of 4 produces killScore of 40 points. If the other contribution is 20 points and comboMult is 2, that kill adds (40 + 20) × 2 = 120 points. This is an illustration, not a default enemy profile.

Changing this field is not a way to configure every future kill: the next eligible death overwrites it before using it. Configure the enemy profile’s deathMult when that profile contribution is what you intend to change. Objective deaths use their separate handling path.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.kingSpawner
member.summary: Optional dedicated ProfileSpawner connected to base NPC registration and used to request the PROTECT king.

remarks.para: NPC means non-player character, a character controlled by the game. When the arena controller is enabled, a valid kingSpawner is connected to BaseGameController.RegisterNPCBase through its NPC-spawn notification. Disabling the controller removes that connection. Registration records the spawned NPC, its team and death callbacks, routines called to report actions such as its death.

SpawnKing requests StaticProfiles.friendlyProfileList[1] through this spawner as a friendly and marks that shared enemy profile as a king. The controller then calls ARENA_RingTheBell immediately, without waiting for the spawn to finish. PROTECT setup schedules the king request after 5 real-time seconds.

Assign it before enabling the controller. Replacing the reference while enabled does not reconnect the existing notification. SpawnKing requires the spawner and the second static friendly profile to exist; it does not fall back to a random normal spawner.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.lastPlayerCheck
member.summary: Game-time timestamp in seconds used to schedule the next player-position sample.

remarks.para: StartPlayerDist initializes it from Time.time, Unity’s elapsed game time, and CoPlayerDist replaces it when a sample is taken. A new sample is taken only while a wave is ongoing and current game time is greater than lastPlayerCheck plus playerDistTick, the requested sampling interval in game-time seconds.

For example, timestamp 10 and interval 0.5 make the next sample eligible after game time passes 10.5. Slow motion stretches that interval in real time. This is a game-clock reading, not a wall-clock date or a timer of how far the player moved. Editing it changes when the running sampler can next take a sample, not the player’s position.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.lastPlayerPos
member.summary: Previous playerProxy world-position sample used to measure movement between sampling steps.

remarks.para: playerProxy, the component representing the tracked player, supplies the world position. A Vector3 stores its X, Y and Z coordinates. StartPlayerDist initializes this Vector3 from playerProxy’s world position. CoPlayerDist compares the new world-position sample with it, adds dx² + dy² + dz² to totalPlayerDist, and then replaces lastPlayerPos with the new sample. dx, dy and dz are changes along the three world-coordinate axes; the accumulated result uses squared world units.

For example, a change of 2 world units along X with no Y or Z change adds 4 squared world units. This is sampled displacement, not the full path walked between the samples. Changing lastPlayerPos does not teleport the player, but can change the next movement-score increment and the launcher’s low-movement comparison.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.launcher
member.summary: Optional arena launcher that can fire enemy capsules and shoot at a player who has moved too little between samples.

remarks.para: SpawnHoiPoi passes an enemy profile and this arena controller to its LaunchCapsuleEnemy operation. The launcher requests a capsule at its turret’s world position; its spawn callback, a routine called when the object is available, starts the capsule’s arena launch sequence. It is not the player’s match-selection handset.

StartNextWave starts player-position tracking when the launcher is assigned. While a wave is ongoing, the tracker requests LaunchProjectile when the player’s world Y position is above 3 world units and the squared sample displacement is below thresh squared. thresh is a distance in world units; the comparison measures movement since the previous sample, not distance from the turret.

A projectile request is not a guaranteed shot: the launcher checks aiming directions and raycasts. A raycast checks along a line for the first collider, a physical collision shape, that it hits. The launcher only requests the shot when the first hit is on its required player layer. Assigning or clearing this reference does not itself start or stop the saved playerDistRoutine; wave-start setup and the running sequence handle those actions.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.loopingMusicClips
member.summary: Music choices queued to loop when StartNextWave begins an odd-numbered wave.

remarks.para: With a nonempty array, waves 1, 3, 5 and so on select a clip, store its chosen array index in currClip and cue it through Audio2dManager using musicVol, a unitless playback-volume level. The cue requests nominal 5-second fades and enables looping. The new clip’s fade has a minimum rate, so actual elapsed fade time also depends on the target volume and frame steps. Even-numbered waves do not make this music-selection request.

The selection passes 0 and array length minus 1 to Unity’s integer Random.Range, whose upper bound is excluded. With several entries, the last entry is therefore not selected by this path. For example, a three-clip array chooses index 0 or 1, not 2. This differs from the array helper used for round-start sounds, which can select every entry.

EndOfMode requests a 5-second music stop when this array is nonempty. The clips use the shared music manager, so assigning the array is not itself a playback command, and the manager can reuse an already playing clip rather than restart it. Keep the array assigned for the wave-start and end-of-mode paths; those paths read its length.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.lootSpawner
member.summary: Arena loot producer used to request a wave’s items and remove its tracked spawned weapons.

remarks.para: SpawnLoot skips a request when arenaState is QUIT. Otherwise it uses this component, looking for a GenGameControl_Spawner in the controller’s children and caching it here if the current reference is missing. It passes currentWave, the cached wave profile, to SpawnWaveLoot. The bell-start path also uses this lookup and request.

The loot producer chooses its ordinary or WEAPON-mode path from its configuration and the supplied profile. A request can continue over later frames; it is not a promise that all items already exist when SpawnLoot returns. Change the wave’s loot configuration to change its rewards rather than treating this reference as the reward list.

DespawnLootWeapons forwards its force-despawn choice to this spawner when it exists. Normal cleanup leaves held/attached tracked weapons in place, while forced cleanup can detach and despawn them. EndOfMode also reads this spawner’s granted-ammunition tallies for QUIT score bookkeeping. Replacing the reference does not transfer the old spawner’s tracked objects or counts.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.maxConcurrentLimit
member.summary: Enemy-count limit supplied when arena difficulty changes or custom profiles rebuild a wave’s simultaneous-enemy setting.

remarks.para: Difficulty growth only applies a proposed increase to a wave’s maxConcurrent setting when the new count is at or below this limit. It does not reduce a wave that already exceeds the limit. For example, a limit of 6 accepts a proposed increase from 5 to 6 and rejects one from 6 to 7.

UpdateProfileEnemyCount stores its requested count here. Its fixed-count path copies the assigned group and writes that count into each wave’s maxConcurrent setting. Its other path records custom count-growth settings in the copied group. This is profile preparation, not a command to despawn excess live enemies.

The ordinary enemy producer actually compares activeEnemyCount, the number of registered living enemies, with currentWave.maxConcurrent. Changing this controller field alone does not change that already cached wave setting or impose a new global cap. The objective-start producer also uses the wave setting for its initial batch.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.modeEnd
member.summary: No-argument event fired by EndOfMode after resetting the round and wave numbers, before the remaining end-of-mode cleanup.

remarks.para: A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action. Attach callbacks here to react when the controller reaches this stage of ending a mode, including win, failure and quit cleanup. The optional modeWin event runs earlier when its own condition is met.

Friendly proxies are the stored targets enemies can choose. NPC means non-player character; despawn means remove from active play. arenaTimerValue is the arena timer in game-time seconds, advancing with the scaled game clock rather than real time. Before this event, EndOfMode resets the friendly-proxy list, clears the despawned-NPC list, clears totalEnemiesKilled and sets currRoundIndex and currWaveIndex to 1. After the event it resets arenaTimerValue, refreshes displays, clears isPlayerReady and sets arenaState to WAITING, then performs the remaining ammunition, music, geometry and health handling.

Listeners therefore see round and wave already reset, but readiness, arena state and the stored timer still at their earlier values. This event is a cleanup-stage notification, not proof that every cleanup action is complete. It is the UltEvent field actually invoked by the checked Arena routines; onModeEnd is a separate UnityEvent field.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.modeQuit
member.summary: No-argument quit notification fired by ARENA_QuitChallenge while the arena is still ACTIVE.

remarks.para: ARENA_QuitChallenge returns unless arenaState is ACTIVE. On an accepted quit it first requests playerEnterClip as a 2D sound, invokes this event, enables weapon spawning when its spawner is present, then changes arenaState to QUIT and starts wave-reset cleanup.

A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action. Callbacks attached here observe the state before it changes to QUIT; this event does not mean the non-player characters (NPCs), timer, readiness or music have already been cleaned up. EndOfMode and its modeEnd notification happen later through the reset sequence.
This is the UltEvent field invoked by the quit path. The separately stored onModeQuit UnityEvent does not receive this invocation.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.modeWin
member.summary: No-argument event fired by EndOfMode after score and completion updates when its success condition is met.

remarks.para: The condition is broader than arenaState being WIN: the state must not be FAILED, and either the assigned group must be SURVIVAL or the state must not be QUIT. Consequently, quitting SURVIVAL can invoke this event, while quitting another mode skips it. It is not a safe standalone test that the controller has recorded WIN.

EndOfMode calls CalculatePlayerScore and UpdateChallengeCompletion before this event. Completion updates set supported difficulty flags and then invoke the static OnSaveReady notification before modeWin. A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action; listeners here see those earlier updates, while the round/wave reset, modeEnd event, readiness clear and WAITING state change happen afterward.
No state argument is supplied. Read arenaState and the assigned mode if a listener needs to distinguish these outcomes. The invoked field is this UltEvent; onModeWin is a separate UnityEvent.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.musicVol
member.summary: Unitless volume level passed to the shared music manager when this arena cues a selected looping clip.

remarks.para: An AudioSource is the Unity component that plays a sound. Its volume is unitless: 0 is silent and 1 is the normal full level. For example, 0.5 requests half that volume setting; it is not a guarantee of half the perceived loudness. StartNextWave reads this field when a nonempty loopingMusicClips array selects music on an odd-numbered wave.

The cue requests nominal 5-second fades and looping. A new clip’s fade advances by at least 0.04 unitless volume units per real-time second, so a target below 0.2 can be reached sooner; frame steps determine the actual completion time. For example, a target of 0.1 from zero takes about 2.5 seconds before frame rounding. The music manager can keep an already playing identical clip, adjust its volume, or fade in a different clip. Its volume adjustment uses unscaled frame time, the real-time seconds between frame steps, so slow motion does not stretch that fade in the same way as a game-time countdown.

Changing musicVol does not immediately update an existing AudioSource: another cue must read the new value. Supply a sensible 0-to-1 volume yourself; the checked consumers do not establish one consistent runtime clamp for every music-cue branch. This is the music level, separate from the entry, round and wave sound-effect requests.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.nextWaveExists
member.summary: Cached continuation result used by the end-of-wave sequence to decide whether to request next-wave loot.

remarks.para: CoEndOfWave is a coroutine, a sequence that continues over frames. It first clears this flag. Only in WEAPON mode it removes the player inventory’s weapons and requests forced tracked-loot cleanup, which can detach held tracked weapons, before the initial configured wait of 1 game-time second. Coroutine frame resumption determines when work continues after that wait. It then calls CheckProfileForNextWave and stores that routine’s returned result here before starting wave-reset cleanup.

A true result can mean another wave in the current round, a move into the next round, or a newly created continuation for an unlimited profile. A false result means that checked path did not continue, such as finishing a limited profile. This is a result of that progression call, not a permanent statement about the profile asset.

A true result leads to a next-wave loot request in either WEAPON or another mode. WEAPON mode adds the extra configured 2-game-second wait before that request; all waits use scaled game time, so slow motion stretches them in real time. Changing the field before that read can alter the loot request, but does not itself advance round/wave numbers, start enemies, or create the next wave. A later end-of-wave sequence overwrites it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.onModeEnd
member.summary: Separate UnityEvent field; the checked Arena flow invokes modeEnd for this notification.

remarks.para: The complete checked Arena_GameController methods and its sequences that continue over frames do not invoke this UnityEvent. The notification in EndOfMode uses the distinct modeEnd UltEvent field. Both event types store configurable actions, but adding an action to this field does not also add it to modeEnd.

Attach actions to modeEnd when you want the controller’s verified notification. A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action; this UnityEvent can still run if other code explicitly invokes it. Assigning or invoking it does not by itself perform the arena’s state transition. This finding is limited to the checked Arena routines, not a claim that no external scene or mod can use the field.
