member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.playerDistRoutine
member.summary: Saved handle for the coroutine that samples player movement and can request launcher shots.

remarks.para: A coroutine is a sequence that continues over frames. StartPlayerDist stops the handle already stored here, initializes the previous world-position sample and game-time timestamp, clears totalPlayerDist and starts a new CoPlayerDist sequence. StartNextWave calls that setup when launcher is assigned.

playerProxy is the component representing the tracked player. The sequence samples playerProxy’s world position at the playerDistTick interval, the requested time between samples in game-time seconds, while isWaveOngoing is true. It adds squared sample displacement to totalPlayerDist and can request a launcher projectile when squared sample displacement is strictly below thresh². Written as dx² + dy² + dz², dx, dy and dz are the changes between successive samples in world X, Y and Z coordinates, so both sides have squared-world-unit quantities; a negative thresh acts like its positive magnitude. The separate height gate requires world Y above 3 world units. The displacement is between samples, not total path length or distance from the launcher.

The handle can remain stored after the sequence ends, so non-null does not prove it is running. Assigning null or replacing the reference does not stop an existing sequence. Restarting through StartPlayerDist also clears the accumulated movement value, which affects later score calculation.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.playerDistTick
member.summary: Requested game-time interval, in seconds, between samples of the player’s world position.

remarks.para: CoPlayerDist is a coroutine, a sequence that continues over frames. While a wave is ongoing it samples only when Time.time, Unity’s game clock in seconds, is greater than lastPlayerCheck plus this interval. For example, an interval of 0.5 with lastPlayerCheck of 10 makes a sample eligible after game time passes 10.5.

Sampling happens on frame steps, so the actual interval can be longer than the requested value. Slow motion makes the same game-time interval last longer in real time. Changing this value affects subsequent checks in the running sampler; it does not restart the sampler or clear the previous position.

This interval affects both the accumulated squared-displacement score and the launcher’s comparison of movement between samples. It is not a speed threshold. Zero or negative values are not clamped by the checked sampler and can make samples eligible much more often; they do not create additional steps inside a single frame.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.playerEnter
member.summary: No-argument entry event fired at the start of each ARENA_PlayerEnter call that passes the readiness gate.

remarks.para: The method returns without this event when isPlayerReady is false. Otherwise it invokes playerEnter before the entry sound, trigger-mode countdown or readyUpBell notification, ammunition snapshot, cached profile setup and difficulty effects. A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action; its listeners here see readiness already true but the remaining entry setup has not yet happened.

This is a controller entry action, not a fresh physical-overlap measurement. Code can call ARENA_PlayerEnter directly, and repeated eligible calls can invoke the event and repeat setup again. No player, position or trigger argument is passed.

Use this UltEvent for actions that must run at that early entry stage. The separate onPlayerEnter UnityEvent is not invoked by the checked entry method. This event does not mean enemy spawning has already started.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.playerEnterClip
member.summary: 2D sound requested on accepted arena entry and at the start of an ACTIVE-mode quit.

remarks.para: ARENA_PlayerEnter requests this clip after invoking playerEnter and before its countdown/bell handling and remaining setup. Entry requires isPlayerReady to be true; a rejected entry does not request the sound.

ARENA_QuitChallenge also requests this same clip when the arena is ACTIVE, before modeQuit and before changing the state to QUIT. Changing the clip therefore changes both those sound requests, even if its name suggests only entry.

The request goes to the shared 2D audio manager rather than using the player’s or an NPC’s world position. It does not start the match by itself, and changing the reference does not replace a sound already playing.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.playerReady
member.summary: No-argument ready-transition event fired after isPlayerReady changes from false to true in the ready setup paths.

remarks.para: ARENA_StartMatch returns if isPlayerReady is already true. Otherwise it sets the flag true, invokes this event and then performs geometry and optional weapon-spawning setup. The custom-challenge selection path likewise sets true before this event and then toggles the chosen geometry.

A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action. Listeners therefore see the ready flag already true, while the later setup is still pending. Some session and objective paths set the flag directly before entry without invoking playerReady, so this event is not a notification for every possible assignment to isPlayerReady.

Attach ready-transition actions to this UltEvent. The separately stored onPlayerReady UnityEvent is not invoked by these checked paths. No player or flag argument is supplied, and the notification does not by itself mean a wave or countdown has already begun.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.projectilesShot
member.summary: Counter increased by global RigidbodyProjectile shot notifications while the arena controller is enabled, used for an extra score contribution.

remarks.para: RigidbodyProjectile is the physics-projectile component. OnEnable connects ProjectileShot to RigidbodyProjectile.OnProjectileShot, and OnDisable removes that connection. A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action; this callback simply adds 1 without checking the shooter, projectile owner or arenaState. It can therefore count notifications while the arena is waiting as well as during combat.

CalculatePlayerScore adds 1500 points per counted notification when the count is positive, before applying the unitless difficulty multiplier: 1 for EASY, 2 for MEDIUM, 3 for HARD, 4 for HARDER or 5 for HARDEST. For example, 2 counted notifications contribute 3000 points to that part of the calculation. These are notifications received, not a proven count of only the player’s weapon shots or launcher shots.

After a successful score calculation finishes reporting the result, it clears this counter. Paths that skip scoring do not get that reset from the calculation; new shot notifications can increase it again. Manually replacing its value changes a later score calculation, not projectiles already in the scene.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.randToggleObjs
member.summary: Candidate scene objects for TestToggle and RandomToggle to enable or disable.

remarks.para: TestToggle disables every object in the array, then chooses one random index and enables that object if it is valid. With three valid entries, this leaves one of the three active. Supply a nonempty array with valid objects for that operation.

RandomToggle instead chooses only one index and sets that object to the supplied active state. It does not first disable the other entries, so several candidates can remain active. A GameObject is a scene object that holds components. Making it inactive disables the object’s behavior and collision participation as well as its display; a renderer only draws it. These operations change GameObject activation, not just a renderer’s visibility.

Editing this array does not immediately toggle anything; the operation must be called. The array itself supplies no schedule or arena-state condition for those calls. An empty array cannot provide a valid selected index, and TestToggle’s initial disable pass requires each object reference.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.readyUpBell
member.summary: No-argument event requesting the bell-ready stage during ON_TRIGGER_BELL entry, except in PROTECT mode.

remarks.para: After playerEnter and the entry sound, ARENA_PlayerEnter invokes this event when arenaStartMode is ON_TRIGGER_BELL and the assigned group is not PROTECT. It runs before the entry ammunition snapshot and cached-profile setup. isPlayerReady must already be true for entry to reach this stage.

A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action. This event gives configured callbacks a place to present or enable the ready bell; the controller does not itself identify a physical bell through this field. Invoking the event does not change isRung or start the countdown.

ringBell is the later notification from ARENA_RingTheBell after that method accepts a ring and sets isRung true. Repeated eligible entry calls can invoke readyUpBell again; there is no one-time latch in this event path.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.ringBell
member.summary: No-argument event fired after the controller accepts a bell action and sets isRung true.

remarks.para: ARENA_RingTheBell acts only when arenaStartMode is ON_TRIGGER_BELL and isRung is false. It sets isRung true before invoking this event, then starts a countdown using arenaStartDelay, the configured delay in game-time seconds. Immediately after starting that countdown it requests current-wave loot if the arena is not QUIT and a valid loot spawner is found. That QUIT check occurs after the event and countdown have already been started.

A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action. Listeners see the bell already latched and run before the new countdown starts. Another call is suppressed until ARENA_ResetTheBell or another setup path clears isRung.

This event reports the controller’s accepted action; it does not verify that a physical bell moved or that a bell sound finished playing. It is distinct from the preparatory readyUpBell event and the separate onRingBell UnityEvent. Calling the event manually runs its configured actions without changing the latch or scheduling the countdown.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.round
member.summary: Current one-based round number stored by the controller, including the upcoming round during progression.

remarks.para: This read-only property returns currRoundIndex directly: round 1 corresponds to the first entry in the assigned group’s roundProfileList list. StartNextWave uses round minus 1 to look up the profile. For example, round 3 selects list index 2. It is not a zero-based index or a count of completed rounds.

EndOfRound increments the stored number and resets currWaveIndex to 1 before invoking roundEnd, so a listener to that event already sees the next round number. EndOfMode resets it to 1 before modeEnd. ARENA_ChallengeResume can also set it to its requested round.

The value can refer to an upcoming round while a countdown is running, rather than a currently active wave. This getter does not check bounds, refresh cached profiles or prove that arenaState is ACTIVE.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.roundBegin
member.summary: No-argument event fired by StartNextWave when the selected wave is the round’s first wave.

remarks.para: StartNextWave requires arenaState to be ACTIVE and resolves currentRound and currentWave from the stored one-based numbers first. If currWaveIndex is 1 it invokes roundBegin before requesting a roundStartClips sound, refreshing the display, setting isWaveOngoing true and invoking waveBegin.

A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action. Callbacks here can read the newly cached profiles, but the wave-start flag has not yet been set by this call and the new timer/enemy producers are started later. The event supplies no round number argument; read round or currRoundIndex if needed.

This test is on the selected wave number, not a separate once-per-round latch. Calling StartNextWave again for wave 1 can repeat the notification. onRoundBegin is the distinct UnityEvent field, not the event invoked here.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.roundEnd
member.summary: No-argument event fired after EndOfRound advances the round number and resets the wave number.

remarks.para: EndOfRound first adds 1 to currRoundIndex and sets currWaveIndex to 1, then invokes this event. A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action; its listeners already observe the next round number, not the round that just finished. For example, ending round 2 makes the event see round 3 and wave 1.

After the event the method requests normal tracked-weapon cleanup. It removes loose tracked weapons from active play and leaves weapons still attached to a hand or body in place. The method then asks the optional geometry manager to advance and toggle geometry. It does not itself request roundEndClips; that sound is requested by the separate wave-profile progression check.

No completed-round argument is supplied. The event does not guarantee that another playable round exists, since progression decides between configured continuation, an unlimited profile’s generated continuation and finishing a limited profile. The separate onRoundEnd UnityEvent is not invoked by this method.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.roundEndClips
member.summary: 2D sound choices requested when progression passes a round’s last wave; the first clip is also used by PassEscapeMode.

remarks.para: CheckProfileForNextWave increments currWaveIndex and, when it passes the current round’s wave count, requests a sound from this array. The sound request occurs before the routine decides whether to advance or generate a continuation or finish the limited profile; only branches that call EndOfRound also invoke roundEnd. The audio-array helper randomly chooses from all entries when the array is nonempty.

PassEscapeMode instead requests index 0 only, when an entry exists, and then ends the base session. Adding more clips changes the round-progression choices but not that escape-completion selection. These are sound requests; they do not themselves mark a round finished or schedule the next wave.

The requests use 2D audio rather than a position attached to a non-player character (NPC) or bell. Keep the array assigned for these checked paths; an empty array produces no selection, and changing it does not replace a sound already playing.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.roundProfileGroupList
member.summary: Ordered challenge/profile choices selected by a nonnegative ARENA_ChallengeSelect index and traversed by objective profile progression.

remarks.para: Index 0 selects the first RoundProfileGroup, index 1 the second, and so on. Selecting one stores it as assignedRoundProfile, refreshes the arena display and clears the score. A negative selection uses survivalProfile instead, so survival is not required to be an entry in this list.

Objective progression increments currProfile, the zero-based challenge selection number, and selects that group entry. InitObjectiveMode’s index 0 refers to allNPCObjectives, the list of objective components, not this challenge list; InitObjectiveContainer only runs its special setup when currProfile is 1 and does not itself select a challenge. ObjectiveBlueKeyedTest is the operation that explicitly selects challenge index 1, which requires a second group entry. Order matters to these operations; the list is not a live collection of currently spawned rounds.

Changing the list does not automatically replace an already assigned group or its cached currentRound/currentWave. Use the selection/progression operation for its setup. Nonnegative selection checks the upper bound, while the objective paths need the referenced entries and profile components to exist.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.roundStartClips
member.summary: 2D sound choices requested when StartNextWave begins wave 1 of a round.

remarks.para: After resolving the selected profiles, StartNextWave invokes roundBegin and then passes this array to the audio helper. With a nonempty array, the helper chooses a random index across all its entries. For example, a three-clip array can select index 0, 1 or 2.

This request occurs before the display refresh, the isWaveOngoing flag is set true and waveBegin fires. Later waves use waveStartClip instead. Repeating StartNextWave while currWaveIndex is 1 can request another round-start sound; the array itself does not enforce one playback per round.

These are nonpositional sound effects, separate from loopingMusicClips background music. Keep the array assigned; an empty array gives the helper no sound to choose. Editing the array affects later requests, not a sound already playing.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.scoreText
member.summary: Optional TextMeshPro label written when the arena’s score-update paths refresh the displayed point total.

remarks.para: Challenge selection and resume clear score and write the new value here when the label exists. Eligible enemy deaths write the total after awarding their points, and CalculatePlayerScore writes it after applying its movement, shot, difficulty, ammunition and damage arithmetic.

This is a display target, not the score value itself. ClearScore only changes the stored score to zero; it does not refresh this label. Likewise, editing the score or replacing scoreText does not make the text continually follow the new value. A score-writing path must run afterward.

UpdateArenaDisplay refreshes mode, difficulty, round and wave labels rather than this score label. An unassigned scoreText skips the checked score-text writes, so the score calculation can still proceed without this particular HUD element.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.spawnerHash
member.summary: Set used to prevent AddZoneSpawners from adding the same ProfileSpawner repeatedly to the arena’s spawn-choice list.

remarks.para: For each queued item, AddZoneSpawners first checks spawnerHash. If the set contains that item, it removes the item from both spawnerHash and profileSpawnerList; after processing the queue it clears removeSpawnerList. It next adds each incoming spawner only when it is not already in spawnerHash. A set stores distinct entries, so the same reference normally gets only one zone-add registration.

RemovedZoneSpawners queues removals; it does not immediately remove entries from this set. The next AddZoneSpawners call processes them. ClearSpawnerList and ARENA_SwapSpawnerList change profileSpawnerList without synchronizing this set, so its contents are not a guaranteed snapshot of every current spawn choice.

For example, clearing only profileSpawnerList can leave a spawner in this set, making a later zone-add skip it. Keep the two collections consistent if modifying them directly. NPC means non-player character. Editing spawnerHash alone does not spawn an NPC or change an NPC’s registration/death subscriptions.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.sublimationDict
member.summary: NPC records keyed by their GameObject so despawn cleanup can restore gravity after death-triggered sublimation.

remarks.para: NPC means non-player character. A GameObject is the scene object holding its components; the puppet is the character’s connected physics bodies, which simulate motion. An impulse is a one-time push. Despawn means removal from active play. When the assigned group enables sublimateOnDeath, the registered-death handler adds the dying NPC’s GameObject and NPC_Data record here and calls Sublimate. That operation disables gravity on its puppet’s physics bodies and applies an upward impulse to a selected body. This can apply to enemies or friendly NPCs; it is not only a friendly post-mode list.

OnDespawn looks up the object in this dictionary, restores gravity on the stored puppet’s physics bodies and removes the entry. An NPC_Data record carries the brain and physical-character references needed for that cleanup; the GameObject key identifies which spawned character is being removed.

Changing the dictionary does not itself apply or reverse the floating effect. Removing a record prematurely can prevent this despawn path from finding it and restoring gravity. The separate CoFriendlySublimation sequence works from the friendly-data list, so this dictionary is not its whole work list.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.survivalProfile
member.summary: RoundProfileGroup assigned by negative challenge selection or ordinary survival resume.

remarks.para: ARENA_ChallengeSelect uses this reference whenever its selection index is negative, rather than selecting an entry from roundProfileGroupList. ARENA_ChallengeResume also selects it when its projectedProfile argument is false and sets currRoundIndex to the requested round number.

The profile contains the actual rounds, waves, enemy choices and progression settings. Assigning it here does not automatically make its rounds unlimited: the first RoundProfile’s roundMode chooses LIMITED, which finishes, or UNLIMITED, which can generate a continuation after configured rounds run out.

Changing the reference affects a later selection or ordinary resume; it does not replace an already assignedRoundProfile or start a run immediately. survivalProfileProjected is the alternate reference chosen when the resume call’s projectedProfile argument is true.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.survivalProfileProjected
member.summary: Alternate RoundProfileGroup selected when ARENA_ChallengeResume is called with projectedProfile set to true.

remarks.para: That resume path assigns this group as assignedRoundProfile, stores the requested one-based round number, refreshes the display, resets friendly-proxy bookkeeping, clears the score and sets the arena ACTIVE. It selects an existing group reference; the method does not calculate or fill a projected profile for you.

For example, requesting round 4 requires the selected group to provide the fourth round for later profile lookup. The stored round is not clamped to the group’s count by the resume method. Prepare the group and requested round before resuming.
With projectedProfile false, resume uses survivalProfile instead. Changing this reference does not update a run already using a group, clear its spawned objects or start the next wave on its own.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.thresh
member.summary: Distance threshold, in world units, below which a movement sample can cause the arena launcher to request a shot.

remarks.para: CoPlayerDist is a coroutine, a sequence that continues over frames. playerProxy is the component representing the tracked player. At each eligible sample it compares dx² + dy² + dz² with thresh². dx, dy and dz are changes in playerProxy’s world-position coordinates since the previous sample; both sides of the comparison are squared world units. A shot is requested only when displacement is strictly below the threshold and the player’s current world Y coordinate is above 3 world units, meaning 3 world units above the coordinate origin.

For example, thresh of 2 makes the comparison against 4 squared world units. Moving 1 world unit between samples qualifies, moving exactly 2 does not, and the separate height condition must still pass. A raycast checks along a line for a physical collision shape. The launcher can reject the shot request if its aiming/raycast tests do not find the required player hit.

playerDistTick sets the sample interval in game-time seconds, so changing that interval also changes how much movement this threshold sees. thresh is not a speed, distance from the launcher or threshold for updating the score. The native comparison squares it without a range clamp: a negative value behaves like its positive magnitude, and zero cannot pass the strict less-than test for a nonnegative squared displacement.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.timeBender
member.summary: Optional slow-motion limiter enabled on arena entry for HARDER and HARDEST difficulty.

remarks.para: ARENA_PlayerEnter calls ToggleSlowLimits(true) for those two difficulties when this component exists. EndOfMode later calls ToggleSlowLimits(false). ToggleSlowLimits sets the flag used by later slow-motion notifications; switching it off does not cancel a drain or regeneration already running. Assigning this reference does not itself change the game’s time scale.

The TimeBender listens to time-manager slow-motion notifications. Its callbacks, routines called to report that action, start a fuel-draining sequence during limited slow motion and a regeneration sequence afterward. Fuel means slowMoJuice, the remaining slow-motion budget. Real frame time is the elapsed seconds between frame steps, unaffected by slow motion. The slow-motion step is the unitless level supplied by TimeManager, separate from the fraction by which game time is slowed. The drain subtracts real frame time multiplied by that step: for example, step 2 over 0.1 real seconds spends 0.2 budget units. While slow motion is active, a remaining budget strictly below 0.5 can end slow motion through the time manager and temporarily prevent another use until regeneration restores availability. Drain and regeneration are coroutines, sequences that continue over frames; their continuing checks use slow-motion state and remaining budget rather than the limit flag.

ToggleSlowLimits also shows or hides the limiter’s visual object when its visual option is enabled. Entry on EASY, MEDIUM or HARD does not explicitly turn an already enabled limit off through this field. Changing the reference while a run is active does not apply the entry setting to the new component or clean up the old one.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.totalEnemyCount
member.summary: Enemy-producer progress count for the current wave, used as the next enemy-profile index and the ordinary wave’s spawn limit.

remarks.para: The ordinary spawn loop uses this value to select the next entry from currentWave.enemyProfilesList and proceeds only while it is below that list’s count. After its ordinary spawn request completes, or after it issues a launcher-capsule request, it increases the count. This does not guarantee that every counted request produced a live registered NPC.

The objective-start sequence also increases it after each request in its initial batch. Wave-reset cleanup later sets it to zero along with the wave’s kill and active-enemy counters. It is therefore not a total for the whole run, and it is separate from activeEnemyCount, the registered living-enemy count.

For example, with four ordinary enemy profiles and totalEnemyCount of 2, the next selection uses index 2, the third entry, before increasing the counter. Editing it can skip or repeat profile choices or stop further ordinary requests. Negative values are not made into a safe list index by the producer.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.totalHeadShots
member.summary: Counter of global SubBehaviourHealth headshot notifications received while this arena controller is enabled, used for bonus points.

remarks.para: OnEnable connects HEAD_SHOOTER to the static headshot notification and OnDisable removes that connection. A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action; this callback adds 1 with no shooter, victim or arenaState check and receives no arguments. It is not established as a player-only count.

CalculatePlayerScore adds 2000 points per counted notification when the value is positive, before applying the unitless difficulty factor: 1 for EASY, 2 for MEDIUM, 3 for HARD, 4 for HARDER or 5 for HARDEST. For example, 3 notifications contribute 6000 points to that part of the score. Editing this field changes the later calculation rather than making a headshot happen.

After a successful score calculation finishes reporting the result, it clears this counter. Paths that skip scoring do not get that reset from the calculation; new headshot notifications can increase it again. The counter follows notifications the enabled controller receives, not an independent search of every headshot in the game.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.totalPlayerDist
member.summary: Accumulated sum of squared player-position changes between samples, used for movement bonus points.

remarks.para: CoPlayerDist is a coroutine, a sequence that continues over frames. playerProxy is the component representing the tracked player. For each sample it adds dx² + dy² + dz², where dx, dy and dz are changes along the world axes since the previous playerProxy position sample. The stored unit is squared world units. This is not a normal distance in meters or the length of the full path walked.

For example, two separate 1-world-unit moves add 1 + 1 = 2, while one sampled 2-world-unit move adds 4. Movement that returns to the same position before the next sample can add zero. playerDistTick, the sampling interval in game-time seconds, therefore affects the accumulated value.

StartPlayerDist clears this value when it starts or restarts tracking; StartNextWave performs that restart when launcher is assigned. CalculatePlayerScore, when the value is positive, discards its fractional part and adds 100 points per remaining whole squared world unit before the unitless difficulty multiplier: 1 for EASY, 2 for MEDIUM, 3 for HARD, 4 for HARDER or 5 for HARDEST. For example, 3.9 contributes 300 points before that multiplier. A successful score calculation clears this value after reporting its result; starting or restarting movement tracking clears it too. Paths that skip scoring do not get that reset from the calculation.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.triggeredSpawnerList
member.summary: Ordered Arena_TriggeredSpawners groups from which ARENA_SwapSpawnerList copies a selected set of enemy spawn choices.

remarks.para: ARENA_SwapSpawnerList uses its zero-based index to read one group from this list, clears profileSpawnerList and copies that group’s spawners array entries into it. For example, index 1 chooses the second group. The group contains ProfileSpawner references, not the spawned NPCs themselves.

This is a selectable list of groups, not a live registry automatically filled whenever a zone fires. AddZoneSpawners and RemovedZoneSpawners use their own input arrays and bookkeeping. The swap does not synchronize spawnerHash, the set used by the zone-add path to prevent duplicates.

Prepare valid groups and an in-range selection before swapping. Changing this list does not automatically replace the current profileSpawnerList, invoke a zone trigger or reconnect NPC notifications; a swap call performs only its checked list replacement.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.wave
member.summary: Current one-based wave number stored by the controller, including a pending next wave during progression.

remarks.para: This read-only property returns currWaveIndex directly. Wave 1 selects the first wave in the current round; StartNextWave looks it up using wave minus 1. For example, wave 4 corresponds to list index 3. NPC means non-player character, a character controlled by the game. The getter does not calculate how many remain.

CheckProfileForNextWave increases currWaveIndex before checking whether another wave exists. EndOfRound resets it to 1 before roundEnd, and EndOfMode resets it to 1 before modeEnd. During a continuation countdown it can already identify the next wave while the previous wave’s cleanup is still running.

StartNextWave uses the stored number; it does not increment it. Reading this property does not validate the index, refresh currentWave or prove that combat is active. The stored number and cached profile can temporarily describe different progression stages.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.waveBegin
member.summary: No-argument event fired by StartNextWave after the display refresh and isWaveOngoing is set true.

remarks.para: StartNextWave requires arenaState to be ACTIVE, resolves the current round/wave profiles and requests the appropriate round-start or later-wave sound first. It refreshes the arena display, sets isWaveOngoing true and then invokes waveBegin. A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action; its listeners see the flag already true.

After the event, the method replaces the saved arena timer with the upward timer, performs its music and survival-difficulty handling, starts enemies and, when a launcher exists, restarts movement tracking. The notification therefore comes before those new producers are started, rather than proving the first NPC has appeared.

No wave-number argument is passed; use wave or currWaveIndex. Calling StartNextWave again can repeat the notification without advancing the number. The separate onWaveBegin UnityEvent is not invoked by this flow.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.waveEnd
member.summary: No-argument event fired at the beginning of the wave-reset coroutine, before its spawning and wave flags are cleared.

remarks.para: A coroutine is a sequence that continues over frames, and a callback is a routine called to perform or report an action. CoResetOnWaveCompleteOrFail invokes this event on its first step, then clears isSpawning, stops the saved enemy/friendly coroutines, requests cancellation through enemySpawnCTS, the source that tells the ordinary async loop to stop when it checks the request, clears isWaveOngoing and resets the kill combo.

Async work can finish later while its caller continues; the cancellation request does not mean the loop has already stopped. Listeners therefore can still see the previous isSpawning and isWaveOngoing values and active producer handles during the event. NPC means non-player character, a character controlled by the game. Despawn means remove from active play. NPC despawning, count resets and any later EndOfMode handling happen afterward; the notification does not mean those actions have finished.

The reset can be started by normal completion, failure, quit or manual code, so this event is not exclusively a victory signal. It supplies no wave number or outcome argument. The separately stored onWaveEnd UnityEvent is not invoked by the checked reset flow.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.waveEndClip
member.summary: 2D sound requested by the end-of-wave sequence after its initial one-game-second wait.

remarks.para: CoEndOfWave is a coroutine, a sequence that continues over frames. It clears nextWaveExists and, only in WEAPON mode, removes inventory weapons and requests forced tracked-loot cleanup, which can detach held tracked weapons. It then waits the configured 1 game-time second before requesting this clip; coroutine frame resumption determines the actual continuation time. It then handles HARDEST health restoration, checks wave/round progression, saves the continuation result and starts wave-reset cleanup.

The waveEnd event belongs to that later reset sequence, so this sound request occurs before that event when normal CoEndOfWave reaches the reset. A failure or quit path that starts reset directly does not request this clip through CoEndOfWave.

This is a shared 2D sound effect, not a sound attached to a non-player character (NPC) or a victory marker. Editing the reference affects later requests, not sounds already playing. roundEndClips may also be requested when the subsequent progression check passes the round’s last wave.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.waveStartClip
member.summary: 2D sound requested by StartNextWave for a round’s second and later waves.

remarks.para: When currWaveIndex is 1, StartNextWave uses roundStartClips instead. For any later selected wave it requests this clip after resolving the profiles and before refreshing the display, setting isWaveOngoing true and invoking waveBegin.

The method requires arenaState to be ACTIVE and starts the new timer and enemy producer after the event. This sound is a cue for the start sequence, not proof that the first enemy has spawned. Repeating StartNextWave for the same later wave can request the sound again.
The request uses shared 2D audio with no world-position source. Changing the reference does not start a wave or replace a sound already playing; it affects the next eligible request.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.weaponSpawner
member.summary: Scene weapon-selection spawner whose permission and tracked weapons the arena changes during ready, cancel and quit flows.

remarks.para: When ARENA_StartMatch makes the player ready in WEAPON or PROTECT mode, it disables this spawner’s weapon-selection requests and calls DespawnAllWeapons. The ready flag is set and playerReady fires before those actions. DespawnAllWeapons removes the spawner’s tracked spawned weapon objects; it is separate from the wave loot tracked by lootSpawner.

ARENA_QuitChallenge enables weapon spawning after modeQuit but before setting arenaState to QUIT. CancelCurrentChallenge also enables it. Enabling sets the spawner’s permission flag and reports the choice through its global IsSpawningAllowed notification; it does not itself create a weapon. OnWeaponSelected also requires room under that spawner’s weaponLimit before it can request the selected weapon or pack.

IsSpawningAllowed needs a registered listener, a routine that receives the chosen true/false permission. ToggleWeaponSpawning writes its permission flag before invoking that notification unconditionally. If no listener is registered, it throws after the permission changes. In StartMatch, readiness has already been set and playerReady has fired when this failure stops the later DespawnAllWeapons call. In quit, modeQuit has already fired, but the later QUIT-state write and reset sequence have not run. In cancel, it stops the later score reset and arena-state write. Earlier event actions can also throw or change state, so this ordering describes the path that reaches ToggleWeaponSpawning. Assign the scene’s configured WeaponSpawner before using these flows. StartMatch and quit skip their optional spawner work when the reference is missing, while CancelCurrentChallenge requires the reference. Replacing the field does not move old spawned weapons, copy the old spawner’s tracking or update the new spawner’s permission until a relevant operation runs.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_GameController.winModeClip
member.summary: 2D success sound requested by the controller’s WIN-state and victory-effect paths.

remarks.para: SetArenaState(WIN) writes arenaState first and then requests this clip. The end of a limited profile, ARENA_ObjectiveProfileCompleted and StopSpawningAndCureAll also set WIN before requesting it through their own paths. It is a shared 2D sound effect rather than a sound attached to an NPC’s world position.

WinStateFX requests this same clip without changing arenaState, completing a profile, awarding points or running modeWin. Calling that helper can therefore play the sound while the controller is in another state. Sound playback is not proof that the mode has been won or its cleanup completed.

modeWin is a separate event from EndOfMode’s conditional score/completion handling and does not directly play this clip in the checked body. Changing winModeClip affects future requests; it does not replace a sound already playing or alter the success conditions.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_SpawnCapsule.finalExpandRadius
member.summary: Target radius for the capsule’s expanding spherical physics shape, expressed in the collider’s local-space units.

remarks.para: During expansion the sequence writes radius = startRadius + (finalExpandRadius − startRadius) × progress. startRadius is the starting/reset radius in the same local-space units; progress is a unitless time fraction from 0 to 1 across a 0.5-game-time-second interval. For example, startRadius of 0.1 and finalExpandRadius of 1 produce radius 0.55 at progress 0.5. Collider-local radius is measured before object scaling. Game time follows the game’s clock, so slow motion makes the interval take longer in real time; updates happen on game frames. Object scaling affects the sphere’s world-space size; this field does not set the spawned enemy’s size.

The frame sequence stops when its stored progress is at least 0.95, disables the collider and restores startRadius. Depending on frame timing, it can reset before writing the exact target. This is the interpolation endpoint, not a permanently installed final collider radius.

The Inspector slider advertises 0.25 through 1.5. That editor range is not a runtime clamp on this field: the checked sequence clamps the time fraction, then interpolates the stored radius inputs. A target smaller than startRadius makes the interpolation shrink. Changing this value during growth affects the next radius calculation; it does not alter the separate world-origin bounds check.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_SpawnCapsule.maxDistFromCenter
member.summary: Distance limit, in world units from the world origin, used to decide whether the capsule’s later spawn can use its own location.

remarks.para: After the timed beep stage, the sequence checks x² + y² + z² against maxDistFromCenter². x, y and z are the capsule’s world-position coordinates relative to (0, 0, 0); both sides are squared world units. It includes height and does not use the arena controller’s Transform as the center. Equality passes the distance check.

There is a separate inclusive height requirement of world Y from 0 to 4. For example, a limit of 5 and position (3, 0, 4) pass both checks. Position (0, 5, 0) passes the distance check but fails the height check. These are illustrative positions, not arena layout settings.

This does not clamp launch velocity or keep the capsule inside that sphere. The position is checked once before collider growth, and the saved result chooses between success and fallback later. A failed check calls the arena’s normal-spawner fallback, which only requests an enemy while the arena is ACTIVE. Changing the field after the check does not recompute that saved result.

The code squares this input: a negative value has the same distance-test magnitude as its positive counterpart, and zero only admits the world origin for the distance test. The Inspector name does not make the reference point a movable scene center.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Arena_SpawnCapsule.startRadius
member.summary: Starting radius used by the growth interpolation and restored when the capsule disables its expanding collider.

remarks.para: This is the radius of expandCollider, a SphereCollider, Unity’s spherical physics shape. Its collider-local radius is measured before the object’s scaling is applied. Each growth frame writes startRadius + (finalExpandRadius − startRadius) × progress, where finalExpandRadius is the target radius in the same units and progress is a unitless fraction from 0 to 1 across the 0.5-game-time-second interval. Game time follows the game’s clock and slows during slow motion; the 0.5-second interval sets interpolation timing, with radius updates on game frames. Transform scale affects the corresponding world-space sphere size.

The sequence does not first assign this value when it enables the collider. It enables the existing shape, waits 0.1 game-time seconds and then starts interpolation. At the end of growth it disables the collider before writing startRadius back to the radius. Editing this field alone therefore does not immediately resize an idle collider or establish its radius during that initial enabled wait.

For example, startRadius 0.1 with finalExpandRadius 1 gives radius 0.55 halfway through the interpolation and restores 0.1 when the reset stage runs. The sequence reads the field during growth and reset rather than taking one immutable launch-time snapshot; a mid-sequence edit affects later writes. The end check is at stored progress 0.95 or above, so it need not write the exact target before resetting.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ArmFinale._armStage
member.summary: Selects the finale rule that Update runs, including waiting for a grip, handling release and clearing the player in the Void stage.

remarks.para: The stages are Preshow (0), Decent (1), Hold (2), Ascent (3), Dropped (4) and Void (5). Awake is the routine Unity calls to initialize this component and sets Preshow. Update runs once each rendered frame; Time.time is the scaled game clock in seconds, following changes to game speed. GongHit sets Decent before playing decent. ReadyForAscent sets Hold; Update enters Ascent only while the reported hand count is positive, then stops decent, plays ascent and changes the windmill drive.

Ascent records Time.time while hands remain attached. With no positive hand count, more than 0.5 game-time seconds since the last such timestamp changes it to Dropped. Dropped repeatedly requests seating of _lastRmToDetatch. ReadyForVoid sets Void, activates holeStopper and records the new timestamp; Void Update performs the timed seat and grip release checks.

Assigning this property changes the selected Update branch. It does not perform the entry actions of GongHit, ReadyForAscent or ReadyForVoid, initialize _timer, start a timeline or cancel the windmill coroutine, a sequence that continues over frames. For example, directly assigning Ascent skips the Hold-to-Ascent timeline and drive changes. Choose the stage-changing methods when those entry actions are needed.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ArmFinale._attachedHandCount
member.summary: Reported number of attached hands used to start ascent and decide when the arm should seat or detach the player.

remarks.para: OnEnable and OnDisable are the routines Unity calls when this component becomes enabled or disabled. A RigManager groups the objects representing the player’s body and controls. OnEnable subscribes to hostManager’s attach and detach callbacks, routines called to report a hand joining or leaving a managed grip. Each attach adds one. Each detach subtracts one before recording that hand’s RigManager in _lastRmToDetatch. This is a callback counter, not a fresh count of distinct hands or players each frame.

Hold starts ascent when the count is greater than zero. During Ascent, positive counts refresh _timer; zero or negative counts allow the half-second release timeout. During Void, a positive count allows ForceDetachAll after the one-second threshold.

There is no clamp to the two hands of one player and no reset in ArmFinale’s OnEnable or OnDisable. Repeated manual attachment reports or duplicate subscriptions can inflate it; unmatched detach reports can make it negative. Editing the number changes these tests but does not physically grab or release anything, and later callbacks continue adding or subtracting from that edited value.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ArmFinale._ceilingTiles
member.summary: Ordered tile bodies that startup turns into physics connections and maps to the tile-release indices.

remarks.para: BuildJoints, also executed by Unity’s Start callback when this component begins running, adds a MarrowJoint to every listed body and supplies _jointInfo. The resulting ConfigurableJoint is cached at the same index in _tileJoints. JointDestroyEvent(3), for example, changes the cached connection for the fourth listed tile; indices start at zero.

Populate this scene list before startup, with valid MarrowBody entries. Inactive or disabled bodies can defer their underlying joint creation, leaving null entries in ArmFinale’s cache. The constructor gives the list room for 16 entries initially, but that capacity is not a count or a limit on the list. The separate _tileJoints array has 16 slots unless replaced and is not enlarged by BuildJoints.

Editing the list after building does not rearrange, remove or recreate existing joints. The cached index relationship remains the one established during that build. Running BuildJoints again adds more MarrowJoint components rather than first cleaning up the old ones.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ArmFinale._jointInfo
member.summary: Settings supplied to each ceiling tile’s physics connection, controlling how it moves, resists movement and breaks.

remarks.para: BuildJoints passes this ConfigurableJointInfo object to every new MarrowJoint. Its settings include joint axes and anchors, permitted motion, limits, drive spring/damping strengths, break force/torque and collision options. Break force and break torque are thresholds for breaking under pushing/pulling or twisting; assigning them does not apply those forces. Anchors are the points where the connection attaches. A drive’s spring pulls the body toward its target; damping resists relative movement. MarrowJoint copies the settings into a ConfigurableJoint when the body is active and enabled and the underlying joint is built.

Assign valid settings before the setup pass; changing this reference alone does not immediately retune already-created ConfigurableJoints. This is a shared settings object, not a fresh copy for each tile: creation retains the supplied object and updates its startRotation from that tile’s initial world rotation because there is no connected tile body. That value can therefore be overwritten as successive tiles are prepared.

JointDestroyEvent later changes a chosen cached joint’s six motion settings to Locked and breakForce to zero directly. It does not edit this settings object. A template edit and a change to a live joint are different operations; avoid assuming that one automatically updates the other.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ArmFinale._lastRmToDetatch
member.summary: Player rig recorded by the most recent detach report and offered to the palm seat after all grips are released.

remarks.para: A RigManager groups the objects representing the player’s body and controls. Every OnHandDetached callback, a routine called to report a hand leaving a managed grip, subtracts from _attachedHandCount and then records that hand’s manager here. It does not wait for the last remaining hand to let go, and it is not restricted to a particular palm grip.

Update is Unity’s routine called once each rendered frame. During Ascent, a nonpositive hand count lasting more than 0.5 game-time seconds since the last positive-count Update changes the stage to Dropped. Dropped Update repeatedly sets palmSeat’s entry-position smoothing time to 0.75 seconds and calls IngressRig with this cached rig. This time controls gradual movement toward the seat; it does not promise that entry finishes in exactly 0.75 seconds. Seat ignores the entry request if it already has a rig, but an empty seat requires a valid supplied rig.

Editing this reference changes the rig supplied to later seating requests; it does not itself seat anyone or update the hand count. ArmFinale’s enable/disable handlers do not clear it. Upstream uses "detatch" in the member name.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ArmFinale._tileJoints
member.summary: Cached ceiling tile connections that JointDestroyEvent selects to lock all six motion settings and set a zero break-force threshold.

remarks.para: BuildJoints fills each slot with the ConfigurableJoint obtained for the _ceilingTiles entry at the same index. A ConfigurableJoint is a physics connection with movement limits and drive settings. This array is a cache of those connections, not the tile bodies themselves or a record that a tile has already broken.

The constructor creates 16 slots. The build pass does not resize the array, and inactive or disabled tile bodies can leave a slot null when their joint creation is deferred. JointDestroyEvent requires a valid index and a non-null cached joint; it does not silently skip missing entries.

Reordering _ceilingTiles after the build does not reorder this array. JointDestroyEvent changes the selected connection’s settings but does not clear its slot. Replacing a cached reference changes the object future JointDestroyEvent calls target; it does not create or move a tile. Repeated BuildJoints calls overwrite slots with newly added connections without removing the old components first.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ArmFinale._timer
member.summary: Saved scaled-game-time timestamp used for the ascent release timeout and the Void-stage release delays.

remarks.para: Update is Unity’s routine called once each rendered frame. It stores Time.time in seconds, not the number of seconds the current stage has lasted. During an Ascent Update with _attachedHandCount greater than zero, it is replaced by the current game time. Once the count is nonpositive, Time.time − _timer greater than 0.5 changes the stage to Dropped. The subtraction is elapsed game-time seconds since that last recorded positive-count Update.

ReadyForVoid sets the Void stage, activates holeStopper, then records a new Time.time here. Void Update requests palm-seat exit after elapsed time is greater than 0.75 seconds, subject to the seat Rigidbody check (a Rigidbody is Unity’s component for physics motion), and forces grips off after greater than one second while the count is positive. If both checks pass in one Update, the force-detach request is made first.

For example, an illustrative timestamp of 10 and current Time.time of 10.6 give 0.6 seconds elapsed: the ascent release threshold passes, while both Void thresholds remain false. Time.time follows Unity’s time scale, so these are game-time delays, not guaranteed wall-clock delays.

GongHit and ReadyForAscent do not reset this value. The Hold-to-Ascent transition also does not initialize it; the next positive-count Ascent Update does. If every grip is released before that Update, the timeout can use an older timestamp. Editing this value affects subsequent comparisons but does not immediately change the stage or start a timer routine.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ArmFinale.armMesh
member.summary: Skinned arm renderer whose offscreen updates are enabled for descent and disabled during the Void stage.

remarks.para: GongHit sets this renderer’s updateWhenOffscreen to true before setting Decent and playing the descent timeline. A skinned renderer draws a mesh shaped by animated bones; allowing offscreen updates lets that mesh keep updating even when it is outside the camera’s view.

Update is Unity’s routine called once each rendered frame. While Void is selected, every Update sets updateWhenOffscreen back to false. This restores the renderer’s normal offscreen-update restriction; it does not deactivate the arm GameObject or force the visible arm to disappear. The assignment is optional in both places. Changing this reference alone does not immediately apply either setting, and an earlier renderer is not restored when the reference is replaced.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ArmFinale.ascent
member.summary: Timeline director played when the waiting arm has a reported hand grip and begins its ascent.

remarks.para: Update is Unity’s routine called once each rendered frame. A PlayableDirector plays a prepared timeline of animation and other scene actions. The angular drive is the joint’s physics motor; its target angular velocity requests a rotation rate. ReadyForAscent first selects Hold. On an Update where _attachedHandCount is greater than zero, the component sets Ascent, stops decent, calls Play on this director, then sets the windmill joint’s target angular velocity and angular-X drive.

Assign the director before this transition; it is required on that path. Changing the reference does not automatically move the arm, select a stage or stop the previous director. The checked ArmFinale methods do not stop this director on the release timeout or in ReadyForVoid, so those state changes should not be described as automatically cancelling the ascent timeline. The actual animated tracks come from the assigned timeline.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ArmFinale.decent
member.summary: Timeline director played by GongHit and stopped when the waiting arm begins its ascent.

remarks.para: Update is Unity’s routine called once each rendered frame. A PlayableDirector plays a prepared timeline of animation and other scene actions. GongHit enables offscreen updates on an assigned armMesh, sets the stage to Decent, then calls Play on this director. Later, ReadyForAscent selects Hold, and a positive hand count on Update causes the stage to become Ascent before this director is stopped and ascent is played.

Assign this required reference before those calls. Editing it alone does not start or stop playback, and ReadyForAscent itself does not stop it while the arm is still waiting for a reported grip. Another GongHit has no stage guard and requests playback again. The name is spelled "decent" upstream even though it is the descent director.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ArmFinale.holeStopper
member.summary: Scene object activated when ReadyForVoid moves the arm into the Void stage.

remarks.para: ReadyForVoid sets _armStage to Void, activates this GameObject and only then stores the new game-time timestamp in _timer. SetActive affects the object and its components, so its enable callbacks, routines Unity calls when components become active, can run before that timestamp is replaced.

Assign this required object before calling ReadyForVoid. Its name suggests a stopper for the ceiling opening, but the checked method only activates the configured scene object; whether it blocks the opening physically depends on that object’s actual geometry, colliders and other components. A collider is the shape Unity uses for collision tests.

Changing the reference does not immediately activate it. ArmFinale’s checked methods do not deactivate this object when returning to another stage or on disable. A repeat ReadyForVoid call activates it again and resets the later release timing after that activation.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ArmFinale.hostManager
member.summary: Grip-report source used to count attachments, remember the latest detached player and force remaining grips off during the Void stage.

remarks.para: OnEnable and OnDisable are Unity routines called when this component becomes enabled or disabled. OnEnable connects ArmFinale’s hand-report callbacks, routines called when a hand attaches or detaches, to this manager’s onHandAttached and onHandDetached actions. Each report supplies the managed grip host and a Hand representing the reported hand. ArmFinale ignores the host argument. Attach reports increment _attachedHandCount. Detach reports decrement it before reading that supplied Hand.manager and storing its RigManager for later palm-seat entry. A RigManager groups the objects representing the player’s body and controls. Reports from this manager are not filtered to one chosen grip or one player in those callbacks.

Update is Unity’s routine called once each rendered frame. During Void Update, more than one game-time second after ReadyForVoid’s timestamp and a positive reported hand count cause ForceDetachAll to iterate the manager’s hosts and request detachment from each. The manager’s configured host collection determines which grips are affected.

Assign this required reference before enabling ArmFinale. OnDisable removes one matching registration from each of the current manager’s two actions; repeated manual OnEnable calls can add duplicates, which one OnDisable does not fully remove. These handlers do not reset the stored count or detached-player cache. Replacing the manager while enabled does not rewire subscriptions automatically, and disable uses the current reference rather than a saved original manager.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ArmFinale.palmSeat
member.summary: Player seat offered to the most recently detached rig after the ascent grip-release timeout, then exited during the Void stage.

remarks.para: Update is Unity’s routine called once each rendered frame. After Ascent has a nonpositive reported hand count for more than 0.5 game-time seconds since its last positive-count Update, the stage becomes Dropped. Each following Dropped Update sets this seat’s ingressSmoothTime, its entry-position smoothing time, to 0.75 seconds and calls IngressRig with _lastRmToDetatch. That smoothing time controls gradual movement toward the seat, not an exact duration until entry finishes. IngressRig registers the supplied player only when the seat is empty; an occupied seat ignores that entry request.

ReadyForVoid starts a new timestamp. Void Update requests EgressRig(true), an immediate seat exit, after more than 0.75 game-time seconds when this seat has an assigned seat Rigidbody. A Rigidbody is Unity’s component for physics motion. EgressRig itself checks for a registered player before performing the exit. The Rigidbody check is not a check that someone is seated.

Assign a configured Seat before those stages. The Dropped branch keeps requesting entry on later frames rather than advancing to another stage after one attempt, and it overwrites ingressSmoothTime each time. Replacing this reference does not automatically transfer an already-seated player. The cached detached rig must be valid when an empty seat is asked to register it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ArmFinale.windmillBlades
member.summary: Windmill Rigidbody whose current world rotation and angular velocity supply the later blade-alignment prediction.

remarks.para: A Rigidbody is Unity’s component for physics motion. WindmillProjectRotation reads this body rather than estimating motion from the arm timeline. Its world-space angular velocity is in radians per second; the vector’s length supplies angular speed and its direction supplies the spin axis. The method predicts orientation after secondsFromNow game-time seconds assuming that velocity remains constant.

For example, an illustrative angular speed of 1 radian per second over 2 seconds adds about 114.6 degrees to the prediction. The predicted directions select a target for windmillJoint, whose drive, its physics motor, is adjusted by a coroutine, a sequence continuing over frames. The routine does not directly assign a predicted rotation or angular velocity to this Rigidbody.

Assign the blade body and the matching windmillJoint before calling the projection method. Changing this reference affects later predictions, not an existing prediction already calculated by an earlier call. The checked ArmFinale paths do not apply a force or torque to this body directly; the visible response depends on the configured joint and physics.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ArmFinale.windmillJoint
member.summary: Physics connection whose angular drive spins the windmill during ascent and pulls it toward the later chosen blade orientation.

remarks.para: Update is Unity’s routine called once each rendered frame. The joint drive acts like a motor: its spring pulls toward the target angle, and damping resists relative rotational motion. When Hold sees a positive reported hand count, Update changes the stage to Ascent, stops decent and plays ascent before setting this joint’s targetAngularVelocity to (0.5, 0, 0), in radians per second around its drive axes. It also writes angular-X spring strength zero and damping 10000 while preserving that drive’s maximum-force value. A target velocity asks the joint to move; it is not a guaranteed instantaneous blade speed.

WindmillProjectRotation chooses one of four targetRotation values from the blades’ predicted world orientation and writes the target immediately. It starts a coroutine, a sequence that continues over frames, that increments the target angular velocity’s X component and ramps angular-X spring strength as 1000 × progress². progress is elapsed scaled game-time seconds divided by the supplied duration seconds, clamped from 0 to 1.

deltaTime is the current frame’s scaled game-time length in seconds; duration is the secondsFromNow argument supplied to WindmillProjectRotation, also in scaled game-time seconds. Each loop pass tests elapsed time before adding a whole frame’s deltaTime and yielding. The last increment can cross the configured duration; completion writes occur on the first resumed frame after accumulated deltaTime reaches or exceeds that duration. At completion the sequence sets angular-X spring strength to 1000000, damping to 100000 and targetAngularVelocity to zero. It does not restore the original spring or damping. During the ramp it writes a drive captured at sequence start, so other edits to that drive can be overwritten; repeated projection calls can run competing sequences.

Assign the joint before the ascent transition or projection method. Its axes, motion limits, connected bodies and other physics settings determine how the requested drive affects the windmill. Editing this reference alone does not start a stage or projection; an in-progress sequence reads the current reference for its later writes.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ArticulatedArmController.ArmStretchCurve
member.summary: Sets how much the upper arm and forearm lengthen at different requested wrist reaches.

remarks.para: The horizontal axis is shoulder-to-desired-wrist distance divided by the starting upper-arm plus forearm length. The desired wrist is targetHand's world position shifted by the current wrist-minus-hand displacement. With a 0.30-meter upper arm and a 0.25-meter forearm, input 1 means a 0.55-meter reach; input 0.8 means 0.44 meters.

The vertical axis multiplies both starting lengths. Output 1 keeps them unchanged; output 1.05 makes each 5% longer, giving a combined length of 0.5775 meters in that example. The curve is sampled only when input is strictly greater than stretchThreshold. The final reach also has a 4 mm margin and additional near/far reach limits.

CalibrateArmStretch, and Update after a stretch setting changes, request adjustments to the points currently at index 0, then index 1, including their tangents, which shape the bend between points. A custom curve can produce values beyond the setting named maxStretchFactor; the sampled multiplier is not clamped to that setting.

A key is a point on the curve; its index is its position in the list ordered by horizontal input, starting at 0. Calibration requests adjustments to the points currently at index 0, then index 1. Moving the first point can change the list order, so a custom curve's extra points are not guaranteed to keep their original values.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ArticulatedArmController.WristElbowIsNotCurve
member.summary: Maps the tracked wrist-twist angle to an angle considered when relaxing the arm's roll.

remarks.para: Both axes are in degrees. The horizontal input is the accumulated signed twist between the elbow and wrist orientations, carried forward by _handTwistLf. The calculation accounts for the previous twist and shifts values above 240 degrees down by 360, or below -240 degrees up by 360.

The vertical output is an angle, not a percentage of twist sent to a particular bone. A key at (90, 30) supplies 30 degrees when the tracked twist is 90 degrees. ElbowIsNot combines that output with posture-dependent limits and a world-up preference; WristRelax then smooths the resulting angle before rotating the shoulder. A 30-degree curve value therefore does not guarantee a 30-degree final shoulder rotation.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ArticulatedArmController._carpalLength
member.summary: Stores half the starting wrist-to-hand distance, in meters, for positioning the two small segments between wrist and hand.

remarks.para: Awake, a routine Unity calls when this component is first initialized, measures the world-space distance from wristLf to handLf and divides it by two. For a starting gap of 0.08 meters, this value is 0.04 meters. CarpalHand uses that distance once from wrist to carpal and again from carpal to hand, along directions blended between the wrist and target rotations.

This value is saved during setup rather than remeasured each frame. Changing it changes the small segment spacing; the helper also moves the wrist by the difference between the hand's previous position and its newly calculated position to compensate for that movement.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ArticulatedArmController._forearmLength
member.summary: Stores the starting forearm length in meters, which controls its solved length and the reach used to sample the stretch curve.

remarks.para: Awake, a routine Unity calls when this component is first initialized, measures the world-space distance from elbowLf to wristLf. SolveArm multiplies this stored length by the stretch-curve output when stretching is active and places the corresponding next bone along its parent's local blue Z axis. For a stored length of 0.30 meters and a curve output of 1.05, that segment becomes 0.315 meters long in an unscaled bone hierarchy.

This is a saved starting length, not a measurement refreshed each frame. CalibrateArmStretch edits the curve without remeasuring these lengths. Editing this value also changes the total starting arm length used to normalize reach.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ArticulatedArmController._handTwistLf
member.summary: Carries the signed wrist-twist angle between solves so arm relaxation can follow twisting over time.

remarks.para: The value is in degrees. ElbowIsNot adds the signed angle between the elbow's twist-adjusted up direction and the wrist's up direction, around the elbow's forward direction. Values above 240 degrees are shifted down by 360; values below -240 are shifted up by 360. This is accumulated state, not just a fresh single-frame angle.
WristRelax replaces this value with the result and uses it to sample WristElbowIsNotCurve. Editing it changes the twist history the next relaxation solve starts from.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ArticulatedArmController._initialIndex1
member.summary: Stores the index finger's base segment starting rotation so animator poses can be converted into its physics-joint targets.

remarks.para: This is a quaternion, Unity's four-number representation of a rotation. Awake, a routine Unity calls when this component is first initialized, calculates the finger segment's rotation relative to the body connected by its physics joint. A physics joint connects two objects in the physics simulation. SolveHandPose uses this saved rotation as the reference when applying the animator's new parent-relative rotation.
It is a setup cache, not the current curl. Changing it shifts how later animator rotations are translated into joint targets; the controller does not refresh it each frame.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ArticulatedArmController._leftHandVector3
member.summary: Stores the current world-space vector from the shoulder to the desired wrist for the arm and twist calculations.

remarks.para: SolveArm overwrites it each call: desired wrist = targetHand position + wristLf position - handLf position, then this vector = desired wrist - shoulderLf position. All positions and vector components are world-space meters. Its length sets requested reach, and its direction is the axis for the shoulder roll applied by WristRelax.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ArticulatedArmController._neutHumLf
member.summary: Sets the reference orientation of the upper arm relative to the shoulder blade for aiming the arm and judging twist.

remarks.para: This is a quaternion, Unity's four-number representation of a rotation. SolveArm combines it with scapulaLf's world rotation to choose the reference arm direction before aiming toward the desired wrist. ElbowIsNot uses the same reference when judging how the arm is pointed.
The constructor supplies a fixed reference rotation; Awake does not measure it from shoulderLf. Changing it changes the aiming and twist reference, so it must suit the axes of this arm rig.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ArticulatedArmController._oldMaxStretchFactor
member.summary: Remembers the maxStretchFactor value last copied when the stretch curve was calibrated.

remarks.para: maxStretchFactor is the unitless setting for the generated upper multiplier of the starting shoulder-to-elbow and elbow-to-wrist lengths. It is not a current measured length or a hard clamp on every stretch-curve output. Update is Unity's routine that runs once per rendered frame.

Update compares this saved value with maxStretchFactor. A difference in any of the three saved settings requests curve adjustments at current index 0, then current index 1, then copies all three current settings into their saved values. The saved value is unitless. Changing the current setting is the normal way to request recalibration; changing this cache can trigger or suppress that comparison.

A key is a point on the curve; its index is its position in the list ordered by horizontal input, starting at 0. Calibration requests adjustments to the points currently at index 0, then index 1. Moving the first point can change the list order, so a custom curve's extra points are not guaranteed to keep their original values.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ArticulatedArmController._oldStretchRatio
member.summary: Remembers the stretchRatio value last copied when the stretch curve was calibrated.

remarks.para: stretchRatio controls how much extra requested wrist reach, relative to the starting arm length, is needed to arrive at the generated upper length multiplier. Desired wrist reach is the world-space distance from the shoulder to the target hand position shifted by the current wrist-minus-hand displacement. Starting arm length is the shoulder-to-elbow plus elbow-to-wrist lengths measured during initialization. This unitless ratio does not divide stretching between the two segments. Update is Unity's routine that runs once per rendered frame.
