member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ArticulatedArmController._upperArmLength
member.summary: Stores the starting upper-arm length in meters, which controls its solved length and the reach used to sample the stretch curve.

remarks.para: Awake, a routine Unity calls when this component is first initialized, measures the world-space distance from shoulderLf to elbowLf. SolveArm multiplies this stored length by the stretch-curve output when stretching is active and places the corresponding next bone along its parent's local blue Z axis. For a stored length of 0.30 meters and a curve output of 1.05, that segment becomes 0.315 meters long in an unscaled bone hierarchy.

This is a saved starting length, not a measurement refreshed each frame. CalibrateArmStretch edits the curve without remeasuring these lengths. Editing this value also changes the total starting arm length used to normalize reach.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ArticulatedArmController._wristRelaxLerpLf
member.summary: Stores the smoothed upper-arm roll angle applied by WristRelax, in degrees.

remarks.para: Despite its name, this is an angle rather than a 0-to-1 blend weight. Each call moves it toward the requested roll by a fraction equal to the smaller of 0.12 and 0.0025 × the absolute angle difference in degrees. A stored 0 degrees and requested 40 degrees become 4 degrees after one call.
WristRelax rotates shoulderLf by this angle around the shoulder-to-desired-wrist direction. The value is overwritten by that smoothing step, which runs per call without an elapsed-time multiplier.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ArticulatedArmController.carpalLf
member.summary: Is the small wrist-area bone positioned between wristLf and handLf to distribute their change in direction.

remarks.para: A Transform stores position, rotation, and scale. During SolveArm, CarpalHand places it a saved half-wrist-to-hand distance from the wrist along a direction blended between wrist and target rotations, and gives it an intermediate world rotation. The saved distance is _carpalLength, measured in meters during Awake, a routine Unity calls when this component is first initialized.

The helper places handLf another saved segment distance beyond this bone, then moves the wrist by the difference between the hand's previous and newly calculated positions to compensate for that movement. Assign this reference before use; its world position and rotation are overwritten by the arm solve.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ArticulatedArmController.elbowLf
member.summary: Is the elbow bone the solver moves and bends to connect the upper arm to the forearm.

remarks.para: A Transform stores position, rotation, and scale. SolveArm sets its local position to (0, 0, current upper-arm length) in meters along its parent's blue Z axis, then sets its local bend around the red X axis. Current length is the starting shoulder-to-elbow distance, multiplied by the stretch curve when active. An unscaled bone hierarchy makes these local distances match world meters.

Awake, a routine Unity calls when this component is first initialized, measures distances to this bone to establish starting arm lengths. The twist calculation also reads its world directions. Assign it before initialization; its solved local position and rotation are overwritten each frame.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ArticulatedArmController.handAnimator
member.summary: Creates the finger rotations that this controller converts into targets for its finger physics joints.

remarks.para: SolveHandPose supplies the five curl inputs, calculates the animator's pose, applies it to the animator's finger bones, and reads those bones' rotations relative to their parents. Each becomes a target for the matching physics joint, a connection between two objects in the physics simulation. If handAnimator is unassigned (null), SolveHandPose skips this pipeline. When it is assigned, initialize its finger references before use.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ArticulatedArmController.handLf
member.summary: Is the solved hand bone that follows the arm's reachable position and receives targetHand's world rotation.

remarks.para: A Transform stores position, rotation, and scale. Awake, a routine Unity calls when this component is first initialized, measures the wrist-to-hand distance and saves half for each of the two small wrist/hand segments. SolveArm reads the current wrist-minus-hand displacement when finding the desired wrist, positions the hand through CarpalHand, and finally sets its rotation to the target's rotation.
This hand Transform is separate from the 15 finger physics joints. The native controller does not check or establish their parenting relationship through this field.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ArticulatedArmController.index
member.summary: Requests how tightly the index finger curls in the animator pose that drives its physics joints.

remarks.para: In the smoothing calculation, clamp means keeping a number between the given lower and upper limits. Multiply the frame duration in seconds by 20 per second, then keep the result between 0 and 1. The animator applies that fraction of the difference from its current curl to the requested curl. For a 0.01-second frame, the fraction is 0.2; a current curl of 0 moving toward a request of 1 becomes 0.2. The fraction is unitless.

The intended input is unitless, from 0 for the animator's minimum curl to 1 for its maximum curl; 0.5 requests the halfway input. The visible angles depend on the selected hand pose and the animator's curl limits, so 0 and 1 do not always mean a perfectly straight finger and a complete fist.

SolveHandPose sends this value to handAnimator each frame. The animator moves its current curl toward the request by a fraction of clamp(20 × frame duration in seconds, 0, 1), and a queued override can replace the request for that call. It then blends the finger pose and this controller writes the resulting rotations as physics-joint targets. A physics joint connects objects in the physics simulation; reaching a target can take time.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ArticulatedArmController.index1
member.summary: Connects the index finger's base segment to another physics body and makes it aim for the animator's matching finger rotation.

remarks.para: A ConfigurableJoint is a physics connection whose movement and rotation can be limited or driven toward a target. Awake, a routine Unity calls when this component is first initialized, records this segment's starting rotation relative to the joint's connected body. SolveHandPose later reads the matching handAnimator segment's rotation relative to its parent and converts it into this joint's target using that saved starting rotation.

Assign the joint and its connected body before initialization. The controller updates the target each frame; it does not simply restore the original rotation, and the physical segment can lag behind its target.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ArticulatedArmController.maxStretchFactor
member.summary: Sets the upper length multiplier written into the stretch curve and the far-reach cutoff.

remarks.para: This setting is unitless: 1.05 represents approximately 5% extra length. With starting upper-arm and forearm lengths totaling 0.55 meters, that factor corresponds to 0.5775 meters before the solve's 4 mm reach margin. The constructor starts this setting at 1.05; serialized scene or prefab settings can replace that value.

Calibration requests a curve-point adjustment with horizontal input 1 + (maxStretchFactor - 1) × stretchRatio and vertical output maxStretchFactor + 0.0001. The horizontal input is desired wrist distance divided by the two starting arm lengths; stretchRatio is the unitless setting controlling how much farther the target must reach to arrive at that key. For factor 1.05 and ratio 2, the requested point has input 1.10.

When this setting changes, Update requests curve adjustments at current index 0, then current index 1. This is not a hard clamp on every custom curve value; SolveArm also caps the requested solve distance when reach exceeds the generated cutoff.

A key is a point on the curve; its index is its position in the list ordered by horizontal input, starting at 0. Calibration requests adjustments to the points currently at index 0, then index 1. Moving the first point can change the list order, so a custom curve's extra points are not guaranteed to keep their original values.

The desired wrist is targetHand's world position shifted by wristLf's world position minus handLf's. Desired wrist distance is the world-space distance from shoulderLf to that shifted point, in meters.

remarks.para: This setting is unitless. For the normal ordered two-point curve, the requested upper point's horizontal input is 1 + (maxStretchFactor - 1) × stretchRatio, where maxStretchFactor is the configured upper multiplier of both starting arm lengths. Input means desired wrist distance divided by the starting upper-arm plus forearm length. With factor 1.05, ratio 2 puts the key at 1.10; ratio 4 puts it at 1.20. A larger ratio spreads the generated stretch response across more requested reach.

The constructor starts this at 2; serialized settings can replace it. When it changes, Update requests curve adjustments at current index 0, then current index 1. Calibration also requests changes to that point's tangents, which shape the bend of the curve. This setting does not divide stretching between the upper arm and forearm: both use the same sampled multiplier.

A key is a point on the curve; its index is its position in the list ordered by horizontal input, starting at 0. Calibration requests adjustments to the points currently at index 0, then index 1. Moving the first point can change the list order, so a custom curve's extra points are not guaranteed to keep their original values.

The desired wrist is targetHand's world position shifted by wristLf's world position minus handLf's. Desired wrist distance is the world-space distance from shoulderLf to that shifted point, in meters.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ArticulatedArmController.stretchThreshold
member.summary: Sets the requested reach at which the solver begins sampling the arm-stretch curve.

remarks.para: This is a unitless fraction of the starting upper-arm plus forearm length. Requested reach is shoulder-to-desired-wrist distance; the desired wrist is targetHand's world position shifted by the current wrist-minus-hand displacement. With a 0.30-meter upper arm and 0.25-meter forearm, 0.8 corresponds to 0.44 meters. Sampling begins strictly above that distance, not at equality.

The constructor starts this at 0.8; serialized settings can replace it. Changing it causes Update to request curve adjustments at current index 0, then current index 1; the first requested point is (stretchThreshold, 1). The curve's vertical output multiplies both starting segment lengths.

A key is a point on the curve; its index is its position in the list ordered by horizontal input, starting at 0. Calibration requests adjustments to the points currently at index 0, then index 1. Moving the first point can change the list order, so a custom curve's extra points are not guaranteed to keep their original values.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ArticulatedArmController.targetHand
member.summary: Supplies the world-space hand position and rotation the arm tries to follow each frame.

remarks.para: Assign a Transform, an object storing position, rotation, and scale. SolveArm adjusts its position by the current wrist-to-hand displacement to find the desired wrist, then bends and stretches the arm toward that goal. Reach limits can prevent the hand from reaching an impossible position, while handLf receives this target's world rotation at the end of the solve.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ArticulatedArmController.thumb
member.summary: Requests how tightly the thumb curls in the animator pose that drives its physics joints.

remarks.para: In the smoothing calculation, clamp means keeping a number between the given lower and upper limits. Multiply the frame duration in seconds by 20 per second, then keep the result between 0 and 1. The animator applies that fraction of the difference from its current curl to the requested curl. For a 0.01-second frame, the fraction is 0.2; a current curl of 0 moving toward a request of 1 becomes 0.2. The fraction is unitless.

The intended input is unitless, from 0 for the animator's minimum curl to 1 for its maximum curl; 0.5 requests the halfway input. The visible angles depend on the selected hand pose and the animator's curl limits, so 0 and 1 do not always mean a perfectly straight finger and a complete fist. One animator mode changes only the thumb blend: when HandPoseAnimator.hoverFingers is true and its pose reference differs from defaultHandPose, BlendOpenPose offsets the current thumb blend factor by 0.25. This later pose-blend adjustment is not added to this controller's curl request.

SolveHandPose sends this value to handAnimator each frame. The animator moves its current curl toward the request by a fraction of clamp(20 × frame duration in seconds, 0, 1), and a queued override can replace the request for that call. It then blends the finger pose and this controller writes the resulting rotations as physics-joint targets. A physics joint connects objects in the physics simulation; reaching a target can take time.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ArticulatedArmController.thumb1
member.summary: Connects the thumb's base segment to another physics body and makes it aim for the animator's matching finger rotation.

remarks.para: A ConfigurableJoint is a physics connection whose movement and rotation can be limited or driven toward a target. Awake, a routine Unity calls when this component is first initialized, records this segment's starting rotation relative to the joint's connected body. SolveHandPose later reads the matching handAnimator segment's rotation relative to its parent and converts it into this joint's target using that saved starting rotation.

Assign the joint and its connected body before initialization. The controller updates the target each frame; it does not simply restore the original rotation, and the physical segment can lag behind its target.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BalloonGun.balloonColor0
member.summary: Stores preview queue slot 0; it moves to balloonColor1 on the next color shift.

remarks.para: A renderer draws the visible preview shape; changing this stored color alone does not update its displayed surface color.
Start is Unity's one-time setup routine before this enabled component's first normal update.

SetBalloonColor displays this slot on balloonMesh element 0 after shifting the queue. Start initializes the slots with random colors and immediately shifts them. These fields are changing queue contents, not a fixed palette of available choices.
Setting the field alone does not recolor its renderer. Each later shift overwrites it from the preceding slot, except slot 0, which receives a new random color.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BalloonGun.balloonJitterDelta
member.summary: Sets how far each preview target may vary along each local axis from its cached starting position.

remarks.para: Each center is the preview object's position relative to its parent, saved during Start, Unity's one-time setup before the first regular update. The random X, Y and Z offsets follow that parent's axes.
Each target adds independent random X, Y and Z values between -balloonJitterDelta and +balloonJitterDelta. This forms a box around the cached position, not a sphere with this maximum radius.

The values are local-position units. With parent scale 1, 0.02 means up to 2 cm on each axis; a diagonal offset can be about 3.46 cm from the center. Parent rotation/scale changes how that local box appears in the world. This moves preview transforms, not balloon mesh vertices or the spawned projectile.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BalloonGun.balloonMesh
member.summary: Lists the preview renderers whose materials show the color queue and whose transforms drift while the gun is held.

remarks.para: Start, Unity's one-time setup before the first regular update, saves each renderer Transform's position relative to its parent in the matching balloonMeshOrigin entry.

A renderer draws a visible mesh; its Transform stores position, rotation and scale. The matching motion arrays hold the cached starting local position, current target local position, smoothing velocity in local distance units per second, and next due game-time timestamp in seconds. Local positions are measured along each preview object's parent axes, in scene-distance units corresponding to meters when parent scale is 1. Time.time is elapsed game seconds, affected by the game's time-speed setting; slow motion or a zero time-speed setting changes how this clock advances.

SetBalloonColor directly colors elements 0 through 3, so those four entries must exist and be valid. The held update moves each listed renderer's local position using the matching origin, target, velocity and timestamp entries.

The constructor creates four-element motion arrays. If the renderer list grows, those arrays must have enough matching entries too. This code changes renderer transforms and material colors; it does not deform mesh vertices.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BalloonGun.balloonMeshOrigin
member.summary: Stores the preview renderers' starting local positions, used as the centers for random drift targets.

remarks.para: Start is Unity's one-time setup routine before this enabled component's first normal update. Local positions are measured along each preview object's parent axes, in scene-distance units corresponding to meters when parent scale is 1. RandomVector3 chooses independent X, Y and Z offsets between -balloonJitterDelta and +balloonJitterDelta in those same distance units.
Start copies each balloonMesh transform's localPosition into its matching entry. Later target changes add RandomVector3(balloonJitterDelta) to that cached position.

These are transform positions in the renderer parent's coordinate frame, not mesh vertices. Changing an entry moves the center of later drift targets; the current target is not immediately recalculated. Start overwrites values assigned before it runs.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BalloonGun.balloonRoot
member.summary: Groups the preview visuals so holding the trigger grip can show and rotate them together.

remarks.para: A GameObject is a scene object that can group child visuals. Start is Unity's one-time setup routine before this enabled component's first normal update. meshSpinSpeed supplies a base rate in degrees per game second for the group's rotation relative to its parent.
Start deactivates this GameObject. Trigger-grip attachment activates it and detachment deactivates it. While attached updates run, its local rotation changes according to meshSpinSpeed.
It is the held gun's preview group, not the spawned balloon entity or an attachment target for that entity.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BalloonGun.balloonSpawnable
member.summary: Chooses the balloon object requested when the gun fires.

remarks.para: The pool creates or reuses object instances. Start is Unity's one-time setup routine before this enabled component's first normal update. A spawn callback is a routine called with the object when a spawn succeeds; the request can finish after the requesting routine returns and does not itself guarantee success.

A Spawnable is an asset definition used by the object pool to create an object. Start registers it. Fire requests it at firePointTransform's world pose, and its completion callback looks for ProjectileBalloon to assign color and the muzzle aiming reference.

The projectile component controls its own aiming range, collision mask and attachment. The callback does not copy the similarly named BalloonGun range or layer fields. An object without ProjectileBalloon skips that setup.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BalloonGun.collisionLayers
member.summary: No shot-layer filtering effect was verified for this field in the complete audited BalloonGun class.

remarks.para: A raycast checks a straight line through the scene for an allowed collision shape.

BalloonGun does not perform the aiming raycast or copy this mask into its spawned projectile. ProjectileBalloon performs that raycast using its own collisionLayers. A layer mask is a set of physics layers that a query may hit.
This finding covers BalloonGun's checked methods and spawn callback, plus the projectile aiming consumer; it does not prove that no external game code or mod can read the field.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BalloonGun.effectiveRange
member.summary: No aiming-distance effect was verified for this field in the complete audited BalloonGun class.

remarks.para: A raycast searches along a straight line for a collision shape; the projectile's separate effectiveRange limits that search distance in world meters.

BalloonGun's spawn callback does not copy this value to ProjectileBalloon. The spawned component uses its own effectiveRange as the maximum raycast distance. That separate field is a world-space distance in meters.

This finding is limited to the checked gun methods and projectile aiming path. Changing this gun field is not an established way to reach more distant targets; no external whole-game absence is claimed.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BalloonGun.firePointTransform
member.summary: Places and orients newly requested balloons and muzzle effects, and supplies the projectile's later aiming origin.

remarks.para: A Transform stores a scene object’s position, rotation and scale; this one marks the gun’s muzzle, the point where its shot starts.

A spawn callback is a routine called with the object when a spawn succeeds; the request can finish after the requesting routine returns and does not itself guarantee success. Pool initialization prepares the created or reused projectile and captures its forward direction. The later raycast is a straight-line collision search. World positions use the scene-wide frame and scene-distance units, normally meters.

Fire initially reads its world position and rotation for both spawn requests. When the balloon spawn callback runs, it reapplies this transform's current world pose and assigns the transform to ProjectileBalloon.hosttransform.

The projectile captures its forward direction during pool initialization, then after a one-frame wait casts from the current hosttransform position. Moving the muzzle can therefore affect the later ray origin. The aim uses the projectile's own range and layer mask.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BalloonGun.gunSFX
member.summary: Plays the gunshot sound after a trigger-down update requests the balloon and muzzle effect.

remarks.para: The attach/detach callbacks are routines the grip calls when a hand grabs or releases it. Those routines show or hide the preview root; they do not play the gun-shot sound in the inspected class.

OnTriggerGripUpdate calls GunSFX.GunShot after its spawn requests. The standalone Fire method does not call it. The attach/detach callbacks only show or hide the preview root, so no mechanical-audio behavior is established for them through this reference.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BalloonGun.maxUpdateInterval
member.summary: Sets the upper random time bound, in seconds, between choosing new drift targets for each preview renderer.

remarks.para: Time.time is elapsed game seconds, affected by the game's time-speed setting; slow motion or a zero time-speed setting changes how this clock advances. minUpdateInterval is the lower random delay bound in seconds, this field is the upper bound, and nextTargetTime stores each renderer's next due timestamp on that game clock.

After retargeting a mesh, the gun stores Time.time plus Random.Range(minUpdateInterval, maxUpdateInterval) in that mesh's nextTargetTime. These bounds control target changes, not how often the gun receives input updates or how long smoothing takes.

For illustrative lower and upper bounds 0.1 and 0.3 seconds, the gun schedules the next retarget 100 to 300 milliseconds later on that game clock. The target changes only on an attached-grip update after that timestamp has passed, so it can last longer; these bounds do not guarantee its actual lifetime.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BalloonGun.meshSpinSpeed
member.summary: Sets the base angular speed for rotating the preview root in its local frame while the gun is held.

remarks.para: The rate is degrees per game second. Time.deltaTime supplies the game seconds for that frame and follows the game's time-speed setting, so slow motion reduces the rotation added per real second. Each stated axis factor is unitless; multiplying rate, frame game seconds and that factor gives the angle increment in degrees.
Euler angles describe rotation with an angle around each X, Y and Z axis. Local axes are the preview group's own axes; the stored local rotation describes its orientation relative to its parent.

The value is degrees per second. Each attached update adds an Euler rotation of meshSpinSpeed times elapsed-frame seconds times (1.271, 1, -0.732) around local X, Y and Z, composed with the root's current local rotation.

For meshSpinSpeed = 10, the increments correspond to 12.71, 10 and -7.32 degrees per second on those axes. A value of 0 adds no rotation. This rotates balloonRoot; the preview meshes do not each receive an independent spin setting here.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BalloonGun.minUpdateInterval
member.summary: Sets the lower random time bound, in seconds, between choosing new drift targets for each preview renderer.

remarks.para: maxUpdateInterval is the upper random delay bound, in seconds. Time.time is elapsed game seconds, affected by the game's time-speed setting; slow motion or a zero time-speed setting changes how this clock advances. Smoothing means gradually moving toward the chosen target on each held update.

The gun schedules each next target time from Time.time plus a random interval between this field and maxUpdateInterval. A larger pair of bounds makes targets change less often; the renderer still smooths toward its target on each attached update.
The clock is scaled game time, not a frame count. With bounds both 0.2, the requested interval is 0.2 seconds; the target changes on an attached update after that timestamp has passed.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BalloonGun.nextBalloonColor
member.summary: Stores the queued color that the balloon spawn callback applies to ProjectileBalloon.

remarks.para: A spawn callback is a routine called with the object when a spawn succeeds; the request can finish after the requesting routine returns and does not itself guarantee success. Start is Unity's one-time setup routine before this enabled component's first normal update.
SetBalloonColor overwrites it with the previous balloonColor3 before each Fire request. Setting this field before calling Fire therefore does not directly override that shot's queue selection.
The spawn callback reads the field when its object becomes available; it does not capture a separate immutable color for every request. Start also advances the initial color queue.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BalloonGun.nextTargetTime
member.summary: Stores the scaled-game-time timestamp after which each preview renderer may receive a new drift target.

remarks.para: Time.time is elapsed game seconds, affected by the game's time-speed setting; slow motion or a zero time-speed setting changes how this clock advances. A held callback is a routine the grip calls while a hand holds it; targets can only change when that routine runs after their due timestamp.

Each element is compared with Time.time in seconds. Once current time is strictly greater, the gun chooses that mesh's target and replaces the timestamp with current time plus a random configured interval.
For example, a value of 5.0 becomes due after the game-time clock passes 5 seconds, not 5 seconds after you assign it. It is a timestamp, not an interval. Entries must match balloonMesh indices.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BalloonGun.smoothTime
member.summary: Controls how quickly preview renderer positions settle toward their current drift targets.

remarks.para: Time.deltaTime is the game seconds between the previous and current frame. The stored velocity is the smoothing algorithm's continuing motion in local distance units per second. SmoothDamp gradually approaches the target and updates that velocity; positions follow the parent's axes and scale, with meters as the distance unit at parent scale 1.

The value is seconds and is passed to Unity's Vector3.SmoothDamp together with the stored velocity and Time.deltaTime. Smaller values make the position respond more quickly; larger values make it settle more slowly. It is a smoothing time scale, not a promise to arrive exactly at that duration.
The positions and velocities are in each renderer parent's local frame. This affects preview motion, not spawned-balloon buoyancy or the interval between selecting new targets.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BalloonGun.targetPos
member.summary: Stores the local position each preview renderer is currently being smoothed toward.

remarks.para: The starting-position cache is recorded during Start, Unity's one-time setup before the first regular update. Each saved position is measured relative to that preview object's parent; later retargets reuse it rather than capturing a new starting point.

balloonMeshOrigin is the cached starting position along this renderer's parent axes. Each random offset component is between -balloonJitterDelta and +balloonJitterDelta in the same local distance units, corresponding to meters at parent scale 1. SmoothDamp gradually moves the current position toward this target while preserving and updating its smoothing velocity, in local distance units per second.

When that mesh's target time passes, its entry becomes balloonMeshOrigin plus an independently randomized offset on each axis. The attached update SmoothDamps the renderer's localPosition toward this entry.
Writing a target changes the next smoothing step, but a scheduled retarget can overwrite it. These are local transform positions, not world aiming points or mesh vertices.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BalloonGun.triggerGrip
member.summary: Supplies the hand callbacks that show the preview and drive trigger-down firing while the gun is held.

remarks.para: Callbacks or handlers are routines run when grip events occur. Subscribing registers those routines to receive the events. Unity calls OnEnable when the component becomes active to register them, and OnDisable when it stops being active to unregister them.

OnEnable subscribes attach, detach and attached-update handlers to this Grip; OnDisable removes those handlers. Attachment shows balloonRoot, detachment hides it, and the held update reads the hand's trigger-down flag.
Changing triggerGrip while enabled does not move existing subscriptions automatically. A valid grip must be assigned for the checked enable/disable paths.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BalloonGun.velocity
member.summary: Keeps the per-renderer velocity state used by SmoothDamp to continue preview movement smoothly across updates.

remarks.para: SmoothDamp gradually moves a position toward its target. Passing this velocity by reference lets the routine write its updated value back into the same array entry for the next call. A Rigidbody is Unity's component that moves an object through physics; this array instead belongs to preview smoothing.

The vector is passed by reference, so SmoothDamp updates it after each position step. Its components are local-position units per second along the renderer parent's axes; with parent scale 1 those correspond to meters per second.

It is not a Rigidbody velocity and does not launch the spawned balloon. Resetting an entry to zero removes its stored smoothing momentum. The entries must correspond to balloonMesh and targetPos indices.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BalloonGun.vfxFlareSpawnable
member.summary: Chooses the separate muzzle visual requested whenever Fire requests a balloon.

remarks.para: Start is Unity's one-time setup routine before this enabled component's first normal update. The pool creates or reuses object instances. A completion callback is a routine called with a successfully obtained object; the flare request has no BalloonGun callback that assigns its color or aim. It is requested independently after the balloon request, without testing whether that first request succeeded.

Start registers this asset definition with the pool. Fire requests it at firePointTransform's world position and rotation after requesting the balloon. This spawn has no BalloonGun completion callback assigning color or aim; those steps belong to the balloon spawn.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BaseGameController.Alive_Enemy_List
member.summary: Tracks registered hostile NPCs that have not yet been recorded as dead.

remarks.para: RegisterNPCBase adds hostile brains, and OnNPC_DeathBase removes them when it records death. KillAll uses this list to request deaths; TimeTrial also uses it to create seeker markers for remaining enemies.

A brain is the component that controls an NPC's behavior. This is controller bookkeeping, not a fresh scan of the scene. Manually editing the list does not update activeEnemyCount or connect the death notifications.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BaseGameController.Alive_Friendly_List
member.summary: Tracks registered friendly NPCs that have not yet been recorded as dead.

remarks.para: RegisterNPCBase adds friendly brains and increments activeFriendlyCount. OnNPC_DeathBase removes the brain and decrements the counter. A brain is the component controlling an NPC's behavior.

Changing this collection alone does not set behavior teams, adjust activeFriendlyCount, or maintain the target-proxy pool. Use registration and death handling to keep those related values synchronized.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BaseGameController.Dead_Enemy_List
member.summary: Retains brains of registered hostile NPCs whose deaths the controller has recorded.

remarks.para: A brain is an NPC behavior component. OnNPC_DeathBase adds the brain here after removing it from Alive_Enemy_List. These references are death history, not a count of bodies still present in the scene.

The base OnDespawn handler does not remove entries here when a body returns to its pool. A pooled object can later be reused, so this list is not an immutable snapshot of that NPC's old physical state.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BaseGameController.Dead_Friendly_List
member.summary: Retains brains of registered friendly NPCs whose deaths the controller has recorded.

remarks.para: A brain is an NPC behavior component. OnNPC_DeathBase adds a friendly brain here after removing it from Alive_Friendly_List. Enemy-kill counters are not increased for that death.
The base OnDespawn handler does not remove these references when the bodies return to their pool. Entries therefore describe the controller's death bookkeeping, not which bodies are still visible.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BaseGameController.FriendlyNPC_List
member.summary: Stores a separate friendly-brain collection, but the base controller does not populate or use it for live-friendly tracking.

remarks.para: A brain controls an NPC's behavior. In the inspected BaseGameController methods, registration instead fills Alive_Friendly_List and friendly_Data_List. Changing FriendlyNPC_List alone does not register a friendly, change its team, or update the displayed friendly count.
This finding covers the base controller's complete runtime methods and its timer/spawn callbacks; outside code or mods can still use this collection.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BaseGameController.LevelKey
member.summary: Selects the save-progression entry that attempts to mark completed.

remarks.para: This is a stored string key passed to the progression system. DoCompleteLevel does not replace it with the active scene's barcode. Set the intended progression key before requesting completion; changing this string does not load a different level.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BaseGameController.NPC_Data_Dict
member.summary: Finds the registered record for an NPC's GameObject.

remarks.para: Registration checks this dictionary to reuse an existing record instead of adding another new record and count. Death handling and delayed despawning use it to find that NPC's saved tracking state.

When a record already marked dead is despawned, OnDespawn marks it removed and deletes this dictionary entry. It leaves NPC_Data_List history in place. Despawning a still-living record does not take that removal path in the base handler.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BaseGameController.NPC_Data_List
member.summary: Retains the records created when NPC GameObjects are first registered with the controller.

remarks.para: Records describe the NPC's brain, profile, spawner, zone and tracking flags. CheckForProxyTarget walks them to replace living NPC targets; DespawnAllNPCs walks records not marked despawned to request removal.

The base death/despawn handlers keep records in this list. It is therefore registration history, including dead or despawned NPCs, rather than a living-NPC list. Adding a record manually does not perform registration's count updates or notification setup.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BaseGameController.NPC_List
member.summary: Retains the behavior components added for newly registered NPC GameObjects.

remarks.para: RegisterNPCBase appends both friendlies and hostiles when the GameObject has no current NPC_Data_Dict record. It uses the new list count as that record's spawnOrder.

The base death/despawn handlers do not remove entries. These are reusable-object references, so the list need not contain only alive NPCs or one distinct object for each entry after pooling and re-registration.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BaseGameController.NPC_Zone_Dict
member.summary: Maps each to the first registered for it.

remarks.para: RegisterNPCBase adds a spawner-to-record entry only when that spawner has no key yet. A later NPC from the same spawner does not replace the earlier mapping.
This is a single-record lookup, not a collection of every NPC in the spawner's zone. The base despawn handler removes GameObject dictionary entries, but does not refresh this spawner mapping.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BaseGameController.OnPlayerFound
member.summary: Notifies connected routines after a player-reference and NPC-spawner-target setup attempt.

remarks.para: OnLevelLoadGetPlayer invokes this callback, a routine called to report an action, with no arguments. At that point rigManager, playerObject and playerProxy have been stored; a valid player proxy has seeded friendlyProxyList, and configured spawners have received the found reference as their private cached playerProxy.
The method is registered during Awake, Unity's initialization callback. There is no one-shot flag in OnLevelLoadGetPlayer, so another successful invocation can fire this notification again.

rigManager refers to the player rig, the set of objects controlling the player's body. playerObject is the scene object holding that rig component. playerProxy is the targeting component that identifies the body to game-controlled characters.

This notification reports the end of the setup attempt. If the proxy is missing or destroyed, friendlyProxyList keeps its old entries and the configured spawners can still receive a missing playerProxy reference before this no-argument notification fires. It therefore does not guarantee a valid targeting proxy or a freshly cleared target list.
Awake is the initialization routine Unity calls before normal component startup. A listener is a routine connected to run when this notification is sent.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BaseGameController.OnRegisteredNPCDeath
member.summary: Notifies listeners with the same NPC record after its dead flag and faction counts/lists have been updated.

remarks.para: The argument is the NPC_Data record found for the dying brain's GameObject. Its isDead flag and puppet targetRoot position in world coordinates have already been recorded. targetRoot is the puppet's stored root Transform, the component holding an object's position and rotation; its position is in meters along the scene's axes. The brain has left its alive list and entered its dead list, and its controller death notification has been disconnected.

This callback—a routine called to report an action—fires before auto-despawn is scheduled, before the text labels refresh, and before ARENA writes deathTime or appends to dead_NPC_Data_List. Unknown NPCs do not produce this notification. Repeating OnNPC_DeathBase manually is not protected by an already-dead check.

A brain is the NPC's behavior component; its puppet is the system controlling its simulated body. A GameObject is the Unity scene object holding those components. A listener is a routine connected to receive this notification and its NPC_Data record.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BaseGameController.activeEnemyCount

remarks.para: Registration increments it for a new hostile record; recorded hostile death decrements it. The unit is NPCs, not kills or points. UpdateNPCDisplay shows this stored number without recounting the scene.

For example, three hostile registrations followed by one recorded hostile death change the counter by +2 overall. Editing the number changes the displayed count on the next refresh but does not add or remove NPCs.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BaseGameController.currFriendlyProxy

remarks.para: This is a zero-based list index: 0 starts at the first entry. GetFriendlyProxy resets it to 0 when it reaches or exceeds friendlyProxyList.Count and increments it once after selecting a player or eligible NPC target.

Skipped entries advance only the local search index, so the stored value is not always the selected entry's index plus one. ResetFriendlyProxyList does not reset it. Use a valid nonnegative index; the method does not clamp negative values.

This is a logging preference, not a switch for the NPC text labels or a guarantee that all errors disappear. It does not change timer or faction bookkeeping.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BaseGameController.defaultDelayedMaxTime
member.summary: Supplies the start-countdown duration when CoDelayedStart sees a negative .

remarks.para: Measured in scaled game seconds. The sequence copies this value into delayedMaxTime and timerValue when it begins with a negative delay; it does not automatically restore it between every run.

For example, defaultDelayedMaxTime = 5 with delayedMaxTime = -1 requests a 5-second countdown. A positive delayedMaxTime uses its own value, while exactly zero begins immediately. Changing the default after the countdown has started does not change the already-copied timerValue.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BaseGameController.defaultEndDelayedMaxTime
member.summary: Supplies the end-transition countdown when CoDelayedEnd sees a negative .

remarks.para: Measured in scaled game seconds. At sequence start, a negative delayedEndMaxTime copies this value into delayedEndMaxTime and timerValue. A positive delay uses its own value, while exactly zero exits without loading or reloading.

For example, a default of 5 with delayedEndMaxTime = -1 requests roughly 5 game seconds before the configured transition. This is fallback setup, not an automatic reset between runs or an exact wall-clock schedule. Changing the default later does not change the copied countdown.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BaseGameController.defaultMaxTime
member.summary: Supplies the session countdown's starting seconds when is not positive.

remarks.para: CoTimerDown copies this value into maxTime and timerValue when it starts without a positive maxTime. For example, defaultMaxTime = 60 and maxTime = 0 starts from 60 game-time seconds.
A positive maxTime takes precedence. This default is not a deadline for either count-up timer. Changing it during an already-started countdown does not alter the copied timerValue.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BaseGameController.delayedEndMaxTime
member.summary: Sets the game-time countdown before an end-session reload or explicit level transition.

remarks.para: Measured in seconds and read when CoDelayedEnd starts. A positive value is copied into timerValue; the duration field itself is not decremented. A negative value selects defaultEndDelayedMaxTime, while exactly zero stops the sequence without a transition.

The session has already been marked ended before this countdown starts. Slow motion stretches the real wait, time-scale pausing stops it, and the eventual transition is checked on a later frame. LOAD_NEXT performs no load in the compiled base sequence. Changing this field after it has been copied does not change the running countdown.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BaseGameController.delayedMaxTime
member.summary: Sets the countdown displayed before CoDelayedStart begins the session.

remarks.para: Measured in scaled game seconds. When that sequence starts, a positive value is copied into timerValue; a negative value selects defaultDelayedMaxTime; exactly zero calls BeginSession immediately.

This duration field is not decremented. Changing it after the sequence has copied it does not change the current wait. A value of 3 requests about 3 game seconds, with completion occurring on a frame after the countdown reaches zero. BeginSession alone does not use this delay.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BaseGameController.despawnDelay
member.summary: Sets how many game-time seconds auto-despawn waits after a registered NPC death.

remarks.para: OnNPC_DeathBase copies this into a delayed coroutine when isAutoDespawn is true. A coroutine is a routine that continues across frames. Its WaitForSeconds delay uses scaled game time, so slow motion stretches the real wait and a paused game stops it.

When the wait finishes, it checks that the NPC still has a registered record marked dead and not despawned, then requests the despawn effect and pool removal. For example, 4 game seconds take about 8 real seconds at half time scale. Completion occurs on a frame; changing this field after scheduling does not change that already-copied wait.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BaseGameController.despawnedDataList
member.summary: Stores DeadData history records and is cleared when an arena mode ends.

remarks.para: A DeadData record can hold a brain reference, spawn order, death position, round and wave. This differs from the NPC_Data records in NPC_Data_List.

The inspected base constructor creates this collection, but its complete runtime methods and timer/spawn callbacks do not add records when NPCs die or despawn. The inspected Arena_GameController.EndOfMode clears it. Do not assume the base despawn callback has populated it; any other producer must be supplied by outside code.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BaseGameController.despawnedDataWaveList
member.summary: Stores a separate DeadData collection, with no verified automatic population by the base controller.

remarks.para: DeadData can hold a brain reference, spawn order, death position, round and wave. The complete inspected BaseGameController runtime methods and timer/spawn callbacks construct this list but do not add, read, or respawn entries from it.
Placing a record here does not by itself queue an NPC to return in a later wave. Outside game systems or mods were not exhaustively checked, so this is a scoped finding about the base controller.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BaseGameController.elapsedTime
member.summary: Reads the controller's current timerValue in seconds.

remarks.para: Its meaning depends on what last wrote the shared timer: COUNT_UP and COUNT_UP_REALTIME accumulate time; COUNT_DOWN stores remaining session time; REALTIME stores seconds since the application started. Start/end transition countdowns can also replace it with remaining wait time.
This getter performs no elapsed-duration calculation and does not subtract a session-start timestamp. A countdown can briefly return a negative value after the final frame crosses zero.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BaseGameController.endMode
member.summary: Selects the transition attempted after .

remarks.para: RELOAD_CURRENT starts an end countdown then requests a reload. EXPLICIT starts the countdown then requests explicitSceneCrate through the fade effect when that reference exists. NONE starts no end countdown.

In the compiled base implementation, LOAD_NEXT starts the countdown but requests no next-level load when it finishes. The delayed sequence also performs no transition if delayedEndMaxTime is exactly zero. It reads endMode again after waiting, so changing the selection during the wait can change the eventual branch.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BaseGameController.enemiesKilled
member.summary: Counts registered hostile-NPC deaths since this counter was last reset.

remarks.para: OnNPC_DeathBase adds one for a hostile death, and UpdateNPCDisplay copies the count to killsTexts. Friendly deaths do not add to it. NPC means a character controlled by the game.

BeginSession does not reset this number. Arena objective setup and wave cleanup reset it to zero, so it can represent an objective or wave rather than the entire session. Setting it changes the stored count; labels change on their next refresh.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BaseGameController.explicitSceneCrate
member.summary: Selects the destination for and the EXPLICIT end transition.

remarks.para: This is a level-asset reference. An EXPLICIT end countdown reads it when the wait finishes; changing it before then can change the destination. With no reference, that path requests no load.

The destination load is requested after a successfully spawned fade effect reports completion. Assigning this field or returning from the loading method does not mean the destination has finished loading.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BaseGameController.foldArray
member.summary: Stores on/off entries without expanding or collapsing runtime score labels in the base controller.

remarks.para: This is an array of Boolean values: each entry is true or false. The complete inspected BaseGameController methods and their timer/spawn routines do not read it or map its indices to scoreboard sections.
Changing an entry therefore has no verified display effect through those methods. Code outside that inspected base scope would have to define what each index means and apply the state.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BaseGameController.friendlyProxyList
member.summary: Supplies the player and friendly-NPC target identifiers considered by enemy targeting.

remarks.para: A target proxy is a component that identifies an object an NPC can aim at. Player setup clears this list and adds the player proxy only when that proxy is valid; otherwise it keeps the existing entries. Registering a new friendly NPC adds its own proxy; its recorded death removes that proxy.

GetFriendlyProxy searches from a saved index. A Player entry returns the cached playerProxy. An NPC entry needs an AgentLinkControl whose puppet has its state set to Alive; a puppet controls the NPC body, and that setting is a request whose physical transition may still be in progress. If the search finds no eligible entry, it falls back to playerProxy.

The player is included, so this is not a list containing only NPCs. Keep the list and its entries valid: null entries or missing referenced components can fail during selection. ResetFriendlyProxyList clears it back to the player when that proxy is valid.
AgentLinkControl is the NPC component that connects its movement and body control. This search reads that component's puppet and target proxy when checking an NPC entry.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BaseGameController.friendlyRespawnAmount
member.summary: Caches the number of dead friendly NPCs during arena wave cleanup and gates a friendly respawn attempt.

remarks.para: During cleanup in the ACTIVE arena state, the arena controller replaces this integer with Dead_Friendly_List.Count, the number of entries in its dead-friendly list. A value of at least one lets supported arena modes start the friendly spawning routine.

The requested friendly total comes separately from the current wave's friendlyProfileList count, with one added in PROTECT mode. For example, three recorded friendly deaths can set this to 3 while the current wave supplies a different friendly spawn target. This field is not a maximum number of friends allowed alive.

The spawning routine continues across frames and checks activeFriendlyCount against its copied target. A spawn request can finish later; the stored cleanup count alone does not prove any replacement has spawned.

The current wave's friendlyProfileList contains its friendly character descriptions. SURVIVAL and CUSTOM request that list's count as the friendly total; PROTECT requests that count plus one. activeFriendlyCount is the controller's stored number of living registered friendly characters, measured as a whole-character count. A frame is one game update.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BaseGameController.friendly_Data_List
member.summary: Tracks records for registered friendly NPCs whose target proxies are added to .

remarks.para: RegisterNPCBase adds a new friendly NPC_Data record here after filling its brain, spawner, zone, profile and target information. NPC_Data is a bundle of information about one game-controlled character.

OnNPC_DeathBase removes that friendly record and its own target proxy. The player proxy can be in friendlyProxyList without an NPC_Data entry here, so the two collections are not matching arrays that can safely be paired by index.
A target proxy is a component identifying an object a game-controlled character can aim at. The proxy is a targeting reference; NPC_Data is the stored information about that character.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BaseGameController.gameMode
member.summary: Selects the branches used during NPC registration and death recording.

remarks.para: ARENA makes hostile registration choose a target from the friendly target pool and give the NPC that behavior target. Arena deaths also record Time.time, measured in scaled game seconds since startup, and append the record to the dead-NPC data list.

The inspected Linear and TimeTrial controllers set this to LINEAR and TIME_TRIAL in Awake, Unity's initialization callback. Changing this enum alone does not replace the controller component or install another controller's session rules.

A frame is one game update. timeScale is the unitless game-speed multiplier: scaled frame seconds follow that multiplier, while unscaled frame seconds measure real elapsed time. At timeScale 0.5, a frame lasting 0.02 real seconds normally contributes 0.01 game seconds.
An enum is a named integer choice. Awake is the initialization routine Unity calls before normal component startup; a callback is a routine called to report or respond to an action.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BaseGameController.graveMesh
member.summary: Stores a 3D mesh reference without creating NPC death markers in the base controller.

remarks.para: A mesh contains the shape of a 3D object. The complete inspected BaseGameController methods and their timer/spawn routines do not read this reference, instantiate gravestones, or draw death markers from it.
Assigning a mesh therefore does not add a grave when an NPC dies through the base death handler. Any other consumer outside that inspected scope must provide the rendering or spawning behavior.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BaseGameController.isAutoDespawn
member.summary: Controls whether a registered NPC death schedules a delayed request to remove its body.

remarks.para: OnNPC_DeathBase reads this after firing the registered-death event. If true, it starts a coroutine, a routine that continues across frames, with a copy of despawnDelay in game-time seconds. This applies to both hostile and friendly deaths.

After the wait, the routine requires a registered record that is still dead and not already despawned before requesting the despawn effect and object removal. Changing this flag later does not cancel an already scheduled wait. For example, turning it off after a death does not retain that body if its removal was already queued.
A pool stores objects so they can be reused. The removal request can return an object to its pool; an object outside a pool can instead be deactivated, meaning it stops being active in the scene.

A frame is one game update. timeScale is the unitless game-speed multiplier: scaled frame seconds follow that multiplier, while unscaled frame seconds measure real elapsed time. At timeScale 0.5, a frame lasting 0.02 real seconds normally contributes 0.01 game seconds.

The wait uses game-time seconds, so slow motion lengthens the real wait and a time-scale pause stops its progress. After that wait, the routine resumes on a later frame; the configured seconds do not promise an exact wall-clock completion time.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BaseGameController.isDevToolSpawned
member.summary: Remembers a developer-tool notification and prevents this controller from submitting leaderboard scores.

remarks.para: DevToolSpawn sets this to true when called. OnEnable, Unity's component-enabled callback, subscribes that method to developer tool-spawn notifications. SubmitScoreByType returns without sending a score when this flag is true.

The flag is a stored record of a notification, not a search for tools that currently exist. The inspected base methods do not reset it when tools disappear or when BeginSession runs. Setting it manually also changes the leaderboard gate.

OnEnable is the routine Unity calls when this component becomes enabled. Subscribing connects DevToolSpawn as the routine called when a developer tool-spawn notification arrives; that routine is the callback for the notification.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BaseGameController.isSessionOngoing
member.summary: Marks whether base session timers should continue, set by and cleared by .

remarks.para: BeginSession fires sessionBegin first, then sets this to true and starts the selected timer. EndSession fires sessionEnd first, then sets it to false and stops the stored timerRoutine. An event listener can therefore observe the previous flag value.

The timer routines test this flag as they continue across frames. Setting it alone does not start a timer or fire either session event. A running count-down routine that continues after the flag becomes false follows its EndSession path.
An event listener is a routine connected to run when the event fires.
A frame is one game update.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BaseGameController.isSlowTime
member.summary: Records whether the last received slow-time step number was at least one.

remarks.para: The controller subscribes to TimeManager.OnSlowTime while enabled. Its handler sets this true for slowStep greater than or equal to 1 and false below 1. The native producer sends a numbered slow-motion step, not a time multiplier: normal step 0 gives false, while step 1 gives true.

This flag does not change Unity's time scale. The base timers choose scaled or unscaled frame time directly, so changing this stored value does not slow their arithmetic. It describes the last notification, which can differ from manually changed time-scale settings.

A frame is one game update. timeScale is the unitless game-speed multiplier: scaled frame seconds follow that multiplier, while unscaled frame seconds measure real elapsed time. At timeScale 0.5, a frame lasting 0.02 real seconds normally contributes 0.01 game seconds.
Subscribing connects OnSlowTime as the routine called when the time manager sends a slow-time notification.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BaseGameController.isTrackingEnemies
member.summary: Controls whether component setup subscribes to NPC spawn notifications from profileSpawnerList.

remarks.para: OnEnable, Unity's component-enabled callback, reads this flag. When true, it adds RegisterNPCBase to each listed spawner's spawn event. OnDisable checks the flag again before removing those handlers.

It is a setup choice, not proof that subscriptions are currently active or a switch checked on every spawn. Changing it while enabled does not automatically add or remove handlers. Turning it false before disabling can leave handlers installed because the removal path then skips them.

Registration and death handling count friendly as well as hostile NPCs. Calling RegisterNPCBase directly still records an NPC regardless of this flag. Keep the flag and spawner list stable across enable/disable if relying on this subscription setup.

Unity calls OnEnable when the component becomes enabled and OnDisable when it becomes disabled. A handler is a routine connected to run when a notification arrives; subscribing installs that connection.
An NPC is a game-controlled character.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BaseGameController.killsTexts

remarks.para: UpdateNPCDisplay turns enemiesKilled into a whole-number string and writes it to these labels. A hostile registered death increments that counter; friendly deaths do not.

The counter is not reset by BeginSession, and arena objective/wave cleanup can reset it, so the text is not guaranteed to mean all kills in one complete session. Changing the label list or counter takes effect on the next refresh.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BaseGameController.linkList

remarks.para: A component is an attachment on a Unity scene object. GetAllLinkData clears this list, searches the scene for LinkData components, then adds each returned reference if it is not already listed.

Calling GetAllLinkData refreshes the stored collection. Merely changing the list does not create or move a scene link, and the inspected base controller does not refresh this collection on every frame.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BaseGameController.maxDeadDespawnLimit

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BaseGameController.maxTime

remarks.para: A positive value is copied into timerValue. Zero or a negative value is replaced with defaultMaxTime, and that fallback is also copied into timerValue. For example, 60 starts near 60 seconds remaining.

The countdown then subtracts scaled frame durations: slow motion lengthens the real wait and a time-scale pause stops it. It can pass slightly below zero before EndSession runs on the next continuation.

This is copied setup data, not the changing remaining time. Editing it after initialization does not resize that countdown. The base COUNT_UP, COUNT_UP_REALTIME and REALTIME routines do not stop at this limit.

A frame is one game update. timeScale is the unitless game-speed multiplier: scaled frame seconds follow that multiplier, while unscaled frame seconds measure real elapsed time. At timeScale 0.5, a frame lasting 0.02 real seconds normally contributes 0.01 game seconds.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BaseGameController.nothingGOList

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BaseGameController.onNPCRegistration

The payload is therefore not guaranteed to be newly allocated or to represent a newly counted spawn. Arena registration can also retarget an existing hostile NPC before notifying listeners.

remarks.para: A Unity event stores listeners that can be called from scene setup. The dump marks this field obsolete and asks for migration to the newer UltEvent field sessionBegin.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BaseGameController.profileSpawnerList
member.summary: Supplies the configured components for NPC subscriptions, player targets and arena spawn choices.

remarks.para: A ProfileSpawner is a component that requests NPCs from a profile. With isTrackingEnemies true, OnEnable subscribes RegisterNPCBase to each entry's spawn event. Player setup also assigns each entry's private cached playerProxy to the player proxy.

This is not an automatic list of every spawner in the scene. The arena controller adds and removes entries as zones change and its spawn routines choose from this current list. Adding an entry while enabled does not automatically install the base spawn-event handler; subscription setup occurs when OnEnable runs.
