member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BaseGameController.staticProfile
member.summary: Supplies the reference that can initialize the shared game profile.

remarks.para: Awake, Unity's initialization callback, checks the shared StaticProfiles.instance. If that instance is missing, it calls CreateStatProfile with this field; that method stores this same reference as the shared instance.

If a valid shared instance already exists, Awake keeps it rather than replacing it with this field. Later inspected startup and seeker/hub methods read the shared instance. Changing this field after initialization therefore does not switch those consumers to another profile.

StaticProfiles is the shared collection of friendly and enemy character descriptions and other level resources. Awake is the initialization routine Unity calls before normal component startup; the word callback means a routine called in response to an action.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BaseGameController.timerMode
member.summary: Chooses which base timer routine BeginSession starts.

remarks.para: COUNT_UP adds scaled frame time, measured in game seconds, to the existing timerValue. COUNT_DOWN initializes remaining seconds from a positive maxTime or defaultMaxTime and subtracts scaled frame time. Scaled time runs more slowly in slow motion and stops at time scale zero.

REALTIME replaces timerValue with real seconds since the application started, including while time scale is zero. COUNT_UP_REALTIME adds each frame's real duration to the existing value, but skips addition while time scale is zero.

BeginSession reads this choice when starting the routine. Changing the enum afterward does not replace an already running timer. The count-up routines do not clear their starting value or stop at maxTime.

A frame is one game update. timeScale is the unitless game-speed multiplier: scaled frame seconds follow that multiplier, while unscaled frame seconds measure real elapsed time. At timeScale 0.5, a frame lasting 0.02 real seconds normally contributes 0.01 game seconds.

An enum is a named integer choice. maxTime is the configured initial COUNT_DOWN length in game-time seconds. defaultMaxTime is its configured fallback length in the same units, used when maxTime is zero or negative. timerValue holds the resulting running timer quantity in seconds.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BaseGameController.timerRoutine
member.summary: Stores the coroutine handle most recently returned when BeginSession started the timer selected by .

remarks.para: A coroutine is a routine that continues in steps across frames. This reference lets EndSession stop that stored timer; EndSession does not clear the field afterward, so a non-null handle is not proof that the routine is still running.

There is no already-running check in BeginSession. Calling it again can start another timer and replace this handle, leaving the earlier routine without a handle here. EndSession only explicitly stops the stored one, though the session flag also controls timer continuation.
Changing timerMode or this stored reference does not automatically switch a running routine. Start and end delay routines are not stored in this timer handle.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BaseGameController.timerTexts
member.summary: Lists text labels that receive during base timer-display updates.

remarks.para: UpdateTimeDisplay formats the current shared timerValue in seconds and writes its cached string to each label whose GameObject is active in the scene hierarchy. Labels under an inactive parent do not receive that update.

Normal updates first discard fractional seconds. The final EndSession refresh requests the format hours:minutes:seconds.hundredths, such as 00:00:12.34 for 12.345 seconds. Merely changing timerValue does not immediately update the labels.

Refresh timing depends on the selected timer routine. The compiled countdown comparison normally does not refresh a decreasing value after its initial update, even though the stored remaining time keeps falling.

A GameObject is a Unity scene object that holds the label component. Its hierarchy is its chain of parent objects; an inactive parent makes the label inactive in that chain. A frame is one game update.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BaseGameController.timerValue
member.summary: Stores the shared timer quantity in seconds, whose meaning depends on the last routine that wrote it.

remarks.para: COUNT_UP accumulates scaled game time, while COUNT_UP_REALTIME accumulates real frame time unless time scale is zero. Both add to the existing value. COUNT_DOWN stores remaining game-time seconds and can pass slightly below zero on its final subtraction.

REALTIME instead writes seconds since the application started: beginning at application uptime 120 seconds gives a value near 120, not elapsed session time zero. Start/end delay routines also reuse this field for their remaining wait.

Timer displays read it on refresh. Time-based leaderboard types read it as whole seconds or convert seconds to integer milliseconds by multiplying by 1000. A positive end delay can replace the session value after sessionEnd listeners run, so code needing the finish time must capture it at the right point.

A frame is one game update. timeScale is the unitless game-speed multiplier: scaled frame seconds follow that multiplier, while unscaled frame seconds measure real elapsed time. At timeScale 0.5, a frame lasting 0.02 real seconds normally contributes 0.01 game seconds.
An event listener is a routine connected to run when the event fires.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BaseGameController.totalEnemiesKilled
member.summary: Counts registered hostile-NPC deaths until other controller code resets the total.

remarks.para: Each recorded hostile death adds one, alongside enemiesKilled. Friendly deaths do not add to either enemy-kill counter. UpdateNPCDisplay copies this total to totalKillsTexts, and time-trial completion checks can compare it with a required kill target.

This is not a saved lifetime statistic. BeginSession does not reset it, but Arena_GameController.EndOfMode sets it to zero. It can cover several arena waves until that mode ends; changing it also changes later completion checks and label refreshes.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BaseGameController.totalEnemiesTexts
member.summary: Lists text labels that the time-trial controller fills with its required enemy-kill target.

remarks.para: A valid SetRequiredKillCount call stores the required count and writes that whole number to these labels. ProgPointKillCount adjusts the required count and also refreshes them. For example, a required count of 8 produces the text 8, not a live count of enemies left.

SetRequiredKillCount validates that the target is positive and no larger than profileSpawnerList.Count. Its invalid-input fallback changes the stored requirement to the spawner count without writing these labels in that branch, so their text can remain stale.
The complete inspected base UpdateNPCDisplay method writes other kill/alive labels, not this list. This field alone does not count every enemy in the scene.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BaseGameController.totalKillsTexts
member.summary: Lists text labels that receive the totalEnemiesKilled count when NPC displays refresh.

remarks.para: UpdateNPCDisplay writes this whole-number hostile-kill count. Friendly deaths do not increase it. The total lasts until controller code resets it; the arena EndOfMode method sets it to zero.
These labels therefore do not automatically show lifetime kills across sessions or a persisted save statistic. Editing the counter or this list takes effect on a later display refresh.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BaseGameController.tsTimerString
member.summary: Caches the last formatted clock string; base updates copy it to .

remarks.para: UpdateTimeDisplay normally discards fractional timerValue seconds before creating a TimeSpan, a value representing a duration, and converting it to text. Its fractional option uses hours:minutes:seconds.hundredths, such as 00:00:12.34 for 12.345 seconds. There are two fractional digits, not three-digit milliseconds.

This is a display cache, not a string recalculated whenever timerValue changes. UpdateArenaTimeDisplay can overwrite it from the separate arenaTimerValue and send it to the arena label, so it is not always a formatted copy of the base timer.
Assigning this string alone does not push it to the labels. The next base display update computes a new string from timerValue and may replace your text.
arenaTimerValue is the arena controller's separate numeric clock, measured in seconds. timerValue is the base controller's shared numeric timer, also measured in seconds.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BaseGameController.tsTimerValue
member.summary: Caches the produced by the most recent display conversion of or the arena clock.

remarks.para: A TimeSpan represents a duration. Normal base display updates first discard fractional timerValue seconds, then convert those whole seconds to this value; the fractional option converts the floating seconds before formatting hundredths.

It is not a continuously precise copy of timerValue. It stays unchanged between display updates, and UpdateArenaTimeDisplay can overwrite it using the separate arenaTimerValue after discarding that clock's fractions.
Setting it alone does not change the base numeric timer or refresh a label. The next display conversion can overwrite it.
arenaTimerValue is the arena controller's separate numeric clock, measured in seconds.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BaseGameController.zoneDisplayList
member.summary: Stores records whose NPC lists arena objective setup clears.

remarks.para: A zone is a region in the scene. A ZoneDisplayEditor record can hold a zone reference and lists of spawners and NPC data. The constructor creates this collection, and Arena_GameController.StartNextObjectiveProfile walks it and clears each record's NPC-data list.

It is not automatically every zone display in the scene. Base RegisterNPCBase can create a zone record in zoneNPCLookup and append an NPC there without adding that record to this separate list. Filling the dictionary therefore does not guarantee the arena cleanup visits the same records here.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BaseGameController.zoneList
member.summary: Stores configured zone references without automatically gathering children of .

remarks.para: A zone is a region in the scene. The constructor creates an empty list. The complete inspected BaseGameController methods and their timer/spawn routines do not fill it by walking a parent object's children.

Assigning a parent or adding an entry here does not by itself register NPCs or add an entry to zoneNPCLookup. Base registration takes an NPC's zone from its ProfileSpawner and records it in that separate dictionary. Any other setup outside that inspected scope must populate this list.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BaseGameController.zoneNPCLookup
member.summary: Maps each registered spawner , a scene region, to its NPC-data record.

remarks.para: When creating a new NPC record, RegisterNPCBase reads the ProfileSpawner's zone. If the dictionary has no record for that zone, it creates one and stores it; then it adds the NPC_Data record to that zone record's NPC list.
A zone is a scene region, and this dictionary lets code find its recorded NPC data by the zone reference. It is filled by registration, not by automatically discovering every zone in the scene.

The base death and despawn handlers do not remove the NPC from this zone record. These entries can therefore retain dead or despawned NPC data until separate cleanup. New dictionary records are not automatically added to zoneDisplayList.
NPC_Data is the stored information about one registered game-controlled character.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BaseGameController.zoneParentObj
member.summary: Holds a proposed parent for setup, without collecting its children in the base controller.

remarks.para: A GameObject is a scene object that can hold child objects and components. The field's setup tooltip describes placing all zones under one parent, but the complete inspected BaseGameController methods and their timer/spawn routines do not walk this object's children.

Assigning this reference therefore does not populate zoneList or zoneNPCLookup through those methods. The base registration path obtains its zone from the NPC's ProfileSpawner instead. Any additional setup outside that inspected scope must perform the intended collection.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BehaviourCrablet.crumbleDeath
member.summary: Enables the crablet’s joint-loosening crumble routine and its matching joint-recovery routine.

remarks.para: When true, DoCrumbleDeath frees the selected body joints, pushes the parts outward, and starts a configured 3-second wait in scaled game time before returning the enemy to its object pool. A physics joint limits how simulated body parts move, and an object pool stores inactive objects for reuse. A frame is one game update. Scaled time is affected by slow motion, and the waiting routine resumes on an eligible later frame rather than exactly at a wall-clock deadline. RestoreFromCrumbleDeath relocks linear movement on its expected joints and stops pending coroutines, routines that can pause across frames.

Both routines check this flag when called. Setting it does not itself kill, crumble, restore, or remove the enemy. For example, changing it to false after crumbling also makes the recovery routine skip its joint cleanup; it does not rebuild the already loosened body.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BehaviourCrablet.enableJumpAttack
member.summary: Allows the combat AI to charge and choose an automatic Attack or FaceMount leap.

remarks.para: The normal combat decision checks this flag after its timing and unobstructed-target tests. Other conditions still matter, including target range, facing, jump charge, and body state. True permits that decision; it does not launch a jump by itself. The default is true.

The Jump routine and the ongoing airborne attack processing do not test this flag. Setting it to false therefore does not cancel a jump already launched, prevent a direct Jump call, or disable every navigation jump.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BehaviourCrablet.jumpCooldown
member.summary: Sets the time threshold, in scaled game seconds, used before the combat AI can consider another jump attack.

remarks.para: The default is 3 seconds. Increasing it delays automatic attack eligibility; decreasing it makes that check pass sooner. The check is currentTime - jumpTiming + 1.1 seconds >= jumpCooldown. Here currentTime is the current scaled game clock in seconds, and jumpTiming is the recorded launch clock plus a stun-related timing adjustment written by Jump. The 1.1-second term is a built-in offset in the eligibility test.

This is not an exact promise that two launches will be this many real seconds apart. Stun changes the recorded timing, slow motion changes the scaled clock, and AI checks occur at scheduled updates. Range, facing, charge, and target visibility can delay the next attack further. Direct Jump calls do not enforce this cooldown.

For example, with jumpTiming = 10 seconds, currentTime = 12 seconds, and jumpCooldown = 3 seconds, the test gives 12 - 10 + 1.1 = 3.1 seconds, which is at least 3 seconds. The timing gate permits the AI to consider an attack; the other conditions can still prevent a launch. The AI’s scheduling clock is unscaled, meaning slow motion does not change that clock, even though this eligibility test uses scaled game time.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Blip.Cache
member.summary: Returns the shared component-cache object for references.

remarks.para: A ComponentCache is a lookup table associating a GameObject, one scene object, with Blip references previously registered for it. A lookup returns the first stored Blip, or no result when that object has no entry or its stored list is empty; it does not discover an unregistered component. The first access creates a ComponentCache if _cache is null. Later accesses return the same stored object. The getter itself does not search the scene, collect active Blip components, or register this component; getting Cache therefore does not establish that every scene instance is present.
This cache is separate from the warning-only effect calls. CallSpawnEffect and CallDespawnEffect do not access it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Blip.ForceUsePreviewMesh
member.summary: Stores the old preference for using a preview mesh, with no mesh-selection effect in the current Blip effect calls.

remarks.para: A preview mesh is a saved surface shape for displaying an object. This component still exposes the preference, but CallSpawnEffect and CallDespawnEffect only log warnings and never choose a preview mesh, renderer, or collider. Setting this true does not make either method display a dissolve effect.

The Inspector description mentions choosing a preview mesh for objects with several physics bodies. That description explains the retained setting; it is not behavior implemented by these two methods in this build.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Blip.Renderers
member.summary: Stores references to components that draw the object; the current Blip effect calls leave them alone.

remarks.para: A Renderer is a Unity component that draws a visible surface. This saved array can identify several such components, but CallSpawnEffect and CallDespawnEffect do not read it, build a preview shape from it, or change whether those surfaces are visible. Adding a renderer here does not by itself add a spawn or despawn animation.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Blip.ThisCrate

remarks.para: A SpawnableCrate describes an object that can be created from game content; it is the asset description rather than an already spawned scene object. CallSpawnEffect and CallDespawnEffect do not read ThisCrate or fill it in. Assigning it does not make either method create that object or its visual effects.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Blip.ThisEntity
member.summary: Stores the scene-object reference associated with this Blip.

remarks.para: A MarrowEntity groups a game object’s interaction and physics parts. This reference identifies the object, rather than the SpawnableCrate asset from which an object may be created. CallSpawnEffect and CallDespawnEffect do not read or set ThisEntity, and calling the despawn-effect method does not remove that entity.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Blip._cache
member.summary: Stores the shared component-cache object returned by Cache.

remarks.para: A ComponentCache is a lookup table associating a GameObject, one scene object, with Blip references previously registered for it. A lookup returns the first stored Blip, or no result when that object has no entry or its stored list is empty; it does not discover an unregistered component. This field belongs to the type, so all Blip components share it. Cache creates a new ComponentCache when this reference is null, stores it here, and returns it. Setting _cache to null means the next Cache access creates a different cache; it does not preserve the old container automatically.
The Cache getter does not scan the scene or register Blip instances. CallSpawnEffect and CallDespawnEffect do not read or modify _cache.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Blip.fizzlerSpawnable

remarks.para: A Spawnable is a description of content to create, rather than an effect already playing in the scene. A prefab is a reusable saved object setup; saved scene or prefab settings can override that initial value.

CallDespawnEffect only logs its deprecation warning and does not pass this selection to a spawner. Changing fizzlerSpawnable therefore does not change what that method shows or sounds like. This statement describes the inspected Blip methods, rather than every possible external script.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Blip.forceBlip

Unity’s Inspector, the editor panel for component settings, hides this field, and its header says DO NOT SET IN INSPECTOR. Leave it unchanged in that panel and out of manual scene tuning. Treat it as stored component state rather than an animation switch supplied by these methods.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Blip.isDestructible

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Blip.spawnSpawnable

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BoardGenerator.ButtonDown
member.summary: Stored held-button state that keeps the placement-line coroutine running.

remarks.para: A coroutine is a sequence that can pause and resume over several frames.

PrimaryButtonDown sets it true before taking the first raycast and starting lineloop. PrimaryButtonUp sets it false before hiding the line and starting a board spawn. CeaseFire also clears it before hiding the line, but does not spawn a board.

The grip’s attached-hand input path uses the same state changes. Setting this field directly does not take the first shot, start a coroutine, hide the line, or perform the release spawn; use the action routines for those effects.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BoardGenerator.EndPoint
member.summary: Saved world position, in meters, of the most recent successful aim hit during the placement coroutine.

remarks.para: A coroutine is a sequence that can pause and resume over several frames.

lineloop replaces this on a hit and leaves it unchanged on a miss. The line’s second position and BoardSpawnerAsync use this saved value. Releasing does not perform a fresh raycast, and the point is not stored relative to EndRb, so it does not automatically follow that body while aiming.

The board spawn uses it to calculate gap, midpoint and orientation before waiting, but reads it again afterward for the second joint and endSFX position. Editing it during that wait can therefore change the final anchor without changing the already requested board placement.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BoardGenerator.EndRb
member.summary: The MarrowBody found on the latest successful aim hit, used as the board’s second connected body.

remarks.para: A MarrowBody is one physical piece. A Rigidbody is Unity’s component for simulating an object’s mass and motion, and a GameObject is the Unity object that carries components. A joint is a physics connection between objects. A coroutine is a sequence that can pause and resume over several frames.

lineloop looks for this through the hit rigidbody’s GameObject. A hit with no matching MarrowBody sets this to null, allowing a world anchor; a ray miss leaves the previous value unchanged. The coroutine waits for a physics update once, then uses ordinary frame pauses.

After the board finishes spawning, SetJoint converts EndPoint from world space to this body’s local coordinates when the body is live. With no live body, that saved world point is used directly for the connected anchor. Changing this field does not move a joint that already exists.
A physics update is one step of the physics simulation, separate from a frame that draws the view.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BoardGenerator.FirePoint
member.summary: Muzzle transform whose world position starts the targeting rays and whose forward direction determines where they aim.

remarks.para: PrimaryButtonDown and lineloop read it for their raycasts; RaycastDistance is the maximum travel in meters. Rotating this transform changes the aim direction for the next cast.

After a successful first shot, the initial line’s far position is the muzzle position; later successful aim hits replace that far position with EndPoint. This transform is not the board’s midpoint or either physical joint anchor.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BoardGenerator.FirstRb
member.summary: The MarrowBody found on the first anchor hit, used as the board’s first connected body.

remarks.para: A MarrowBody is one physical piece. A Rigidbody is Unity’s component for simulating an object’s mass and motion, and a GameObject is the Unity object that carries components. A joint is a physics connection between objects.

The first-shot raycast looks it up on the hit rigidbody’s GameObject. A successful hit without a matching MarrowBody stores null, allowing a world anchor. A first-shot miss leaves the old reference unchanged.

The saved firstPoint is a world position, not a point that follows this body while aiming. After the board spawns, SetJoint converts the saved point into this body’s local coordinates if the body is live; otherwise it uses the world point as the connected anchor.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BoardGenerator.LineMaterial
member.summary: Material assigned to the placement line during component initialization, controlling how that line is rendered.

remarks.para: Awake, Unity’s initialization callback (a routine called to initialize the component), assigns this to line after configuring two positions and its width. Changing this stored field later does not itself assign a new material to an already initialized renderer; update that renderer’s material too.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BoardGenerator.RaycastDistance
member.summary: Maximum targeting ray length in world-space meters for both the first anchor shot and later aim updates.

remarks.para: For example, an illustrative value of 5 permits ray hits up to 5 m from FirePoint along its forward direction, subject to layerMask. It limits each muzzle ray, not the gap between the two anchors or the board-length budget.
A ray miss does not clear saved anchor state. Increasing the range affects the next cast, while decreasing it can leave an older endpoint visible until another successful hit.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BoardGenerator.Valid
member.summary: Stored boolean that the inspected board-placement routines do not use as a hit-validity test.

remarks.para: The complete BoardGenerator methods and its board-spawn and line-update state machines do not calculate or read this field. First-shot and coroutine raycasts use their actual hit results; release starts spawning from saved values without consulting this flag.
Changing it alone is therefore not a verified way to approve, reject or clear a placement in those routines. Other code or mods can still read the stored value.
A coroutine is a sequence that can pause and resume over several frames.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BoardGenerator._grip
member.summary: Grip whose attachment callbacks supply holding state and primary-button input to this board generator.

remarks.para: A grip is the holdable handle. A callback is a routine called to report or handle an action, such as a hand attaching to that handle or changing its button input.

OnEnable subscribes three routines: attached-hand updates take the first shot on a press and start a board spawn on release, attachment shows laserPointer, and detachment hides it. OnDisable removes those subscriptions.

Set the reference before enabling. Replacing it while subscribed does not move the existing listeners to the new grip; preserve the old reference for unsubscription, then enable subscriptions on the new one.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BoardGenerator._mapActions
member.summary: Audio player used to request one of the start, completion or short-gap failure sounds at a world position.

remarks.para: The native constructor creates this player. PlaySFX forwards the chosen clip array and position to it; startSFX is requested at the first hit, endSFX after successful joint setup at the end point, and misfireSFX for a gap shorter than 10 cm at the generator.
The OnDisable routine only removes grip listeners and does not stop or release this player. Replacing the field does not cancel a request made through its previous value.

ManagedAudioPlayer is a sound-request helper, not the AudioPlayer that emits sound. When no matching AudioPlayer is already available, it requests a reusable player from the pool, a stash of reusable game objects; that request can continue into a later frame. While it is waiting, another sound request replaces the cached clip and playback settings instead of queueing a second sound. The position is used when the pooled player is requested; the later play step does not reposition it from a newer request.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BoardGenerator.ammoDistance
member.summary: Remaining board-length budget, measured in meters for the spawn length check when isUsingAmmo is true.

remarks.para: A callback is a routine called to report or handle an action. Here, OnBoardDestruction is called for the ObjectDestructible component’s OnDestruction notification when the breakable object reports its destruction.

The measured gap must be strictly smaller than this budget; a 2 m gap needs more than 2 m remaining, not exactly 2 m. On an allowed ammo-enabled placement, the gap is deducted before the async spawn is requested. This is a length budget rather than a count of boards.

OnBoardDestruction credits transform.localScale.z for an object present in destBoardHash. With the spawner’s unchanged matching scale that number represents the requested length, but custom prefab scale, later scale edits and repeated manual callback calls can change the credit. The routine does not remove the object from the set.

Disabling isUsingAmmo bypasses both this spawn check and deduction. Existing tracked boards can still credit this field when their callback runs, because the refund routine checks membership rather than that flag.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BoardGenerator.boardSpawnable
member.summary: Board assets registered for spawning during initialization and randomly selected when a placement is allowed.

remarks.para: A prefab is the object template used to create a board. A MarrowEntity groups an object’s physical pieces; a MarrowBody is one physical piece. A joint is a physics connection between objects. The refund callback is a routine called for the ObjectDestructible component’s OnDestruction notification.

Awake, Unity’s initialization callback (a routine called to initialize the component), registers every array entry with AssetSpawner. BoardSpawnerAsync chooses one random index after its gap and budget checks; provide a nonempty array of usable board spawnables.

The chosen prefab needs a MarrowEntity with at least one MarrowBody: the first body receives both connecting joints. Its forward direction and scale determine how it fits the requested gap. Ammo-enabled boards only get the refund callback when an ObjectDestructible is found on the spawned object.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BoardGenerator.breakforce
member.summary: Force threshold, in newtons, assigned to each new board joint’s breakForce setting.

remarks.para: breakTorque is the separate turning-force threshold for breaking a joint, measured in newton-meters (N·m).

A joint is a physics connection between objects. SetJoint copies this value into the configuration for both ends; the physics simulation can break a connection when its required force exceeds that threshold. Board destruction and its length refund are handled separately.

This is copied when a joint is created. Editing the generator field later does not update joints on boards already placed, and it does not set their breakTorque, the separate rotational breaking threshold.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BoardGenerator.destBoardHash
member.summary: Set of destructible objects recorded for the generator’s board-length refunds.

remarks.para: A callback is a routine called to report or handle an action. Here, OnBoardDestruction is called for the ObjectDestructible component’s OnDestruction notification when the breakable object reports its destruction.

Only the ammo-enabled spawn branch adds a found ObjectDestructible after installing its OnBoardDestruction callback and creating both joints. The free-placement branch does not add it. This set is not a complete list of every live board.

OnBoardDestruction checks membership before refunding but neither removes the object nor unregisters the callback. Old entries can remain, and manually calling the routine again for a tracked board refunds again. Adding or removing set entries alone does not add or remove the destruction subscription.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BoardGenerator.distance
member.summary: Stored distance value that is not maintained or used by the inspected board-placement code.

remarks.para: The complete BoardGenerator methods and its two state machines do not update or read this field. BoardSpawnerAsync instead calculates a fresh world-space gap between firstPoint and EndPoint in a local value for the 10 cm minimum, ammo check and requested scale.
Do not use this field as the current measured gap without calculating and assigning it yourself. Setting it does not change the spawn’s length or budget deduction in those routines.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BoardGenerator.endSFX
member.summary: Sound choices requested at EndPoint after a board has spawned and both endpoint joints have been set up.

remarks.para: A joint is a physics connection between objects. EndPoint is the saved second aim hit’s position in world coordinates, measured in meters.
PlaySFX asks _mapActions to choose one random clip from the array. This completion sound is used in both ammo-enabled and free-placement success branches.
Simply releasing, calling CeaseFire, or failing the budget check does not reach this request. Use a nonnull array; an empty array produces no clip in the inspected audio player.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BoardGenerator.enemyLayer
member.summary: Stored enemy layer index that is not used to filter the inspected targeting or board-spawn routines.

remarks.para: The native constructor stores layer index 12 here. The complete BoardGenerator methods and its two state machines do not read it; their targeting rays receive layerMask instead.

A layer index identifies one layer, while a layer mask combines layer bits. Changing this integer alone does not exclude or include enemies in those raycasts. Other code or mods can still inspect the stored value.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BoardGenerator.firstPoint
member.summary: Saved first anchor hit position in world-space meters, used as the line’s starting point and the board’s first attachment point.

remarks.para: A successful first-shot raycast replaces it; a miss leaves the previous value. It is saved in world space, so it does not automatically move with FirstRb while the next endpoint is being aimed.

BoardSpawnerAsync uses this with EndPoint to calculate gap, midpoint and forward direction. After waiting for the spawn, it reads the field again to create the first joint. Editing it during that wait can change the joint’s anchor without changing the placement already requested from the spawner.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BoardGenerator.isUsingAmmo
member.summary: Makes allowed board placements spend the remaining board-length budget and installs destruction refunds on suitable boards.

remarks.para: ObjectDestructible is the breakable-object component. Its destruction callback is a routine called for its OnDestruction notification. A joint is a physics connection between objects.

When true, a gap must be strictly smaller than ammoDistance, the remaining length in meters. The gap is deducted before requesting the spawn. After successful joint setup, a found ObjectDestructible receives OnBoardDestruction and is recorded in destBoardHash.

When false, the budget check, deduction and new refund subscription are skipped. The free branch requests the board’s spawn effect after joint setup. Both branches still reject a gap shorter than 10 cm and choose a random boardSpawnable.

Switching this off does not remove subscriptions or set entries installed on earlier boards. Those callbacks can still refund their recorded boards because OnBoardDestruction tests set membership rather than this flag.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BoardGenerator.laserPointer
member.summary: Separate aiming object shown when a hand attaches to the grip and hidden when the hand detaches.

remarks.para: Awake, Unity’s initialization callback (a routine called to initialize the component), initially deactivates it. The hand-attached callback activates it, and the hand-detached callback deactivates it.

This is separate from line, the placement renderer. CeaseFire hides line without changing this object, and OnDisable only unregisters grip callbacks. Provide the object before initialization and attachment actions run.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BoardGenerator.layerMask
member.summary: Layer-selection bit mask supplied to both the first-shot and the continuing aim raycasts.

remarks.para: Each set bit includes that physics layer in the ray test. This is a mask combining layers, not one layer index. For example, a mask containing only bit 8 selects layer 8; its integer value is 256, not 8.

The rays start at FirePoint and extend along its forward direction for RaycastDistance meters. The stored playerLayer and enemyLayer integers are not consulted by these inspected raycast paths, so configure exclusions in this mask.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BoardGenerator.line
member.summary: Two-position renderer that displays the board-placement line while the primary button is held.

remarks.para: Awake, Unity’s initialization callback (a routine called to initialize the component), adds a LineRenderer if this reference is absent, configures two positions and width, applies LineMaterial, and disables it. The first-shot routine enables it.

A successful first shot starts the line at firstPoint and ends it at FirePoint. Successful coroutine hits change its far end to EndPoint while keeping the saved first point. Misses leave the positions unchanged. PrimaryButtonUp and CeaseFire disable the renderer after clearing ButtonDown.

These routines pass world positions to SetPosition. Use a renderer configured to interpret its positions in world space; the inspected initialization does not set useWorldSpace. Replacing this field later does not repeat initialization on the new renderer.
A coroutine is a sequence that can pause and resume over several frames.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BoardGenerator.misfireSFX
member.summary: Sound choices requested when the saved anchor gap is shorter than 0.1 m, or 10 cm, and no board is spawned.

remarks.para: The request plays at the generator’s current world position through _mapActions, which chooses one random clip. A targeting ray miss does not itself play these clips, and an insufficient or exactly equal ammoDistance budget stops spawning silently in the inspected routine.
Provide a nonnull array; the inspected audio player skips playback for an empty array.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BoardGenerator.playerLayer
member.summary: Stored player layer index that is not used to exclude the player from the inspected targeting rays.

remarks.para: The native constructor stores layer index 8 here. The complete BoardGenerator methods and its board-spawn and line-update state machines do not read it. Their raycasts use layerMask directly.
Changing this integer alone does not change those raycast exclusions. A layer index names one layer; configure the layer-selection bits in layerMask to control which layers the rays can hit.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BoardGenerator.startSFX
member.summary: Sound choices requested at the saved first anchor point after a successful first-shot raycast.

remarks.para: PlaySFX passes the array and world hit position to _mapActions, which chooses one random clip. The held-button flag and enabled line are already set by then. A first-shot miss skips this sound request.
Provide a nonnull array; the inspected audio player skips playback for an empty array.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BoardGenerator.upDir
member.summary: Saved world-space surface normal from the first anchor hit, used to orient the board’s up direction.

remarks.para: A surface normal is the direction pointing straight out from the hit surface.
The first-shot raycast replaces this on a hit. A miss leaves the previous value. BoardSpawnerAsync uses it with the direction from firstPoint to EndPoint when building the board’s requested rotation.

It is a direction with no length units, not a position or a rotation in degrees. It stays in world space rather than following rotation of FirstRb, and it is not updated from the second endpoint’s surface normal.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BoardGenerator.vfxBlasterSpawnable
member.summary: Stored effect-spawnable reference that the inspected board-generator firing routines do not spawn.

remarks.para: The complete BoardGenerator methods and its board-spawn and line-update state machines do not read this field. Changing it alone is therefore not a verified way to add a muzzle effect to those routines.
The free-placement branch does request the spawned board entity’s own spawn effect; that request is separate from this stored reference. Other code or mods can still use the asset held here.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BodyVitals.beltFlipped
member.summary: Chooses whether flippable belt slots are mirrored across the player’s left/right center plane.

remarks.para: ApplyUILayoutSettings passes this value to Inventory.FlipSlot. For each ready normal slot marked flippable, true uses the negative of its cached angle around the torso; false restores the cached angle. For example, an eligible slot at +90 degrees becomes −90 degrees. Slots not marked flippable keep their angle.

Assigning this property stores the preference. Call PROPEGATE_SOFT, or PROPEGATE if body measurements also changed, to copy it to the live player systems. The player, active avatar, UI rig, tutorial rig, and inventory must already be set up.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BodyVitals.bodyLogEnabled
member.summary: Controls whether the applied Body Log device runs its normal pull-cord update behavior.

remarks.para: PROPEGATE_SOFT copies this flag into the expected PullCordDevice. False disables its ball handle immediately and makes its normal Update return early; true allows that update to run. The ball handle is the part the player pulls to choose an avatar. This is separate from hasBodyLog, which controls whether the device’s whole object is active.

Assigning this property stores the preference. Call PROPEGATE_SOFT, or PROPEGATE if body measurements also changed, to copy it to the live player systems. The player, active avatar, UI rig, tutorial rig, and inventory must already be set up.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BodyVitals.bodyLogFlipped
member.summary: Chooses the Body Log’s inventory side and reverses the pull-cord device’s local orientation.

remarks.para: ApplyUILayoutSettings uses true to select the left lower-arm region for ready special inventory slots, and false for the right lower-arm region. During PROPEGATE_SOFT, the pull-cord device gets a local Y rotation of 0 degrees for true or 180 degrees for false, relative to its parent. Its reach check uses the opposite hand: right for true and left for false.

Assigning this property stores the preference. Call PROPEGATE_SOFT, or PROPEGATE if body measurements also changed, to copy it to the live player systems. The player, active avatar, UI rig, tutorial rig, and inventory must already be set up.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BodyVitals.chestCircumference
member.summary: The real-world distance around the player’s chest, in meters, used to shape the calibrated torso.

remarks.para: CalibratePlayerBodyScale divides this circumference by its estimated player eye height to get a size relative to eye height. The eye-height estimate uses realWorldHeight, the real player’s full standing height from floor to top of head in meters, divided by the template’s cached full-height/eye-height ratio, which has no units. The resulting circumference ratio also has no units. underbustCircumference is the distance around the torso just below the chest, in meters. Compared with that measurement, chest circumference adjusts the template’s chest bulge depth.

For example, store 0.90 for a 90-centimeter circumference; store the distance around the body, not its width or radius. Assigning a measurement stores it; CalibratePlayerBodyScale applies the measurements to the player template. PROPEGATE runs that calibration and then updates the UI and controller settings. The player template is the body description used to relate real tracked movement to the current avatar.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BodyVitals.hasBodyLog
member.summary: Controls whether the expected Body Log device object is made active when preferences are applied.

remarks.para: PROPEGATE_SOFT looks for a PullCordDevice under the first special inventory slot. If it finds one, it calls SetActive with this flag: true activates the object and false deactivates it. This stored flag is copied from saved unlock progress, but it is not a live check that an object currently exists. Setting true does not create or spawn a missing device.

Assigning this property stores the preference. Call PROPEGATE_SOFT, or PROPEGATE if body measurements also changed, to copy it to the live player systems. The player, active avatar, UI rig, tutorial rig, and inventory must already be set up.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BodyVitals.hipsCircumference
member.summary: The real-world distance around the player’s hips, in meters, used to shape the calibrated torso.

remarks.para: CalibratePlayerBodyScale divides this circumference by its estimated player eye height to get a size relative to eye height. The eye-height estimate uses realWorldHeight, the real player’s full standing height from floor to top of head in meters, divided by the template’s cached full-height/eye-height ratio, which has no units. The resulting circumference ratio also has no units. It sets hip widths and front/back depths, and contributes to the shape between the waist and hips.

For example, store 0.90 for a 90-centimeter circumference; store the distance around the body, not its width or radius. Assigning a measurement stores it; CalibratePlayerBodyScale applies the measurements to the player template. PROPEGATE runs that calibration and then updates the UI and controller settings. The player template is the body description used to relate real tracked movement to the current avatar.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BodyVitals.inseam
member.summary: The player’s real-world crotch-to-floor leg measurement, stored in meters for the calibration call.

remarks.para: The player template is the body description used to relate tracked real movement to the avatar. realWorldHeight measures the player’s full standing height from floor to top of head, in meters. CalibratePlayerBodyScale passes inseam and realWorldHeight, both in meters, to the player template’s matching limb-measurement setter. The built-in RealHeptaAvatar setter is empty in this build, so changing this field does not change its limb proportions through that call. The settings loader still copies the saved measurement into this field.
For example, 0.80 represents an 80-centimeter inseam. Storing the value alone does not perform calibration or save it to disk.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BodyVitals.isRightHanded
member.summary: Selects the handedness used to divide movement and secondary controls between the two controllers.

remarks.para: PROPEGATE_SOFT copies this into the controller rig. Its input processing uses true for primary movement on the left controller and secondary controls on the right; false swaps those roles. It also affects which controller supplies forward direction in controller-relative movement mode.

The propagation pass chooses the direction-reference controller before copying the new handedness. If changing handedness while using controller-relative movement, apply the preferences again so that direction selection sees the new value. Assigning this property stores the preference. Call PROPEGATE_SOFT, or PROPEGATE if body measurements also changed, to copy it to the live player systems. The player, active avatar, UI rig, tutorial rig, and inventory must already be set up.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BodyVitals.loco_CurveMode
member.summary: Chooses the curve that reshapes the direction of primary movement input. Turning speed is set separately by .

remarks.para: The choices are Linear = 0, Poles = 1, GenesisDpad = 2, Dpad = 3, SmoothGenesis = 4, and SmoothDpad = 5. PROPEGATE_SOFT selects the controller rig’s matching configured curve; an out-of-range value leaves its previous curve selected.

The curve’s horizontal axis is the signed input angle, in degrees, from straight forward on the stick or pad. Its vertical axis is the resulting movement angle, also in degrees. The direction curve receives the processed input’s signed angle in degrees, not its distance from the center. Its output changes the processed movement vector’s angle while preserving that vector’s unitless magnitude (its distance from the center). Earlier MagnitudeRemapAxis processing can change the raw stick or pad deflection before the curve runs. For example, a curve mapping 30 degrees to 0 degrees makes that angled input move straight forward. Actual behavior depends on the configured curve points. Assigning this property stores the preference. Call PROPEGATE_SOFT, or PROPEGATE if body measurements also changed, to copy it to the live player systems. The player, active avatar, UI rig, tutorial rig, and inventory must already be set up.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BodyVitals.loco_DegreesPerSnap
member.summary: Controls smooth-turn speed and snap-turn smoothing speed, despite its name.

remarks.para: PROPEGATE_SOFT copies this value into the controller rig’s turning-speed parameter. In smooth mode, the nominal speed is value × 48 + 60 degrees per second, multiplied by processed stick input and adjusted by the rig’s time-scale compensation. Here value is the stored speed setting and has no units. Processed stick input is the signed sideways stick value after ignoring small movements near the center, rescaling the remainder, and smoothing it; it also has no units. Time scale is the game-time multiplier, with 1 meaning normal speed. The rig adjusts each update’s time contribution during slow motion, so actual rotation also depends on elapsed update time in seconds. For example, value 5 gives a nominal 300 degrees per second at full processed input.

For snap turns, the smoothing-time parameter is 0.2 / value + 0.01 seconds. Here value is this dimensionless speed setting; the resulting time controls how quickly the remaining turn is reduced, rather than guaranteeing an exact completion time. A larger positive value makes the snap settle faster. The snap’s total angle is selected by loco_SnapDegreesPerFrame: 1, 2, 3, and 4 choose 15, 30, 45, and 90 degrees. Assigning this property stores the preference. Call PROPEGATE_SOFT, or PROPEGATE if body measurements also changed, to copy it to the live player systems. The player, active avatar, UI rig, tutorial rig, and inventory must already be set up.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BodyVitals.loco_Direction
member.summary: Chooses the reference orientation for forward movement.

remarks.para: PROPEGATE_SOFT selects Controller = 0, Head = 1, or Custom = 2. Controller uses the primary-movement controller: left when the rig is right-handed, right when left-handed. Head uses the tracked head orientation. Custom uses the controller rig’s CustomDirection object. The selected orientation tells movement input what “forward” means before the result is expressed relative to the player body’s own forward and right directions.

For example, in Head mode, pushing forward follows where the head faces; in Controller mode, it follows the movement hand’s orientation. An invalid selector leaves the previous reference selected. Assigning this property stores the preference. Call PROPEGATE_SOFT, or PROPEGATE if body measurements also changed, to copy it to the live player systems. The player, active avatar, UI rig, tutorial rig, and inventory must already be set up.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BodyVitals.loco_SnapDegreesPerFrame
member.summary: Selects snap turning, smooth turning, or no new thumbstick turn input; it is not a degrees-per-frame amount.

remarks.para: The controller input code uses 1 for a 15-degree snap, 2 for 30 degrees, 3 for 45 degrees, 4 for 90 degrees, and 5 for smooth turning. Other values do not select a new turn in that thumbstick-processing branch. For example, 3 requests 45-degree turns when the stick passes the snap threshold; it does not rotate 3 degrees every frame. On this input branch, a snap requires absolute sideways deflection of 0.65 or greater while absolute vertical deflection is below 0.5; it rearms when absolute sideways deflection is below 0.4. These are unitless stick values (0 is center), not angles or seconds.

Snap turns are spread over updates by the rig’s smoothing routine. Their smoothing speed comes from loco_DegreesPerSnap. Assigning this property stores the preference. Call PROPEGATE_SOFT, or PROPEGATE if body measurements also changed, to copy it to the live player systems. The player, active avatar, UI rig, tutorial rig, and inventory must already be set up.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BodyVitals.measurementPresets
member.summary: Records the size-preset label loaded with the player’s measurements.

remarks.para: The labels are CUSTOM = 0, XSMALL = 1, SMALL = 2, MEDIUM = 3, LARGE = 4, XLARGE = 5, XXLARGE = 6, and XXXLARGE = 7. These are choices with no measurement units. The settings UI uses the saved preset to estimate torso circumferences, then the settings loader copies the resulting measurements and this label into BodyVitals.

Changing this BodyVitals property alone does not regenerate the circumference fields: neither calibration nor either propagation method reads the label. For example, writing LARGE here does not automatically replace a stored waist circumference with a large-preset estimate.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BodyVitals.mod_globalHaptic
member.summary: Multiplies the strength of vibration sent through both controller haptic components.

remarks.para: A haptic is a controller vibration. PROPEGATE_SOFT copies this dimensionless multiplier to both Haptor components. Their send routine first limits requested intensity to 0–1, then multiplies it by this value before passing it to the controller. For example, requested intensity 0.8 with multiplier 0.5 becomes 0.4; multiplier 0 produces a zero intensity request.

The multiplier itself is not clamped in this propagation path. The applied strength still depends on the controller and the particular vibration request. Assigning this property stores the preference. Call PROPEGATE_SOFT, or PROPEGATE if body measurements also changed, to copy it to the live player systems. The player, active avatar, UI rig, tutorial rig, and inventory must already be set up.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BodyVitals.quickmenuEnabled
member.summary: Allows the normal controller-button path to open and operate the quick menu after settings are applied.

remarks.para: PROPEGATE_SOFT copies the flag into the controller rig. UIControllerInput checks that applied flag: when false and the popup menu is closed, its menu-input update returns before the normal opening code. When true, the normal button/hold opening path can run. This is permission to respond to input, not a request to open the menu immediately.

Assigning this property stores the preference. Call PROPEGATE_SOFT, or PROPEGATE if body measurements also changed, to copy it to the live player systems. The player, active avatar, UI rig, tutorial rig, and inventory must already be set up.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BodyVitals.realWorldHeight
member.summary: The player’s real-world full standing height, in meters, used to scale tracked movement to the active avatar.

remarks.para: For example, 1.75 means 175 centimeters. CalibratePlayerBodyScale stores this on the player template and estimates player eye height by dividing it by the template’s cached full-height/eye-height ratio. The full-height/eye-height ratio is already stored on the template when calibration starts and is reused by this call. The tracking root is the object whose scale adjusts how tracked headset and controller motion fits the avatar. Calibration applies uniform scale, meaning one multiplier on all three axes. That multiplier is active avatar eye height divided by the estimated player eye height; both heights are in meters and the resulting scale has no units. The same eye-height estimate makes the torso circumferences relative to body size.

The Unity Inspector shows a range of 1–2.1 meters. That editor range does not clamp values assigned through the proxy. Use valid positive heights because calibration divides by the height estimate. Assigning a measurement stores it; CalibratePlayerBodyScale applies the measurements to the player template. PROPEGATE runs that calibration and then updates the UI and controller settings. The player template is the body description used to relate real tracked movement to the current avatar.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BodyVitals.rescaleEvent
member.summary: The no-argument functions notified after popup-position and tutorial-scale updates during UI layout application.

remarks.para: A callback is a function called when a piece of work reaches a chosen point. ApplyUILayoutSettings invokes this list after updating the popup starting position and tutorial scale, before moving open inventory slots back to their panel targets and before inventory flips. It only reaches this notification when the active-avatar, UI-rig, and tutorial-rig block runs.

PROPEGATE_SOFT performs two layout passes, so callbacks can run twice during one call. CalibratePlayerBodyScale alone does not invoke this list. Add and remove handlers through add_rescaleEvent and remove_rescaleEvent; assigning this proxy property directly replaces the stored callback list.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BodyVitals.slowTimeEnabled

Do not use this value as the current slow-motion state. This description is limited to the inspected BodyVitals methods; other systems can have their own ability controls.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BodyVitals.uiScaling

That ratio has no units and is multiplied by the UI rig’s separate uiScale setting, also without units.

For example, writing 2 here and calling ApplyUILayoutSettings does not double the menus through that method. This statement covers the inspected BodyVitals implementation rather than every possible external script.

member.summary: The player’s real-world fingertip-to-fingertip span with the arms stretched out, stored in meters for the calibration call.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BonelabGameControl.CompleteOnLoad
member.summary: Records this level as completed when the controller’s level-load callback runs.

remarks.para: A callback is a function saved to run when another operation reaches a stage. Start, Unity’s startup call, registers this work with the scene loader. The callback attempts inventory and ammunition restoration first when that feature is enabled, clears IsResuming, then checks this setting.

When true, it writes completion for LevelKey even if SaveFeatures does not include Completion. It does not reset saved progress or request a file write. For example, use it when simply entering a level should satisfy its completion requirement; leave it false when an objective must be finished first.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BonelabGameControl.FadeoutVFXOverride
member.summary: Selects an optional fade effect to spawn before the controller loads another level.

remarks.para: A crate reference identifies an asset in BONELAB’s asset warehouse. The level-jump path chooses this spawnable reference when its barcode, the asset’s identifier, is accepted; with no usable override, it uses the runtime default fade-out effect.

The chosen asset must contain a FadeVolume component, which manages the fade and exposes a completion action. After the effect successfully spawns, the controller connects that action to the level-load request. The spawn request itself does not mean the next level has loaded.

For example, assign a fade effect asset to customize the transition. Changing this property after a jump has already requested its effect does not replace that effect, and an override without FadeVolume cannot complete this controller’s normal transition hookup.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BonelabGameControl.HubLevel
member.summary: Provides the BONELAB Hub asset reference used for the controller’s initial level-jump destination.

remarks.para: A level crate reference identifies a level asset in BONELAB’s asset warehouse. The controller initially puts this shared Hub reference at index 0 of LevelJumpList, so the default jump index selects it unless that list is changed.

The jump method also creates a Hub destination when the requested list index is invalid or the list is absent. For example, keep HubLevel as the first entry to make an index-0 exit return to the Hub. Reading this reference does not start loading a scene.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BonelabGameControl.InventorySaveFilter
member.summary: Applies optional replacement rules to saved item identifiers during inventory restoration.

remarks.para: The filter maps an item barcode, its asset identifier in BONELAB’s warehouse, to a replacement barcode. A configured replacement changes the identifier used to request a restored inventory-slot item; an identifier without a rule stays unchanged. An empty or invalid result can cause an item entry to be skipped.

Start, Unity’s startup call, registers a level-load callback. When that callback runs with the Inventory save feature enabled, it passes the assigned filter to the restoration helper. The filter prepares its replacement lookup when the filter asset is enabled; change and enable the asset’s configuration before restoration so the lookup contains the intended rules.

For example, replace a saved weapon’s identifier with another weapon’s identifier to control what appears in an inventory slot. The separate left- and right-hand item-spawn branches still construct their spawn asset from the original saved identifier after checking the filtered result, so this is not a guarantee that held-item replacements use the new asset. This controller does not apply the filter when gathering inventory to save.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BonelabGameControl.IsResuming
member.summary: Reports whether startup is currently using the saved-checkpoint resume path.

remarks.para: Awake, Unity’s initialization call, starts with this false. It becomes true only when PartialProgress is enabled, the saved checkpoint number is nonzero, and TemporaryLoadData.ResumeFromSave requests resuming. The flag helps the inventory and ammunition helpers choose resume data instead of fresh-visit data.

The level-load callback requests restoration, then sets this false before checking CompleteOnLoad. Item spawning can finish later while the game continues running. Therefore, false does not prove every restored item has appeared, and true does not prove the player teleport has already been applied.

For example, a saved checkpoint of 2 with a resume request selects the resume path; checkpoint 0 does not. Changing the property’s stored flag does not itself register loading work, move the player, or restore inventory.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BonelabGameControl.LevelJumpList
member.summary: Supplies the level assets selected by the controller’s numbered level-jump methods.

remarks.para: The jump number is a zero-based list index: 0 chooses the first reference, 1 the second. A level crate reference identifies a level asset in BONELAB’s asset warehouse. The initial list contains only HubLevel at index 0.

A negative number, a number at or beyond the list length, or an absent list makes the jump choose its Hub fallback. A valid index selects the entry as stored, so configure usable references. The fade effect must spawn and signal completion before the scene-load request is made.

For example, put HubLevel first and a custom level second, then use jump index 1 for the custom level. NextLevel’s text save key does not select entries in this list. Once a jump has captured a destination, later list edits do not change that pending transition.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BonelabGameControl.LevelKey
member.summary: Identifies which level’s saved completion, checkpoint, object state, and inventory records this controller reads or changes.

remarks.para: This is a text save identifier, not a scene filename, display title, or asset reference. Awake, Unity’s initialization call, rejects a null, empty, or whitespace-only key. Completion and checkpoint writes, fresh-visit cleanup, and inventory finalization use this key.

Configure a stable key before initialization. For example, keep the same key for repeated visits to a level so its saved checkpoint can be found again; changing the key later redirects later save operations but does not automatically reload the live Progress value. The inventory-load path treats the built-in keys "Hub_A", "Hub_B", and "Hub_C" as "Hub" for item records; completion, checkpoint, and ammunition operations still use the configured key.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BonelabGameControl.NextLevel
member.summary: Names the next level’s save record that receives starting inventory during finalization.

remarks.para: This is a text level key in progression data, not a level crate reference. With the Inventory save feature enabled, FinalizeInventory gathers carried-item identifiers and prepares starting inventory under this key and the Hub key. A null, empty, or whitespace-only key skips that transfer.

For example, set it to the save key used by the level that should receive your carried items. It does not choose a scene to load: the jump path selects its destination from LevelJumpList. FinalizeInventory also does not write the active save to a file by itself.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BonelabGameControl.PriorLevels
member.summary: Lists earlier level save keys used to choose inherited inventory and work out starting ammunition.

remarks.para: Each entry is a text identifier in saved progression data. With Inventory enabled, the level-load work checks current-level inventory first, then can search earlier levels’ final-inventory records from the end of this list toward the beginning. It also passes these keys to the ammunition-restoration helper.

The ammunition helper builds a starting number of rounds for each type from these levels’ saved final-ammunition changes, in the order listed. Already loaded count dictionaries are added per type. Records deserialized from JSON, a text save-data format, are merged with the counts built so far by keeping the larger value per type instead of adding them. FinalizeInventory calculates this level’s new change as current rounds minus that starting number. Ammunition counts are whole numbers of rounds, grouped by ammunition type. For example, 50 current rounds minus a calculated 60 starting rounds gives -10 rounds. This list therefore affects carried supplies, rather than deciding whether a level is completed or which scene loads next.

Provide a list even when there are no earlier levels; an empty list is useful for a standalone level. For example, list the earlier campaign levels in play order so the inventory fallback starts with the most recent one. For the item-inventory lookup, the load path changes earlier keys "Hub_A", "Hub_B", and "Hub_C" to "Hub". Ammunition restoration and finalization use the earlier keys as supplied.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BonelabGameControl.Progress
member.summary: Stores the current checkpoint-list index loaded from the save or changed through SetProgress.

remarks.para: This is a whole-number index with no physical unit: 0 selects the first ProgressionPoint, 1 the second, and 2 the third. It is not a percentage. Awake, Unity’s initialization call, reads saved progress when PartialProgress is enabled; a missing or unusable saved number becomes 0.

TeleportToProgress, ResumeProgress, and inventory setup use this number to select a point. Use SetProgress to record an advance: when PartialProgress is enabled and the requested index differs from the current value, it first stores the new live index. For a valid point it then runs its reached event when configured: the actions set up to run when the point is reached, with no arguments passed to them. It writes saved progress afterward. The property’s underlying setter only stores the number and does not perform those actions.

SetCompleted can reset the saved number to 0 without changing this live value. No clamping makes an invalid live index safe for resuming. For example, with three configured points, use indices 0, 1, and 2; reordering the list also changes what an existing saved number refers to.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BonelabGameControl.ProgressionPoint
member.summary: Maps saved checkpoint numbers to player placement, item locations, and scene-object changes.

remarks.para: Progress selects an entry by zero-based list index: Progress = 2 means the third entry, not 2 percent complete. A point supplies a spawnLocation for the player’s feet and facing, item-placement transforms for left and right hands, an optional death checkpoint, object arrays to disable and enable, and an event for reaching that progress number.

A Transform stores an object’s position and rotation. TeleportToProgress queues the player’s feet to spawnLocation’s world position, measured from the scene’s origin in Unity world units. The native path does not convert its scale or establish how many Unity world units equal a metre. Facing comes from that Transform’s forward direction, its blue Z axis expressed in world coordinates; this direction has no distance unit. The rig manager, which coordinates the player’s body objects, applies the queued move during EarlyUpdate, its early update each frame. A frame is one round of game updates. ResumeProgress sets the selected death checkpoint, disables the configured objects, then enables the configured objects. The inventory-load work also reads the selected hand-item locations when the index is valid.

When PartialProgress is enabled and the requested index differs from the current one, SetProgress stores the new live Progress before invoking the selected point’s configured OnReachedResumePoint event for a valid index. This reached event is a set of actions configured to run when the point is reached, with no arguments passed to them. Saved progress is written afterward; ResumeProgress does not invoke the event. Configure the list before loading, keep saved indices in range, supply spawn locations, and use empty object arrays rather than missing arrays. For example, the third point can place the player beyond a door and disable the spawners from the preceding section.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BonelabGameControl.RegisteredSaveables
member.summary: Holds configured records pairing scene objects that support saving with their unique save identifiers.

remarks.para: Each record contains a Saveable component, an object’s save-data component, and its UniqueId text identifier. The property stores the list as supplied, so replacing it changes the configured records available through this controller.

The base BonelabGameControl startup, checkpoint, completion, inventory, and jump methods do not register or serialize this list. For example, adding an object-and-identifier pair here does not by itself restore that object’s state; code that handles these records must perform the registration or restoration. This is separate from FinalizeInventory’s gathering of the player’s carried items.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BonelabGameControl.SaveFeatures
member.summary: Selects the controller’s completion saving, checkpoint resuming, and inventory-and-ammunition behavior.

remarks.para: These options can be combined: Completion is 1, PartialProgress is 2, Inventory is 4, and Everything is 7, meaning all three together. The controller initially selects Everything. The numbers are option bits, not physical measurements.

PartialProgress allows loading the saved checkpoint in Awake, Unity’s initialization call, queueing its teleport, and recording changes through SetProgress. Completion allows SetCompleted to write completion. Inventory allows the load callback to restore items and ammunition and allows FinalizeInventory to prepare their carryover.

The Completion option does not block CompleteOnLoad: that setting’s load callback writes completion independently. JustSave also makes its save request independently of these options. For example, combine Completion and PartialProgress for objective and checkpoint saving without this controller restoring carried inventory.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.BonelabGameControl._isLoadCalled
member.summary: Prevents this controller’s level-jump path from starting another transition after its first request.

remarks.para: The jump method returns immediately when this flag is true. On the first call, it sets the flag before checking the requested list index or choosing and spawning the fade effect. Later calls are therefore ignored even if the first transition has not completed.

This records that a request started, not that a new level successfully loaded. The base jump path does not clear it after a failed effect spawn or a missing FadeVolume component. FadeVolume is the spawned component that manages the screen fade and runs the connected level-load action when fading completes. For example, pressing an exit trigger twice starts one transition attempt; a stalled first attempt is not automatically retried by the second call.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ButtonHoverClick.clipToPlay
member.summary: Selects a default sound-list entry when the current audio category uses single mode.

remarks.para: This integer is a zero-based list index, not an AudioClip object, a time, or a universal sound ID. For example, 2 means the third entry in whichever list is active: Hover, Click, Confirm, or Deny.

The audio provider's mode for that category controls whether this value matters. Random mode chooses its own index; order mode advances its saved sequence counter; single mode uses clipToPlay. The same number can select different sounds in different category lists.

In single mode, use a nonnegative value smaller than the active list's entry count. An invalid index causes an index error before any override is substituted. An empty list produces no audio, even with an override. The methods read this value on each call; changing it does not immediately play a sound.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ButtonHoverClick.clip_override_click
member.summary: Replaces the selected ordinary click sound when confirmer is false.

remarks.para: This is an AudioClip reference: the sound recording to play. Leave it empty to keep the default sound selected from clips_Click on feedback_audio. Assigning the clip does not play it immediately; CLICK reads it during feedback.

The default clips_Click list must still exist and contain an entry. Its mode selects and validates an index before this override is considered. In single mode, clipToPlay must still be within that list even when the override is assigned. An empty list skips audio; an invalid index causes an error.

This changes only the sound recording. It does not change controller vibration or the audio provider's loudness and spatial settings. Playback uses this button's world position at the time of the call and does not follow the button afterward.
