member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ButtonHoverClick.confirmer
member.summary: Makes use confirmation audio instead of ordinary click audio.

remarks.para: True selects feedback_audio's clips_Confirm list and clip_override_confirmer. False selects clips_Click and clip_override_click. The selected category also supplies its own random, order, or single selection mode.

The flag is checked during each CLICK call, so changing it affects the next call without rerunning setup. It does not immediately play a sound, change the click vibration, or determine whether the button's action is allowed.
Hover feedback still uses the hover category, and LOCKED still uses denial feedback, regardless of this flag.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ButtonHoverClick.feedback_audio
member.summary: Provides the sound lists, selection modes, and playback settings for this button's feedback.

remarks.para: HIGHLIGHT selects Hover sounds, LOCKED selects Deny sounds, and CLICK selects Click or Confirm sounds according to confirmer. The button passes clipToPlay and the matching optional AudioClip override to that selection. The provider must have a nonempty matching list even when an override is assigned.
Sound is requested at this button's world position when feedback runs, and does not follow it afterward. The provider's settings decide loudness and whether position affects what the listener hears.

The setup check fills this reference from the main UI rig only when it is missing; it preserves a provider you assigned yourself. That check runs from the level-load callback and on pointer entry. A callback is a function saved for another system to run when an event occurs. The level callback can run during Awake if loading is already done; Awake is Unity's early component setup method.

Direct CLICK, HIGHLIGHT, and LOCKED calls do not perform that lookup. If this reference is missing, they skip audio while still allowing their tactile request. Swapping the reference affects subsequent calls, rather than stopping a sound already requested.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ButtonHoverClick.feedback_tactile
member.summary: Enables the controller-vibration channel for this button's hover, click, and denial feedback.

remarks.para: Tactile feedback means vibration you can feel in the controller. HIGHLIGHT and LOCKED use the controller's configured subtle pattern. CLICK uses its press-click pattern, including when confirmer chooses confirmation audio.

These calls supply no controller argument, so they use the controller currently marked active by the in-game UI. The vibration pattern settings belong to that controller's Haptor, its vibration driver. Missing active-controller or driver references leave no device to receive the request.

The setup check fills a missing reference from the main UI rig and preserves one you assigned yourself. It runs through the level-load callback and on pointer entry. A callback is a function another system runs for an event; the load callback may run during initial setup if loading has already finished.

Direct CLICK, HIGHLIGHT, and LOCKED calls do not look up a missing provider. A missing tactile reference skips vibration and leaves audio available. Changing this reference does not itself send a vibration or select a different hand.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ChallengeSelectMenu.OnChallengeCanceled
member.summary: Stores the event called by CancelCurrentChallenge to let connected actions handle cancellation.

remarks.para: A UnityEvent is a list of actions that a scene author can connect in Unity's Inspector. These events take no arguments, so listeners receive no challenge number or enemy-count value directly.

CancelCurrentChallenge checks whether this event is assigned before invoking it. That method leaves the menu's saved indices and controller selection unchanged by itself; actions connected here provide any arena stop, selection reset, or screen change.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ChallengeSelectMenu.OnChallengeSelected
member.summary: Stores the confirmation event called before the optional enemy-count goal is applied.

remarks.para: A UnityEvent is a list of actions that a scene author can connect in Unity's Inspector. These events take no arguments, so listeners receive no challenge number or enemy-count value directly.

OnChallengeSelect refreshes the active challenge title first, invokes this event if assigned, then checks updateEnemyCount and sends the stored count to the controller. SelectChallenge alone does not call this event. A listener reading the profile during this event sees the state before that following enemy-count configuration step.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ChallengeSelectMenu.OnChallengeStarted
member.summary: Stores the per-challenge events from which ChallengeStarted chooses one by challengeID.

remarks.para: A UnityEvent is a list of actions that a scene author can connect in Unity's Inspector. These events take no arguments, so listeners receive no challenge number or enemy-count value directly.

The array order must match the challenge indices: element 0 is for challenge 0, element 1 for challenge 1, and so on. ChallengeStarted invokes only the selected element. Assign the array and every event that can be selected; missing or out-of-range entries cause the lookup or call to fail.
These are actions to invoke, not a record that a challenge is currently running. A connected action may start gameplay, but the menu method itself only calls the event.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ChallengeSelectMenu.OnLoadoutSelected
member.summary: Stores the shared callback that receives the saved loadout index when OnLoadoutSelect is called.

remarks.para: A callback is a method called to react to a notification. This static Action<int> is shared by all ChallengeSelectMenu instances, and its integer argument is the notifying menu's loadID at that moment.

SelectLoadout only stores a new loadID. OnLoadoutSelect separately checks whether this callback exists and, if so, invokes it with that saved number. For example, selecting index 2 and then notifying sends 2; this notification does not itself prove that any items were equipped.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ChallengeSelectMenu.activeChallengeText
member.summary: Stores the label that OnChallengeSelect fills with the assigned challenge's display title.

remarks.para: The title comes from arenaGameController.assignedRoundProfile.displayTitle when OnChallengeSelect runs. When the label exists, OnChallengeSelect also requires a valid arenaGameController and its assigned challenge profile; otherwise the method fails before the selection event. A profile holds stored challenge settings. The label is optional: if it is missing, that method still reaches its event and optional enemy-count step.
It is a saved display, not a live lookup. SelectChallenge updates the description labels but does not refresh this title, so it can keep the previous title until OnChallengeSelect is called.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ChallengeSelectMenu.arenaGameController
member.summary: Stores the whose challenge profiles, difficulty, and enemy-count settings this menu reads or configures.

remarks.para: Start and SelectChallenge ask this controller to choose a profile. OnChallengeSelect reads its assigned profile title and can configure a concurrent-enemy goal; UpdateDiffText reads its difficulty. These uses connect menu choices to the arena's stored settings.

Assigning this reference does not itself select or start a challenge. Start and SelectChallenge can skip controller selection when it is absent, while text and count operations that read its profile require it to be assigned.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ChallengeSelectMenu.chalDescriptionTexts
member.summary: Stores the labels that all receive the currently chosen profile's description.

remarks.para: Start selects profile 0, and SelectChallenge selects the requested profile; each copies that profile's descriptionText into every label in this array. It is not one different description per array slot.
Assign the array before those methods run. An empty array skips text updates; every entry in a nonempty array must be a valid text label. Changing the array alone does not fill its new labels.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ChallengeSelectMenu.challengeID
member.summary: Stores the menu's selected challenge number, also used to choose its start event.

remarks.para: The number is a zero-based index: 0 means the first challenge. SelectChallenge writes it before requesting that controller profile, and Start normally initializes it to 0. ChallengeStarted uses it to index OnChallengeStarted.

Assigning this value directly does not select the controller's profile, refresh labels, or send a selection event. Keep it consistent with the controller profile list and the start-event array. An invalid selection can leave this stored value changed even when a later lookup fails.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ChallengeSelectMenu.diffDescriptions
member.summary: Stores the difficulty-description strings that UpdateDiffText indexes with the controller's difficulty.

remarks.para: When this component is created, its constructor (creation-time setup code) creates five entries for EASY, MEDIUM, HARD, HARDER, and HARDEST, in that order. The difficulty numbers are 0 through 4. UpdateDiffText copies the matching string into difficultyDescText.

Replacing these strings changes what a later refresh can show; it does not change gameplay difficulty or immediately repaint the label. Keep enough entries for every difficulty number the controller can use.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ChallengeSelectMenu.difficultyDescText
member.summary: Stores the optional label refreshed from the arena controller's current difficulty description.

remarks.para: UpdateDiffText fills this label from diffDescriptions using the controller's difficulty number. For example, difficulty HARD = 2 uses the third description string.
If this label is missing, UpdateDiffText returns without work. The label is a cached display: neither changing challengeID nor assigning a new description array automatically refreshes it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ChallengeSelectMenu.enemyCountText
member.summary: Stores the label that displays the menu's configured concurrent-enemy count as a number.

remarks.para: A round groups waves, and a wave is a planned batch of enemies. If this label is assigned when Start runs, the menu's controller and its assigned profile's first round and first wave must exist for the initial count read. Start reads maxConcurrent from that first wave into enemyCountValue and displays it. ToggleEnemyCount rewrites the label after every increase or decrease request, even when a bound prevents the number from changing.

This displays the stored menu goal, not the number of enemies currently alive or spawned. Start can skip the label when it is absent, but ToggleEnemyCount requires it and fails if it is missing. updateEnemyCount does not control these label updates.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ChallengeSelectMenu.enemyCountValue
member.summary: Stores the menu's goal for the number of enemies present at the same time.

remarks.para: This is a whole-enemy count. The constructor (setup code that runs when this component is created) starts it at 4. When Unity calls Start as the component begins running, an assigned enemyCountText makes the menu replace it with maxConcurrent from the selected profile's first round and first wave. A round groups waves, and a wave is a planned batch of enemies. ToggleEnemyCount changes the count one step at a time using the configured bounds.

OnChallengeSelect sends it to the arena controller only when updateEnemyCount is true and the controller is available. That call configures deferred custom enemy progression with an increase rate of 3. When it later generates an extra wave, a planned batch of enemies, the new concurrent limit is min(oldLimit + 3, goal), meaning the smaller of those two numbers. oldLimit is the preceding wave's configured concurrent-enemy limit; goal is this value copied at confirmation, both in whole enemies. It also adds six planned enemy entries, rather than guaranteeing six successful spawns. For example, oldLimit = 4 and goal = 10 give a new limit of 7; a goal below the old limit can lower the new limit. This configuration does not immediately change the current wave's limit. The value is not a count of successfully spawned or currently live enemies.

Assigning the value directly does not refresh its label or update the arena profile. For example, storing 10 leaves the old label until a count refresh, and the controller receives 10 only when the confirmation method later applies it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ChallengeSelectMenu.loadID
member.summary: Stores the loadout number later sent to OnLoadoutSelected.

remarks.para: SelectLoadout saves this number without validating or applying equipment. OnLoadoutSelect then sends the current saved number to the shared callback. A callback is a method called to react to a notification; its integer argument is this loadID.
For example, loadID = 2 represents the third numbered choice when listeners use zero-based loadout lists. Assigning this value alone sends no callback and equips no items.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ChallengeSelectMenu.maxEnemyCount
member.summary: Stores the upper threshold checked before increasing the menu's concurrent-enemy goal.

remarks.para: The constructor (setup code that runs when this component is created) sets this to 30 enemies. ToggleEnemyCount(true) adds one only when enemyCountValue is less than this number. At a value of 30 with the default maximum, an increase leaves the value at 30.

Changing this threshold does not clamp an existing value, refresh the label, or change the controller's enemy goal. If the stored value is already above the maximum, an increase leaves that value unchanged.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ChallengeSelectMenu.minEnemyCount
member.summary: Stores the lower threshold checked before decreasing the menu's concurrent-enemy goal.

remarks.para: The constructor (setup code that runs when this component is created) sets this to 3 enemies. ToggleEnemyCount(false) subtracts one only when enemyCountValue is greater than this number. At a value of 3 with the default minimum, a decrease leaves the value at 3.
Changing this threshold does not clamp an existing value, refresh the label, or change the controller's enemy goal. Keep the minimum and maximum consistent when configuring the menu.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ChallengeSelectMenu.updateEnemyCount
member.summary: Controls whether OnChallengeSelect applies the menu's stored concurrent-enemy goal to the arena profile.

remarks.para: With this flag true and a controller available, OnChallengeSelect sends enemyCountValue to the controller after invoking OnChallengeSelected. With it false, that profile update is skipped; the active-title refresh and selection event can still run.

The flag does not enable or disable the count-adjuster buttons in code, and it does not refresh enemyCountText. ToggleEnemyCount still changes the stored number and updates the label regardless of this flag. Assigning true does not immediately apply the current number.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Control_UI_BodyMeasurements.completionEvent
member.summary: Notifies its listeners after Confirm or Guess has applied the settings and hidden the reminder.

remarks.para: A UnityEvent is a list of actions to call when an event occurs. Both button paths attempt saves, apply vitals through controlPlayer, hide obj_pleaseSave, and then invoke this event with no arguments.

For example, a listener can move to the next calibration screen. The event is reached after the earlier calls return; it is not proof that the save attempts succeeded. The event reference must be assigned for those button paths.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Control_UI_BodyMeasurements.controlPlayer
member.summary: Supplies the player controller called to apply the active settings after saving or adjusting measurements.

remarks.para: CheckApprovals keeps an assigned reference. If this reference is missing and UIRig.Instance exists, it fills it from that rig’s controlPlayer. UIRig is the object that coordinates the player’s interface.
SEND_VITALS reads the active save and the current player data through PlayerRefs; the measurement values are not stored inside this field. Calls that apply settings need a valid controller reference.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Control_UI_BodyMeasurements.height_imperial
member.summary: Displays the saved player height as feet and whole inches.

remarks.para: DISPLAY_MEASUREMENTS converts height from centimetres using 0.39370078 inches per centimetre. It rounds feet and the remaining inches down, then uses the “{0:0} ft {1:0} in” display pattern. For example, 180 cm becomes 5 ft 10 in.
It is refreshed with the other measurement labels; a missing label is skipped.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Control_UI_BodyMeasurements.height_metric
member.summary: Displays the saved player height in centimetres.

remarks.para: DISPLAY_MEASUREMENTS writes PlayerHeight followed by “ cm” into this label. Height is already stored in centimetres, so this display does not multiply it by 100. For example, a saved value of 180 displays as 180 cm.
It is refreshed on startup, on panel enable and after adjustment buttons; a missing label is skipped.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Control_UI_BodyMeasurements.img_StandingSeated
member.summary: Shows the posture icon selected by the saved Standing preference.

remarks.para: DISPLAY_MEASUREMENTS assigns sprite_StandingSeated[0] for standing or [1] for seated play. For example, changing the saved preference to seated changes this icon on the next display refresh.
This is a UI image reference. The icon array must be assigned and include both entries for the two postures. A missing image is skipped.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Control_UI_BodyMeasurements.inseamModifier
member.summary: Sets the calculated inseam as a proportion of saved player height.

remarks.para: Inseam is the length of the inside of the leg. The modifier is unitless. CalculateMeasurements writes inseam in metres = height in centimetres × 0.01 × this modifier. The factor 0.01 metres per centimetre converts height to metres.

When the component is created, its initial value is approximately 0.45. Each later CalculateMeasurements call reads the current field value; the panel does not cache an earlier multiplier. With height 180 cm and that default, the estimate is 0.81 m. A larger multiplier produces a longer estimate. Changing this field affects the next calculation, rather than immediately updating stored dimensions or labels.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Control_UI_BodyMeasurements.mediumChest
member.summary: Provides the base chest circumference multiplied by the selected shirt-size factor.

remarks.para: Circumference means the distance all the way around the chest. This base is measured in metres. CalculateMeasurements writes the saved circumference in metres = this base × the selected shirtSizeModifier entry, whose value is unitless.

When the component is created, its initial value is approximately 1.054 m. Each later CalculateMeasurements call reads the current field value; the panel does not cache an earlier base circumference. A multiplier of 1 keeps that base; 1.1 makes the circumference 10% larger. This calculation does not also multiply torso circumference by player height. Changes take effect on the next CalculateMeasurements call.

When the component is created, its initial value is approximately 1.092 m. Each later CalculateMeasurements call reads the current field value; the panel does not cache an earlier base circumference. A multiplier of 1 keeps that base; 1.1 makes the circumference 10% larger. This calculation does not also multiply torso circumference by player height. Changes take effect on the next CalculateMeasurements call.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Control_UI_BodyMeasurements.obj_pleaseSave
member.summary: Shows a reminder after a measurement adjustment and hides it after confirmation or guessing.

remarks.para: SOMETHINGCHANGED calls SetActive on this optional object. Height, shirt-preset and individual-dimension buttons show it after their save attempts and player application. Confirm and Guess hide it before completionEvent, and enabling the panel also hides it.

Its visibility records these UI actions; it does not compare settings against a saved copy or prove that changes remain unsaved. For example, the height button can attempt a save successfully and still show this reminder.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Control_UI_BodyMeasurements.ps
member.summary: Returns the current active save’s object.

remarks.para: Each getter call asks DataManager for ActiveSave and returns its PlayerSettings reference. It does not hold an earlier settings object in a panel cache. PlayerSettings stores height, dimensions, selected preset and posture along with other player preferences.
An active save is required. Changes to the returned object are in-memory changes; writing them to storage and applying them to the player are separate calls.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Control_UI_BodyMeasurements.shirtSizeModifier
member.summary: Scales the four base torso circumferences for each shirt-size preset.

remarks.para: Each array entry is a unitless multiplier. CalculateMeasurements takes the selected MeasurementState value and uses that number as the array index, then multiplies mediumChest, mediumUnderbust, mediumWaist and mediumHips, each in metres, by that entry.

The enum indexes are Custom 0, XSmall 1, Small 2, Medium 3, Large 4, XLarge 5, XXLarge 6 and XXXLarge 7. Include entries for all selected values, including Custom when calculating in that mode. For example, 1.1 makes all four base circumferences 10% larger; it does not change the wingspan or inseam formulas.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Control_UI_BodyMeasurements.shirt_size
member.summary: Displays the name of the selected measurement preset.

remarks.para: DISPLAY_MEASUREMENTS selects shirt_sizes at the current MeasurementState enum value. Custom is index 0 and the seven shirt presets are indexes 1–7. The label reflects that selection; it is not a shirt-size classification calculated from the chest measurement.
A manual dimension button sets Custom before changing its dimension, so the next refresh selects the Custom label.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Control_UI_BodyMeasurements.shirt_sizes
member.summary: Supplies the display name at each measurement-preset index.

remarks.para: DISPLAY_MEASUREMENTS uses these names for the shirt_size label. Indexes match the enum values: Custom 0, XSmall 1, Small 2, Medium 3, Large 4, XLarge 5, XXLarge 6 and XXXLarge 7.
Assign an entry for each preset the screen can display. For example, entry 3 supplies the displayed Medium name; changing that text changes the label without changing any dimension calculation.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Control_UI_BodyMeasurements.sprite_StandingSeated
member.summary: Supplies the standing icon at index 0 and seated icon at index 1 for .

remarks.para: DISPLAY_MEASUREMENTS chooses between these entries using the active settings’ Standing Boolean and writes the selected sprite into img_StandingSeated. A sprite is the picture used by the UI image.
Assign both entries to support both postures. The icons reflect the saved preference; this array does not detect whether the real player is standing.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Control_UI_BodyMeasurements.string_DisplayText

remarks.para: During startup and whenever the panel is enabled, DISPLAY_TEXT copies each string into the text_DisplayText label at the same index. For example, string entry 0 supplies label 0.

Assign this string array. When it contains strings, the text_DisplayText array must also be assigned and have at least one slot per string. An unassigned individual label is skipped; labels beyond the string-array length are left unchanged. An empty string array changes no labels.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Control_UI_BodyMeasurements.text_DisplayText

Assign string_DisplayText and, when it contains strings, assign this label array with at least one slot per string. An unassigned individual label is skipped; labels beyond the number of strings keep their existing text. An empty string array changes no labels.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Control_UI_BodyMeasurements.txt_Standing

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Control_UI_BodyMeasurements.wingspanModifier
member.summary: Sets the calculated wingspan as a proportion of saved player height.

remarks.para: Wingspan is fingertip-to-fingertip reach with the arms spread. The modifier is unitless. CalculateMeasurements writes wingspan in metres = height in centimetres × 0.01 × this modifier. The factor 0.01 metres per centimetre converts height to metres.

When the component is created, its initial value is approximately 1.025. Each later CalculateMeasurements call reads the current field value; the panel does not cache an earlier multiplier. With height 180 cm and that default, the estimate is 1.845 m. A larger multiplier produces a longer estimate. Changing this field affects the next calculation, rather than immediately updating stored dimensions or labels.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.DrawBezierCurve.Liner
member.summary: Cached LineRenderer whose vertices UpdateLines replaces to draw the sampled curve.

remarks.para: A LineRenderer draws connected line segments through a list of positions. Awake, Unity’s setup call when this component is loaded, finds the LineRenderer on the same GameObject and stores it here. The class requires that component.

The component reads the four point objects’ Transform.position values, which are world coordinates in Unity length units, normally meters. It writes those coordinates directly to the LineRenderer. Use a renderer configured for world-space positions; this method does not change useWorldSpace or convert them to the renderer’s local coordinates.

UpdateLines sets its vertex count and positions. Width, materials and other line appearance settings stay on the renderer. Replacing the renderer after Awake does not make this cache search for a new one automatically.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.DrawBezierCurve.OnlySetOnStart
member.summary: When true during Awake, disables this component’s automatic rendering updates.

remarks.para: Awake is Unity’s setup call when the component is loaded. It first caches the LineRenderer, then sets this component’s enabled property false when this flag is true. It does not capture point positions or call UpdateLines to draw the curve once.

The renderer can keep displaying vertices it already had, but its normal OnWillRenderObject callback will no longer rebuild them through this disabled component. A callback is a method Unity calls for an event; this one runs before each camera renders a visible enabled object.

Call UpdateLines explicitly after the renderer cache and points are ready if you want a single draw. That call still reads the points’ current world positions. Changing this flag after Awake does not itself enable or disable the component again.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.DrawBezierCurve.Point1
member.summary: Point object whose world position supplies the cubic curve’s start endpoint.

remarks.para: At curve parameter t = 0 the curve is exactly at this object. Moving it moves the line’s first vertex.

This component uses the object’s current Transform.position in world coordinates, normally meters, each time it evaluates a sample. Its rotation and scale do not supply the curve shape; the four objects’ positions do. Assign every point before redrawing.

Moving the point becomes visible on the next UpdateLines call. Automatic redraw happens through the rendering callback while this component is enabled; OnlySetOnStart disables that path during setup rather than saving a position snapshot.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.DrawBezierCurve.Point4
member.summary: Point object whose world position supplies the cubic curve’s end endpoint.

remarks.para: At curve parameter t = 1 the mathematical curve is exactly at this object. Moving it changes that endpoint and the nearby curve shape.

This component uses the object’s current Transform.position in world coordinates, normally meters, each time it evaluates a sample. Its rotation and scale do not supply the curve shape; the four objects’ positions do. Assign every point before redrawing.

The rendered vertices use t = (i / N) * F, where N is lineSteps, i is the zero-based vertex index from 0 to N - 1, and F is the unitless linePercentageFill. With N = 6 and F = 1, the final vertex is at t = 5/6, so it stops short of this endpoint.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.DrawBezierCurve.linePercentageFill
member.summary: Unitless multiplier for the curve parameter sampled by the line vertices.

remarks.para: Let N be lineSteps, the requested vertex count; i be a vertex’s zero-based index, from 0 through N - 1; and F be linePercentageFill, a unitless curve-parameter multiplier. Each vertex samples t = (i / N) * F. Here t = 0 is Point1 and t = 1 is Point4. Mathematically the last sample is F * (N - 1) / N. For ordinary vertex counts, F = 1 therefore stops short of Point4; native floating-point rounding can affect the result with very large counts.

This is a fraction such as 0.5, not a percentage number such as 50. With N = 6 and F = 0.5, the last sample is t = 5/12, about 0.417. That describes a curve parameter, not 41.7 percent of its physical length.

The constructor starts F at 1. UpdateLines does not clamp it: negative values sample curve parameters below zero, extrapolating the cubic beyond its normal 0-to-1 range, and sufficiently large values can sample beyond the end of the mathematical cubic. With six vertices, F = 1.2 makes the last sample t = 1, allowing for ordinary floating-point rounding. Changing it affects the next redraw.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.DrawBezierCurve.lineSteps
member.summary: Number of vertices UpdateLines requests from the LineRenderer; more vertices give a finer sampled curve.

remarks.para: This integer is a count, not a distance or a number of segments. Let N be this vertex count. N vertices form N - 1 connecting segments for an ordinary non-looping renderer. The constructor initializes N to 6, making five segments.

Use a positive count large enough for the detail you need. One vertex samples only the start and provides no connecting segment; zero requests an empty line but still requires all point references for this method’s setup checks. This code does not validate or repair negative counts.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Feedback_Audio._last_activate
member.summary: Keeps the advancing counter for ordered activation sound selection from .

remarks.para: This is a whole-number counter with no physical units. It normally starts at 0 and is updated only when the matching audio method uses order mode with a nonempty clip array. Random and single modes leave it unchanged.

In order mode, each call with a nonempty clip array first adds 1 to the stored counter. It resets the counter to 0 only if it is greater than the number of clips, then chooses the remainder after dividing the counter by the number of clips as the array index. Array indices start at 0. For three clips and an initial counter of 0, the selected indices are 1, 2, 0, 0, 1, 2, and so on. The first clip therefore repeats at the wraparound.

The counter is changed before playback is requested. It can equal the clip count even though the selected index is 0, and it is not a reliable record of the last sound heard. Playback can still fail or wait for an audio player to become available.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Feedback_Audio._sourceRadius
member.summary: Sets the minimum-distance radius in Unity world units passed to the audio player for positional sound; scenes commonly treat 1 unit as 1 meter.

remarks.para: This describes the area around the sound source where distance alone does not reduce its volume. Outside that radius, a 3D sound becomes quieter according to the audio source's distance settings. It is not a hard cutoff beyond which the sound disappears. For example, 2 means a minimum-distance radius of 2 Unity world units (typically 2 meters in a scene using the common 1 unit = 1 meter scale).

When the component is created, its constructor, the code that sets its initial values, sets 1 Unity world unit. The Inspector, Unity's panel for editing component settings, offers a range of 0.1 to 10 Unity world units. A scene using the common 1 world unit = 1 meter scale treats those values as 1 meter and 0.1 to 10 meters. Playback reads the current value and passes it unchanged as minDistance to the audio player, which assigns it to its AudioSource, Unity's sound-playing component. This component does not convert the value to centimeters or add the volume setting to the radius.

The distance effect depends on spatialBlend: 0 is 2D sound with no positional distance effect; 1 is fully 3D sound. Editing this setting affects later sound requests rather than updating an already spawned player.
That Inspector range describes the editor controls. The inspected feedback request code does not clamp the value to that range while the game runs.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Feedback_Audio._sourceVolume
member.summary: Sets the unitless volume level passed to the audio player for later feedback sounds.

remarks.para: The usual range is 0 to 1: 0 is silent, 1 leaves the clip at the source's full volume, and 0.5 uses half that numerical volume setting. This is not a decibel value, and half the setting does not guarantee that a listener hears exactly half the loudness. Mixer and user volume settings can also affect the sound.

When the component is created, its constructor, the code that sets its initial values, sets 0.25. The Inspector, Unity's panel for editing component settings, offers a range of 0 to 1. PlayAudio reads the current value when requesting a sound, and the player assigns that value to its AudioSource, Unity's sound-playing component. Editing it later does not change an already requested player.

The Inspector tooltip says values above 1 increase the minimum-distance sphere. In the inspected feedback playback path, volume and minimum distance are passed separately and volume does not enlarge that radius. Use _sourceRadius, measured in Unity world units (typically meters in scenes scaled 1 unit = 1 meter), to configure that distance.
That Inspector range describes the editor controls. The inspected feedback request code does not clamp the value to that range while the game runs.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Feedback_Audio.activateMode
member.summary: Chooses how AUDIOACTIVATE picks an activation sound from .

remarks.para: random (0) chooses a fresh random array index each call and may repeat the same clip. order (1) advances the saved whole-number counter and uses it to choose an index. single (2) uses the method's clip argument as an index; an omitted clip argument means index 0, the first entry. These values have no distance or time units.

In order mode, each call with a nonempty clip array first adds 1 to the stored counter. It resets the counter to 0 only if it is greater than the number of clips, then chooses the remainder after dividing the counter by the number of clips as the array index. Array indices start at 0. For three clips and an initial counter of 0, the selected indices are 1, 2, 0, 0, 1, 2, and so on. The first clip therefore repeats at the wraparound.

Changing this setting affects later calls; it does not play a sound or restart the saved order counter. Provide a non-null clip array. An empty array produces no request, and single mode needs an index from 0 through the clip count minus 1.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Feedback_Audio.audioPlacementOverride
member.summary: Provides the default object whose scene position is sampled when a feedback sound is requested.

remarks.para: A GameObject is an object in a Unity scene; its Transform holds its position, rotation and size. Start, Unity's setup call before the component's first regular update, fills this field with the component's own GameObject if it is missing. That fallback is stored once, rather than chosen again on every audio call.

Each AUDIO method first uses a location argument if one is supplied. Otherwise it reads this object's Transform. PlayAudio samples that Transform's world position in Unity world coordinates and requests a sound there. Unity scenes commonly use a scale where 1 world unit represents 1 meter; this code does not convert the coordinates. For example, assigning a menu button object makes calls without a location play at that button's current position.

The six AUDIO methods request playback at a fixed world position; moving the object afterwards does not make that sound follow it. Changing this field affects later calls without a location. Configure it before calling an AUDIO method before Start. If you clear this field after Start, another call must supply a location or you must restore a valid fallback first; with neither, the native no-location path reaches its failure helper.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Feedback_Audio.clips_Activate
member.summary: Supplies the activation sounds requested by .

remarks.para: Each AudioClip is a sound asset. Entries use indices starting at 0: in single mode, clip 0 chooses the first entry and clip 1 chooses the second. Random mode may choose any entry again; order mode advances its counter before selecting a clip.

In order mode, each call with a nonempty clip array first adds 1 to the stored counter. It resets the counter to 0 only if it is greater than the number of clips, then chooses the remainder after dividing the counter by the number of clips as the array index. Array indices start at 0. For three clips and an initial counter of 0, the selected indices are 1, 2, 0, 0, 1, 2, and so on. The first clip therefore repeats at the wraparound.

An empty array makes this audio method return without requesting sound. A null array is an error, and an index outside the array is an error in single mode. Configure this array before calling the method. Changing its entries changes future requests, without changing sounds already requested.

The call requests a sound at a position in the scene. The audio manager may need to wait for a reusable audio player before playback starts, so returning from the method does not prove the clip is already audible.

remarks.para: random (0) chooses a fresh random array index each call and may repeat the same clip. order (1) advances the saved whole-number counter and uses it to choose an index. single (2) uses the method's clip argument as an index; an omitted clip argument means index 0, the first entry. These values have no distance or time units.

In order mode, each call with a nonempty clip array first adds 1 to the stored counter. It resets the counter to 0 only if it is greater than the number of clips, then chooses the remainder after dividing the counter by the number of clips as the array index. Array indices start at 0. For three clips and an initial counter of 0, the selected indices are 1, 2, 0, 0, 1, 2, and so on. The first clip therefore repeats at the wraparound.

Changing this setting affects later calls; it does not play a sound or restart the saved order counter. Provide a non-null clip array. An empty array produces no request, and single mode needs an index from 0 through the clip count minus 1. A clipOverride whose clip still exists replaces the selected array clip only after a valid index has been selected; a missing or destroyed override leaves the selected array clip in use, so it cannot bypass these array requirements.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Feedback_Audio.spatialBlend
member.summary: Sets how much feedback sounds use their position in the scene: 0 is 2D and 1 is fully 3D audio.

remarks.para: This is a unitless blend from 0 to 1. At 0, the sound is 2D and does not change with source position as a 3D sound does. At 1, direction and distance from the listener affect the sound. Values between them mix the two behaviors; for example, 0.5 is halfway through that blend, not half a meter.

When the component is created, its constructor, the code that sets its initial values, sets 1. Each request passes the current value to the audio player, which assigns it to its AudioSource, Unity's sound-playing component. It is a setting for future requests, not a measurement of how loudly a current sound can be heard.

The placement is the supplied location's world position, or the audioPlacementOverride object's world position when location is missing. The six AUDIO methods sample it once. _sourceRadius supplies the 3D minimum distance in Unity world units (typically meters when a scene uses 1 unit = 1 meter), inside which distance alone does not reduce volume.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GachaPlacer.onlyPlaceIfBeatGame
member.summary: Requires the active save’s campaign-completion flag before this placer requests a capsule spawn.

remarks.para: The represented crate is the capsule’s selected item definition. Non-redacted means its Redacted visibility flag is false. When true, OnPersistentLoad and ShouldSpawn require PlayerProgression.BeatGame to be true. When false, they skip only that completion requirement: the represented crate must still resolve, be non-redacted, and have fewer than one recorded unlock.

This is read when the placement check runs. Changing it does not remove an already spawned capsule or immediately create a new one, and it does not stop the CrateSpawner’s separate automatic loading path. Use Manual Mode on that spawner so this placer controls its loading-time request.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GachaPlacer.unlockCrate
member.summary: The crate represented by the capsule, used both for placement eligibility and the capsule’s selected item.

remarks.para: A crate is an item definition in the Asset Warehouse, the game’s catalog of item definitions and assets. Its barcode, the crate’s identifying code, is used to read the active save’s unlock count; the resolved definition also supplies the Redacted flag checked before placement. Assign a reference that resolves to the intended collectible’s crate.

When the spawner reports a spawned object, this placer looks for a GachaCapsule on that object, assigns this reference to its selectedCrate, then requests its preview mesh, the 3D shape or model used to show the represented item. The spawner’s spawnableCrateReference chooses the capsule object to create; unlockCrate chooses the item that capsule represents. For example, a capsule object and its represented prop can be two different crate definitions. An object without GachaCapsule receives no such configuration.
Changing this reference affects later checks and spawn notifications. It does not update capsules that have already been configured or award an unlock by itself.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Descent.IntroMusicCues.fadeInTime
member.summary: Sets the requested time in seconds for this cue's incoming music to reach its target volume.

remarks.para: PlayIntroMusic reads this when the cue is requested. With an introClip, it applies to the incoming intro; without one, it applies to clipMain. If that clip is already selected, the audio manager uses this time to adjust its current volume instead of restarting it. Editing the cue alone does not update playing music.

Fades advance in real-time seconds, unaffected by game slow motion. Zero or a negative value requests an immediate volume change. Volume is a dimensionless source-level setting: 0 is silent and 1 is the ordinary full source level. A rate of 0.04 volume units per real-time second changes that setting by 0.04 each second. A newly selected clip has that minimum fade rate, so the configured time is not an exact guarantee. For example, target volume 0.1 over a requested 10 seconds reaches that target in about 2.5 seconds because of the minimum rate; frame timing can add a small delay.
When an intro transitions into the main loop, that transition uses fadeOutTime for both sides of its fade instead.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Descent.IntroMusicCues.fadeOutTime
member.summary: Sets the requested fade-out time for the previous music when this cue is selected, and the intro-to-loop transition time when this cue has an intro.

remarks.para: This is measured in seconds. The audio manager fades the outgoing music with this value while fading in the new cue. Selecting an already active clip only adjusts its volume, so that branch does not use an outgoing fade.

When the request actually starts a newly selected introClip, the same value also sets how early the main loop is requested: the audio manager waits the intro's length minus fadeOutTime in real-time seconds, then requests the main loop with this value as both its fade-in time and the intro's fade-out time. For example, a 12-second intro and a value of 2 request the loop after a 10-second wait. The sequence continues on later frames, so this is configured timing rather than an exact audio-sample boundary.

Zero or a negative value requests an immediate outgoing stop. Volume is a dimensionless source-level setting: 0 is silent and 1 is the ordinary full source level. Fading has a minimum rate of 0.04 volume units per real-time second, meaning that setting changes by at least 0.04 each second while fading, and a partly faded source can finish earlier, so the requested seconds do not always equal the actual fade duration. Changing this cue field alone does not alter a transition already requested.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Descent.IntroMusicCues.loop
member.summary: Requests repeating main-clip playback when this cue has no introClip.

remarks.para: Without an intro, true asks a newly selected clipMain to repeat after it ends; false asks for one playthrough. With an introClip, PlayIntroMusic takes a separate intro-then-loop path that requests a repeating main clip regardless of this flag.

This is cue configuration, not a report of the audio source's current loop state. Editing it does not change playing music. Even requesting the same clip again can only adjust volume or return without changing its existing loop setting; the direct path installs this flag when it switches to a new clip.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Descent.IntroMusicCues.volume
member.summary: Sets the target loudness requested for this soundtrack cue.

remarks.para: This is a dimensionless audio-source volume setting: 0 is silent, 0.5 is lower than 1, and 1 is the ordinary full source level before other audio settings. It is not measured in decibels and does not change every game sound. The Inspector suggests 0 through 1; that display range does not prove every playback path clamps values assigned by code.

PlayIntroMusic supplies this value for the intro if present, otherwise for the main clip. Fade times control how it is reached. The later intro-to-loop transition takes the then-current intro source volume as the main loop's target, so it can inherit a volume still partway through a fade. Editing the cue field alone does not update the active audio source.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Descent.amb_fadeInTime
member.summary: Sets the requested time in seconds for the field ambience to reach amb_volume.

remarks.para: SetupFieldReverbAndAmbience and the post-noose transition read this setting when cueing fieldAmbClipMain. When a new clip is selected, it fades up from silence; when that clip is already selected, it adjusts the current volume instead. Zero or a negative duration requests an immediate change.

amb_volume is the dimensionless source-volume target, with 0 silent and 1 the ordinary full source level. Fades advance in real-time seconds, unaffected by game slow motion. For a new clip with volume 0.1 and duration 1, the ordinary fade rate is 0.1 volume units per second. A rate of 0.1 volume units per second changes that setting by 0.1 each second. The new-clip fade has a minimum rate of 0.04 volume units per real-time second, and updates happen on frames, so the requested duration is not always the exact elapsed time.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Descent.amb_fadeOutTime
member.summary: Sets the requested fade-out time in seconds for the old ambience when switching to the field clip.

remarks.para: This controls the outgoing ambience in the global audio manager, not the field clip's lifetime. SetupFieldReverbAndAmbience and the post-noose transition pass it when cueing fieldAmbClipMain. Re-cueing the same clip changes its volume without switching sources, so this outgoing fade is not used in that case.

Zero or a negative duration requests an immediate stop. Ordinary fading advances in real-time seconds and stops the old source at zero volume. Volume is a dimensionless source level, with 0 silent and 1 the ordinary full level. Its minimum fade rate is 0.04 volume units per real-time second, meaning the setting changes by at least 0.04 each second while fading; a partially faded sound can also finish sooner than the requested duration.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Descent.amb_volume
member.summary: Sets the target loudness of fieldAmbClipMain when the field ambience is requested.

remarks.para: This is a dimensionless audio-source volume setting: 0 is silent, 0.5 is a lower level than 1, and 1 is the ordinary full source level before other audio settings. It does not set every environmental sound's volume.

SetupFieldReverbAndAmbience and the post-noose transition read it along with the fade times. Changing it alone does not adjust the currently playing ambience; cue the ambience again. The Inspector suggests 0 through 1, but that display range is not a universal runtime clamp on this field.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Descent.canForceGrab
member.summary: Controls whether the avatar-selection stage starts its one-time delayed force-grab hint.

remarks.para: True lets the main sequence save and start ForceGrabCoroutine. Its first step clears this flag, then waits 10 game-time seconds before possibly showing module_ForceGrab. CONFIRMFORCEGRAB also clears it after canceling the hint. This flag does not grant or remove the player's ability to force-grab items.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Descent.clip_HeightParticleWoop
member.summary: Selects the whoosh played at the height reveal effect when its X growth starts and again when Y growth starts.

remarks.para: Playback uses module_HeightSpawnEffect's world position, the position in the level. Changing the clip affects later playback requests; it does not change the curves or stage duration. No third playback is made at the start of Z growth by the inspected sequence.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Descent.curve_HeightCloseX
member.summary: Shapes how the height reveal effect changes its local X size when the height area closes.

remarks.para: The horizontal curve input is elapsed game-time seconds divided by 0.1 game-time seconds for this closing stage. Elapsed time accumulates the game-time seconds since the previous frame on each frame. The vertical output is a dimensionless blend limited to 0 through 1: 0 selects module_HeightInTarget's local X scale, and 1 selects module_HeightOutTarget's local X scale. Local scale is a dimensionless size multiplier relative to the parent, so 1 means the original size along that axis. These values change size in the effect's local axes, not entry/exit positions.

For example, blending from axis scale 2 to 0.1 with output 0.5 gives scale 1.05. After gate_mirror, Z closes first; then module_Height is disabled and X/Y close together with a new 0.1-second timer. The loop does not guarantee a final sample at curve input 1. Direct child effects are separately kept at world scale 0.03 on each axis.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Descent.curve_HeightOpenX
member.summary: Shapes how the height reveal effect grows along its local X axis.

remarks.para: The horizontal curve input is elapsed game-time seconds divided by 0.5 seconds for this axis, normally increasing from 0 toward 1. The vertical output is a dimensionless blend, limited to 0 through 1: 0 gives local scale 0.001 and 1 gives module_HeightInTarget's local X scale. Local scale is a size multiplier along an axis that turns with the object's parent, not movement in meters.

For example, if the target axis scale is 2, a curve output of 0.5 gives scale 1.0005. Opening runs X, then Y, then Z, resetting the timer before each axis; this curve changes only its named stage. Sampling stops once the timer reaches 0.5 seconds, without a guaranteed final input-1 write. Direct child effects are separately kept at world scale 0.03 on each axis.
