member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Descent.curve_Mirror
member.summary: Shapes the local size of the mirror's spawn particles as they grow in X, then Z, then Y.

remarks.para: Each axis has a separate 1-second game-time timer. The horizontal input is elapsed seconds divided by 1 second; the vertical output is a dimensionless blend limited to 0 through 1. Output 0 gives local scale 0.001 and output 1 gives local scale 2. For example, output 0.5 gives scale 1.0005.

This curve animates module_MirrorSpawnParticles, not the mirror object's movement or the mirror-frame material fade. It changes a size multiplier relative to the particles' parent. The timer resets between axes, and there is no guaranteed final sample at input 1.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Descent.daggerEntity
member.summary: Selects the dagger entity requested visible after the lightning bolt's first material-progress stage.

remarks.para: The sequence requests showing it after the bolt's first material-progress loop, then enables lightning hit/path particles and plays module_DaggerHitClip. The entity's hide system applies visibility separately; this field is a scene reference, not proof that the dagger is currently visible.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Descent.dynamicGallows
member.summary: Selects the gallows object whose world Y rotation must become at most 232 degrees before the lock pin is enabled.

remarks.para: The sequence checks this after requesting the noose reveal sound and requesting intro music cue 0. It waits frame by frame while the Y angle is greater than 232 degrees; equality passes. World Y rotation is the object's angle relative to the level, not its parent. This reader only measures the object's orientation; it does not rotate or assemble the gallows.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Descent.fieldAmbClipMain
member.summary: Selects the background clip requested when the sequence reaches the field after the noose stage.

remarks.para: SetupFieldReverbAndAmbience also requests this clip directly, using amb_volume as its target source volume. This volume is dimensionless, with 0 silent and 1 the ordinary full source level. amb_fadeInTime controls the incoming clip or adjusts this clip if already selected; amb_fadeOutTime controls the outgoing old clip when switching. Both fades use real-time seconds, unaffected by game slow motion. The global audio manager changes it over later frames. Assigning a different clip does not replace playing ambience until another request is made.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Descent.fieldReverbObj
member.summary: Selects the echo preset requested for the field's global audio after the noose stage.

remarks.para: Reverb is the lingering room-like echo added to sound. SetupFieldReverbAndAmbience and the main sequence pass this preset to the global audio manager before cueing the field ambience. The preset changes mixer settings over later frames with its own timing; amb_fadeInTime and amb_fadeOutTime control ambience volume instead.
Changing this reference alone does not start a new echo transition. Request the field audio setup again to apply the new preset.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Descent.forceGrabRoutine
member.summary: Stores the delayed-hint sequence so CONFIRMFORCEGRAB can stop it before the force-grab prompt appears.

remarks.para: A coroutine is a sequence that pauses and continues over several frames. The avatar-selection stage assigns a new ForceGrabCoroutine here and starts it only when canForceGrab is true. The stored object is not cleared when it finishes or is stopped, so a non-null reference does not prove the hint sequence is still running.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Descent.forwardFacing
member.summary: Stores an orientation marker, but no player-facing behavior was verified for it in the inspected Descent code.

remarks.para: The complete GameControl_Descent methods and its four sequence loops, plus all DescentIntroSequenceCtrl methods, do not read this reference. Assigning a marker here is therefore not a verified way to turn the player in those routines. Other game code and mods were not exhaustively checked.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Descent.gate_cut
member.summary: Lets the intro sequence finish once its final effects and waits have reached the rope-cut milestone.

remarks.para: SEQUENCE(6) sets this flag. The sequence checks it after the lightning effects and a final 2-second game-time pause, waiting frame by frame while false. True ends that sequence when observed; this final branch does not itself load another level. It is a recorded milestone, not a live check of the rope.
SEQUENCE only sets milestones true; it does not reset them. A flag set early remains available when its wait is reached, while earlier waits and timed effects still run.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Descent.gate_d6
member.summary: Lets the sequence leave avatar selection and move toward the noose reveal.

remarks.para: SEQUENCE(3) sets this flag. ConfirmAvatarButton sets it before requesting that the die and button be hidden. When the main sequence sees true, it first clears gate_forceGrab, then hides the pedestal and avatar-selection objects and starts the mirror-closing animation. This flag records a milestone, not the die's current visibility.
SEQUENCE only sets milestones true; it does not reset them. A flag set early remains available when its wait is reached, while earlier waits and timed effects still run.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Descent.gate_drop
member.summary: Lets the sequence begin the radio and lightning timing after the trapdoor milestone.

remarks.para: SEQUENCE(5) sets this flag. After the post-noose pause, the sequence waits while it is false. When true it waits 1.5 game-time seconds before playing the radio, then continues to lightning. This flag does not directly open the gate object or prove it is currently open.
SEQUENCE only sets milestones true; it does not reset them. A flag set early remains available when its wait is reached, while earlier waits and timed effects still run.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Descent.gate_forceGrab
member.summary: Controls whether the delayed hint may show the force-grab tutorial object when its wait finishes.

remarks.para: The main sequence sets this true after optionally starting ForceGrabCoroutine at avatar selection. That delayed-hint sequence, which pauses and continues across frames, clears canForceGrab, waits 10 game-time seconds and checks this flag once before showing module_ForceGrab.

When gate_d6 is observed, the main sequence clears gate_forceGrab before hiding the avatar-selection objects. Clearing it suppresses a hint that has not yet reached its check; it does not itself hide a hint already displayed. CONFIRMFORCEGRAB cancels the routine and hides the hint object separately.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Descent.gate_height
member.summary: Records the height milestone when SEQUENCE(1) is called.

remarks.para: The main intro sequence does not read this flag, and ConfirmHeightSettings changes the height UI and enables the mirror directly without setting it. True does not itself recalibrate the player or prove calibration ran.
SEQUENCE only sets milestones true; it does not reset them. If this flag is set early, it stays true, but the inspected main sequence has no wait for it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Descent.gate_mirror
member.summary: Lets the sequence close the height area and begin revealing the mirror.

remarks.para: SEQUENCE(2) sets this flag. The main sequence checks it after the height-opening effects and waits frame by frame while false. Setting it does not immediately move or show an object; its effects occur when that wait is reached.
SEQUENCE only sets milestones true; it does not reset them. A flag set early remains available when its wait is reached, while earlier waits and timed effects still run.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Descent.gate_noose
member.summary: Lets the sequence switch to field audio, save the chosen avatar and release the player at the gallows.

remarks.para: SEQUENCE(4) sets this flag. Its wait is reached after dynamicGallows world Y rotation becomes at most 232 degrees and module_GallowLockPin is enabled. On true it requests music cue 1, field echo/ambience and saving of the avatar identifiers, releases the player, then changes the void/gallows objects and waits 5 game-time seconds.
SEQUENCE only sets milestones true; it does not reset them. A flag set early remains available when its wait is reached, while earlier waits and timed effects still run.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Descent.introMusicCues
member.summary: Configures the soundtrack entries requested during the noose reveal and field transition.

remarks.para: PlayIntroMusic uses a zero-based index: the main sequence requests entry 0 when requesting the noose reveal sound and entry 1 after gate_noose. Provide both entries for that normal path. Each entry supplies a main clip, optional intro clip, volume, fade times in real-time seconds and a loop setting. Volume is a dimensionless source level, with 0 silent and 1 the ordinary full source level; volume fades use real time and are unaffected by game slow motion.

A supplied introClip requests intro-then-loop playback. The manager can adjust an already selected intro or main clip instead of starting a new intro, and an active audio override can defer the request. Audio override is a mode that temporarily gives other music priority and holds ordinary cue requests. Without an introClip, clipMain follows the entry's loop setting. These settings are read when PlayIntroMusic is called; editing the array does not itself replace playing music.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Descent.levelLoaded
member.summary: Records that Descent's loading callback has finished its initial setup, allowing DISABLEDEATHRELOAD to run.

remarks.para: A callback is a routine called when an operation reaches a particular point. The level-load callback caches player health and the mirror Renderer, Unity's drawing component, then starts the intro sequence or resumes the player, and finally sets this flag true. That sequence pauses and continues across frames and can still have many timed effects and player waits remaining.

DISABLEDEATHRELOAD returns immediately while false. On the resume path its call is attempted before this final true assignment, so that call can be skipped on the first callback. This flag does not mean the entire tutorial has finished.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Descent.module_AvatarDie
member.summary: Selects the avatar die requested to appear on the pedestal during avatar selection.

remarks.para: It is requested hidden when this control is enabled, then requested shown after the mirror grows and its 3-second wait ends. ConfirmAvatarButton and the main gate_d6 transition request hiding it again. These requests use the entity hide system; they do not prove visibility changed immediately.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Descent.module_ConstellationParticles
member.summary: Selects the constellation effect shown on a fresh intro and disabled when the noose milestone passes.

remarks.para: When the control is enabled, it activates this object for a fresh intro and disables it for a resumed save. The main sequence disables it after requesting the avatar save and releasing the player at gate_noose. Assigning another object changes which object those later calls affect.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Descent.module_DaggerHitClip
member.summary: Selects the impact sound requested when the lightning reveal makes the dagger available.

remarks.para: After the bolt's first material-progress loop, the sequence requests showing daggerEntity, enables hit/path particles and requests this clip at module_DaggerHitPoint's world position. This playback is timed by the intro sequence, not by a collision test in the inspected method.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Descent.module_DaggerHitPoint
member.summary: Supplies the world position for the dagger reveal's impact sound.

remarks.para: A Transform stores an object's position, rotation and scale. The sequence reads this transform's position in the level when requesting module_DaggerHitClip after the first lightning material-progress loop. Moving it before that request changes where the sound starts. The inspected sequence does not move hit particles to this point or use its rotation.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Descent.module_DaggerLightningHit
member.summary: Selects the extra dagger-lightning object disabled when this control is enabled.

remarks.para: The complete GameControl_Descent methods and four sequence loops do not turn it on or otherwise read it after that setup. An active strike effect was therefore not verified for this reference in those routines; other scene scripts or mods may act on the assigned object.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Descent.module_DaggerParticles
member.summary: Selects the particle object enabled alongside the height reveal near the start of the intro.

remarks.para: The control disables it when enabled. After the opening 1-second wait, the main sequence enables it with the pedestal particles and height reveal effect. The inspected sequence does not later disable it, so its own particle settings or other code determine its remaining lifetime.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Descent.module_DropGate
member.summary: Selects the gate object disabled after the noose sound request and enabled after the noose milestone.

remarks.para: The control disables it at setup, and the sequence disables it again after requesting the noose reveal sound. After gate_noose it enables this object after releasing the player. gate_drop is a separate milestone that the sequence waits for later; this field does not report whether the gate is currently open.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Descent.module_ForceGrab
member.summary: Selects the tutorial hint object shown if the player is still at avatar selection after the delayed hint wait.

remarks.para: The control disables it at setup. ForceGrabCoroutine can enable it after a 10-game-time-second wait if gate_forceGrab is still true. CONFIRMFORCEGRAB stops the saved sequence and disables this object. Enabling it displays the assigned hint; it does not grant force-grab ability.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Descent.module_GallowLockPin
member.summary: Selects the lock-pin object enabled once the gallows reaches the required orientation.

remarks.para: The control disables it at setup. After requesting the noose reveal sound, the sequence reads dynamicGallows world Y rotation each frame and enables this object when the angle is at most 232 degrees. World rotation is relative to the level. The inspected sequence does not configure a physics constraint here; it activates the assigned scene object.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Descent.module_GallowPin
member.summary: Selects the gallows pin object disabled before the noose sound request and re-enabled after gate_noose.

remarks.para: The control enables it at setup. The sequence disables it before requesting the noose reveal sound, then enables it again after saving the avatar and releasing the player at the noose milestone.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Descent.module_Height
member.summary: Selects the height area shown during height-effect growth and hidden when the mirror milestone is reached.

remarks.para: The control disables it at setup. During opening, the sequence enables it after the effect's Y growth finishes and before Z growth starts. During closing after gate_mirror, it disables this area after Z closing and before X/Y closing. The curves animate module_HeightSpawnEffect separately.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Descent.module_HeightInTarget
member.summary: Supplies the local scale values the height reveal effect grows toward and closes from.

remarks.para: The sequence reads this object's transform.localScale components, not its position. A scale is a dimensionless size multiplier relative to a parent: local X scale 2 means twice that axis size before parent scaling. Opening blends each effect axis from 0.001 to this value; closing blends from this value toward module_HeightOutTarget. The respective curves choose a blend limited to 0 through 1. The values are read during the animation, so edits during a stage can change later frames.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Descent.module_HeightOutTarget
member.summary: Supplies the local scale values the height reveal effect closes toward.

remarks.para: The sequence reads this object's transform.localScale, not its position. Scale values are dimensionless size multipliers relative to a parent. After gate_mirror, Z blends from module_HeightInTarget's Z scale toward this object's Z scale; X and Y then do the same together. Each closing stage uses a 0.1-second game-time timer and its curve's clamped 0-to-1 blend. The target components are read during the animation.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Descent.module_HeightSpawnEffect
member.summary: Selects the effect object stretched to reveal and close the height area.

remarks.para: The sequence grows its local X, then Y, then Z scale using separate 0.5-game-time-second timers and the opening curves. After gate_mirror it closes Z, then X/Y together, using separate 0.1-second timers and the closing curves. Scale is a dimensionless size multiplier relative to the parent: 1 means the original axis size. These change size along the object's parent-relative axes, not position.

The control initially disables this object. The sequence enables it for opening, disables it after a 0.5-second pause, enables it for closing, then disables it after the final 0.1-second pause. While changing its scale, the sequence keeps direct child effects at world scale 0.03 per axis. World scale includes the parent's scaling; 0.03 is a dimensionless multiplier requesting 3 percent of the original size for each scale component.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Descent.module_LightingBolt
member.summary: Selects the lightning object whose material is animated before the dagger is revealed.

remarks.para: The control disables it at setup. After the lightning sound and a 1.4-game-time-second wait, the sequence takes the Renderer material from this object and enables it. It advances one material value over a configured 0.2 seconds, then another over 1 second, setting each to 1 at completion.

After the second loop it waits 4 seconds, disables the bolt and hit particles, then waits 2 more seconds before checking gate_cut. The cached material is chosen when the lightning phase begins; changing the object reference afterward does not replace that phase's saved material. A Renderer is the component that draws an object; its material controls appearance.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Descent.module_LightingHitParticles
member.summary: Selects the impact particle object enabled when the lightning animation reveals the dagger.

remarks.para: The sequence enables it after finishing the bolt's first material-progress loop. After the second loop and a 4-game-time-second wait, it disables this object together with the bolt. The assigned scene object determines the effect's location and appearance.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Descent.module_LightingPathParticles
member.summary: Selects the lightning-path particle object enabled at the same moment the dagger is revealed.

remarks.para: The control disables it at setup. The sequence enables it after the bolt's first material-progress loop, alongside hit particles and the dagger reveal. Unlike the hit particles, this path object is not disabled later by the inspected sequence; its particle setup or other code determines how it stops.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Descent.module_LightningAudioClip
member.summary: Selects the lightning sound requested before the bolt visual is enabled.

remarks.para: After the radio starts and a 0.5-game-time-second wait, the sequence requests this clip at module_LightningAudioTransform's world position. It then waits 1.4 game-time seconds before enabling and animating the bolt. Changing the clip does not alter those waits.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Descent.module_LightningAudioTransform
member.summary: Supplies the world position where the lightning sound starts.

remarks.para: A Transform stores position, rotation and scale. The sequence reads this position in the level when requesting module_LightningAudioClip, then waits 1.4 game-time seconds before the bolt visual begins. Rotation and scale are not read by this sound request; moving the transform changes the position of future requests.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Descent.module_Mirror
member.summary: Selects the mirror area enabled for avatar selection and disabled before the noose reveal.

remarks.para: The control disables it at setup. The main sequence enables it when beginning the mirror spawn effect, then disables it 2.5 game-time seconds after starting mirror closure following gate_d6. DescentIntroSequenceCtrl.ConfirmHeightSettings also enables it directly after hiding the height UI. The main mirror curve changes the spawn particles' scale, not this object's transform.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Descent.module_MirrorButton
member.summary: Selects the confirmation entity requested visible after the avatar die produces a result.

remarks.para: The control requests it hidden at setup. DescentIntroSequenceCtrl.DieRollResult requests showing it; ConfirmAvatarButton sets gate_d6 and requests hiding both this button and the die. The main sequence also requests hiding it when gate_d6 passes. These use the entity hide system, so a request is not proof of immediate visibility.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Descent.module_MirrorPedestal
member.summary: Selects the pedestal object enabled when avatar selection begins and disabled when its milestone passes.

remarks.para: The control disables it at setup. The sequence enables it after the mirror spawn effect and following 3-game-time-second wait, just before requesting the avatar die visible. When gate_d6 is observed it clears the hint gate first, then disables this pedestal.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Descent.module_MirrorPedestalParticles
member.summary: Selects the pedestal particle object enabled near the beginning of the intro.

remarks.para: The control disables it at setup. After the initial 1-game-time-second wait, the sequence enables it alongside dagger particles and the height reveal effect. The inspected sequence does not later disable it; the particle setup or another script controls its remaining lifetime.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Descent.module_MirrorReflectVol
member.summary: Selects the reflection object enabled after the mirror spawn particles finish growing.

remarks.para: The control disables it at setup. Once the spawn particles finish their Y growth, the sequence enables this object and module_MirrorVoidParticles, then stops the spawn particle system. The inspected sequence does not later disable this reference directly. This field selects the scene object; it does not expose a reflection-strength value.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Descent.module_MirrorSpawnParticles
member.summary: Selects the mirror arrival effect grown along local X, then Z, then Y before avatar selection.

remarks.para: The sequence enables it with module_Mirror. curve_Mirror blends each axis scale from 0.001 to 2 using a separate 1-game-time-second timer; scale is a size multiplier relative to its parent. After growth it stops this object's ParticleSystem, the component that emits particles, while enabling the reflection and void effects. Once gate_d6 passes it deactivates this object entirely.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Descent.module_MirrorVoidFrame
member.summary: Selects the object whose Renderer is cached for the mirror-frame reveal and closing animations.

remarks.para: A Renderer is the component that draws an object. During the loading callback, the control gets this object's Renderer and stores it in voidFrame. MirrorInProgress and MirrorOutProgress later change a float in that renderer's material, which controls appearance. Reassigning module_MirrorVoidFrame after that setup does not replace the cached renderer.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Descent.module_MirrorVoidParticles
member.summary: Selects the void particle object shown after the mirror arrival effect finishes.

remarks.para: The control disables it at setup. After mirror-particle Y growth, the sequence enables it with the reflection object. When gate_d6 passes, it stops this object's ParticleSystem, the component emitting particles; after gate_noose it deactivates the whole object. Stopping particle emission and deactivating an object are separate operations.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Descent.module_SphereVolume
member.summary: Stores a scene object reference, but no sequence effect was verified for it in the inspected Descent code.

remarks.para: The complete GameControl_Descent methods, its four sequence loops and all DescentIntroSequenceCtrl methods do not read this reference. Those routines therefore do not establish it as a spherical trigger or give it a useful radius or stage effect. Other game code and mods were not exhaustively checked.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Descent.module_startVoid
member.summary: Selects the opening void object shown for a fresh intro and hidden after the noose milestone.

remarks.para: When this control is enabled, it activates this object for a fresh intro and disables it when resuming a save. gate_noose is the true/false noose milestone flag; its true value lets the sequence continue past that wait. The main sequence later disables this object after that wait, after requesting the avatar save and releasing the player. Assigning another object selects the target of future activation calls; it does not itself change which object is currently active.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Descent.nooseScript
member.summary: Selects the noose controller whose reveal sound is played before the gallows rotation wait.

remarks.para: gate_d6 is the true/false stage flag checked after the avatar-selection die is shown. Once it becomes true, the sequence starts closing the mirror and requests a 2.5-game-time-second pause. After that pause, the sequence disables the mirror and gallows pin, calls this controller's Reveal, then disables the drop gate and requests intro music cue 0. Reveal requests the configured nooseReveal sound at the noose component's world position, meaning its position in the level.
That Reveal call only requests audio; the inspected body does not enable noose geometry or start hanging physics. The reference must be assigned for this sequence stage to proceed.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Descent.playerAvatarDecorator
member.summary: Selects the avatar override component that Descent prevents from swapping the player's avatar when resuming a save.

remarks.para: Start is the startup routine called when this control begins running. It copies the inherited IsResuming flag before calling the inherited startup routine. If that copied value is true, it sets this component's preventSwap flag true. Its OnLevelLoad and SwapAvatar routines check preventSwap before requesting the configured override avatar, so this avoids that override on a resumed run.

This reference does not perform height calibration. The fresh-start branch does not reset preventSwap; changing the reference or clearing the flag after a load does not itself request a new avatar swap.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Descent.playerHealth
member.summary: Caches the player health component whose reload-on-death setting Descent changes during startup and progression.

remarks.para: The level-load callback fills this reference from the player rig if it is missing. The player rig is the group of components that tracks and simulates the player’s body. A callback is a routine called when an operation reaches a particular point. On a fresh intro it enables reloadLevelOnDeath before starting the scripted sequence.

levelLoaded is this control’s true/false callback-completion flag. The callback sets it true after starting the fresh intro coroutine, a sequence that pauses and continues over frames, or after releasing the player on a resumed save. DISABLEDEATHRELOAD later clears that health setting only when this flag is true. That prevents this reload-on-death path without restoring health or making the player invincible. Changing this cached reference changes which health component those later calls affect.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Descent.sfx_MirrorVoidParticles
member.summary: Selects the optional sound player triggered when the mirror and its spawn particles are enabled.

remarks.para: The main sequence checks this reference before calling SIMPLEPLAY. It does so after closing the height area and its following 1-game-time-second pause, before the mirror-particle scale animation begins. A missing sound player skips this playback without skipping the mirror animation.
The assigned sound player's configuration supplies the audio. Changing this reference affects later requests rather than the particle curves or how long the mirror remains visible.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Descent.sfx_radioIntro
member.summary: Selects the radio sound player requested after the drop milestone and a configured 1.5-game-time-second wait.

remarks.para: gate_drop is the true/false drop-stage milestone flag set by SEQUENCE(5). True passes this wait; the check does not verify that a fall has finished. After that flag passes, the sequence waits 1.5 game-time seconds, calls this player's SIMPLEPLAY, waits another 0.5 seconds, then requests the lightning sound. These are configured waits that resume on later frames; game speed and frame timing affect elapsed real time.
This reference is required at that playback stage. Reassigning it changes which player receives the future request, not the stored contents or length of the configured sound.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Descent.torchPit
member.summary: Selects the spawner asked to create its configured object when Descent resumes a save.

remarks.para: A level-load callback is a routine called when level loading reaches its callback stage. This callback calls SpawnSpawnable on this spawner only on the resuming path, then continues with the death-reload guard and releasing the player. SpawnSpawnable starts asynchronous work, which can finish later, so returning from the callback does not prove an object has spawned successfully.

A crate is an asset reference identifying the object template to load. The spawner caches the resolved crate reference and pool policy during setup or when SetSpawnable is called. Pool policy means the rules for limiting and reusing spawned objects. With query selection turned off, the crate reference comes from spawnableCrateReference; changing that field later does not automatically refresh the cache. The asset warehouse, the game’s library of object assets, must be ready when GetCrateReference runs; otherwise it returns null, which setup can cache, and the spawn routine exits without requesting object creation while that cached reference is null. Transform is the Unity component that supplies an object’s position and rotation. The spawner’s Transform supplies its world-space position and rotation when the spawn request starts. World space expresses these values in the scene’s coordinates rather than relative to the parent; a parent transform can still affect this world pose. The position uses Unity world units; this spawn path establishes no conversion to meters. These values are read at request time and are not saved in the setup cache. This controller does not select a specific torch object template or wait for successful spawn completion.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Descent.voidFrame
member.summary: Caches the drawing component whose material is animated while the mirror opens and closes.

remarks.para: A level-load callback is a routine called when loading reaches its callback stage. This callback gets a Renderer from module_MirrorVoidFrame and stores it here. A Renderer is Unity's drawing component, and its material contains appearance settings. Reassigning module_MirrorVoidFrame afterward does not refresh this cached component.

MirrorInProgress starts its stored progress at -0.2 and adds 0.5 progress units per game-time second multiplied by the game-time seconds since the previous frame. It writes that updated value to the material, continuing on frames until progress reaches or passes 1. MirrorOutProgress starts its stored value at 1 and subtracts the same amount, writing the updated value until progress reaches or passes -0.2. The stored starting value is not separately written before the first change. For example, a 0.02-second frame adds 0.01, so the first opening write is -0.19. Progress is dimensionless, meaning it has no physical units; each animation takes about 2.4 game-time seconds, with a possible final-frame overshoot. The material determines the visual response.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Holodeck.UI
member.summary: Identifies the Holodeck UI root object that this controller hides during startup.

remarks.para: UI means user interface: the onscreen controls and display. A GameObject is a Unity scene object holding components; its hierarchy means that object and its children. Start calls SetActive(false) on this object before registering the level-load callback. Disabling a GameObject hides its hierarchy and prevents its enabled components from running normally.

The complete inspected controller methods do not enable this root again during material changes or door-cover toggles. Showing it requires another scene system or caller to activate it. Provide the reference before Start; the startup path does not skip a missing UI root.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Holodeck.beachAmbience
member.summary: Supplies the background sound recording requested by the timed transition for preset 3 (beach).

remarks.para: The timed routine copies this AudioClip into clipMain on both zoneAmbience objects, then asks the global ambience manager to use it at a volume factor of 0.1 with configured 1-second fade-in and fade-out times. AudioClip means the stored sound recording; the volume factor is unitless and 1 means the recording's unscaled level.

The audio manager can adjust an already playing matching clip rather than restarting it. The fade request is made before panel updates finish, so the sound and the final lighting need not change at the same moment.

Assigning a different clip here does not immediately replace the current sound. The timed routine reads it when preparing this preset, and the two zones keep the clip reference copied at that time for their own later activation. The fast CYCLEMATERIAL routine and SetSky do not select this ambience.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Holodeck.cityAmbience
member.summary: Supplies the background sound recording requested by the timed transition for preset 4 (city).

remarks.para: The timed routine copies this AudioClip into clipMain on both zoneAmbience objects, then asks the global ambience manager to use it at a volume factor of 0.1 with configured 1-second fade-in and fade-out times. AudioClip means the stored sound recording; the volume factor is unitless and 1 means the recording's unscaled level.

The audio manager can adjust an already playing matching clip rather than restarting it. The fade request is made before panel updates finish, so the sound and the final lighting need not change at the same moment.

Assigning a different clip here does not immediately replace the current sound. The timed routine reads it when preparing this preset, and the two zones keep the clip reference copied at that time for their own later activation. The fast CYCLEMATERIAL routine and SetSky do not select this ambience.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Holodeck.cubemaps
member.summary: Stores each visual preset's two reflection images and its saved directional ambient-light data.

remarks.para: The lighting data is a pair of cubemaps plus saved spherical-harmonic numbers. A cubemap is a six-sided image of the surroundings, used here for reflections. Spherical harmonics are a small set of numbers describing the color and brightness of light arriving from different directions.

A reflection probe is a Unity component supplying an environment image for reflective surfaces. Here, the controller assigns already stored images. Each ProbePair contains cubemap0, cubemap1, and harmonics. SetSky uses the chosen entry to fill the first two reflection probes, copies harmonics into the live global ambient-light setting, and assigns cubemap0 as the global custom reflection texture.
The preset index should line up with wallMaterials. A panel transition finishes by applying lighting with the same selected index; OnLevelLoad independently applies entry 0.

GenerateSHs rebuilds each entry's harmonics from cubemap0 only, using 4096 random directions across that image. Replacing a cubemap does not automatically rebuild the saved numbers, and editing them does not update the already copied live data until SetSky runs again. Provide valid pair objects and at least entry 0 for loading.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Holodeck.desertAmbience
member.summary: Supplies the background sound recording requested by the timed transition for preset 2 (desert).

remarks.para: The timed routine copies this AudioClip into clipMain on both zoneAmbience objects, then asks the global ambience manager to use it at a volume factor of 0.1 with configured 1-second fade-in and fade-out times. AudioClip means the stored sound recording; the volume factor is unitless and 1 means the recording's unscaled level.

The audio manager can adjust an already playing matching clip rather than restarting it. The fade request is made before panel updates finish, so the sound and the final lighting need not change at the same moment.

Assigning a different clip here does not immediately replace the current sound. The timed routine reads it when preparing this preset, and the two zones keep the clip reference copied at that time for their own later activation. The fast CYCLEMATERIAL routine and SetSky do not select this ambience.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Holodeck.doorCheckImage
member.summary: Identifies the UI image whose drawing flag is matched to the door-cover toggle.

remarks.para: TOGGLEDOOR sets this image's enabled flag to the new doorHide active state for nonzero selections. Enabling an Image permits it to draw; disabling it hides that image without changing its sprite or color.

The fast routine disables the image for index 0. The timed routine also disables it for index 0, but that write is inside the light loop and is skipped when lights is empty. Neither routine enables it merely because a nonzero preset was selected.
It is a display reference, not a test that the physical door is open or closed. Provide the reference before door-cover toggling and index-0 cover setup.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Holodeck.doorHide
member.summary: Identifies the door-cover object whose visibility the controller can switch.

remarks.para: TOGGLEDOOR flips this object's own active flag for nonzero selections and matches the check image to that flag. At selection 0 it does nothing.

The fast routine disables the object for index 0 and enables it for other indices. The timed routine disables it for index 0 inside the light-object loop; an empty light list skips that update. For nonzero indices, the timed routine changes the cover renderer's material but leaves this object's active flag unchanged.

This is a configured scene object, not a saved open/closed state. Activating it enables its hierarchy; whether that visually covers an entrance depends on the scene setup. These methods do not directly animate a physical door.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Holodeck.doorHideRenderer
member.summary: Receives the selected wall material on the door-cover surface when the selection is nonzero.

remarks.para: Both material routines set this renderer's material from wallMaterials at materialIndex in their nonzero branch. A renderer draws the object's surface; assigning its material changes appearance, not the object's active flag.

At index 0 these routines leave its material unchanged. The cover can still be hidden separately through doorHide. The fast routine activates that object for nonzero selections, while the timed routine leaves its existing active flag alone.
TOGGLEDOOR does not read this renderer. Give it the renderer for the intended cover surface, and provide the reference before using a nonzero material selection.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Holodeck.hugeRoomReverb
member.summary: Supplies the large-room echo settings requested by the timed transition for preset indices 0, 5.

remarks.para: AudioReverbData is a saved group of reverb settings: controls for the reflections and fading tail of sound that make a space sound large, enclosed, or open. It is a settings object, not a duration in seconds.

For these indices, the timed routine copies this reference to reverbSettings on both zoneAmbience objects and asks the global audio manager to fade toward it. The manager saves a target and starts its own transition, so making the request does not mean all mixer settings have already reached it.

Changing this field alone does not request a new fade or replace the copies held by the zones. It is read when the timed routine prepares a matching preset. The fast editor routine and SetSky do not apply these reverb presets.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Holodeck.lights
member.summary: Lists scene objects enabled for selection 0 and disabled for nonzero panel selections.

remarks.para: These are GameObject references, rather than individual numeric light brightness settings. Activating or disabling each object affects its whole hierarchy, so it can include a light component and related objects.

Both material routines change these objects near their beginning. The timed routine's index-0 loop also hides the cover, disables the check image, and requests the large-room reverb once per light. With an empty lights array, those per-light effects are skipped, although the later preset audio branch still handles its own reverb request.
The fast routine handles the cover and image outside its light loop. Use valid object entries; changing this list does not immediately change their active states until a routine runs.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Holodeck.matCycle
member.summary: Stores the iterator last started by a material-selection method so it can be stopped before another transition.

remarks.para: An iterator holds the progress of a coroutine, a routine that can pause and resume on later frames. CYCLEMATERIAL and SELECTMATERIAL stop this saved iterator when it exists, then replace it and start the new routine.
The timed routine clears this field after its final lighting update. The fast editor routine leaves the finished iterator stored, so a nonnull value does not prove that a transition is still running.
This stores an iterator, not Unity's separate Coroutine handle. Assigning it alone does not start or resume a routine, and stopping a saved routine does not undo changes already applied.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Holodeck.materialIndex
member.summary: Stores the selected preset number requested for panel and environment changes.

remarks.para: This is a zero-based index: 0 means the first entry. It selects a wallMaterials entry for panel appearance and the matching cubemaps entry for final lighting. It is not a count or an indication that the transition has finished. CYCLEMATERIAL increments it with wrapping; SELECTMATERIAL replaces it immediately before starting the timed routine.

Panel and lighting changes happen as the selected routine runs, so this number can be ahead of the currently visible panels. The timed routine updates lighting only at the end. Setting this field alone does not start a transition.

The fixed audio routing is 0: ship, 1: space, 2: desert, 3: beach, 4: city, 5: stadium, 6: meadow, and 7: void. The visual materials can be replaced, but these audio meanings remain tied to the numbers. Valid visual indices above 7 still update panels and lighting but do not select new ambience or reverb in this routine.
TOGGLEDOOR ignores requests when this is 0. SetSky takes its own index argument and OnLevelLoad applies lighting for 0 without changing this stored selection.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Holodeck.maxPanelTicTime
member.summary: Sets the upper limit of the random requested wait before each panel in the timed transition, in seconds of scaled game time.

remarks.para: A coroutine is a routine Unity can pause and resume, and a frame is one game-update step. The timed routine chooses a duration from 0 to this value and yields a wait before changing each panel, including the first. This is not a fixed pause and is not the duration of the whole transition.

Scaled game time follows the game clock: slowing or pausing that clock also slows or pauses these waits. For example, 0.1 requests up to one tenth of a game-clock second before each panel. Actual elapsed time can be longer because the coroutine resumes on a later frame. A zero requested wait still passes through the coroutine's waiting step.

The constructor starts this field at 0.1 seconds; saved settings can override it. It is read for each new panel wait, so changing it can affect later waits in an ongoing timed transition. The fast editor routine does not use it. Use a nonnegative duration.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Holodeck.meadowAmbience
member.summary: Supplies the background sound recording requested by the timed transition for preset 6 (meadow).

remarks.para: The timed routine copies this AudioClip into clipMain on both zoneAmbience objects, then asks the global ambience manager to use it at a volume factor of 0.1 with configured 1-second fade-in and fade-out times. AudioClip means the stored sound recording; the volume factor is unitless and 1 means the recording's unscaled level.

The audio manager can adjust an already playing matching clip rather than restarting it. The fade request is made before panel updates finish, so the sound and the final lighting need not change at the same moment.

Assigning a different clip here does not immediately replace the current sound. The timed routine reads it when preparing this preset, and the two zones keep the clip reference copied at that time for their own later activation. The fast CYCLEMATERIAL routine and SetSky do not select this ambience.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Holodeck.outsideReverb
member.summary: Supplies the outdoor echo settings requested by the timed transition for preset indices 1, 2, 3, 4, 6.

remarks.para: AudioReverbData is a saved group of reverb settings: controls for the reflections and fading tail of sound that make a space sound large, enclosed, or open. It is a settings object, not a duration in seconds.

For these indices, the timed routine copies this reference to reverbSettings on both zoneAmbience objects and asks the global audio manager to fade toward it. The manager saves a target and starts its own transition, so making the request does not mean all mixer settings have already reached it.

Changing this field alone does not request a new fade or replace the copies held by the zones. It is read when the timed routine prepares a matching preset. The fast editor routine and SetSky do not apply these reverb presets.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Holodeck.probes
member.summary: Supplies the two reflection-probe targets that receive the selected cubemap pair.

remarks.para: The lighting data is a pair of cubemaps plus saved spherical-harmonic numbers. A cubemap is a six-sided image of the surroundings, used here for reflections. Spherical harmonics are a small set of numbers describing the color and brightness of light arriving from different directions.

A reflection probe is a Unity component supplying an environment image for reflective surfaces. Here, the controller assigns already stored images. SetSky assigns cubemap0 to probes[0].customBakedTexture and cubemap1 to probes[1].customBakedTexture. These are zero-based entries: the first and second probes. Further entries are left untouched.

Provide at least two valid probe references before the level-load callback or a completed material transition applies lighting. The method assigns custom textures without rendering the probes or changing their mode, so their scene settings must be appropriate for using custom reflection data.
GenerateSHs reads the stored cubemaps directly; it does not obtain new images from this probe array. Changing the array does not itself update its new targets until lighting is applied again.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Holodeck.wallMaterials
member.summary: Supplies the surface material selected for the wall panels and, for nonzero selections, the door-cover renderer.

remarks.para: A material is the settings controlling a surface's appearance. A renderer is the component drawing that surface, and a slot is one material entry on it. The array uses zero-based indices: 0 is the first material. CYCLEMATERIAL increments the stored selection and wraps using this array's length; SELECTMATERIAL uses the exact index supplied by the caller.

Keep its entries aligned with the cubemaps lighting-preset array, because finishing a panel transition uses the same index for lighting. The fixed audio routing for indices 0 through 7 also remains tied to those numbers, even if you replace their visual materials.

Changing an array entry does not by itself update panels already drawn. The fast routine reads it during its update; the timed routine prepares two-slot and four-slot material arrays at startup, so those cached arrays keep their chosen material during that transition. Other slot counts read the current wallMaterials entry and materialIndex after each panel's wait, then change the first slot. For example, replacing the selected array entry between waits can change a later first-slot update while a later two- or four-slot panel still receives the earlier captured material. Use a new selection call to restart the transition cleanly.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Holodeck.wallPanels
member.summary: Lists the renderers whose material slots are replaced when a panel transition runs.

remarks.para: A material controls a surface's appearance. A renderer is the component that draws it, and a material slot is one surface-material entry on that renderer. Panels with two or four slots receive the selected material in every slot. Other slot counts use the single-material setter, which changes the first slot.

Both routines shuffle this array in place, so the stored order is not preserved. The timed routine waits before each renderer and changes them one by one; the fast editor routine changes all renderers after its initial frame pause.

The selected material comes from wallMaterials at materialIndex. Use valid renderer references. An empty list changes no panels but still lets the routine reach its lighting update. Editing the array alone does not apply a new material.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Holodeck.zoneAmbience0
member.summary: Receives the selected clip and reverb settings so this ambience zone can use the current timed preset.

remarks.para: For preset indices 0 through 7, the timed routine copies the matching ambience AudioClip into clipMain and the matching echo-settings reference into reverbSettings. Both zone references receive the same values; they are not alternating crossfade tracks in this controller.

An ambience zone is a region whose entry event can ask for background sound and reverb. Its own volume and fade-time settings are preserved. The controller separately requests immediate global ambience and reverb transitions through the audio manager; those fades are not performed by switching between these two zone fields.

Provide both references for the fixed presets. Changing this reference alone does not copy the current preset into the new zone. The next timed preset setup performs the copies; the fast editor routine and SetSky do not.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.ArenaKeyPlaced
member.summary: Save-entry name for whether the Arena module key has been inserted.

remarks.para: The string value is SLZ.Bonelab.ArenaKeyPlaced. DataRead reads this boolean from the shared Hub save section into isKeyInserted[1], and DataWrite copies that runtime flag back. Missing flags read as false. For example, KEYINSERTED(1) records this state and refreshes the game’s displays.
This is a string identifying a saved value, not the current true/false state or a physical key object.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.ArenaKeyUnlocked
member.summary: Save-entry name for whether the Arena module key has been made available.

remarks.para: The string value is SLZ.Bonelab.ArenaKeyUnlocked. DataRead reads this boolean from the shared Hub save section into isKeyUnlock[1], and DataWrite copies that runtime flag back. Missing flags read as false. For example, UNLOCKKEY(1) records this state and refreshes the game’s displays.
This is a string identifying a saved value, not the current true/false state or a physical key object.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.BWBox
member.summary: The Big Walk box entity that Hub setup hides after the game is finished.

remarks.para: GameDone and OnLevelLoad hide this entity when isGameFinished is true and disable flooring separately. BWBOXDESTROYED reports that a box break occurred and starts the conditional floor/seat progression, but does not destroy this reference itself. Keep it assigned to the box entity that should be hidden.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.BatteryAPlaced
member.summary: Save-entry name for whether generator battery A has been recorded as inserted.

remarks.para: The string value is SLZ.Bonelab.BatteryAPlaced. DataRead loads this boolean from the shared Hub section into isBattery1Inserted; missing entries read as false. DataWrite saves that flag. SetupKeys uses a true restored flag to hide the loose battery and request its seated replacement.
For a new insertion, BATTERYINSERTED(0, false) records it and refreshes progress. This saved flag does not prove that a replacement spawn has finished or that the generator is powered.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.BatteryBPlaced

remarks.para: The string value is SLZ.Bonelab.BatteryBPlaced. DataRead loads this boolean from the shared Hub section into isBattery2Inserted; missing entries read as false. DataWrite saves that flag. SetupKeys uses a true restored flag to hide the loose battery and request its seated replacement.
For a new insertion, BATTERYINSERTED(1, false) records it and refreshes progress. This saved flag does not prove that a replacement spawn has finished or that the generator is powered.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.ElevatorBroken
member.summary: Save-entry name for whether the Hub elevator breakout has been recorded.

remarks.para: The string value is SLZ.Bonelab.ElevatorBroken, a boolean in the shared Hub save section. ELEVATORBREAKOUT checks it to avoid repeating its music/save actions, then writes true and saves respawn index 10. DataRead forces its cached respawn index to 9 when this flag is missing or false.
This is a saved progression marker, not a live test of the elevator’s physical damage.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.HubSpawnLocation
member.summary: Save-entry name for the integer index selecting a Hub resume point.

remarks.para: The string value is SLZ.Bonelab.HubSpawnLocation in the shared Hub save section. DataRead copies the number into _loadedTeleportSpot; Teleport uses that cached number as an index into hubSpawnPoints. For example, 10 means list entry 10, the eleventh entry, rather than a position in meters.

A missing value starts at 0, but a missing or false ElevatorBroken flag makes DataRead use 9 instead. Changing the saved value does not immediately move the player or update an already-loaded cache. The list must contain the selected index.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.JimmyKeyPlaced
member.summary: Save-entry name for whether Jimmy’s key has been recorded as inserted.

remarks.para: The string value is SLZ.Bonelab.JimmyKeyPlaced, a boolean in the shared Hub section. DataRead copies it into isJimmyKeyInserted and DataWrite saves that flag. SetupKeys restores the board’s insertion state and, when the key is also unlocked, shows jimmyKey_Inserted.
This recorded flag is one of the checks for opening the Big Walk door and entering its seat sequence. The string is not the current boolean value or the seated key object.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.JimmyKeyUnlocked
member.summary: Save-entry name for whether Jimmy’s key is available during Hub restore.

remarks.para: The string value is SLZ.Bonelab.JimmyKeyUnlocked, a boolean in the shared Hub section. DataRead reads it into isJimmyKeyUnlocked; SetupKeys can show the loose key when unlocked and not inserted, or the seated key when it is inserted.

DataWrite does not write this particular flag, even though UNLOCKJIMMYKEY updates it in memory and calls DataWrite. Code that needs this state saved must ensure that the saved flag is written separately.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.LabPoweredOn
member.summary: Save-entry name for whether lab power has been recorded in shared Hub progression.

remarks.para: The string value is SLZ.Bonelab.LabPoweredOn. DataRead loads this boolean into isLabPowered and DataWrite saves that runtime flag. A missing value reads as false, although normal-mode restore can also treat a readable LongRun completion record as powered.
SetupKeys applies restored power by setting generatorPower and slzSignBypass outputs to 1. Changing this saved entry alone does not immediately apply those outputs in a running level.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.LevelKey
member.summary: Returns the Hub stage’s save identifier from the active player progression.

remarks.para: Returns Hub_C when BeatGame is true. Otherwise it returns Hub_B when BodyLogEnabled is true, and Hub_A when false. BeatGame takes priority when both flags are true. For example, enabling the BodyLog before beating the game changes this result from Hub_A to Hub_B.
This is calculated from the active save each time it is read. It is different from the shared Hub identifier used to store key, battery and respawn flags; it does not itself load another level.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.LevelKeyA
member.summary: Save identifier Hub_A for the Hub stage before the BodyLog is enabled and before the game is beaten.

remarks.para: LevelKey chooses among the three stage identifiers from the active save: BeatGame selects Hub_C first; otherwise BodyLogEnabled selects Hub_B, and the remaining case selects Hub_A. These stage identifiers organize stage inventory and progression; key, battery and respawn flags use the shared Hub section.
The constant identifies saved data. Selecting or reading it does not immediately load a scene.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.OneTrueLevelKey
member.summary: Shared save identifier Hub, which groups the Hub’s keys, batteries, power and respawn progress across its campaign stages.

remarks.para: The value is Hub. HubUtilities reads and writes the named boolean flags in this shared section, and DataRead/DataWrite store the respawn index there. It also holds the migrated initial inventory. LevelKey instead returns Hub_A, Hub_B or Hub_C for a particular campaign stage.
For example, an ArenaKeyPlaced flag belongs to the shared Hub section rather than being a separate flag for each of the three stage identifiers.
