member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.isAllInserted
member.summary: Cached result of checking whether every module-key insertion flag is true, required for Big Walk door and seat progression.

remarks.para: CheckTotal scans isKeyInserted and stops at the first false entry. For the normal six entries, true means all six are recorded as inserted. An empty array leaves the previous result unchanged.

OPENBWDOOR checks this result together with Jimmy’s inserted key and its own request flag. The box-destruction and box-entry paths also use it before removing the floor and requesting the seat sequence. Jimmy’s key and both batteries are separate from this all-module result.
Changing an insertion flag directly does not recalculate this cache. The key-reporting methods call CheckTotal after changing their flags.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.isBWBoxBroken
member.summary: Records that BWBOXDESTROYED reported the Big Walk box as broken and enables the later box-entry seat path.

remarks.para: BWBOXDESTROYED sets this true before checking the keys or removing the floor. ENTERBWBOXVOL uses it together with isAllInserted and isJimmyKeyInserted before starting the backup load, disabling flooring and asking seatTrigger.Yoink to begin the seat movement.
It is a reported runtime state, not a scan of the box or proof that this method physically destroyed it. DataWrite does not save this field in the inspected Hub save routine.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.isBWDoorOpen
member.summary: One-shot flag recording that the Big Walk door release sequence was requested successfully.

remarks.para: OPENBWDOOR requires this false, all module keys recorded as inserted and Jimmy’s key recorded as inserted. It sets the flag true before constructing and starting BWBoxSequence, a coroutine that pauses and continues across later frames.

The sequence still has sounds, waits and lock-bar releases to perform before disabling doorStopper. This flag therefore does not confirm the physical door is already open. A repeat request invokes bwDoorLocked. The inspected Hub routines do not clear this flag afterward.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.isBattery1Inserted
member.summary: Recorded insertion progress for generator battery A, checked before generator startup.

remarks.para: BATTERYINSERTED(0, fromSave) sets this true before any saved-state object restoration. DataRead loads it from the shared Hub boolean SLZ.Bonelab.BatteryAPlaced, and DataWrite saves it. LABPOWERED also sets both battery flags true.
CheckGeneratorStatus can start or stop its stored startup sequence only while both battery flags are true and isLabPowered is false. Reporting this flag true does not start the generator by itself.

SetupKeys rebuilds a recorded inserted battery by hiding battery1 and requesting battery1_Inserted once. The separate battery1Placed flag records that spawn request; neither flag proves a physical spawn finished successfully or that a battery is currently touching the socket.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.isBattery2Inserted
member.summary: Recorded insertion progress for generator battery B, checked before generator startup.

remarks.para: BATTERYINSERTED(1, fromSave) sets this true before any saved-state object restoration. DataRead loads it from the shared Hub boolean SLZ.Bonelab.BatteryBPlaced, and DataWrite saves it. LABPOWERED also sets both battery flags true.
CheckGeneratorStatus can start or stop its stored startup sequence only while both battery flags are true and isLabPowered is false. Reporting this flag true does not start the generator by itself.

SetupKeys rebuilds a recorded inserted battery by hiding battery2 and requesting battery2_Inserted once. The separate battery2Placed flag records that spawn request; neither flag proves a physical spawn finished successfully or that a battery is currently touching the socket.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.isGameFinished
member.summary: Finished-Hub flag that makes load/setup hide the Big Walk box and disable its floor.

remarks.para: OnLevelLoad checks this flag after rebuilding the keys and displays. If true, it hides BWBox and disables flooring. GameDone uses the same condition and effects.

These consumers act when their methods run; setting this flag directly does not immediately hide either object. The inspected Hub methods do not set it from the active save’s BeatGame flag, so a caller must supply the desired value.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.isGateUnlock
member.summary: Runtime flag slot with no verified gate-release effect in the inspected Hub methods.

remarks.para: The complete inspected GameControl_Hub methods and nested routines do not read or write this slot. The Big Walk release instead uses isAllInserted and isJimmyKeyInserted to accept a request, then changes lock-bar joints and disables doorStopper.
Setting this flag alone has no demonstrated effect in those routines. This scoped finding does not rule out another component or external code using the slot.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.isInBWBoxVolume
member.summary: Reported box-volume occupancy used when box destruction decides whether to start the seat and backup-load sequence.

remarks.para: ENTERBWBOXVOL sets this true before checking all module keys, Jimmy’s inserted key and the broken-box flag. When those checks pass, it starts the backup sequence, removes the floor, and requests seatTrigger.Yoink.

BWBOXDESTROYED also checks this flag after the key checks and floor removal, so breaking the box while occupancy is already reported can start that path. EXITBWBOXVOL only sets this false: it does not cancel a backup sequence already started or restore the floor.
This flag comes from those occupancy-reporting calls. It does not perform its own collision scan.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.isJimmyKeyInserted
member.summary: Recorded Jimmy-key insertion progress required by the Big Walk release and seat paths.

remarks.para: JIMMYKEYINSERTED sets this true before notifying progressBoard. DataRead loads the shared Hub boolean SLZ.Bonelab.JimmyKeyPlaced, and DataWrite saves it.

OPENBWDOOR requires this together with isAllInserted and an unused release request. ENTERBWBOXVOL and BWBOXDESTROYED use it in their floor/seat checks. It also prevents the special spawn-9 elevator setup branch from playing its intro cue.
When restoring saved state, SetupKeys shows jimmyKey_Inserted only if Jimmy’s key is also unlocked. The progress flag does not itself measure whether the physical key currently occupies a slot.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.isJimmyKeyUnlocked
member.summary: Recorded availability of Jimmy’s key, associated with the shared save key, used when restoring its loose or inserted display.

remarks.para: DataRead reads the shared Hub boolean SLZ.Bonelab.JimmyKeyUnlocked. UNLOCKJIMMYKEY sets this flag true; saved-state setup can show jimmyKey when it is not inserted, or jimmyKey_Inserted when it is inserted.
DataWrite does not write this particular flag, even though UNLOCKJIMMYKEY calls DataWrite. A caller that needs its change to survive a reload must ensure the shared saved entry is written separately.
It is separate from isJimmyKeyInserted: making the key available does not satisfy the Big Walk insertion requirement.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.isKeyInserted
member.summary: Per-module recorded insertion flags matching that control key displays, inserted-key counts and the Big Walk all-key requirement.

remarks.para: Module index 0 is Tactical Trial, 1 Arena, 2 Sandbox, 3 Parkour, 4 Experimental, and 5 Mods. Keep matching key, flag, stopper and lamp arrays aligned to that order.

KEYINSERTED(i) sets entry i true, saves Hub progress, recalculates the all-key result and display, then refreshes the board. DataRead restores the six entries from their shared Hub placed flags; DataWrite saves them.

DisplayKeys hides each loose key when its insertion entry is true and shows its seated copy; false selects the loose copy instead. CountKeys counts true entries for the three-key large-door check. CheckTotal checks every entry for the Big Walk gate.
These are recorded progress flags, rather than live collision tests. Direct array edits do not automatically refresh the count, save or displays.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.isKeyUnlock
member.summary: Per-module availability flags matching that release the matching key stopper and restore the board’s unlocked state.

remarks.para: Module index 0 is Tactical Trial, 1 Arena, 2 Sandbox, 3 Parkour, 4 Experimental, and 5 Mods. Keep matching key, flag, stopper and lamp arrays aligned to that order.

UNLOCKKEY(i) sets entry i true, notifies the board, saves progress and refreshes the displays. DataRead restores the six shared Hub unlocked booleans, and DataWrite saves them. DisplayKeys deactivates keyStopperLocks[i] when the matching flag is true and counts unlocked entries into keyUnlock.

Unlocking and insertion are separate records. A true unlock entry does not increase keyCount, which counts isKeyInserted instead. Direct array edits need the appropriate refresh/save calls to update the board and visible state.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.isLabPowered
member.summary: Recorded lab-power progress that permits airlock access and enables the module menus when the display refreshes.

remarks.para: LABPOWERED sets this and both battery insertion flags true, then saves and refreshes the displays. GeneratorStartSequence sets it only after all three startup events and a further requested 0.3-second game-time wait.

DataRead restores SLZ.Bonelab.LabPoweredOn. In normal mode, a readable LongRun completion record can also make it true even if that record’s stored boolean is false. In old Hub mode, DisplayKeys makes it true after recounting at least three inserted module keys.

DisplayKeys uses it to enable the module-menu GameObjects and choose all three generator lamp materials. Large-door opening also needs at least three inserted keys. SetupKeys applies restored generatorPower and sign-bypass outputs, while the timed startup path separately enables the sign source later.
This progress flag is different from the electrical outputs and physical battery state. Setting it directly does not immediately apply every connected device’s output or finish startup.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.jimmyKey
member.summary: Loose Jimmy-key entity shown by saved-state setup when the key is unlocked but not inserted.

remarks.para: OnLevelLoad hides both Jimmy-key forms first. SetupKeys restores the loose form through UNLOCKJIMMYKEY(true) when the saved unlock flag is true and the insertion flag is false.
UNLOCKJIMMYKEY(false) records progress and refreshes the board without showing this entity through that path. Assign the loose key object separately from the seated jimmyKey_Inserted object.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.jimmyKey_Inserted
member.summary: Seated Jimmy-key entity shown during saved-state restore when the key is both unlocked and inserted.

remarks.para: OnLevelLoad initially hides both Jimmy-key forms. JIMMYKEYINSERTED(true), including the restored setup path, shows this entity only when isJimmyKeyUnlocked is true as well as the newly set insertion flag.

Reporting a new insertion with fromSave false updates progress and the board without showing this reference through that path. Assign this object to the key’s seated form; the progress flag and entity visibility are separate.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.keyCount
member.summary: Cached number of module keys recorded as inserted, used by large-door and old-mode access checks.

remarks.para: CountKeys and DisplayKeys reset it to zero and add one for each true isKeyInserted entry. With normal six-module setup its range is 0 through 6. Jimmy’s key and batteries are excluded.

OpenBigDoors calls CountKeys and requires at least 3 in either Hub mode. Old-mode DisplayKeys also uses 3 to mark lab power, while CheckAirLockOpenAnimStatus and CheckTotal can read the existing cached count.

For example, four unlocked keys but only two inserted keys produce keyCount 2. Direct flag edits do not refresh the cache until CountKeys or DisplayKeys runs. keyUnlock separately counts unlocked module keys.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.keyStopperLocks
member.summary: Per-module blocker GameObjects deactivated when the matching key-unlock flag is true.

remarks.para: Module index 0 is Tactical Trial, 1 Arena, 2 Sandbox, 3 Parkour, 4 Experimental, and 5 Mods. Keep matching key, flag, stopper and lamp arrays aligned to that order.

DisplayKeys calls SetActive(false) for an entry whose isKeyUnlock flag is true. Deactivating an object disables its active components, including any collider that blocks that key. A collider is the contact shape Unity uses to detect or block collisions.

The inspected loop leaves false-flag entries as they already are; it does not automatically reactivate a previously disabled stopper. This is an unlock-based display/setup effect, rather than an enforced sequence for inserting keys.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.keyUnlock
member.summary: Cached count of true module-key unlock flags, recomputed during DisplayKeys.

remarks.para: DisplayKeys resets this integer to zero, then adds one for every true isKeyUnlock entry while disabling that module’s stopper. With six module flags its range is 0 through 6.
It is a count, not the index of the most recently unlocked key. keyCount separately counts inserted keys for the large-door checks. Direct array edits do not update this cache until DisplayKeys runs.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.key_Inserted
member.summary: Seated module-key entities matching the loose keys in whose visibility follows the recorded insertion flags.

remarks.para: Module index 0 is Tactical Trial, 1 Arena, 2 Sandbox, 3 Parkour, 4 Experimental, and 5 Mods. Keep matching key, flag, stopper and lamp arrays aligned to that order.
OnLevelLoad initially hides both configured key forms. DisplayKeys then shows this seated form when isKeyInserted[i] is true and hides it when false.

A MarrowEntity groups an object and its physical parts. This array supplies visible objects, while isKeyInserted supplies recorded progress. The visibility decision uses insertion flags, not a physical check that a key is touching the reader.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.key_Modules
member.summary: Loose module-key entities whose visibility follows the recorded insertion flags.

remarks.para: Module index 0 is Tactical Trial, 1 Arena, 2 Sandbox, 3 Parkour, 4 Experimental, and 5 Mods. Keep matching key, flag, stopper and lamp arrays aligned to that order.
OnLevelLoad initially hides both configured key forms. DisplayKeys then hides this loose form when isKeyInserted[i] is true and shows it when false.

A MarrowEntity groups an object and its physical parts. This array supplies visible objects, while isKeyInserted supplies recorded progress. The visibility decision uses insertion flags, not a physical check that a key is touching the reader.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.klaxon
member.summary: Alarm clips requested when the Big Walk release starts its rotating-light sequence.

remarks.para: BWBoxSequence starts KlaxonLight after the radiation stage’s requested 14-second wait, then requests these clips at local (0, 0, 0) relative to bwDoorPismatic’s Transform. That places the sound at the configured SFX component’s position.

The sequence next requests a 2.5-second game-time wait before releasing bars. The clips are played through a separate audio request; the light routine does not itself play these clips or confirm their playback has finished.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.klaxonJoint
member.summary: Physics joint given the alarm light’s spin target during KlaxonLight.

remarks.para: A ConfigurableJoint constrains and drives a physics body relative to another body. KlaxonLight sets targetAngularVelocity to (2, 0, 0): a target of 2 radians per second around the target frame’s X axis, about 115 degrees per second, with zero targets on Y and Z. The joint’s configuredInWorldSpace setting chooses world axes when enabled; otherwise targets use its local frame. This routine does not change that setting.

After the routine’s accumulated game time is strictly greater than 22 seconds, it sets the target vector to zero. It ends at accumulated time at least 25 seconds. This is a requested spin target; the body’s actual speed depends on the configured joint, forces and collisions.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.klaxonLight
member.summary: Light enabled and smoothly brightened, then dimmed and disabled by the Big Walk alarm sequence.

remarks.para: KlaxonLight reads and caches this light’s current intensity at startup, sets intensity to zero, and enables it. Each later update moves intensity toward the cached value using SmoothDamp, which smooths a change over time, with a 0.3-second smoothing setting.

While accumulated game time is at most 22 seconds, the target is the cached intensity. After 22 seconds, the target becomes zero. At accumulated time at least 25 seconds, the routine disables the light before another intensity update. It accumulates Time.deltaTime, the game-time seconds since the previous frame, so frame boundaries affect the actual timestamps.

Intensity is Unity’s brightness setting, not a color value. The routine does not set the light’s color; configure that separately. Later changes to the initial intensity do not replace the already cached target.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.klaxonRB
member.summary: Physics body awakened when the alarm light’s spin target is first applied.

remarks.para: A Rigidbody lets Unity simulate an object’s motion. KlaxonLight sets klaxonJoint’s target angular velocity to (2, 0, 0) radians per second, then calls WakeUp on this body so sleeping physics can respond. A physics joint restricts and drives a simulated body. The vector requests rotation at 2 radians per second about the target X axis, with zero rotation targets on Y and Z. The joint’s configuredInWorldSpace setting selects world target axes when enabled and its local target frame otherwise; this routine leaves that setting unchanged.

The routine does not directly set this body’s velocity or repeatedly wake it every frame. Assign the body that belongs to the configured alarm-light joint; the joint settings determine its actual motion.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.labFloorChunk
member.summary: Separately loaded lab-floor area whose loaded state selects the airlock route.

remarks.para: A scene chunk is a part of a level that can load separately. AirlockEnter can request this chunk with airlockChunk when the lab floor is the currently loaded neighboring area.

AirlockExitCycle closes the large doors and loads the funicular side when the lab floor is loaded and funicularChunk is not. With the opposite loaded combination, it closes the small door and requests this lab-floor area before trying to open the large doors.
Those loading and door waits continue over later frames. This reference is not enabled automatically just by changing the isLabPowered progress flag.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.labModuleUIs
member.summary: Module-menu components whose GameObjects DisplayKeys activates according to recorded lab power.

remarks.para: DisplayKeys gets each component’s GameObject and sets its active state to isLabPowered. True enables the object; false disables the object and its active components, so the menus follow the power display refresh.
Changing isLabPowered directly does not update the menus until this refresh runs. In old Hub mode, the same refresh can mark lab power true once it has counted three inserted keys.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.layerMask
member.summary: Layer selection limiting which colliders the door-clearing overlap scan can find.

remarks.para: A layer groups Unity objects; a LayerMask selects groups by bits. A collider is an object’s contact shape. A trigger reports overlap without physically pushing objects. A MarrowEntity groups an object and its physical parts. DoorEmancipator passes this mask to its rotated box-overlap test. Trigger-only colliders are ignored even when their layers are selected.

Found colliders need an attached physics body and a recognized MarrowEntity before their entities can be collected for removal. Both configured door entities are protected, and repeated colliders on the same entity are combined into one removal.

For example, selecting a props layer allows props on that layer to be detected, while leaving it unselected excludes those colliders from this scan. An empty mask finds no layers. Keep the selection appropriate for the obstructing objects you want cleared.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.lockBar
member.summary: Big Walk lock-bar GameObjects whose joints and bodies are cached before the timed release sequence.

remarks.para: Start, Unity’s setup method before the component’s first regular updates, fetches each object’s ConfigurableJoint and Rigidbody into lockBarJoints and lockBarRB. A physics joint constrains movement; a Rigidbody provides the simulated body. The constructor allocates six cache slots, so this setup supports at most six configured bars unless the caches are resized elsewhere.

BWBoxSequence uses the cached joint/body for each release and the current lockBar entry’s Transform for its sound origin. It sets the joint’s X motion to Limited, which permits movement only within the joint’s configured limits, wakes the body, then requests a one-second game-time wait, including after the last cache entry.

The default release loop visits all six cache entries, so configure six usable bars with both required components. Keep this array and the component caches aligned. Replacing a bar after Start does not automatically refresh the cached joint or body, so sound and physics could refer to different objects.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.lockBarJoints
member.summary: Cached physics joints whose X-axis constraints are changed one at a time during the Big Walk release.

remarks.para: Start fetches the ConfigurableJoint on each lockBar GameObject into the matching cache slot. The constructor creates six slots. A physics joint constrains how bodies may move relative to each other.

BWBoxSequence loops over this cache, sets each joint’s xMotion to Limited, wakes the matching lockBarRB body, then requests a one-second wait. Limited permits motion within the configured limits; this code does not force a particular final bar position.

The default release loop visits all six cache entries; each needs an assigned joint and matching body and bar. These references are captured during setup. Replacing a lockBar object later does not rebuild the cache automatically; keep the joint, body and bar arrays aligned.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.lockBarRB
member.summary: Cached physics bodies awakened one at a time as the Big Walk lock-bar joints are released.

remarks.para: Start, Unity’s startup setup method, fetches the Rigidbody on each lockBar object into its matching cache slot; the constructor creates six slots. A Rigidbody lets Unity simulate an object’s motion.

BWBoxSequence changes the matching cached joint’s X motion to Limited, which allows motion only within its configured limits. A physics joint restricts how bodies move. The sequence then wakes this body so sleeping physics can respond. It requests a one-second wait before the next release. Waking the body does not directly choose its velocity or final position.

The default release loop visits all six cache entries, so each needs an assigned body and matching joint and bar. Keep this array aligned with lockBarJoints and lockBar. The references are captured during setup and do not update automatically when a bar object is replaced later.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.longRun
member.summary: Destination level reference selected by GOTOSCENE(1).

remarks.para: A level crate reference identifies a level asset. GOTOSCENE(1) updates the current Hub stage’s ammunition carryover, carries saved inventory toward this level and the shared Hub, and requests the fade/loading path. After that request, it raises MenuResume, the saved menu-resume progress number, to at least 2 and requests a save.

The request begins asynchronous work, which continues after this call returns. The selected level is loaded only through the later fade-completion action. The LongRun saved-completion record also participates in normal power restore and the one-shot airlock notification check.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.mat_Lamp
member.summary: Five indexed material roles applied to key, generator and airlock lamp renderers.

remarks.para: A material controls an object’s drawn appearance. The Hub uses index 0 for an uninserted/unavailable key display, index 1 for an inserted or avatar-unlocked display at an even module index, and index 2 for the corresponding odd module index.

Index 3 lights the counted-key progress lamps and powered generator/access lamps, and is applied by opening-door routines. Index 4 resets generator lamps while unpowered or early startup is canceled, and is applied when door-closing waits end. The middle airlock blink alternates indices 4 and 3 with requested 0.75-second game-time waits.

Provide at least five assigned materials. Their assets determine the colors; these consumers do not impose an off/on color pair. For example, the two parity materials can visually distinguish alternate key-reader positions.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.mat_StripLight
member.summary: Strip-light material array whose entry 1 is applied when the airlock-access check reaches its powered display path.

remarks.para: CheckAirLockOpenAnimStatus uses mat_StripLight[1] on every render_StripLight entry after its occupancy, power and one-shot checks pass; old Hub mode also checks three counted keys. A readable LongRun completion record can suppress the notification event while this material update still runs.

Provide at least two entries for that index. A material determines the strip’s appearance, and this code does not guarantee its color. The complete inspected Hub routines do not apply entry 0 as an automatic power-off counterpart.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.p
member.summary: Returns the active save’s , the player-progression object for reading and changing campaign and Hub records.

remarks.para: The getter reads DataManager.ActiveSave each time and returns its Progression object. This is a shared live object, not a copy or a saved snapshot. Changing the object changes memory; saving to disk still requires the appropriate save request.
An active save is required. The inspected getter has no fallback when ActiveSave is absent. The Hub’s data read/write and stage selection paths also obtain progression from the active save.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.progressBoard
member.summary: Board controller notified when Hub keys, batteries and power progress are restored or reported.

remarks.para: UNLOCKKEY records a module flag before calling BALLSACTIVE for that module. KEYINSERTED saves and refreshes the key display before calling UPDATEDBOARD and CheckProgressText. Jimmy-key insertion records its flag before calling the board’s KEYINSERTED notification.

Battery and explicit-power reporting also refresh the board after saving and updating the displays. Generator startup calls CheckActivation and CheckProgressText after setting the power flag. These calls supply the board’s progress feedback; assigning a board alone does not perform the Hub’s save or spawn work.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.quarantineDoorLocked
member.summary: Event invoked when OpenBigDoors rejects its large-airlock-door opening request.

remarks.para: A UnityEvent calls its configured listeners. This event supplies no arguments. Opening is rejected when lab power is false, bigDoorsOpening is already true, or the fresh inserted module-key count is below 3.
After invoking it, the routine cancels and clears airlockCoroutine when that source exists. This notification does not itself send a closing command or confirm that the door physically locked.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.quarantineDoorUnlocked
member.summary: One-shot event invoked when the powered airlock access check permits its entry notification.

remarks.para: A UnityEvent calls its configured listeners and supplies no arguments here. CheckAirLockOpenAnimStatus requires inAirLockProxy true, lab power true and hasPlayedAirlockProxy false; old Hub mode also requires cached keyCount at least 3.

If the LongRun completion record cannot be read, it sets hasPlayedAirlockProxy true first, invokes this event, then requests AIRLOCKENTERSOUTH. A readable completion record suppresses the event even if its saved boolean is false.

The subsequent entry and opening work continues over later frames and applies its own door checks. This event marks the access-notification path, rather than a guarantee that the physical door finished opening.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.radiation
member.summary: Radiation-warning clips requested between the warning and klaxon stages of the Big Walk release.

remarks.para: BWBoxSequence requests these clips after its first two configured two-second waits. It plays them at local (0, 0, 0) relative to bwDoorPismatic’s Transform, placing the sound at that SFX component’s position, then requests a 14-second game-time wait before the klaxon stage.
The sound request and sequence wait are separate. This field does not depend on the player standing under a lamp, and the wait does not confirm a clip finished playing.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.render_Lamp
member.summary: Per-module display objects whose child mesh renderers show the matching key-insertion state.

remarks.para: Module index 0 is Tactical Trial, 1 Arena, 2 Sandbox, 3 Parkour, 4 Experimental, and 5 Mods. Keep matching key, flag, stopper and lamp arrays aligned to that order.

DisplayKeys finds each object’s child MeshRenderers and applies mat_Lamp[0] when the matching isKeyInserted entry is false. An inserted key uses material 1 at an even index or material 2 at an odd index.

A mesh renderer draws an object’s visible surface. These entries are the module/key display objects searched for child renderers, rather than ceiling lights automatically switched by lab power. The material assets determine their colors.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.render_LockLamp
member.summary: Per-module lamp renderers whose materials reflect the matching avatar asset’s unlock count.

remarks.para: Module index 0 is Tactical Trial, 1 Arena, 2 Sandbox, 3 Parkour, 4 Experimental, and 5 Mods. Keep matching key, flag, stopper and lamp arrays aligned to that order.

DisplayKeys checks the player’s unlock count for avatarCrates[i] using its barcode, the identifier for that avatar asset. A count above zero applies mat_Lamp[1] at an even index or mat_Lamp[2] at an odd index; zero applies material 0.

Keep these lamp and avatar arrays aligned. This unlock display is separate from render_Lamp, whose child renderers show whether the module key is inserted. A renderer draws the lamp, and its assigned material defines its appearance.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.render_StripLight
member.summary: Strip-light renderers switched to mat_StripLight[1] when the airlock access check reaches its powered display path.

remarks.para: A renderer draws each strip’s visible surface. CheckAirLockOpenAnimStatus applies that material to every entry after the occupancy, power and notification-guard checks pass. Old Hub mode additionally needs three counted inserted keys.

A readable LongRun completion record can skip the unlock event while still reaching this material update. The material controls the appearance. The inspected Hub routines do not automatically restore another strip material whenever power is cleared.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.sceneExitTriggers
member.summary: Configured GameObject array with no verified scene-exit action in the inspected Hub methods.

remarks.para: The complete inspected GameControl_Hub methods and nested routines do not read or activate these entries. The verified level-switch path is GOTOSCENE, which selects longRun or ascent and requests fade-before-load work.

Assigning objects here alone therefore has no demonstrated loading effect in those routines. Any trigger component or event binding on an assigned object needs its own behavior configured. This scoped finding does not rule out external code using the array.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.seatTrigger
member.summary: Seat controller asked to begin the Big Walk seat-pull sequence after the box and key checks pass.

remarks.para: ENTERBWBOXVOL sets occupancy, then requires all module keys, Jimmy’s inserted key and the broken-box flag before starting BackUpYoinkLoad, disabling flooring and calling Yoink on this controller. BWBOXDESTROYED can request the same seat path if occupancy was already reported.

Yoink starts a coroutine, a sequence that continues across frames, only if the seat controller has no stored pull sequence. It requests the player’s entry into its Seat and later moves its configured Rigidbody between the controller’s start and end points. A Rigidbody supplies the object Unity simulates. A Transform stores an object’s position, rotation and scale. The pull reads the start and end Transforms’ world positions during movement and writes the body’s Transform world position between them, in scene length units (meters at normal Unity scale). World positions are measured in the scene’s shared coordinate frame; the endpoints are read during movement rather than captured once.

The Hub also runs a separate backup: after a configured 10-second game-time wait it requests GOTOSCENE(2), the ascent destination. Leaving the box clears occupancy but does not cancel that already started backup.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.slzSign
member.summary: Sign power-source output set to 1 near the end of normal generator startup.

remarks.para: After the three startup events, GeneratorStartSequence requests 0.3 seconds, records lab power, refreshes the board and saves. In normal Hub mode it then checks airlock access, requests another 0.3-second wait and sets this output to 1. Old Hub mode finishes earlier and skips that final output write.

The value 1 is a circuit signal, not a measurement in volts or watts. Connected devices determine its visible effect. A true isLabPowered flag can precede this applied output, and the configured waits resume on later frames.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.slzSignBypass
member.summary: Alternate sign power-source output set to 1 by powered saved-state setup.

remarks.para: SetupKeys sets this source and generatorPower to output value 1 when isLabPowered is true. The value is a circuit signal, not a measurement in volts or watts. The connected devices determine what it powers.

This restore path applies an already recorded powered state. The inspected timed GeneratorStartSequence writes slzSign instead; assigning the bypass or changing the progress flag alone does not immediately run either path.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.smallDoor
member.summary: North airlock-door GameObject whose joint drive is changed and whose local Y position is checked during door tasks.

remarks.para: OpenSmallDoor fetches this object’s ConfigurableJoint, a physics constraint between bodies, applies smallDoorOnSettings as its X drive, and wakes its Rigidbody, the simulated body. CloseSmallDoor applies smallDoorOffSettings and wakes it in the same way. A joint drive supplies spring forces toward the joint’s separately configured position target and damping forces that resist movement relative to its target velocity.

The tasks continue over later frames. Parent-local Y is the Y coordinate measured relative to the parent object. Opening waits until this Transform’s parent-local Y position is at least 7.2; closing waits until it is at most 5.15. With normal Unity scale these local length units correspond to meters. The measured parent-local Y axis can differ from the joint’s own X drive axis.

Each wait also ends on cancellation. Closing starts a separate task that waits a configured one second, then performs one doorway-clearing scan, unless cancellation prevents it. Game time follows the slow-motion or pause setting, and the wait resumes on a later frame; this is not a promise of an exact real-time timestamp. Ending a task does not guarantee physical motion has stopped, because the last drive remains applied.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.smallDoorEntity
member.summary: Small-door entity protected from the object-clearing scan around either airlock side.

remarks.para: A MarrowEntity groups a spawned object and its physical parts. DoorEmancipator skips this entity and bigDoorEntity before removing other detected entities with attached physics bodies.
Assign the entity that owns the small door so clearing the doorway cannot remove the door itself. The reference is an exclusion from removal, rather than an object selected for destruction.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.smallDoorOffSettings
member.summary: Spring, damping and force-limit settings applied to the small door’s joint X drive when closing starts.

remarks.para: The vector stores three different settings: x becomes positionSpring, y becomes positionDamper, and z becomes maximumForce. CloseSmallDoor creates a JointDrive from those values, assigns it to the door’s ConfigurableJoint.xDrive, then wakes the Rigidbody. A physics joint constrains movement; a Rigidbody supplies the simulated body.

Spring is the pull strength toward the joint’s separately configured target. Damping resists movement relative to the target velocity. Maximum force caps the drive’s push or pull. For a linear force drive at normal Unity meter/kilogram scale, their units are newtons per meter, newton-seconds per meter and newtons respectively.

For example, (1000, 100, 500) requests spring strength 1000, damping 100 and a 500-newton force cap. Raising the cap allows stronger drive forces; raising damping increases resistance to relative motion. These values do not set a target position.

The drive uses the joint’s configured X direction; its configuredInWorldSpace setting chooses world-space target values when enabled, otherwise local ones. Completion is measured from the door Transform’s parent-local Y position. Changing this vector takes effect the next time that opening or closing task copies it into the drive; it does not continuously overwrite an already applied drive.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.smallDoorOnSettings
member.summary: Spring, damping and force-limit settings applied to the small door’s joint X drive when opening starts.

remarks.para: The vector stores three different settings: x becomes positionSpring, y becomes positionDamper, and z becomes maximumForce. OpenSmallDoor creates a JointDrive from those values, assigns it to the door’s ConfigurableJoint.xDrive, then wakes the Rigidbody. A physics joint constrains movement; a Rigidbody supplies the simulated body.

Spring is the pull strength toward the joint’s separately configured target. Damping resists movement relative to the target velocity. Maximum force caps the drive’s push or pull. For a linear force drive at normal Unity meter/kilogram scale, their units are newtons per meter, newton-seconds per meter and newtons respectively.

For example, (1000, 100, 500) requests spring strength 1000, damping 100 and a 500-newton force cap. Raising the cap allows stronger drive forces; raising damping increases resistance to relative motion. These values do not set a target position.

The drive uses the joint’s configured X direction; its configuredInWorldSpace setting chooses world-space target values when enabled, otherwise local ones. Completion is measured from the door Transform’s parent-local Y position. Changing this vector takes effect the next time that opening or closing task copies it into the drive; it does not continuously overwrite an already applied drive.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.smallDoorsClosing
member.summary: Runtime flag set while the small-door closing task waits for its position threshold or cancellation.

remarks.para: The closing task sets this flag before applying its drive settings and waking the door’s physics body. It clears the flag when the door’s Y position relative to its parent reaches 5.15 or less, in scene length units (meters at normal Unity scale), or cancellation is requested. CANCELCYCLE also clears it.

The flag describes the waiting task, rather than an animation percentage or proof of actual movement. Canceling can clear it while the last applied joint drive still moves the door. A physics joint restricts movement; its drive supplies forces that pull or push the body toward its configured target. The inspected small-door task does not use this flag as a duplicate-start guard.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.smallDoorsOpening
member.summary: Runtime flag set while the small-door opening task waits for its position threshold or cancellation.

remarks.para: The opening task sets this flag before applying its drive settings and waking the door’s physics body. It clears the flag when the door’s Y position relative to its parent reaches 7.2 or more, in scene length units (meters at normal Unity scale), or cancellation is requested. CANCELCYCLE also clears it.

The flag describes the waiting task, rather than an animation percentage or proof of actual movement. Canceling can clear it while the last applied joint drive still moves the door. A physics joint restricts movement; its drive supplies forces that pull or push the body toward its configured target. The inspected small-door task does not use this flag as a duplicate-start guard.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.steamParticles
member.summary: First two particle systems played briefly at the start of the Big Walk door release sequence.

remarks.para: A particle system draws effects such as steam. BWBoxSequence disables the backup box collider object, plays entries 0 and 1, requests the clunk sound, then requests a two-second game-time wait. On continuation it stops both particle systems before requesting the warning sound.

Provide at least two assigned systems. This consumer belongs to the Big Walk release sequence, rather than being triggered automatically whenever generator power is true. The wait resumes on a later frame, so it does not promise an exact wall-clock steam duration.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.u
member.summary: Returns the active save’s , the player-unlock records including the avatar unlock counts checked by the Hub lamps.

remarks.para: The getter reads DataManager.ActiveSave each time and returns its Unlocks object. It supplies the shared live records, rather than a copy. DisplayKeys checks UnlockCountForBarcode on those records to select each render_LockLamp material.

A barcode is an asset identifier. An unlock count above zero selects lamp material 1 for an even module index or material 2 for an odd module index; zero selects material 0. The assigned material controls the lamp’s appearance. The inspected getter requires an active save and has no missing-save fallback.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.useOldHubMode
member.summary: Selects the Hub’s older key-count power and achievement paths.

remarks.para: When true, DisplayKeys marks lab power once it recounts at least three inserted module keys. CheckTotal’s Hub achievement check also uses the cached count of at least three instead of requiring isLabPowered.

Old mode adds that cached three-key check to the airlock notification path and prevents DataRead from deriving lab power merely from a readable LongRun completion record. Generator startup requests the battery achievement and skips the final sign-source write in this mode.

Large-door opening still requires lab power and a fresh count of at least three inserted keys in either mode. This setting changes the described progress paths; changing it during play does not itself replay setup or refresh already applied objects and outputs.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.vfxFadeOutSpawnable
member.summary: Fade-effect spawn description requested before the Hub loads a selected destination level.

remarks.para: A spawnable describes an asset to create. LoadFXAndLevel saves progress, registers this spawnable and requests its spawn. A callback is a function called later when an operation reports a result; the spawn callback gets the created object’s FadeVolume component and assigns its completion action.

That later fade-completion action calls SceneStreamer.Load for the chosen destination and the configured loading-screen level. The spawn request returning does not mean the effect was created or the destination finished loading. Configure an asset with the expected FadeVolume component and working fade completion behavior.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_Hub.workingDoorsGroup
member.summary: Working elevator-door entity shown when SETUPELEVATOR hides the breakable door group.

remarks.para: SETUPELEVATOR hides breakableDoorsGroup and shows this entity before requesting gauntletElevator to open its doors after a configured two-second game-time delay. Both setup branches perform the visibility swap; only one requests the ding and intro music.

A MarrowEntity groups an object and its physical parts. Assign the working elevator-door entity for that swap. Showing it does not confirm the delayed opening has already completed, and this field is not the airlock scan’s protected-door reference.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_KartRace._elapsedLapTime
member.summary: The current lap’s running clock, in seconds.

remarks.para: The clock adds unscaled frame seconds: the real elapsed time between Unity frames, without multiplying by the game’s slow-motion setting. It skips the addition when Time.timeScale, the game’s speed setting, is exactly zero. For example, a frame lasting 0.02 second adds 0.02 to both lap and race clocks at a time scale of 1 or 0.5, but adds nothing at a time scale of 0. The clock is updated frame by frame, so a line crossing records the latest stored frame value, not a separately measured instant of crossing.

StartTimer adds to this value and copies it into lapTimes, the array of lap durations in seconds, at _lapIndex, the zero-based slot of the lap currently being driven, each advancing frame. NEWLAP records it, then resets it to zero; STARTRACE and RESETRACE also zero it. UI_DisplayLapTime uses it for the current-lap labels. ENDRACE stops timing but does not zero this field; on the normal final-lap path NEWLAP has already zeroed it.

Changing this value changes the next displayed lap time and next stored split. It does not change the separate running race total. For example, replacing this clock with 10 seconds does not add 10 to the race-total clock.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_KartRace._elapsedSumOfLapTimesTotal
member.summary: The running race-total clock in seconds, including the current lap.

remarks.para: The clock adds unscaled frame seconds: the real elapsed time between Unity frames, without multiplying by the game’s slow-motion setting. It skips the addition when Time.timeScale, the game’s speed setting, is exactly zero. For example, a frame lasting 0.02 second adds 0.02 to both lap and race clocks at a time scale of 1 or 0.5, but adds nothing at a time scale of 0. The clock is updated frame by frame, so a line crossing records the latest stored frame value, not a separately measured instant of crossing.

StartTimer adds to this value independently of the lap clock. Completing a lap does not reset it. RESETRACE zeros it, while STARTRACE only zeros the lap clock and retains this total. UI_DisplayLapTime displays it, and ENDRACE copies it into the final-result snapshot used for best-time comparison.

It is not recomputed by adding the lapTimes array. For example, 40 seconds on the first lap plus 15 seconds on the current second lap gives a running total of about 55 seconds; editing the first lap’s array entry does not recalculate those 55 seconds.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_KartRace._lapIndex
member.summary: The zero-based lap slot being timed and filled in lapTimes.

remarks.para: Index 0 is the first lap, index 1 the second, and so on. The running timer writes into lapTimes at this index. NEWLAP stores the split at the old index, then increments it and compares the new value with totalLaps, the configured number of laps required to finish. The normal final-lap path leaves it equal to totalLaps after stopping the timer; at that point it no longer names a valid active slot in an exactly sized lap array.

RESETRACE returns the index to 0; STARTRACE does not reset it. The lap label adds 1 while timerRoutine is non-null, so index 1 displays lap 2. Keep the index within the lapTimes array while timing is running. Editing it does not move the kart, mark checkpoints or clear either clock.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_KartRace._sumOfLaps_Current
member.summary: The final race-total snapshot copied when ENDRACE runs, in seconds.

remarks.para: ENDRACE copies _elapsedSumOfLapTimesTotal, the live race-total clock, into this field before comparing best times. It does not sum lapTimes and is not updated on each NEWLAP. RESETRACE leaves the previous snapshot stored even though it zeros the live clocks. For example, after ending a 125-second race then resetting, this field can still be 125 while the live race total is 0.
Changing this snapshot alone does not change the live clock, split array or saved personal best. The next ENDRACE replaces it with the live total before its best-time checks.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_KartRace._sumOfLaps_PersonalBest
member.summary: The personal-best total time loaded from, or selected for saving to, this level’s active save, in seconds.

remarks.para: Start attempts to read the saved sum-of-laps personal-best value for the controller’s level and stores it here if that read succeeds. ENDRACE compares the session best with the saved value, and updates this field and requests a save when the saved value is missing or strictly slower. Equal times do not replace it. For example, a 120-second session best replaces a saved 125; a matching 125 does not.

UI_DisplayBests formats this value for the personal-best text entries. RESETRACE preserves it; WIPE_PB requests deletion of the saved entry and sets this field and the session best to zero. Assigning this field by itself updates neither the saved record nor the displays; the display needs a refresh, and persistence uses the save path.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_KartRace._sumOfLaps_SessionBest
member.summary: The fastest final race total recorded by this controller since its session best was last cleared, in seconds.

remarks.para: ENDRACE replaces it when its old value is approximately zero, treated as an unset best, or the final result is strictly smaller. RESETRACE and STARTRACE retain it, so a second race can be compared with the first. WIPE_PB clears it along with the personal best. For example, after results of 130 and 125 seconds, this value is 125.

ENDRACE compares this session best against the saved personal best and uses it for the extra achievement thresholds strictly below 120 and 110 seconds. A slower current race does not erase an earlier qualifying best. UI_DisplayBests displays it. Setting the field alone does not save it or request an achievement.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_KartRace.aff_Finish
member.summary: The final-lap hint object shown when one lap remains and hidden when the race ends.

remarks.para: NEWLAP activates this GameObject when the newly advanced lap index, the zero-based slot of the next lap, equals totalLaps minus 1, where totalLaps is the configured number of laps required to finish, provided the exact end condition was not reached. With three laps, finishing lap 2 shows this hint before lap 3. Start, RESETRACE and ENDRACE hide it. It is therefore a prompt for the last lap, not an object shown as the final race result.

A GameObject is a scene object that can contain visible components. Activating this one lets its configured components appear or run; it does not itself complete a lap. Assign a valid object before race setup. With a one-lap race, this NEWLAP branch never shows the hint: the first accepted lap goes directly to ENDRACE.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_KartRace.aff_Start
member.summary: The ready-to-start hint object shown during setup and reset, then hidden when timing starts.

remarks.para: Start and RESETRACE activate this scene object. STARTRACE deactivates it before clearing timing arrays and starting the clock. For example, put the starting instructions on this object to show them while the race is ready, then hide them during a run. This corrects the name’s possible implication that the object becomes visible at race launch.

A GameObject is a scene object whose configured components can appear or run when it is active. Assign a valid object before setup; assigning the reference alone does not start or reset the race. ENDRACE does not show it again, so a retry uses RESETRACE.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_KartRace.confettiFinish
member.summary: The particle effect requested to play by ENDRACE.

remarks.para: A ParticleSystem emits the configured visual particles. These calls request Play on this configured effect; its emission and appearance depend on its own settings. The finish line starts or advances the race through a separate dispatcher; this effect is requested by the end action, not automatically on every crossing. ENDRACE requests the lap, start and finish effects in that order.

Awake, Unity’s early component setup call, finds the SimpleSFX component on this particle object’s GameObject and caches it in confettiFinish_sfx. A SimpleSFX component chooses and requests a configured sound. Configure both before Awake. Replacing this particle reference later does not automatically replace the cached sound player, so visuals and audio can then come from different objects.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_KartRace.confettiFinish_sfx
member.summary: The cached sound player asked to play alongside confettiFinish by ENDRACE.

remarks.para: Awake, Unity’s early component setup call, gets this SimpleSFX component from the GameObject containing confettiFinish. Its settings choose the clip and playback behavior. The race actions call SIMPLEPLAY with 0, the first slot as a starting choice. Its playback setting can replace that choice: random mode chooses a clip, ordered mode advances to the next clip, and single mode keeps the first slot. This is a playback request, not a measurement of whether sound is already audible.

The calls occur in ENDRACE. ENDRACE asks the lap, start and finish sound players in that order, after requesting all three particle effects. Configure a valid SimpleSFX on the particle object before Awake; replacing the particle reference afterward does not refresh this cached component. Assigning this reference by itself requests no playback.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_KartRace.finishedRace
member.summary: The flag set after ENDRACE records the race’s final total.

remarks.para: FinishLineTrigger uses this together with raceStarted: when the race was started and this flag is true, later line-trigger calls do nothing. ENDRACE sets it after objective completion and hiding the final-lap hint, at the same stage as copying the final total. Calling ENDRACE directly can set it even before all laps were driven.

RESETRACE clears it. STARTRACE does not clear it, and ENDRACE leaves raceStarted true. This is stored control state, not a measured proof of a final-line crossing. Setting it true alone does not stop the timer, save a result, play confetti or run objective completion. The lap label uses it for finished only when timerRoutine is null.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_KartRace.lapTimes
member.summary: Lap durations in seconds, including a live value in the currently timed lap’s slot.

remarks.para: Allocate a slot for every lap before starting: an array of three entries uses index 0 for lap 1, index 1 for lap 2 and index 2 for lap 3. The timer copies _elapsedLapTime into the current _lapIndex slot each advancing frame. NEWLAP writes that same split again before resetting the lap clock and advancing the index, leaving previous slots as completed splits.

STARTRACE and RESETRACE clear the whole array to zero. UI_DisplayLapTime pairs txt_lapTimes[i] with lapTimes[i], so provide a matching slot for each lap-time label that will be enabled. This is not an array of cumulative totals: if two laps take 40 and 45 seconds, their entries are 40 and 45. The separate race-total clock is about 85 seconds and is not recomputed from edits to this array.

The clock adds unscaled frame seconds: the real elapsed time between Unity frames, without multiplying by the game’s slow-motion setting. It skips the addition when Time.timeScale, the game’s speed setting, is exactly zero. For example, a frame lasting 0.02 second adds 0.02 to both lap and race clocks at a time scale of 1 or 0.5, but adds nothing at a time scale of 0. The clock is updated frame by frame, so a line crossing records the latest stored frame value, not a separately measured instant of crossing.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_KartRace.raceMusic
member.summary: The music clip queued as override music when STARTRACE begins a race.

remarks.para: STARTRACE requests this clip through the 2D music manager before clearing race timing and starting the clock. ENDRACE and RESETRACE request stopping the override music. The request is for non-positional race music, not a sound attached to the kart’s position.

Assign a suitable clip before starting. Assigning the field during a run does not itself queue the new clip; the controller only supplies it when STARTRACE runs. The started guard makes an extra STARTRACE call do nothing while raceStarted is already true. A playback request alone does not prove that the clip is already playing.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_KartRace.raceStarted
member.summary: The latch that remembers a race has been started until RESETRACE clears it.

remarks.para: STARTRACE sets it after starting the timer and refreshing the lap label. It prevents another STARTRACE from starting a second normal race sequence. FinishLineTrigger starts a race when this is false, or attempts a new lap when it is true and finishedRace is false.

ENDRACE does not clear this flag, so true can describe a race that has already finished. RESETRACE clears it together with finishedRace. It is therefore not a reliable timer-running indicator. Setting it alone neither starts nor stops the timer coroutine, a sequence that pauses and resumes over later frames; it also does not start or stop the music or clocks. timerRoutine and explicit start/stop methods handle those actions.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_KartRace.timerRoutine
member.summary: The stored coroutine handle used to stop the race clock started by STARTRACE.

remarks.para: A coroutine is a sequence that pauses and continues on later frames. STARTRACE stores the handle returned by Unity when it starts StartTimer. ENDRACE and RESETRACE stop that stored sequence and clear the handle. STARTRACE also stops an old stored handle before replacing it.

UI_DisplayLaps treats any non-null handle as the timed-lap display state. There, _lapIndex is the zero-based slot of the lap currently being driven, and totalLaps is the configured number of laps required to finish; adding 1 turns that slot into the human lap number shown before the slash. A reference alone is not proof that the sequence is still executing. Clearing it yourself does not stop an already running sequence and removes the controller’s handle for stopping that sequence later. Keep the handle paired with the actual coroutine lifecycle; editing raceStarted or finishedRace does not stop the timer either.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_KartRace.totalLaps
member.summary: The exact number of accepted lap completions needed for NEWLAP to call ENDRACE.

remarks.para: A newly created component starts with a default of 3 laps, but the scene can configure another count. With 3, accepted NEWLAP calls advance _lapIndex from 0 to 1, then 2, then 3; reaching exactly 3 ends the race. The prior step, reaching 2, shows the final-lap hint. The lap label displays this count as the denominator, such as 2/3.

Use a positive count and allocate at least that many lapTimes entries before starting. A zero or negative count is not a useful no-laps shortcut: the clock still needs a valid slot and the finish comparison happens after incrementing. Raising or lowering this setting during a run does not resize lapTimes, reset progress or recompute the total; an index that has already passed the new count does not match the equality finish test.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_KartRace.trackCheckPoint
member.summary: The per-lap checklist that must have every entry true before NEWLAP accepts the lap.

remarks.para: Each entry is one checkpoint flag: TRACKCHECKPOINT(0) marks the first, TRACKCHECKPOINT(1) the second, and so on. NEWLAP rejects the lap if any entry is false. It does not check order, distance or which kart crossed a checkpoint. A repeated mark leaves the same entry true.

STARTRACE, RESETRACE and each accepted NEWLAP clear every flag to false. Configure a non-null array matching the intended checkpoints. An empty array passes NEWLAP because it contains no false entry; that disables this checklist rather than proving the whole course was driven. The scene must call TRACKCHECKPOINT for the corresponding crossing events.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_KartRace.trigger_NewLap

remarks.para: This stores a GameObject reference, meaning a scene object that can hold a trigger volume and other components. The race controller’s complete native methods do not read this field to detect a crossing, activate or deactivate the object, or connect an event. Assigning the reference alone therefore has no start or lap-completion effect.

For example, a scene event calling FinishLineTrigger starts timing on the first call and later applies the checkpoint-gated lap action. These details describe this controller’s inspected methods; other scene components or scripts can still use the stored reference.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_MagmaGate.laserBeams
member.summary: The ordered list of scene objects that the loss sequence sets active before scheduling the loss event.

remarks.para: LoseSequence reads the assigned array when called and sets each object's active setting to true in array order. The objects must have their own beam visuals, collision, or damage behavior configured; this field contains references to objects, not beam lengths or damage amounts.

Assign the array and all its entries before calling LoseSequence. A null array or null entry causes an error and prevents the delayed event call from being scheduled. An assigned empty array still allows the delayed call. Changing this property alone does not activate or deactivate any object.
For example, assign three laser GameObjects to activate all three at the beginning of the loss sequence. GameObject is Unity's container for a scene object and its attached components.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GameControl_MagmaGate.loseEvent
member.summary: The configured listener list that DoorDissolve invokes, normally after the loss sequence's laser activation and delay.

remarks.para: A UnityEvent holds callbacks: methods configured to run when the event is invoked. DoorDissolve invokes the currently assigned event with no arguments. If the field is null, DoorDissolve does nothing.

LoseSequence first sets every assigned laser object active, then requests DoorDissolve after a delay of 1.25 seconds. This property is read when DoorDissolve runs, so replacing the event while a call is waiting changes which listener list that call invokes. Assigning an event alone does not invoke it.

Connect listeners for the desired scene effect, such as animating a door or removing a barrier. These controller methods do not themselves detect failure or dissolve a door; their configured listeners supply those scene actions.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GenGameControl_Display.aliveFriendsText
member.summary: Exposes the friendly-alive count text component so code can replace its displayed string.

remarks.para: Assign the TMP_Text component that should carry this friendly-alive count. TMP_Text is a TextMeshPro component that draws its text string. For example, setting aliveFriendsText.text to "3" requests that visible string on the assigned component; assigning the reference alone does not calculate or fill the readout.

A value written for this intended readout normally counts friendly characters, rather than meters or seconds. The inspected display class does not find those objects, calculate the count or decide when to reset it. The code supplying the string chooses that behavior.

ChangeAllTextColor finds text through the object hierarchy. This reference receives that color only if its component is found on the same object or an active child; assigning a text component elsewhere does not add it to that search.
The hierarchy is Unity’s tree of scene objects. A child is an object nested under another object; the search includes active descendants at any depth.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GenGameControl_Display.textColor
member.summary: Default text color requested on hierarchy text components when ChangeAllTextColor is called.

remarks.para: The constructor is the code that sets initial values when this component is created. It initializes this to opaque white: red, green, blue and alpha are all 1. Color channels are unitless values normally from 0 to 1. Red, green and blue choose the tint; alpha normally controls transparency, with 0 transparent and 1 opaque.

For example, (1, 0, 0, 1) requests opaque red. ChangeAllTextColor passes the current four components to each found text object’s color property. This class does not clamp the values or automatically apply later edits; call the method again after changing them.

TMP_Text skips a color-property update when the new color is effectively equal to the existing color. The assigned value supplies the default letter color, and text formatting color tags can override it. The search covers the same object and active children, independently of the named text-reference fields.

TMP_Text is the TextMeshPro component that draws the string. The hierarchy is Unity’s tree of scene objects. A child is an object nested under another object; the search includes active descendants at any depth.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GenGameControl_Spawner._spawnClip
member.summary: The sound requested when a wave-loot sequence starts.

remarks.para: SpawnWaveLoot requests this clip at the spawner's world position before starting its paused spawning routine. It makes one sound request for that call, including a wave containing only ammo; the sound is not delayed until a weapon has successfully finished spawning. A missing arena controller stops the call before this sound request.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GenGameControl_Spawner.ammoPickupList
member.summary: Records ammo pickups that ForceCollectAllAmmo will check for automatic collection.

remarks.para: The ordinary spawn callbacks add newly created light, medium and heavy AmmoPickup components after assigning their round counts. The weapon-mode heavy callback also adds its pickup; the weapon-mode light and medium callbacks do not. A callback is code run after a spawn request returns an object, so pending requests do not yet have an entry here.

This list can still contain inactive pickups. ForceCollectAllAmmo collects only entries active in the scene, then clears the whole list, including skipped entries. Its count is therefore a number of recorded pickups, not a count of all active ammo boxes or of ammunition rounds.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GenGameControl_Spawner.ammoSpawnTrans
member.summary: The position marker for newly requested ammo pickups outside weapon mode.

remarks.para: A transform stores an object's position, rotation and scale. The ordinary wave routine reads this transform's current world position when it needs a new heavy, medium or light pickup. It requests the pickup with no world rotation. Reusing an active saved pickup adds rounds where that pickup already is rather than moving it to this marker.

If this reference is missing during Initialize, the method creates a child marker at local position (0, 0, 0.25): 0.25 units forward along this spawner's axis. With normal scale that is 25 centimetres; the parent's scale affects its world distance. Weapon mode uses the player-relative drop point instead.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GenGameControl_Spawner.arenaGameController
member.summary: The whose assigned round profile selects this spawner's ordinary or weapon-mode loot path.

remarks.para: Initialize stores this controller and copies its current rig manager for player-relative helper setup. SpawnWaveLoot reads the controller's assigned round profile each call to choose weapon mode or the ordinary path. Assigning a different controller directly does not repeat initialization or refresh the saved player rig. A missing controller makes SpawnWaveLoot log a message and return.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GenGameControl_Spawner.despawnedWeaponObjList
member.summary: Temporary list of weapons to remove from the tracked weapon list during cleanup.

remarks.para: DespawnLootWeapons adds a weapon here only after finding the interaction and pool components needed for cleanup. It requests any available despawn effect and despawns that weapon, then uses this list to remove the recorded objects from spawnedWeaponObjList after the first pass finishes. It clears this temporary list before returning. This is cleanup bookkeeping, not a saved inventory of objects ready to spawn again.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GenGameControl_Spawner.heavyAmmoSpawned
member.summary: Running total of wave heavy ammo amounts credited by new-pickup spawn callbacks, measured in rounds.

remarks.para: A callback is code run after a spawn request returns an object. Each new heavy ammo callback adds the wave's heavy round amount to this number. This increment can happen even if the returned object has no AmmoPickup component, so the number alone does not prove that a usable ammo box exists.

Adding rounds to an already active saved heavy pickup does not increase this counter. Collection does not subtract rounds or reset it, and Initialize does not reset it. For example, a newly spawned box requested for 20 rounds adds 20 here; later adding another 20 rounds to that same active box leaves this counter unchanged. Treat it as callback accounting, not ammunition currently available or collected.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GenGameControl_Spawner.playerRelGunSpawns
member.summary: The saved location-and-marker helper for weapon-mode loot drops relative to the player.

remarks.para: SetupPlayerRelativeGunSpawns obtains this component from the newly created helper prefab, attaches the helper at the cached rig's center-of-pressure reference point, and assigns its player pelvis physics body. A physics body is Unity's object for mass and motion.

The weapon-mode routine asks the helper to update its drop point, shows its marker, waits 1 real-time second, and requests selected weapons and new ammo at the drop point's current world position. It hides the marker at the end of that sequence. The helper must exist before this path runs; its presence does not mean a weapon has already spawned.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GenGameControl_Spawner.playerRelSpawnPrefab
member.summary: The helper-object prefab instantiated to provide the player-relative weapon-mode drop point and marker.

remarks.para: A prefab is a saved object template. This one needs a PlayerRelativeGunSpawns component and its drop-point and marker references. Setup creates an instance, parents it to the cached player rig's center-of-pressure reference point, aligns it with that parent, saves its helper component and assigns the player's pelvis physics body.

Initialize creates this helper only when both the cached rig and this prefab exist. Changing the prefab afterward does not replace the existing helper automatically; another setup call creates a new instance. The wave's loot entries choose the weapons: this field is the helper template rather than the gun template.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GenGameControl_Spawner.rigManager
member.summary: The cached player used to attach and connect the weapon-mode location helper.

remarks.para: Initialize copies the arena controller's current rig manager here. Setup uses that saved rig to parent the helper at its center-of-pressure reference point and assign the player's pelvis Rigidbody, the Unity component that gives a body mass and motion for physics.

This reference is captured during initialization rather than fetched anew for every wave. Replacing the controller's rig afterward does not refresh this reference or reparent an existing helper automatically.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GenGameControl_Spawner.spawnedHeavyPickup
member.summary: The heavy pickup most recently saved by the ordinary wave-spawn callback, reused for later ammo top-ups while active.

remarks.para: When an ordinary new-pickup spawn returns an object containing AmmoPickup, its callback saves that component here, sets its ammoCount to the wave's heavy amount in rounds, and adds it to the automatic-collection list. A callback is code that runs after the spawn request returns its object; an outstanding request may therefore leave the previous reference here.

A later ordinary wave adds its positive heavy amount to this same pickup if it still exists and is active in the scene; otherwise it requests a replacement. For example, adding 20 rounds to a box with 10 remaining sets that box to 30 rounds, without increasing the heavy spawn counter.

Weapon-mode callbacks do not update this saved reference. ForceCollectAllAmmo clears its collection list but leaves this reference in place, so this field can still refer to an inactive or previously collected pickup. Check activity before treating it as an available box.
