member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GenGameControl_Spawner.spawnedWeaponObjList
member.summary: Records weapon objects returned by this spawner's ordinary and weapon-mode spawn callbacks for later cleanup.

remarks.para: A callback is code run after a spawn request returns an object. Both weapon callbacks append the returned object here; issuing the request alone does not add it. Those callbacks do not test whether the supplied object is active.

DespawnLootWeapons walks this list, cleans up weapons that pass its component and attachment checks, and removes those cleaned-up entries afterward. Skipped entries remain. The list is therefore tracking history for cleanup, not a fresh search of every live weapon in the arena.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GeoManager.OnMoveUpComplete
member.summary: Shared callbacks invoked after a mover is recorded as raised and geoState is set to UP.

remarks.para: A callback is a routine called to report an action. This static Action is shared by all GeoManager instances and receives no arguments. The manager has already updated activeGeoMover and stopped its movement sound when it invokes the callbacks.

For a death-pit raise, the callbacks run before the cover floor starts lowering. They also precede the mover's own onMoveUpComplete event and its dynamic-prop spawn request in the normal movement sequence. A floor raise can send this notification too, so it does not by itself mean that a particular obstacle preset or the whole pit transition is ready.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GeoManager._currMoverIndex
member.summary: Stored integer returned by moverIndex, separate from the preset counter currGeoIndex.

remarks.para: The getter returns this value directly. The inspected manager initialization, selection, increment, toggle and completion methods do not update it from geoMoverList or activeGeoMover. It therefore is not a reliable report of which preset has just deployed.
Changing this stored value changes what moverIndex returns, but does not move geometry or alter currGeoIndex.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GeoManager._mapLoop
member.summary: Managed audio player that ToggleAudio starts, retunes and stops for geometry movement.

remarks.para: The manager creates this player during construction. ToggleAudio requests a looping moveGeoClip when the player reports it is not playing, or changes its pitch when it is already playing. Every completed raise stops it; a completed lowering stops it only for a mover with isFloor set; a death-pit raise can stop and then restart it for the floor movement.
This is the audio player reference, not a report that every mover is idle. Setting it to null leaves the audio and completion paths without the player they require.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GeoManager.activeGeoMover
member.summary: The most recently recorded by a move-up completion report.

remarks.para: MoveUpComplete sets this after any floor-specific death-pit hiding and before notifying listeners. It can be a normal preset, a death-pit structure, or the raised cover floor. ToggleGeo starts a deployment without assigning this field, so it can still name an earlier mover while the new one is moving.

ClearCurrentGeo uses this reference to clean dynamic destructibles and a timber joint, a physics connection used for the timber setup; ToggleGeo checks its isDeathPit flag to decide whether to delay deployment. Clearing or lowering geometry does not automatically clear the reference. It is not proof that the referenced GameObject, the Unity scene object containing the mover, is still active.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GeoManager.currGeoIndex
member.summary: Saved list-position counter used when cycling presets or requesting the currently chosen preset.

remarks.para: IncrementGeoIndex and IncrementAndToggleGeo add 1 and wrap to 0 beyond the last geoMoverList position. For [Bridge, Towers, Pit], positions 0, 1 and 2 name those entries. The arena controller also passes this stored value into ToggleGeo when starting a selected custom challenge.

SelectGeo, ToggleGeo and the completion reports do not synchronize it to the mover they choose or finish. Assigning the counter does not deploy anything by itself. It is separate from the stored integer returned by moverIndex.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GeoManager.deathPitFloorMover
member.summary: Mover for the cover floor that closes the pit before a new preset and lowers to expose a raised death pit.

remarks.para: ClearCurrentGeo activates and raises this floor only when its GameObject, the Unity scene object containing the mover, has its own activeSelf flag set to false. This checks the floor object's own active setting, rather than whether its parent objects are active. When a death-pit mover reports a completed raise, the manager first sends OnMoveUpComplete and then starts this floor downward. Its downward completion disables the floor and stops the movement sound.

When activeGeoMover is a death pit, ToggleGeo waits this floor's configured moveUpDuration plus 0.1 game-time seconds before activating the next preset. Game-time seconds advance with the game-speed setting, so this wait can take a different number of real-time seconds. That wait is based on a saved duration, not the floor's completion flag. A floor raising to cover the pit can become activeGeoMover when it reports completion.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GeoManager.deathPitGeoMover

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GeoManager.geoDict
member.summary: Setup lookup from mover names to list positions, which SelectGeo uses to choose a deployment.

remarks.para: Construction creates an empty dictionary. Awake, Unity's initialization callback, is a routine Unity calls while setting up the component. member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GeoManager.geoMoverDict

The dictionary starts empty during construction and requires unique, nonmissing movers when populated.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GeoManager.geoMoverList
member.summary: Ordered preset collection that supplies deployment targets, selection-counter bounds and setup names.

remarks.para: Awake, Unity's initialization callback, is a routine Unity calls while setting up the component. It builds the name lookups from this list. ToggleGeo selects an entry by zero-based position; the increment methods wrap currGeoIndex at its last position. ClearCurrentGeo disables entries whose isDeathPit flag is false.

Each entry is an existing GeoMover component, which moves between its configured local starting and ending positions across frames. Local positions are measured relative to the object's parent axes, in local length units, meters at parent scale 1. A prefab is a saved object template. Adding an entry does not instantiate a prefab or update either name dictionary automatically. Configure a nonempty list with valid, uniquely named entries before using preset selection.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GeoManager.geoMoverPrefab

If another system creates movers from a template, their list entries and name lookups still need to be configured for this manager. This field is not a substitute for that setup.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GeoManager.geoState
member.summary: Stored transition label set to MOVING when deployment starts and UP when a mover reports its raise complete.

remarks.para: The immediate ToggleGeo path sets MOVING after activating the target and before starting its movement. The delayed path does so after its wait. MoveUpComplete sets UP after recording activeGeoMover and stopping the sound, before sending the shared completion notification.

This label is not a fresh check of all mover positions. ClearCurrentGeo does not set CLEARED, and MoveDownComplete does not change it. A death-pit raise can set UP while its cover floor is still about to lower, and a floor-cover raise can also set UP. Assigning a label alone does not move anything.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GeoManager.moveGeoClip
member.summary: Sound clip requested as the geometry movement loop when the audio player is not already playing.

remarks.para: ToggleAudio(true, ...) loops this clip at the manager's local origin. The supplied pitch factor P is 1 normally; pit-cover movement supplies P = 1.2 for the higher, faster setting. Every completed raise stops the loop; a completed lowering stops it only for a mover with isFloor set.

For a new loop, the audio helper uses P × (0.75 × S + 0.25), where P is the supplied unitless playback-speed/pitch factor and S is Time.timeScale, Unity's unitless game-speed multiplier: 1 means normal game speed and 0.5 means half speed. The constants 0.75 and 0.25 are unitless weights. For S = 0.5 and P = 1.2, the result is 1.2 × 0.625 = 0.75. This adjustment happens when the loop is requested; this call does not recalculate it every frame. When the player already reports playing, ToggleAudio sets P directly instead.

Changing this clip while the player reports it is already playing does not replace that running clip through ToggleAudio: that path only changes pitch. The new clip is used on a later loop-start request.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.GeoManager.moverIndex

It is different from currGeoIndex, the saved preset-cycling counter, and is not a reliable report of the last deployed preset. Reading it does not change geometry.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.HighlightUI.color1
member.summary: Stores the first highlight color, applied to the shader’s _Color0 property.

remarks.para: A shader is the drawing program that makes the surface appear; a material supplies its drawing settings. A Renderer is the Unity component that draws the visible surface and receives the applied color settings. This is a Color with red, green, blue and alpha channels. The numbers are unitless: ordinary RGB values commonly run from 0 to 1, HDR values can be brighter than 1, and alpha is the fourth channel commonly used for opacity. HDR means high dynamic range. The Inspector accepts HDR colors, and SetColors passes the values through rather than clamping them. The material’s shader decides how intensity and alpha affect the final appearance.

Start applies color1 together with color2. SetColors also updates both stored fields whenever it applies a new pair; the timed FadeToColors overload repeatedly updates them while blending. Assigning this field alone after startup does not immediately change the renderer. For example, assign the desired pair and call SetColors(color1, color2) to apply it.

A timed fade captures the starting pair and blends toward its requested pair in HSV, where hue chooses the color family, saturation chooses how colorful it is, and value chooses brightness; alpha is blended separately. A direct field edit does not replace that captured target, so a running fade can overwrite the edit on its next update. The shader determines where this color appears; this component does not define a near/far spatial endpoint.

The numbers are unitless: ordinary RGB values commonly run from 0 to 1, HDR values can be brighter than 1, and alpha is the fourth channel commonly used for opacity. HDR means high dynamic range. member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.HighlightUI.fadeToColorsCoroutine
member.summary: Stores the handle used to stop and replace a timed highlight-color fade.

remarks.para: A coroutine is a sequence that continues over several frames. FadeToColors(c1, c2, duration) first stops the coroutine referenced here, if there is one. If the HighlightUI component is active and enabled, it starts the new sequence and stores its handle. If the component is inactive or disabled, it applies the requested pair immediately instead; that branch does not start a new sequence or clear this field.

For a positive duration, fade progress is u = clamp(elapsed / duration, 0, 1), where elapsed and duration are seconds, u is unitless, and clamp keeps the result between 0 and 1. Elapsed time starts at zero and increases by unscaledDeltaTime, the real frame interval unaffected by the game’s time scale, the factor controlling game speed. The routine updates both colors, yields until a later frame, and clears this handle on completion after elapsed time exceeds duration. For example, with a 0.2-second duration, elapsed time of 0.1 seconds gives halfway progress in HSV and alpha. HSV describes hue (the color family), saturation (how colorful it is) and value (brightness); alpha is the unitless opacity channel.

The two-color FadeToColors(c1, c2) overload actually calls SetColors immediately; it does not start a coroutine or stop the stored one. SetColors, EnableMesh and DisableMesh also leave this handle alone. Setting the field to null is not a StopCoroutine call and does not itself cancel the sequence already running.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.HighlightUI.m_Color1ID
member.summary: Shared shader-property ID used to write color1 into _Color0.

remarks.para: A shader is the surface’s drawing program. m_PropertyBlock is a MaterialPropertyBlock, a container of setting overrides for that program; m_Renderer is the Renderer component that draws the surface and receives those settings. The ID is a lookup key made by Shader.PropertyToID, which converts a shader property name into an integer key. It is not a color channel, brightness setting or layer index. SetColors uses it when writing the corresponding Color into m_PropertyBlock, then applies that block to m_Renderer.

Awake, Unity’s initialization callback (a routine called to perform or report an action), computes both IDs only when it creates the missing shared property block. All HighlightUI components use the same IDs. Changing this field redirects the subsequent SetColors writes for all instances to a different property key; it does not immediately recolor an already drawn surface. The property name is _Color0 even though the field’s numbering starts at 1.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.HighlightUI.m_PropertyBlock
member.summary: Shared used to apply the highlight color pair to an instance’s renderer.

remarks.para: A shader is the drawing program that turns its settings into the visible surface. A material stores drawing settings used with a shader for a surface. A MaterialPropertyBlock is a container of shader settings supplied for a renderer, the Unity component that draws a surface. SetColors writes both color values into this block under the cached IDs for _Color0 and _Color1, then applies it to that HighlightUI instance’s m_Renderer. It supplies renderer settings without replacing the material asset.

Awake, Unity’s initialization callback (a routine called to perform or report an action), allocates the block if it is missing and computes both property IDs in the same branch. All instances share this working container, while each has its own color1, color2 and cached renderer. Applying one instance’s colors does not call SetColors on the other instances.

SetColors does not clear the block before writing the two colors. Replacing the block or inserting other property overrides changes the container passed by later SetColors calls. Calling SetColors before the block has been prepared lacks the shared storage that this code requires.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.HighlightUI.m_Renderer
member.summary: Cached Renderer that receives the highlight colors and whose visibility EnableMesh and DisableMesh control.

remarks.para: A Renderer is the Unity component that draws the visible surface. A GameObject is a Unity scene object that holds components such as this HighlightUI and its Renderer. SetColors checks this reference and, if it is missing, gets a Renderer from this same GameObject and caches it. The lookup does not search child objects or create a new renderer. Start calls SetColors to apply the initial pair.

The shared property block is a container of settings for the shader, the surface’s drawing program. SetColors supplies the shared property block to this renderer; EnableMesh and DisableMesh directly change its enabled switch. Those two visibility methods require the reference already to be available and do not perform the lookup themselves. member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.KeyDecorator.code
member.summary: Replaces the compatibility code on Key and Keycard components when the configured spawner reports a spawn.

remarks.para: A GameObject is a Unity object that can be in a scene or stored in a prefab. Components attached to it can hold data or add behavior; a prefab is a saved template for making an object. OnSpawn looks for Key and Keycard components on the supplied GameObject and overwrites the code value on each one it finds. It changes the spawned object’s copy, not the saved prefab asset. It checks Key first, then Keycard; an object with both receives the value in both components. It does not search child objects.

Compatibility flags are named on/off choices that can be combined; they have no physical units. For a physical Key, these codes are compatibility flags for KeyReceiver, the insertion socket that checks the key. A receiver requires every flag selected in its own code; a key may carry extra flags. For example, a key with CODE_A and CODE_B can pass a receiver requiring CODE_A, but a key with only CODE_A cannot pass a receiver requiring both. Passing the code check is one condition of insertion, not an immediate unlock action.

KeycardReceiver uses a different code check after the card slides into the slot: it lets the card pass this code check when at least one named flag is set on both the card and receiver. For the defined flags, at least one must be shared. A card with CODE_A can therefore pass the code check of a receiver selecting CODE_A and CODE_B. The physical key’s requirement to carry every receiver flag does not apply to cards.

Configure this decorator’s inherited _crateSpawner reference before the component is enabled. Unity calls its inherited OnEnable routine when it becomes enabled; that registers this decorator for the configured spawner’s notifications. A spawn notification is a callback, a routine called to report a spawn with the object that was spawned. It does not guarantee a newly created object. Changing code affects later notifications; it does not continuously update keys or cards that have already received their code.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LaserCursor._last_despawn

For an illustrative three-clip array and a counter starting at zero, selected indices are 1, 2, 0, 0, 1, 2. The wrap boundary repeats clip zero. An empty assigned array returns before incrementing this counter; changing it affects the next cue selection.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LaserCursor._sourceRadius
member.summary: Meter distance passed as AudioSource.minDistance: for a 3D sound, moving closer than this no longer makes it louder.

remarks.para: PlayAudio passes this as AudioSource.minDistance in meters. For a 3D sound, getting closer than this distance no longer makes it louder; farther away, the AudioSource settings start making it quieter. This is not the maximum distance at which the sound can be heard or the laser’s reach. Its relevance depends on spatialBlend, the unitless 2D/3D mix where 0 is fully 2D and 1 fully 3D, and the audio source’s settings.
This value is copied when a new cue is requested; changing it does not reconfigure a cue already playing. The Inspector range does not establish a runtime clamp in LaserCursor.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LaserCursor._sourceVolume
member.summary: Unitless volume level passed when requesting a laser cue.

remarks.para: PlayAudio sends this to Audio3dManager as the source volume. Zero requests silence and, for example, 0.5 requests half the numeric volume level of 1; this is not a claim of half the perceived loudness. Mixer routing and other audio settings can further affect what is heard.

The checked playback path treats it as volume, separately from _sourceRadius passed as AudioSource.minDistance in meters. For a 3D sound, getting closer than that distance no longer makes it louder; farther away, the AudioSource settings start making it quieter. This is not the farthest audible distance or the laser’s reach. Changing it affects new requests rather than an already playing cue. The Inspector’s volume range and radius wording do not add a LaserCursor runtime radius adjustment.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LaserCursor.activeController

The selected controller must have an entry in Initialize’s cursor-target mapping. Writing this cache alone does not change the shared selection or build that mapping.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LaserCursor.bezCurve

remarks.para: A Bezier curve is a smooth path shaped by control points. FireRayPulse asks this component for points at unitless parameters from 0 to 1, using pulseAceleration’s result to choose the position. The DrawBezierCurve component needs its four point objects assigned.

LaserCursor positions its visual markers, but this reference does not automatically connect those markers to DrawBezierCurve’s point fields. Configure the curve and its rendered line consistently with the intended pointer path.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LaserCursor.canShowCursor

Update requires this together with isOnPlane to use the valid-region display path. The geometry calculation itself can select an inactive region before later regions are tested.
This field is refreshed during candidate examination, not continuously for every region. Reading or writing it does not activate a region or guarantee the pointer is inside its bounds.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LaserCursor.lineEnd
member.summary: End marker given the same world endpoint position and region rotation as cursorEnd.

remarks.para: The endpoint is offset 0.025 meters, or 2.5 centimeters, opposite the region’s forward direction from endPosition. ShowCursor and the normal Update place it; show/hide routines animate its visibility.

The positions are world-space meter positions derived from the current startPosition and endPosition caches. Assign the PageElementView used for this role. Changing the reference redirects later visual updates; moving its Transform manually can be overwritten by the next cursor update.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LaserCursor.m_IsActiveThisFrame
member.summary: Queued press passed to the next successful UI ray dispatch.

remarks.para: Trigger sets it when the cursor is active. UpdateCursor, ShowCursor and the valid-region Update path pass it as the input module’s isPressed value, then clear it after that dispatch. If the cursor is inactive or no module is available, those dispatch paths leave it pending.

The normal Update dispatches the previous value before checking this update’s controller button and queuing another press. It can therefore survive more than one frame. Writing it true queues input data; it does not immediately invoke a button event.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LaserCursor.m_IsTrigger
member.summary: Stored trigger flag with no effect in the checked LaserCursor routines.

remarks.para: The complete checked class does not read or assign this field. Its press path uses m_IsActiveThisFrame instead, and pulse bookkeeping uses isFireingPulse. Changing this field does not alter those checked targeting, input or pulse routines.
This is scoped to the inspected LaserCursor class, not a claim that external scripts never access the stored field.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LaserCursor.maxMillimeters
member.summary: Distance reference in millimeters used by the endpoint’s KnollFilter helper.

remarks.para: For a positive value, the helper computes a unitless blend factor equal to the squared movement distance divided by the squared reference distance, clamped to 0–1. The movement distance is the meter distance from the current endpoint Transform to its requested position; the reference distance is maxMillimeters divided by 1000, in meters. For an illustrative 10 mm reference and a 5 mm move, the factor is 0.25. A larger reference reduces small-movement response. A nonpositive value skips this filtering step.

In the checked normal Update, the helper temporarily writes a filtered cursorEnd position, but the later PageElementView.SetTransform call writes the earlier unfiltered endpoint position back. Its blend therefore does not determine the final endpoint from that update. This field does not change the ray’s region or button-hit tests, and changing it does not establish an effective final jitter filter in this path.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LaserCursor.prismaticSFX
member.summary: Sound-effect component whose Transform supplies the playback position for laser cues.

remarks.para: AUDIOSEND lazily caches this component’s Transform and uses its current world position for the pooled Audio3dManager cue. Initialize and HideCursor disable the component. ShowCursor plays the appearance cue first, then moves this sound Transform to the display endpoint and enables it.

Its own continuous sound behavior is separate from the one-shot cue arrays. Assign it even when cue arrays are empty, since initialization and show/hide code also use the reference. Disabling it does not turn off Audio3dManager cue requests.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LaserCursor.pulseAceleration
member.summary: Curve mapping elapsed pulse time to position along the curved beam.

remarks.para: The input is curentPulseTime / pulseLength. Both named values are seconds, so the input is a unitless fraction of the duration. The curve output is a unitless Bezier position parameter: 0 is the curve’s start and 1 its end. It is not directly a speed or an acceleration despite the field’s spelling.

For example, elapsed 0.25 seconds with pulseLength 0.5 seconds gives input 0.5. A curve output of 0.8 draws the marker at parameter 0.8. The stored pulseProgress keeps the unmodified output, while drawing clamps it to 0–1. A stored output at least 1 ends the sequence at its next completion check; otherwise the duration also limits it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LaserCursor.pulseLength
member.summary: Game-time duration in seconds that limits the travelling pulse sequence.

remarks.para: During travel, curve input is curentPulseTime / pulseLength: elapsed time and this duration are both seconds, giving a unitless fraction. For example, a 0.5-second duration produces curve input 0.5 after 0.25 seconds. The curve selects marker position rather than being multiplied by a distance or speed.

Completion occurs when elapsed time reaches this duration or stored pulseProgress reaches 1, so a curve reaching the end early can shorten travel. A nonpositive duration skips travel. Changing this value while a sequence runs affects its later checks; it does not reset elapsed time or start another pulse.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LaserCursor.pulseProgress
member.summary: Last unitless position parameter produced by the running pulse curve.

remarks.para: The first coroutine advance resets it to zero. Later advances overwrite it with pulseAceleration evaluated at curentPulseTime / pulseLength; elapsed time and duration are seconds, so that curve input is unitless. The stored result is not clamped, even though the marker position uses a copy clamped to 0–1.

It controls the progress-above-0.35 middle-marker blips and the progress-at-least-1 completion check. Changing it is temporary if the sequence evaluates the curve again. It is a curve parameter, not a measured fraction of physical beam distance or a speed.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LaserCursor.pulseSound
member.summary: Cue clips selected when the pulse sequence first starts.

remarks.para: AUDIOSEND action 0 selects from this assigned array. Empty arrays skip playback; each array has its own counter, advanced before selection. For an illustrative three-clip array with its counter at zero, selected indices are 1, 2, 0, 0, 1, 2, including the repeated zero at the wrap boundary.

The cue is requested at the cached prismaticSFX Transform’s current world position with the configured volume, _sourceRadius and spatial blend. _sourceRadius is passed as AudioSource.minDistance in meters: for a 3D sound, getting closer than this distance no longer makes it louder; farther away, the AudioSource settings start making it quieter. This is not the farthest audible distance or the laser’s reach. Changing clips affects later requests rather than an already playing clip.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LaserCursor.rayDespawn
member.summary: Cue clips selected when HideCursor or the automatic disappearance transition runs.

remarks.para: AUDIOSEND action 2 selects from this assigned array. Empty arrays skip playback; each array has its own counter, advanced before selection. For an illustrative three-clip array with its counter at zero, selected indices are 1, 2, 0, 0, 1, 2, including the repeated zero at the wrap boundary.

The cue is requested at the cached prismaticSFX Transform’s current world position with the configured volume, _sourceRadius and spatial blend. _sourceRadius is passed as AudioSource.minDistance in meters: for a 3D sound, getting closer than this distance no longer makes it louder; farther away, the AudioSource settings start making it quieter. This is not the farthest audible distance or the laser’s reach. Changing clips affects later requests rather than an already playing clip.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LaserCursor.rayPulse
member.summary: Marker moved along the configured Bezier curve by the pulse coroutine.

remarks.para: A coroutine is a sequence that continues over several frames. The pulse sequence places this marker at curve parameter zero, shows it, then updates its world position using the clamped pulseProgress parameter and the current ray rotation. pulseProgress is a unitless curve position; its drawing copy is clamped to 0–1, where 0 is the curve’s start and 1 its end. This is not a measured fraction of physical beam distance. Normal completion hides it before clearing isFireingPulse.

ShowCursor and HideCursor do not directly manage this marker’s visibility. Assign this PageElementView and the curve’s point references before starting a pulse; changing the reference redirects later sequence updates.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LaserCursor.raySpawn
member.summary: Cue clips selected when ShowCursor runs.

remarks.para: AUDIOSEND action 1 selects from this assigned array. Empty arrays skip playback; each array has its own counter, advanced before selection. For an illustrative three-clip array with its counter at zero, selected indices are 1, 2, 0, 0, 1, 2, including the repeated zero at the wrap boundary.

The cue is requested at the cached prismaticSFX Transform’s current world position with the configured volume, _sourceRadius and spatial blend. _sourceRadius is passed as AudioSource.minDistance in meters: for a 3D sound, getting closer than this distance no longer makes it louder; farther away, the AudioSource settings start making it quieter. This is not the farthest audible distance or the laser’s reach. Changing clips affects later requests rather than an already playing clip.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LaserCursor.regions
member.summary: Ordered UI-plane regions used to choose where the controller laser may target.

remarks.para: Each entry needs a center Transform and Bounds. The Transform supplies the plane’s world position, forward direction and rotating axes; Bounds describe the accepted hit area in those axes. The ray origin is translated relative to the center and the calculated hit is inverse-rotated for the bounds check; Transform scale is not applied.

CalcCursor stops at the first entry passing its below-10-meter distance, bounds and positive-forward-direction tests, then separately records whether that region is active in the hierarchy. An inactive geometric match can therefore prevent later entries from being considered. Update shows the cursor only with both geometric and active results.

Changing the array changes later calculations rather than immediately moving the cursor. An empty array does not clear previous cached hit flags or positions, so it is not a reliable hide/reset action by itself.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LaserCursor.spatialBlend
member.summary: Mix of 2D and 3D spatial audio requested for laser cues: 0 is fully 2D and 1 fully 3D.

remarks.para: Intermediate unitless values blend the two modes. PlayAudio copies this into the pooled cue’s AudioSource.spatialBlend along with _sourceRadius, passed as AudioSource.minDistance in meters, and _sourceVolume, its unitless numeric volume level where 0 requests silence. For a 3D sound, moving closer than _sourceRadius no longer makes it louder; farther away, the AudioSource settings start making it quieter. This is not the farthest audible distance or the laser’s reach. The world playback position comes from the cached prismaticSFX Transform.
Changing it affects later cue requests, not a cue already playing or the separate PrismaticSFX component’s own settings. The Inspector range is not a LaserCursor runtime clamp.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LaserCursor.startPosition
member.summary: Cached world-space origin at the selected UI cursor target of the pointer, in meters.

remarks.para: CalcCursor recomputes this while focused, using the mapped controller cursorTarget and each candidate region. The UI cursor target supplies its Transform position; this is not necessarily the controller device’s physical center.

The value is used to place the marker path. With no focus or an empty region array, the previous cache can remain; reading it alone does not establish a current valid active-region hit. A direct write can be overwritten by the next calculation.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LevelsPanelView._completedStoryLevelBarcodes
member.summary: Caches the story-level identifiers that pass this panel’s saved ammo-delta completion test.

remarks.para: A barcode uniquely identifies a content crate. During a successful CalculateSceneList scan, the panel clears this list and checks each barcode in its runtime barcode-to-save-key mapping against the active save. It adds the barcode when the gathered final-ammo-delta map contains the mapped save key. Ammo deltas are saved changes in ammunition counts. A map, also called a dictionary, is a lookup table; this gathered map has saved level keys paired with tables of ammunition names and whole-number count changes.

A JSON object is saved data containing named values, which the helper can convert to an ammunition-count lookup table. A valid saved ammo-delta dictionary, or a converted JSON object, can satisfy that test even with a false completion flag. If the ammo-delta key is absent, a saved boolean true completion flag supplies an empty entry and also satisfies it. This is the panel’s eligibility test rather than a fresh check of gameplay state.

Normally only candidates in this list can appear, subject to the source flags. BeatGame and DeveloperMode both true bypass that restriction. Changing the save does not immediately rebuild this cache; the next loaded scan does. A scan attempted before the content catalog is initially loaded leaves this list’s previous contents in place even though it empties the selectable-level list.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LevelsPanelView._currentPage
member.summary: Stores the zero-based page used to display rows and calculate which level a row selects.

remarks.para: Page 0 is the first page. For selection, list index = page × rows + row, where page is this value, rows is items.Length, and row is the selected zero-based row index. For example, page 2, four rows, and row 0 select list index 8.

NextPage and PrevPage update labels and rows before storing a new value. PopulateMenu preserves this value after a rescan, and LoadFirstLevel also keeps it while selecting row zero. A shorter refreshed list can therefore leave the stored page beyond the new page count.

Changing this field directly changes later selection and navigation calculations; it does not itself redraw the page. UpdatePageItems and UpdatePageText likewise draw their supplied page without storing it here. Keep it consistent with the page you display.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LevelsPanelView._levelCrates
member.summary: Caches the eligible, title-sorted level records from the panel’s most recent scan.

remarks.para: A level crate is the catalog record for a level, not an already loaded scene. CalculateSceneList clears this list, removes menu-hidden crates, sorts candidates by Title using string comparison, then stores candidates that pass the completion and source rules. It is the selectable subset of the catalog, not every level the scan found.

Normally eligibility requires the level’s barcode in the completed-story cache plus an allowed source. A barcode is the crate’s unique identifier. Source filtering allows game content only, external content only, or both; both source flags false also allow both. If the active save has BeatGame true and settings have DeveloperMode true, all non-hidden candidates are included regardless of those two checks.

UpdatePageItems reads this list for titles, while SelectItem and LoadFirstLevel read it to choose a loading request. If a scan occurs before the catalog’s InitialLoaded flag is true, the list is empty. Editing this list alone does not update _totalScenes, _numberOfPages, or the visible rows; keep those caches consistent when changing it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LevelsPanelView._numberOfPages
member.summary: Caches the number of pages calculated during the last full menu refresh.

remarks.para: PopulateMenu calculates ceil(levels / rows), where levels is the number of selectable levels, rows is items.Length, the page’s row capacity, and ceil means round upward to a whole number. The division uses floating-point numbers, meaning numbers that can contain fractions, so nine divided by four gives 2.25 before rounding upward. With nine levels and four rows, the count is three; with no levels and a positive row capacity, it is zero. Configure at least one row to avoid division by zero.

NextPage uses this count as its upper bound. UpdatePageText uses the stored count to decide whether to hide both navigation objects and clear the page label: it does so below two pages, even if its total argument differs.
CalculateSceneList alone does not recalculate this count. Directly changing it affects later navigation and page-label decisions but does not redraw the rows or clamp _currentPage.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LevelsPanelView._storyLevelBarcodeKeyPair
member.summary: Maps each story-level barcode configured in to the save-data key used by the completion filter.

remarks.para: A barcode is a unique content identifier. Awake, the routine Unity calls when initializing the component, builds this dictionary, a lookup table, from storyLevelBarcodeKeyPair. Each pair contributes its levelCrate reference’s barcode and its key string. Repeated barcodes keep the first configured key because later duplicates are not added.

CalculateSceneList reads these mappings, tests the active save’s gathered ammo-delta map for each key, and puts passing barcodes in the completed-story cache. Ammo deltas are saved ammunition-count changes. The gathered map is a lookup table of saved level keys: a valid ammo-delta entry supplies a key, and a true completion flag supplies one when no ammo-delta key was saved. The strings are save-data keys, not displayed title or translation keys.

The serialized source array is saved configuration. Changing that source array after Awake does not rebuild this dictionary. Editing the dictionary directly changes the mappings tested by the next loaded scan; it does not immediately refresh the completed-story cache or visible menu.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LevelsPanelView._totalScenes
member.summary: Caches the number of selectable levels retained by the latest scene-list scan.

remarks.para: This is a count of entries in _levelCrates after the panel’s hidden-content, source, and completion rules, not a count of loaded Unity scenes or every installed level. CalculateSceneList resets it to zero before clearing the list, then stores the final list count. A scan attempted before the content catalog is initially loaded leaves it at zero.

PopulateMenu divides this count by items.Length, the rows per page, and rounds upward to calculate the page count. UpdatePageItems uses it as the upper bound for deciding which row objects should be active. For example, a count of ten with four rows per page makes three pages and leaves two occupied rows on the final page.

Changing this count directly does not add or remove crate records. If it disagrees with _levelCrates.Count, the display can hide valid entries or try to read beyond the list. Use a full menu refresh to keep the count, page count, and rows in agreement.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LevelsPanelView.backButton
member.summary: References the navigation scene object that the panel shows when a previous page is available.

remarks.para: UpdatePageText deactivates this GameObject when the stored page count is below two. Otherwise it activates the object when its supplied zero-based page index is at least one and deactivates it at index zero. Deactivation hides the scene object and disables its attached active UI behavior.

Assign a non-null navigation object in the Inspector, Unity’s component-settings panel. This field controls visibility; connect the button’s click action to PrevPage when setting up the UI. Assigning the reference does not immediately change the page or its visibility.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LevelsPanelView.forwardButton
member.summary: References the navigation scene object that the panel shows when a later page is available.

remarks.para: UpdatePageText deactivates this GameObject when the stored page count is below two. Otherwise it activates the object when its supplied zero-based page index is less than the supplied total page count minus one. At the last page it deactivates the object, hiding it and disabling its attached active UI behavior.

For example, with three pages it is active on indices 0 and 1 and inactive on index 2. Assign a non-null navigation object in the Inspector, Unity’s component-settings panel, and connect the button’s click action to NextPage. Assigning the reference does not immediately change the page or its visibility.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LevelsPanelView.includeExternalLevels
member.summary: Controls external-content filtering together with includeInternalLevels on the next level scan.

remarks.para: The source flags are read during CalculateSceneList. Only internal true means game sources only; only external true means external sources only; both true or both false mean both sources. A source is internal when its pallet, or content package, is recognized as belonging to the current game. This source test does not use the pallet’s older Internal flag.

Passing the source test normally also requires the level’s barcode, its unique content identifier, in the panel’s completed-story cache. When the active save’s BeatGame and the settings’ DeveloperMode flags are both true, the scan bypasses both source and completion restrictions. Crates marked Redacted, meaning hidden from menus, are still removed.

The constructor, the code that assigns initial values when this component is created, defaults both source flags to true, though saved scene settings can supply other values. Changing a flag affects the next scan; it does not immediately rebuild the cached list or displayed rows. For example, set this flag and then refresh the menu to see the new eligible list.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LevelsPanelView.includeInternalLevels
member.summary: Controls game-content filtering together with includeExternalLevels on the next level scan.

remarks.para: The source flags are read during CalculateSceneList. Only internal true means game sources only; only external true means external sources only; both true or both false mean both sources. A source is internal when its pallet, or content package, is recognized as belonging to the current game. This source test does not use the pallet’s older Internal flag.

Passing the source test normally also requires the level’s barcode, its unique content identifier, in the panel’s completed-story cache. When the active save’s BeatGame and the settings’ DeveloperMode flags are both true, the scan bypasses both source and completion restrictions. Crates marked Redacted, meaning hidden from menus, are still removed.

The constructor, the code that assigns initial values when this component is created, defaults both source flags to true, though saved scene settings can supply other values. Changing a flag affects the next scan; it does not immediately rebuild the cached list or displayed rows. For example, set this flag and then refresh the menu to see the new eligible list.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LevelsPanelView.items
member.summary: Supplies the reusable row scene objects and determines how many levels fit on each page.

remarks.para: The array length is the normal page capacity in rows. PopulateMenu uses it to calculate the number of pages; NextPage and PrevPage use it when drawing rows; SelectItem calculates list index = page × rows + row, where page is the zero-based current page, rows is this array’s length, and row is the selected zero-based slot.

UpdatePageItems deactivates each requested row, then activates the ones with a corresponding selectable level. The matching text array element supplies that row’s title label. For example, four items create four row slots per page; a final page with two levels activates only the first two slots.

Assign at least one non-null GameObject, meaning a scene object, and matching text labels. Zero row slots cause division by zero when calculating pages. Changing the array or its length does not redraw the menu by itself; a changed length also changes later selection indices, so refresh the menu before using the rows.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LevelsPanelView.modLoadScreen
member.summary: Supplies the loading-scene choice passed when requesting a level from an external content package.

remarks.para: SelectItem and LoadFirstLevel pass this LevelCrateReference, a reference to a catalog level, alongside the selected target level when its pallet, the content package containing the level, is neither marked Internal nor recognized as belonging to the current game. They request game/internal levels by barcode without this loading-scene choice. The source-filter flags use game membership rather than that older Internal marker.

Assign the level you want SceneStreamer to use as the external level’s loading scene. This field is a configured reference, not a report that a loading screen is currently visible. These panel methods start background loading requests and return without confirming that either the loading scene or target scene has finished loading. Changing the reference affects a later qualifying request.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LevelsPanelView.pageText
member.summary: References the text label that displays the current page number and total page count.

remarks.para: UpdatePageText writes a one-based page number followed by “ / ” and the supplied total. For example, zero-based page index 1 with three pages shows “2 / 3”. When the stored _numberOfPages is zero or one, it writes an empty string and hides both navigation objects instead.

Assign a non-null TextMeshProUGUI label in the Inspector, Unity’s component-settings panel. PopulateMenu and successful page-navigation calls update this label through UpdatePageText. Assigning another label, or changing _currentPage directly, does not immediately rewrite the text.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LevelsPanelView.storyLevelBarcodeKeyPair
member.summary: Configures the story-level references and save-data keys used to build the panel’s completion lookup.

remarks.para: Each pair contains levelCrate, a reference to a story level’s catalog record, and key, the string under which that level’s progress is saved. Awake, the routine Unity calls when initializing the component, copies the level reference’s barcode and the key into a runtime dictionary, a lookup table created while the game is running. A barcode is a unique content identifier. When multiple pairs have the same barcode, the first key wins.

During a loaded scene-list scan, the panel looks for each mapped key in the active save’s gathered final-ammo-delta map, another lookup table indexed by saved level keys. Ammo deltas are saved changes in ammunition counts. A valid ammo-delta entry puts its level key in that table; when the ammo-delta key was not saved, a true saved completion flag supplies an empty entry instead. The panel tests whether the level key is present, rather than testing the ammunition-count numbers. Passing barcodes enter the completed-story cache that normally restricts which levels can appear. These strings identify saved progress; row labels instead use the crate’s Title.

Set up the array and non-null level references before initialization, using the exact save keys your levels record. For example, pair a story-level reference with its saved level key, rather than with the text you want on its menu row. Editing this source array after Awake does not automatically rebuild the runtime dictionary or refresh the menu.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LevelsPanelView.text
member.summary: Supplies the title labels matched by row index to the reusable row objects in .

remarks.para: When UpdatePageItems displays a level in items[row], it writes that level crate’s Title into text[row]. A level crate is a catalog record, and its Title is the displayed name; the configured story-level save keys do not supply these labels.

Assign a non-null TextMeshProUGUI label for every row that can be occupied, in the same order as the items array. For example, with four row objects, text[2] is the label for the third row. Hidden rows keep their old label text, but their row objects are inactive. Changing the label array does not populate the new labels until a row update occurs.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.OnLaunchAction
member.summary: Functions notified after the player’s initial launch-force requests, carrying the requested world-space velocity change.

remarks.para: This is an Action<Vector3>, meaning functions you can register to receive a three-number vector. LaunchPlayer invokes it after the body-force calls and before restarting its optional correction coroutine or playing final launch audio. The cooldown deadline and any required path-order reversal are already updated.

The vector is the requested change from the rig’s tracked velocity to the computed launch velocity, in metres per second on world X/Y/Z. For example, (0, 5, 2) requests 5 m/s upward and 2 m/s along world Z. It is not a position or a force in newtons, and need not equal the resulting velocity of every body after other physics effects. Skipped launches do not notify it.

A callback is a function registered to run when this notification is sent. A coroutine is a routine that resumes its work over later frames. The player rig groups the movement and body controllers. The initial force calls request a change processed during a later physics simulation; this notification does not establish completed movement or a successful landing.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.addFallForce
member.summary: Adds a forward chest impulse when an agent enters the Fallen locomotion state during an ordinary jump traversal.

remarks.para: After removing the jump’s first chest joint, the agent jump routine switches to the Fallen locomotion state (enum value 2). When this flag is true, pushes its chest along the link’s world forward direction with impulse 75 × jointForceMult. jointForceMult is the agent controller’s unitless joint-force multiplier; the impulse is in newton-seconds. At multiplier 1, a 15-kilogram chest gets a 5 m/s velocity change before other physics effects.
The direction follows the link’s forward axis; it is not always downward. This flag is read by that agent jump stage, not by the inspected player LaunchPlayer routine.

A physics joint is a connection that constrains or pulls bodies. Here the chest joint holds the agent’s chest during the first jump stage; removing it lets the agent jump routine apply its optional one-off push.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.agentDot
member.summary: Caches the signed distance of the last checked body position along the link’s forward axis.

remarks.para: CheckAgentDot subtracts the link’s world position from the checked position and takes the part along the link’s forward direction. With a unit forward direction, the result is metres: positive lies in front of the link origin, negative behind it, and zero is on the dividing plane. It is not an angle or a normalized facing score.
LaunchPlayer and target-preview selection recalculate this value using the player pelvis. Writing the cached number alone does not choose their next direction, because the next check overwrites it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.allNavLinks
member.summary: Cached navigation links whose endpoints and two-way flags are updated together by this component.

remarks.para: A navigation link is an AI route shortcut between two positions. CreateEdgeObjectsByType replaces this array with NavMeshLink components on this same GameObject, rather than searching its children.

SetStartEndPoints and SetExplicitStartAndEndLaunchPoints copy calculated local endpoints into each array entry. ToggleBiDirectional sets each entry’s two-way flag. Assigning this array does not gather components or update them immediately; a later setup call does, and rebuilding the target hierarchy refreshes the array again.
A GameObject is a scene object that holds components. A component is an attached part that supplies behavior or data; each cached NavMeshLink supplies the navigation shortcut’s settings.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.applyConstForce
member.summary: Starts trajectory-error monitoring after a player launch so corrective thrust can be enabled when needed.

remarks.para: When true, LaunchPlayer starts CoMeasureError after its initial force requests and launch callback. A coroutine is a routine that resumes over later frames. This one compares the pelvis position with ideal samples in positions during the calculated flight time.

Error is the distance from the player pelvis to the current ideal path position. thrustThreshold is the lower distance threshold and failThreshold is the upper one, both in metres. With finite settings satisfying 0 ≤ thrustThreshold ≤ failThreshold, monitoring sets the thrust flag true when error is strictly between them, false when strictly outside, and leaves its existing value unchanged at exact equality. A previously true flag can therefore keep requesting thrust at a boundary. FixedUpdate, Unity’s physics-step update, requests pushes along the sampled path while the flag is true. The name does not mean a constant force is always applied. The launch needs usable ideal samples; the drag-compensation branch builds them before starting this routine.

Monitoring uses the calculated flight time in game-time seconds. It resumes on frames and checks the previously stored progress before calculating new progress, so it can finish after that estimated deadline rather than at an exact instant.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.applyCorrectiveThrust
member.summary: Current switch that lets physics updates add corrective impulses to the player along the sampled path.

remarks.para: FixedUpdate, Unity’s physics-step update, reads this flag. When true, each player body receives an impulse toward a look-ahead sample in positions; the velocity added per step is thrustFactor × fixedDeltaTime. thrustFactor acts as metres per second squared, and fixedDeltaTime is the step duration in seconds.

The launch-monitoring coroutine, a routine resumed over later frames, updates the flag when it has adjacent path samples for the pelvis-to-ideal-position comparison. It compares squared error with the squares of thrustThreshold and failThreshold. Error is the distance from the pelvis to the current ideal path position. For finite settings with 0 ≤ thrustThreshold ≤ failThreshold, it sets true strictly between the two distances, false strictly outside them, and leaves it unchanged at exact equality. thrustThreshold is the lower distance threshold and failThreshold the upper one, both in metres. The routine does not validate their signs or order before squaring them. With reversed thresholds, equality to one can be strictly outside the other; for example, thrustThreshold 10, failThreshold 1 and error 10 metres clear the flag. Clears the flag when monitoring ends. Setting it manually does not start monitoring.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.applyDragForce
member.summary: Chooses the launch calculation that scales initial velocity to compensate for drag.

remarks.para: When true, the player drag-compensation branch selects forwardObj for a positive pelvis side value and reverseObj for zero or a negative value. CoLaunch uses the same object selection for agent calculations; scene placement determines actual direction. The player branch multiplies vertical velocity by yDragMult and horizontal velocity by xzDragMult, then applies a mass-scaled impulse. These are unitless multipliers; for example, 1.25 increases the relevant calculated velocity by 25 percent. Agent launches use yDragMult_npc for vertical velocity and xzDragMult_npc for horizontal velocity; these NPC multipliers are also unitless.

When false, player launch uses its alternate launchTarget calculation and launchForceMult, a unitless multiplier applied to that branch’s computed velocity. This flag selects the initial calculation. It does not directly change a body’s drag setting or guarantee that the estimated arc exactly matches the live physics motion.

Drag is resistance that slows motion. Compensation raises or lowers the calculated launch velocity to allow for that slowing; velocity is measured in metres per second, and a mass-scaled impulse is a one-off push in newton-seconds.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.autoMat
member.summary: Stored material reference whose assignment has no verified effect in this component’s inspected pad and target setup.

remarks.para: A material controls a rendered surface’s appearance. The inspected pad switch assigns brightLampMat or darkLampMat to its lamp renderers; it does not read autoMat. Target creation and preview methods also do not apply this material. Assigning it alone therefore does not perform a verified material swap through those methods.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.autoTriggerForwObj
member.summary: Optional automatic-trigger object repositioned above its parent during launch endpoint setup.

remarks.para: For a LAUNCH link, SetStartEndPoints places this object at local (0, 1, 0) when assigned. Local Y is up relative to its own parent; at scale 1 this is one metre above the parent origin. Each endpoint setup call repeats that placement.

This reference supplies the object to reposition. The pad on/off routine uses separate configured object and collider arrays, so assigning this reference alone does not wire it into those activation lists.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.avgDrag
member.summary: Stored drag-related value with no verified input role in the inspected launch calculations.

remarks.para: Starts at 0.175 in a newly constructed component. This private field is not marked to be saved as scene configuration in the inspected metadata. The inspected launch calculations use the vertical/horizontal compensation multipliers instead and do not read avgDrag. No force unit or averaging rule is established by those methods; changing this value alone does not alter their calculated launch velocity.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.barObjs
member.summary: Ordered existing bar objects from which the bar builder creates hand-grab markers.

remarks.para: CreateClimbBarObjects makes one grabObjs marker at each bar’s origin, raises it 0.1 local units, and alternates right/left offsets by edgeWidth. edgeWidth is a sideways local distance, normally metres at scale 1. Array order becomes the climb sequence, with even zero-based indices on the right and odd indices on the left.

The builder reads the assigned objects; it does not instantiate them from climbingBarsPrefab. Changing the array does not move existing grab markers until the builder runs again. The normal bar traversal needs at least two grab markers for its initial stages.
The new grab markers are parented under rotaterParentObj. Their local X, Y and Z mean right, up and forward relative to that parent, so the 0.1-unit raise is along its up axis.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.brightLampMat
member.summary: Material assigned to both lamp-ring renderers when the launch pad is switched on.

remarks.para: A material defines a rendered surface’s appearance. ToggleLaunchPadLink(true) assigns this material to forwLampRingRend and revLampRingRend, even for a one-way link. Switching off assigns darkLampMat instead.

Replacing this reference does not immediately repaint the lamps. The next pad-switch call applies the material. Its visual brightness comes from the material’s own shader and settings; this field supplies the material rather than a numeric light intensity.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.chestColor
member.summary: Stored chest-related color with no verified effect on the inspected preview and traversal drawings.

remarks.para: A newly constructed component starts with red 0.2, green 0.5, blue 0 and alpha 1, where alpha controls opacity. Scene data can replace that default. The inspected LinkData methods do not read this color, and the inspected AgentLinkControl gizmo drawing uses its own agent color. Assigning chestColor alone does not change those drawings.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.chestDepth
member.summary: Local forward placement used when rebuilding ledge chest and head markers.

remarks.para: In the single-edge and ledge builders, sets the secondary chest marker’s local Z directly, and offsets the head forward from edgeTarget by this distance. Z is forward relative to rotaterParentObj; the distance is normally metres at scale 1.

For example, chestDepth 1 puts the ledge’s secondary chest marker at local Z = 1. The value is placement configuration, not the thickness of the avatar’s chest. Changing it requires rebuilding targets to change those marker positions. The slide builder uses fixed positions instead.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.chestHeight
member.summary: Vertical placement distance used when rebuilding chest and head targets, with a different rule for each link type.

remarks.para: Measured in local units along the generated target parent’s Y axis, normally metres at scale 1. Ledge builders place the primary chest and head chestHeight above the edge, and the secondary chest twice that far above it. Launch targets sit chestHeight above the navigation endpoints. Jump’s primary chest sits chestHeight above the edge. Zip targets use local Y = chestHeight.

The bar builder instead places its primary chest chestHeight below the edge and the secondary half that distance below. The slide builder uses fixed heights and ignores this setting. For example, increasing this value by 0.2 raises a ledge’s primary chest marker 0.2 units but lowers a bar link’s primary marker 0.2 units.
This sets marker placement, not an avatar measurement. Editing it does not move existing markers until their builder runs again.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.chestJoint
member.summary: Cached reference to an agent’s temporary chest physics joint during inspected jump, slide and ledge traversals.

remarks.para: A physics joint connects bodies or constrains their motion. These agent routines copy their current chest joint into this field while building traversal connections. Later stages can destroy or replace that joint, so the cached reference can become invalid.
The agent also keeps its own chest-joint reference. Assigning this field does not automatically replace the joint stored by the agent or retarget an already created connection.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.chestPointGoal
member.summary: Stored chest-point transform that does not select an anchor in the inspected slide setup and traversal.

remarks.para: A transform stores an object’s position, rotation and scale. The slide marker builder and full slide traversal read chestTargetPrimary and chestTargetSecondary instead. The builder also does not populate this field. Assigning it alone does not redirect either chest anchor through those methods; use the actual target markers for that setup.
A joint anchor is a connection point where a physics joint constrains or pulls the chest. These routines copy the actual chest target’s world position when setting up that connection.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.chestPointStart
member.summary: Stored chest-point transform that does not select an anchor in the inspected slide setup and traversal.

remarks.para: A transform stores an object’s position, rotation and scale. The slide marker builder and full slide traversal read chestTargetPrimary and chestTargetSecondary instead. The builder also does not populate this field. Assigning it alone does not redirect either chest anchor through those methods; use the actual target markers for that setup.
A joint anchor is a connection point where a physics joint constrains or pulls the chest. These routines copy the actual chest target’s world position when setting up that connection.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.chestTargetPrimary
member.summary: First chest-position marker that traversal routines use when preparing the agent’s physics connections.

remarks.para: A transform stores a marker’s position, rotation and scale. Link-type builders replace this marker and give it local coordinates under rotaterParentObj. Ledge, jump, slide and bar routines read its world position for their chest setup; distances normally use metres at scale 1.

For example, the slide first anchors the chest at this target, then moves to chestTargetSecondary in a later stage. Bar setup adds a kinematic Rigidbody, a body whose motion is controlled by the game, and a mover joint to the primary marker’s GameObject, then connects that joint to the agent later.

Moving the marker before an anchor is calculated changes that setup. A copied joint anchor does not automatically follow every later marker edit. Rebuilding replaces the marker object, so obtain the current reference after setup.

A physics joint is a connection that constrains or pulls bodies; the mover’s springs pull the chest toward its target. A joint anchor is the connection point. A GameObject is a scene object that holds components, the attached parts supplying behavior or data.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.chestTargetSecondary
member.summary: Later chest-position marker used by staged traversal and the bar mover’s destination calculation.

remarks.para: Link-type builders replace and position this transform under rotaterParentObj. A transform stores position, rotation and scale. Slide and ledge routines use its world position for a later chest connection, while bar traversal uses it while moving the chest joint toward the route’s far side. World positions normally use metres.

This is a marker, not a command to move the agent immediately. Its role and placement depend on linkType, and not every builder creates it. Rebuilding discards previous marker edits. Joint anchors that have already been copied from its position do not automatically update just because the marker moves.
A physics joint is a connection that constrains or pulls bodies. Its anchor is the connection point; these routines copy a target’s position into that point when setting up a stage.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.climbingBarsPrefab
member.summary: Stored bar template reference that the inspected bar builder does not instantiate.

remarks.para: A prefab is a saved GameObject template. CreateClimbBarObjects uses bars already assigned in barObjs and creates empty grab markers at those bars. It does not read climbingBarsPrefab. Assigning this template alone therefore does not create bars through that builder; provide the existing bar objects before rebuilding the grab markers.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.colorizedRends
member.summary: Stored renderer array that the inspected pad switch does not use for its material changes.

remarks.para: A renderer draws an object’s mesh, the shape made from its 3D surface, and its material controls the surface appearance. The pad on/off method changes forwLampRingRend and revLampRingRend directly; it does not loop over colorizedRends. The inspected target creation and preview methods also do not recolor this array. Assigning it alone does not apply a verified color change through those methods.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.compTrigger
member.summary: Stored trigger reference whose assignment does not wire escalator completion in the inspected traversal methods.

remarks.para: A trigger detects when another object enters its volume. The inspected proxy-entry handler compares the incoming trigger-region reference with the agent controller’s triggerProxy, its stored reference to the expected region. When they match for an ESCALATOR link and the agent is not zipping, that handler signals completion. The escalator traversal itself does not read triggerProxy, and neither method reads this field. LinkData’s inspected setup methods do not register compTrigger as a completion listener. Assigning it alone does not establish that connection through those methods.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.coolDownDuration
member.summary: Game-time seconds added to the deadline before another player launch is allowed.

remarks.para: On an accepted LaunchPlayer call, sets launchableTime to current game time plus this value before applying the initial forces or invoking listeners. Calls made while current time is less than that deadline return immediately. Exactly at the deadline they can proceed if the other checks pass.

For example, 3 requests a three-game-second gap, with actual opportunity depending on when the next call occurs. A new component starts at 3 before scene data is loaded. Changing this setting does not replace an already stored deadline; the next accepted launch uses the new duration. The method does not clamp negative durations.

The clock is Unity Time.time, elapsed scaled game time. Pausing scaled game time stops this cooldown’s clock, and changing game speed changes how quickly it advances relative to real-world seconds. The duration is therefore game seconds, rather than a promise of that many seconds on a wall clock.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.correctiveMax
member.summary: Stored correction-related number with no verified role in the inspected player launch and thrust routines.

remarks.para: A newly constructed component starts at 0.5, before scene data may replace it. The full inspected LaunchPlayer, CoMeasureError and FixedUpdate routines do not read this value. Those routines gate thrust using thrustThreshold and failThreshold, which are position-error distances in metres, and size the impulse with thrustFactor, which acts as acceleration in metres per second squared.
Changing this stored number alone therefore does not change the verified correction behavior through those routines. They establish no unit, percentage rule or limiting operation for this field.
