member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.crabJumpForce
member.summary: Aiming-speed input for a crablet link jump, measured in metres per second.

remarks.para: The crablet link-jump routine raises values below 7 to a minimum aiming speed of 7 m/s, copies the result to the crablet behavior and requests its Link jump. The jump’s predictive aiming calculation takes this value as projectile speed. For example, 10 requests a 10 m/s aiming input; gravity compensation and later behavior multipliers can change the final velocity, so this is not a guarantee of exactly 10 m/s.

This is not a force in newtons. CreateLaunchObjects overwrites it with twice edgeHeight, where edgeHeight is the edge’s local vertical distance, normally metres at scale 1. At edgeHeight 4, rebuilding sets this number to 8; set your desired speed after the rebuild when needed.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.crabTarget
member.summary: Optional position that crablets aim at for their link jump, taking priority over launchTarget.

remarks.para: The crablet jump routine copies this transform’s world position into its jump target when the reference exists. A transform stores position, rotation and scale. If this marker is missing, falls back to launchTarget. The position is read when preparing the jump; it is not continuously followed after being copied.

The ordinary jump builder replaces this marker and puts it at local (0, edgeHeight + 1.2, 0). edgeHeight is the edge’s local height above the link origin; the extra 1.2 is an upward local distance, normally metres at scale 1. Moving the marker before jump preparation changes the aim, but does not guarantee a successful landing.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.crabletAgentID
member.summary: Stored crablet navigation identifier that does not select the crab link in the inspected target builder.

remarks.para: An agent type ID is a unitless number identifying a set of AI navigation settings. CreateEdgeObjectsByType checks the first navigation link against legAgentID, then records the second link as navLinkCrab when available. It does not match either link against this crabletAgentID.

Assigning this number alone therefore does not change which crab navigation-link reference that builder records. The inspected agent starter uses the agent controller’s own crablet identifier for its choices.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.currLinkAgent
member.summary: Agent controller recorded by a link claim, which can remain separate from the occupied flag.

remarks.para: ClaimLink stores the supplied controller before setting isOccupied. ReleaseLink clears this reference before clearing that flag. A controller is the component that runs an agent’s traversal routines.

ZipLinkManager’s upward claim records an agent here only when a valid agent is supplied. Its upward release clears the occupied flag and proxy but does not clear this agent reference. OnZipOccupied also changes only the flag. This field can therefore be empty on an occupied link or retain an old agent after a zip release. Setting it alone does not set occupancy or block routes.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.currProxy
member.summary: Proxy recorded on each upward zip link when the zip manager claims that route.

remarks.para: A TriggerRefProxy identifies an object that a trigger volume detects. ClaimZipUpLinks copies its supplied proxy to each managed upward link; if none is supplied, uses the manager’s playerProxy. It also sets those links occupied.

ReleaseZipUpLinks clears this reference and the occupied flag. This is the recorded claim information, not a detector that updates itself when somebody moves. The inspected agent completion handler compares the entering proxy with the agent controller’s triggerProxy, rather than this field.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.darkLampMat
member.summary: Material assigned to both lamp-ring renderers when the launch pad is switched off.

remarks.para: A material defines a rendered surface’s appearance. ToggleLaunchPadLink(false) assigns this material to both forwLampRingRend and revLampRingRend before removing the player-jump listener and changing configured pad objects. Both renderers are updated even for a one-way link.

Changing the reference does not repaint lamps immediately; the next pad-switch call applies it. Its darkness depends on the material’s own shader and settings, rather than a numeric light intensity stored here.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.destArmTime
member.summary: Seconds the block-climb routine waits after moving its chest anchor to the secondary target, before releasing its arm joints.

remarks.para: In that stage, the routine changes the chest connection to chestTargetSecondary, reads this value, and waits for it before destroying the arm joints. A physics joint is a connection that constrains body motion. This is a pause before releasing those connections, rather than the speed at which the arms travel.

A new component starts at 0.1 seconds before scene data is loaded. WaitForSeconds uses game time and resumes on a later frame, so actual elapsed time can be longer than the configured pause. Editing this field after that wait is created does not change the value already passed to it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.disableOnLinkCompletion
member.summary: Tells successful agent completion to destroy temporary joints, stop its routines and disable that agent’s traversal controller.

remarks.para: CompleteLink reads this flag after its type-specific release work and navigation completion. When true, calls the agent’s joint cleanup, stops its coroutines and sets its AgentLinkControl component disabled. A coroutine is a routine that resumes over later frames; a physics joint is a connection constraining bodies.

This does not disable the LinkData GameObject or its navigation-link components. Completion then continues with distance bookkeeping, optional leg repair and clearing the agent’s current-link references. Set this before completion to affect that call.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.displayAngle
member.summary: Stored angle-display flag with no verified drawing effect in the inspected trajectory methods.

remarks.para: The inspected LinkData preview and launch methods do not read this field. Those previews calculate and store ideal path samples without reading this display flag. Assigning it alone therefore does not change the verified behavior through those methods.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.dragPositions
member.summary: Stored world-position samples that the height debug helpers scan.

remarks.para: Each Vector3 is a world X/Y/Z position, normally in metres. FindMaxHeight scans adjacent heights starting with indices 1 and 2 and returns the last strict rise; DisplayMaxHeight uses that selection to draw a vertical debug line. These helpers expect the array to be supplied; they do not generate a drag simulation.

The inspected ideal-path builder fills positions instead, and the correction routine also uses positions. ToggleReversePositionArray reverses only positions, leaving dragPositions in its existing order. Changing this array affects the height scans, not that correction path.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.dragSplineResolution
member.summary: Stored drag-preview sample count that does not control the inspected ideal-path builder.

remarks.para: Starts at the unitless integer 30 on a newly constructed component, before scene data may replace it. These methods do not establish a rule connecting that number to dragPositions length.

The inspected LinkData launch and preview methods do not read this field. DrawEditorIdealPath uses splineResolution to allocate positions; the height helpers scan the existing dragPositions array. Assigning it alone therefore does not change the verified behavior through those methods.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.drawPlayer
member.summary: Stored player-preview flag with no verified effect in the inspected preview methods.

remarks.para: Starts true on a newly constructed component, before scene data may replace it.

The inspected LinkData preview and launch methods do not read this field. DrawEditorPathWithPlayerBody uses the player body at index 8 when called, without checking this flag. Assigning it alone therefore does not change the verified behavior through those methods.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.edgeDepth
member.summary: Forward/back spacing used when rebuilding ledge hand, knee and chest markers, and bar chest markers.

remarks.para: Ledge primary hands and knees sit edgeDepth behind edgeTarget; secondary hands sit that far forward. The primary ledge chest sits twice edgeDepth behind the edge. Bar chest targets use edgeDepth forward and backward for their first and second positions.

For example, 0.25 places the ledge primary hand 0.25 local units behind the edge and its primary chest 0.5 units behind. This is an offset used for placement, not necessarily the full visible thickness of a ledge.

Local distances are measured along rotaterParentObj’s axes: X right, Y up, Z forward. They normally mean metres when the link and parent have scale 1. Editing placement settings does not move existing markers until their builder runs again.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.edgeHeight
member.summary: Local height of the generated edge marker, also read directly by launch-height calculations.

remarks.para: CreateEdgeObjectsByType puts edgeTarget at local Y = edgeHeight. Endpoint ray markers are placed one local unit above that height. The ordinary jump builder puts crabTarget 1.2 local units above it. A value of 4 therefore builds an edge marker 4 units above the link origin.

Launch calculations use edgeHeight plus launchHeight, the extra height above the edge, and subtract the chosen launch endpoint’s local Y where that calculation requires it. Editing edgeHeight can change a later launch calculation even before markers are rebuilt. Existing marker positions still keep their earlier setup until rebuilt.
CreateLaunchObjects also overwrites crabJumpForce with twice this number. That separate value is treated later as a crablet aiming speed in m/s, so rebuilding can replace a manually chosen speed.

Local distances are measured along rotaterParentObj’s axes: X right, Y up, Z forward. They normally mean metres when the link and parent have scale 1. Editing placement settings does not move existing markers until their builder runs again.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.edgeTarget
member.summary: Generated edge-position marker from which several target builders place the hands, chest and head.

remarks.para: A transform stores position, rotation and scale. CreateEdgeObjectsByType replaces this marker and places it under rotaterParentObj at local (0, edgeHeight, 0), where edgeHeight is a vertical distance, normally metres at scale 1.

The ledge, jump, slide and launch builders read its local position as a placement reference. Block-climb traversal also reads it for initial chest positioning. Moving the marker before those calculations changes their starting reference; rebuilding replaces the marker and discards hand edits.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.edgeWidth
member.summary: Sideways offset used to space the generated hands, knees and alternating bar-grab markers.

remarks.para: Ledge hands are placed edgeWidth left/right of edgeTarget, so their separation is twice this value. Knee markers use twice edgeWidth on each side, for separation four times this value. For example, 0.5 gives hand-marker spacing 1 local unit and knee-marker spacing 2 units.
Bar setup shifts even-index grab markers right by edgeWidth and odd indices left. OffsetBarGrabObjects adds that offset again on each call, so repeated calls accumulate sideways movement.

Local distances are measured along rotaterParentObj’s axes: X right, Y up, Z forward. They normally mean metres when the link and parent have scale 1. Editing placement settings does not move existing markers until their builder runs again.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.endMoveTarget
member.summary: Stored movement-end transform that does not select an escalator destination in the inspected routines.

remarks.para: The inspected LinkData setup and AgentLinkControl escalator methods do not read this field. A transform stores position, rotation and scale. CoEscalate completes the navigation crossing and waits; it does not read this marker. Assigning it alone therefore does not change the verified behavior through those methods.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.endPoint
member.summary: Cached world-space floor position found below the end ray marker.

remarks.para: SetStartEndPoints casts down from endRayTarget. On a hit, stores the collision position here and its link-local equivalent in endPosLocal. World X/Y/Z normally use metres. On a miss, leaves this cache at its previous value.

The player target guide can start its line at this cached point, raised 0.01 metre along world Y. SetExplicitStartAndEndLaunchPoints updates navigation endpoints from the placed launch objects but does not refresh this cache, so the guide can retain an older position. TelePlayerToLinkEnd uses reverseObj’s position instead.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.endPosLocal
member.summary: Cached grounded end position, expressed relative to this LinkData transform and copied into navigation links.

remarks.para: SetStartEndPoints finds floor below endRayTarget and converts the hit’s world position into this component’s local coordinates. Local X/Y/Z are right/up/forward relative to the link; distances normally mean metres at scale 1. A missed ray leaves the prior cached value intact.

The same method assigns this position to every cached navigation link’s end, and to an existing reverseObj on a LAUNCH link. Writing the cache alone does not immediately update those objects. SetExplicitStartAndEndLaunchPoints writes its own navigation endpoints directly without updating this cache.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.endRayObj
member.summary: Stored ray-related GameObject that is not the ray origin read by endpoint setup.

remarks.para: The inspected LinkData setup methods do not read this field. SetStartEndPoints reads endRayTarget, a separate transform. CreateStartEndPoints creates that transform’s object rather than assigning endRayObj. Assigning it alone therefore does not change the verified behavior through those methods.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.endRayTarget
member.summary: Transform whose world position starts the downward floor check for the link’s end.

remarks.para: CreateStartEndPoints replaces this marker under rotaterParentObj at local (0, edgeHeight + 1, -linkDepth / 2). edgeHeight is the edge’s local height and linkDepth is start-to-end spacing along local Z, both normally metres at scale 1.

SetStartEndPoints casts from its current world position straight down for up to 100 metres, using startEndLayermask to choose collision layers. A ray is an imaginary line used to check for a collision. Moving this marker before that call changes the area tested; an unsuccessful check preserves the previous cached end coordinates.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.escalator
member.summary: Stored escalator reference that the inspected traversal methods do not use to drive the belt.

remarks.para: The inspected LinkData setup and AgentLinkControl escalator methods do not read this field. CoEscalate completes the navigation crossing; the inspected proxy handler completes the agent when its own proxy enters. Neither changes an Escalator speed through this field. Assigning it alone therefore does not change the verified behavior through those methods.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.explicitMat
member.summary: Stored material reference that is not applied by the inspected target and pad methods.

remarks.para: The inspected LinkData target, preview and pad methods do not read this field. A material controls surface appearance. The pad switch assigns brightLampMat or darkLampMat directly to its lamp renderers instead. Assigning it alone therefore does not change the verified behavior through those methods.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.failThreshold
member.summary: Outer position-error distance beyond which the launch monitor stops requesting corrective thrust.

remarks.para: CoMeasureError compares the squared distance between the player pelvis and the ideal path point against failThreshold squared and thrustThreshold squared. Both settings are distances in metres. With ordinary finite settings satisfying 0 ≤ thrustThreshold ≤ failThreshold, monitoring turns corrective thrust on when error is strictly above the inner thrustThreshold and strictly below this outer value.

An error strictly beyond this threshold clears applyCorrectiveThrust; it does not itself declare a failed traversal or teleport the player. With those ordered nonnegative thresholds, when squared error equals either squared threshold, the current flag is unchanged. The routine squares both values without rejecting negative settings, so −0.1 m has the same comparison boundary as +0.1 m. A previously true flag can therefore continue requesting thrust at a boundary. For example, with inner distance 0.1 and outer 10, error 2 metres requests thrust, while error 11 metres clears it.
Starts at 10 metres on a new component before scene data is loaded. The monitoring routine reads the thresholds while running, so changing them affects later sampled comparisons.

CoMeasureError is a coroutine, a routine that resumes over later frames. It clears the flag whenever squared error is strictly below thrustThreshold squared or strictly above failThreshold squared; it does not validate the threshold order before comparing. With thrustThreshold 0.1, failThreshold 0.05 and error 0.1 metre, the error equals the inner threshold but exceeds the outer one, so the flag is cleared.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.forwAmbSFX
member.summary: Forward-side sound controller asked to power up or fade down when the pad is switched.

remarks.para: ToggleLaunchPadLink(true) calls this controller’s PowerUp with its power-up cue requested. Disabling calls PowerDown(false) to fade its ambient sound, then PowerDown(true) to play the configured power-down cue. Forward-side sound work occurs for both one-way and two-way links.

The controller supplies its own clips and volume settings. Replacing this reference does not change sound immediately; the next pad switch calls the newly assigned controller. PowerUp requests playback through its sound setup callback, a function called when setup is ready, so the pad call is not proof that sound setup has already completed.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.forwFXTrig
member.summary: Stored forward effects trigger collider that is not toggled directly by the inspected pad switch.

remarks.para: The inspected LinkData pad methods do not read this field. A collider is a shape used for contact detection. ToggleLaunchPadLink loops through fwdTrigCols; place a collider in that array if it should follow this switch. Assigning it alone therefore does not change the verified behavior through those methods.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.forwLampRingRend
member.summary: Renderer whose material is replaced when the forward pad lamp switches between bright and dark states.

remarks.para: A renderer draws an object’s surface. ToggleLaunchPadLink assigns brightLampMat on enable and darkLampMat on disable to this renderer, and also updates the reverse lamp renderer. This happens before configured objects, colliders and sound controllers are switched.

Both renderer references are required by that method. Assigning this field only chooses the renderer for the next switch; it does not apply a material immediately. The renderer’s GameObject is not automatically activated or deactivated through this field.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.forwToggleObjs
member.summary: Forward-side GameObjects activated or deactivated together by the pad switch.

remarks.para: ToggleLaunchPadLink applies its enable argument to every entry’s active state. This forward array is processed for both one-way and two-way links. For example, include a pad glow object here to make it appear on enable and disappear on disable.

Setting a GameObject inactive also makes its children inactive in the hierarchy. The array and entries must be assigned. Replacing this array does not immediately change object states; the next pad-switch call applies them. Sound and collider arrays are handled separately afterward.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.forwardObj
member.summary: Placed forward launch endpoint used for launch calculation, forward audio and the start teleport helper.

remarks.para: SetStartEndPoints places this object at startPosLocal on a LAUNCH link. SetExplicitStartAndEndLaunchPoints instead reads its world position, uses it as the explicit navigation start and places the simulation origin there. It also moves the LinkData root between the two launch objects.

The opposite-side launch calculation can aim toward this endpoint, while LaunchAudio(true) plays here and TelePlayerToLinkStart moves the rig and all stored body-part transforms to this point. World coordinates normally use metres. Replacing the object reference changes which object later calls read; it does not recalculate endpoint caches or teleport immediately.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.fwdTrigCols
member.summary: Forward-side collider components enabled or disabled together by the pad switch.

remarks.para: A collider is a shape used by physics to detect contact. ToggleLaunchPadLink sets every entry’s enabled flag to its enable argument after switching forwToggleObjs. The forward collider array is processed for both one-way and two-way links.

Disabling these components stops their collision/trigger participation; it does not deactivate their GameObjects. The array and entries must be assigned. Merely assigning forwTrig or forwFXTrig does not add a collider to this list. Replacing this array takes effect on the next pad-switch call.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.grabObjs
member.summary: Ordered grab-position markers that the bar-climbing routine follows.

remarks.para: CreateClimbBarObjects replaces the array with one marker per existing barObjs entry, raises each 0.1 local units and alternates right/left spacing by edgeWidth. edgeWidth is a local sideways distance, normally metres at scale 1. OffsetBarGrabObjects can add another alternating sideways shift to the existing positions.

The bar routine starts from entries 0 and 1 and proceeds through the sequence while preparing the arm physics connections. It requires at least two valid markers for those initial stages. Editing marker positions before they are read changes that stage’s anchors; assigning the array does not start a climb. Rebuilding destroys old markers and replaces the array.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.headColor
member.summary: Shared stored head color with no verified effect in the inspected drawings.

remarks.para: The type’s initial setup sets red, green, blue and alpha to (1, 0, 0.5, 1). Color channels are unitless; alpha 1 is fully opaque. This is a static value, meaning all LinkData instances share the same stored color.

The complete inspected LinkData preview methods do not read this color. AgentLinkControl’s inspected gizmo drawing uses its own color instead. Changing this value alone therefore does not recolor those drawings.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.headJoint
member.summary: Cached reference to the head joint created during a later ledge-climb stage.

remarks.para: The ledge routine adds a ConfigurableJoint to the agent’s head body, aims its connection at headTarget and copies the joint reference here. Later it shifts that connection and destroys the agent’s head joint as the climb finishes.

A physics joint connects bodies or constrains their motion. The agent also keeps its own joint reference; assigning this cached field does not automatically replace that reference or retarget an existing connection. Traversal can destroy or replace the joint later, so this cache can become invalid.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.headTarget
member.summary: Head-position marker read when the ledge routine prepares its temporary head connection.

remarks.para: The single-edge and ledge builders replace this transform and place it chestHeight above and chestDepth forward from edgeTarget. A transform stores position, rotation and scale. chestHeight is a vertical offset and chestDepth is a forward offset under rotaterParentObj, normally metres at scale 1.

The ledge routine first copies its world position into a head joint’s connection point. A joint is a physics connection that constrains bodies. A later stage reads the marker’s local position, offsets it, and converts that result through the LinkData transform for another anchor. Moving the marker before a stage reads it changes that setup; an already copied anchor does not continuously follow it. Rebuilding replaces the marker.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.idealLaunchData
member.summary: Stored initial velocity and estimated flight time for the ideal trajectory sample builder.

remarks.para: Its iVel is a world X/Y/Z velocity in metres per second, and ttTarg is estimated flight time in seconds. DrawEditorPath and DrawEditorPathWithPlayerBody calculate these without drag-compensation multipliers, then store them here and rebuild positions.

The sample builder uses the stored velocity and time to calculate an ideal no-air-resistance arc. The player’s drag-compensated launch also replaces this data before starting optional path-error monitoring. Editing this value alone does not rebuild the sample array or change forces already applied to bodies.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.ignoreLaunchTarget
member.summary: Preserves the launch target’s local placement when the target hierarchy is rebuilt.

remarks.para: With this flag enabled, CreateEdgeObjectsByType reads the current launchTarget local position into lastLaunchTargPos before destroying the old target parent. CreateLaunchObjects then uses that saved position for the new target instead of the usual edge-plus-launchHeight placement. Requires the old launch target to exist for the save.
It controls target rebuilding, not whether a launch calculation reads the target. CalculateLaunchData still aims using launchTarget. Setting the flag does not reposition the target until setup runs.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.isDrawingError
member.summary: Shows the player-to-ideal-path error line while the launch monitor is comparing valid adjacent samples.

remarks.para: When true, CoMeasureError draws a debug line between its calculated ideal world position and the player pelvis. It uses red when corrective thrust is active and green when it is inactive. Debug lines are development visual aids, not physical objects.

This controls drawing inside the running monitor; it does not start that coroutine or turn thrust on. A coroutine is a routine that resumes over later frames. If the current path index has no next sample, that comparison and error line are skipped.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.isDrawingSim
member.summary: Stored simulation-drawing flag that does not start the inspected trajectory preview methods.

remarks.para: The inspected LinkData launch and preview methods do not read this field. Those preview methods run when called and prepare positions without testing this flag. Assigning it alone therefore does not change the verified behavior through those methods.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.isObstructed
member.summary: Makes block climbing pause before its arm-attachment stage until the flag clears or its wait budget expires.

remarks.para: After the first chest-hold stage, CoClimbBlock reads this flag every resumed frame. While true and obstructionTimer remains positive, subtracts that frame’s deltaTime and waits for the next frame. deltaTime is elapsed game time in seconds; the normal starter supplies a 10-second wait budget.

Clearing this flag lets the next resumed check proceed. Exhausting the wait budget also proceeds even if it stays true. This field is a supplied status flag: the inspected routine does not perform a collision test or automatically discover an obstruction to set it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.isOccupied
member.summary: Claim flag that makes the normal agent starter wait before using this link.

remarks.para: StartLinkByType checks this flag, and its occupation-wait coroutine keeps checking it across frames until the link is free. A coroutine is a routine that resumes over later frames. ClaimLink and OnZipOccupied set true; ReleaseLink sets false. The zip manager also marks its managed upward route claimed or released.

This flag is a record, not a guaranteed count of objects physically on the link. OnZipOccupied does not assign an agent; a zip release can leave currLinkAgent recorded. Setting the flag alone does not apply the cost change performed by ClaimLink, and ClaimLink itself does not reject an already occupied link.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.isPosArrayReversed
member.summary: Bookkeeping flag that the player launch uses to decide whether positions needs reversing for its direction.

remarks.para: ToggleReversePositionArray reverses positions in place, then flips this flag. It leaves dragPositions unchanged. LaunchPlayer checks the flag during optional correction setup and may call that reversal helper for the selected side.

Writing true does not reverse the array. If the flag and actual array order disagree, a later launch can choose the wrong sample order. The ideal-path builder creates a new positions array without resetting this flag, so rebuilding samples does not automatically prove the flag matches the new order.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.isSubbedToJump
member.summary: Bookkeeping flag used to prevent duplicate player-jump listener changes.

remarks.para: SubToPlayerJump(true) adds LaunchPlayer to the rig’s jump event only if this is false, then sets it true. SubToPlayerJump(false) removes the listener only if the flag is true, then clears it. A listener is a function called when an event happens.

Writing the flag directly does not add or remove a listener and can put this record out of sync with the actual subscription. The pad-off method requests unsubscribe, while pad-on does not request subscribe.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.jointDrive
member.summary: Stored spring, damping and force-cap settings copied to the mover joint’s three movement axes.

remarks.para: A drive is the part of a physics joint that pulls bodies toward a target. positionSpring is spring strength in newtons per metre, positionDamper resists relative speed in newton-seconds per metre, and maximumForce limits force in newtons.

CreateMoverJoint fills this value with the requested positive spring and force cap, or 2500 for each nonpositive input, plus damping 100. UpdateMoverJointDrive replaces spring and maximum force directly while keeping damping, then applies the stored drive to X, Y and Z. Editing this stored struct alone does not update an already created joint until such an application call runs.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.kneeHeight
member.summary: Downward distance from edgeTarget used when rebuilding the ledge knee markers.

remarks.para: The single-edge and ledge builders put leftKneeTarget and rightKneeTarget kneeHeight below edgeTarget. Their sideways positions use twice edgeWidth on each side, and they sit edgeDepth backward. edgeWidth is sideways spacing and edgeDepth is a forward/back offset.
For example, kneeHeight 0.5 puts both knee markers half a local unit below the edge. This controls marker placement, not the measured size of an avatar’s legs.

Local distances are measured along rotaterParentObj’s axes: X right, Y up, Z forward. They normally mean metres when the link and parent have scale 1. Editing placement settings does not move existing markers until their builder runs again.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.lastLaunchTargPos
member.summary: Saved local position used to restore the launch target across a target-hierarchy rebuild.

remarks.para: When ignoreLaunchTarget is true, CreateEdgeObjectsByType copies launchTarget.localPosition here before destroying the old parent hierarchy. CreateLaunchObjects reads it when placing the replacement target. Local X/Y/Z are relative to the target’s parent, normally in metres at scale 1.

This is a rebuild snapshot, not the target’s live world position. Moving the target later does not update this cache automatically. Calling the launch builder directly with preservation enabled can reuse an older snapshot; the dispatcher refreshes it first.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.launchAngle
member.summary: Stored launch-angle number that does not affect the inspected launch calculations.

remarks.para: The inspected LinkData launch and preview methods do not read this field. Those calculations use positions, arc height and gravity; no degree/radian convention or display behavior is established for this field. Assigning it alone therefore does not change the verified behavior through those methods.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.launchData
member.summary: Stored launch-data struct that is not automatically filled by the inspected launch calculators.

remarks.para: The inspected LinkData launch and preview methods do not read this field. CalculateLaunchData and CalcInitialVelocity return values to their callers; those inspected callers use local results, while previews store idealLaunchData instead. This struct’s iVel represents a world velocity in m/s and ttTarg represents flight time in seconds, but this field can remain stale unless separately assigned. Assigning it alone therefore does not change the verified behavior through those methods.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.launchForce
member.summary: Stored launch-related number that is not the force applied by the inspected player and agent launches.

remarks.para: Starts at 1 on a new component before scene data is loaded. No force unit is established for this field by those routines.

The inspected LinkData calculations and AgentLinkControl launch routine do not read this field. Those routines calculate velocity changes and impulses from other settings; they do not use this value as a force cap or speed. Assigning it alone therefore does not change the verified behavior through those methods.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.launchForceMult
member.summary: Unitless multiplier for launch velocity in the branch that does not apply drag compensation.

remarks.para: With applyDragForce false, LaunchPlayer multiplies its computed arc velocity plus its direction adjustment by this value before subtracting the rig’s tracked current velocity. Agent launch similarly multiplies the velocity it adds to its bodies. For example, 1.5 increases the requested added/target velocity components by 50 percent in these branches.

The drag-compensation branches instead use their vertical and horizontal multipliers and do not apply launchForceMult. Starts at 1 before scene data is loaded. Changing it affects a later launch calculation, not motion already applied to bodies; it does not multiply a field named launchForce.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.launchHeight
member.summary: Extra local height above the edge used to place launchTarget and calculate launch arcs.

remarks.para: The jump and launch builders normally place launchTarget launchHeight above edgeTarget. edgeTarget itself is generated at edgeHeight above the link origin. These are local vertical distances, normally metres at scale 1. With edgeHeight 4 and launchHeight 3, the ordinary generated target has local Y = 7.

Player and agent launch calculations also read edgeHeight + launchHeight directly, subtracting the selected starting endpoint’s local Y for their arc-height input. Thus editing this value can change later launch calculations even while the existing marker still has an older position. Rebuild to update the marker; ignoreLaunchTarget can preserve its manual placement instead.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.launchLinePoints
member.summary: Stored four-point vector array that is not the trajectory array read by the inspected helpers.

remarks.para: The constructor creates an array of four zero Vector3 values. No coordinate-frame or line-rendering rule for this array is established by those methods.

The inspected LinkData launch and preview methods do not read this field. The ideal-path builder and corrective thrust use positions, while the height debug helpers use dragPositions. Assigning it alone therefore does not change the verified behavior through those methods.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.launchMag

remarks.para: The inspected LinkData launch calculations and AgentLinkControl launch routine do not read this field. Those routines derive velocity from height, gravity and endpoint positions and use launchForceMult where applicable. They establish no physical unit for launchMag. Assigning it alone therefore does not change the verified behavior through those methods.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.launchRoutine
member.summary: Stored coroutine handle that does not identify the correction routine started by the inspected player launch.

remarks.para: The inspected LinkData launch and correction methods do not read this field. A coroutine is a routine resumed over later frames, and a handle identifies a started routine. LaunchPlayer starts and stores its error-monitoring routine in thrustRoutine instead. Assigning it alone therefore does not change the verified behavior through those methods.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.launchTarget
member.summary: Position marker read by launch calculations and the player’s launch-direction guide.

remarks.para: CalculateLaunchData reads its world position to choose horizontal displacement and target height. The crablet jump uses its world position when crabTarget is missing. TogglePlayerTarget draws its direction guide toward this marker. World positions normally use metres.

Jump and launch builders replace it above edgeTarget by launchHeight, a local vertical offset. With ignoreLaunchTarget enabled, rebuilding restores a saved local placement instead. Editing the marker changes calculations that read it afterward; it does not alter forces already applied. The drag-compensated player launch aims toward the opposite endpoint object instead.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.launchTime
member.summary: Configured agent jump/launch state duration in game-time seconds, separate from the calculated arc’s flight time.

remarks.para: The normal agent starter passes this duration into its jump or launch coroutine. A coroutine is a routine that resumes over later frames. The launch sequence waits through its preparation stages, applies the launch, enters its launch movement state for this duration and waits before completing the link.

The arc calculation returns its own estimated flight time from height, gravity and positions; that estimate is not replaced by launchTime. Crablet link-jump preparation also uses launchTime for its behavior timeout. Starts at 3 seconds on a new component. Frame-based waits may finish later than the configured interval; it is not the exact total traversal time.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.LinkData.launchableTime
member.summary: Next game-time deadline at which LaunchPlayer can pass its cooldown check.

remarks.para: LaunchPlayer returns while Time.time is strictly less than this value. Time.time is elapsed game time in seconds. At equality, the cooldown check allows the attempt, though active-object and player-reference checks still apply.

An accepted launch replaces the deadline with current game time plus coolDownDuration before applying forces or notifying launch listeners. For example, a launch at game time 12 with duration 3 sets the deadline to 15. This is an absolute game-time deadline, not seconds remaining. Setting it in the past allows a new attempt without changing the duration setting.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.MineCartControl.damper_boost
member.summary: Velocity-response strength for the Boost preset, measured in newton-seconds per meter.

remarks.para: A contact joint is the physics connection guiding part of the cart along the track; its drive acts like a motor. Although the field is called a position damper, the spline contact drive uses it to respond to the difference between target and actual velocity. Each contact joint’s X drive has its position spring set to zero, so this damping coefficient supplies the velocity correction, subject to that joint’s force limit.

A larger nonnegative coefficient asks for a stronger correction for the same speed difference; a zero coefficient removes this velocity-correction contribution. The requested correction can accelerate toward the target or oppose motion that is too fast. This value is a force-per-speed coefficient, not a delay in seconds or a fraction from zero to one.

UpdateSpeed(5) copies this preset value into the corresponding current cache and sends it to splineBody. Editing this field alone does not change the already selected drive; call UpdateSpeed again to apply the edited preset. The preset name does not enforce a particular stopping, braking or boosting behavior; its configured velocity, damping and force limit determine the drive request.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.MineCartControl.director
member.summary: Stored Timeline playback-controller reference that the inspected speed-selection methods do not use.

remarks.para: Timeline is Unity’s timed sequence of animation, sound or other game events.
A PlayableDirector controls playback of a Timeline sequence. The complete MineCartControl constructor and all three speed methods do not read this reference or start, stop or change its playback.

Changing this field alone is therefore not a verified way to make UpdateSpeed drive a ride animation. Timeline events or other scripts can still call the speed methods or use the stored reference; the checked class does not establish that external wiring.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.MineCartControl.force_boost
member.summary: Maximum motor force in newtons for each spline contact joint in the Boost preset.

remarks.para: A contact joint is the physics connection guiding part of the cart along the track; its drive acts like a motor. This caps the force generated by that joint’s X drive while it tries to reach the target velocity. For example, an illustrative value of 50 limits each configured contact drive to 50 N; it is not a request to continuously push with 50 N, and multiple contact joints each receive the same cap.

The cap limits how strongly that drive can accelerate or brake when its damping response asks for more force. It does not limit every force acting on the cart, such as gravity or collisions, or set a joint-breaking threshold.

UpdateSpeed(5) copies this preset value into the corresponding current cache and sends it to splineBody. Editing this field alone does not change the already selected drive; call UpdateSpeed again to apply the edited preset. The preset name does not enforce a particular stopping, braking or boosting behavior; its configured velocity, damping and force limit determine the drive request.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.MineCartControl.hasShot
member.summary: Prevents from applying another preset while true.

remarks.para: That routine checks this flag first, applies UpdateSpeed only when it is false, and writes true after the application returns. It is a latch for this trigger across all preset indexes, not a separate “already used” record for each ride preset.

Clear this flag to allow the trigger again; clearing it alone neither restores an old preset nor updates the cart’s drive. The other flag, hasShot2, is independent, and ordinary UpdateSpeed does not clear either latch. A returned application with an out-of-range index also sets this latch, even though it reused the old current caches.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.MineCartControl.rideSpeed
member.summary: Stored label for the last UpdateSpeed request.

remarks.para: The index mapping is 0 Off, 1 Station, 2 Lift, 3 Coast, 4 Brake, 5 Boost, 6 SuperBoost, 7 MatchSpeed1 and 8 MatchSpeed2. UpdateSpeed stores the requested value before selecting and applying the three drive settings. Assigning this field directly does not apply a preset or read the preset fields.

An out-of-range request can leave an undeclared value here while the old current caches are reapplied. This label alone therefore does not prove which values the spline body currently holds. Preset names are categories, not automatic guarantees that a cart stops, brakes, boosts or matches another speed.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.MineCartControl.splineBody
member.summary: Spline-driven physical body that receives the cart’s selected target velocity, damping and force limit.

remarks.para: A contact joint is a physics connection guiding part of the cart along the track; its drive acts like a motor. The target is signed meters per second (m/s) along the contact joint’s track-oriented X direction, so its sign follows that joint’s orientation rather than a fixed direction in the scene. Damping sets how much motor force responds to each m/s of difference between target and actual speed, in newton-seconds per meter (N·s/m). The force setting caps each contact motor in newtons (N).

A spline is the curved path used as the track. Its body holds the Rigidbody, the object’s simulated physical body, and the contact joints that guide it along that path. UpdateSpeed requires this reference and the body’s Rigidbody, then calls its three setting routines in velocity, damping, force order.

Those routines store the values, mark the settings changed and wake the physical body. The associated SplineJoint later copies them into contact-drive settings during an eligible physics update. Assigning this reference alone does not attach a cart to a spline, create contact joints or apply the selected preset.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.MineCartControl.velocity_boost
member.summary: Target velocity in meters per second for the Boost preset’s track drive.

remarks.para: splineBody.axis is a direction vector expressed relative to the cart body: its components describe a direction that turns with that body, with no distance units. It supplies the contact joint’s X direction, which this setup aligns with the track.

A contact joint is the physics connection guiding part of the cart along the track; its drive acts like a motor. This is passed into the X component of each spline contact joint’s targetVelocity, with the other components zero. The joint’s X direction is configured from splineBody.axis and aligned with the track; the sign is relative to that joint orientation, not a fixed world direction.

For example, an illustrative value of 2 requests 2 m/s in that drive direction. It is a target, not a guaranteed measured cart speed: the drive’s damping, force limit and the forces on the cart affect whether it reaches that target.

UpdateSpeed(5) copies this preset value into the corresponding current cache and sends it to splineBody. Editing this field alone does not change the already selected drive; call UpdateSpeed again to apply the edited preset. The preset name does not enforce a particular stopping, braking or boosting behavior; its configured velocity, damping and force limit determine the drive request.

For example, an illustrative value of 2 requests 2 m/s in that drive direction. It is a target, not a guaranteed measured cart speed: the drive’s damping, force limit and the forces on the cart affect whether it reaches that target.

UpdateSpeed(8) copies this preset value into the corresponding current cache and sends it to splineBody. Editing this field alone does not change the already selected drive; call UpdateSpeed again to apply the edited preset. MatchSpeed is a preset name here; the checked control methods copy stored values and do not measure another cart’s speed.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.MineCartLapBar.OnBarLocked
member.summary: Event run by LockBar after the bar’s motor target and strong angular drive have been set.

remarks.para: An event is a list of listener functions to run at that point. This UnityEvent passes no player, angle or other arguments. A listener could play a latch sound or turn on a lock indicator.

The event reports the command being applied, not a physics measurement proving that the bar is motionless. Every successful LockBar call invokes it, including repeated calls. In the automatic seating check, it runs inside LockBar before the checking routine finishes.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.MineCartLapBar.OnBarUnlocked
member.summary: Event run by UnlockBar after the bar’s motor target and gentler angular drive have been set.

remarks.para: An event is a list of listener functions to run at that point. This UnityEvent passes no arguments. For example, a listener can play an unlatch sound when the gentler drive is applied.

The bar may still be moving or resting against another object when listeners run; this event does not wait for an open position. Each successful UnlockBar call invokes it again. Leaving the seat invokes OnUnseat instead and does not automatically invoke this event.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.MineCartLapBar.OnSeat
member.summary: Event run after a player is registered with the seat and this component has started its bar-angle checks.

remarks.para: An event is a list of listener functions to run at that point. This UnityEvent passes no player or other arguments. The seat’s registration notification triggers the handler; registration attaches the player to the seat system and can happen before the seating motion has finished.

The handler first stops any previous checker, starts a new coroutine and stores its handle, then runs OnSeat. A coroutine is a routine that can pause and continue on later frames. This checker first waits until a later frame before measuring an angle, so OnSeat runs before its first possible automatic OnBarLocked event.
A listener could turn on a “close the bar” prompt. Starting these checks does not drive the bar closed: the checker waits for the measured twist to reach lockAngle.

The checker compares the Servo’s signed turning angle in degrees around its joint’s configured primary axis, the direction around which twist is measured, with lockAngle, the threshold in degrees. The angle is measured against the reference set during Servo initialization, relative to the connected physics body when present, otherwise fixed in the world. A physics body is an object whose motion Unity simulates.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.MineCartLapBar.OnUnseat
member.summary: Event run after the seat deregisters the player and this component stops and clears its bar-angle checker.

remarks.para: An event is a list of listener functions to run at that point. This UnityEvent passes no player or other arguments. The seat sends its deregistration notification after clearing its registered player reference.

The lap-bar handler stops the stored coroutine, a routine that pauses and continues on later frames, when there is a handle; it then clears _checkingBar and runs OnUnseat. It does not change the bar’s joint drive or call UnlockBar. For example, an OnUnseat listener can explicitly call UnlockBar if leaving should also release the bar.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.MineCartLapBar._checkingBar
member.summary: Stored handle for the most recently started routine that checks whether the seated player’s bar has reached the locking angle.

remarks.para: A coroutine is a routine that can pause and continue on later frames; its handle lets Unity stop that particular routine. On seating, this component stops an old handle if present, starts a replacement and stores the returned handle here. On unseating it stops the stored routine and sets this field to null before running OnUnseat.

The routine waits one frame before its first check. Below the threshold it requests a wait of 0.25 game seconds before checking again. Game seconds follow the game’s time scale, so slow motion lengthens the real wait; frame scheduling also means this is not an exact quarter-second wall-clock timer.

Once the threshold is met, the routine calls LockBar and ends, but does not clear this field. A non-null handle therefore does not prove that checks are still running. Calling UnlockBar does not clear it or cancel the checker. The component’s own OnDisable handler only removes seat listeners; it does not explicitly clear this field.

The checker compares the Servo’s signed turning angle in degrees around its joint’s configured primary axis, the direction around which twist is measured, with lockAngle, the threshold in degrees. The angle is measured against the reference set during Servo initialization, relative to the connected physics body when present, otherwise fixed in the world. A physics body is an object whose motion Unity simulates.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.MineCartLapBar.cj
member.summary: Physics joint whose rotation target and angular X motor drive LockBar and UnlockBar change.

remarks.para: A ConfigurableJoint is a physics connection between the bar and another body, or a fixed place in the scene. Its primary axis defines the direction around which the angular X motor twists; this need not be the scene’s X direction.

Assign the joint before Start, Unity’s setup call before the first update. Start reads this joint object’s local rotation, its orientation relative to its parent, into startRotation before its later fallback check. A missing joint cannot safely rely on that late fallback. Reset, the component’s reference-filling helper, obtains the joint on this same object.

Both lock commands use local rotation targets and replace the angular X drive. The local-target helper logs an error if this joint’s configuredInWorldSpace setting is true, then continues down its local-target path, so configure this joint for local targets and a working angular X drive. For these angular-X values to control rotation, set Rotation Drive Mode to X & YZ; Slerp mode uses the separate Slerp drive. When cj.swapBodies is enabled, the helper exchanges the requested target and reference rotations; the roles described for LockBar, UnlockBar and startRotation assume it is disabled. Joint limits still affect how the bar can move. The servo field supplies the measured angle separately, so point that Servo at the same bar joint for the threshold and the commanded motor to agree.
Replacing this field after setup does not automatically rebuild startRotation. The old orientation cache can then describe a different joint object.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.MineCartLapBar.lockAngle
member.summary: Signed twist threshold in degrees at or above which the seated player’s checker calls LockBar.

remarks.para: Twist means turning around the Servo joint’s configured primary axis, with sideways swing removed from the measurement. The angle is measured against the orientation cached when that Servo was initialized, relative to its connected physics body when it has one. A physics body is an object whose movement and rotation Unity simulates. This is not the bar’s raw three-axis rotation in the scene or a fraction of a full turn.

The checker reads this value again on each check. For example, with a threshold of 30 degrees, a measured 29 degrees keeps waiting; 30 or 31 degrees calls LockBar and ends that checker. Positive and negative twist are different: a measured -30 degrees does not reach a positive 30-degree threshold. Choose the sign after testing which direction your joint reports.

The first check is on a later frame after seating. Below threshold, later checks request 0.25 game seconds of waiting; time scale and frame timing affect the real interval. Changing this field does not perform an immediate check. The value is not clamped, and a threshold already met at the first sample can lock immediately at that sample.

This is a trigger for a strong motor hold at the bar’s current rotation, not the motor’s requested target angle. An explicit LockBar call does not test this threshold. CheckBar compares the measured angle immediately during its call and can also call LockBar.
Game time follows the game’s slow-motion or pause setting, so the requested wait need not last 0.25 seconds on a real clock.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.MineCartLapBar.seat
member.summary: Seat whose player registration and deregistration notifications start and stop this bar’s angle checker.

remarks.para: Assign this reference before the component is enabled. OnEnable, Unity’s call when the component becomes active, subscribes the seating and unseating handlers to this seat’s two events. OnDisable removes those handlers.

Registration starts a coroutine, a routine that can pause and continue on later frames, then runs OnSeat. Deregistration stops and clears it, then runs OnUnseat. These are seat-system notifications; the registration notification does not mean that the player’s seating motion has finished.

Changing the reference while enabled does not transfer the existing subscriptions to the new seat. Set it before enabling, or disable with the old reference still assigned before replacing it. Leaving the seat does not automatically unlock the bar.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.MineCartLapBar.servo
member.summary: Servo that supplies the signed twist angle for deciding when the lap bar should lock.

remarks.para: The checker asks this Servo for the angle of its own joint around that joint’s primary axis, in degrees. The Servo removes sideways swing and compares the current orientation with its initialized orientation. If the joint connects to another physics body, an object whose movement Unity simulates, that moving body supplies the reference frame; without one, the reference is fixed in the world.

Servo.Start, Unity’s setup call before the first update, finds the relevant joint and physics body and calls its initialization routine. That initialization caches the body’s starting rotation relative to the connected body, or relative to the world when there is no connected body. Give the Servo time to initialize before using its angle; moving or replacing the joint afterward does not automatically rebuild that cache.

MineCartLapBar.Start finds a Servo on this same object if this field is missing, after reading cj’s starting rotation. Reset also fills the reference from this object. Configure the Servo to measure the same bar joint assigned to cj: the checker measures through servo but the lock commands apply their drive through cj.
Assigning this field does not itself make the bar close. In the inspected lap-bar methods it supplies angle measurements; LockBar and UnlockBar write the joint’s motor settings directly.
A physics joint is a simulated connection that controls how the bar can move. Its configured primary axis is the direction around which twist is measured; it need not be the scene’s X direction.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.MineCartLapBar.startRotation
member.summary: Cached startup local orientation used when converting the lap bar’s lock and unlock targets into the joint’s frame.

remarks.para: Start, Unity’s setup call before the first update, copies cj’s transform.localRotation here. Local rotation describes how the joint’s object is turned relative to its parent. A quaternion is Unity’s four-number representation of an orientation; its four values are not separate degree angles.

With cj.swapBodies disabled, LockBar supplies the current local rotation as the requested target and this cached rotation as the reference. UnlockBar supplies this cached rotation as the requested target and the current local rotation as the reference. When cj.swapBodies is enabled, the helper exchanges those target and reference inputs in each command. The helper then converts that pair into the joint’s rotation target.

The cache is not refreshed on each command. Changing the visible bar rotation or assigning a different cj later does not update it. Reset fills the joint and Servo references; it does not save or restore this rotation. For example, set up the initial bar orientation and assign cj before Start so the reference is saved from the intended pose.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.NooseBonelabIntro.GALLOWSEntity
member.summary: The gallows entity requested to hide after the cut sequence’s five-second cleanup delay.

remarks.para: A MarrowEntity groups the gallows objects for game management. On a Cut-stage Update after scene streaming reports DONE and a player rig is available, cleanup requires game time strictly beyond the five-second deadline and _nooseBool to be false. Update stops and disables the cutscene, marks cleanup complete, and requests hiding of the dagger followed by this entity. The request uses the entity manager’s normal update path. Passing the deadline alone does not trigger another hide request while the retained _nooseBool latch is true.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.NooseBonelabIntro._armJointInitial0
member.summary: Cached world rotation of [0], read by when restoring the platform.

remarks.para: Recorded from armPlatformJoints[0] in OnEnable, Unity’s callback when the component becomes enabled, after any reset attempted there. member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.NooseBonelabIntro._chestToKnot
member.summary: The live physics connection holding the player’s chest to the noose knot.

remarks.para: AttachNeck creates this ConfigurableJoint on the chest body and connects it to knotRb. A joint limits or drives relative movement between two physics objects. Reeling updates its spring and side target; Hanging checks its upward world-space force to decide choking damage.
NooseCut, an eligible ResetNoose, and OnDisable request destruction of this joint and clear the saved reference. Changing this reference does not create, configure, or destroy a joint by itself.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.NooseBonelabIntro._daggerInitRot
member.summary: Cached world rotation used to return the dagger to its saved pose during ResetNoose.

remarks.para: OnEnable, Unity’s callback when this component becomes enabled, records dagger.transform.rotation after any reset attempted there. This is a quaternion, Unity’s four-number representation of orientation, not an angle measured in degrees. ResetNoose reads it together with _daggerInitV3.

Changing the cache changes the restored orientation if reset reaches the dagger step. It does not rotate the current dagger immediately, and moving the dagger does not update this cache until the next enable callback.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.NooseBonelabIntro._daggerInitV3
member.summary: Cached world position used to return the dagger to its saved location during ResetNoose.

remarks.para: OnEnable, Unity’s callback when this component becomes enabled, records dagger.transform.position after any reset attempted there. The vector’s X, Y, and Z values are absolute world coordinates in meters, not offsets from the noose or the dagger’s parent.

Changing this cache changes the position reset attempts to restore; it does not move the current dagger immediately. For example, adding 0.1 to its world Y value raises the saved reset location by 10 cm. The next enable callback records a new cache.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.NooseBonelabIntro._hostManager
member.summary: Manages the noose grab points that attachment and cutting forcibly release, enable, or disable.

remarks.para: OnEnable, Unity’s callback when this component becomes enabled, obtains this InteractableHostManager from the same object. A host is an object’s grab point. AttachNeck releases and disables hosts 6, 7, and 8; NooseCut releases all hosts and disables their interaction and collisions; ResetNoose attempts to enable those again.

Enable and disable also add and remove hand-attachment callbacks, routines called when a grab starts or ends. Both of this class’s attached/detached callbacks have empty bodies in the inspected native code, so those subscriptions do not themselves advance the noose sequence.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.NooseBonelabIntro._isHanging
member.summary: Enables choking checks after the platform-release sequence reaches its dagger cue.

remarks.para: HangingSequence sets this flag true at step 7 before invoking daggerSpawnEvent. Update only uses it for damage while _nooseStage is also Hanging, so it is a sequence flag rather than a measurement that the player is physically suspended.

NooseCut changes the stage without immediately clearing this flag. Cut cleanup clears it after the five-second deadline; ResetNoose does not clear it. Setting it alone does not attach the chest joint or complete platform release.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.NooseBonelabIntro._minDistanceJoint
member.summary: No pulling or distance-limiting effect was verified for this SpringJoint field in NooseBonelabIntro.

remarks.para: A SpringJoint would normally be a spring-like physics connection between two objects. In all 22 unique native method bodies of this class and the LoadFXAndLevel continuation inspected for this audit, this field is not created, read, or written. Attachment and choking instead use _chestToKnot. This finding does not cover unrelated classes or mods.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.NooseBonelabIntro._nooseBool
member.summary: Remembers that the delayed Cut-stage cleanup has already been performed.

remarks.para: After the five-second cut deadline, Update stops the cutscene, sets this flag true, clears _isHanging, and requests hiding of the dagger and gallows. Later Cut updates skip that cleanup while this flag is true. NooseCut and ResetNoose do not clear it in the inspected class, so repeating the sequence requires handling the latch separately.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.NooseBonelabIntro._nooseStage
member.summary: Selects the current part of the attachment, hanging, and escape sequence.

remarks.para: Initial checks whether the noose is positioned for attachment. Reeling pulls the chest and knot together. Locked waits for the reveal deadline. Hanging runs platform release and then force-gated damage. Cut cancels pending intro death work when needed and later hides the scene objects.

Changing this value only changes which Update branch runs; it does not perform the joint setup, deadlines, events, or cleanup that normally accompany a transition. _isHanging separately enables damage after the platform joints have released.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.NooseBonelabIntro._nooseTimer
member.summary: The game-time deadline for the next reeling, reveal, platform-release, or cut-cleanup action.

remarks.para: Stored as an absolute Time.time value in seconds, not elapsed time or a countdown. The usual calculation is deadline = current game time + delay seconds. For example, at game time 20 seconds, a four-second delay stores 24.

AttachNeck schedules one second for reeling. Locking schedules nooseOnToSceneReveal; entering Hanging schedules sceneRevealToPlankDrop; each platform release schedules plankDropTimer; cutting schedules five seconds. The time-based Reeling transition, reveal, and Cut cleanup require game time strictly beyond the deadline, while platform release accepts equality. Reeling can also finish before its deadline when the distance from the midpoint of the two rope-side anchor points to the physical chest is strictly below 0.1 metre, or 10 centimetres. Exactly 10 centimetres still waits for the time-based route. Timed actions happen when a later eligible Update observes the boundary; Cut cleanup additionally requires _nooseBool to be false.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.NooseBonelabIntro._sideLeft
member.summary: Remembers whether the chest-to-knot joint is targeting the left side of the chest.

remarks.para: CheckAndSetTargetSide sets this true when the knot anchor is more than 2 cm to the chest’s left, and false when it is more than 2 cm to the right. It measures sideways displacement in the virtual chest’s orientation and keeps the old side within that center band.

The corresponding joint targets are (-0.2, 0, 0.2) meters for left and (0.2, 0, 0.2) meters for right in the joint’s target coordinates. Editing the flag alone does not write a new target; it changes which crossing the next check waits for.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.NooseBonelabIntro._skipUpdate
member.summary: Prevents the intro from starting its delayed death/fade sequence more than once at a time.

remarks.para: Update sets this true before starting LoadFXAndLevel when Hanging health is at or below zero. That coroutine is a sequence that pauses and continues across frames. This flag does not disable Update or its damage checks.
If the stage becomes Cut while the flag is true, Update stops this component’s coroutines, restores full health, and then clears the flag. ResetNoose does not clear it in the inspected class.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.NooseBonelabIntro._stageInt
member.summary: Selects the next platform joint to release, then records completion of the dagger cue.

remarks.para: Entering Hanging resets this counter to 0. Steps 0 through 6 release the matching armPlatformJoints entry when its deadline is reached. Step 7 increments it to 8, sets _isHanging, and invokes daggerSpawnEvent; step 8 has no further release action.
OnEnable, Unity’s callback when the component becomes enabled, also resets this counter. ResetNoose itself does not. It is an integer step index, not time in seconds or the NooseStage enum.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.NooseBonelabIntro._timeSinceLastDamageTick
member.summary: Accumulated game-time seconds checked before the next choking damage tick.

remarks.para: Update adds each frame’s deltaTime while the stage is Hanging and _isHanging is true. Damage requires this value to be strictly greater than damageTickRate and the chest joint’s upward world-space force to exceed massTotal × 9.81 × 0.5 newtons. Here massTotal is the avatar’s cached total mass in kilograms, 9.81 is the weight conversion in meters per second squared, and 0.5 selects half its weight.

The timer resets after a damage call and also whenever upward joint force is 500 newtons or less, checked after that possible call. It is not simply time spent wearing the noose. Excess time is discarded on a tick, and ResetNoose does not clear the accumulator.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.NooseBonelabIntro.armPlatformJoints
member.summary: The ordered physics connections released one at a time during the platform-drop sequence.

remarks.para: A ConfigurableJoint connects objects in the physics simulation and can restrict their rotation. HangingSequence processes entries 0 through 6, freeing each joint’s X-axis angular movement at its deadline. Supply at least seven non-null entries in the intended release order. This code does not identify them as the player’s arm joints.

OnEnable, Unity’s callback when this component becomes enabled, caches world rotations for only entries 0 through 4. ResetNoose attempts to restore those five rotations and their Limited X-axis angular movement; entries 5 and 6 are not restored there. plankDropTimer controls the game-time gap between consecutive releases.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.NooseBonelabIntro.dagger
member.summary: The dagger’s Rigidbody whose pose and movement ResetNoose attempts to restore.

remarks.para: A Rigidbody is Unity’s physics body, which stores an object’s movement, mass, and rotation. OnEnable, Unity’s callback when this component becomes enabled, saves this dagger’s world position and rotation. ResetNoose attempts to restore those caches and set both its movement and spinning velocity to zero.
Visibility is requested through daggerEntity instead. The daggerSpawnEvent cue does not assign, create, or reveal this Rigidbody in the inspected class.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.NooseBonelabIntro.daggerEntity
member.summary: The dagger’s , which this intro requests to hide during setup, manual hiding, reset, and cut cleanup.

remarks.para: The entity groups the dagger objects for game management. These calls use its normal hide request rather than forcing its GameObject inactive immediately. daggerSpawnEvent is only invoked as a cue; the inspected NooseBonelabIntro methods do not unhide or spawn this entity themselves.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.NooseBonelabIntro.daggerSpawnEvent
member.summary: Cue invoked after all seven platform joints have been released, with _isHanging already true.

remarks.para: A UnityEvent runs the listener routines attached to it, with no arguments here. Step 7 first advances _stageInt to 8 and sets _isHanging true, then invokes this event. The code does not confirm that a dagger has spawned or reveal the saved dagger; listeners must supply any such action. Damage checks follow the invocation in the normal Update path.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.NooseBonelabIntro.damagePerTick
member.summary: Health points requested from the player for each qualifying choking damage tick.

remarks.para: Update passes this amount directly to pH.TAKEDAMAGE after the upward-force and damageTickRate time conditions pass. It uses the same scale as pH.curr_Health, not a percentage: for example, damagePerTick = 1.5 requests a reduction of 1.5 health points when current health is positive.

The timer resets after each request, and at most one tick is requested per rendered frame. Player_Health then handles its usual damage reactions and regeneration or dying behavior; this value is not a per-second damage rate.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.NooseBonelabIntro.damageTickRate
member.summary: The game-time interval threshold, in seconds, before a qualifying choking damage tick can occur.

remarks.para: Update requires _timeSinceLastDamageTick to be strictly greater than this value, while the chest joint’s upward world-space force exceeds half the avatar’s calculated weight. The avatar’s weight is its cached total mass in kilograms multiplied by 9.81 meters per second squared, giving newtons. The timer is reset after a tick and when upward force is 500 newtons or less, checked afterward.

For an example value of 3, reaching exactly three accumulated seconds is not enough; the next qualifying frame can deal damage. The frame check and force-dependent resets mean actual damage times need not be exactly three seconds apart. No loop catches up missed ticks, and this field is an interval, not ticks per second.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.NooseBonelabIntro.hasChokePlayed
member.summary: Records that NooseChoke has already issued its first looping-audio request.

remarks.para: NooseChoke sets this true after requesting the loop. While true, further calls request stopping the player; they do not start a second loop and do not clear the flag. It therefore does not report whether audio is currently playing or whether an asynchronous audio request completed successfully.
ResetNoose and OnEnable do not clear it in the inspected class. Clearing it separately allows a later NooseChoke call to issue a new loop request.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.NooseBonelabIntro.intoFallingWind
member.summary: Wind audio requested at this component’s world position after a successful Hanging-stage NooseCut reaches its sound step.

remarks.para: NooseCut requests this sound after changing the stage to Cut and calling the dagger joint’s cut helper, and before invoking nooseCutEvent. ResetNoose plays the rope-cut sound but does not request this wind clip. The sound is played at a world point rather than attached to the falling avatar.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.NooseBonelabIntro.introCutscene
member.summary: The Unity timeline player enabled and started when the Locked reveal delay ends.

remarks.para: A PlayableDirector plays scripted scene animation through a timeline. The transition first changes _nooseStage to Hanging and invokes nooseOnAndHeldEvent, then enables this player’s object, resets its playback time to zero, and starts it.

OnEnable stops it and leaves its object disabled. Delayed Cut cleanup also stops and disables it. If ResetNoose reaches its final command, it stops playback but leaves the object enabled. Starting and enabling it also issues the torch spawn request once when torchSpawned is false.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.NooseBonelabIntro.knotRb
member.summary: The knot’s physics body connected to the player’s chest when the noose attaches.

remarks.para: A Rigidbody is Unity’s physics body, which stores mass, movement, and rotation. The attachment anchor is (-0.116, 0, -0.004) meters in this body’s local axes: 11.6 cm toward negative X and 0.4 cm toward negative Z. Its world position and rotation also help decide whether attachment is allowed and which side of the chest the joint targets.

Reeling completion sets its mass to 30 kilograms; cutting or an eligible reset sets it to 2 kilograms. OnEnable, Unity’s callback when the component becomes enabled, adds a world-space velocity change of (2, 0, 2) meters per second to this body and nooseBottomRb. AddVelocityToNoose applies the supplied velocity change to both bodies.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.NooseBonelabIntro.level
member.summary: NooseBonelabIntro’s death/fade path reloads the current scene without reading this level reference.

remarks.para: All 22 unique native method bodies of this class and the LoadFXAndLevel continuation were inspected. The loader uses the game’s default fadeout effect, then SceneStreamer.Reload when that effect reports completion. Changing this field is not a verified way to select a different destination in that path; unrelated classes and mods were not exhaustively checked.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.NooseBonelabIntro.nooseBottomRb
member.summary: The lower noose physics body that receives the same added velocity as knotRb.

remarks.para: A Rigidbody is Unity’s physics body. OnEnable, Unity’s callback when this component becomes enabled, adds (2, 0, 2) meters per second in world axes to this body and the knot. AddVelocityToNoose applies its supplied world-space velocity change to both as well. This body is not one of the three anchor bodies read by the attachment geometry test.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.NooseBonelabIntro.nooseChoke
member.summary: The clip NooseChoke requests to loop on its first call.

remarks.para: The managed audio player receives nooseChokePoint as its parent and that point’s localPosition as the audio offset. hasChokePlayed is set after the request; later NooseChoke calls stop the player instead of requesting another loop. This class’s Update does not itself call NooseChoke, so the clip alone does not establish an automatic hanging trigger.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.NooseBonelabIntro.nooseChokePlayer
member.summary: The managed audio player used to request and stop the choking loop.

remarks.para: NooseChoke requests the loop through this object on its first call, then calls Stop on later calls while hasChokePlayed stays true.
