The component’s constructor creates a managed player, but assigning this field only changes which player those calls use; it does not start sound by itself.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.NooseBonelabIntro.nooseChokePoint
member.summary: The parent transform and source of the local offset supplied for the choking audio loop.

remarks.para: NooseChoke passes this transform as the audio parent and also passes its localPosition as the offset relative to that parent. A transform stores an object’s position and orientation; localPosition normally means position relative to its own parent. Here that numeric value is reused in the point’s own coordinate frame, so the sound is not necessarily centered exactly on this transform.

With localPosition = (0, 0, 0), the supplied offset is zero. With (0, 0.1, 0) and point scale 1, the supplied offset is 10 cm along this point’s local up direction, in addition to the point’s placement. These values are captured when the loop request is issued.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.NooseBonelabIntro.nooseCut
member.summary: The rope-cut sound requested when NooseCut or an eligible ResetNoose releases the chest connection.

remarks.para: Both methods only proceed from the Hanging stage. They request this clip at the NooseBonelabIntro component’s world position before forcibly releasing noose grabs and clearing the chest joint. The lowercase nooseCut field supplies audio; the uppercase NooseCut method performs the gameplay action.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.NooseBonelabIntro.nooseCutEvent
member.summary: Invoked after a Hanging-stage NooseCut has switched to Cut, cleared the chest-joint reference, and called the dagger cut helper.

remarks.para: A UnityEvent runs attached listener routines, with no arguments here. It fires after the chest-joint reference is cleared, the knot mass is set to 2 kilograms, the stage becomes Cut, the dagger helper is called, and the falling-wind sound is requested. If an earlier required step fails, this invocation is not reached.

The _isHanging flag can still be true during listeners. A later eligible Cut-stage Update can clear it when game time is strictly beyond the five-second deadline and _nooseBool is false. That Update also requires scene streaming to report DONE and a player rig to be available, so this is not an exact or unconditional five-second clear. ResetNoose does not invoke this event even though it also performs cut-like cleanup.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.NooseBonelabIntro.nooseDaggerJointScript
member.summary: The helper asked to remove the dagger’s configured physics connection during cutting and reset.

remarks.para: A joint is a connection between two objects in the physics simulation. This helper builds a joint between its own configured bodies. NooseBonelabIntro calls its NooseCut method to remove that connection; the inspected intro code does not check whether the dagger is grabbed as a condition for cutting.

ResetNoose calls the helper twice. When the first call successfully clears its joint reference, the second can fail on that missing reference. The connection is defined by the helper’s body settings, so this field alone does not prove which rope body it connects to.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.NooseBonelabIntro.nooseDeath
member.summary: Invoked after the delayed hanging-death sequence has waited pH.deathTimeAmount seconds.

remarks.para: A UnityEvent runs attached listener routines, with no arguments here. Update starts the coroutine, a sequence that pauses across frames, when Hanging health is at or below zero and sets _skipUpdate first. The coroutine waits the configured health-component death delay, then invokes this event without another health check at that step.

It next waits three game seconds before checking that health is exactly zero and requesting the fade effect. This event therefore does not confirm a completed reload or fade. Entering Cut can cancel the pending sequence before the event is reached.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.NooseBonelabIntro.nooseLeftRb
member.summary: The left side physics body supplying one of the noose’s measured anchor points.

remarks.para: A Rigidbody is Unity’s physics body. CheckReel and CheckRelativeToHead measure a point 8 cm along this body’s negative local X axis, rotated with the body and added to its world position. The midpoint of that point and the matching right-body point is compared with the physical chest.

The attachment test also uses these two side points and the knot point to measure the noose plane’s tilt. Moving or rotating this body changes those checks; this field does not select the left/right chest target by itself.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.NooseBonelabIntro.nooseOnAndHeldEvent
member.summary: Invoked when the Locked reveal delay ends and the stage changes to Hanging, before the cutscene starts.

remarks.para: A UnityEvent runs attached listener routines, with no arguments here. The code sets _nooseStage to Hanging, resets _stageInt to 0, and schedules the first platform-release deadline before invoking the event. It then starts and enables introCutscene.
Despite the name, this transition does not test whether a hand holds a grab point. _isHanging is set later, after seven platform releases, before daggerSpawnEvent.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.NooseBonelabIntro.nooseOnEvent
member.summary: Invoked when reeling finishes and the stage becomes Locked, after the reveal deadline has been scheduled.

remarks.para: A UnityEvent runs attached listener routines, with no arguments here. Reeling finishes when the side-point midpoint is strictly less than 10 cm from the chest or when its one-second deadline has passed. The code clears the joint’s limit spring strength and damping, sets Locked, changes the knot mass to 30 kilograms, and sets _nooseTimer before invoking this event.
Attachment itself has already happened before this cue. The invocation does not test a particular hand grab or mean the platform joints have already released.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.NooseBonelabIntro.nooseOnToSceneReveal
member.summary: Game-time seconds to wait in Locked before starting the reveal cutscene and Hanging stage.

remarks.para: When reeling finishes, the code schedules _nooseTimer as the current game time plus this delay, then invokes nooseOnEvent. Locked proceeds only on a frame whose game time is strictly later than the deadline; equal time still waits.

For an example value of 4, the reveal transition occurs on the first later qualifying frame after four game seconds. Editing this field after locking does not change the deadline already saved in _nooseTimer.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.NooseBonelabIntro.noosePutOn
member.summary: The sound requested by AttachNeck after it creates and configures the chest-to-knot connection.

remarks.para: The sound uses this component’s world position. The request occurs before the three designated noose grab points are released and disabled, and before the stage becomes Reeling. Assigning the clip alone does not attach the noose or start playback.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.NooseBonelabIntro.nooseReveal
member.summary: The reveal sound requested at this component’s world position by Reveal.

remarks.para: Reveal only requests this clip’s playback. It does not switch stages, start introCutscene, or spawn the torch. The inspected Update method does not call Reveal itself, so its timing can be supplied by scene or mod calls.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.NooseBonelabIntro.nooseRightRb
member.summary: The right side physics body supplying one of the noose’s measured anchor points.

remarks.para: A Rigidbody is Unity’s physics body. CheckReel and CheckRelativeToHead measure a point 8 cm along this body’s negative local X axis, rotated with the body and added to its world position. Its midpoint with the left side’s corresponding point is compared with the physical chest.

The attachment test also uses both side points and the knot point to measure the noose plane’s tilt. Moving or rotating this body changes those checks; the _sideLeft target flag is instead decided from the knot anchor relative to the chest.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.NooseBonelabIntro.pH
member.summary: The player-health component receiving choking damage and providing health for the intro’s death/fade decisions.

remarks.para: When Update has to fetch a missing rM, it also obtains this Player_Health from that rig’s health reference. Qualifying hanging ticks call TAKEDAMAGE with damagePerTick health points. Health at or below zero starts the delayed death sequence; its later fade request requires health exactly zero.

If Cut cancels a pending death sequence, Update calls SetFullHealth through this reference before clearing _skipUpdate. Replacing rM while it is already non-null does not automatically refresh pH in the inspected Update path.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.NooseBonelabIntro.plankDropTimer
member.summary: Game-time seconds scheduled between consecutive platform-joint releases.

remarks.para: HangingSequence releases the next armPlatformJoints entry when current game time reaches or passes _nooseTimer, then stores current time plus this delay for the next entry. Entries 0 through 6 release in order, at most one per call. The initial delay before entry 0 instead comes from sceneRevealToPlankDrop.

With an example value of 0.5, each next release is scheduled half a game second after the actual previous release. Late frames shift that schedule; the code does not catch up several releases in one frame. Editing this field affects the next deadline calculation, not the deadline already stored.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.NooseBonelabIntro.rM
member.summary: The player’s , supplying the chest bodies, orientation, and avatar mass for the noose checks.

remarks.para: Update obtains the current player rig when this reference is missing, then caches its Player_Health in pH. A rig groups the tracked, virtual, and physical parts of the player. This intro reads the physical chest position, the physical head’s orientation, the virtual chest’s orientation, and the avatar’s cached total mass through the rig.

Attachment adds its chest connection to this rig’s physical chest body. Assigning this field alone does not create the connection or refresh pH while rM remains non-null; keep the rig and health references consistent when replacing them.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.NooseBonelabIntro.sceneRevealToPlankDrop
member.summary: Game-time seconds from entering Hanging and starting the reveal cutscene until the first platform joint can release.

remarks.para: The Locked-to-Hanging transition stores _nooseTimer as current game time plus this delay before invoking nooseOnAndHeldEvent and starting introCutscene. HangingSequence releases entry 0 on the first later call where time reaches or passes that deadline.

For an example value of 1, the first release is scheduled one game second after that transition. Later releases use plankDropTimer instead. Editing this field after the transition does not replace the deadline already stored.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.NooseBonelabIntro.torchIntro
member.summary: The crate spawner asked to create the intro torch when the reveal cutscene is first started and enabled.

remarks.para: The cutscene helper issues SpawnSpawnable when both playback and enabling are requested and torchSpawned is false. It sets that flag after issuing the request. The helper does not wait for a completed spawn or check a returned torch object; assigning this field does not spawn anything by itself.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.NooseBonelabIntro.torchSpawned
member.summary: Records that the intro has issued its one-time torch spawn request.

remarks.para: The cutscene helper sets this true after calling torchIntro.SpawnSpawnable while starting and enabling the cutscene. It is not a check that a torch object exists or that spawning succeeded. While true, later starts skip another request.
OnEnable and ResetNoose do not clear it in the inspected class. Clearing it separately permits the next qualifying cutscene start to issue another request, even if a previous torch still exists.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PageItem.direction
member.summary: Chooses which of the radial menu's eight configured buttons receives this item when the page is rendered.

remarks.para: The slots run clockwise by name: NORTH is 0, NORTHEAST 1, EAST 2, SOUTHEAST 3, SOUTH 4, SOUTHWEST 5, WEST 6, and NORTHWEST 7. These are menu-slot numbers, not distances, angles, or world compass headings. PageView maps each number to the button at that array index; the configured button determines its actual placement.

For example, EAST routes the item to buttons[2], the third button because array indices start at 0. Changing direction stores a new choice of slot; render the page again to move the displayed item to that slot. Values outside the eight named slots have no matching branch in the renderer.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PageItem.m_Callback
member.summary: Stores the action that Invoke and menu triggers call to perform this item's choice.

remarks.para: An action here is a callback: a saved function that takes no arguments. The constructor adds its c argument to this stored action. On a newly created item, this saves c; passing null leaves no action to call. The callback decides the effect, such as opening another page or starting your own game action.

Invoke, PageItemView.Trigger, and the selected-button path in PageView.Trigger all read this stored action when triggered and call it immediately if it is present. Replacing m_Callback changes what future triggers run, including a button already holding this item. Changing the label or direction alone does not run the callback.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PageItem.name
member.summary: Supplies the label text that the menu view copies onto this item's button when rendered.

remarks.para: For example, "Inventory" tells the player what the choice is meant to do. The renderer copies name into the button's assigned text component when that button has its segment and text references configured. The name does not choose the slot or decide the action; direction and m_Callback supply those separately.
Changing name updates the stored text. Render the item or its page again to copy the new label into an existing button. A button can therefore still show the old label until it is rendered again.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PageView.TextCanvas
member.summary: Holds the scene object enabled for page text during normal opening and disabled during deactivation.

remarks.para: A GameObject is an object in a Unity scene. Activate enables this object when it opens an inactive view. Deactivate clears text in the view's child TextMeshPro labels and disables TextCanvas; Start also runs that text-hiding setup.

Assign the correct canvas object before these calls. Render fills individual button labels but does not enable TextCanvas itself, and CoSummonAnimation alone does not enable it. For example, rendering a page while its text canvas is disabled can update the labels without making them visible.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PageView.audioPlacementOverride
member.summary: Provides the required scene object whose position is used for this page's sound requests.

remarks.para: This field is a GameObject, not a Transform. Its Transform holds the object's position, rotation and size. Hover, selection, closing and summon feedback read this object's Transform and pass it as the sound location. Sound requests sample its world position in scene meters. If playback starts, it uses that sampled position rather than the hovered button position.

Start and CheckRefs test whether this reference is missing but do not fill it with a fallback. Assign a valid object before using those sound-producing paths. For example, a shared menu-center object gives all four sound requests the center position even when the cursor moves to different buttons.
Feedback_Audio samples the supplied location once for the request; later object movement does not move that sound. Its underlying audio settings still control how positional the sound is.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PageView.buttons
member.summary: Supplies the directional button objects that Render fills and the cursor and animations operate on.

remarks.para: Each PageItemView is a Unity component that displays one item and stores its PageItem data. Render maps directions to array indices from 0 through 7 in this order: NORTH, NORTHEAST, EAST, SOUTHEAST, SOUTH, SOUTHWEST, WEST, NORTHWEST. For example, EAST uses buttons[2]; use eight configured slots for a page that can contain every direction.

Render clears all slots first, then enables the slots needed by the page. Cursor updates inspect enabled button objects, while opening and closing animations process every array entry. Keep the array and each entry valid during rendering or animation. Replacing the array does not by itself render new data or clear the cached m_SelectedButton.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PageView.cancelButton
member.summary: Supplies the visual cancel indicator shown when the cursor is near the center or far outside the menu.

remarks.para: The normal popup supplies x and y as horizontal and vertical cursor offsets from the menu center, in the menu's orientation and measured in scene meters. Cursor updates calculate q = x*x + y*y, the squared distance in square meters (m²). The cancel indicator is shown when q is strictly below the stored 0.005f limit or strictly above the stored 0.65f limit, and hidden otherwise. Those limits also use m². For example, cursor (0, 0) gives q = 0 m² and shows it. Custom callers must supply coordinates matching this menu convention.

Show and Hide are requested with a 0.15-second color fade. Deactivate also hides the indicator. Assign a valid PageElementView with its visual elements configured. This reference supplies the indicator visuals; Trigger operates on m_SelectedButton and does not invoke an action on cancelButton.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PageView.clip_closeDown
member.summary: Supplies the sound asset requested for ShutOff when its first-play flag is false.

remarks.para: This AudioClip is a sound asset requested for ShutOff when its first-play flag is false. The request uses audioPlacementOverride's scene position and the feedback_audio component. Assigning the clip alone does not play it.

PageView passes this sound as clipOverride to Feedback_Audio.AUDIOCLICK. That component still needs a valid nonempty clips_Click array, even when this override is present. If this clip is null, AUDIOCLICK uses its selected array clip instead, so clearing this field does not necessarily silence the cue. Playback can wait for a reusable audio player after the request returns.

clip_closeDownFirstPlay initially suppresses the first ShutOff sound and vibration, then becomes false. Later ShutOff calls can request this clip repeatedly. Deactivate and CoCloseAnimation do not themselves request it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PageView.clip_closeDownFirstPlay
member.summary: Suppresses closing sound and vibration on the next ShutOff call when true.

remarks.para: The constructor sets this flag true. ShutOff changes true to false and skips its feedback, then still calls Deactivate. When the flag is already false, ShutOff requests its closing sound and click vibration and leaves it false.

It is not a record that the closing clip has successfully played. Normal activation does not reset it. For example, setting it true again suppresses one future ShutOff feedback step; leaving it false allows later closing requests each time.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PageView.clip_hover
member.summary: Supplies the sound asset requested for entering a different cursor-selected item.

remarks.para: This AudioClip is a sound asset requested for entering a different cursor-selected item. The request uses audioPlacementOverride's scene position and the feedback_audio component. Assigning the clip alone does not play it.

PageView passes this sound as clipOverride to Feedback_Audio.AUDIOCLICK. That component still needs a valid nonempty clips_Click array, even when this override is present. If this clip is null, AUDIOCLICK uses its selected array clip instead, so clearing this field does not necessarily silence the cue. Playback can wait for a reusable audio player after the request returns.

It is requested when cursor selection changes to another matching item, not on every frame spent over the same item. The same transition also requests a strong click vibration when tactile feedback is available.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PageView.clip_select
member.summary: Supplies the sound asset requested for Trigger accepting a selected button.

remarks.para: This AudioClip is a sound asset requested for Trigger accepting a selected button. The request uses audioPlacementOverride's scene position and the feedback_audio component. Assigning the clip alone does not play it.

PageView passes this sound as clipOverride to Feedback_Audio.AUDIOCLICK. That component still needs a valid nonempty clips_Click array, even when this override is present. If this clip is null, AUDIOCLICK uses its selected array clip instead, so clearing this field does not necessarily silence the cue. Playback can wait for a reusable audio player after the request returns.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PageView.clip_summon
member.summary: Supplies the sound asset requested for the first step of the summon animation.

remarks.para: This AudioClip is a sound asset requested for the first step of the summon animation. The request uses audioPlacementOverride's scene position and the feedback_audio component. Assigning the clip alone does not play it.

PageView passes this sound as clipOverride to Feedback_Audio.AUDIOCLICK. That component still needs a valid nonempty clips_Click array, even when this override is present. If this clip is null, AUDIOCLICK uses its selected array clip instead, so clearing this field does not necessarily silence the cue. Playback can wait for a reusable audio player after the request returns.
The summon routine also requests a subtle controller vibration. The sound is requested when that routine begins, not when the buttons reach full size.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PageView.color1
member.summary: Stores an HDR-capable color value on the page view.

remarks.para: The color contains red, green, blue and alpha values; alpha controls opacity. Values usually range from 0 to 1, and the Inspector permits higher color brightness values for HDR, meaning high dynamic range. For example, (1, 0, 0, 1) is opaque red. These components are unitless.

In the inspected PageView methods and its three animation routines, button rendering, cursor highlights and fades use each PageItemView's own colors. Those paths do not read this PageView color field or apply changes to it. To change a button's visible colors in those paths, configure that button's color settings.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PageView.color2
member.summary: Stores an HDR-capable color value on the page view.

remarks.para: The color contains red, green, blue and alpha values; alpha controls opacity. Values usually range from 0 to 1, and the Inspector permits higher color brightness values for HDR, meaning high dynamic range. For example, (1, 0, 0, 1) is opaque red. These components are unitless.

In the inspected PageView methods and its three animation routines, button rendering, cursor highlights and fades use each PageItemView's own colors. Those paths do not read this PageView color field or apply changes to it. To change a button's visible colors in those paths, configure that button's color settings.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PageView.controller
member.summary: Supplies the controller that receives this view's tactile feedback through .

remarks.para: The surrounding popup menu assigns the controller when it opens this page view. This reference is passed to Feedback_Tactile for subtle opening vibration and strong click vibration during cursor changes, selection and an unsuppressed ShutOff closing-feedback request.

A haptic is a controller vibration. If this controller is missing, Feedback_Tactile tries the currently saved UI controller; if no valid controller with vibration support is available, it produces no vibration. Assigning this field does not select a button or read a trigger by itself.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PageView.feedback_audio
member.summary: Provides the audio component that handles this view's hover, selection, closing and summon sound requests.

remarks.para: Start, the Unity initialization method, and CheckRefs fill a missing reference from the shared UIRig's Feedback_Audio. PlayAudioClip skips its request when this reference is missing; otherwise it calls AUDIOCLICK with the page clip as clipOverride and the page's configured placement object as location.

The Feedback_Audio component's click selection mode, clips_Click array, volume, minimum distance and spatial blend control that request. Volume is a unitless level. Minimum distance is the scene-meter distance before distance fading starts. Spatial blend is unitless: 0 means nonpositional sound, 1 means full positional sound, and intermediate values mix them. These numeric settings are read when a sound is requested. A nonempty clips_Click array is still required for an override, and a null page clip falls back to the selected array clip. Configure the audio component before requesting cues; returning from a request does not prove playback has started.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PageView.feedback_tactile
member.summary: Provides the component that requests controller vibrations for opening, cursor changes, selection and closing feedback.

remarks.para: A haptic is a controller vibration. Start and CheckRefs fill a missing reference from the shared UIRig's Feedback_Tactile. The summon animation asks for subtle vibration; entering a different cursor-selected item, Trigger and an unsuppressed ShutOff ask for a strong click vibration.

These requests pass controller as their recipient. Feedback_Tactile can fall back to the saved UI controller when that reference is missing. A missing tactile component makes the PageView feedback calls skip vibration; changing this reference alone does not start a pulse.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PageView.m_HomePage
member.summary: Stores the page Render uses during the next normal opening of an inactive view.

remarks.para: SetHomePage saves this reference and renders it immediately. Activate renders it again when m_IsActivated is false and a home page exists. GetHomePage returns the same reference.

Render and ChangePage do not replace this stored default. For example, a temporary submenu can be rendered while the home page still refers to the main menu. Assigning this field alone stores the reference without invoking SetHomePage's immediate rendering step.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PageView.m_IsActivated
member.summary: Stores the view's logical activation state that controls its open-versus-selected-action behavior.

remarks.para: The constructor starts this flag true, and Start calls Deactivate to set up the initially hidden view. Normal opening sets it true after rendering the home page; Deactivate sets it false while closing may still be running.

This is separate from whether the GameObject is enabled or an animation has finished. Clear and the close-animation routine can disable the object without changing this flag. Trigger also does not check it. For example, a false flag can coexist with a visible object during closing, and setting the flag alone does not open or close the view.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PageView.m_SelectedButton
member.summary: Caches the button last chosen by cursor matching and consulted by Trigger or an already-active Activate call.

remarks.para: UpdateCursor can replace this reference with an enabled button whose directional segment matches the cursor. For the normal popup, x and y are cursor offsets from the menu center, in the menu's orientation and measured in scene meters. q = x*x + y*y is squared distance in square meters (m²). For finite input, the selection range includes the stored 0.005f and 0.27f limits, both in m². Below or above that range, it clears the reference; Deactivate also clears it during cleanup. For example, cursor (0.6, 0) meters gives q = 0.36 m² and clears selection. Moving from one selected item to another updates highlights and requests hover sound and click vibration.

The cache can remain when an in-range cursor matches no button. Render clears button data without clearing this reference, and Trigger does not check whether it is enabled. For example, a cached button whose PageItem was removed can still cause Trigger to request feedback and return true without running an item action. Setting this reference alone does not update cursor highlights.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PageView.onActivated
member.summary: Runs at the start of every Activate call, passing this view before its object or activation state is updated.

remarks.para: A callback is a function supplied by other code to run when this view signals something. The callback receives this PageView object.

Activate invokes it before enabling the GameObject or checking m_IsActivated. It also runs when an already-active view is about to invoke its selected item or shut off. A handler can therefore see the previous state, and repeated Activate calls can produce repeated notifications.

For example, a handler can prepare page data before a normal opening continues. This callback is not an opening-animation completion signal, and changing the callback reference alone does not activate the view.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PageView.onDeactivated
member.summary: Runs when the close animation finishes, after disabling the view's GameObject, and passes this view.

remarks.para: A callback is a function supplied by other code to run when this view signals something. The callback receives this PageView object.

CoCloseAnimation first clears button data and animates the buttons. At completion it forces their local scales to zero, disables the view object and then invokes this callback. Deactivate may return earlier after clearing its logical activation flag; the callback is not called directly by Deactivate.

Clear and the page-change routine also use the close animation, so this notification can come from those paths. If closing is stopped before completion, the notification need not occur. The callback itself does not prove m_IsActivated is false, because Clear and direct close-animation use do not set that flag.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PanelView.IsActive
member.summary: Reports whether the panel’s stored active flag allows the base panel to handle cursor input.

remarks.para: Activate sets this flag to true; Deactivate sets it to false. While it is false, the base Trigger and cursor-update methods skip their normal input work.

This is the panel’s own flag, rather than a check that it is visible. For example, an inactive parent Unity object can hide the panel while IsActive still returns true. Changing m_isActive directly also changes this result without enabling or disabling the object.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PanelView._module
member.summary: Caches the input component that receives the panel’s pointing ray and pending trigger press.

remarks.para: The input module is the component that turns pointing and pressing into menu input. The module getter fills this cache when it is missing, using Unity’s current EventSystem, its menu-input manager, and the Unity object containing that system’s current input module. A usable cached component is reused by later cursor updates.

Assigning a different usable module here redirects later cursor forwarding to it. Clearing the cache makes the next lookup try to find a module again. For example, clear it after replacing an EventSystem if the old module still exists and you want the panel to find the new one; merely changing the current EventSystem does not refresh this cache.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PanelView.m_IsActiveThisFrame
member.summary: Stores a pending trigger press until an active panel forwards it to the cursor input module.

remarks.para: Despite the name, this true-or-false value does not track a change in activation or automatically expire at the end of a frame. A frame is one round of game updates. The base Trigger method sets it to true when the panel is active.

An active panel’s cursor update passes this value to the input module, the component that turns pointing and pressing into menu input, and then resets it to false. If the panel is inactive or no usable module is found, that forwarding and reset are skipped. Activate and Deactivate leave the value unchanged.

For example, two Trigger calls before one cursor update still produce one pending true value. A cursor update with a usable module forwards true and clears the flag, even if the pointing ray hits no button; clearing the flag is not proof of a successful click.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PanelView.m_isActive
member.summary: Stores the flag that allows the base panel to record trigger presses and forward cursor input.

remarks.para: This true-or-false value is read by IsActive. Activate sets it to true before enabling the panel’s Unity object; Deactivate sets it to false before disabling that object.

Writing this field alone changes the input gate, but does not show or hide the panel’s GameObject, the Unity object containing it. For example, use Activate to both allow input and turn on the panel, instead of only assigning true here. The flag does not describe whether a parent object is hiding the panel.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PanelView.module
member.summary: Gets the cached component that receives this panel’s pointing ray and pending press, looking it up when needed.

remarks.para: An input module turns pointing and pressing into menu input. On the first lookup, or if the cached module has been removed, this getter checks Unity’s current EventSystem, the object that manages menu input. It looks for a VRStandaloneInputModule on the same Unity object as that system’s current input module and stores the result in _module.

If there is no current EventSystem, no current input module, or no matching component, the result can be missing. A later lookup can try again. Once a usable module has been cached, changing the current EventSystem does not make this getter replace it automatically.
For example, set up an EventSystem with the VR input component before sending panel cursor updates. The lookup happens when input needs the module; Activate itself does not fetch it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PanelView.popUpMenu
member.summary: Stores the that this panel asks to close when CloseMenu is called.

remarks.para: Assign the surrounding popup menu here during setup. The base CloseMenu method uses this reference directly; it does not find a menu by walking up the Unity object hierarchy. With no usable menu assigned, CloseMenu has no effect.

For example, link a preferences panel to its popup menu so its Close button can close the surrounding menu. Merely assigning the reference does not open the menu, activate the panel, or select an input module.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PlayerAvatarDecorator._hasSpawned
member.summary: Stores whether this decorator has recorded a spawned player, allowing its level-load avatar override attempt.

remarks.para: The marker’s OnSpawn notification sets this flag true and OnDespawn sets it false. OnEnable can also set it true after finding a player already recorded by _playerMarker, but only performs that lookup when this flag is currently false.
OnLevelLoad requires this flag to be true; SwapAvatar does not read it. Setting it true does not create a player or change the avatar, and it does not prove that an avatar swap has finished.
OnDisable leaves the flag unchanged. Because it is stored state, it can retain an earlier value while this decorator is no longer listening to the marker.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PlayerAvatarDecorator._playerMarker
member.summary: Selects the PlayerMarker whose spawn and despawn notifications update this decorator’s player-readiness flag.

remarks.para: A PlayerMarker is the scene component that records the spawned player’s GameObject and reports spawn/despawn notifications. A GameObject is a scene object holding components. OnEnable registers this decorator with the stored marker and can query whether its player already spawned; OnDisable unregisters it.

Reset, Unity’s editor setup routine, fills this reference by searching this object and its parents, including inactive parents. Awake, Unity’s initialization routine, does not perform that search, so the reference must be prepared before enabling.

Changing the reference while enabled does not move an existing listener registration to the new marker. The later disable routine uses whichever marker is stored then. This reference controls readiness notifications; the avatar request itself uses the current global PlayerRefs avatar manager.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PlayerAvatarDecorator.overrideAvatar
member.summary: Chooses the avatar asset package requested by this decorator when its override is allowed.

remarks.para: An AvatarCrateReference identifies an avatar package through its barcode, an asset identifier. Both OnLevelLoad and SwapAvatar read that identifier from this reference and ask the current player’s avatar manager to load and apply it. They enable caching so the player rig, the system that controls the player’s body, can keep an avatar instance and reuse it for a later request with the same identifier.

Changing the reference selects a different package for the next allowed request. Assignment alone does not swap the avatar. The level-load path also requires _hasSpawned to be true, while the direct helper does not; both are blocked by preventSwap.

Provide a non-null reference and an available avatar package. The manager ignores invalid identifiers before starting the operation, and the request can finish later while assets load and the rig applies the avatar.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PlayerAvatarDecorator.preventSwap
member.summary: Blocks this decorator’s avatar requests while true.

remarks.para: Both OnLevelLoad and SwapAvatar return before reading the avatar reference when this flag is true. False permits their usual checks; the level-load routine still needs _hasSpawned to be true.

Setting the flag does not enable or disable the component, change the marker listener registration, or undo an avatar swap already requested. Clearing it does not automatically retry an earlier skipped level-load attempt; an allowed request must run again.
This guard belongs to this decorator. It does not prevent other code from asking the player’s avatar manager or rig to change avatars.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PlayerHealthDecorator.OnPlayerDeath
member.summary: Actions run when the player reaches final death, before the health component chooses its reload or respawn path.

remarks.para: This is an UltEvent: a configurable list of function calls, such as actions to hide a display or start a scene effect. It receives no arguments. It is connected after this decorator handles a player spawn, and it does not run merely because health reaches zero and the player enters the recoverable dying state.

During automatic death handling, Player_Health.Death first calls the base Health.Death cleanup, which clears deathIsImminent, the flag for the recoverable dying state, and sets alive to false. It then invokes the final-death event and afterward chooses the reload or respawn path. Calling this decorator’s PlayerDeath manually only runs the configured actions; it does not make those health-state changes.

The player's death event is global. Its callback is a routine called to report the player's death and run these configured actions. Disabling this decorator leaves that death callback connected. OnDestroy, Unity's destruction cleanup, removes one matching subscription; duplicates added by repeated spawns can remain. Handling repeated spawns adds repeated subscriptions, so the actions can run more than once. Calling PlayerDeath manually also runs these actions without killing the player.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PlayerHealthDecorator.PlayerMarker
member.summary: The spawn marker this decorator listens to and uses to position the player.

remarks.para: This returns the same reference stored in _playerMarker. On a spawn notification, the decorator copies its health settings to the spawned player and asks the rig manager to teleport the player to this marker's world position and orientation, clearing velocity. A marker is a scene component identifying where the player should spawn; it is not the player's body or health component.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PlayerHealthDecorator._healthMode
member.summary: Selects the spawned player's rules for surviving depleted health.

remarks.para: Invincible prevents the normal death countdown when health reaches zero. Mortal starts the recoverable countdown whose starting duration, in seconds of scaled game time, comes from deathTime. InsantDeath, spelled that way in the enum, uses Player_Health.instaDeathTimeAmount, a separate starting countdown duration in seconds of scaled game time, and does not allow the puppet-death recovery described by deathTime. Its name does not mean this decorator's deathTime controls that countdown.

OnSpawn copies this value into the player's health component. Changing the decorator afterward does not continually update the current player; apply changes to the player's healthMode for an existing player, or set this value before the next spawn.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PlayerHealthDecorator._playerMarker
member.summary: Assigns the marker whose spawn notifications configure this player's health and starting pose.

remarks.para: Assign it before enabling the decorator. OnEnable subscribes to this marker and OnDisable unsubscribes from it. Reset can fill the reference from a marker on this object or a parent. PlayerMarker returns the same reference.

During OnSpawn, the marker's world position and orientation become the requested player teleport destination, with velocity cleared. Moving the marker does not continuously move a player that has already spawned.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PlayerHealthDecorator._reloadLevelOnDeath
member.summary: Chooses whether the spawned player's final death reloads the level or returns the player to a checkpoint.

remarks.para: When true, Player_Health waits one second of game time after its death event and requests a level reload. When false, it teleports to the rig manager's saved checkpoint and then respawns the player after its recovery wait. This does not make the player unable to die; it chooses what happens after death.

The value is copied during OnSpawn. Changing it on this decorator after spawning does not update the current player's reloadLevelOnDeath setting. deathTime controls the earlier dying window, not the delay before the reload.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PlayerHealthDecorator.deathTime
member.summary: Sets the starting duration, in seconds of game time, of a Mortal player's recoverable dying window after health reaches zero.

remarks.para: OnSpawn copies this into Player_Health.deathTimeAmount. The dying effect progresses toward final death using Unity's deltaTime, which is elapsed game time between frames. For example, a value of 5 starts an approximately five-second window if there are no further hits or recovery events; slowed game time can make it last longer in real time.

The audited recovery path listens for PuppetMaster.OnDeathStatsEvent: a notification that a character controlled by the physics animation system has died. While death is imminent and the mode is not InsantDeath, that notification cancels the dying routine and restores half of maximum health. Simply dealing any amount of damage is not the trigger in this path, despite the Inspector tooltip's wording. The listener does not check which character sent the notification or who killed it.

Further damage while dying can reduce the duration value used by the fade and make it progress faster. This is therefore a starting duration, not a guaranteed safe period. InsantDeath uses a different timer. Changing this decorator after spawning does not change the current player's timer setting, and changing the setting during an existing countdown does not restart that countdown.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PlayerRefs.HasRefs
member.summary: True after this component has copied the player rig references during persistent-scene initialization, before its completion callbacks and object activation.

remarks.para: The persistent scene holds shared objects across gameplay levels. A callback is a method called when player-reference setup finishes.

Initialization finds a player entity using the configured player tag, copies its rig manager, searches for an ammo receiver, and copies the physics rig and controller rig references. A rig is a group of objects that represents or controls the player's body. The controller reference is kept only if it is an OpenControllerRig or a type based on OpenControllerRig.

HasRefs is set to true before OnRefsComplete is invoked and before _enableWhenReadyObjects are set active. It does not prove that every reference is non-null: the ammo receiver, physics rig, and OpenControllerRig may be missing, and the separately assigned body-vitals and avatar-manager references are not checked by this initialization.

Check both HasRefs and the particular reference you need. For example, wait for initialization, then check PlayerPhysicsRig before accessing the simulated player body. If no matching player entity is found, this initialization attempt returns without setting the flag. Reading HasRefs does not perform another search.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PlayerRefs.Instance
member.summary: The globally stored component, assigned when that component initializes and used to reach its cached player references.

remarks.para: A rig is the group of objects that represents or controls the player's body.

Awake, Unity's early component initialization method, assigns this component to Instance before requesting player-reference initialization from the persistent-scene load system. The persistent scene contains shared objects that can remain present while gameplay levels change. Instance can therefore exist while HasRefs is still false, and it can be null before a PlayerRefs component has initialized.

The getter returns the stored component; it does not create one, locate a player, or verify its cached references. Each PlayerRefs that runs Awake replaces the stored Instance. This Awake implementation does not reject duplicate components or make this object persistent itself.

For example, obtain Instance, check that it exists, then check HasRefs and the particular rig reference you want to use. Use OnRefsComplete for work that must wait for initialization. If HasRefs is already true, run that setup directly; adding a callback now does not replay it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PlayerRefs.OnRefsComplete
member.summary: The callbacks invoked after the player references are cached and HasRefs is set, before the configured waiting objects are activated.

remarks.para: A callback is a method called in response to something happening. This Action takes no arguments and may hold a single callback or a combined list. Add a callback with += to preserve callbacks already assigned; replacing this field with a new Action replaces that list.

The order is: copy the rig references, set HasRefs to true, invoke the currently assigned callbacks if any, then set _enableWhenReadyObjects active in array order. Callbacks can see HasRefs as true, but must still check the particular reference they use because not every cached or scene-assigned reference is validated.

Adding a callback after initialization does not invoke it automatically. For example, if HasRefs is already true, run your setup work directly; otherwise add a callback to do it after the references are copied. The initializer does not use HasRefs to prevent another invocation if initialization is called again.

Callbacks finish before the waiting-object array is read. A callback can replace that array for the subsequent activation. If a callback throws an error, activation does not continue normally; HasRefs was already set to true.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PlayerRefs.OpenControllerRig
member.summary: The cached that BodyVitals uses to apply player calibration and control settings.

remarks.para: The persistent scene holds shared objects across gameplay levels. Calibration adjusts the virtual body to the player's real body measurements.

An OpenControllerRig organizes tracked headset and controller information for the player. During persistent-scene initialization, PlayerRefs takes the discovered rig manager's controllerRig only if it is an OpenControllerRig or a type based on it; a missing controller or an unrelated controller-rig type produces null even when HasRefs becomes true.

The getter returns that cached reference rather than re-reading the rig manager's current controllerRig. BodyVitals uses it to apply body calibration, turning choices, handedness, quick-menu settings, and controller vibration settings. Reading this property alone applies none of those settings.
For example, check the reference before applying a saved body-calibration setup. A later replacement of the rig manager's controller does not automatically update this cached property.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PlayerRefs.PlayerBodyVitals
member.summary: The scene-assigned player body-measurement and comfort-settings component, used when calibrating and configuring the VR rig.

remarks.para: A rig is the group of objects that represents or controls the player's body. Calibration adjusts the virtual body to the player's real body measurements. An avatar is the player's in-game body.

The getter returns the component assigned to _bodyVitals. BodyVitals stores body measurements and choices such as turning, handedness, quick-menu availability, and vibration strength. Its calibration and propagation methods apply those values to the controller rig and other player systems; merely reading this reference does not apply them.

This is a configured component reference, not a new lookup of the current avatar. PlayerRefs' persistent-load initializer neither assigns nor validates _bodyVitals, so HasRefs can be true while this property is null.
For example, obtain this component to call CalibratePlayerBodyScale after the needed controller and avatar references are ready. Check the component itself as well as player-reference readiness.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PlayerRefs.PlayerInvAmmoReceiver
member.summary: The cached ammo-receiver component found on the tagged player and its children, which handles taking magazines from inventory.

remarks.para: The persistent scene holds shared objects across gameplay levels. The configured player tag is a label used to find the player. Children, or objects in the player hierarchy, are scene objects nested under the player object.

Persistent-scene initialization performs a child-component search for InventoryAmmoReceiver and stores its result. This component handles an empty hand grabbing a magazine, using the selected magazine and cartridge type and the available ammunition. Those actions occur in its grab methods; reading this property does not give the player ammunition.

The search can return null and initialization can still set HasRefs to true. The getter returns the saved search result, not a fresh search. Check this reference before using it; a later change to the player hierarchy does not update it automatically.
For example, use this reference when connecting custom inventory interaction to the existing player ammo receiver, after checking that it was found.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PlayerRefs.PlayerPhysicsRig
member.summary: The cached for the discovered player, giving access to the simulated body used for physical interactions.

remarks.para: A physics rig contains the player's simulated body parts, including the hands and torso. Initialization copies PlayerRigManager.physicsRig after finding the player by the configured tag. Other systems use this cached rig to reach the player's physical entity and body parts, such as when setting up player link interactions.

The getter returns the copied reference rather than reading the manager again. That reference may be null even when HasRefs is true. If the manager later receives a different physics rig, this cached value does not change automatically.
For example, check PlayerPhysicsRig before accessing its leftHand or rightHand for a physical interaction. Obtaining the reference does not itself move or change the player's body.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PlayerRefs.PlayerRigManager
member.summary: The cached manager of the tagged player's rigs, used to reach the player's controller, physics body, inventory, and avatar systems.

remarks.para: An avatar is the player's in-game body; an avatar-change request asks the manager to replace that body.

A rig is a group of objects that represents or controls the player's body. Initialization finds a player entity by the configured tag, obtains its Rig component, and copies that component's manager reference. The other cached rig references are then copied from this manager.

PlayerAvatarManager uses this cached manager when requesting an avatar override. For example, a valid avatar identifier can start an avatar-change request through the manager. Reading PlayerRigManager itself only returns the reference and does not request a swap.

This is the reference copied during initialization, not a new player search on every read. Check readiness and that the reference exists before use. Changing a manager or its child rigs later does not automatically refresh the other references cached by PlayerRefs.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PlayerRefs._HasRefs_k__BackingField
member.summary: Stores the readiness flag returned by HasRefs; changing it alone does not resolve player references or invoke callbacks.

remarks.para: A callback is a method called when player-reference setup finishes.

A backing field is the storage behind a property. Player-reference initialization sets this flag to true after copying the rig references, before invoking OnRefsComplete and activating _enableWhenReadyObjects.

The flag is not a check that every reference exists. The ammo receiver, physics rig, controller rig, body-vitals component, or avatar manager can still be null. Setting this storage to true does not find or assign any of them; setting it to false does not clear them.
For example, read HasRefs and check the component you need instead of changing this field to bypass waiting.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PlayerRefs._Instance_k__BackingField
member.summary: Stores the global component returned by Instance, without initializing that component's player references.

remarks.para: The persistent scene holds shared objects across gameplay levels. A rig is the group of objects that represents or controls the player's body.

A backing field is the storage behind a property. Awake, Unity's early component initialization method, puts the initializing PlayerRefs into this static storage before it registers for persistent-scene loading. Static means all callers share one stored value.

Changing this field changes what Instance returns, but does not locate the player, set HasRefs, or invoke OnRefsComplete. The stored component may exist before its references are ready, and each component that runs Awake replaces it.
For example, use Instance as the entry point and then check its readiness. This storage does not itself prove that a component belongs to the persistent player rig or has finished initialization.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PlayerRefs._OpenControllerRig_k__BackingField
member.summary: Stores the cached returned by OpenControllerRig, rather than continually following the rig manager's controller reference.

remarks.para: The persistent scene holds shared objects across gameplay levels. Calibration adjusts the virtual body to the player's real body measurements.

A backing field is the storage behind a property. Persistent-scene initialization copies the discovered manager's controllerRig here only if it is an OpenControllerRig or a type based on it, the VR rig that handles tracked headset and controller information. A missing or unrelated controller type stores null.

BodyVitals reads this cached controller when applying calibration and control settings. HasRefs may be true with this field null. Changing this storage changes the getter's result but does not apply calibration, refresh other cached rigs, or invoke completion callbacks.
For example, check OpenControllerRig before applying body settings; a later controller replacement in the manager is not automatically reflected here.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PlayerRefs._PlayerInvAmmoReceiver_k__BackingField
member.summary: Stores the child-search result returned by PlayerInvAmmoReceiver, for the player component that handles inventory magazine grabs.

remarks.para: The configured player tag is a label used to find the player. Children, or objects in the player hierarchy, are scene objects nested under the player object.

A backing field is the storage behind a property. Initialization searches the tagged player and its children for InventoryAmmoReceiver and stores the result here. The component's grab logic selects ammunition and starts obtaining a magazine for an empty hand.

The search result can be null even with HasRefs true. Changing this storage changes the property's returned reference; it does not search the scene, add ammunition, give the player a magazine, or invoke completion callbacks. Moving or replacing an ammo receiver later does not refresh this storage automatically.
For example, check PlayerInvAmmoReceiver before wiring a custom inventory interaction to it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PlayerRefs._PlayerPhysicsRig_k__BackingField
member.summary: Stores the copied reference returned by PlayerPhysicsRig, for reaching the player's simulated body.

remarks.para: A backing field is the storage behind a property. Initialization copies the discovered rig manager's physicsRig here. That rig groups the simulated player body parts used for physical interaction, including hands and torso.

The copy may be null even when HasRefs is true. Changing this storage changes the property's result without rebuilding the player body, updating the manager's physicsRig, refreshing other cached references, or invoking callbacks.
For example, check PlayerPhysicsRig before using its hand references. A later change to the manager's physics rig does not automatically change this cached value.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PlayerRefs._PlayerRigManager_k__BackingField
member.summary: Stores the discovered , which PlayerRigManager returns and initialization uses to copy the controller and physics rigs.

remarks.para: A rig is the group of objects that represents or controls the player's body. An avatar is the player's in-game body.

A backing field is the storage behind a property. Initialization finds a player entity using the configured player tag, obtains its Rig component, then copies that rig's manager here. The manager coordinates the player's body, controller, inventory, and avatar systems.

Changing this storage changes PlayerRigManager's result but does not refresh PlayerPhysicsRig or OpenControllerRig, locate an ammo receiver, set readiness, or invoke callbacks. For example, replacing just this manager can leave the other cached references pointing to an earlier player setup.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PlayerRefs._avatarManager
member.summary: The scene-assigned returned by , whose methods can request a player avatar override.

remarks.para: An avatar is the player's in-game body; an avatar-change request asks the manager to replace that body.

PlayerAvatarManager.OverrideAvatar checks the supplied avatar identifier and, when valid, asks the cached PlayerRigManager to change the avatar. That change is a request whose eventual success is not established by reading this field.

PlayerRefs returns this assigned component directly; its persistent-load initializer does not find, replace, or validate it. Assign it in the scene before code needs it, and check it separately from HasRefs. Changing this field alone does not change the player's avatar.
For example, connect the existing scene PlayerAvatarManager to this field so other systems can reach it through playerAvatarManager.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PlayerRefs._bodyVitals
member.summary: The scene-assigned returned by , for calibrating and configuring the player's VR rig.

remarks.para: A rig is the group of objects that represents or controls the player's body. Calibration adjusts the virtual body to the player's real body measurements.

BodyVitals contains the player's body measurements and control choices, including turning, handedness, quick-menu access, and controller vibration strength. Its calibration and propagation methods apply those choices; storing the reference here does not apply them.

PlayerRefs' persistent-load initializer does not discover or validate this component. Assign it in the scene before use. It can be null even with HasRefs true, and it does not automatically follow the current avatar.
For example, provide the configured BodyVitals component here so PlayerBodyVitals can return it when player-calibration code runs.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PlayerRefs._enableWhenReadyObjects
member.summary: The ordered list of scene objects set active after player-reference initialization and completion callbacks.

remarks.para: A completion callback is a method called after the player references have been copied.

After caching the rig references, the initializer first sets HasRefs to true and invokes OnRefsComplete. It then reads this array and calls SetActive(true) on each GameObject in array order. A GameObject is a scene object with attached components. This sets each object's active setting; visible behavior depends on its scene setup.

Assign the array and all its entries before this activation step. An assigned empty array is allowed. A null array or null entry causes an error after HasRefs was already set and callbacks were already invoked; earlier entries may already have been activated.

Awake, Unity's early component initialization method, does not deactivate these objects. For example, configure a UI panel inactive in the scene and put it in this list to activate it after references are copied. A callback may replace this array before the initializer reads it. Changing this field after initialization does not run another activation pass by itself.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PlayerRefs.playerAvatarManager
member.summary: The scene-assigned component that can request a player avatar override through the cached rig manager.

remarks.para: An avatar is the player's in-game body; an avatar-change request asks the manager to replace that body.

The getter returns _avatarManager directly. PlayerAvatarManager.OverrideAvatar checks an avatar identifier and, if valid, asks PlayerRigManager to change the avatar. Reading this property does not load or swap an avatar, and a change request does not guarantee a completed swap.

PlayerRefs' persistent-load initializer does not assign or validate this component. Check that it exists separately from HasRefs; setup must supply it before code uses it. For example, reach the scene's avatar manager through this property when making a configured avatar override request.
Yes, the lowercase name shipped with the game.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PreferencesPanelView.defaultPage
member.summary: Selects the page object to activate when Unity enables this preferences panel.

remarks.para: This is a zero-based index into pages, the ordered array of page objects: 0 means the first page and 1 means the second. OnEnable is Unity's call when this component becomes enabled on an active scene object. That call first turns all page objects off, then activates the entry named by this index.

Set -1 to leave all pages off when the panel opens. Other negative values and values greater than the number of entries also leave every page off. Use 0 through pages.Length - 1 to show a page, where pages.Length is the entry count. A value exactly equal to the entry count triggers an array bounds failure after hiding the pages.

Changing this stored index does not immediately switch the currently shown page. It is read on the next enable call; PAGESELECT uses its own argument instead. For example, with defaultPage = 2 and three page objects, reopening the panel selects the third page, while PAGESELECT(-1) hides all three.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PreferencesPanelView.pages
member.summary: Holds the ordered page objects that this preferences panel turns off and selects between.

remarks.para: Each GameObject is a Unity scene object holding a settings page and its components. Its position in this array gives its page index: the first entry is 0, the second is 1, and the third is 2. Supply an array with every entry assigned before the panel's setup, enable, disable, or page-selection calls run.

ALLOFF turns off every listed object. PAGESELECT first does the same, then turns on the entry at its supplied valid index. The panel's enable call instead chooses defaultPage. These operations change the listed objects' active state; a page under an inactive parent still cannot appear.

Replacing this array changes the targets of later calls without immediately switching pages. Objects removed from the list are no longer touched by those calls. A missing array or entry causes the operation to fail; an empty array can be cleared, but has no valid index to select.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PullCordDevice.DepthFader
member.summary: Numeric lookup key for the hologram material’s depth-fade drawing setting.

remarks.para: The key identifies a setting for the shader, the drawing program; it is not the current depth-fade amount. Class initialization converts the setting’s name to this key once. Awake, Unity’s initialization callback, reads the actual material value separately and saves it. The pull hologram animation blends that saved value toward five times itself, then restores it. The added-avatar ending effect blends between five times the saved value and the saved value before writing the five-times endpoint on completion. The drawing program determines the visible meaning and units of its depth-fade amount.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PullCordDevice.EmissionColor
member.summary: Numeric lookup key for the hologram material’s emission tint.

remarks.para: The key identifies a color setting for the shader, its drawing program; it is not the tint itself. Class initialization creates the key once from the setting’s name. Awake, Unity’s initialization callback, reads and saves the actual material tint separately. The pull animation blends toward the saved tint with alpha 0.5, then restores the saved tint. The added-avatar ending effect blends between that tint with alpha 0 and the ordinary saved tint, then writes the alpha-0 endpoint on completion. Alpha is the color’s opacity component, conventionally 0 for transparent and 1 for opaque; the drawing program determines the appearance.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PullCordDevice.ScanlineSize

remarks.para: The key selects a named setting for the shader, the drawing program; it is not a scanline size. Class initialization creates it once from the setting’s name. Awake, Unity’s initialization callback, reads and saves the actual material value separately. The pull hologram animation blends that baseline toward three times itself, then restores it. The added-avatar ending effect blends between three times the saved value and the baseline before writing the three-times endpoint on completion. The drawing program determines how its size number changes the visible lines and what units it uses.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PullCordDevice.addAnimation
member.summary: Saved add-avatar hologram sequence that prevents AddAvatarToPCD from starting a second one while it is non-null.

remarks.para: A coroutine is an animation sequence spread across several frames. AddAvatarToPCD saves and starts it here only when this field is null. Normal completion destroys the temporary preview object and clears the field. A saved sequence is not proof that a new favorite slot was written, or that an interrupted sequence is still running.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PullCordDevice.addAvatar
member.summary: Clip bank for the completion cue after the new-avatar hologram reaches the Body Log.

remarks.para: The add-avatar animation plays this bank after its configured 3-second travel phase and 0.5-second wait, just before its 0.4-second scale-and-shader ending phase and the mini-blast particles. The audio player randomly selects a clip; an empty bank plays nothing. This visual sequence does not itself add a favorite barcode to avatarCrateRefs.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PullCordDevice.addAvatarCurve
member.summary: Controls how the acquired-avatar hologram travels, turns, and changes size between its pickup presentation and the Body Log preview.

remarks.para: The horizontal axis is elapsed time divided by the configured 3-second travel phase, limited to 0 through 1. The vertical output is a blend amount: 0 chooses the Body Log preview position, rotation, size and mesh-centering offset; 1 chooses the captured pickup presentation. Intermediate values use Unity’s curved vector and rotation blending.

A curve descending from output 1 at input 0 to output 0 at input 1 moves from the pickup presentation toward the dial. A flat output of 1 holds the pickup endpoint during the travel phase; the code then places the temporary hologram at the Body Log when that phase ends. Both axes are unitless.

The outer hologram’s position uses world coordinates in meters, and its rotation turns it relative to the world axes. Mesh-centering offsets are positions in meters relative to their parent; size is unitless scale relative to that parent. Curved vector blending bends between the two position or offset vectors as the blend amount changes, while rotation blending gradually turns between the two orientations. It does not promise a straight-line path.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PullCordDevice.addAvatarFlickerCurve
member.summary: Controls scanline, depth-fade, and tint blending during the added hologram’s ending effect.

remarks.para: The horizontal axis is elapsed time divided by the configured 0.4-second ending phase, limited to 0 through 1. The vertical value is a unitless blend amount, also limited to 0 through 1.

Output 0 uses three times the saved scanline size, five times the saved depth-fade value, and the saved hologram tint with alpha 0. Output 1 uses the ordinary saved scanline size, depth-fade value and tint. For example, output 0.5 selects the midpoint of each pair. On completion, the animation writes the output-0 endpoint and destroys its temporary object.

A shader is the drawing program that gives the hologram its appearance; a material stores the settings given to that program. Awake, Unity’s initialization callback, reads and saves the assigned material’s scanline-size, depth-fade and tint values once. The animations blend from these saved values rather than recapturing the material each frame. Tint alpha is its opacity component, conventionally 0 for transparent and 1 for opaque; the drawing program determines the visible result.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PullCordDevice.addAvatarOffCurve
member.summary: Adds a curve-shaped change to the new hologram’s local scale during its ending effect.

remarks.para: The horizontal axis is elapsed time divided by the configured 0.4-second ending phase, limited to 0 through 1. The output is a unitless amount multiplied by hologramAnimDisplacement, the three configured additions to local X, Y and Z scale, and added to the fitted preview scale.

For example, with a fitted scale of (0.1, 0.1, 0.1), hologramAnimDisplacement = (-0.1, -0.1, -0.1), and curve output 1, the requested local scale is (0, 0, 0). Curve output is not clamped by this scale calculation. This changes size, not position; completion destroys the temporary hologram.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PullCordDevice.addAvatarVolume
member.summary: Requested volume of the completion cue in the add-avatar hologram animation.

remarks.para: This is a unitless volume request, normally 0 for silence through 1 for full requested volume, not decibels. It is read when the addAvatar bank plays after the travel phase and wait. member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PullCordDevice.anchorCoroutine
member.summary: Saved anchor-adjustment sequence that the grab callback starts only when this field is null.

remarks.para: A coroutine is a sequence spread across several frames. A normal grab stores and starts LerpAnchor with a configured 0.4-second duration; normal completion clears this field. The release callback stops a non-null sequence but does not clear the field itself. A non-null value therefore does not reliably prove that anchor adjustment is still running.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PullCordDevice.anchorLerp
member.summary: Tells the held-pull update to leave live joint drives to the anchor-adjustment sequence.

remarks.para: LerpAnchor sets this true when it begins and false when it completes normally. While true, OnBallGripUpdate still calculates and smooths jointDriver but skips applying it to the joint; the anchor sequence ramps the drive itself. Stopping the sequence in the release callback does not reset this flag there.

A joint is a physics connection; its drive supplies the spring-like force resisting or pulling the ball. jointDriver contains calculated, smoothed settings. While this flag is true, those calculated settings are not directly assigned by the held update. Instead the anchor sequence applies its gradually increasing blend from zero toward the strength-scaled settings. A drive supplies a spring-like pulling force. Its three settings are spring strength in newtons per meter of position error, damping in newton-seconds per meter of velocity error, and maximum force in newtons. These settings are applied to each of the joint’s X, Y and Z movement axes. The avatar’s upper-body strength multiplier is unitless and multiplies all three settings.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PullCordDevice.apv
member.summary: Body Mall avatar panel that is notified when the ball is docked or pulled out of its receiver. Panel type: .

remarks.para: When the handle is in the receiver and the ball is released, the device calls the panel’s BodyLogSet method after locking the ball to the world. Grabbing a docked ball clears isBallInReceiver before calling DisconnectBodyLog(true). This reference links the physical device to those panel actions.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PullCordDevice.armLength
member.summary: Calculated hand-distance threshold in meters for revealing the ball when lookMode is false.

remarks.para: Each enabled Update in hand-distance mode overwrites this with (upperArmLength + lowerArmLength + max(palmSizeX, palmSizeY)) × handShowDist. upperArmLength and lowerArmLength are the current avatar’s cached upper and lower arm measurements in meters. palmSizeX and palmSizeY are its two cached palm-size dimensions, also in meters; max chooses the larger one. handShowDist is a unitless fraction. For example, measurements 0.30, 0.25 and a larger palm dimension of 0.10 meters with handShowDist = 0.2 give 0.13 meters.

The hand must be strictly closer than this distance to ballStartTrans to reveal a hidden ball. This is a display threshold, not the full pull range or the avatar’s anatomical arm length. It is also checked when a ball-return sequence decides whether to hide the ball. Editing it can be overwritten on the next applicable Update.

The avatar’s setup precomputation measures its skeleton and saves proportions and palm dimensions. RefreshBodyMeasurements converts the arm proportions into cached lengths in meters using the avatar’s eye height. The upper arm runs from the right upper-arm bone to the right lower-arm bone; the lower arm runs from there to the optional wrist point, or to the hand bone when no wrist point is configured. Palm dimensions come from the finger positions. The device reads these saved measurements; moving the hand does not recalculate them.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PullCordDevice.armLengthMultiplier
member.summary: Scales the cord extension needed to reach the last avatar slot while pulling.

remarks.para: The full selection distance is (2 × sidewaysShoulderOffset + upperArmLength + armSum) × armLengthMultiplier, in meters. sidewaysShoulderOffset is the signed sideways offset from the chest to the right upper-arm bone along the avatar’s rightward axis, measured during setup; it is not the straight-line distance between those points. upperArmLength is the right shoulder-to-elbow measurement. armSum is upperArmLength + lowerArmLength + 0.5 × wristToHandLength. lowerArmLength is elbow-to-wrist when an optional wrist point is configured, otherwise elbow-to-hand. wristToHandLength is that optional wrist-to-hand distance, or 0 without the wrist point. All these measurements are cached meters, and armLengthMultiplier is unitless.

OnBallGripUpdate maps the measured world distance from fxLineGroup to the ball across all avatar slots using that distance. Doubling a positive multiplier doubles the pull distance for the same slot boundary. It also increases the distance between the visible cord tick markers. This is separate from the armLength hand-show threshold, which uses handShowDist.

RefreshBodyMeasurements converts the arm proportions into cached lengths in meters using the avatar’s eye height. The upper arm runs from the right upper-arm bone to the right lower-arm bone; the lower arm runs from there to the optional wrist point, or to the hand bone when no wrist point is configured. Palm dimensions come from the finger positions. The device reads these saved measurements; moving the hand does not recalculate them.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PullCordDevice.avatarAddLocation
member.summary: Captured world-space endpoint for the pickup side of the added-avatar hologram animation.

remarks.para: The animation initially records addPosition’s world position in meters, then offsets this saved endpoint 0.25 meters opposite the temporary preview’s horizontal forward direction, which faces the camera. It does not keep following addPosition as that transform moves.

addAvatarCurve blends between the Body Log preview endpoint at output 0 and this endpoint at output 1. This is a saved animation target, not necessarily the temporary preview object’s current position.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PullCordDevice.avatarAddPreviewMeshCrate
