member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PullCordDevice.avatarBlaster
member.summary: Spawnable effect requested around the active avatar’s skinned meshes after an avatar change. Effect description type: .

remarks.para: Awake, Unity’s initialization callback, registers this spawnable with the asset spawner. When an object finishes spawning, its ParticleTint component, if present, receives the renderer and a bounding-box surface-area multiplier for its particle burst.

A renderer is the component that draws a mesh, its surface shape. A skinned mesh bends with the avatar’s bones. ParticleTint uses the captured renderer’s mesh as the particle emission shape, and the captured surface-area multiplier changes how many particles its burst requests, rather than scaling the spawned object itself.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PullCordDevice.avatarCrateRefs

LoadFavoriteAvatars can replace these entries from the save or default favorites. After changing choices, refresh the preview-crate cache before expecting the corresponding holograms. The ordinary device is constructed with six slots, and its glyph animation and tick layout contain fixed six-part logic; resizing this array alone does not reconfigure the whole dial.
A barcode is a crate’s unique identifier. The release compares those identifiers to avoid requesting the avatar already in use.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PullCordDevice.avatarIndex

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PullCordDevice.avatarTransformationSequence
member.summary: Saved scripted transformation sequence that blocks further ForceAvatarChange calls while it is non-null.

remarks.para: A coroutine is a sequence spread across several frames. ForceAvatarChange creates, saves and starts it here. Non-null means the guard is set, not proof of the player’s current avatar.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PullCordDevice.ballArt

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PullCordDevice.ballGripCollider

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PullCordDevice.ballGripCollider2

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PullCordDevice.ballHeld
member.summary: Saved attachment flag that prevents ordinary Update hiding while the ball is held.

remarks.para: The grab callback, a routine called when a hand attaches, sets this true after any undocking work. The release callback clears it only after its docking or avatar-request branch and visual cleanup. Update reads this flag to preserve a held ball during its ordinary hide checks. It records those callbacks rather than counting the currently attached hands every time it is read. Assigning it alone does not grab or release the grip.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PullCordDevice.ballHost
member.summary: Interaction host that supplies the ball’s physics body and its attached hands.

remarks.para: The device obtains ballRb from this host, freezes the host when hiding the ball, and restores its saved local pose through the host’s transform. HapticEvent asks the host for every attached hand and sends each controller a vibration. A host is the game component that groups those object interactions; its reference alone does not show or hide the ball.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PullCordDevice.ballJoint
member.summary: Physics connection between the ball and the device’s body slot, providing the cord’s movement limit and pulling force. Joint type: .

remarks.para: A joint connects objects in the physics simulation. Awake, Unity’s initialization callback, saves the initial joint configuration and connects it to the parent slot’s body Rigidbody. EnableBall later creates a replacement joint from that saved configuration; DisableBall destroys the current one.

Held updates change its drives to create pull resistance, and RetractBall shrinks its linear movement limit to draw the ball home. worldJoint is a separate extra connection for docking to a receiver. Editing ballJoint’s live settings does not automatically update the saved configuration applied to future replacements.

A Rigidbody is the component that gives a physics object its mass and motion. The joint connects the ball to that component on the body slot. A drive supplies a spring-like pulling force. Its three settings are spring strength in newtons per meter of position error, damping in newton-seconds per meter of velocity error, and maximum force in newtons. These settings are applied to each of the joint’s X, Y and Z movement axes. The avatar’s upper-body strength multiplier is unitless and multiplies all three settings.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PullCordDevice.ballLine

Moving this object can therefore move the drawn cord’s starting point.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PullCordDevice.ballMass

The complete inspected PullCordDevice methods and its animation bodies do not read this cache after startup or change Rigidbody mass during pulls. To change the ball’s physical mass, change its Rigidbody mass rather than relying on this cache. This finding does not cover external game code or mods.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PullCordDevice.ballRb

The complete inspected device and animation methods do not temporarily change its mass during pulls.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PullCordDevice.ballRetraction

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PullCordDevice.ballShown

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PullCordForceChange.avatarCrate

With randomize false, an active pull cord receives this reference for its animated change sequence. A pull cord whose own scene object is inactive uses this component's direct asynchronous SwapAvatar path instead.

With randomize true, the component chooses from its six defaultFavoriteAvatarsBarcodes entries. In the inactive-cord branch it stores the chosen reference here before requesting the swap. In the active-cord branch it sends the chosen reference directly to the cord and leaves this field unchanged.

For example, assign a Heavy avatar reference and leave randomize false to request Heavy when an eligible trigger entry occurs. Assigning this field alone does not change the player's current body; the trigger starts a request and loading can finish later.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PullCordForceChange.choice
member.summary: Stores the list index most recently sampled by this component's random avatar selection.

remarks.para: The random path overwrites this with an integer from 0 through 5, where 0 is the first entry in defaultFavoriteAvatarsBarcodes and 5 is the sixth. The number has no physical unit. If that entry's barcode matches the player rig's recorded AvatarCrate barcode, the code keeps sampling until it gets a different identifier.

An active pull cord also receives choice as the index that offsets its transformation glyph animation. In the inactive-cord path it only selects the reference for the direct swap. For example, choice equal to 2 selects the third reference in the list.
This is selection state, not a completion result. Fixed-avatar requests do not update it, and setting it before an entry does not force the next random pick because random selection overwrites it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PullCordForceChange.defaultFavoriteAvatarsBarcodes
member.summary: Holds the avatar crate references sampled by random forced changes.

remarks.para: This list stores AvatarCrateReference objects, each carrying an avatar's barcode, its unique asset identifier. The constructor fills six entries in this order, identified by the last part of their barcodes: Strong, Fast, Heavy, CharFurv4GB, Anime and CharTallv4. The component builds this list itself; the inspected trigger code does not replace it with the player's saved favorites.

When randomize is true, selection samples only indices 0 through 5, where index 0 means the first list entry. Additional entries are outside the sampled range. Keep the first six references valid: a shortened list can cause an out-of-range error and a missing reference can cause an error.

The code rejects any sample whose barcode matches the rig's recorded current AvatarCrate barcode, then samples again. At least one of the six candidates must have a different identifier, or the repeat-selection loop cannot finish. For example, replacing the third entry changes the candidate picked when choice is 2.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PullCordForceChange.onlyTriggerOnce
member.summary: Marks this trigger as used after it sends its first eligible avatar-change request.

remarks.para: This setting defaults to true. After requesting a direct swap or calling the active cord's ForceAvatarChange, the trigger sets used to true when onlyTriggerOnce is true. Later ForceChange calls return immediately while used remains true.

The flag is recorded after the request call, without waiting for a successful avatar change. An active cord can ignore the request because its transformation sequence is already running, and an asynchronous swap can later fail; the trigger can still be consumed.

Set onlyTriggerOnce to false before the first request for a reusable trigger. Changing it to false after used has become true does not reopen the trigger, because the used check happens first. For example, a one-use transformation zone can remain consumed even if its requested avatar fails to load.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PullCordForceChange.optionalPullCordStopIndex
member.summary: Offsets the active pull cord's six-glyph transformation animation for a fixed-avatar request.

remarks.para: With randomize false and an active pull-cord object, this integer is passed to the transformation sequence. It has no physical unit. The sequence accepts 0 through 5; it treats any other value, including the default -1, as 0 in its own working copy. The first glyph it shows is the next entry, wrapping around the six glyphs.

For example, value 2 starts the animated cycle at glyph index 3, the fourth glyph; value 5 starts at glyph index 0, the first glyph. The requested avatar comes from avatarCrate. The glyph index affects the animation, not which asset reference is sent.
Random selection passes choice in place of this setting. If the pull-cord object is inactive, the component requests a direct asynchronous avatar swap and does not use this animation index.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PullCordForceChange.randomize
member.summary: Requests a random choice from this component's six avatar candidates instead of the configured .

remarks.para: When true, ForceChange samples integer indices 0 through 5 from defaultFavoriteAvatarsBarcodes, where 0 selects the first entry. It stores the sample in choice. If the selected barcode, an asset's unique identifier, matches the rig's recorded AvatarCrate barcode, it samples again until it finds a different identifier. The comparison uses that stored crate reference.

For an active pull cord, it sends the chosen reference and choice as the animation index. For an inactive pull-cord object, it first stores the chosen reference in avatarCrate and then starts the direct asynchronous swap. With randomize false, the request uses avatarCrate and the active-cord animation uses optionalPullCordStopIndex.

For example, enable this for a transformation zone that chooses among the six built-in candidate references on each allowed entry. Keep six valid candidates, including at least one different from the rig's recorded avatar; a shorter list can fail and a list of only matching candidates makes the repeat-selection loop unable to finish.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PullCordForceChange.rigManager
member.summary: Stores the global player's to find the pull cord and make direct avatar-swap requests.

remarks.para: A RigManager coordinates the player's body, controls and inventory. Each ForceChange attempt that passes the used check replaces this field with PlayerRefs.PlayerRigManager, the global player reference. Assigning it manually does not choose another target for the normal trigger path.

The trigger looks for exactly one entry in that rig's Inventory.specialItems array. It then checks the first child of that slot's scene object for a PullCordDevice. A different number of special slots or a child with no PullCordDevice causes the attempt to return without sending a request.

The inactive-cord branch uses the stored rig in SwapAvatar. That method requires the field to have been set already and does not perform this lookup itself. For example, changing this property before calling the trigger's normal path is overwritten by the global player lookup.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.PullCordForceChange.used
member.summary: Prevents further trigger requests once a request with enabled has consumed this component.

remarks.para: ForceChange checks this first and returns immediately when it is true, even if onlyTriggerOnce has since been switched off. The component sets it to true after a request call when onlyTriggerOnce is true. It does not wait for the avatar to load or check whether the active cord accepted the request.

It is request state, not proof of the player's current avatar. A busy pull cord can ignore a request and still leave used true. The complete methods of this component contain no automatic reset when the player leaves the trigger or when a swap fails.

For example, if you deliberately reuse a consumed trigger through its proxy properties, clear used as well as setting onlyTriggerOnce to false. Clearing it permits another eligible entry to request a change; it does not itself start the swap.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.RandomObject.Objects
member.summary: Supplies the candidate list whose chosen position is turned on while other positions are turned off.

remarks.para: A GameObject is a Unity scene object holding components such as its drawing or game scripts. The enable routine immediately chooses a random list position, then visits the list in order to change each entry’s activation setting. The Static Pick editor command uses the same selection and then disables this component.

For [RedBox, BlueBox, GreenBox], choosing position 1 turns BlueBox on and the other two off. Assign a list of non-null, distinct objects: repeated entries can turn the chosen object off again during a later visit. Changing this list selects candidates for the next pick; it does not immediately change which objects are on.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.RandomObject.spawnFragment
member.summary: Stores a SpawnFragment reference that the inspected RandomObject routines do not use when choosing from .

remarks.para: In the complete enable, random-pick, scale-reapply, Static Pick and constructor bodies inspected for this component, this reference is neither read nor written. Assigning it does not change those routines’ selection or request a fragment spawn. They select existing scene objects from Objects and change their activation settings. This finding is limited to those inspected routines.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.RigScreenOptions.OverlayCam
member.summary: The camera used to draw the temporary overlay when the spectator screen enters Void mode.

remarks.para: RenderOverlay activates this camera's GameObject, calls Camera.Render once immediately, then schedules the whole object to be hidden after 0.2 seconds. Assign an existing camera configured to draw the wanted overlay; this class does not create it or choose its contents.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.RigScreenOptions.SpecCamLocalpos
member.summary: Stores the last eye offset calculated for the separate spectator camera's follow target.

remarks.para: This is a local position relative to TargetTransform's parent, normally the headset's main camera. SetCameraLocation replaces it with (minus half eye separation, 0, 0) for Left, (plus half eye separation, 0, 0) for Right, or (0, 0, 0) for Center. With parent scale 1, the distances use meters.
This is a calculated cache, not a live position control. Changing it alone does not move the target, and the next Fisheye setup calls SetCameraLocation and overwrites it before applying the position.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.RigScreenOptions.TargetTransform
member.summary: The moving position and rotation that cam's SmoothFollower tries to follow.

remarks.para: During setup, this class creates a new child of Camera.main, starts it at local position zero, identity rotation (no extra rotation relative to its parent), and scale 1, and assigns it to the SmoothFollower on cam's GameObject. Fisheye setup then moves it sideways for the selected eye and rotates it by tiltAngle, a tilt in degrees about the target’s local X axis: positive values tilt downward and negative values tilt upward. This tilt is applied when Fisheye is selected. The follower smoothly moves the spectator camera toward this target's world position and rotation as the headset moves.

Setup replaces this field with the generated transform. Assigning a different transform to this field afterward does not automatically retarget the follower: its targetTransform reference was assigned separately. The standard target follows the head; this code does not select a hand target.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.RigScreenOptions.cam
member.summary: The separate spectator camera that is activated for Fisheye mode.

remarks.para: Passthrough and Void deactivate this camera's GameObject and disable its Camera component. Fisheye activates both. During setup, its GameObject must contain a SmoothFollower; that component is given the generated TargetTransform and smooths the camera's movement toward the headset-based target.
This class expects an existing camera reference. Changing the field after setup does not configure a follower on the replacement camera. The headset's Camera.main and OverlayCam have different jobs.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.RigScreenOptions.cameraMode
member.summary: The fallback spectator mode used at startup when the settings object has no spectator settings.

remarks.para: Passthrough mirrors headset eye images, Fisheye uses cam, and Void turns off those outputs and renders the overlay once. If spectator settings exist, startup uses their mode instead of this field. SetSpectatorCamera applies its own mode argument without writing this field, so this value does not reliably tell you which mode is currently active. Changing it after startup does not switch the screen by itself.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.RigScreenOptions.eyeTarget
member.summary: The fallback eye choice used at startup when the settings object has no spectator settings.

remarks.para: For Fisheye, Left and Right move the follow target half the headset camera's eye separation sideways, while Center uses the midpoint. For Passthrough, Left and Right choose the corresponding headset image, while Center selects both images.

Startup prefers the saved spectator settings when present. SetCameraLocation, SetPassthroughLocation, and SetSpectatorCamera use their arguments without updating this field. Changing it alone after startup does not change the displayed view.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.RigScreenOptions.tiltAngle
member.summary: Tilts the separate spectator camera's follow target up or down when Fisheye mode is applied.

remarks.para: The value is an angle in degrees around the target's local X axis, relative to its parent camera. Zero adds no tilt; positive values aim its forward direction downward with Unity's usual axes, while negative values aim upward. For example, 10 requests a 10-degree downward tilt. The camera's SmoothFollower then moves toward that target rotation.

SetSpectatorCamera reads this when applying Fisheye and replaces the target's local rotation with that X rotation. Changing the field alone does not immediately rotate the target. Passthrough does not use this tilt, and no runtime angle clamp was found in this setup method.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.RoundProfileGroup.arenaGameMode
member.summary: Selects the arena rules that the game controller applies when this group is played.

remarks.para: The choices are SURVIVAL, CHALLENGE, CUSTOM, PROTECT, WEAPON, INSTA_DEATH and KING_OF_THE_HILL. For example, CUSTOM and PROTECT request friendlies (allied NPCs, meaning non-player characters controlled by the game) from the current wave’s friendly list; PROTECT also starts the arena king’s entrance sequence, and INSTA_DEATH enables the player’s instant-death setting on entry. PROTECT and WEAPON also disable the ordinary weapon spawner when starting a match.

Changing this stored value does not immediately restart a running mode. The controller checks it during mode entry, wave setup and other arena actions. isObjectiveMode is a separate flag for objective targeting and replacement rules.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.RoundProfileGroup.awardAmmoOnDeath
member.summary: Enables light, medium and heavy ammo rewards for registered enemy deaths in the ordinary arena death path.

remarks.para: The reward path skips friendly NPCs and is bypassed by the objective-mode branch. NPC means a game-controlled character. The three Award fields choose ammo categories; they do not choose different rewards based on the enemy’s size.

For each category, the reward is its configured award divided by difficulty code plus one, rounded to the nearest whole ammo round; exact halves round to the even integer. Difficulty codes are easy 0, medium 1, hard 2, harder 3 and hardest 4. For example, an award of 40 gives 20 rounds at medium difficulty. The controller adds the ammo directly to the player’s inventory.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.RoundProfileGroup.boneLeaderData
member.summary: Chooses the leaderboard data that the arena focuses when the player enters this group.

remarks.para: When both this asset and the controller’s leaderboard manager exist, mode entry passes this asset to FocusExplicitLeaderboard. Focusing selects the leaderboard; it does not submit a result by itself.

Later submission uses the selected data’s scoreType to choose a score, a time in seconds, or a time converted to milliseconds. CopyGroupProfile keeps the same boneLeaderData reference, so the asset is shared between source and copy.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.RoundProfileGroup.clearAmmoOnModeEnd
member.summary: Makes arena mode cleanup remove its loot weapons and clear the player’s ammo inventory.

remarks.para: A new group starts with this true. In EndOfMode, the controller first requests removal of all loot weapons, then performs the mode-end notification and resets arena displays and state. The ammo inventory is cleared afterward. Code responding to the mode-end notification can therefore still see ammo before the clear.
This is checked during that cleanup path, not on every wave change. Setting it false lets that path leave the inventory alone.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.RoundProfileGroup.currEnemy
member.summary: Holds an enemy profile reference on the group; it does not identify the controller’s active spawned enemy.

remarks.para: A profile describes planned settings; it is not a spawned actor. The arena’s PlayerEnter and StartNextWave paths choose rounds and waves from roundProfileList using the controller’s own indices and currentRound/currentWave references. They do not update this group.currEnemy reference.

CopyGroupProfile leaves currEnemy null in the new group. Treat it as separately stored data for code that explicitly assigns and reads it, not as an automatically refreshed report of what the arena is playing.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.RoundProfileGroup.currRound
member.summary: Holds a round profile reference on the group without selecting the controller’s active round.

remarks.para: A profile describes planned settings; it is not a spawned actor. The arena’s PlayerEnter and StartNextWave paths choose rounds and waves from roundProfileList using the controller’s own indices and currentRound/currentWave references. They do not update this group.currRound reference.

CopyGroupProfile leaves currRound null in the new group. Treat it as separately stored data for code that explicitly assigns and reads it, not as an automatically refreshed report of what the arena is playing.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.RoundProfileGroup.currWave
member.summary: Holds a wave profile reference on the group without selecting the controller’s active wave.

remarks.para: A profile describes planned settings; it is not a spawned actor. The arena’s PlayerEnter and StartNextWave paths choose rounds and waves from roundProfileList using the controller’s own indices and currentRound/currentWave references. They do not update this group.currWave reference.

CopyGroupProfile leaves currWave null in the new group. Treat it as separately stored data for code that explicitly assigns and reads it, not as an automatically refreshed report of what the arena is playing.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.RoundProfileGroup.descriptionText
member.summary: Supplies the description text shown when this group is selected and on the active arena menu page.

remarks.para: ChallengeSelect and TrialSelect combine this text with displayTitle for their selection text. SetupActivePage places it in the active page’s description label. Assigning text changes the stored value; the visible label updates when one of these menu refresh calls runs.
CopyGroupProfile does not copy this field, so a newly copied group needs its description assigned separately.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.RoundProfileGroup.displayTitle
member.summary: Supplies the group name shown in arena selection text, the active menu page and arena mode labels.

remarks.para: ChallengeSelect and TrialSelect display the title alongside descriptionText. SetupActivePage and UpdateArenaDisplay read it when refreshing their text labels; changing the field alone does not trigger those refresh calls. This text can differ from the Unity asset’s name.
CopyGroupProfile copies this string into the new group.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.RoundProfileGroup.enemySpawnDelay
member.summary: Sets the whole-number game-time wait after an enemy spawn attempt in the arena spawning loop.

remarks.para: The unit is seconds. A new group starts at 1. The loop converts this integer to milliseconds for its delay and follows Unity’s time scale, so slow motion stretches the wall-clock wait and a paused game stops scaled time. A frame is one game update; wall-clock time is real elapsed time.

This wait follows the attempt and, for the ordinary path, its awaited spawn work. The loop also checks the living-enemy limit, remaining enemy entries, session state and cancellation before requesting another enemy. A value of 2 adds a two-game-second wait; it does not promise one successfully created enemy every exactly two seconds. Frame timing and spawn work can add time.
The loop reads the field for each new wait. Changing it does not shorten a wait already started. CopyGroupProfile resets it to the new-group default instead of copying it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.RoundProfileGroup.friendlyCount
member.summary: Stores the friendly-count choice copied from the custom arena menu when its waves are rebuilt.

remarks.para: UpdateCustomGroup reads the menu’s chosen count once, stores it here and separately fills each new wave’s friendlyProfileList with that many entries. A friendly profile is the planned configuration for an allied game-controlled character. Each entry refers to the first friendly profile in StaticProfiles, the game’s shared profile registry. NPC means a non-player character controlled by the game.

CUSTOM and PROTECT mode entry use the current wave’s friendly-list length to request friendlies, rather than reading this stored group count. Changing only friendlyCount therefore does not rebuild those lists or change the controller’s live friendly count. Rebuild the custom group or edit its wave lists for that setup path. CopyGroupProfile leaves this count at zero.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.RoundProfileGroup.friendlySpawnDelay
member.summary: Sets the whole-number game-time wait after each friendly spawn request in the arena friendly-spawn routine.

remarks.para: A friendly is an allied, game-controlled character. The unit is seconds, with a new-group default of 1. The friendly-spawn coroutine is a sequence that continues over multiple game frames: it requests a friendly spawn, advances its spawner index and then waits this many scaled game seconds. Scaled time follows slow motion and pauses. A frame is one game update; wall-clock time is real elapsed time. It resumes on a later game frame, so the actual wall-clock interval may be longer.

A request does not prove a friendly was successfully created before the next wait begins. The routine uses its requested target count and the controller’s live friendly count to decide whether to continue. It reads this setting when starting each wait; changing the field does not change a wait already underway. CopyGroupProfile does not preserve this delay.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.RoundProfileGroup.heavyAward
member.summary: Sets the base amount of heavy ammunition rewarded for an eligible enemy death.

remarks.para: The amount is measured in rounds of heavy ammo, not a count or size of enemies. It applies when awardAmmoOnDeath is true, the dead NPC (non-player character, a game-controlled character) is not friendly, and the death follows the non-objective reward path. A new group starts at 40.

The actual reward is roundToEven(A / (D + 1)). A is this configured ammo amount in rounds, D is the current difficulty code (easy 0, medium 1, hard 2, harder 3, hardest 4), and roundToEven means nearest whole number with exact halves choosing the even number. For example, A=40 and D=1 reward 20 rounds. The controller grants all three configured ammo categories for the eligible death.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.RoundProfileGroup.increaseEnemyRate
member.summary: Sets how many concurrent enemy places a custom difficulty increase adds before applying its goal.

remarks.para: For each IncreaseWaveDifficultyAtCustomRate call, rate r raises the proposed living-enemy limit by r, capped at maxConcGoal. When r > 0, the call adds 2 × r enemy-list entries; when r <= 0, it appends none. A negative r can still lower the proposed limit. For example, a rate of 2 proposes two more simultaneous enemies and adds four planned entries to that wave.

The new-group default is 1. This setting is read when the helper runs; assigning it does not spawn actors or recalculate a wave immediately. The gradual UpdateProfileEnemyCount path enables custom-count mode and stores the chosen rate. CopyGroupProfile resets the rate to its default.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.RoundProfileGroup.isCustomEnemyCount
member.summary: Makes newly generated waves use the group’s custom growth rate and concurrency goal.

remarks.para: CreateNewWave checks this flag. True calls IncreaseWaveDifficultyAtCustomRate with increaseEnemyRate and maxConcGoal; false uses the ordinary difficulty-tier increase. This chooses an algorithm for the next generated wave, not a record of where a count originally came from.

The gradual UpdateProfileEnemyCount path sets this flag true when storing a new rate and goal. Merely toggling the flag does not regenerate a wave, change currently alive enemies or refresh saved totals. CopyGroupProfile preserves it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.RoundProfileGroup.isObjectiveMode
member.summary: Enables the objective-targeting and enemy-replacement rules for this group.

remarks.para: This flag enables the arena’s special objective target and replacement branch. An NPC is a non-player character controlled by the game. When this flag is true, NPC registration assigns objective targets; on registered character deaths, the controller removes the character from objective tracking, schedules a delayed replacement or starts objective completion based on kills and limitReached, then returns before the ordinary ammo-reward path.
This is separate from arenaGameMode. Assigning the flag alone does not build the scene’s objectives or start an objective session; the controller still needs its objective objects and setup.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.RoundProfileGroup.isStacked
member.summary: Makes mode-end cleanup advance to the next profile group in the controller’s group list.

remarks.para: EndOfMode calls ProgressToNextProfile when this is true. That method increases the group index, selects the next group and prepares its next mode. Reaching the end of the group list invokes stack completion and ends the session.

For stacked challenge-style groups, mode entry also skips the normal IncreaseChallengeDifficulty call. The flag sequences groups; the inspected progression path does not merge one group’s enemy lists into another. CopyGroupProfile preserves it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.RoundProfileGroup.killLimit
member.summary: Sets the enemy-kill target used to begin objective-profile completion and restrict replacements.

remarks.para: The unit is registered enemy deaths; friendly deaths do not increment the controller’s enemiesKilled counter. A new group starts at 20. In objective mode, when the updated counter is at least this value and limitReached is false, the death handler sets limitReached true before starting objective-profile completion.

This is not a strict instantaneous stop on every kill or spawn. Below the target, or when limitReached is already true, that handler can still schedule delayed replacements. SpawnReplacement later refuses only when the count is greater than the limit or the session has ended. A previously scheduled request at exact equality can therefore still proceed.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.RoundProfileGroup.lightAward
member.summary: Sets the base amount of light ammunition rewarded for an eligible enemy death.

remarks.para: The amount is measured in rounds of light ammo, not a count or size of enemies. It applies when awardAmmoOnDeath is true, the dead NPC (non-player character, a game-controlled character) is not friendly, and the death follows the non-objective reward path. A new group starts at 40.

The actual reward is roundToEven(A / (D + 1)). A is this configured ammo amount in rounds, D is the current difficulty code (easy 0, medium 1, hard 2, harder 3, hardest 4), and roundToEven means nearest whole number with exact halves choosing the even number. For example, A=40 and D=1 reward 20 rounds. The controller grants all three configured ammo categories for the eligible death.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.RoundProfileGroup.limitReached
member.summary: Records that objective-profile completion has been started by the enemy-kill target check.

remarks.para: The objective death handler sets this true when enemiesKilled is at least killLimit and the flag was false, then calls ProgressToNextObjectiveProfile. Setting it before that call stops later deaths from starting the same completion branch again.

It is cleared by InitObjectiveMode and by the next objective-profile setup. An already true value still sends later registered deaths toward delayed replacement scheduling; the replacement itself checks the session and kill count. This flag is not a report that the wave’s concurrent enemy cap has been reached.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.RoundProfileGroup.maxConcGoal
member.summary: Caps the concurrent enemy limit calculated by custom-rate wave increases.

remarks.para: The unit is living enemies allowed at one time. IncreaseWaveDifficultyAtCustomRate chooses the smaller of the old wave limit plus increaseEnemyRate and this goal. It can even lower a wave limit that already exceeds the goal. This caps concurrency, not the total number of planned enemy entries.

The new-group default is 10. Changing it affects the next helper call; it does not immediately remove enemies or set all existing wave limits. IncreaseConcurrentEnemyCount edits each wave directly without assigning this goal. CopyGroupProfile resets it to 10.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.RoundProfileGroup.medAward
member.summary: Sets the base amount of medium ammunition rewarded for an eligible enemy death.

remarks.para: The amount is measured in rounds of medium ammo, not a count or size of enemies. It applies when awardAmmoOnDeath is true, the dead NPC (non-player character, a game-controlled character) is not friendly, and the death follows the non-objective reward path. A new group starts at 40.

The actual reward is roundToEven(A / (D + 1)). A is this configured ammo amount in rounds, D is the current difficulty code (easy 0, medium 1, hard 2, harder 3, hardest 4), and roundToEven means nearest whole number with exact halves choosing the even number. For example, A=40 and D=1 reward 20 rounds. The controller grants all three configured ammo categories for the eligible death.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.RoundProfileGroup.objectiveRespawnDelay
member.summary: Sets the whole-number game-time wait before a delayed objective-mode replacement spawn attempt.

remarks.para: The unit is seconds, with a new-group default of 5. CoDelayedRespawn is a coroutine, a sequence that continues across game updates; it reads the setting when it starts and waits that many scaled game seconds before calling SpawnReplacement. A frame is one game update, and wall-clock time is real elapsed time. Slow motion, pauses and frame scheduling affect wall-clock time.

The later replacement can still be refused if the session has ended or the enemy-kill count is greater than killLimit. The delay does not guarantee a successfully spawned enemy. Changing the setting does not alter a wait already started. CopyGroupProfile does not preserve it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.RoundProfileGroup.roundProfileList
member.summary: Provides the ordered rounds from which the arena selects the current round and its waves.

remarks.para: Each RoundProfile holds its waveGroupList. PlayerEnter and StartNextWave select roundProfileList at the controller’s round number minus one, then select the wave list at its wave number minus one. For example, displayed round 1 uses list position 0. Both lists must contain valid entries at the selected positions.

Runtime generation can append rounds and waves. Replacing this list does not by itself update the controller’s already selected currentRound/currentWave references. CopyGroupProfile creates a new round list and new round/wave containers while sharing some referenced data inside them.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.RoundProfileGroup.showGroupGraph
member.summary: Stored Boolean that starts false and is reset to false when the profile group is copied.

remarks.para: CopyGroupProfile creates a new group but does not copy this field. For example, a source group with this flag true produces a copy with it false. Assign the flag separately on the result if your own code needs to retain it.

The inspected Arena menu challenge selection, trial selection and active-page setup do not read this flag when building their displayed text. Those paths do not establish a graph-drawing effect for the flag. The verified behavior here is storage and omission from the group-copy operation.
The inspected Arena player-progress save/load route stores player statistics and trial completion data, rather than this whole group. Loading that player-progress file does not restore this flag.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.RoundProfileGroup.showGroupInfo
member.summary: Stored Boolean that starts false and is omitted when CopyGroupProfile makes a new group.

remarks.para: A copied group leaves this flag false even when the source flag is true. If your own code uses it, copy the flag separately after CopyGroupProfile. Changing it stores a value on this group.

The inspected Arena menu challenge selection, trial selection and active-page setup read the group title and description directly, without checking this flag. Those paths do not establish a show-or-hide effect for an information panel.
The inspected Arena player-progress save/load route restores player statistics and trial completion data. It does not restore this flag from a saved whole profile group.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.RoundProfileGroup.sublimateOnDeath
member.summary: Makes the registered-death handler turn off a body’s gravity and push it upward.

remarks.para: The controller tracks the dead character for cleanup, then calls Sublimate with the effect enabled. That method disables gravity on its Rigidbody components. A Rigidbody is the Unity component that gives an object physical motion and collisions. It applies upward force in the world frame, meaning toward the scene’s fixed up direction rather than the character’s own rotated up direction.

The verified immediate effect is a floating, upward-moving body. This flag does not itself guarantee an immediate particle conversion or removal. When the tracked object is despawned, the arena restores its gravity and removes the cleanup entry. CopyGroupProfile leaves this flag false in the new group.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.RoundProfileGroup.teleportDist
member.summary: Stored floating-point setting that defaults to 15 and is preserved by CopyGroupProfile.

remarks.para: The group constructor, its setup routine for a newly created group, initializes this value to 15. CopyGroupProfile then replaces that default with the source value unchanged. For example, a source value of 23.5 produces 23.5 in the copy. This describes new-group creation and copying; it does not force an existing configured asset back to 15.

The inspected Arena challenge setup, NPC registration, enemy/friendly spawning and player-distance checks do not read this field to calculate a position. They do not establish a distance unit, a reference point such as the player, or a teleport trigger for this value.

The inspected Arena player-progress save/load route stores player statistics and trial completion data, rather than this whole profile group. That route does not restore this numeric setting. The verified effect of the group-copy helper is to retain it without conversion.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.RoundProfileGroup.teleportTick

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SaveData.GraphicsManager.CustomVolumetricRenderingSettings
member.summary: Holds the grid and distance settings that the graphics controls apply to fog and lighting through the air.

remarks.para: Volumetric lighting divides the air into small cells to calculate fog and light beams. This data contains the grid's width, height, and depth in cell counts, a surrounding clipmap resolution, and near/far distances in meters. A clipmap is a separate 3D cache of nearby lighting samples around the volumetric camera, with grids at different scales. Its resolution counts cells along each side, so resolution 64 means 64 × 64 × 64 cells per grid. Near and far are the front and back depth limits of the volumetric camera's lighting grid, measured forward from that camera in meters.

SetVolumetricVariables changes this data according to the selected quality, assigns it to the volumetric renderers it finds, and restarts their resources. Directly changing or replacing this reference does not perform that rebuild. The quality setter can also overwrite manually edited resolutions.

GraphicsManager loads this reference during its static setup. The custom, PC, and Quest volumetric references are loaded from the same resource path in that setup; their names do not establish three independent copies.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SaveData.GraphicsManager.HBAOFeature
member.summary: Selects the renderer-feature list entry that the corner-shading controls turn on or off.

remarks.para: A renderer feature is a component that can add rendering steps to Unity's rendering pipeline, the process that draws the camera image. CustomRendererData is the renderer-data asset holding the ordered list of those features. HBAO darkens corners and places where nearby surfaces block light. This is a zero-based index into that list, initialized to 2 during GraphicsManager's static setup.

CheckRenderfeatures enables that entry when the stored HBAO level is not Disabled and disables it otherwise. Changing the index redirects that activation, so it must match the renderer's feature order. The index is assigned during setup rather than discovered by searching for a feature type.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SaveData.GraphicsManager.MainSceneVolume
member.summary: Identifies the scene object whose collection of image effects is replaced during custom graphics setup.

remarks.para: A Unity volume applies image-effect settings such as bloom and corner shading to camera images. If this reference is missing, InitializeCustomSettings looks for RigVolumeSettings and gets the Volume on that object.

Initialization saves the volume's original profile when needed and assigns CustomVolumeProfile to it. Replacing this reference redirects later setup to another volume; it does not by itself copy a profile or update the newly referenced volume.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SaveData.GraphicsManager.MainVolumeProfile
member.summary: Caches the scene volume's original image-effect profile as the source for custom setup. Pairs with .

remarks.para: A volume profile is a collection of image-effect components. InitializeCustomSettings fills this cache from MainSceneVolume when the cache is empty. It creates a custom profile only if none exists, using a new list that contains these same component objects.

The components are shared rather than individually copied, so later custom bloom or corner-shading changes can also affect the components referenced by this original profile. After initialization, the scene volume is assigned CustomVolumeProfile; this cached original is not necessarily the currently applied profile.
Changing this cache affects a later first-time custom-profile construction. An already existing CustomVolumeProfile is reused instead of rebuilt from the new cache.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SaveData.GraphicsManager.PCVolumetricRenderingSettings
member.summary: Holds the PC-named volumetric-data reference loaded during GraphicsManager setup.

remarks.para: Volumetric data describes the grid and distances used to calculate fog and light through the air. In the complete inspected GraphicsManager methods, this reference is initialized but is not selected by the quality setters; those setters apply CustomVolumetricRenderingSettings.

The PC, Quest, and custom references are loaded from the same resource path. Do not assume these names provide independent platform presets. Assigning a different object here has no verified application effect in the inspected GraphicsManager methods; callers outside this class and mods were not exhaustively checked.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SaveData.GraphicsManager.PercentToFloat
member.summary: Sets the factor used to convert integer render-scale, mesh-detail, and custom foveated settings into fractional values.

remarks.para: Initialized to 0.01 during GraphicsManager's static setup. Multiplying a percentage by 0.01 divides it by 100: render scale 150 becomes a width-and-height multiplier of 1.5, while an outer-radius setting 40 becomes an angular fraction of 0.4 before the foveated projection calculation.

For the integer LOD setter, the product is a unitless base mesh-detail multiplier before a correction for the main camera's viewing angle; LOD means level of detail, choosing between more detailed and simpler meshes. Only the Custom foveated preset uses PercentToFloat for its custom radii; the built-in presets use fixed values instead. For foveated outer radius, the fraction multiplies a reference angle of about 88.2 degrees from the center direction; Foveated rendering keeps more image detail near the center and reduces shading work farther out. The inner ratio compares the inner region's angle with the outer region's angle. The ellipse-axis scale compares the angular half-widths along its two axes, changing the region's oval shape; these ratios have no meter or degree unit. Projection converts those viewing angles into positions on the image. For example, outer setting 40 gives 40 × 0.01 × 88.2 degrees = about 35.28 degrees before projection.

Changing this shared factor affects later calls that read it, rather than recalculating already applied settings immediately. Some other conversions use fixed 0.01 or 100 constants, including preset-based custom LOD and percentage storage, so changing the factor does not change every percentage conversion together.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SaveData.GraphicsManager.QuestVolumetricRenderingSettings
member.summary: Holds the Quest-named volumetric-data reference loaded during GraphicsManager setup.

remarks.para: Volumetric data describes the grid and distances used to calculate fog and light through the air. In the complete inspected GraphicsManager methods, this reference is initialized but is not selected by the quality setters; those setters apply CustomVolumetricRenderingSettings.

The PC, Quest, and custom references are loaded from the same resource path. Do not assume these names provide independent platform presets. Assigning a different object here has no verified application effect in the inspected GraphicsManager methods; callers outside this class and mods were not exhaustively checked.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SaveData.GraphicsManager.SSAOFeature
member.summary: Stores a feature-list index for which no runtime use was found in the complete inspected GraphicsManager methods.

remarks.para: SSAO means screen-space ambient occlusion: shading calculated from the camera image to darken corners and nearby surfaces. This field is initialized to index 0 during GraphicsManager's static setup.

The inspected class uses a separate HBAOFeature index for its working corner-shading control. Its complete native methods do not read SSAOFeature after initialization, so changing this field is not a verified way to change that control. This finding is limited to GraphicsManager; callers outside the class and mods were not exhaustively checked.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SaveData.GraphicsManager.VRSRenderFeature
member.summary: Selects the renderer-feature list entry that the foveated graphics controls configure and activate.

remarks.para: CustomRendererData is the renderer-data asset holding an ordered feature list. A renderer feature is a component that can add rendering steps to Unity's rendering pipeline, the process that draws the camera image. This is a zero-based index into that list, initialized to 4 during GraphicsManager's static setup. VRS means variable rate shading, which uses supported graphics hardware to vary shading detail across image regions. Foveated rendering keeps more image detail near the center and reduces shading work farther away.

The controls expect a VRSRenderFeature at that entry. They change its central-region radii, hardware-versus-fallback request, and debug visualization; CheckRenderfeatures enables it when the stored foveated preset is not Disabled. The feature follows its fallback pass path when VRS support is unavailable or fallback is requested; with hardware support and no fallback request, it follows the hardware path.
Changing the index redirects those controls and must match the renderer's feature order and type. The index itself does not enable foveated rendering.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SaveData.GraphicsManager.graphicsSettings
member.summary: Holds the current game graphics choices that GraphicsManager reads and updates when applying presets or individual controls.

remarks.para: This is BONELAB's save-data GraphicsSettings object, not Unity's engine GraphicsSettings class. DataManager is BONELAB's source for the current saved settings and exposes that settings object. During static setup, GraphicsManager caches (keeps a reference to) the GraphicsSettings object it reads from DataManager. Its fields record choices such as render-scale percentage, mesh-detail percentage, effect quality levels, and the foveated mode and radii. Foveated rendering keeps more image detail near the center and reduces shading work farther out; its radii set the sizes of those regions.

Editing a stored choice directly does not run its rendering setter. For example, changing the stored RenderScale alone does not change the applied image size; use SetRenderscale or custom initialization to apply it. An applied value can differ from its stored request because of clamps or preset replacement.

Replacing this reference redirects later GraphicsManager reads and writes, but does not install rendering assets or automatically save a file. The inspected class does not refresh the cached reference from DataManager on each control call.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SaveData.PlayerSettings.BeltLocationRight
member.summary: Stores which side of the player the belt slots should use.

remarks.para: True requests the right side; false requests the left. Left and right mean the player’s own sides, even when the player turns around. Applying the settings copies this choice to the body setup and mirrors belt slots that were configured to allow flipping.
The menu’s belt-side button changes this choice and applies the body setup. The property setter alone does not move an existing pouch. Which slots can move depends on their setup.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SaveData.PlayerSettings.BodyLogLocationRight
member.summary: Stores which side of the player should hold the BodyLog, the pull-cord avatar changer.

remarks.para: True requests the right side; false requests the left. These are the player’s own sides, not fixed directions in the level. Applying the settings updates the special inventory slot and the pull-cord device’s side flag.
This chooses a side; it does not grant or enable the BodyLog. Those decisions come from separate progression flags. Setting this property alone does not move the device.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SaveData.PlayerSettings.ChestCircumference
member.summary: Stores the distance around the player’s chest in metres for body calibration.

remarks.para: Circumference means the full distance around the body, as measured with a tape, rather than its width from side to side. For example, 1.00 means 100 centimetres around this part of the body.

Applying body settings copies this measurement to the body setup, which estimates the torso’s width and front-to-back depth on the hidden calibration avatar. That avatar is the model used as a ruler for the player’s real body proportions. Before estimating its shape, the game divides the saved circumference by the ratio of the player’s measured height to the calibration avatar’s height; both heights are in metres.

The measurement menu adjusts this value by 0.01 metre per button press and marks the measurements as custom. Choosing a shirt-size preset recalculates it. The property setter itself does not clamp the value or rebuild the body.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SaveData.PlayerSettings.CurrentAvatar
member.summary: Stores the avatar barcode that the game tries to restore from the player’s save.

remarks.para: A barcode is the text identifier of an avatar asset, not an avatar object already present in the level. The startup loader checks this text, requests an avatar swap, and waits for the request to finish. Storing a barcode does not prove that the avatar has loaded.

The avatar menu writes this value after its swap reports success, then saves the active save. Directly assigning the property only changes the stored text; it does not start a swap. For example, replacing the text with another installed avatar’s barcode changes the saved choice, not the body currently being worn.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SaveData.PlayerSettings.FallbackAvatar
member.summary: Stores the backup avatar barcode recorded for restoring the player’s avatar.

remarks.para: A barcode is the text identifier of an avatar asset. After a successful swap in the avatar menu, this backup is updated only when the selected avatar belongs to an internal (built-in) pallet. A pallet is the package that contains the avatar asset.

There is a limitation in this build’s startup loader: when the current-avatar choice is invalid or its swap fails, the loader validates this backup text but passes the current-avatar text to the retry again. A valid backup therefore does not guarantee that the backup avatar will load. Assigning this property does not spawn or swap an avatar.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SaveData.PlayerSettings.FavoriteAvatars
member.summary: Stores the ordered avatar barcodes for the player’s favorite avatar slots.

remarks.para: Each string is a barcode: the text identifier of an avatar asset. The avatar panel resolves these strings into assets and fills its favorite-slot buttons in list order. Confirming favorites builds a new list from those slots and saves it.

When the list is null or shorter than the panel’s default-favorites list, the panel uses its default choices. If an individual saved avatar cannot be found, it tries the default for that slot. For example, swapping the first two barcodes swaps their saved slot order; assigning the list does not immediately rebuild an already open panel.
This property holds the list itself, not a copy. Editing an item changes this object’s stored list, but saving it to disk and refreshing a menu remain separate steps.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SaveData.PlayerSettings.FavoriteSpawnables
member.summary: Stores the spawnable-asset barcodes shown as favorites in the spawn menu.

remarks.para: A spawnable is an object the spawn gun can create; its barcode is the text identifier of the asset. The spawnables panel reads these strings and builds its favorite-item collection. Toggling an item’s favorite button rebuilds the menu, writes the collection’s barcodes back here, and requests a save.

For example, adding an installed object’s barcode records it as a favorite; it does not create that object in the level. The loader skips strings that fail barcode validation. A correctly shaped barcode can still refer to an asset that is missing.
The property holds a shared list, not a copy. Direct edits do not automatically refresh an open menu or write the save file.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SaveData.PlayerSettings.Haptics
member.summary: Stores the strength multiplier for controller vibration feedback.

remarks.para: This value has no physical unit. The normal menu range is 0 to 1: 0 gives zero requested vibration strength, 1 keeps the effect’s original strength, and 0.5 halves it. The controller hardware can still limit the final vibration.

Applying body settings copies the value to both controllers’ vibration helpers. Each helper first limits an effect’s base strength to 0–1, then multiplies it by this saved scale before sending the request. The property setter does not limit the scale, so assigning a value outside the menu range can send a strength outside that usual range.
Assigning this property only changes the saved-settings object in memory. The game applies the choice through its player-settings update; writing the save file is a separate step.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SaveData.PlayerSettings.HipsCircumference
member.summary: Stores the distance around the player’s hips in metres for body calibration.

remarks.para: Circumference means the full distance around the body, as measured with a tape, rather than its width from side to side. For example, 1.00 means 100 centimetres around this part of the body.

Applying body settings copies this measurement to the body setup, which estimates the torso’s width and front-to-back depth on the hidden calibration avatar. That avatar is the model used as a ruler for the player’s real body proportions. Before estimating its shape, the game divides the saved circumference by the ratio of the player’s measured height to the calibration avatar’s height; both heights are in metres.

The measurement menu adjusts this value by 0.01 metre per button press and marks the measurements as custom. Choosing a shirt-size preset recalculates it. The property setter itself does not clamp the value or rebuild the body.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SaveData.PlayerSettings.InseamLength
member.summary: Stores the player’s inside-leg distance from the crotch toward the floor in metres.

remarks.para: For example, 0.80 means an inseam of 80 centimetres. The measurement menu displays centimetres by multiplying the saved value by 100 and changes it by 0.01 metre per press.

Choosing a preset recalculates this length from the saved height and the menu’s configured proportion. Manually changing it selects custom measurements. Applying body settings copies the length to the body setup and passes it, together with the player’s height in metres, to the calibration avatar.

The calibration avatar’s method for this length has an empty body in this build. This inspected calibration path therefore stores and displays the measurement without changing arm or leg proportions through that method. The property setter also performs no clamp or recalibration.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SaveData.PlayerSettings.InventoryHudEnabled
member.summary: Stores the saved on/off preference named for the inventory HUD.

remarks.para: HUD means information drawn over the game view. True and false are stored as the inventory_hud JSON setting, so the value can survive saving and loading.

The setter only stores the flag. The inspected Control_Player startup and SEND_VITALS settings-update methods do not read it or show or hide an inventory overlay. Do not use this setter as a command to make an existing HUD visible; a component that reads the flag would need to apply it. These inspected methods also do not establish whether an overlay belongs on the wrist.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SaveData.PlayerSettings.LocomotionCurve
member.summary: Stores which configured curve reshapes the movement input’s direction.

remarks.para: The choices are 0 = Linear, 1 = Poles, 2 = GenesisDpad, 3 = Dpad, 4 = SmoothGenesis, and 5 = SmoothDpad. Applying the settings selects the corresponding curve asset on the controller rig, the object that reads the headset and hand controls. The actual curve shapes come from those assets.

In the movement-input calculation, the curve’s horizontal axis is the signed input angle in degrees from forward on the two-dimensional control surface. Its vertical axis is the replacement direction angle in degrees. The game rebuilds the movement vector from that angle while keeping its length, which represents how far the control is pushed. Thus this is a direction response, not a saved speed or deadzone number.

For example, a configured curve that maps a 30-degree input angle to 45 degrees steers movement at 45 degrees for that input. Selecting an index does not edit the curve. Unsupported indices leave the rig’s previously selected curve in place; assigning the property alone does not select a curve on the live rig.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SaveData.PlayerSettings.LocomotionDegreesPerSnap
member.summary: Stores the turn-speed setting despite the property’s angle-like name.

remarks.para: This is a number without a degree unit. The menu cycles it from 1 through 10, and a new settings object starts at 6. Larger positive values make a snap turn settle faster. The snap calculation uses a smoothing time of 0.2 / s + 0.01 seconds, where s is this saved speed setting; for s = 6, that time is about 0.043 seconds. That is a smoothing parameter, not a promise that every turn finishes in that exact time.

For smooth turning, the full-input speed before time adjustments is 48 × s + 60 degrees per second. Here s is again this saved setting: 6 gives 348 degrees per second. Actual movement also depends on control input, frame time, input smoothing, and slow-motion adjustments.

The total snap angle comes from the separate saved angle selector: 1 requests 15 degrees, 2 requests 30, 3 requests 45, and 4 requests 90. The property setter neither applies nor limits this speed setting.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SaveData.PlayerSettings.LocomotionDirection
member.summary: Stores what orientation defines forward for control-based movement.

remarks.para: 0 means the controller reference, 1 means the head reference, and 2 means a custom reference set up on the controller rig. These orientations turn with the chosen hand, head, or custom object; they are not fixed compass directions in the level. The normal menu cycles only between controller and head.

Controller mode selects the left controller when the rig’s cached handedness is right-handed, and the right controller otherwise. Head mode uses the head object’s orientation. A custom mode needs its custom reference to be set up. An unsupported value leaves the previous reference unchanged.

For example, head mode makes control-forward follow the head’s facing direction. The settings update chooses this reference before copying the new handedness flag to the rig, so a simultaneous handedness change can leave controller mode using the previous hand until the reference is selected again. Setting the saved property alone does not update the live reference.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SaveData.PlayerSettings.LocomotionSnapDegreesPerFrame
member.summary: Stores the turning-mode and snap-angle selector, despite the property’s speed-like name.

remarks.para: This is an integer choice, not a count of degrees applied each frame. For thumbstick input, 0 does not calculate a new turn, 1 selects a 15-degree snap, 2 selects a 30-degree snap, 3 selects a 45-degree snap, 4 selects a 90-degree snap, and 5 selects smooth turning. A snap turn means one requested angle spread across updates; smooth turning keeps turning while the control is held. Unsupported values do not select a new turn in that thumbstick path. The snap method itself falls back to 15 degrees if it receives an unrecognized angle choice.

The menu cycles the selector from 0 through 5, and new settings start at 5. A snap request adds the selected angle to the amount still left to turn, with its sign chosen from the horizontal input. The rig then spreads that turn across updates using its separate saved speed setting.
For example, selector 3 requests a 45-degree snap, not 3 degrees per frame. Assigning the property only stores the choice; the player-settings update copies it to the controller rig.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SaveData.PlayerSettings.MeasurementPresets
member.summary: Stores the shirt-size preset or custom-measurement mode for body calibration.

remarks.para: The choices are CUSTOM = 0, XSMALL = 1, SMALL = 2, MEDIUM = 3, LARGE = 4, XLARGE = 5, XXLARGE = 6, and XXXLARGE = 7. A new settings object selects MEDIUM.

The measurement menu’s shirt-size buttons change this choice and recalculate chest, underbust, waist, and hip circumferences using configured size multipliers. Wingspan and inseam are recalculated from the saved height converted to metres and their configured proportions. Manual measurement buttons set the choice to CUSTOM.

For example, selecting LARGE in the menu replaces measurements with that preset’s calculated values. Assigning this property to LARGE alone only stores the selection; it does not run the menu’s calculation. The menu indexes its preset arrays, so values outside its configured choices are not safe input.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SaveData.PlayerSettings.Modified
member.summary: Stores the UTC date-and-time text created with the player-settings object.

remarks.para: UTC is a shared time reference that does not depend on the player’s local time zone. The constructor formats the current UTC time with the culture-independent universal-sortable date-and-time pattern and stores that text.

The property setter can replace the text, but changing another PlayerSettings property does not automatically refresh it through that property’s accessor. Treat this as saved timestamp text rather than proof that every gameplay setting was last edited at that exact time.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SaveData.PlayerSettings.OffsetFloor
member.summary: Stores the floor-calibration correction in centimetres.

remarks.para: For example, 5 means a stored correction of 5 centimetres, not 5 metres. The floor-calibration command estimates the tracked standing height and stores H − T, where H is the saved player height in centimetres and T is the command’s estimated standing height in centimetres. A positive value means that estimate was below the saved height.

The seated-calibration command includes this value when finding the remaining seated correction: S = H − T − F, where S is the seated correction in centimetres, H is saved height in centimetres, T is that command’s tracked-height estimate in centimetres, and F is this floor correction in centimetres.

The in-game adjustment buttons add or subtract 1 centimetre. The setter only stores the value. The inspected Control_Player settings-update methods do not directly move the rig by this correction, so assigning it is not an immediate command to raise or lower the floor.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SaveData.PlayerSettings.OffsetSitting
member.summary: Stores the seated-calibration correction in centimetres.

remarks.para: The seated-calibration command stores S = H − T − F. S is this seated correction in centimetres, H is the saved standing height in centimetres, T is the command’s tracked-height estimate in centimetres, and F is the saved floor correction in centimetres. For example, H = 176, T = 134, and F = 0 gives S = 42 centimetres.

When standing mode is false, the player-settings update copies this value into the player controller’s stored seated offset. Standing mode true makes that cached offset zero without erasing the saved seated value. A new settings object starts with 42 centimetres.

The adjustment buttons change it by 1 centimetre. The setter only stores the value; the inspected Control_Player methods cache it without directly moving the headset or rig. It is not a guaranteed eye-height change at the instant of assignment.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SaveData.PlayerSettings.PlayerHeight
member.summary: Stores the player’s measured standing height in centimetres for body calibration.

remarks.para: For example, 176 means 176 centimetres, or 1.76 metres. A new settings object starts at 176. Applying body settings multiplies this value by 0.01 before giving it to the body-calibration setup in metres.

Calibration uses the real height compared with the hidden calibration avatar’s height to scale the headset/controller tracking space for the currently worn avatar. It also adjusts the torso measurements into the calibration avatar’s scale. This is the real player’s size, not a command to make every avatar exactly that tall.

The normal height buttons move by 1 centimetre and check 90 and 244 centimetres before stepping. The automatic height guess uses its own limits of 90–228 centimetres. These menu checks are not clamps in this property’s setter; direct assignments are stored unchanged and do not immediately recalibrate.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SaveData.PlayerSettings.RightHanded
member.summary: Stores the handedness preference copied to the player’s controller rig.

remarks.para: True selects the right-handed preference; false selects the left-handed preference. Applying body settings copies the flag to the rig that reads the hand controls. Controller-relative movement then uses the opposite-hand controller as its forward reference: left for right-handed, right for left-handed.

The settings update selects the movement reference before copying the new flag. Switching this preference while controller-relative movement is active can therefore leave that reference using the old hand until it is selected again. The belt side and BodyLog side are separate saved choices; changing this property does not automatically change those choices.
Assigning this property only changes the saved-settings object in memory. The game applies the choice through its player-settings update; writing the save file is a separate step.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SaveData.PlayerSettings.Standing
member.summary: Stores whether body setup uses standing or seated mode.

remarks.para: True means standing; false means seated. When the player controller applies the settings, it stores zero as the active seated offset in standing mode and copies the saved seated correction in seated mode. That correction is in centimetres, and the saved value is retained when standing is selected.

For example, a saved seated correction of 42 centimetres remains available after switching to standing and back. This flag records the chosen setup; it is not a live sensor reading that detects whether the player is physically sitting. The property setter alone does not apply the setup.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SaveData.PlayerSettings.TooltipsEnabled
member.summary: Stores whether the game should enable its tutorial hints and menu tooltips.

remarks.para: True requests hints on; false requests them off. At player-controller startup, the game applies this value to the tutorial rig’s whole object, which contains the controller hint displays. Applying body settings also copies the flag to the menu’s tooltip option.

The menu’s tooltip button uses the player controller’s tooltip setter, which updates the saved flag, enables or disables the tutorial object, and updates the menu flag. Directly assigning this PlayerSettings property only stores the choice and does not toggle those existing objects.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SaveData.PlayerSettings.UnderbustCircumference
member.summary: Stores the distance around the player’s torso just below the chest in metres for body calibration.

remarks.para: Circumference means the full distance around the body, as measured with a tape, rather than its width from side to side. For example, 1.00 means 100 centimetres around this part of the body.

Applying body settings copies this measurement to the body setup, which estimates the torso’s width and front-to-back depth on the hidden calibration avatar. That avatar is the model used as a ruler for the player’s real body proportions. Before estimating its shape, the game divides the saved circumference by the ratio of the player’s measured height to the calibration avatar’s height; both heights are in metres.

The measurement menu adjusts this value by 0.01 metre per button press and marks the measurements as custom. Choosing a shirt-size preset recalculates it. The property setter itself does not clamp the value or rebuild the body.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SaveData.PlayerSettings.VolumeGlobal
member.summary: Stores the master audio setting on the game’s 0–10 menu scale.

remarks.para: This number is a menu level, not a direct loudness multiplier or percentage. The menu changes it by 1, normally between 0 and 10; a new settings object starts at 8. Applying player settings passes it to the master mixer control. A mixer combines and adjusts sound channels.

For nonnegative levels, the mixer calculates d = 90 × sqrt(v / 10) − 80. Here v is this saved menu level with no physical unit, sqrt means square root, and d is the channel gain in decibels, a scale for making audio louder or quieter. Level 0 gives −80 decibels and level 10 gives +10 decibels. Level 8 gives about +0.50 decibels. Level 0 is a very low gain, not a mathematical zero-amplitude guarantee.

The menu applies the mixer change and copies its audio choices back into the save data. Directly assigning this property only stores the value; it does not change the live mixer or limit the value to 0–10. Negative levels are outside the square-root calculation’s normal range.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SaveData.PlayerSettings.VolumeMusic

remarks.para: This number is a menu level, not a direct loudness multiplier or percentage. The menu changes it by 1, normally between 0 and 10; a new settings object starts at 8. Applying player settings passes it to the music mixer control. A mixer combines and adjusts sound channels.

For nonnegative levels, the mixer calculates d = 90 × sqrt(v / 10) − 80. Here v is this saved menu level with no physical unit, sqrt means square root, and d is the channel gain in decibels, a scale for making audio louder or quieter. Level 0 gives −80 decibels and level 10 gives +10 decibels. Level 8 gives about +0.50 decibels. Level 0 is a very low gain, not a mathematical zero-amplitude guarantee.

The menu applies the mixer change and copies its audio choices back into the save data. Directly assigning this property only stores the value; it does not change the live mixer or limit the value to 0–10. Negative levels are outside the square-root calculation’s normal range.

For nonnegative levels, the mixer calculates d = 90 × sqrt(v / 10) − 80.
