Level 0 gives −80 decibels and level 10 gives +10 decibels. Level 8 gives about +0.50 decibels. Level 0 is a very low gain, not a mathematical zero-amplitude guarantee.

The menu applies the mixer change and copies its audio choices back into the save data. Directly assigning this property only stores the value; it does not change the live mixer or limit the value to 0–10. Negative levels are outside the square-root calculation’s normal range.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SaveData.PlayerSettings.WaistCircumference
member.summary: Stores the distance around the player’s waist in metres for body calibration.

remarks.para: Circumference means the full distance around the body, as measured with a tape, rather than its width from side to side. For example, 1.00 means 100 centimetres around this part of the body.

Applying body settings copies this measurement to the body setup, which estimates the torso’s width and front-to-back depth on the hidden calibration avatar. That avatar is the model used as a ruler for the player’s real body proportions. Before estimating its shape, the game divides the saved circumference by the ratio of the player’s measured height to the calibration avatar’s height; both heights are in metres.

The measurement menu adjusts this value by 0.01 metre per button press and marks the measurements as custom. Choosing a shirt-size preset recalculates it. The property setter itself does not clamp the value or rebuild the body.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SaveData.PlayerSettings.WingspanLength
member.summary: Stores the player’s distance from one fingertip to the other with both arms spread in metres.

remarks.para: For example, 1.80 means a wingspan of 180 centimetres. The measurement menu displays centimetres by multiplying the saved value by 100 and changes it by 0.01 metre per press.

Choosing a preset recalculates this length from the saved height and the menu’s configured proportion. Manually changing it selects custom measurements. Applying body settings copies the length to the body setup and passes it, together with the player’s height in metres, to the calibration avatar.

The calibration avatar’s method for this length has an empty body in this build. This inspected calibration path therefore stores and displays the measurement without changing arm or leg proportions through that method. The property setter also performs no clamp or recalibration.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ScrollButton.button
member.summary: Caches the whose press permission this component checks and updates.

remarks.para: A Button is Unity's clickable UI component. Awake, Unity's first setup call for this component, finds the Button on the same scene object and stores it here. The required-component attribute expects that Button to exist. Setting this field before Awake can be overwritten by that lookup.

Press handling checks whether this cached button is interactable, meaning it is allowed to accept presses. The scroll-boundary handlers disable that permission when the scrollbar's value rounds to the directional endpoint, or when a content-change check finds its handle fills the whole track. Disabling also cancels repeated scrolling and stops this component's animation coroutines, routines that resume across frames.

Changing the cached reference redirects later permission checks and changes to another Button. It does not attach this component's pointer handlers to that other scene object or enable its scene object. The scrollbar and container event connections are made separately during Start, Unity's startup call.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ScrollButton.direction
member.summary: Chooses the startup sign of the scrolling step and which scrollbar endpoint disables the button.

remarks.para: UP has value 0 and DOWN has value 1. Start, Unity's startup call, sets signedStepSize to stepSize for UP and to -stepSize for DOWN. A positive stepSize therefore increases the scrollbar value for UP and decreases it for DOWN. The value normally ranges from 0 to 1 across the scrollbar's travel. This field changes the numeric movement sign and endpoint check; this class does not decide how a connected view displays that value.

Boundary checks read direction live: UP disables the button when the value rounded to two decimal places is approximately 1, and DOWN does so near 0. Disabling cancels repetition and animation. Changing direction after Start changes those checks without recalculating signedStepSize, so the stopping endpoint and actual movement sign can disagree until you update the cached step too.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ScrollButton.incremental
member.summary: Chooses one animated step per press or repeated animated moves while the button is held.

remarks.para: When true, pointer-down stops this component's existing animations and starts one move from the current scrollbar value to that value plus signedStepSize. signedStepSize is the startup copy of stepSize, negated for DOWN; values normally measure fractions of the scrollbar's 0-to-1 travel. This mode is animated rather than an immediate jump.

When false, pointer-down schedules ScrollContent repeatedly, starting with no requested delay and using scrollFrequency as the repeat interval in seconds. Each repeat cancels the previous animation, calculates a target from the current value plus signedStepSize multiplied by the scrollbar handle size rounded to two decimal places, clamps that target to 0 through 1, and starts the older SmoothScrolling routine. Handle size is the fraction of the scrollbar track occupied by its handle.

Both paths pass scrollFrequency as an animation time setting. The one-step path honors that positive duration through the refactored routine; the older repeated path has the duration-calculation bug described in SmoothScrolling. Release schedules stopping about 0.2 seconds later, and endpoint checks can stop work sooner. The constructor sets incremental to true, but a saved scene configuration can replace that value. Changing the flag only affects later presses; it does not convert work already running.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ScrollButton.scrollElementsContainer
member.summary: Connects this button to notifications that the scrollable container's direct children have changed.

remarks.para: The container is a scene component that announces when a child object is added, removed, or reparented. Start, Unity's startup call, registers HandleScrollViewChanged with its OnContainerChildrenChanged action. A callback is a function called when such a notification happens.

That callback checks the assigned scrollbar: a handle size approximately 1 means the handle fills the track, so scrolling is unnecessary. It also checks the current value, rounded to two decimal places, against 1 for UP or 0 for DOWN. It enables the button away from the stopping boundary, or disables it and cancels scrolling at the boundary.

Assign this container and the scrollbar before Start. Replacing this field later does not automatically remove the callback from the old container or register it with the new one. Destruction removes the callback from the container currently stored here. The container notification itself does not recalculate the list layout; the button reads the scrollbar values present when it is notified.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ScrollButton.scrollFrequency
member.summary: Supplies the animation duration and, for held-button repetition, the repeat interval in seconds of game time.

remarks.para: Use a positive value. In incremental mode, each press captures scrollFrequency as the duration for one refactored animation, measured in seconds of game time. Unity's time-scale setting can make game time pass faster or slower than real time, or pause it at zero. For example, 0.25 requests a quarter-second move in game time, with completion occurring on frame updates rather than at an exact wall-clock instant.

When incremental is false, the press also captures this value as the interval between scheduled ScrollContent calls. A value of 0.25 requests four calls per second of game time after the initial zero-delay call. Each repeat starts a new animation from the then-current scrollbar value and cancels the previous animation; it also reads the current scrollFrequency for the older routine's time setting, whose arithmetic does not honor that duration as intended.

Changing the field does not change the captured duration of an animation already running or the interval of an existing repeat schedule. Later presses and repeat-created animations read the new value. A larger interval means fewer repeat requests per second of game time, not more. Actual calls and writes depend on Unity's frame timing and time scale.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ScrollButton.scrollbar
member.summary: Holds the UI scrollbar whose position these button animations write and whose state controls press permission.

remarks.para: A scrollbar has a position value normally running from 0 to 1 across its travel, and a size giving the fraction of the track occupied by the handle. Assign the scrollbar connected to your scrollable view. This component writes that value; the view's own connection determines how the visible content responds. These units are fractions rather than pixels or meters.

Start, Unity's startup call, subscribes to the scrollbar's value-change event. An event calls registered callbacks, functions notified when its value changes. This button's callback rechecks its permission: UP stops near value 1 and DOWN near 0 after rounding to two decimal places; container-change notifications also disable it when handle size is approximately 1.

The direct incremental path and refactored animation do not clamp target values to 0 through 1, and the native scrollbar setter can store values outside that range. The held-repeat path clamps its target explicitly. If the scrollbar has more than one configured step, its reported value is rounded to those positions, so observed changes can be discrete.

Assign this reference before Start. Changing it later redirects animation writes and state reads without moving the old value-change subscription to the replacement. On destruction, the component calls RemoveAllListeners on the currently assigned scrollbar's change event, which can remove callbacks registered by other scripts too.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ScrollButton.signedStepSize
member.summary: Stores the cached increase or decrease in scrollbar position used to form later scrolling targets.

remarks.para: Start, Unity's startup call, copies stepSize here and negates it when direction is DOWN. For a positive stepSize of 0.1, UP stores 0.1 and DOWN stores -0.1. The unit is a fraction of the scrollbar's usual 0-to-1 travel, not pixels or meters.

The one-step path targets current value + signedStepSize without a target clamp. The repeated path targets current value + signedStepSize × rounded handle size, then clamps the target from 0 to 1. Current value is the scrollbar position at that move's start; rounded handle size is the fraction of its track filled by the handle, rounded to two decimal places. For current 0.4, signed step 0.1 and rounded size 0.2, the targets are 0.5 and 0.42 respectively.

Changing stepSize or direction after Start does not recalculate this field. Writing signedStepSize directly changes later targets without changing those settings. An animation already running keeps its captured endpoints; the next press or repeat reads the updated step.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ScrollButton.stepSize
member.summary: Configures the base scrollbar-position change that is copied into the signed step during startup.

remarks.para: Values measure fractions of the scrollbar's usual 0-to-1 travel. For example, stepSize = 0.1 means a base change of one tenth of that range. Start, Unity's startup call, copies it to signedStepSize for UP and copies its negative for DOWN. A negative stepSize reverses that normal sign; it is not converted to an absolute size.

With incremental true, a press animates toward the current value plus that cached signed step. With incremental false, repeated moves multiply the cached step by the scrollbar handle-size fraction rounded to two decimal places before forming their clamped target. For a base step 0.1 and rounded handle size 0.2, the repeated target change is 0.02.

Changing stepSize after Start leaves signedStepSize unchanged, so later movement keeps using the old cached amount unless you update that field too. The step is not a speed or duration; scrollFrequency supplies those animation and repetition time settings.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.ScrollElementsContainer.OnContainerChildrenChanged
member.summary: Holds the listener routines called when Unity reports a change to this container’s child list.

remarks.para: A callback is a routine called when a notification occurs. Each routine here takes no arguments and returns no result. Because this notification supplies no changed child or item count, a listener that needs those details must read the current hierarchy or keep its own item data.

OnTransformChildrenChanged reads this field and calls it directly if assigned. Assigning a different routine changes the next notification’s listeners; it does not immediately send a notification. Use += to add a listener while preserving those already registered, and -= to remove it. Assigning with = replaces the current listener list.

At startup, ScrollButton adds its scroll-state refresh listener to the referenced container. During destruction, ScrollButton removes its scroll-state refresh listener from the container it currently references if its scrollbar and scrollbar event are still present. For example, an additional listener could rebuild your displayed item list when a child is added, while keeping the button’s existing refresh listener.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SecurityCamera.cameraFlashSFX
member.summary: Chooses the sound recording requested when the camera indicates a save.

remarks.para: An AudioClip is a recorded sound asset. The save-effect sequence samples this AudioClip and requests playback at the world position of the Unity scene object that holds this SecurityCamera, rather than at cameraRb’s position. It requests volume 0.3, a unitless playback level, base pitch 1, a normal-speed playback-rate multiplier, and minDistance 2 metres, the near-distance setting within which getting closer no longer makes the sound louder.

The audio helper applies slow-motion pitch adjustment: a Time.timeScale of 0.5, meaning half-speed game time, changes base pitch 1 to 0.625. Changing the clip selects the recording for the next request; assigning the field does not start playback.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SecurityCamera.cameraMoveSpeed
member.summary: Controls how quickly the camera’s blend from a captured starting rotation reaches its stored target.

remarks.para: This is a blend rate per second, rather than a fixed number of degrees per second. The blend fraction is timeTick × cameraMoveSpeed × lerpTime: timeTick is elapsed seconds accumulated on a clock weighted by game time, and lerpTime is the unitless alignment weight calculated when a new target is accepted.

For an unchanged target and a positive alignment weight, increasing this value makes the blend reach its target sooner. Zero keeps the captured starting rotation. The rotation-blending operation clamps its fraction between 0 and 1, where 0 is the start and 1 is the target.

The clock adds Time.deltaTime, the already game-scaled seconds since the previous frame, multiplied again by Time.timeScale, Unity’s unitless game-time rate with 1 meaning normal speed. A newly accepted target resets the clock before rotation is requested, so frequent aim resets can prevent progress despite a large speed value.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SecurityCamera.cameraRb
member.summary: Chooses the simulated physics body whose world rotation is driven to face the scene’s main-view camera.

remarks.para: A Rigidbody is a body controlled by Unity’s physics simulation. On each valid pass, Unity’s per-frame tracking method Update reads this body’s world position to find the direction toward Camera.main, Unity’s enabled camera marked MainCamera, and uses MoveRotation to request a blended world rotation.

This tracking code changes orientation rather than moving the body to a target position. OnEntityUncull also uses this reference to seed the next aim. Supply a valid body for those paths; if no main-view camera exists, Update returns without tracking.

The save sound uses the world position of the Unity scene object carrying this SecurityCamera; it does not use the scene object carrying the selected Rigidbody. Changing cameraRb changes the tracking body without changing the sound position.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SecurityCamera.cameraUpdateDot
member.summary: Sets how far the desired aim must change before a new target rotation is accepted.

remarks.para: The test compares the stored goal’s forward direction with a fresh direction from cameraRb’s world position toward Camera.main, Unity’s enabled camera marked MainCamera. It does not compare the body’s actual facing with the target. The unitless direction dot product is 1 for the same direction, 0 for a right angle and −1 for opposite directions.

A new target is accepted when that dot is strictly less than this threshold, or when firstLoop requests the initial refresh. Higher thresholds respond to smaller changes; lower thresholds allow larger changes before resetting the target. For example, 0.95 corresponds to an aim change greater than about 18.2 degrees.

Accepting a target captures the current body rotation as the blend’s start and resets its timer. This field is not clamped by Update; a threshold above 1 can reset the blend every valid frame and prevent it from advancing.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SecurityCamera.entity
member.summary: Supplies the whose culling notifications tell this camera to prepare a fresh aim.

remarks.para: A MarrowEntity groups a game object’s physics and lifecycle processing. Culling is its temporary inactivity processing. Awake, Unity’s initialization callback, registers this camera with the assigned entity; a callback is a routine called to perform or report an action.

Reset, Unity’s editor setup/reset routine, tries to find a MarrowEntity on the same Unity scene object this camera is attached to; it does not search parent or child objects. Awake requires a valid assigned entity and does not perform that lookup itself.

Replacing this field after Awake does not unregister the camera from the old entity or register it with the new one. OnEntityUncull uses the notification to refresh aiming; this camera’s OnEntityCull body is empty.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SecurityCamera.firstLoop
member.summary: Forces the next valid tracking update to accept a fresh target even if the aim-change threshold has not been crossed.

remarks.para: The constructor and OnEntityUncull set this flag true. Unity’s per-frame tracking method Update clears it when it accepts a target, captures the current camera-body world rotation, resets timeTick, the rotation-blend clock, and calculates a new lerpTime alignment weight.

It is a pending-refresh flag rather than a check that this is the first frame of every activation. If Camera.main, Unity’s enabled camera marked MainCamera, is missing, Update returns without clearing it. Setting it true requests the refresh on a later valid Update.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SecurityCamera.flashActiveTime
member.summary: Sets the game-time delay before the save indicator hides its flash cone.

remarks.para: The sequence reads this value in seconds after starting sound, particles and renderer material changes. For example, 0.2 requests a delay of 0.2 game-time seconds. Slow motion makes the game clock advance more slowly, so the same interval lasts longer in real time.

Only flashCone is hidden after normal completion. This value does not schedule a particle Stop command, limit the audio clip’s length or restore materials. Once a request has sampled the duration, later edits affect subsequent requests rather than rescheduling that wait.

Use a nonnegative duration; the delay helper rejects a negative interval. Each save-indicator request waits separately, so an earlier request can hide the cone before a newer request’s interval ends. Destroying the Unity scene object that holds this camera cancels its pending delay.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SecurityCamera.flashCone
member.summary: Chooses the Unity scene object shown at save-indicator start and hidden after its delay finishes.

remarks.para: This reference points to a Unity scene object; activating it enables that object and its contents. The sequence activates it before playing particles, then hides the current reference after flashActiveTime game-time seconds. Slow motion makes that clock run more slowly, extending the interval in real time.

Supply a valid object for both operations. If the reference is replaced during a wait, completion hides the newly stored object rather than remembering the original one. Separate requests can overlap, and an earlier completion can hide the cone while a later request is still waiting.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SecurityCamera.goalRot
member.summary: Stores the world-space target orientation used to turn the camera’s physics body toward the main-view camera.

remarks.para: A Quaternion represents orientation with four components rather than three axis angles in degrees. Unity’s per-frame tracking method Update calculates a fresh orientation whose forward axis points from cameraRb’s world position toward Camera.main, Unity’s enabled camera marked MainCamera.

The stored target is replaced only when its aim-change threshold is crossed or firstLoop requests a refresh. OnEntityUncull also seeds it when a main-view camera exists. Update blends from lastGoalRot, the captured starting body orientation, toward this target and requests that world rotation with MoveRotation.

A manual assignment changes the stored target, but a later accepted automatic aim can overwrite it. The threshold compares this target’s direction with the newly desired direction, rather than measuring the body’s remaining turn.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SecurityCamera.goalVec
member.summary: Stores a vector that this camera’s inspected tracking routines do not use.

remarks.para: Unity’s per-frame tracking method Update calculates its aim directly from cameraRb’s world position and Camera.main’s world position. Neither Update nor OnEntityUncull reads or writes goalVec; the inspected setup and save-effect routines do not use it either.

Changing this value alone changes stored data without changing the aim or moving the camera in those routines. No position-versus-direction meaning or coordinate frame is established for this unused value by those paths.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SecurityCamera.lastGoalRot
member.summary: Stores the camera body’s captured starting world orientation for the current rotation blend.

remarks.para: When Unity’s per-frame tracking method Update accepts a new aim, it reads the current world rotation of the Unity scene object carrying cameraRb into this field. It then blends from this captured orientation toward goalRot, the stored target orientation. The field is not a snapshot of the previous desired target.

A Quaternion is a four-component orientation representation rather than three axis angles in degrees. Assigning a different starting orientation affects the blend until a later accepted target captures the actual body orientation again.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SecurityCamera.lastoffsetDot
member.summary: Stores a number that is unused by this camera’s inspected aim and save routines.

remarks.para: Unity’s per-frame tracking method Update writes offsetDot, the unitless comparison between the stored target direction and the newly desired direction, but it does not read or write lastoffsetDot. OnEntityUncull and the inspected setup and save-effect routines do not use this field either.
Changing it does not smooth tracking or alter the target in those routines. No previous-frame sample, units or external use is established by this inspected code.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SecurityCamera.lerpTime
member.summary: Stores the unitless alignment weight that scales the camera’s rotation-blend progress.

remarks.para: When a new aim is accepted, Unity’s per-frame tracking method Update calculates this as Clamp01((offsetDot + 1) / 2). offsetDot is the unitless dot product between the old target direction and the newly desired direction, with 1 meaning equal directions, 0 a right angle and −1 opposite directions. Clamp01 limits the calculated value between 0 and 1.
For example, an offsetDot of 0 produces a weight of 0.5; −1 produces 0. This is a cached multiplier rather than elapsed time. It stays unchanged until another target is accepted.

The blend fraction is lerpTime × timeTick × cameraMoveSpeed: timeTick is the elapsed seconds on the camera’s game-time-weighted blend clock, and cameraMoveSpeed is its blend rate per second. A zero weight prevents that blend from advancing until the weight or target-refresh calculation changes.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SecurityCamera.material
member.summary: Chooses the surface appearance assigned to each listed renderer when save indication starts.

remarks.para: A Material controls how a mesh surface is drawn, such as its colour, texture and shading. After starting the cone and particles, the save sequence assigns this material through each renderer’s single-material setter. The setup assumes one material per renderer; it does not iterate a renderer’s material-slot array.

The previous materials are not saved or restored after the cone’s delay. Changing this field affects later assignments during another save-indicator request; it does not apply the material immediately just by changing the reference.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SecurityCamera.offsetDot
member.summary: Reports the unitless direction comparison used to decide whether the camera needs a fresh aim.

remarks.para: On each valid pass, Unity’s per-frame tracking method Update compares goalRot’s forward direction, the stored target direction, with a newly calculated direction from cameraRb toward Camera.main, Unity’s enabled camera marked MainCamera. A dot product of 1 means those directions match, 0 means a right angle and −1 means opposite directions.

This comparison concerns the old target, not the camera body’s actual facing. It is calculated before a target refresh, so after a refresh the cached number can still describe the comparison that caused that refresh.

If it is strictly below cameraUpdateDot, the configured aim-change threshold, or firstLoop is true, the routine accepts a new target and derives lerpTime, its unitless alignment weight, from this number. Manual changes are overwritten by the next valid Update.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SecurityCamera.particles
member.summary: Chooses the particle system started when the camera indicates a save.

remarks.para: A ParticleSystem emits small visual elements for effects such as a flash or sparks. The save sequence calls Play after activating flashCone and before changing renderer materials; assigning this field does not play it by itself.

The camera sequence never calls Stop after its delay. The system’s configured emission, looping and particle lifetimes affect visibility; hiding flashCone can also hide these effects if their object is placed beneath it. flashActiveTime controls hiding the separate cone object, rather than a stop command for this system. Supply a valid reference for the save sequence.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SecurityCamera.renderers
member.summary: Selects the mesh surfaces whose material changes when save indication begins.

remarks.para: Each MeshRenderer draws an assigned mesh. The save sequence walks this array and assigns material, the surface appearance asset controlling colour, texture and shading, through each renderer’s single-material setter. The setup assumes each renderer has one material that can be replaced; the code does not walk multiple material slots.
The array must exist, and every listed renderer must be valid. An empty array makes no surface changes. Only the supplied array is used; the sequence does not search for other renderers.

These assignments happen after the cone and particles start and before the delay begins. They are not reversed when the cone is hidden. Editing the list changes the surfaces affected by a later request rather than applying or undoing a swap immediately.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SecurityCamera.timeTick
member.summary: Stores elapsed seconds on the camera’s weighted clock for blending toward the current target rotation.

remarks.para: Unity’s per-frame tracking method Update resets this to zero when a new aim is accepted. It uses the current value for the rotation request, then adds Time.deltaTime × Time.timeScale. Time.deltaTime is the already game-scaled seconds since the previous frame; Time.timeScale is Unity’s unitless game-time rate, with 1 meaning normal speed.

Because the clock multiplies an already scaled interval by that rate again, steady half-speed game time makes it advance at about one quarter of the normal real-time rate. With no main-view camera, Update returns before advancing this value.

The blend fraction is timeTick × cameraMoveSpeed × lerpTime: cameraMoveSpeed is the blend rate per second, and lerpTime is the cached unitless alignment weight. Changing the clock changes blend progress until a later accepted target resets it; it is not a separate timer for save effects or scanning to another position.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SimpleGripEvents.Grips
member.summary: The grab points whose attach, release, and held-input notifications run this component’s events.

remarks.para: Assign the array before Awake, Unity's initialization callback, runs. Awake connects each listed grip's attach, release, and held-input notifications to this component's three callback methods; these connections are called subscriptions. OnDestroy, called when the component is destroyed, removes those connections from the array it finds at that time. Empty arrays monitor nothing; a null array or null entry is not skipped safely.

Changing the array after Awake does not transfer subscriptions to the new grips and can prevent cleanup of the old ones. Listing the same grip twice adds duplicate callbacks. All listed grips share the same leftHand and rightHand flags.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SimpleGripEvents.OnAttach
member.summary: Actions run when a hand grabs a monitored grip, subject to the two-hand suppression option.

remarks.para: This UnityEvent is a configurable list of function calls and receives no hand or grip argument. For example, connect an action to turn on an object’s light when it is picked up.

With doNotRetriggerOnMultiGirp off, every attach callback runs the event. With it on, only an attachment received while both hand flags are false runs it. The arriving hand’s flag is set after the event runs.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SimpleGripEvents.OnDetach
member.summary: Actions run when a hand releases a monitored grip, subject to the two-hand suppression option.

remarks.para: This UnityEvent receives no arguments. With doNotRetriggerOnMultiGirp off, every detach callback runs it. With the option on, the releasing hand’s flag is cleared and the event runs only when both hand flags are false.
For an object held in both hands, enabling the option keeps a release action, such as turning its light off, from running when only the first hand lets go.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SimpleGripEvents.OnIndexDown
member.summary: Actions run when an attached hand starts pressing its index trigger.

remarks.para: This UnityEvent receives no arguments. It uses Hand.GetIndexButtonDown’s cached press flag, rather than the continuous trigger amount or the grip squeeze used to hold an object. The hand suppresses this input if the trigger was already held when attaching; release it and press again to produce a new press.

Either attached hand can run the event. doNotRetriggerOnMultiGirp does not suppress input events. The callback does not clear the cached press flag after running the event, so repeated update calls while that flag stays true can run the event again.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SimpleGripEvents.OnMenuTapDown
member.summary: Actions run when an attached hand’s controller reports a short menu-button tap.

remarks.para: This UnityEvent receives no arguments. Despite Down in the name, the audited OpenController creates its tap when the B/menu input is released less than 0.2 seconds after it was pressed. The measurement uses real time, so slowing the game does not lengthen that threshold. The physical button mapping can differ between controller types.

The normal OpenController tap processing requires ControllerRig.IsMenuTapDisabled to be false. This component reads GetMenuTap, rather than the separate application-menu press. Either attached hand can run it, and doNotRetriggerOnMultiGirp does not suppress it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SimpleGripEvents.doNotRetriggerOnMultiGirp
member.summary: Groups grab and release actions so a two-hand hold starts with the first hand and ends when the last hand releases.

remarks.para: For example, left-hand attach runs OnAttach, right-hand attach does not run it again, left-hand release does not run OnDetach, and right-hand release runs OnDetach. This assumes the recorded flags begin clear and the corresponding notifications arrive.

When false, each attach or detach callback runs its event and does not maintain the hand flags. Set the option before grabbing; switching it on during a hold does not rebuild which hands are already attached. The flags are shared across all Grips and store one yes/no value per hand, rather than counting individual grip attachments.
This option affects only OnAttach and OnDetach. It does not change OnIndexDown or OnMenuTapDown, and it does not prevent either hand from physically grabbing the object.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SimpleGripEvents.leftHand
member.summary: Recorded left-hand hold state used to suppress repeated grab and release actions.

remarks.para: This flag updates only while doNotRetriggerOnMultiGirp is true. A left-hand attach sets it after OnAttach runs; a left-hand release clears it before checking whether OnDetach should run. It is shared across the whole Grips array.
When the option is false, the flag can stay stale and is not a reliable live attachment query. Changing it alters event suppression without attaching or releasing a real hand.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SimpleGripEvents.rightHand
member.summary: Recorded right-hand hold state used to suppress repeated grab and release actions.

remarks.para: This flag updates only while doNotRetriggerOnMultiGirp is true. A right-hand attach sets it after OnAttach runs; a right-hand release clears it before checking whether OnDetach should run. It is shared across the whole Grips array.
When the option is false, the flag can stay stale and is not a reliable live attachment query. Changing it alters event suppression without attaching or releasing a real hand.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SmoothFollower.RotationalSmoothTime
member.summary: Scales the current frame interval to control how gradually the follower turns toward the target.

remarks.para: This is a unitless multiplier. MoveCameraUpdate passes RotationalSmoothTime × Time.deltaTime as the rotation smoother's response interval in seconds, where Time.deltaTime is the current frame interval in scaled game time. For example, 0.15 with a 0.02-second frame supplies 0.003 seconds; with a 0.01-second frame it supplies 0.0015 seconds. Setting 0.15 does not request a fixed 0.15-second turn.

With a positive frame interval, larger positive values give a more gradual response and smaller values approach the target more quickly. Each quaternion component, one of the four numbers representing rotation, is smoothed using the remembered rate in quatVel. The result is normalized, meaning its four numbers are rescaled to unit length so they can represent a rotation.

The constructor starts this multiplier at 0.15, but saved scene settings can replace it. It is read on each follow step, so changing it affects later steps without enabling the component again. The frame interval follows the scaled game clock; frame timing and slow motion can change the supplied interval. There is no fixed real-time completion deadline.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SmoothFollower.TranslationSmoothTime
member.summary: Scales the current frame interval to control how gradually the follower moves toward the target.

remarks.para: This is a unitless multiplier. MoveCameraUpdate passes TranslationSmoothTime × Time.deltaTime as the position smoother's response interval in seconds, where Time.deltaTime is the current frame interval in scaled game time. For example, 0.15 with a 0.02-second frame supplies 0.003 seconds; with a 0.01-second frame it supplies 0.0015 seconds. Setting 0.15 does not request a fixed 0.15-second move.

With a positive frame interval, larger positive values give a more gradual response and smaller values approach the target more quickly. The smoother also reads and updates velocity, its remembered world-axis movement rate in Unity world units per scaled game-time second. That rate is in meters per second only if this scene uses one Unity unit per meter. Its response interval is an approximate setting, not an exact arrival time; a moving target can keep the follower catching up.

The constructor starts this multiplier at 0.15, but saved scene settings can replace it. Each follow step reads the current value. The frame interval follows the scaled game clock; frame timing and slow motion can change the supplied interval. No maximum movement speed is configured by this field.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SmoothFollower.quatVel
member.summary: Remembers the rotation-component rates that shape the follower's next smoothed turn.

remarks.para: A quaternion is Unity's four-number representation of a rotation. quatVel holds the rate of change of those four numbers, in component units per scaled game-time second. It is not a three-axis angular speed in degrees per second and is not another target rotation.

The rotation smoother reads and updates all four rates while approaching the target, normalizes the resulting rotation, and removes the part of the rate that would change the quaternion's length rather than its direction. That preserves useful turning history between follow steps.

For example, after the target changes its facing, these remembered rates affect the next turn as well as the current and target rotations. Disabling and re-enabling the component changes its callback registration but does not reset quatVel, so that history can survive an interruption. Editing this state changes the calculation; it does not directly rotate the object.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SmoothFollower.targetTransform
member.summary: Supplies the current world position and rotation that this object approaches on each follow step.

remarks.para: A transform stores an object's position, rotation and scale. The follower reads this target's position and rotation in the whole level's coordinates, not relative to the target's parent. It smooths its own transform toward those values with no separate offset and leaves its own scale unchanged.

For example, you can assign a separate camera target that moves with the player; the follower will catch up to that target's position and facing. If you want an offset, place the target transform at the desired offset. Changing this reference affects the next follow step and keeps the existing velocity and quatVel smoothing history.

Assign a valid target before the active follower updates. The update does not silently skip an unassigned target while active. The component also needs the player's camera-update references ready when it enables so it can register its update callback, a saved function called when that signal fires.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SmoothFollower.velocity
member.summary: Remembers the world-axis movement rate that shapes the follower's next smoothed position update.

remarks.para: The three components are Unity world units per scaled game-time second along the level's X, Y and Z axes. They are meters per second only if this scene uses one Unity unit per meter. MoveCameraUpdate passes velocity by reference to the position smoother, meaning the smoother can update this same stored value as it calculates the next position. It uses the remembered rate together with the current position, target position and response interval.

For example, a positive X component represents remembered movement toward positive world X. Changing the target can leave an existing movement rate for the next step to adjust. This value belongs to the follow calculation; it is not a reading of a Rigidbody's physical velocity, which is the speed of an object simulated by Unity physics.

Each active follow step can change velocity. Disabling or re-enabling this component does not clear it, so the calculation can retain movement history across that interruption. Editing it affects later smoothing steps rather than moving the transform immediately.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SpawnGun.ColorTint
member.summary: Identifies the _ColorTint shader color used to tint the placement bounds lines.

remarks.para: A shader is the drawing code used by a material, the collection of appearance settings for a rendered surface. This ID names the color setting that the line shader can read.

The held update writes the same interpolated validity color to each placerPreviewBoundsLines material through this property. It is a numeric Shader.PropertyToID result, not a Color and not the gun-body mode tint.
The line material shader must use _ColorTint for the assignment to change its appearance.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SpawnGun.EmissionColor
member.summary: Identifies the _EmissionColor shader color used by the gun display and main placement preview.

remarks.para: A material supplies a rendered surface's appearance settings, and a shader is the drawing code that uses them. This numeric ID names an emission-color setting; the assigned shader determines how that setting changes the appearance.
The held update reads/writes this property on material slot 1 of gunBodyRenderers for the mode screen transition, and on placerPreivewRenderer.material for the placement-validity transition.
It is a cached numeric shader property ID, not an emission strength or stored color. targetScreenColor and targetColor provide the colors for those separate transitions.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SpawnGun.FlashCoroutine
member.summary: Identifies the _FlashCoroutine shader float animated by the display flash.

remarks.para: A coroutine is a sequence that continues over frames. The shader is the drawing code for a material, which supplies appearance settings. Here game time follows game speed and pausing. CoFireFlash uses curve input u = 4 × elapsed game seconds, where 4 has units per game second and u is unitless: fireCurve is evaluated through u = 1, then returnCurve receives the continuing u above 1. Each curve maps input to a numeric flash-progress output; that output is clamped to 0 through 1 and subtracted from 1 for the shader float.

Despite its name, this is a numeric shader property ID, not a running coroutine handle. CoFireFlash writes it on material slot 1 of each gunBodyRenderers entry using a configured 0.5-second game-time threshold. It writes before testing accumulated time, so a frame that crosses the threshold can be followed by one final write; its actual elapsed duration depends on frame sampling.
The written value is 1 minus the clamped curve result. Setting this property ID does not start, stop or track a coroutine; FlashScreen starts the animation.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SpawnGun._hitInfo
member.summary: Stores the latest aim-ray hit used for placement calculations and removal targeting.

remarks.para: A raycast tests an invisible straight line against colliders, the shapes used for collision queries. Its normal is a direction pointing away from the hit surface. The actual line starts at firePointTransform's world position and follows its forward direction: that Transform holds the gun's muzzle position and orientation. A Rigidbody is Unity's physics body for simulated movement and rotation.

While the trigger is held in Spawner mode, the attached update raycasts from firePoint using effectiveRange and collisionLayers and uses the hit point/normal to position the preview. On trigger release it raycasts again before requesting base Gun.Fire.

The hit point and normal are in world space. Remover OnFire uses the hit collider's attached Rigidbody to locate a whole Marrow entity. This is a cached result, not a continuously refreshed target; invoking OnFire directly uses whatever was last stored.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SpawnGun._isOptionsActive
member.summary: No options-menu control through this field was verified in the complete audited SpawnGun class.

remarks.para: The checked enable/disable, grip, held-update, selection, firing and async callbacks do not read or update this flag. Menu setup is performed through the popup menu and spawnables panel instead.
Treating it as the live open/closed state is therefore unsupported by this code. This finding concerns the audited SpawnGun methods, not every external game component or mod.

A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action. The callbacks here respond to the grip, selection or asynchronous completion described above; assigning a related field does not invoke them automatically.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SpawnGun._lastSelectedCrate
member.summary: Remembers the crate whose preview asset should be unloaded when the preview is replaced.

remarks.para: SetPreviewMesh unloads this crate's preview asset, then assigns the current _selectedCrate here before loading the next mesh. After that assignment it can be the same crate as _selectedCrate.
It is asset-cleanup bookkeeping, not a permanent history slot for the selection before the current one. Changing it can cause the next refresh to unload a different crate's preview asset.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SpawnGun._selectedCrate
member.summary: Selects the asset definition used for the preview and the next Spawner action.

remarks.para: A pool supplies reusable game-object instances. The cached world placement pose is truePlacePosition, a stored scene position conventionally in meters, plus truePlaceRotation, the stored orientation. A rig manager controls the player body/avatar. If this selection is an avatar crate and currentHand is available, the avatar branch requests that swap; after a successful awaited result, its save continuation reads the then-current _selectedCrate again. Changing the selection while awaiting can therefore change the crate used by that later save work.
OnSpawnableSelected stores this crate, refreshes the UI title and requests its preview mesh. The held placement calculation uses its collider bounds to place and size the preview.

SpawnCrate reads the current selection when its async operation runs. An ordinary spawnable crate becomes a pool spawn at the cached world placement pose; its separate avatar-crate branch asks currentHand's rig manager to change avatar. Assigning this field alone does not update the UI or reload the mesh.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SpawnGun._selectedMode
member.summary: Chooses whether the held gun places a crate or tries to remove a targeted entity.

remarks.para: A Rigidbody is Unity's physics body for simulated movement and rotation. Here an entity is a group of game objects managed as one unit, which the removal branch can despawn together after its player-tag check.

Spawner (0) shows the held placement preview and runs the spawn branch. Remover (1) requires an aim hit with an attached Rigidbody in the normal release path and runs the entity-removal branch. Other values do not run either action in OnFire.

OnModeSelect also refreshes the UI label/image. Assigning this field alone skips that refresh and the normal input path's sound/screen-color work. isDespawnMode is not the flag read for this choice in the audited class.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SpawnGun._spawnGunUISpawnable
member.summary: Provides the pool asset used to create the gun's selection UI, including the spawn book. See .

remarks.para: A pool keeps reusable game objects and supplies an instance when a spawn is requested. This Spawnable is the object definition used for that UI request, not the object selected for placement.
A Spawnable describes an object the pool can create. Start registers and requests this asset only if the global SpawnGunUI does not already exist, initially placing it at a remote world position.
The grip callbacks then connect this gun to the global menu and UI. This asset creates the UI; it is separate from _selectedCrate, which chooses the object to place.

A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action. The callbacks here respond to the grip, selection or asynchronous completion described above; assigning a related field does not invoke them automatically.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SpawnGun.accumulatedDist
member.summary: Adds up how far the aim hit point has traveled since the last placement blip.

remarks.para: While a hand holds the trigger in Spawner mode, a selected crate and an aim-ray hit allow this path; placerValid need not be true. It adds the world-space distance from lastHitPoint to the current aim hit. When the sum is strictly greater than blipIncrement, it first resets the sum to zero, discarding any excess distance, then requests blip playback. Placement smoothing, obstruction checks and color work follow, and lastHitPoint is saved at the end of the placement update. Thus obstructed placement can still accumulate distance and request a blip.

Distances are world units, conventionally meters. This measures the path of the ray hit across updates, not the smoothed preview's speed or distance from the gun. First showing the preview also resets it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SpawnGun.blip
member.summary: Supplies the short sound clips played after enough aim-hit movement during placement.

remarks.para: The held Spawner update first clears accumulatedDist when it becomes strictly greater than blipIncrement, then requests these sounds through map2 at the main preview's local origin. The placement checks occur later, so an obstructed preview can still request this sound.

This sound follows aim-hit travel, including movement across a surface; it is not a test that smoothing has settled. The preview, clips and audio-player references must be valid for this playback path.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SpawnGun.blipIncrement
member.summary: Sets the aim-hit travel distance needed before another placement blip plays.

remarks.para: It is a world-space distance in meters. For an illustrative value of 0.2, the accumulated hit-point path must exceed 20 cm before a blip is requested. Equality alone does not trigger one.
Before requesting a blip the accumulator becomes zero, so a large movement requests one blip rather than one for every crossed increment. This is a distance threshold, not seconds between sounds.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SpawnGun.boundColor
member.summary: Stores a red or green placement-state color, separate from the color actually interpolated onto the preview.

remarks.para: The constructor sets it green. CheckBox is a physics overlap test for a proposed box against other colliders, the shapes used in collision queries. A blocked result writes red only when placerValid changes from true to false; a clear result writes green only when placerValid changes from false to true. Repeated results with the same flag state do not make those color writes.

The audited held update uses targetColor and colorLerpTime to tint the preview and bounds lines. No rendering read of boundColor was found in the complete checked SpawnGun methods/callbacks, so changing it is not an established way to recolor that display. External readers are outside this finding.

A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action. The callbacks here respond to the grip, selection or asynchronous completion described above; assigning a related field does not invoke them automatically.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SpawnGun.boundPoints
member.summary: Stores transform references described as bounds points, without a verified placement effect in the audited SpawnGun code.

remarks.para: A Transform holds an object's position, rotation and scale. This array therefore stores references to objects that could represent points, but the array's name does not establish how their positions are generated or used.

The complete checked SpawnGun class and its async callbacks do not read this array. Start sets placerPreviewBoundsLines to local coordinates, and the held update adjusts bounds art/collider transforms and line material colors through separate references.
No automatic corner generation or alternate placement behavior through this array is established here. This does not rule out an external component or mod using the references.

A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action. The callbacks here respond to the grip, selection or asynchronous completion described above; assigning a related field does not invoke them automatically.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SpawnGun.canFireGunDown
member.summary: Remembers a trigger press that hit UI so its later release will skip firing.

remarks.para: On trigger down, the held update sets this flag when VRStandaloneInputModule reports a UI hit. On trigger release, a true value is cleared and the update returns without the aim/fire attempt.

Its name is misleading: true suppresses that release; it does not authorize a shot. It is separate from the popup-menu restriction, the aim ray and the base gun readiness checks. Setting it true yourself consumes the next checked release.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SpawnGun.chargeSFX
member.summary: Supplies the charge sounds requested when the held hand presses the trigger.

remarks.para: After checking the popup/UI restriction, a trigger-down event plays a nonempty clip array through map at the gun transform's local origin. This happens before any successful placement or release shot is established.
It is one request for the down event, not a repeating sound for every held frame. An empty array skips this playback.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SpawnGun.collisionLayers
member.summary: Filters the physics layers used for aiming and placement-obstruction queries.

remarks.para: A collider is a shape used for physics collision queries. A trigger collider detects overlap without behaving as a solid contact barrier. CheckBox asks whether a proposed box overlaps another collider; BoxCast moves an imaginary box along a line to test for a hit. Both aiming rays, the CheckBox and the BoxCast use this mask and ignore trigger colliders.

A layer mask selects groups of colliders a query is allowed to hit. The held preview and trigger-release rays use this mask, as do the placement CheckBox and obstruction BoxCast. These queries ignore trigger colliders.
Excluding a layer makes its colliders invisible to these queries, affecting both the aim hit and the overlap preview. This is not a list of layers assigned to the spawned object.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SpawnGun.colorLerpTime
member.summary: Stores the blend progress for changing the main placement preview and bounds-line colors.

remarks.para: Time.deltaTime is this frame's duration in game seconds, affected by game speed and pausing. In progress += Time.deltaTime × 10, the fixed 10 means ten units of blend progress per game second. For a 0.02-game-second frame, the progress increases by 0.2 after that frame's color writes.

On a placement-validity transition it resets to zero. Each placement update clamps it to 0 through 1 for a Color.Lerp from the material's current color toward targetColor, then increases it by Time.deltaTime times 10.

It is dimensionless blend progress, not elapsed seconds or a configurable transition duration. For example, 0.5 blends halfway from the current color toward the target on that update. It does not drive the gun body screen transition; screenColorLerpTime does that.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SpawnGun.currentHand
member.summary: Stores the attached trigger-grip hand used to find the player rig during avatar selection.

remarks.para: The rig manager is the controller for the player's body and avatar. The avatar branch finds it through this stored hand to request a body/avatar change.
OnTriggerGripAttached assigns the reporting hand and OnTriggerGripDetached clears it. The SpawnCrate avatar-crate branch uses this hand's rig manager to request an avatar swap.
The held-input callback reads its own hand argument for buttons. Changing currentHand does not attach a different hand or redirect that grip's event subscriptions.

A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action. The callbacks here respond to the grip, selection or asynchronous completion described above; assigning a related field does not invoke them automatically.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SpawnGun.dampTimePos
member.summary: Sets the time scale for smoothing the placement preview toward its target position.

remarks.para: Time.deltaTime is this frame's duration in game seconds. Local coordinates measure position relative to placerRoot, the parent reference frame, rather than directly from the world origin. SmoothDamp moves gradually toward the target while retaining its motion state in posVelocity.

It is seconds, passed to Vector3.SmoothDamp with Time.deltaTime and posVelocity. Smaller values make movement respond faster; larger values make it settle more slowly. It is not a guaranteed arrival time.

The smoothed position and stored velocity are local to placerRoot. For illustrative values, 0.1 seconds responds faster than 0.5 seconds to the same target change. Rotation uses the separately calculated dampTimeRot blend.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SpawnGun.dampTimeRot
member.summary: Sets how strongly the placement preview turns toward its target rotation each second.

remarks.para: A Quaternion stores an orientation. Slerp blends between orientations so the preview turns gradually toward its target. Time.deltaTime is this frame's duration in game seconds; multiplying seconds by this field's inverse-seconds rate produces the unitless blend amount.

The held update uses Quaternion.Slerp with a blend of Time.deltaTime times dampTimeRot. This value acts as an inverse-seconds response rate: increasing it makes rotation follow faster, despite the Time in its name. It is not a duration in seconds.

For an illustrative 0.02-second update and value 5, the blend is 0.1, moving 10 percent along the remaining rotation toward the target. Slerp clamps the blend to 0 through 1; zero gives no rotation change through this step. The rotations being blended are world rotations.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SpawnGun.effectiveRange
member.summary: Sets the maximum world-space distance for the gun's aiming rays and placement obstruction cast.

remarks.para: The value is meters in the game's world coordinates. For example, a value of 15 lets the aiming ray consider a collider up to 15 meters from firePointTransform's muzzle position along its forward direction, subject to collisionLayers and ignoring triggers. The obstruction BoxCast moves an imaginary box up to 15 meters from its own starting point, which is halfway from the muzzle to the aim-ray hit: muzzle position + muzzle forward × (aim-hit distance × 0.5). The 0.5 is a unitless half-distance multiplier. Its sweep distance is therefore not a 15-meter overall limit measured from the muzzle.

The held Spawner preview and release-fire attempt both use it. It sets query reach, not a spawned object's size, speed or lifetime. The constructor sets 15, while prefab/scene serialization may supply another value.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SpawnGun.fanBladesTransform
member.summary: Rotates the gun's decorative fan locally while attached-grip updates run.

remarks.para: A Transform holds position, rotation and scale. Local Y is this fan's own up direction. AngleAxis constructs a rotation from an angle in degrees and a direction axis, and Time.deltaTime is the frame duration in game seconds. For a 0.02-game-second frame, -833 × 0.02 adds -16.66 degrees about that local axis.

Each update composes its current local rotation with an AngleAxis rotation about local Y of -833 degrees per second times Time.deltaTime. The negative sign chooses the opposite turn direction from a positive Y rotation.
This is visual rotation of the assigned transform, not airflow or a physics force. The reference must be assigned; it is read before the held update reaches input checks.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SpawnGun.gunBodyRenderers

remarks.para: The held update reads _EmissionColor from material slot 1 of element 0, blends it toward targetScreenColor, and writes the resulting color to material slot 1 on every listed renderer. CoFireFlash separately writes the _FlashCoroutine float to that same material slot.
At least one valid renderer is needed for the color read, and every referenced renderer needs at least two valid materials. This code does not tint every material on the body.

Setting this field therefore is not the verified way to switch the tool into Remover mode. The finding covers the checked SpawnGun methods and async callbacks; external readers or writers are outside that scope.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SpawnGun.kneeOffsetPos

remarks.para: Wall mode keeps the placement root fixed at its saved world position for a steep static hit: the surface-normal Y component is between -0.5 and +0.5 inclusive and the hit has no Rigidbody, Unity's physics body. Outside that mode the root follows the player's knee plus this offset.

When leaving wall mode, the held update sets it to lastKneePos minus the current physics-rig knee position. It then places placerRoot at current knee position plus this offset, preserving the previous root position at the transition.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SpawnGun.lastKneePos

remarks.para: Wall mode keeps the placement root fixed for a steep static hit: its surface-normal Y component is between -0.5 and +0.5 inclusive and it has no Rigidbody, Unity's physics body. member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SpawnGun.placerRoot
member.summary: Provides the coordinate frame in which the main placement preview's position is smoothed.

remarks.para: Identity rotation means no world rotation. This Transform is the parent position/rotation/scale reference for the preview's local coordinates. Wall mode freezes its position for a steep static hit, with surface-normal Y between -0.5 and +0.5 inclusive and no attached Rigidbody, Unity's physics body. SmoothDamp gradually moves the preview toward its target while retaining motion state, after the target is converted from world position into this parent frame.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SpawnGun.placerValid
member.summary: Reports whether the placement bounds passed the last checked overlap test.

remarks.para: A collider is a shape used for physics queries; a trigger collider reports overlap without acting as a solid contact barrier. CheckBox tests whether the proposed box overlaps another collider. Bounds half-size means half the selected crate bounds width, height and depth, used as world-length components in this query; 0.94 is a unitless shrink multiplier. This path ignores triggers but tests the other colliders allowed by collisionLayers.

During a held Spawner preview update, Physics.CheckBox uses the preview box world position, 0.94 times the crate bounds half-size, the bounds-art rotation and collisionLayers, ignoring triggers. No overlap sets this flag true; overlap sets it false. Changes reset the preview color blend and choose the valid/invalid target color.

It is calculated preview state, not a complete valid-surface or firing-permission test. The release path and OnFire do not check it before the action. Outside updates that perform this test, it can retain an earlier result; assigning it can be overwritten by a later check.

When the result changes, the update writes placerValid first, resets colorLerpTime second, writes the red/green bookkeeping color third, and copies the configured target color last. This path does not raise a placement-validity event.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SpawnGun.placerValidColor

It does not control the gun body's mode screen color. Changing this field while the valid state stays unchanged does not automatically refresh the cached targetColor, and valid preview coloring is not a firing permission.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SpawnGun.previewBounds

remarks.para: A MeshFilter stores a 3D mesh's geometry, the vertices and faces defining its shape. Here its mesh bounds, the box enclosing that geometry, supply the reference dimensions used by the display-normalization calculation.

The mesh-load callback reads this MeshFilter's mesh bounds size. It divides each size component by the loaded mesh's bounds-size magnitude, then multiplies by previewMeshScaleTune to set previewPoint.localScale.

This is a normalization reference for the small display. The placement overlap box instead uses the selected crate's collider bounds. A valid reference mesh is required; its bounds are not automatically replaced by the selected crate.
Here, the mesh-load callback is a routine called when the requested asset becomes available; that routine performs the preview updates described above.

For the scale/centering calculation, the loaded length is sqrt(width² + height² + depth²), using the loaded mesh bounds dimensions in mesh-coordinate units. member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SpawnGun.previewMeshPosition
member.summary: Centers the small loaded-mesh display by compensating for its mesh-bounds center.

remarks.para: A Transform holds an object's position, rotation and scale. For an illustrative loaded bounds center (1, 0, 0), loaded length 2 in the same mesh-coordinate units, and unitless previewMeshScaleTune 0.1, the formula -center / loaded length × tune gives local offset (-0.05, 0, 0) in this parent frame. It compensates for the displaced mesh center when loading finishes.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SpawnGun.previewMeshRock
member.summary: Rocks the small preview back and forth around its local Z axis while the gun is held.

remarks.para: AngleAxis constructs an orientation from an angle in degrees and an axis. Here time is the stored phase, meaning position within the repeating rocking cycle, measured in radians; 2π radians is a full turn, with π approximately 3.14159. Sine maps this phase to a back-and-forth value between -1 and +1; previewMeshRockAmp multiplies it in degrees. Local Z is the preview's own forward direction. Time.deltaTime is this frame's game-time duration in seconds, and previewMeshRockSpeed is radians of phase per game second. The angle is calculated before the phase advances.

Each attached update replaces its local rotation with AngleAxis(sin(time) times previewMeshRockAmp, forward). The time field is an accumulated phase advanced by Time.deltaTime times previewMeshRockSpeed.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SpawnGun.previewMeshRockAmp
member.summary: Sets the maximum angle of the small preview's rocking motion.

remarks.para: The referenced time is phase, position within the repeating cycle measured in radians; 2π radians is a full turn, with π approximately 3.14159. sin(time) gives a back-and-forth value between -1 and +1. AngleAxis constructs an orientation from that value multiplied by this amplitude in degrees and the preview's local Z, its own forward direction.

It is degrees. The held update uses sin(time) times this value as an AngleAxis rotation about previewMeshRock's local Z axis. For an illustrative value of 10, the angle varies from -10 to +10 degrees; zero produces no rocking angle.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SpawnGun.previewMeshRockSpeed

remarks.para: Time.deltaTime is this frame's duration in game seconds. The equation phase += frame seconds × this rate produces a phase change in radians. In 2π/s, π is approximately 3.14159 and 2π radians is one full cycle; s is the positive constant phase rate in radians per game second, giving a period in game seconds.

Each attached update adds Time.deltaTime times this value to time, whose sine determines the rocking angle. Its units are radians of phase per second, not degrees per second or complete rocks per second.

For a positive constant value s, a full sine cycle takes 2π/s seconds of attached updates. An illustrative value of 2π gives one cycle per second. Zero stops phase advancement; amplitude still comes from previewMeshRockAmp.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SpawnGun.previewMeshScaleTune

remarks.para: The mesh-load callback divides previewBounds.mesh.bounds.size by the loaded mesh's bounds-size magnitude, multiplies by this value and assigns previewPoint.localScale. It also multiplies the corresponding negative bounds-center offset for previewMeshPosition by this value.
