member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SplineBody.angularXLimit
member.summary: Stores a value labelled as an X-axis angular limit; the inspected spline setup and updates do not apply it.

remarks.para: The stored value represents an angle in degrees around a physics joint's X axis, the rotation axis defined by the body's axis setting. For example, 30 represents a 30-degree angle. This field alone does not establish a permitted range of rotation.

The inspected SplineBody setup methods and the spline controller's joint configuration and physics update do not copy this value into Unity's joint limits. Changing it alone therefore does not change the limits through those methods. If you need an applied limit, configure the actual contact joint's angular-limit settings separately.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SplineBody.angularXLimitBounciness
member.summary: Stores a value labelled as angular-limit bounce; the inspected spline setup and updates do not apply it.

remarks.para: Bounciness is a unitless setting intended to describe how much a physics joint rebounds when its rotation reaches an angular limit. An angular limit restricts turning around the joint's own X axis. This stored value alone cannot make the spline body bounce at that limit.

The inspected SplineBody setup methods and the spline controller's joint configuration and physics update do not copy this value into Unity's joint limits. Changing it alone therefore does not change the limits through those methods. If you need an applied limit, configure the actual contact joint's angular-limit settings separately.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SplineBody.angularXLimitContactDistance
member.summary: Stores an angular-limit tolerance; the inspected spline setup and updates do not apply it.

remarks.para: For an angular physics-joint limit, contact distance means an angle tolerance in degrees: how near the rotation is to a limit before Unity starts enforcing it. For example, a 5-degree tolerance would start considering the limit while the rotation is still close to it. This is an angular tolerance, not a distance in metres from the spline.

The inspected SplineBody setup methods and the spline controller's joint configuration and physics update do not copy this value into Unity's joint limits. Changing it alone therefore does not change the limits through those methods. If you need an applied limit, configure the actual contact joint's angular-limit settings separately.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SplineBody.angularXMotion
member.summary: Chooses the X-axis rotation constraint applied when the spline controller configures a one-contact body.

remarks.para: A physics joint connects the body to a contact on the path. Its X axis comes from this body's axis setting; turning around that axis is separate from sliding along it. Locked prevents that turn, Limited uses the actual joint's angular limits, and Free leaves it unrestricted by this constraint.

The spline controller copies this setting to the joint when contactCount is ONE, while locking rotation around the other two joint axes. With TWO or FOUR contacts, it instead sets all three angular motions to Free, regardless of this field. The multiple contacts still constrain the body through their positions.

Changing this stored setting does not itself request a refresh. It takes effect on the next joint reconfiguration caused by sufficient movement of the body's contact origin or by isSpeedChanged. The stored angularXLimit, angularXLimitBounciness and angularXLimitContactDistance values are not copied into the joint by the inspected configuration method.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SplineBody.contactJoints
member.summary: Holds the physics joints created on this object for the spline controller to constrain and drive its contacts.

remarks.para: Awake, Unity's initial component setup method, creates one, two, or four new ConfigurableJoint components according to contactCount and stores them in this array. A ConfigurableJoint is a physics connection whose movement and rotation rules can be adjusted. These are newly added components, rather than a search for any joints already on the object. Unsupported contact counts do not populate an array through this setup.

The spline controller configures the first one, two, or four entries when it refreshes this body. It supplies body-side anchor points in the body's local coordinates and path-side anchor points in scene coordinates. The joints connect to fixed points in the scene, with their connectedBody set to null, rather than to another Rigidbody.

Configuration allows movement along each joint's X direction and locks movement along Y and Z. It also writes the requested X-drive speed, damping and per-joint maximum force. Replacing this array alone does not create, attach, or configure joints; the configured contact count must have enough valid entries.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SplineBody.isSpeedChanged
member.summary: Requests a refresh of this body's spline contact joints even when its contact origin has moved too little for the usual refresh.

remarks.para: All three drive-setting methods set this flag to true: changes to target speed, damping and maximum force use it. The name does not mean that the Rigidbody, Unity's physics body for this object, has actually changed speed. Direct writes to those stored settings do not raise the flag.

During FixedUpdate, Unity's regularly spaced physics update, the assigned spline controller refreshes a registered body if this flag is true or if its contact origin has moved farther than the configured movement threshold since the last refresh. The contact origin is the body's anchor point expressed in scene coordinates.

The controller updates the saved contact position and clears this flag before configuring the joints. Consequently, false does not certify that configuration completed successfully or that the requested speed was reached. Setting the flag directly does not wake a sleeping Rigidbody; the three drive-setting methods also call WakeUp.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SplineBody.maximumForce
member.summary: Stores the force ceiling copied to each contact joint's X movement drive; use to request a runtime refresh.

remarks.para: The value is in newtons per joint. A contact joint is a physics connection that keeps part of the body on the curved spline path; its X drive is the motor pushing along the path. For example, 100 limits that motor to 100 newtons on each joint. It does not limit collision forces, gravity, or the total force produced by several joints together.

New instances initialize this field to positive infinity, meaning this drive setting imposes no finite ceiling. Scene or prefab settings can replace that initial value. The spline controller reads the stored value when it reconfigures the contact joints.

Assigning this property changes the stored number only. It does not change the existing joint drives immediately, set isSpeedChanged, or wake rb, the Rigidbody that simulates the object's motion. SetMaximumForce stores the number and performs the refresh-request and wake steps.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SplineBody.positionDamper
member.summary: Stores the X-drive speed-error correction strength; use to request a runtime refresh.

remarks.para: The spline controller configures each contact joint, a physics connection to the curved path, with an X movement drive whose position spring is zero. Here the damper acts on the difference between requested and current relative speed along the joint's own X direction.

The damper multiplies speed error, measured in Unity distance units per second, to request force. When one Unity unit represents one metre, its SI unit is newton-seconds per metre, and the coefficient multiplied by speed error gives the requested force before the force ceiling. For example, at that scale, 20 N·s/m multiplied by a 2 m/s speed difference requests 40 N. If a scene uses a different distance for one Unity unit, the metre-based unit and example change with that scale. Larger positive values correct speed errors more strongly. A zero coefficient supplies no force from this speed-error term.

The spline controller copies the value when it reconfigures the joints. Assigning this property only changes storage: it does not immediately change the joints, set isSpeedChanged, or wake rb, the Rigidbody that simulates the body's motion. SetPositionDamper also requests the refresh and wakes the body.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SplineBody.rb
member.summary: References the Rigidbody whose physical motion and rotation the spline controller follows and drives.

remarks.para: A Rigidbody is Unity's physics body: it lets an object move under forces and collisions. The spline controller reads this body's rotation while updating the generated contact joints and writes its rotation after that update. The drive-setting methods call WakeUp on this reference so a sleeping body can respond to the requested change.

The component's Reset routine, which Unity uses when resetting component setup, looks for a Rigidbody on this same object and adds one if missing. Awake, the initial runtime setup method, creates the contact joints but does not perform that Rigidbody search. Assign a valid Rigidbody when constructing or configuring a body yourself.

The contact joints are added to the SplineBody's own object. Changing this reference only changes which Rigidbody the controller reads and wakes; it does not move those joint components onto another object.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SplineBody.targetVelocity
member.summary: Stores the requested X-drive speed; use to request a runtime refresh.

remarks.para: The value is a signed speed in Unity distance units per second, normally metres per second when one Unity unit represents one metre. The spline controller copies it to the X component of each contact joint's target velocity and sets the other two components to zero. A contact joint is a physics connection keeping part of the body on the path; its X direction follows the body's axis setting as that direction is aligned to the spline, rather than the scene's fixed world X direction.

For example, 2 requests an X-drive speed of 2 metres per second at the usual scale. A negative value reverses that signed request. This stored number is not a measurement of the Rigidbody's current speed. The actual movement depends on the drive's speed-error correction, its force ceiling and other forces.

Assigning this property only changes the stored request. Existing joint targets receive it on the next reconfiguration, which may wait for sufficient movement unless a refresh is requested. A direct assignment does not set isSpeedChanged or wake the Rigidbody, Unity's physics body for the object. SetTargetVelocity performs those additional steps.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SplineJoint._addedEntities
member.summary: Records the current entity membership used to prevent duplicate registration.

remarks.para: AddEntity checks this HashSet before adding an entity to the entities list and, for a SplineBody, to the physical-body list. A HashSet stores each reference only once. RemoveEntity removes the entity from this set and the corresponding lists, so this is current registration bookkeeping rather than a history of everything ever attached.

UpdatePath clears the set while rebuilding the lists, then registers the previous entities again. Editing this set alone does not attach, move or configure an entity and can make AddEntity or RemoveEntity skip necessary list updates. Use those registration routines, or the entity’s AttachToSplineJoint routine when it also needs to be positioned on the path.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SplineJoint._bodies
member.summary: Lists the registered SplineBody components whose physical joints this rail updates.

remarks.para: These entries are SplineBody components, not raw Rigidbody references. Each supplies a Rigidbody, the Unity component simulating motion and forces, plus its contact joints, contact placement and movement settings. A joint is a physics connection that restricts or drives relative movement. FixedUpdate processes this list to adjust those connections against the sampled rail.

AddEntity adds an entry here only when the entity is a SplineBody. Generic SplineEntity entries can belong to entities without entering this physical update list. RemoveEntity keeps both lists and the registration set aligned; UpdatePath rebuilds them. Direct list edits do not prepare missing bodies or contact joints and can leave registration inconsistent. Prepare the body’s components and use the attachment/registration routines.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SplineJoint._isLoop
member.summary: Caches whether position lookup wraps around the sampled path or stops at its end indices.

remarks.para: BuildPolyPath copies the assigned spline’s loop setting here when it successfully rebuilds its samples. During GetSample position lookup, true wraps searched indices around the available segments; false limits them to the first or last segment and uses special endpoint samples. This affects how the solver searches near the beginning and end of the rail.

The flag is a cached setting, not a live check of the spline on every lookup. Change the spline’s loop setting and rebuild the path to refresh it. Writing this flag alone changes lookup behavior but does not rebuild the spline’s curves. The segment builder links its last stored sample back to the first even when this flag is false; therefore the flag alone does not describe every link stored in _segments.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SplineJoint._minimumUpdateMovementSqr
member.summary: Stores the square of for deciding when to refresh body joints.

remarks.para: Awake, Unity’s initialization routine, sets this to minimumUpdateMovement × minimumUpdateMovement. minimumUpdateMovement is a distance in Unity units; this cached value is therefore in square Unity units. It corresponds to metres only if the relevant scene uses a scale of 1 Unity unit = 1 metre; under that scale, a 0.01 Unity-unit threshold is 0.01 m and produces 0.0001 Unity units² (0.0001 m²).

FixedUpdate compares it with the squared straight-line displacement of each body’s world contact origin from its last joint-refresh position. The contact origin is the body position plus its rotated anchor offset. A refresh happens only when displacement is strictly greater than this threshold, or the body’s isSpeedChanged flag asks for an update. Equal displacement alone does not trigger it.

Sample lookup and segment notifications still run before this test. This threshold does not control rebuilding the rail’s sample data. Changing minimumUpdateMovement after Awake does not automatically refresh this cache, and UpdatePath does not recalculate it. Keep the squared value consistent if changing the threshold after initialization.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SplineJoint._samples
member.summary: Stores the sampled positions and directions used to approximate the smooth rail.

remarks.para: BuildPolyPath reads the assigned spline’s curved sections and records samples containing location, tangent, up direction and distance information. A tangent points along the curve. Locations come directly from the spline’s curve coordinates; this joint’s lookup routines interpret them in the SplineJoint Transform’s local coordinates, relative to its origin and axes, then convert them to world positions when needed. Sample positions and accumulated distances use Unity coordinate units. Treat them as metres only if the relevant scene uses a scale of 1 Unity unit = 1 metre.

For samplesPerSegment = N, each curved section is sampled at fractions 0/N, 1/N through (N−1)/N. It does not add a separate fraction-1 sample for the last section. The stored distance is accumulated straight-line distance between successive sampled positions, so it approximates curved travel rather than measuring exact arc length.

BuildPolyPath replaces this list and the segment list. Editing the input spline or sample count does not automatically replace these cached samples. Use UpdatePath to rebuild the path and reattach its registered entities. Editing only this list can leave _segments and saved segment indices inconsistent.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SplineJoint._segmentCollisionEvents
member.summary: Maps integer notification keys to routines called when a body’s stored segment index changes.

remarks.para: Despite the name, these are segment-index notifications from FixedUpdate, not ordinary collider-contact events. A callback is a routine called to report an action; each registered callback receives the SplineBody being processed. It runs before that body’s new lastSegmentIdx is stored and before the movement threshold decides whether to refresh its joints, so it sees the previous cached index.

The implemented key rule is unusual: when old index and new index differ, the routine checks keys newIndex + 1 through newIndex + abs(oldIndex − newIndex), in increasing order. abs means the positive magnitude of that difference. For example, old 5 to new 2 checks 3, 4 and 5; old 2 to new 5 checks 6, 7 and 8. Only keys present in this dictionary are called. There is no direction-based reversal or loop wrapping in this notification range, so do not assume the key always names the segment just entered.

AddSegmentEventTrigger combines multiple handlers at a key. RemoveSegmentEventTrigger removes the dictionary key when removing a handler leaves no handlers; when other handlers remain, this implementation computes the new combination but does not store it back, so the old combined handlers can remain registered. Remove the dictionary entry explicitly when clearing every handler for a key. Rebuilding the path does not clear these registrations, and changing sample density changes what the indices represent.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SplineJoint._segments
member.summary: Stores the straight links between samples used for closest-path queries and joint placement.

remarks.para: BuildPolyPath creates a CurveSegment from each sample to the next, using _samples as the source. Each stores its endpoints, direction along the link, length and orientation information. The samples are interpreted in this SplineJoint’s local origin and axes; world-space queries convert through its Transform. Length is in local Unity distance units. Convert it to metres only if the relevant scene uses a scale of 1 Unity unit = 1 metre. The native code does not convert this local length to world distance; transformed scale can affect world-space distance.

The final segment links the last stored sample back to sample zero. The builder makes that link even for an open spline; _isLoop separately controls whether the main position lookup wraps or limits its indices at the ends. Do not treat the stored list alone as a guarantee of open-end behavior.

GetSample searches and projects against these links, and the physics update uses the resulting positions to configure body contact joints. BuildPolyPath replaces the list, while UpdatePath also rebuilds membership and repositions registered entities. Direct changes to this cache can invalidate sample/index relationships and notification meanings.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SplineJoint.entities
member.summary: Lists the entities registered with this rail and reattached during a path rebuild.

remarks.para: A SplineEntity describes an object’s contact position, axes and intended spline connection. The entities list can contain generic SplineEntity components as well as physical SplineBody components; only the latter also enter _bodies for FixedUpdate joint processing. A Rigidbody is Unity’s component for simulating motion and forces, and each physical SplineBody supplies its own body and contact joints.

AddEntity registers a reference in this list and the duplicate-prevention set; it does not itself position the object. SplineEntity.AttachToSplineJoint assigns its joint reference, positions and rotates it at its selected path sample, then registers it. RemoveEntity removes registration from the lists and set without destroying the component.

UpdatePath saves the old list, replaces it and _bodies with new lists, clears the registration set, and re-adds each old entity. It chooses a nearby sample index from its world contact origin, then attaches it again, which can change its pose. Editing this list alone does not perform that attachment or maintain the other collections.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SplineJoint.minimumUpdateMovement
member.summary: Sets the world-distance threshold for refreshing a body’s contact-joint settings.

remarks.para: This threshold uses world distance in Unity units and is squared into _minimumUpdateMovementSqr in square Unity units by Awake, Unity’s initialization routine. It corresponds to metres only if the relevant scene uses a scale of 1 Unity unit = 1 metre. FixedUpdate compares each physical body’s current world contact origin with the position saved at its last joint refresh. The contact origin is body position plus the rotated anchor offset. It refreshes joints when the straight-line displacement is strictly greater than the cached threshold, or isSpeedChanged forces a refresh.

This is not accumulated path length: moving away and back near the saved origin can leave little displacement. A larger threshold allows more positional change before joint settings are refreshed; a smaller threshold allows more frequent refreshes. Sample lookup and segment notifications happen before this test and are not skipped by it.

Changing this field after Awake does not recalculate the squared cache, and UpdatePath does not do so either. Keep _minimumUpdateMovementSqr consistent when changing the threshold after initialization. The threshold does not control rebuilding spline geometry; use UpdatePath for a new sampled rail. For example, if the scene uses 1 Unity unit = 1 metre, a 0.01 Unity-unit threshold equals 0.01 m and corresponds to 0.0001 Unity units² (0.0001 m²) in the comparison cache.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SplineJoint.samplesPerSegment
member.summary: Chooses how many parameter samples are taken from each curved section when building the rail.

remarks.para: This is an integer count, not a distance or physics-update rate. If N samples are requested, BuildPolyPath samples each curved section at parameter fractions 0/N through (N−1)/N. These fractions describe progress through that curve’s formula and are not guaranteed to give evenly spaced world distances. For example, two curved sections with N = 4 produce eight samples and eight connecting segments.

More samples give a more finely divided straight-link approximation and more entries for searches and segment-index notifications. Changing the count alone does not rebuild _samples or _segments. Use UpdatePath to rebuild and reattach the registered entities; that can reposition them and changes the meaning of existing notification indices.

Supply a positive count that produces distinct sample points. The builder does not clamp this field to a safe minimum; zero or negative values produce no samples. The native constructor starts at 256, but configured scene values may differ. The last curved section does not receive a separate fraction-1 endpoint sample.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.SplineJoint.spline
member.summary: Supplies the smooth curve data that is sampled into this rail’s physics path.

remarks.para: This SplineMesh.Spline contains curved sections between configured nodes. BuildPolyPath reads those sections and their loop setting to replace _samples and _segments. Their numeric locations are interpreted in this SplineJoint’s local coordinates, relative to its own Transform origin and axes; assigning a spline on another object does not automatically convert its coordinates into that frame.

Assign a prepared spline with at least one curved section and a positive samplesPerSegment count before initialization. Awake, Unity’s initialization routine, calls UpdatePath. Later changing this reference or the curve data alone does not refresh the cached physics path. UpdatePath rebuilds the samples and reattaches registered entities, which can reposition them.

BuildPolyPath returns without replacing its existing sample caches when the spline is missing or has no curves. Removing the reference therefore does not automatically erase an old path. This reference supplies path geometry; a SplineBody’s Rigidbody and contact joints must be prepared separately for physics following.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.StaticProfiles.Instance
member.summary: Provides the shared profile object that game controllers consult for NPC, loot and ammunition choices.

remarks.para: CreateStatProfile replaces the shared reference with the supplied profile. Reading instance returns the reference as stored; it can be null before setup. The getter does not create a profile or load the asset named by path.

BaseGameController normally supplies its configured profile during Awake, Unity's setup call when a component starts, if the shared reference is missing. Setting the shared reference does not itself change existing NPCs or refill inventory.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.StaticProfiles.allyData
member.summary: Supplies the default alliance-data entries copied when an AllianceTable resets its data.

remarks.para: AllianceTable.ResetDefaults clears the table's own list and copies these object references in order. It then selects the first entry as dataA and the second as dataB, the table's two comparison inputs. Provide at least two entries before resetting the table.

The list starts empty on a newly constructed profile. Changing its membership affects a later reset; it does not automatically replace the list already copied into a table. The copied entries still refer to the same AllianceData objects.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.StaticProfiles.animeCollectSpawnble
member.summary: Selects the additional object asset requested alongside each large or small arena health pack.

remarks.para: A Spawnable describes an asset that the object pool can create or reuse. Both arena health-pack routines register this description, request the health pack first, and then request this additional object at the same scene position.

Those routines do not wait for the health-pack completion callback, code called later with a spawned object, before making this second request. They supply no completion callback for this additional object. The configured asset determines what appears; the request alone does not prove it appeared or that the player collected anything.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.StaticProfiles.arenaGCPrefabPath

The complete StaticProfiles instance getter and CreateStatProfile method do not load anything using this path. Changing the string only changes the path available to later callers; it does not reload the shared profile or create a controller.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.StaticProfiles.bladeCrateList

remarks.para: A spawnable-crate reference identifies an object asset in the game's asset warehouse. The constructor creates an empty list here. This is separate storage from the ArenaLootItem list for the same weapon category.

The complete StaticProfiles constructor, instance getter and CreateStatProfile method do not fill this list from the loot entries or request any weapon spawns. For example, adding a blade ArenaLootItem to bladeLootList does not also add its SpawnableCrateReference to bladeCrateList through these methods. Code that needs this separate list must populate it explicitly.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.StaticProfiles.bladeLootList
member.summary: Supplies arena loot entries for bladed melee weapons to RoundProfileGroup.RandomBladeLootWeapon.

remarks.para: Each ArenaLootItem describes a spawnable object and its loot settings. This list starts empty and must contain an entry before the random helper is called.

RandomBladeLootWeapon chooses a whole-number index from 0 up to, but excluding, Count, where Count is the number of entries. Every entry can be selected; this helper does not use the entries' percentage settings as selection weights. For example, three entries allow the first, second or third with equal selection chances.

The helper returns the stored loot entry. Round-building code can put that entry into a wave, and the wave spawner later requests its spawnable object. Editing this list does not directly create a weapon or change a weapon already in the scene.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.StaticProfiles.crownSpawnable

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.StaticProfiles.enemyProfileList
member.summary: Supplies general NPC profiles for default arena waves, random enemy choices and startup asset registration.

remarks.para: An EnemyProfile is a saved NPC setup that includes which object to spawn. BaseGameController.Start, Unity's startup call before regular updates, registers the spawnable asset in every entry with the object pool so it can be requested later. Registration does not create an NPC. The list starts empty and must be configured.

List order matters: CreateDefaultRound and the arena menu fallback use the first entry. RandomCrabOrNull chooses the first or second entry without checking their NPC types. The arena objective-enemy routine can use the fourth entry when its own objective list has no entry for the current position. Configure enough entries for the paths you use.

RandomEnemyProfile chooses a whole-number index from 0 up to, but excluding, Count - 1; Count is the number of entries. With two or more entries it skips the last one. For example, four entries allow the first three; a one-entry list returns that entry. The helper has no empty-list fallback and returns an existing profile reference rather than spawning an NPC.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TaxiController.OnDriveOff
member.summary: Calls listeners when the departure sequence places the taxi on its exit path and selects fast drive targets.

remarks.para: The sequence begins when the rear seat deregisters the player. It waits until _exitedCab is true and at least 11 seconds have accumulated since that sequence began, then changes to jimmyExitPolyLine, places the taxi on that path, and copies fast targets before calling listeners. The exterior-moving engine fade is requested afterward. It does not check the player's distance from the taxi.
This Unity event calls its listeners with no arguments. A listener is a routine attached to the event that runs when the event is invoked.

The departure delay and the requested engine fade use scaled game-time seconds. Slow motion stretches their real-world duration; for example, the 11-game-second delay takes about 22 real seconds at a constant half-speed time scale, while the exit signal is still separately required.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TaxiController.OnEngineStart
member.summary: Calls listeners when the saved push-check speed reaches or exceeds velThresh.

remarks.para: It fires before the engine-start sound, door-opening sound, and exterior-idle loop fade are requested. The push check uses signed local-forward speed, in meters per second, rather than speed in all directions. It does not signal that an audio player has already started.
This Unity event calls its listeners with no arguments. A listener is a routine attached to the event that runs when the event is invoked.

velThresh is the signed forward-speed cutoff in meters per second, along carBody's local blue Z axis. For example, a saved forward value of 1 reaches a cutoff of 1; a backward value of -1 does not reach that positive cutoff. The notification follows the saved-cache comparison and does not require a new sample immediately before it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TaxiController.OnLoopComplete
member.summary: Calls listeners after a loop reaches or exceeds loopGoal and begins the braking sequence.

remarks.para: The count has already increased, and DriveComplete has already started its stop-wait sequence. Earlier loops do not fire this event. Further calls beyond the goal can fire it again; there is no once-only guard.
This Unity event calls its listeners with no arguments. A listener is a routine attached to the event that runs when the event is invoked.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TaxiController.OnPlayerSeated
member.summary: Calls listeners after the rear seat registers the player and the taxi selects its fast drive targets.

remarks.para: Before listeners run, the taxi has been placed on its curved path, the rear seat's unseat action has been blocked, and fast targets have been copied. Hiding toggleObjects, switching seat event subscriptions, stopping push prompts, and requesting interior-moving engine audio happen afterward.
This Unity event calls its listeners with no arguments. A listener is a routine attached to the event that runs when the event is invoked.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TaxiController.OnRideComplete
member.summary: Calls listeners when the stop-wait sequence completes its shared cached-value test.

remarks.para: The sequence compares the shared currVelMag cache with stopThresh squared. stopThresh is a speed cutoff in meters per second; later body samples normally store squared world speed in square meters per square second. Listeners run before the door-opening sound is requested and before toggleObjects are shown again. This can occur while the taxi still has a small speed; it is not a strict zero-velocity test.
This Unity event calls its listeners with no arguments. A listener is a routine attached to the event that runs when the event is invoked.

The sequence first puts the placeholder 20 into currVelMag before testing it. If stopThresh squared is at least 20, the sequence can complete before sampling the body at all; for example, stopThresh = 5 meters per second gives a squared cutoff of 25. When another sample is needed, it normally stores squared world speed in that same cache. A concurrent push checker can overwrite it with signed forward speed, so completion does not guarantee measured slowing or a stationary taxi.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TaxiController.OnStopingStart
member.summary: Calls listeners when DriveComplete begins braking the taxi.

remarks.para: Before listeners run, the rear seat is allowed to unseat the player and brake targets have been copied. Brake audio, the interior-idle engine fade, and the stop-wait sequence are requested afterward. This is a braking-start signal, not proof the taxi is stationary.
This Unity event calls its listeners with no arguments. A listener is a routine attached to the event that runs when the event is invoked.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TaxiController.OnWhiteFlag
member.summary: Calls listeners when the incremented loop count is exactly one less than loopGoal.

remarks.para: For loopGoal = 3, the second SplineLoopCounter call fires this event. It runs after the count changes and before any goal-triggered braking in that call. The method itself does not raise or animate a visible flag.
This Unity event calls its listeners with no arguments. A listener is a routine attached to the event that runs when the event is invoked.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TaxiController._backLfRb
member.summary: Saves the back-left wheel's Rigidbody so setup can raise its allowed spin speed.

remarks.para: A Rigidbody is the component that lets an object move in the physics simulation. Start, Unity's setup routine before normal updates, finds this component on the corresponding wheel joint's object and sets maxAngularVelocity to 300 radians per second, about 48 turns per second.
The saved reference is not refreshed if the wheel joint is later replaced. No later reader was found in the inspected TaxiController methods and its seven coroutine bodies.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TaxiController.cabMusicSource
member.summary: Manages the taxi-song playback and receives the volume changes from music ducking.

remarks.para: The controller creates this player when it is constructed. StartTaxiSong requests fenceMusic at cabMusicTransform with cashedBaseVolume. Music ducking changes this player's volume over several frames and restores the base value afterward. The player may need to obtain an audio object before the song becomes audible.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TaxiController.cabMusicTransform
member.summary: Sets the moving parent and local offset for the requested taxi-song audio object.

remarks.para: StartTaxiSong passes this transform as the audio object's parent and also passes its localPosition as the audio object's offset within that parent. A transform describes position and orientation; localPosition is relative to its parent, not the world. A zero localPosition therefore places the song at this transform's origin, while a nonzero value applies an extra offset in its axes.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TaxiController.cabReverbData
member.summary: Supplies the global echo preset requested by SwapEngineSoundSimple when its selection is 1.

remarks.para: Reverb is the echo-like sound of a space. This preset is not automatically applied to every cab sound: the simple swap helper selects it only for interior idle, while all other selections request voidReverbData. The regular SwapEngineSound method does not make this reverb request.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TaxiController.carBody
member.summary: Supplies the taxi body whose measured motion triggers the push-start and ride-complete checks.

remarks.para: A Rigidbody is the component that moves an object in the physics simulation. While waiting for a push, the controller measures this body's signed speed along its local blue Z axis, in meters per second. While waiting for a stop, it measures squared speed across all world directions, in square meters per square second.
Both checks save their result in currVelMag. The inspected taxi drive update controls splineJoint; it does not set this Rigidbody's velocity directly.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TaxiController.cashedBaseVolume
member.summary: Sets the taxi song's starting volume and the volume restored after music ducking.

remarks.para: This is an audio-volume amount: 0 is silent and 1 is the clip's unattenuated level. Despite its name, the inspected code does not capture the player's current volume into this field. It starts with a constructor value of 0.3, which scene setup or mods may replace.
The fades read this value while running and restore it at the end. For a base of 0.3, duck level 0.1, and curve blend amount 0.5, the fade-down volume is 0.2.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TaxiController.creditsLength
member.summary: Sets the scrolling portion of the credits sequence in seconds.

remarks.para: The sequence assigns the texture, waits 2 seconds, scrolls for this duration, then waits 4 seconds before clearing it. With a positive value of 60, the intended total is about 66 seconds. Actual waits and scrolling finish on frame updates.
Scrolling moves the vertical texture offset by approximately one full image height over this duration. The routine does not force a final endpoint sample. This value excludes the two pauses.

This duration and the two pauses use scaled game-time seconds. Slow motion stretches their real-world duration; the example totaling about 66 game seconds takes about 132 real seconds at a constant half-speed time scale, subject to frame updates.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TaxiController.creditsMaterial
member.summary: Holds the renderer material that the credits sequence changes to display and scroll the image.

remarks.para: A material tells a renderer how to draw a surface. Start, Unity's setup routine before normal updates, obtains creditsRenderer's material and saves it here. The credits routine sets a texture on that saved material, changes its vertical texture offset each frame, and later clears the texture.
Changing creditsRenderer after setup does not refresh this reference. The credits routine uses this saved material and does not enable the renderer itself.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TaxiController.creditsRenderer
member.summary: Provides the surface material saved during setup for displaying the scrolling credits.

remarks.para: A renderer draws an object's visible surface. Start, Unity's setup routine before normal updates, saves this renderer's material in creditsMaterial. Later credits calls change that saved material. Replacing the renderer afterward does not retarget the saved material, and the credits sequence does not turn the renderer on.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TaxiController.creditsTexture
member.summary: Supplies the image assigned to the saved material at the beginning of the credits sequence.

remarks.para: After the initial 2-second pause, the sequence changes the image's vertical texture offset over creditsLength seconds. It leaves the image assigned during a final 4-second pause, then clears that texture slot. The texture is read when the sequence starts; changing this field later does not immediately replace the material's image.

The initial pause, creditsLength scrolling interval, and final pause use scaled game-time seconds. Slow motion lengthens their real-world duration; at a constant half-speed time scale they take about twice as long, subject to frame updates. Texture assignment and cleanup still follow the stated order.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TaxiController.currVelMag
member.summary: Holds the most recent motion value for the currently running push or stop check; its meaning changes between them.

remarks.para: The push check stores signed speed along carBody's local blue Z axis in meters per second. Forward 2 m/s is 2; backward 2 m/s is -2. It compares the existing cache to velThresh before sampling again, so it can be one update behind.

The stop check first writes 20 as an initial placeholder before its first comparison; later body samples normally store squared world-speed in square meters per square second. A speed of 2 m/s then produces 4. It compares this cache to stopThresh squared. This is not a continuously updated speedometer; concurrent push and stop sequences share and overwrite this field.

velThresh is the signed local-forward speed cutoff in meters per second used by the push checker. stopThresh is a speed cutoff in meters per second whose square is used by the stop checker. The placeholder 20 is not a body-speed measurement: if stopThresh squared is at least 20, the stop sequence can complete before sampling. For example, stopThresh = 5 gives a squared cutoff of 25 and can satisfy that first test immediately. A concurrent push checker can also replace the stop value with signed speed.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TaxiController.damper_brake
member.summary: Sets how strongly the brake path-drive preset pushes the taxi toward its requested speed.

remarks.para: This is the linear physics joint's positionDamper coefficient. A physics joint is the connection guiding the taxi along its curved path. The coefficient is force per speed difference, in newton-seconds per meter: increasing it asks for a stronger correction at the same speed difference, subject to the preset's maximum force.

UpdateSpeed(4) copies it together with velocity_brake and force_brake into the drive target. Later physics updates smooth the current values toward that target using throttleTime and apply them to splineJoint. Editing this preset after selection requires selecting it again; it is not an immediately applied wheel setting.

velocity_brake is the requested speed along the path drive in meters per second. force_brake is that drive's maximum force in newtons. throttleTime is the smoothing-response time in seconds for approaching the copied speed, damper, and force targets; it describes an approximate approach rate rather than an exact deadline. The damper coefficient remains force per speed difference, in newton-seconds per meter.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TaxiController.doorClose
member.summary: Stores door-closing sound choices, but no playback trigger was verified in the inspected TaxiController code.

remarks.para: The complete inspected TaxiController methods and seven coroutine bodies do not read this array. Their push-start and stop-complete sequences both request doorOpen instead. Assigning these clips is therefore not a verified way to add a closing sound through those routines. Code outside them, including mods, was not exhaustively checked.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TaxiController.doorOpen
member.summary: Supplies door-opening sound choices requested after a successful push check and when the stop-wait sequence completes.

remarks.para: Each request uses doorTransform's current world position. The push sequence fires OnEngineStart before requesting this sound; the stop sequence fires OnRideComplete first. These requests follow scripted checks, rather than measuring whether the door has physically moved.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TaxiController.doorTransform
member.summary: Supplies the world position where the scripted door-opening sound is requested.

remarks.para: A transform describes an object's position and orientation. The push-start and stop-complete sequences read this transform's world position when requesting doorOpen. They do not pass it as an audio parent that follows the door, and they do not use its position to decide whether the door is open.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TaxiController.duckCoroutine
member.summary: Stores the running music-volume sequence and prevents a second duck request until it finishes.

remarks.para: A coroutine is a sequence that continues over several frames. StartDuckMusicCoroutine ignores a request while this field is non-null. Normal completion restores cashedBaseVolume and clears it. Merely setting this field to null does not stop an already running sequence.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TaxiController.duckCurve
member.summary: Shapes how the taxi song blends down to duckVolumeLevel and back to cashedBaseVolume.

remarks.para: The horizontal axis is elapsed time within one fade divided by duckTime: 0 is its start and 1 is its end. The vertical axis is a blend amount, clamped to 0 through 1, not an absolute volume. During fade-down, 0 chooses cashedBaseVolume and 1 chooses duckVolumeLevel; during fade-up, those endpoints reverse.

For base volume 0.3 and duck volume 0.1, a curve output of 0.5 produces volume 0.2 in either fade. A straight curve from (0, 0) to (1, 1) gives a linear blend. Each fade has its own time counter; the hold between them is the length passed to StartDuckMusicCoroutine.

Elapsed fade time and duckTime are both measured in scaled game-time seconds, so dividing them gives a unitless curve input. The hold uses that same scaled game clock. Slow motion lengthens the real-world fades and hold; at a constant half-speed time scale, the same configured times take about twice as long.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TaxiController.duckTime
member.summary: Sets the duration in seconds of each taxi-song fade, once down and once back up.

remarks.para: The hold between fades comes from StartDuckMusicCoroutine's length parameter. For duckTime = 1 and a 3-second hold, the intended total is about 5 seconds, rounded to frame updates. The code reads duckTime during the fades, so changing it while running can change their progress.

The Inspector displays a range of 0 to 4, but the inspected routine does not clamp this field to that range. A value of 0 skips the frame-by-frame fades and applies the low and restored volumes at their transition points.

Each fade and the separate hold use scaled game-time seconds. Slow motion lengthens their real-world duration: the example with two 1-second fades and a 3-second hold takes about 10 real seconds at a constant half-speed time scale, subject to frame updates. duckTime remains a configured fade duration rather than a promise of exact elapsed wall time.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TaxiController.duckVolumeLevel
member.summary: Sets the absolute taxi-song volume held between the duck-down and restore fades.

remarks.para: This is an audio-volume amount: 0 is silent and 1 is the clip's unattenuated level. It is not a fraction of cashedBaseVolume. For a base of 0.3 and duckVolumeLevel = 0.1, the hold uses 0.1, not 0.03.

The routine interpolates from cashedBaseVolume to this value, explicitly applies it for the hold, then fades back and explicitly restores the base. It does not check that this is below the base; a higher value can make the so-called duck louder. The Inspector range is not a runtime clamp in this routine.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TaxiController.engineCoroutine
member.summary: Stores the engine-loop fade sequence so the next sound swap can stop it and replace it.

remarks.para: A coroutine is a sequence that continues over several frames. SwapEngineSound stops the sequence saved here, stores a new one, and starts it. Normal completion clears the field. The audio loops can continue playing after the fade sequence finishes; this field does not mean the engine sound has stopped.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TaxiController.engineIdleExteriorLoop
member.summary: Supplies the exterior idle engine recording for engine-loop selection 0.

remarks.para: SwapEngineSound(0, blendTime) selects this clip. The loop follows engineTransform and fades on one of the two alternating engine players. Selection 0 uses engineVolume as its volume target; interior and exterior are separate recordings, not an automatically detected listener location. The fade routine also starts this clip silently on engineSource1 if that player is not already playing, before selecting the requested loop.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TaxiController.engineIdleInteriorLoop
member.summary: Supplies the interior idle engine recording for engine-loop selection 1.

remarks.para: SwapEngineSound(1, blendTime) selects this clip. The loop follows engineTransform and fades on one of the two alternating engine players. Selection 1 uses engineVolumeInterior as its volume target; interior and exterior are separate recordings, not an automatically detected listener location. The fade routine also starts this clip silently on engineSource2 if that player is not already playing, before selecting the requested loop.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TaxiController.engineSource1
member.summary: Provides one of the two alternating engine players that let a new loop fade in while the previous loop fades out.

remarks.para: The controller creates both players when constructed. An engine swap chooses one for the requested clip at engineTransform, blends that player toward the selected engine volume, and blends the other toward zero. engineSource1UsedLast determines which player is chosen. Either player can carry an interior or exterior clip.

A managed player may need to obtain an audio object before playback becomes audible. The saved player and the running fade sequence do not by themselves prove that an audio object has finished starting.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TaxiController.engineSource1UsedLast
member.summary: Chooses which engine player receives the next loop so repeated swaps alternate players.

remarks.para: If true when a swap begins, the new loop is requested on engineSource2 and this becomes false. If false, engineSource1 receives it and this becomes true. The routine then fades the selected player up and the other down. This records player selection, not successful audible playback.
