member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TimeTrial_GameController.OnKilledAll
member.summary: Notifies listeners when an ongoing kill trial has met or exceeded its quota.

remarks.para: This UnityEvent is a list of functions registered to run on notification. It receives no arguments. CheckTimeTrialKills invokes it only for KILLS mode with an ongoing session and totalEnemiesKilled greater than or equal to reqKillCount, the required integer number of kills.

Seeker requests, when their threshold is met, happen earlier. The event runs before the end sound, optional NPC despawning and EndSession. Its callbacks therefore see the session still marked ongoing. There is no separate “already fired” flag here; the normal EndSession call stops later ordinary checks from firing it until a session becomes ongoing again.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TimeTrial_GameController.despawnAllOnKillComplete
member.summary: Requests despawning of registered NPCs when the kill quota completes an ongoing kill trial.

remarks.para: Initially true. The quota-completion path reads it after OnKilledAll and the end sound request, and before EndSession. If true, calls the base DespawnAllNPCs routine; if false, this path skips that cleanup.

That routine visits registered NPC records, skips ones already marked despawned and requests their despawn effects and pooled-object removal. It is not restricted to the living-enemy list. This flag does not control the speed-run finish-trigger path, and changing it after cleanup started does not restore removed NPCs.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TimeTrial_GameController.diffReqKillCount
member.summary: Stores the requested kill quota for each difficulty index.

remarks.para: An array of integer kill counts: index 0 is EASY, 1 MEDIUM and 2 HARD. For example, [5, 10, 15] requests those quotas when the corresponding difficulty is applied. The constructor creates three entries initially containing 0; configure useful positive counts for your scene.

UpdateDifficulty reads the selected entry and passes it to SetRequiredKillCount. That setter replaces counts outside 1 through the registered profile-spawner count with the registered count. During Start, a KILLS trial with a nonempty spawnerDifficulties array applies EASY index 0. Editing this array alone does not apply a new quota or change current spawner settings.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TimeTrial_GameController.initHeavyAmmo
member.summary: Stores a heavy-ammunition setting that the inspected player-spawn method does not use.

remarks.para: The field is serialized, so it can be configured in scene data, but OnPlayerSpawn does not read it. That method uses initMedAmmo for the number of default heavy cartridges as well as medium cartridges. For example, initHeavyAmmo 50 with initMedAmmo 8 still requests 8 heavy cartridges in this path.
Changing this value alone has no verified ammunition-addition effect in the complete inspected TimeTrial_GameController methods. Counts represent individual cartridges, not ammunition boxes.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TimeTrial_GameController.initLightAmmo
member.summary: Sets how many default light cartridges are added on each player-spawn notification.

remarks.para: A positive value adds that many default light cartridges to the existing ammunition inventory.

The unit is individual cartridges. For example, 20 adds 20 rounds of light ammunition. Zero or negative values add none. This is an amount to add, not a target inventory total; repeated notifications add it repeatedly.
OnPlayerSpawn reads the value when called, so changes affect a later notification. The addition is tied to the player-spawn event rather than to every timer start.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TimeTrial_GameController.initMedAmmo
member.summary: Sets how many default medium and heavy cartridges are added on each player-spawn notification.

remarks.para: A positive value adds that many default medium cartridges and the same number of default heavy cartridges to the existing inventory. The inspected method reads this field for both categories rather than reading initHeavyAmmo.

The unit is individual cartridges. For example, 20 adds 20 rounds to each of the medium and heavy categories. Zero or negative values add none. This is an amount to add, not a target inventory total; repeated notifications add it repeatedly.
OnPlayerSpawn reads the value when called, so changes affect a later notification. The addition is tied to the player-spawn event rather than to every timer start.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TimeTrial_GameController.isSingleSpawn
member.summary: Stores a single-spawn option without a verified reader in this controller’s inspected methods.

remarks.para: The complete TimeTrial_GameController lifecycle, difficulty, spawn-request and completion methods do not read this flag or change a spawner’s repetition settings from it. Assigning it alone therefore has no verified “spawn only once” effect in those methods.

SpawnDifficultyCrates still requests every configured entry whenever called. Use the actual spawner’s settings when controlling repeated spawning; this saved Boolean is not evidence that only one wave has occurred.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TimeTrial_GameController.leaderManager
member.summary: Caches the leaderboard manager used to select a board for the current difficulty.

remarks.para: SetLeaderboardByDifficulty searches the scene for a BoneLeaderManager if this reference is missing, then saves it here. That manager selects the board at the zero-based ttDifficulty index and queries its data for display.

The reference is a cached component, meaning a saved link to an object’s behavior. It does not store the trial time or prove that a score was submitted. Changing difficulty alone does not refresh the displayed board; call SetLeaderboardByDifficulty when that update is wanted.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TimeTrial_GameController.remainSeekCount
member.summary: Offsets the registered spawner count to choose when remaining-enemy indicators are requested.

remarks.para: The initial value is 3. CheckTimeTrialKills tests totalEnemiesKilled >= profileSpawnerList.Count - remainSeekCount while spawnedSeekers is false. totalEnemiesKilled is the accumulated enemy-death count; profileSpawnerList.Count is the number of registered profile spawners. All these quantities are integer counts, not distances or seconds.

For 12 spawners and value 3, the threshold is 9 kills. A larger offset requests indicators sooner. This calculation uses registered spawner count, not the current number of living enemies; it does not mean “exactly three enemies remain.” The test runs before the session and KILLS-mode checks, and no clamp is applied to the offset.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TimeTrial_GameController.reqKillCount
member.summary: Stores the kill quota compared with the accumulated enemy-death count for completion.

remarks.para: In an ongoing KILLS trial, CheckTimeTrialKills completes when totalEnemiesKilled, the accumulated enemy-death count, is greater than or equal to this integer quota. Setting a field value alone does not immediately run that check.

SetRequiredKillCount validates the quota against the registered spawner count and refreshes text for valid requests. ProgPointKillCount adds its input to this quota without validation. UpdateDifficulty passes its configured difficulty quota through the validating setter. Direct field assignment bypasses those display and validation steps.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TimeTrial_GameController.spawnedSeekers
member.summary: Records that the pass requesting remaining-enemy indicators has started.

remarks.para: CreateActiveSpawnSeekers sets this flag before asking for any seeker objects. Normal kill checks use it to skip another automatic pass. It is a request latch, not a count of spawned objects or a test that their asynchronous creation succeeded.

A seeker is a separate indicator that points from the player toward a remaining enemy after its spawn callback assigns the target. The inspected TimeTrial_GameController methods do not reset this flag when beginning a new session. Clearing it permits another automatic request pass; it does not remove old indicators. Calling CreateActiveSpawnSeekers directly bypasses its normal false-flag check.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TimeTrial_GameController.spawnerDifficulties
member.summary: Lists the spawner profiles updated when a trial difficulty is applied.

remarks.para: UpdateDifficulty visits every entry and applies the same EASY 0, MEDIUM 1 or HARD 2 selection. A profile supplies the chosen spawn asset, AI configuration, home behavior and optional world spawn placement. Configure the array and every entry before calling the update.

During Start, a KILLS trial with a nonempty array automatically applies EASY, including that difficulty’s kill quota. SpawnDifficultyCrates separately visits this array to request spawning through each cached CrateSpawner. Applying profiles does not itself make those spawn requests. An empty array means no entries are visited; a missing array or entry can fail.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TimeTrial_GameController.timeTrialBeginClip
member.summary: Provides the optional sound requested before a trigger-started trial begins.

remarks.para: TIMETRIAL_PlayerStartTrigger requests this clip only for ON_TRIGGER starting while the session is stopped, and only when the clip is assigned. The sound request comes before BeginSession changes the session state and starts its timer.
The controller’s ON_START startup path calls BeginSession without playing this clip in the inspected Start method. A clip is stored sound data; assigning it does not start playback by itself.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TimeTrial_GameController.timeTrialEndClip
member.summary: Provides the completion sound for the speed-run finish or kill-quota path.

remarks.para: The speed-run finish method requests this sound, when assigned, before calling EndSession. The KILLS completion checker requests it after OnKilledAll and before optional NPC despawning and EndSession.

The kill checker passes this reference to audio playback without the missing-clip check used by the speed-run method. Assign a clip for that path. A playback request does not establish that a sound has finished playing, and changing the clip after the request does not retroactively choose a new sound.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TimeTrial_GameController.timeTrialEndTrigger
member.summary: Stores the scene trigger reference intended for the trial’s finish setup.

remarks.para: A trigger reports an object entering an overlap area without acting as a solid barrier. The complete inspected TimeTrial_GameController lifecycle methods do not connect this reference to a callback automatically.

Configure the scene’s player notification to call TIMETRIAL_PlayerEndTrigger. That method checks the trial mode and session state, but it does not examine this stored trigger or identify an entering player. Assigning the reference alone does not start or finish a trial.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TimeTrial_GameController.timeTrialMode
member.summary: Selects whether kills or the speed-run finish callback can complete the trial. selects the named options.

remarks.para: KILLS compares accumulated enemy deaths with the required quota during an ongoing session. SPEED_RUN permits TIMETRIAL_PlayerEndTrigger to end an ongoing session. The remaining-enemy seeker threshold is checked before the mode guard, so that particular request check is not restricted to KILLS.

Start automatically applies EASY difficulty when this value is KILLS and spawnerDifficulties is nonempty. Changing mode later affects future completion checks; it does not itself start or end a session, reset kills or rebuild spawner configuration.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TimeTrial_GameController.timeTrialStartMode
member.summary: Selects automatic startup or a later start-trigger callback. selects the named options.

remarks.para: ON_START calls BeginSession from Start, Unity’s initialization call before regular updates begin. ON_TRIGGER leaves startup to TIMETRIAL_PlayerStartTrigger, which requires the session to be stopped and optionally plays the begin sound first.

BeginSession starts the timer routine chosen by the inherited timerMode; a coroutine is a routine that resumes over later frames. Changing this selector after initialization does not replay Start or automatically begin a stopped session. Configure the scene notification when using ON_TRIGGER.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TimeTrial_GameController.timeTrialStartTrigger
member.summary: Stores the scene trigger reference intended for the trial’s start setup.

remarks.para: A trigger reports an object entering an overlap area without acting as a solid barrier. The complete inspected TimeTrial_GameController lifecycle methods do not connect this reference to a callback automatically.

Configure the scene’s player notification to call TIMETRIAL_PlayerStartTrigger. That method checks the trial mode and session state, but it does not examine this stored trigger or identify an entering player. Assigning the reference alone does not start or finish a trial.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TimeTrial_GameController.ttDifficulty
member.summary: Stores the difficulty index used for quota, spawner-profile and leaderboard selection. selects the named options.

remarks.para: EASY is index 0, MEDIUM 1 and HARD 2. UpdateDifficulty stores this value first, reads that index in diffReqKillCount and applies it to every spawnerDifficulties entry. SetLeaderboardByDifficulty separately uses it as the board-list index.

Directly assigning the field does not apply the quota, update profiles or change the displayed board. For KILLS mode with a nonempty profile array, Start overwrites it with EASY. Use valid array indices; there is no general clamp, and a failing update can leave this selected index changed before the remaining work completes.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Treadmill.directionMill
member.summary: Sets how quickly the material's texture offset changes horizontally and vertically, in texture-coordinate units per game second.

remarks.para: The x value controls horizontal texture scrolling and y controls vertical scrolling. These are texture directions, not the object's directions in the 3D scene. Texture coordinates, also called UVs, tell the material which part of an image to draw on a surface; an offset of 1 moves by one full texture-coordinate width or height.

On each frame, the component sets the offset to (x × t, y × t). Here x and y are the two current directionMill values in texture-coordinate units per second, and t is the current elapsed game time from Time.time, in seconds. This replaces the old offset rather than adding to it. For example, (0.25, 0) gives a horizontal offset of 2 at 8 seconds. A negative value scrolls in the opposite direction.

The values are read again every frame. Changing them during play can jump the offset because the new values are multiplied by all the elapsed game time, not just the time since the change. Setting both values to zero resets the offset to (0, 0) on the next update.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Treadmill.materialMill
member.summary: Holds the material whose _BaseMap texture offset this component replaces on each frame.

remarks.para: A material describes how an object's surface is drawn. Start, Unity's one-time startup call for this component, finds a Renderer on the same object and stores that renderer's material here. A Renderer is the component that draws the object. This startup assignment replaces a material reference assigned earlier.

Later updates use the material currently stored here without looking up the renderer again. Assigning a different material after startup makes later frames update that material; replacing only the renderer's material leaves this stored reference pointing to the earlier material. The material needs a _BaseMap texture property whose offset affects its visible surface.

For example, let startup choose the belt object's material, then set directionMill to (0.1, 0) to change its horizontal texture offset by 0.1 texture-coordinate units per game second. The component changes the material's appearance; its inspected update does not move the belt object or push objects resting on it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Trial_SpawnerEvents.OnKilledAll
member.summary: Listener actions invoked when a reported death reaches the stored local quota while the completion flag is false.

remarks.para: A UnityEvent is a list of actions connected in the editor or by code. This event passes no arguments. Both death handlers first increment deadCount, then invoke this event if deadCount is at least totalCount and sentKillEvent is false.

The stored quota comes from the array-length-times-fraction calculation; useSpawnerTotal changes the startup total broadcast, not this local quota. Startup and GetTotalCountFromPerc do not invoke completion merely because the quota is already zero or met: a death-handler call performs the check.

The completion sound and sentKillEvent assignment happen after the listeners. The death-count display is refreshed afterward. The flag normally prevents later completion dispatches, but is still false during the listeners, so a listener that reports another death can cause another invocation.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Trial_SpawnerEvents.OnTotalKillCalc
member.summary: Shared callback that startup can invoke with this component's configured spawner count or calculated death quota.

remarks.para: This is a static Action<int>: a callback shared by all instances of this type, passing one integer count to its listeners. Startup sends it only when sendTotalEvents is true and a listener is assigned.

With useSpawnerTotal true, the argument is crateSpawners.Length, even when the calculated local quota differs. With useSpawnerTotal false, the argument is totalCount, but only when totalCount is positive. For five entries and requiredPerc 0.5, the local quota is three; this callback receives five with the flag true and three with it false.

GetTotalCountFromPerc only stores counts and does not invoke this callback. A received count describes the startup calculation or configured array, not proof that that many enemies successfully spawned or died.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Trial_SpawnerEvents.crateSpawners
member.summary: The configured entries watched for new enemies and counted when calculating the local quota.

remarks.para: When enabled, this component registers itself as a spawn listener on every entry. When disabled, it unregisters from the entries in the current array. Changing the array by itself does not repeat registration. The array and each referenced spawner must be supplied.

For a newly spawned object, the listener requires an AIBrain AI-control component and a recognized pool component before subscribing to its death event. Disabling this component unregisters future spawn notifications; that method does not remove the death callbacks already attached to previously spawned brains.

The array length, including inactive or repeated entries, supplies the quota calculation and the optional startup broadcast. It is a count of configured slots, not a count of currently active spawners or successful enemy spawns.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Trial_SpawnerEvents.deadCount
member.summary: The number of death reports recorded by this component.

remarks.para: Each OnDeath or OnSpawnerDeath call adds one, including calls after completion and repeated reports about the same enemy. The count is measured in reported deaths, not checked unique enemies. Both methods compare the updated count with totalCount and then refresh deadText if assigned.

The inspected enable, disable, startup and quota-recalculation methods do not reset this count. Changing it directly does not update the display or invoke completion; those effects occur in the death handlers.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Trial_SpawnerEvents.deadText
member.summary: Optional text component refreshed with the recorded death count after each death-handler call.

remarks.para: Both death handlers write deadCount as an integer string to this text when the text component exists. On a completion call, the event listeners and sound request happen before this update. For example, the listener for a third death can still see "2" on the display until it returns.
Assigning the field, enabling the component or recalculating the quota does not refresh this text in the inspected methods. It displays recorded death reports, not the number of living enemies.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Trial_SpawnerEvents.killAllClip
member.summary: The sound clip requested after completion listeners run and before the completion flag is set.

remarks.para: OnSpawnerDeath checks that this clip exists before requesting it. OnDeath requests it without that clip check. Both use a 2D one-shot sound, meaning a single sound without a world-position source, with a requested volume multiplier of 0.5, or half the normal setting.

The sound belongs to the same completion test as OnKilledAll: updated deadCount must be at least totalCount and sentKillEvent must be false. That flag is set after the sound request, so the request is not itself proof that playback completed.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Trial_SpawnerEvents.requiredPerc
member.summary: The unitless fraction of configured spawner entries used to calculate the local death quota.

remarks.para: The quota is the configured array length multiplied by requiredPerc, then rounded upward to an integer. The array length is the number of crateSpawners entries, and requiredPerc is a unitless fraction: 0.5 means half, while 1 means all. For five entries and 0.5, the product is 2.5 and the quota becomes three deaths. Inactive entries still count toward the length; this does not count how many enemies have actually spawned.

Both startup and GetTotalCountFromPerc perform this calculation. They do not clamp the fraction to zero through one. For example, 1.5 with five entries produces a quota of eight. The native multiplication uses a float before rounding upward, so values very close to an integer boundary follow that stored floating-point result.

The default is 1. Changing the fraction afterward does not automatically update totalCount or either display. useSpawnerTotal does not bypass this calculation; it selects the startup callback's payload.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Trial_SpawnerEvents.sendTotalEvents
member.summary: Whether startup sends the optional shared total-count callback.

remarks.para: The default is true. When startup runs and this flag is true, it invokes OnTotalKillCalc if a listener exists. useSpawnerTotal chooses the payload: true sends the configured array length; false sends the local calculated quota only if that quota is positive.

This flag does not control OnKilledAll, the death count or the quota calculation. GetTotalCountFromPerc does not send the total callback even when this flag is true. Changing the flag after startup does not by itself send a new callback.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Trial_SpawnerEvents.sentKillEvent
member.summary: The saved flag checked to prevent later completion dispatches after a death handler finishes its completion sequence.

remarks.para: Both death handlers require this flag to be false before invoking OnKilledAll. They set it true after the listeners and completion sound request, then update the displayed death count. It can be true even when no OnKilledAll listeners are assigned, because the flag records completion handling rather than proving a listener ran.

The flag is still false while listeners execute, so calling a death handler from a listener can enter completion again. Later calls continue to count deaths but normally skip completion. The inspected enable, disable, startup and quota-recalculation methods do not reset this flag for another round.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Trial_SpawnerEvents.spawnerCount
member.summary: The configured spawner-array length most recently stored by GetTotalCountFromPerc.

remarks.para: The value counts array entries, including inactive or repeated entries, rather than checking active spawners. GetTotalCountFromPerc writes crateSpawners.Length here at the same time it updates totalCount.

Startup calculates its quota and callback payload directly from the array length without updating this field. No consumer of this saved field appears in the complete methods inspected for this class. For example, startup can broadcast five configured entries while this field still has its default zero until explicit recalculation.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Trial_SpawnerEvents.totalCount
member.summary: The stored number of reported deaths used as this component's completion threshold.

remarks.para: The quota is the configured array length multiplied by requiredPerc, then rounded upward to an integer. The array length is the number of crateSpawners entries, and requiredPerc is a unitless fraction: 0.5 means half, while 1 means all. For five entries and 0.5, the product is 2.5 and the quota becomes three deaths. Inactive entries still count toward the length; this does not count how many enemies have actually spawned.

Startup and GetTotalCountFromPerc overwrite this field with that calculation even when useSpawnerTotal is true. Each death handler increments deadCount, then completes when the new count is at least this value and sentKillEvent is false.

Setting a zero or already-met quota does not invoke completion immediately; a death-handler call performs the check. Startup writes totalText with the calculated value, while explicit GetTotalCountFromPerc does not refresh that display. The shared total callback can send the full array length instead of this local threshold.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Trial_SpawnerEvents.totalText
member.summary: Optional text component set to the calculated local death quota at startup.

remarks.para: Startup writes totalCount as an integer string here after calculating it from the configured array length and requiredPerc. This happens before the optional OnTotalKillCalc callback. If useSpawnerTotal is true, that callback can receive a different number: for five entries and a half fraction, this display shows "3" while the callback receives five.
The text is not refreshed by GetTotalCountFromPerc or the death handlers in the inspected methods. A later quota change can therefore leave the displayed value behind the stored threshold.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Trial_SpawnerEvents.useSpawnerTotal
member.summary: Chooses whether the startup total callback receives the configured spawner count or the calculated local death quota.

remarks.para: The default is true. With sendTotalEvents enabled and a listener assigned, true sends crateSpawners.Length. False sends totalCount, but only if that calculated value is positive.

This flag does not choose the local completion threshold. Startup still sets totalCount to the array length multiplied by requiredPerc and rounded upward. For example, five entries and requiredPerc 0.5 give a three-death local quota; true broadcasts five and false broadcasts three.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TutorialElevator.abortDoorClip
member.summary: Sound requested at the elevator's position whenever StopDoorRoutine is called.

remarks.para: The abort sound is requested even if no door sequence was running. StopDoorRoutine uses the hard-interaction audio mixer group; changing this clip changes that cancellation sound, not whether the doors reopen.
An audio mixer group routes sound through shared volume and effect settings; those settings can change how this clip sounds.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TutorialElevator.director
member.summary: Timeline player started after the timed closing sequence seals the elevator doors.

remarks.para: A PlayableDirector plays a prepared timeline of animations and actions. CoDoorRoutine calls Play after the closing delay, sound and SealDoors. Merely replacing this reference does not start the timeline; the closing sequence must reach that step, and an assigned director is required there.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TutorialElevator.doorBodies
member.summary: Door-panel physics bodies that SealDoors freezes and snaps to the scripted closed positions.

remarks.para: A Rigidbody lets an object move in the physics simulation. SealDoors makes all bodies in this array kinematic, so forces no longer move them, then rewrites the first four panels' local X positions while preserving Y/Z. Their parent-relative X values become about -1.60, -0.34, -1.60 and -0.33 Unity length units, conventionally meters at parent scale 1.
Assign at least four valid panels in the expected order. This is a setup list, not a measurement of which panels are currently closed.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TutorialElevator.doorCloseClip
member.summary: Sound requested after the closing delay, just before the panels are sealed and the ride timeline begins.

remarks.para: CoDoorRoutine plays this at the elevator's world position through the hard-interaction audio mixer group, then calls SealDoors and director.Play. A direct CloseDoors call does not play this clip.
The audio mixer group routes the sound through shared volume and effect settings. It is the routing used by this sound request, not a request to change when the doors close.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TutorialElevator.doorPower
member.summary: Optional power-logic output receiving -1 to request opening or +1 to request closing.

remarks.para: OPENCLOSEDOOR(true) writes -1 and OPENCLOSEDOOR(false) writes +1. StartElevator writes +1 when the player-inside flag is true. These numbers are control signals with no physical units; connected logic determines the door response.
OpenDoors and CloseDoors separately send 0 or 1 to the powerableJoints controllers. Changing this reference or its output does not itself update isClosing or run the doorway cleanup.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TutorialElevator.doorRoutine
member.summary: Stored handle that prevents StartElevator from starting a second timed door-closing sequence while it is non-null.

remarks.para: A coroutine is a sequence that continues across frames; its handle lets Unity stop that sequence. StartElevator stores this handle after starting CoDoorRoutine. Natural completion leaves it assigned, so non-null does not prove the sequence is still running.

StopDoorRoutine stops the assigned handle when present, plays the abort sound, and clears this field. Setting the field to null yourself does not stop the existing sequence and can allow another to start.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TutorialElevator.doorSeel
member.summary: Optional object activated when StartMoveUpward begins the simulated ascent.

remarks.para: The inspected elevator code turns this object on; it does not inspect its components to prove a physical door seal, and does not turn it off later. Its actual visible or collision effect depends on the object assigned in the scene.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TutorialElevator.doorTrig
member.summary: Optional doorway-object tracker notified immediately after the door controllers receive a close request.

remarks.para: CloseDoors calls its OnDoorClose before DoorEmancipator. The inspected ElevatorDoorTrigger sends a 10-point attack to its tracked destructible objects when it is not configured as an exit trigger. It is not a sensor proving that the door panels have reached their closed positions.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TutorialElevator.doorTrigCol
member.summary: Doorway trigger collider disabled by SealDoors before the shaft and panel changes.

remarks.para: A trigger collider is a volume that reports overlap instead of acting as a solid obstacle. SealDoors turns this collider off and requires an assigned reference. The inspected elevator methods do not re-enable it when OpenDoors is called.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TutorialElevator.doorWaitDuration
member.summary: Game-time delay, in seconds, between requesting door closure and playing the closing sound and sealing the panels.

remarks.para: CoDoorRoutine performs the closing request and doorway cleanup first, then creates a WaitForSeconds using this value. After the wait resumes it plays doorCloseClip, runs SealDoors and starts director. A value of 1.5 requests a one-and-a-half-second wait after closure is requested; it does not hold the doors open for that time.

The wait follows Unity's scaled game time and resumes on a frame, so its actual elapsed time can be longer. Changing this field after the wait has been created does not alter that already-created wait.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TutorialElevator.elevatorAudioSources
member.summary: Audio sources routed to the hard-interaction mixer group during the elevator's Start setup.

remarks.para: An audio mixer group routes sounds through shared volume and effects settings. Start is Unity's setup callback, a routine Unity calls before this component's first frame update. It changes each assigned source's output group; it does not play the sources. The array and its elements must be valid.
Changing this array after Start does not automatically route the new sources. The closing and abort sounds are requested separately through Audio3dManager.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TutorialElevator.elevatorBody
member.summary: Cab Rigidbody made kinematic by StartImpact so physics forces stop moving the cab.

remarks.para: A Rigidbody is the component that simulates a moving body in physics. Kinematic mode leaves movement to scripts rather than forces. The impact step sets this mode; replacing the reference alone does not freeze a body, and the inspected elevator methods do not switch it back.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TutorialElevator.emancipatorBounds
member.summary: Full side lengths in meters of the box that DoorEmancipator searches for entities to remove.

remarks.para: The X/Y/Z lengths follow emancipatorPoint's rotated axes, centered on its world position. The physics query halves these values internally: (2, 1, 0.5), for example, extends 1 meter, 0.5 meter and 0.25 meter each way from the center. emancipatorPoint's transform scale is not multiplied into the query size.
The selected-component editor preview uses the same position, rotation and full size. Changing the lengths affects the next query or preview; it does not run cleanup immediately.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TutorialElevator.emancipatorPoint
member.summary: Supplies the cleanup box's world center and rotation for .

remarks.para: The box's full side lengths come from emancipatorBounds in meters, along this point's rotated X/Y/Z directions. Its scale does not resize the physics query. Moving or rotating the point changes the next cleanup area and the selected-component editor preview.
DoorEmancipator requires this reference; the editor preview simply draws nothing when it is absent.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TutorialElevator.fallSpeed
member.summary: Target shaft-scenery speed reached at the end of the two-second fall transition.

remarks.para: CoFallRoutine writes each shaft's speed as fallSpeed times p, where p is elapsed game time divided by 2 seconds, limited to 0 through 1. In the downward-ride state, positive speed moves the scenery along each shaft's own positive Y direction to simulate the cab falling.

The setting is in meters per second before the shaft loop multiplies it by Time.fixedDeltaTime, the physics-step duration in seconds, each iteration. For an illustrative fallSpeed of 2 and a 0.02-second physics step, full progress requests 0.04 meter of scenery movement per iteration. The loop uses frame waits, so this setting is not a guaranteed measured cab speed.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TutorialElevator.gravityGoal
member.summary: Global gravity target approached during the two-second transition into the elevator fall.

remarks.para: This is a world-axis acceleration vector in meters per second squared, affecting the entire physics scene. CoFallRoutine saves the starting gravity, then blends from that saved vector toward this one using p = elapsed game time / 2 seconds, limited to 0 through 1.

For example, (0, 4, 0) requests upward acceleration of 4 meters per second squared along world Y. Changing the field during that transition changes its next gravity calculation. The following near-weightless sequence has a separate target of (0, -0.1, 0).

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TutorialElevator.hubSpawnLocation
member.summary: Integer initialized to 9, with no verified spawn-location effect in the inspected elevator code.

remarks.para: The complete TutorialElevator methods and six movement/door sequence bodies, plus the inspected TutorialShaft loop and ElevatorDoorTrigger methods, do not read this field to select a spawn. Changing it is therefore not a verified way to move the player's hub arrival point in that code. Other game code and mods were not exhaustively checked.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TutorialElevator.isClosing
member.summary: Records that door closing has been requested, rather than measuring whether a panel is still moving.

remarks.para: CloseDoors sets this true before sending voltage 1 to the door joint controllers and running doorway cleanup. OpenDoors and SealDoors clear it at the start of their work. StopDoorRoutine does not clear it.
A true value can remain after a timed sequence is stopped, and false can be written before the panels finish moving. Writing this flag yourself does not move any doors or cancel the timed sequence.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TutorialElevator.layerMask
member.summary: Selects the physics layers whose solid colliders can lead to entity removal in DoorEmancipator.

remarks.para: A layer mask is a set of enabled layer bits. Only overlapping colliders on those layers are included; trigger volumes are ignored. Matching results must have an attached Rigidbody, the moving physics-body component, for this routine's MarrowBody lookup.
Changing the mask affects the next cleanup query. It does not change a collider's own layer or define which layers the elevator can collide with during normal movement.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TutorialElevator.leftSparkler
member.summary: Spark particle system whose GameObject is activated during the near-weightless fall and deactivated at impact.

remarks.para: CoFallingZeroG turns the containing object on before beginning its three-second gravity blend, and StartImpact turns it off before freezing the cab. The code changes object activation rather than calling ParticleSystem.Play or Stop; the assigned particle system's own settings determine when particles emit.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TutorialElevator.moveUpRoutine
member.summary: Stored handle for the shaft-scenery slowdown started by SlowUpwardMovement.

remarks.para: A coroutine is a sequence that continues across frames; its handle lets Unity stop that sequence. StartMoveDownward stops this handle when assigned, but does not clear the field. Natural completion also leaves the handle assigned, so non-null does not prove a slowdown is still running.
StartMoveUpward does not store its shaft loops here. Replacing or clearing the handle alone does not stop an already-running sequence.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TutorialElevator.ogShaftObj
member.summary: Shaft scene object activated by SealDoors before the ride begins.

remarks.para: SealDoors turns both shaft-object references on; it does not choose one according to which shaft the cab occupies. These references must be assigned. The inspected elevator methods do not turn them off later, and the visible or collision effect depends on the assigned object's contents.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TutorialElevator.otherShaftObj
member.summary: Shaft scene object activated by SealDoors before the ride begins.

remarks.para: SealDoors turns both shaft-object references on; it does not choose one according to which shaft the cab occupies. These references must be assigned. The inspected elevator methods do not turn them off later, and the visible or collision effect depends on the assigned object's contents.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TutorialElevator.outerDoorObjs
member.summary: Scene objects hidden by SealDoors after both shaft objects are activated.

remarks.para: Every assigned object is deactivated as part of the sealed ride setup. This does not command the moving panels through their joints; doorBodies separately holds the panels that are frozen and placed. The inspected elevator methods do not reactivate these objects in OpenDoors.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TutorialElevator.pHealth
member.summary: Cached player health component made invincible when StartElevator runs with playerInElevator true and passed to the scripted impact step.

remarks.para: Only when playerInElevator is true does StartElevator fill this from PlayerRefs if it is missing and set its health mode to Invincible. With that flag false, the call returns without acquiring this component or changing its health mode. A valid cached reference is reused rather than looked up again. StartImpact calls its Dying routine with argument 8 if it is assigned.

In the inspected Player_Health implementation, that Dying call in Invincible mode sets current health to 0 without calling Death. The elevator does not restore the earlier health mode in the inspected completion sequence.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TutorialElevator.perc
member.summary: Shared 0-to-1 time progress for the shaft slowdown, fall transition, and near-weightless gravity and joint-target sequence.

remarks.para: Each running sequence calculates this from elapsed game time divided by its duration: 2 seconds for the slowdown and initial fall, 3 seconds for the near-weightless sequence. The time mapping limits the calculated value to 0 through 1. The fall and near-weightless sequences reset it on entry; the slowdown does not.

For example, 0.5 means halfway through whichever sequence last wrote the field, not halfway through the entire ride. The sequences also check it to decide when to end. Manually writing 1 or more can make a sequence finish at its next check, and concurrent sequences can overwrite each other's progress.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TutorialElevator.playerInElevator
member.summary: Stored player-inside flag that must be true for StartElevator to perform its startup actions.

remarks.para: EnterExitElevator directly writes this flag; it is not a position check. StartElevator returns immediately when it is false. Changing it does not move the player or automatically stop a ride or door sequence already underway.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TutorialElevator.powerableJoints
member.summary: Door joint controllers receiving voltage 0 from OpenDoors or voltage 1 from CloseDoors.

remarks.para: A physics joint is a connection guiding a panel's movement. Each Powerable_Joint stores the supplied voltage and, when powered, changes its configured position, velocity or drive settings. Those controller settings decide how the door responds; the array does not report that the requested positions were reached.
The array and each controller must be assigned. These are direct door-control targets, separate from the signed -1/+1 signal written to doorPower.
The values 0 and 1 are unitless control signals, not physical electrical voltages. A drive is the joint's force settings that try to make the panel follow a requested position or speed.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TutorialElevator.rightSparkler
member.summary: Spark particle system whose GameObject is activated during the near-weightless fall and deactivated at impact.

remarks.para: CoFallingZeroG turns the containing object on before beginning its three-second gravity blend, and StartImpact turns it off before freezing the cab. The code changes object activation rather than calling ParticleSystem.Play or Stop; the assigned particle system's own settings determine when particles emit.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TutorialElevator.shaftColliderObj
member.summary: Shaft collision object activated at the end of SealDoors.

remarks.para: Activation happens after the panels are made kinematic and the first four are placed at their scripted closed X positions. The assigned object's contents determine the actual blocking shape. The inspected elevator methods do not deactivate it again or require a measured door-closure state before enabling it.
Kinematic means the physics body is moved by scripts rather than by physics forces.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TutorialElevator.sparksCrate
member.summary: Spawnable-crate reference with no verified spark-spawning effect in the inspected elevator code.

remarks.para: The complete TutorialElevator methods and six sequence bodies, plus the inspected TutorialShaft loop and ElevatorDoorTrigger methods, do not read this reference or request a spawn from it. The verified fall sparks instead come from activating the objects holding leftSparkler and rightSparkler. Other game code and mods were not exhaustively checked.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TutorialElevator.spikeGravGoal
member.summary: Global gravity applied briefly by the completion sequence before the saved gravity is restored.

remarks.para: This is a world-axis acceleration vector in meters per second squared. CoComplete writes it to Physics.gravity, waits for the next fixed-update continuation, restores startGrav, and then requests Descent level completion. The gravity change affects the physics scene, including objects outside the cab.

For example, (0, -500, 0) requests strong downward world-Y acceleration. It is an acceleration setting, not an impact force or a duration, and the sequence does not interpolate toward it. Changing it after that initial write does not alter the already-applied pulse.

startGrav is the global gravity saved at the beginning of CoFallRoutine, with world X, Y and Z acceleration components in meters per second squared. Before that snapshot the constructor initializes it to (0, -9.81, 0). Completion restores this stored vector rather than measuring gravity again.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TutorialElevator.stage1Speed
member.summary: Shaft-scenery speed copied into every shaft when StartMoveUpward begins the simulated ascent.

remarks.para: Positive values move scenery opposite each shaft's own Y direction. The setting is in meters per second before each shaft loop multiplies it by Time.fixedDeltaTime, the physics-step duration in seconds. With an illustrative setting of 2 and a 0.02-second step, each iteration requests 0.04 meter of scenery movement. Frame waits in the loop mean this is not a guaranteed measured cab speed.

StartMoveUpward copies the value once; changing it afterward does not automatically change the shafts already running. CoInitialBreakRoutine reads it again on each slowdown update and writes stage1Speed times (1 - p), where p is elapsed game time divided by 2 seconds, limited to 0 through 1.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TutorialElevator.startGrav
member.summary: Saved global gravity restored after the impact pulse and when this elevator component is destroyed.

remarks.para: CoFallRoutine copies Physics.gravity here when the fall transition begins, not when StartElevator is called. The vector uses world X/Y/Z axes and meters per second squared. The fall blend reads this saved starting acceleration; CoComplete and OnDestroy later restore it to the physics scene.

Before a fall has captured the actual scene gravity, the constructor initializes this to (0, -9.81, 0). Changing this field changes what will be restored; it does not immediately apply gravity on its own.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TutorialElevator.tutShafts
member.summary: Shaft scenery sections whose loops and speed settings create the illusion of the elevator traveling.

remarks.para: StartMoveUpward starts every loop, sets MOVING_UP and copies stage1Speed. The slowdown adjusts their speed toward 0; the fall transition sets MOVING_DOWN and ramps speed toward fallSpeed. StartImpact sets STOPPED and cancels each loop.

The shaft loop translates along each section's own Y axis and wraps sections using this array's length, that section's shaftHeight and its local Y scale. The sections' elevator references and sizes must be set consistently. These are moving scenery objects, not a list of destinations the cab selects.

For wrapping, the array length is the number of scenery sections, shaftHeight is each section's height setting in Unity length units, and local Y scale is that section's unitless Y size multiplier. Their product is the wrap distance along the parent's local Y axis: number of sections times local Y scale times shaftHeight.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TutorialElevator.vatorColliders
member.summary: Elevator objects whose physics layers SealDoors resets to Unity's default layer, layer 0.

remarks.para: This array holds GameObjects. SealDoors changes each object's own layer after freezing the door bodies; it does not enable or disable collider components or recursively change child layers. The array and its elements must be valid. The collision effect depends on the project's layer-collision settings.
A GameObject is a scene object that holds components, such as a collider or a renderer.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TutorialElevator.vatorJoint
member.summary: Physics connection whose limits, pivot and target position shape the scripted cab swing and fall.

remarks.para: A ConfigurableJoint connects objects in the physics simulation and constrains how they can move. ReleaseJointRot makes all rotation axes and Y/Z translation limited; CoFallRoutine also makes X translation limited. LimitJointRot sets Y/Z angular limits to 1 degree. CoSwing and SwingImpact change its local anchor, the attachment point on its own object.

During CoFallingZeroG, its target position becomes (xPos, 5 times yCurve(p), zPos), where p is elapsed game time divided by 3 seconds, limited to 0 through 1. xPos and zPos are stored X and Z target lengths in meters, and yCurve(p) is the curve output scaled by 5 meters to form the Y target. These are coordinates for the connection's target, not the cab's measured world position. Its configured frame, drives and limits determine the resulting motion.
The joint's drives are force settings that try to follow its requested position or speed. They act within the joint's configured movement limits.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TutorialElevator.vatorRoutine
member.summary: Optional stored coroutine handle that OnDestroy stops after restoring saved gravity.

remarks.para: A coroutine is a sequence that continues across frames, and its handle lets Unity stop it. No assignment to this field was found in the complete inspected TutorialElevator methods, six sequence bodies, TutorialShaft loop or ElevatorDoorTrigger methods. The fall, swing and completion starters do not store their handles here.

It therefore does not reliably report the main ride's current state in that inspected code. Other game code or mods could assign a handle. Clearing the field alone would not stop an already-running sequence.
Unity calls OnDestroy when this component is destroyed, which is when the inspected stop operation uses this handle.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TutorialElevator.xCurve
member.summary: Curve with no verified movement effect in the inspected elevator code.

remarks.para: The complete TutorialElevator methods and six sequence bodies, plus the inspected TutorialShaft loop and ElevatorDoorTrigger methods, do not evaluate this curve. Its input and output units therefore cannot be established from that code, and editing its keys is not a verified way to move the cab there.
The near-weightless sequence evaluates only yCurve and passes stored xPos and zPos directly into the joint target. Other game code and mods were not exhaustively checked.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TutorialElevator.xPos
member.summary: Stored X coordinate included in the elevator joint target during the near-weightless fall.

remarks.para: Each CoFallingZeroG update sends (xPos, yPos, zPos) to vatorJoint.targetPosition. The X coordinate is a length in meters in the joint's target-position frame, which depends on its configuration; it is not the cab's measured world X position. Changing it affects the next target write, and the actual cab response depends on joint drives and limits.
No calculation of this field from xCurve was found in the complete inspected elevator methods and six sequence bodies. Its value is not refreshed from the current Transform position in those bodies.

yPos and zPos are the accompanying stored Y and Z target lengths, also in meters in the configured joint frame. The near-weightless sequence recalculates yPos from its Y curve while keeping the stored X and Z inputs. Joint drives are force settings that try to follow these requested positions or speeds.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TutorialElevator.yCurve
member.summary: Controls the Y target of the elevator's physics connection during the three-second near-weightless fall.

remarks.para: The horizontal input p is elapsed game time divided by 3 seconds, limited to 0 through 1. The vertical output is multiplied by 5 meters to produce yPos. A value of 0.4 at p = 0.5 requests a Y target of 2 meters halfway through that phase; a flat curve at 0 requests a zero Y target.

The routine writes (xPos, yPos, zPos) to vatorJoint.targetPosition. This is a requested physics-connection position, not a measured cab height. The configured joint frame determines the axes, and its drives and limits determine the actual movement. Changing the curve affects later evaluations while the sequence runs.
xPos and zPos are the stored X and Z target lengths in meters in the joint's configured target-position frame. Its drives are force settings that try to follow the requested position or speed.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TutorialElevator.yPos
member.summary: Most recently calculated Y target for the elevator joint during the near-weightless fall.

remarks.para: Each CoFallingZeroG update overwrites this with 5 times yCurve(p) meters, where p is elapsed game time divided by 3 seconds, limited to 0 through 1. For example, a curve output of 0.4 gives a 2-meter Y target. The same update sends (xPos, yPos, zPos) to vatorJoint.targetPosition.

This is a target coordinate in the joint's configured frame, not the cab's measured height. Manually writing yPos while that sequence runs is overwritten on its next update; edit yCurve to change the ongoing requested Y motion.

xPos and zPos are the accompanying stored X and Z target lengths in meters in the joint's configured frame. A physics joint is the connection that guides how bodies move relative to each other; this target asks that connection for a position rather than measuring the cab.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TutorialElevator.zPos
member.summary: Stored Z coordinate included in the elevator joint target during the near-weightless fall.

remarks.para: Each CoFallingZeroG update sends (xPos, yPos, zPos) to vatorJoint.targetPosition. xPos and zPos are the stored X and Z target values in Unity units; they correspond to metres only if the scene uses 1 Unity unit = 1 metre. yPos is the Y target, calculated from the phase's curve. A physics joint is a connection that guides movement between objects; its configuration determines the target's coordinate frame. zPos is not the cab's measured world Z position.

Changing zPos affects the next target write while that sequence runs. The actual cab response depends on the joint's movement limits and drive settings, which control how it tries to reach its target. No calculation of zPos from zCurve or the cab's Transform position was found in the complete inspected TutorialElevator methods and six sequence bodies.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TutorialGrip.handChoice
member.summary: Chooses which controller tutorial is displayed and which hand’s grab or release can start or stop it.

remarks.para: both displays tutorials for both hands when either hand starts it. either displays the tutorial for the hand that caused the grab notification. left and right require a grab notification from that hand and select its tutorial. none does not start a tutorial through the normal grab callbacks.

For both and either, the grab callback starts the tutorial only if TutorialRig does not already have an active tutorial. left and right do not make that same active-tutorial check. tutorialRepeatCount is the remaining number of automatic tutorial starts: zero blocks these grab callbacks, and a positive value decreases after a send. A negative value permits repeated starts through the notification route selected by specificGrip. Positive counts are not additionally restricted to that route.

When exitEnds is true, meaning releasing the object should end its tutorial, this choice also controls release handling. For both and either, a release from either hand stops an active tutorial; it does not wait for both hands to release. left and right stop it only for the selected hand, without the same active-tutorial check. none does not stop it through these release branches. specificGrip selects whether release notifications come from targetGrip (true) or the object containing the grip points, its host (false).

This selects instructions shown to the player; it does not prevent the other hand from physically grabbing the object. The choice is passed into TutorialRig when TUTORIALSEND runs, so editing it alone does not rebuild an already displayed tutorial.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TutorialGrip.highlightLoc_left
member.summary: Chooses the directional arrow prompts around the left controller’s joystick in the tutorial display.

remarks.para: Use the LocationHighlight values ending in _l: none_l clears the left arrow display, left_l/right_l/up_l/down_l select one direction, upDown_l and leftRight_l select a pair, and all_l enables the full arrow set. These are labels for instructional arrows, not world directions, position coordinates, or limits on controller movement.

This is separate from inputHighlight_left: for example, joystick can blink the joystick drawing while leftRight_l adds horizontal direction prompts. Values ending in _r are handled by the right-side selection, so do not put them in this field.

The setting is applied when TUTORIALSEND runs. A non-none selection enables its chosen arrow objects without first clearing every previously enabled direction; none_l clears the set. Changing the field alone does not redraw a running tutorial.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TutorialGrip.highlightLoc_right

remarks.para: Use the LocationHighlight values ending in _r: none_r clears the right arrow display, left_r/right_r/up_r/down_r select one direction, upDown_r and leftRight_r select a pair, and all_r enables the full arrow set. This is separate from inputHighlight_right: for example, joystick can blink the joystick drawing while upDown_r adds vertical direction prompts. none_l does not mean no right-side arrows; choose none_r for this field.

The setting is applied when TUTORIALSEND runs. A non-none selection enables its chosen arrow objects without first clearing every previously enabled direction; none_r clears the set. Changing the field alone does not redraw a running tutorial.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TutorialGrip.inputHighlight_left
member.summary: Chooses the part of the left controller drawing that blinks to show the player which input to use.

remarks.para: trigger, button_A, button_B, grip, and joystick select the matching renderer on the controller tutorial art. gripTrig starts both trigger and grip highlights. none starts no new highlight. The audited ControllerTutorialArt.HIGHLIGHTACTION has no implemented touchpad selection, so choosing touchpad does not start a blink through that method.

For example, use trigger for an instruction to pull the index trigger, or gripTrig for an instruction involving both trigger and grip squeeze. This is a visual cue; this field does not make pressing that input complete the tutorial or change how the object is held.
The value is sent when TUTORIALSEND runs. Editing it alone does not change a running highlight. Use highlightLoc_left separately to add direction arrows.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TutorialRig.Instance
member.summary: The tutorial rig most recently registered during Awake, Unity's initialization callback.

remarks.para: Game tutorial triggers use this reference to call CUSTOMTUTORIAL on the shared controller display. Check that the Unity object exists and its GameObject is active before expecting a tutorial to appear; the tooltip-display setting can deactivate the rig without clearing this reference.

Awake assigns the reference directly. It does not reject a second rig, and the audited TutorialRig methods do not clear the static reference on unload. This reference alone is not proof that a tutorial is active.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TutorialRig._activeControllers
member.summary: Records that this rig has selected controller art and connected the tooltip placement anchors.

remarks.para: SetActiveController chooses an art entry for each detected controller type, hides the art and arrows, copies the entries' offset_text anchors into the tooltips, then sets this to true. CUSTOMTUTORIAL runs that setup only when this flag is false.
This is a setup cache, not a visibility flag. It can remain true after DEACTIVETUTORIAL fades the display out. Setting it true before setup would skip required selection and anchor assignments.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TutorialRig._clip_tutorial
member.summary: The audio clip passed to the controller tooltips when the current custom tutorial is shown.

remarks.para: CUSTOMTUTORIAL replaces this with its clip_tutorial argument. SendToolTip copies it into each active tooltip before requesting its fade-in. Changing this staging field alone does not update a tooltip or play audio.

The tooltip's fade-in audio path schedules the tutorial clip after 0.5 seconds only when audio is enabled, that hand is being shown, and both the tooltip's clip_enable and tutorial clip exist. Each tooltip handles this separately; this field is not an audio player or a guarantee of playback.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TutorialRig._spriteToSend_L
member.summary: The picture staged for the left controller tooltip when the tutorial is applied.

remarks.para: CUSTOMTUTORIAL replaces this as it applies the hand configuration. Some choices clear it; either can store pictures for both hands while showing only one. SendToolTip copies it into toolTip_left.image_Sprite, and a selected tooltip assigns a non-null sprite to its SpriteRenderer during fade-in.

It is not a pending-update flag or a live SpriteRenderer control. Changing it alone does not redraw the tooltip. Shutdown clears this staging field for active tooltip objects; the tooltip's fade-out selects its own default sprite.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TutorialRig.cur_activeTutorial

remarks.para: CUSTOMTUTORIAL stores its specificTutorial argument here. A tutorial called without a trigger can therefore have tutorialActive true while this reference is null. DEACTIVETUTORIAL clears the reference.

SendTutorialComplete, when invoked, uses this reference to set the trigger's repeat count to zero, call its TUTORIALOFF, and deactivate the trigger object. member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TutorialRig.cur_l_art

The right-side art activation path also indexes leftControllerArt with cur_r_art, so keep both arrays compatible.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TutorialRig.standardHeight
member.summary: The reference eye height used to turn avatar height into a tutorial-rig size multiplier.

remarks.para: TUTORIALSCALE divides the supplied avatar eye height by this distance, in meters, then multiplies by tutorialScale, an extra size multiplier. With an illustrative reference height of 1.6 meters, an avatar eye height of 1.6 gives a height ratio of 1; an eye height of 0.8 gives 0.5. A larger reference height makes the tutorial rig smaller for the same avatar.

Use a positive value. TUTORIALSCALE checks the incoming eye height but does not check this divisor for zero or a negative value. Changing it has an effect when scaling is next applied; it is not recalculated from the current avatar.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TutorialRig.textToSend_L

remarks.para: CUSTOMTUTORIAL fills this from its left-text argument according to the selected hand. SendToolTip passes it to toolTip_left.SETTEXT, which writes the TextMeshPro display. Shutdown replaces the staging text with an empty string for active tooltip objects.

Assigning this field alone does not update the visible text. Use CUSTOMTUTORIAL to apply text, pictures, hand selection, and fade behavior together. It displays the supplied string; this field does not fetch or translate a tutorial message.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TutorialRig.tutorialActive
member.summary: Records that CUSTOMTUTORIAL has started a controller tutorial which has not yet been deactivated.

remarks.para: CUSTOMTUTORIAL sets this true after sending the display and arranging its timeout. DEACTIVETUTORIAL tests it before doing the fade-out, then sets it false and clears cur_activeTutorial. Visible fading may continue after the flag becomes false.

This is bookkeeping, not an on/off switch for the display. Assigning true does not send text, highlights, or arrows, and assigning false before DEACTIVETUTORIAL can make that method skip cleanup. It can be true even when no TutorialTrigger was supplied.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TutorialRig.tutorialScale
member.summary: An extra size multiplier applied when the tutorial rig is scaled for the avatar.

remarks.para: TUTORIALSCALE sets local scale to avatarEyeHeight / standardHeight multiplied by this value on X, Y, and Z. avatarEyeHeight is the supplied avatar eye height in meters, and standardHeight is the reference eye height in meters. Their ratio and this extra size multiplier have no distance units. A value of 1 uses the height ratio unchanged; 0.5 halves that size; 2 doubles it. These are illustrative choices, not distances in meters.

This is an input multiplier, not the calculated current scale. The scaling method reads it without replacing it. Changing it alone does not resize the object; call TUTORIALSCALE with a positive eye height, or wait for the normal BodyVitals UI-layout update. The method replaces local scale rather than multiplying the old scale.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TutorialTrigger.handChoice
member.summary: Chooses which hand can start this tutorial through the trigger and which controller instructions the request displays.

remarks.para: The choices are none (0), both (1), either (2), left (3) and right (4). With both, either hand entering can request instructions for both controllers; it does not wait for both hands to enter. With either, either hand can enter and the request selects the hand most recently recorded by the trigger. Left and right allow their matching hand to request instructions for that controller.

The entry path first recognizes a Hand component on the entering collider object and requires tutorialRepeatCount to be nonzero. A collider is Unity's shape used to detect contact or entry into an area. Both and either also wait until the shared TutorialRig is not already running a tutorial; left and right do not make that extra check. none prevents these automatic entry requests.

TUTORIALSEND passes this choice and the stored hand side to TutorialRig, which sets which controller art and tooltip text to send. Entry and exit both update the stored hand, so a later direct TUTORIALSEND uses the most recently recorded side. A direct send needs a recorded Hand and an available TutorialRig whose own scene object is active; it does not repeat the entry path's hand-choice or repeat-count checks.

Changing this setting alone does not open or close the displayed tutorial. When exitEnds is enabled, the same hand-choice rules help decide which hand exit ends it. For example, both can start with one hand entering and end with one hand exiting. This component is marked obsolete because it uses the older zone components.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TutorialTrigger.highlightLoc_left
member.summary: Chooses directional arrow artwork to enable for the left controller when this tutorial is sent.

remarks.para: This enum selects arrows drawn on the controller tutorial art; it does not store a world position or a distance. Use the left-hand choices: none_l, left_l, right_l, up_l, down_l, upDown_l, leftRight_l and all_l. Their numerical values run from 0 through 7. For example, up_l (3) enables the upward-arrow entry, while upDown_l enables both vertical arrows.

TUTORIALSEND reads this setting and passes it to TutorialRig.CUSTOMTUTORIAL, which enables the left arrow group and the selected arrow entries. The arrows' directions refer to the configured controller artwork, rather than the scene's world axes. The rig needs its left arrow-art references configured for the group and four directions.

Directional choices enable their arrows without clearing the other direction entries first, so earlier arrows can remain enabled. none_l (0) disables the group and all four direction entries; use that reset when a new tutorial must clear old arrows. Values from the other hand's family do not select or clear directions in this field's switch.

The setting is applied on a tutorial send, not continuously while the trigger runs. Assigning a new value alone does not update visible arrows. Arrow selection is separate from inputHighlight, which chooses the controller button or grip artwork to flash.

Use the right-hand choices: none_r, left_r, right_r, up_r, down_r, upDown_r, leftRight_r and all_r. Their numerical values run from 8 through 15. Directional choices enable their arrows without clearing the other direction entries first, so earlier arrows can remain enabled. none_r (8) disables the group and all four direction entries; use that reset when a new tutorial must clear old arrows. Values from the other hand's family do not select or clear directions in this field's switch.

The setting is applied on a tutorial send, not continuously while the trigger runs. Assigning a new value alone does not update visible arrows. Arrow selection is separate from inputHighlight, which chooses the controller button or grip artwork to flash.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TutorialTrigger.inputHighlight_left
member.summary: Chooses the controller-input artwork to flash on the left controller when this tutorial is sent.

remarks.para: The supported highlight choices are trigger (1), button_A (2), button_B (3), grip (4), joystick (5) and gripTrig (7). button_A uses the configured primary-button artwork and button_B uses secondary-button artwork, so the visible label depends on the controller model. gripTrig starts highlights for both the trigger and grip.

TUTORIALSEND reads this value and passes it to the currently selected left controller art through TutorialRig. HIGHLIGHTACTION starts a coroutine, work that continues over later frames, to change the chosen artwork's visual intensity. The controller art must be active and its matching Renderer, the component that draws that artwork, must be assigned.

none (0) starts no new highlight. Although touchpad (6) is present in the enum, the inspected HIGHLIGHTACTION method also starts no highlight for that value. These choices do not clear a highlight routine that was already started. For example, selecting grip requests flashing on the grip artwork; it does not press the grip or detect that the player used it.

Configure this before the next tutorial send. Changing the stored value alone does not replace the already running visual effect, and it is separate from highlightLoc, which selects directional arrow artwork.
