member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.Tween.colliders
member.summary: Caches collision shapes that are disabled at startup and enabled by .

remarks.para: A collider is an invisible shape Unity uses to detect contact between objects. During Start, Unity’s setup call before this component’s first normal update, the component finds colliders on its own object and its children, including inactive child objects. It stores that list here, then disables every collider in it.

The private EnableColliders helper later enables each collider in the stored list. It uses the saved list without searching the children again. Changing this field alone does not enable or disable a collider.

For example, a collider added after Start is not automatically added to this cache or disabled by the earlier setup. Enabling a cached collider does not restore the object’s size: startup separately sets the object’s local scale to zero.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.TweenRotation.curve
member.summary: Shapes the one-second turn started by LookAtRotationTween, from this object’s world rotation at the call toward a rotation facing the target position saved by that call.

remarks.para: Calling LookAtRotationTween starts this turn. At that call, the target Transform’s world position is saved. The routine saves this object’s current world rotation as the starting orientation and calculates the target orientation as the rotation that points this object’s forward direction (its local positive Z) toward that saved position. The curve controls the blend between those two saved orientations.

An AnimationCurve is a graph whose shape turns an input number into an output number. Here its horizontal axis is elapsed game-clock time in seconds, restricted to 0 through 1. The routine adds Time.deltaTime, the game-clock time since the previous frame, before reading the curve. Slowing or pausing the game clock also slows or pauses this progress.

The vertical axis is a unitless rotation-blend amount: 0 uses the starting orientation and 1 uses the saved target orientation. The result goes into Quaternion.Lerp, which blends two orientations and limits the amount to 0 through 1. A quaternion is Unity's four-number representation of an orientation. Curve values are neither degrees nor seconds; values outside this output range cannot make this routine rotate past the target.

For example, a curve starting at (0, 0) and ending at (1, 1) can keep its output low early on and rise faster near the end to make the turn start slowly. If its output at 0.5 seconds is 0.25, the routine uses a blend amount of 0.25 between the original and target orientations. That amount does not guarantee an exact fraction of the angle, because this rotation blend does not always turn at a constant angular speed.

The timer stops after reaching one game-clock second, regardless of the curve's shape. There is no separate final assignment forcing the target orientation: to finish facing the target, give the curve an output of 1 at time 1. The first update reads a small positive elapsed time rather than necessarily time 0, and the last update can cross the one-second boundary before its input is limited to 1.

Assign a valid curve before calling LookAtRotationTween; this component does not create a default curve in its constructor. The routine reads this field again on each update, so replacing or editing the curve during a turn can change the remaining motion. The starting and target orientations remain the snapshots taken when that routine began.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.UIControllerInput.CursorTarget
member.summary: Returns the valid override Transform when one is set; otherwise returns the configured default .

remarks.para: A Transform stores position, rotation and scale. The getter uses Unity's object-validity check, so a missing or destroyed override falls back to cursorTarget. The fallback itself is returned without another validity check; configure a usable default rather than assuming the getter creates one.

PopUpMenuView.Activate reads the selected Transform's world position when calculating its opening position and direction. World position means coordinates relative to the scene, not coordinates relative to the hand. Setting an override chooses that reference; it does not itself move an object or guarantee that every cursor consumer uses this getter.
LaserCursor.Initialize is a separate checked consumer that caches cursorTarget directly. A change to the override does not replace that already-cached default reference.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.UIControllerInput._cursorTargetOverride
member.summary: Overrides the Transform returned by while Unity considers this reference valid. and manage it.

remarks.para: A Transform holds an object's position, rotation and scale. AddCursorTargetOverride stores this reference; RemoveCursorTargetOverride clears it. Neither method moves the referenced object. Missing or destroyed overrides cause CursorTarget to return the default cursorTarget.

The popup opening routine reads the selected reference's world position, meaning its position in the scene. This field does not change the controller this input component polls or the virtual hand pose it follows, and it does not replace LaserCursor.Initialize's separately cached default reference.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.UIControllerInput._hasTriggeredThisFrame
member.summary: No per-frame trigger-blocking behavior was verified for this flag in the checked input and popup paths.

remarks.para: The complete UIControllerInput methods, its scene-reload iterator and two reset callbacks do not read or write this field to suppress another trigger, nor reset it at a frame boundary. The complete checked PopUpMenuView.Activate, Trigger and Deactivate bodies also do not use it.

Changing this flag is therefore not a verified way to prevent a second menu action in those paths. The popup keeps its own separate state; this finding does not claim that all other game code or mods ignore the field.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.UIControllerInput.cursorTarget
member.summary: Sets the default Transform used for popup cursor-position calculations when no valid override is selected.

remarks.para: A Transform stores an object's position, rotation and scale. CursorTarget returns this reference when _cursorTargetOverride is missing or destroyed. PopUpMenuView.Activate reads the selected Transform's world position, coordinates relative to the scene, when deriving the menu's opening placement.

LaserCursor.Initialize separately caches this default reference for its controller mapping. Replacing the field later does not automatically rebuild that mapping. This is a configured reference, not a cached result of a raycast, and assigning it does not itself move a scene object or open a menu.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.UIControllerInput.initialActivateTime
member.summary: Records a real-time menu-button press timestamp used by the hold-to-open check.

remarks.para: For the eligible closed-menu press path, Update stores Time.realtimeSinceStartup: seconds since the game started, unaffected by slow motion. The hold-to-open path checks current real-time seconds - initialActivateTime > 0.15 seconds. For example, a stored value of 100 seconds allows that hold check after real time passes 100.15 seconds, subject to the other menu/controller conditions.

After requesting an opening, Update replaces this with a very large finite marker value to prevent the same held press from passing that elapsed-time test again. It is therefore not always a historical timestamp. This is separate from the app-menu reload counter, which uses scaled frame seconds. Writing a timestamp yourself does not directly open the menu.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.UIControllerInput.isLeft
member.summary: Chooses which controller is polled and which virtual-skeleton hand pose this input object follows: true for left, false for right.

remarks.para: Update reads the corresponding BaseController from OpenControllerRig and copies the matching GameWorldSkeletonRig hand Transform's world position and rotation to this component's Transform. A Transform stores position, rotation and scale; world coordinates are measured relative to the scene.

The virtual skeleton is the set of body-pose Transforms stored by the player rig. This pose is separate from a direct read of the physical hand Rigidbody, the Unity component for physics movement, or the hardware controller. Changing isLeft switches both choices on a later Update; placing this component into UIRig's left or right reference does not itself change this flag.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.UIControllerInput.m_IsMenuActive
member.summary: Records the popup menu's active state last observed by this input component; assigning it does not open or close the menu.

remarks.para: When Update first observes an active PopUpMenuView while this flag is false, it stops all this component's coroutines before setting the flag true. A coroutine is a sequence that continues across several frames; this can interrupt an in-progress scene-reload counter. When it later observes the popup closed, it clears the flag.

The authoritative popup state is PopUpMenuView's own activation flag. This local value can lag or stay stale when Update exits early, such as when the global quickmenuEnabled setting is false and the popup is already closed. It is not an instruction to display the radial menu, and the popup can use other panel modes.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.UIControllerInput.m_appMenuButtonHeld
member.summary: Lets the scene-reload counter accumulate time and request reset while the app-menu input remains recorded as held.

remarks.para: Update sets this flag true on GetAppMenuDown before creating and starting the reload iterator. On GetAppMenuUp, when GetAppMenu no longer reports held, it clears the flag before stopping that stored iterator and requesting cancellation of the HUD reset display.

The counter adds scaled deltaTime only while the flag is true, and checks it again before calling ResetLevel at the threshold. A coroutine is a sequence that continues across several frames. Clearing the flag alone pauses accumulation while below the threshold; it does not perform Update's StopCoroutine call. Early returns can leave this recorded value out of step with the physical button. Exact hardware bindings depend on the controller implementation.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.UIControllerInput.m_canOpenMenu
member.summary: Allows the app-menu release path to reopen the popup; it is not a global menu-opening permission switch.

remarks.para: Start sets it true after stopping this component's coroutines and clearing the held-button flag. The scene-reload counter calls ResetLevel first and sets m_canOpenMenu false after that call returns. This prevents the later release-opening branch from reopening the popup while reset is being arranged.

On an eligible app-menu release with the preferences panel inactive, Update first closes an already-active popup, then checks this flag before its release-triggered opening. The separate menu-button hold path does not read it, and direct PopUpMenuView.Activate calls are outside this check. Changing it alone neither opens nor closes a menu. Other conditions, including the global quickmenuEnabled setting, still affect Update.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.UIControllerInput.m_cur_levelReloadCounter
member.summary: Stores scaled seconds accumulated by the current or most recently stopped hold-to-reset sequence.

remarks.para: The reload iterator writes 0 on its first execution. While this value is below m_levelReloadCounter and m_appMenuButtonHeld is true, each frame adds Time.deltaTime, the scaled seconds for that frame. For example, at a constant half-speed time scale, reaching a 2-scaled-second threshold takes roughly 4 real-world seconds, plus frame scheduling.

The threshold is checked before the next increment, so a frame that reaches or overshoots the threshold yields once more before the reset check. ResetLevel is requested only if the held flag is still true at that later check. Stopping the iterator does not clear this field; the next new sequence resets it. Editing the value affects an already-running counter but does not create one.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.UIControllerInput.m_levelReloadCounter
member.summary: Sets the scaled-second threshold used by the app-menu hold-to-reset sequence.

remarks.para: SceneReloadCounter compares m_cur_levelReloadCounter against this value each frame. The current value is accumulated scaled frame seconds; reaching the threshold leads to ResetLevel on a later execution only if m_appMenuButtonHeld is still true. With a threshold of 2 seconds at half-speed time scale, the wait is roughly 4 real-world seconds, subject to frame scheduling.

The threshold is read during the running sequence, so changing it can affect that pass. A nonpositive threshold can pass the initial check immediately; the body does not clamp it to a positive minimum. Reaching it requests the fade-and-reload route rather than guaranteeing that the scene is already reloaded. Direct ResetLevel calls bypass this counter.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.UIControllerInput.reloadCoroutine
member.summary: Stores the iterator used to start and stop the app-menu hold-to-reset sequence.

remarks.para: An iterator is the object that remembers a sequence's progress between frames. A coroutine is the running sequence that continues across those frames. Update creates a SceneReloadCounter iterator, stores it here, then passes it to StartCoroutine; its release path clears m_appMenuButtonHeld and passes this stored iterator to StopCoroutine.

This field is an IEnumerator, not a Coroutine handle and not a level-loading operation. The native code does not clear it when the sequence completes or is stopped, so a non-null reference is not proof of a running countdown. Replacing this reference does not itself start the replacement or stop the previous sequence.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.UIRig.Instance
member.summary: The UI rig most recently registered by Awake, Unity's initialization callback.

remarks.para: This provides the shared HUD, pop-up menu, feedback components, and settings controller used by the player UI. For example, menu pages copy its feedback components when their own references are missing.

Awake assigns this static reference directly. The audited UIRig methods do not reject duplicate rigs or clear the reference when the component is disabled. Check that the Unity object and the component you need still exist; this value alone does not tell you whether a menu is open.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.UIRig.controlPlayer
member.summary: The player-settings component used by menus to apply body, audio, and spectator preferences.

remarks.para: Control_UI_InGameData copies this reference when its own controlPlayer has not been assigned. Control_Player applies saved body settings to BodyVitals, updates HUD preferences, and applies master, music, and sound-effect volume settings; its spectator update applies RigScreenOptions.

This is a reference to the component that performs those actions, not a controller-button mapping table. Replacing it does not run its settings methods or replace references that another menu has already copied.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.UIRig.cur_avatarArmScaleMult
member.summary: Stores the last positive arm-length ratio calculated for the UI.

remarks.para: UI_AVATARSCALE replaces this with armLength / standardArmLength. It excludes uiScale, which is applied separately when sizing the listed transforms. For example, an arm length twice the reference gives a ratio of 2 even if uiScale is 0.5 and the final transform scale is 1.

The normal BodyVitals UI-layout refresh copies this ratio into PopUpMenuView.cur_avatarArmScaleMult and recalculates the menu's starting position. That menu uses it to scale its distance from the player. Assigning this cache alone does not resize the transforms or update the menu's copied value; the next scaling calculation overwrites it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.UIRig.feedbackAudio
member.summary: The fallback sound-feedback component used by menu pages with no audio provider of their own.

remarks.para: PageView.Start and CheckRefs copy this into the page's feedback_audio only when that reference is missing. Page feedback then uses AUDIOCLICK, optionally passing a page-specific clip and location, to play a configured sound through the game's audio system.

Changing this reference after a page has copied it does not replace that page's existing provider. Assign a configured Feedback_Audio component; the field itself does not play a sound or choose an audio clip.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.UIRig.feedbackTactile
member.summary: The fallback vibration-feedback component used by menu pages with no tactile provider of their own.

remarks.para: PageView.Start and CheckRefs copy this into the page's feedback_tactile only when that reference is missing. Hover feedback requests a subtle vibration, and click feedback requests a click vibration on the page's active controller. If no controller argument is supplied, the component tries the controller currently registered for menu interaction; if no controller or vibration device exists, it does nothing.
Changing this rig reference does not replace a provider that a page has already copied. This field is a component reference, not a vibration-strength setting.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.UIRig.leftUIController
member.summary: The UIControllerInput component assigned for the left hand's menu interaction.

remarks.para: The component follows the corresponding tracked hand pose, supplies a CursorTarget for menu pointing, reads controller actions to open or trigger the pop-up menu, and controls the scene-reload progress prompt while its reload input is held.

The component's own isLeft field selects which hand it reads: set it true for this left-hand component. Putting a component in this reference does not change its isLeft setting. CursorTarget uses the component's override transform when one exists, otherwise its configured cursorTarget.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.UIRig.popUpMenu
member.summary: The player's menu view that opens from controller input and switches between radial options and panels.

remarks.para: The menu contains references for inventory, preferences, spawnables, levels, and avatars. UIControllerInput sends its controller and cursor target when opening or triggering this view. Setting this reference alone does not open it; opening and closing use the menu's own methods.

While UIRig is enabled, its early update copies this menu's active state into the player ControllerRig.IsMenuTapDisabled field. The normal BodyVitals UI-layout refresh also copies the arm-length ratio into this menu and recalculates its starting position. The menu and player references must exist for these paths.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.UIRig.rightUIController
member.summary: The UIControllerInput component assigned for the right hand's menu interaction.

remarks.para: The component follows the corresponding tracked hand pose, supplies a CursorTarget for menu pointing, reads controller actions to open or trigger the pop-up menu, and controls the scene-reload progress prompt while its reload input is held.

The component's own isLeft field selects which hand it reads: set it false for this right-hand component. Putting a component in this reference does not change its isLeft setting. CursorTarget uses the component's override transform when one exists, otherwise its configured cursorTarget.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.UIRig.scaleOffset
member.summary: The transforms whose local size is replaced when avatar-based UI scaling is applied.

remarks.para: UI_AVATARSCALE sets every listed transform's X, Y, and Z scale to armLength / standardArmLength multiplied by uiScale. Here standardArmLength is the reference arm length in metres, and uiScale is the extra unitless size multiplier. Despite the field name, the method does not assign localPosition or localRotation. Scaling a parent transform also scales the size and spacing of its children.

List the UI roots you want resized and keep the array and its entries assigned. Old non-uniform scales are replaced with the same value on all three axes. Changing this array alone does not resize its new entries until the scaling method or normal BodyVitals layout refresh runs.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.UIRig.standardArmLength
member.summary: The reference arm length used to calculate avatar-based UI scaling.

remarks.para: The incoming avatar arm length is divided by this distance in meters. For an illustrative reference of 0.4 meters, arm length 0.4 gives a ratio of 1 and 0.8 gives 2. A larger reference makes the listed UI transforms smaller for the same avatar.

Use a positive value: the scaling code checks the incoming arm length but does not check this divisor. This is an input reference, not a measurement updated from the avatar. Changes apply when the next scaling calculation runs.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.UIRig.uiHud
member.summary: The player HUD component that displays ammunition information and the scene-reload prompt.

remarks.para: UIRig.Start calls UpdateUI and then UIHudSetup on this component. The HUD reads ammo information, checks the held weapons for low ammo, and registers ammo-inventory and hand-slot callbacks so later changes can refresh the display.

UIControllerInput also uses this HUD to show or hide the scene-reload progress display. The HUD must already be assigned and configured; replacing the reference alone does not repeat setup or reconnect the old HUD's event subscriptions.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.UIRig.uiScale
member.summary: An extra size multiplier for the transforms listed in scaleOffset.

remarks.para: The scaling calculation sets each listed transform's local scale to the arm-length ratio multiplied by this value on all three axes. For example, uiScale = 0.5 halves their size compared with the same avatar at uiScale = 1. This is a unitless multiplier, not a distance.

It does not get included in cur_avatarArmScaleMult and does not independently multiply the pop-up menu's distance value. It affects only the listed transforms and their children, rather than every canvas in the game. Changing it takes effect when avatar scaling is next applied.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.UI_HUD.Float0
member.summary: Cached shader-property identifier for the reset bar’s "_Float0" material value.

remarks.para: The class’s static setup converts the exact property name "_Float0" into Unity’s integer lookup identifier. ProgressBar uses that identifier when writing the bar material. It is an identifier, not a displayed count, a percentage or a duration.

The written material value is unitless: it starts at 1 and decreases as clamp(1 - elapsed / 2, 0, 1), where elapsed is accumulated game time in seconds and 2 is the routine’s duration in seconds. For example, one accumulated second gives 0.5. How the number changes the visible bar depends on its material.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.UI_HUD._co_ammo_follow
member.summary: Stored iterator for the most recently requested ammo-placement routine.

remarks.para: An iterator remembers a routine’s next step; Unity runs it as a coroutine, a routine that can pause and continue later. SHOWAMMO stops the old iterator when present, stores a new one here, and starts it.

The routine copies the chosen target’s world position and orientation after each physics update. None hides the module and ends after its final yield, but does not clear this field. A non-null iterator therefore does not prove the routine is running. OnEnable and OnDisable stop coroutines without clearing this field.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.UI_HUD._co_follow_head
member.summary: Stored iterator for the head-follower motion routine started by HEADHUDFOLLOW.

remarks.para: An iterator remembers a routine’s next step; its coroutine can pause and continue later. HEADHUDFOLLOW stops a previous iterator before replacing it when following is enabled. Disabling following stops the routine and resets and hides target_HEADFOLLOWER, but does not clear this field.

The routine updates the follower’s world pose after physics updates using the cached head and motion-smoothing history. A non-null reference is not proof of current motion, because this iterator remains stored after explicit stop or StopAllCoroutines.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.UI_HUD._co_headFollowTimmer
member.summary: Stored iterator for the current timed head-follow countdown request.

remarks.para: An iterator remembers a routine’s next step; its coroutine can pause and continue later. HEADHUDFOLLOWTIMED stores a countdown in game seconds, stops an existing iterator, replaces this field, and starts the replacement.

The routine enables head following while the countdown is positive. On a later step at zero or below, it turns following off, clears this field and ends. OnEnable and OnDisable can stop all routines without clearing it, so a stored iterator alone does not prove the countdown is running.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.UI_HUD._co_progressBar
member.summary: Stored iterator for the reset bar’s two-game-second material countdown.

remarks.para: An iterator remembers a routine’s next step; its coroutine can pause and continue later. Opening the reset popup creates and starts the progress iterator only when this field is null. Closing stops it and clears the field.

Each physics step writes a descending unitless value to the material, using elapsed game seconds. On the step where elapsed time has reached 2 seconds, the routine clears this field and ends without explicitly writing a final zero. A later popup opening can then start a new countdown. StopAllCoroutines alone does not clear this reference.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.UI_HUD._co_resetLevel_follow
member.summary: Stored iterator that scales and positions the reset popup when POPUPRELOADSCENE is called.

remarks.para: An iterator remembers a routine’s next step; its coroutine can pause and continue later. Each popup request stops the old iterator, sets _resetting true, stores a replacement with the requested opening/closing direction and starts it.

The routine scales the popup toward a unitless local scale of (1, 1, 1) when opening or (0, 0, 0) when closing, and copies the reset target’s world pose. While open it keeps following that pose after physics updates. Closing hides the popup and clears _resetting, but the stored iterator is not cleared when the routine ends.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.UI_HUD._cur_ammo_displayLocation
member.summary: Target transform most recently selected by the running ammo-placement routine.

remarks.para: A transform describes position and orientation. Each ammo-follow step chooses Belt, Head or Inventory’s target and stores it here, then copies its world position and rotation to hud_AMMO. Head selects the right or left target using lowAmmoPopupRight.

None instead hides hud_AMMO and stores this HUD component’s own transform. Thus a non-null reference does not mean the ammo display is visible. The routine overwrites this cache from ammo_displayLocation on its next step; assigning it directly does not permanently select another mode.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.UI_HUD._cur_resetLevel_scale
member.summary: Cached starting local scale for interpolation toward the reset popup’s next scale target.

remarks.para: Scale is a unitless multiplier on the popup’s own axes: (1, 1, 1) is its original size, and (0, 0, 0) collapses it. The reset routine interpolates each axis from this cache toward _tar_resetLevel_scale using the clamped curve output.

At the end of a scaling stage it copies the target scale into this field. It does not read back the transform’s actual visible scale, and interrupting a stage does not refresh this cache from the current appearance. The final visible frame may therefore differ from the cached target; this field is not a live scale measurement.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.UI_HUD._cur_resetLevel_timeToScale
member.summary: Accumulated game-time animation clock for the current reset-popup scale transition.

remarks.para: The routine resets this clock to zero when opening or closing starts. It uses clock / _resetLevel_timeToScale as the curve’s horizontal input; both clock and duration are in seconds, so the ratio is unitless.

Opening adds Unity’s reported game-time step after each scale write. Closing adds six times that step, so it progresses through the same curve about six times faster. The clock can step past the configured duration; frame and physics scheduling mean it is not an exact wall-clock timer.
Once this clock is no longer below the duration, the routine caches the target scale. It does not explicitly force an extra visible scale write at the exact endpoint.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.UI_HUD._followingHead
member.summary: Last following choice written by HEADHUDFOLLOW, which other HUD routines use when deciding whether to start or stop following.

remarks.para: HEADHUDFOLLOW writes this value before setting up or hiding target_HEADFOLLOWER. True starts the head-motion routine after resetting its smoothing history; false stops the routine, resets the target’s world position and orientation, and hides its object.

The timed routine and reset-popup request test this flag before enabling following. The motion routine does not test it on every step. Writing this bool alone therefore does not start or stop movement.

OnEnable and OnDisable stop coroutines without clearing this flag, and it is set before setup operations that require valid references. True is therefore a recorded request, not proof that the follower is currently moving.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.UI_HUD._headFollowCountDown
member.summary: Remaining timed head-follow countdown in game seconds.

remarks.para: HEADHUDFOLLOWTIMED(seconds) replaces this value with the requested duration and restarts the timer routine. Each timer step first tests it, enables following if it is positive, then subtracts Unity’s reported game-time step before waiting for a physics update.

For example, a remaining 0.01 seconds can become negative after subtraction, and the next step performs shutdown. At zero or below, the routine turns head following off, clears its stored iterator and ends. Slow motion, pause settings and frame scheduling affect the real elapsed time.
Changing this value changes the next test of an already running timer; it does not start a timer by itself.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.UI_HUD._headGimbalOffset
member.summary: World-space positional lag added to the desired head-follower point.

remarks.para: This vector is measured in world units, normally metres. The helper updates it by (smoothed velocity - desired point velocity) multiplied by the physics step duration. Both velocities are in metres per second and the duration is in seconds, so that update is a distance.

The helper then blends the offset toward zero using a rate of 5 per second and limits its length to 0.2 metres. The final world position is desired point plus this offset. It does not rotate this offset into head-local coordinates.
HEADHUDFOLLOW(true) resets it to zero. For example, a -0.1-metre scene-Z offset leaves the follower 10 centimetres behind its desired point along the scene’s Z direction.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.UI_HUD._headGimbalVel
member.summary: Smoothed world velocity of the desired head-follower point.

remarks.para: This vector is smoothing history in world units per second, normally metres per second; it is not an angle. The helper estimates desired point velocity from the change in desired world position divided by the physics step duration in seconds, then smooths this stored velocity toward that estimate.

The difference between this smoothed velocity and the desired point velocity updates the follower’s positional lag. HEADHUDFOLLOW(true) resets this vector to zero before starting the routine. Direct edits while running change that smoothing history rather than applying a force to the player.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.UI_HUD._headGimbleAccel
member.summary: Velocity-changing history used while smoothing the head-follower’s world velocity.

remarks.para: The smoothing helper passes this vector by reference to Vector3.SmoothDamp while smoothing a velocity measured in metres per second. Its units are therefore metres per second squared: it records how the smoothed velocity changes, not the physical acceleration of the head.

The head-motion routine uses a smoothing time of 0.1 seconds. This vector is updated by that velocity-smoothing call and reset to zero by HEADHUDFOLLOW(true). A direct edit changes the next smoothing result; it does not start following or push a physics body.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.UI_HUD._lastHead
member.summary: Previous desired follower point saved by the head-motion smoothing helper.

remarks.para: Despite the name, this is the previous desired world point in front of the head, not the previous actual head position. World positions use scene coordinates, normally measured in metres.

HEADHUDFOLLOW(true) initializes it to the newly calculated desired point. Each normal smoothing step computes target velocity as (current desired point - this previous point) / physics step duration. The two points are in metres and the duration is in seconds, giving metres per second. The helper then stores the current desired point here for the next step.
Keeping this history consistent prevents an artificial jump in the calculated motion. Starting following resets it; directly editing it during motion changes the next velocity estimate.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.UI_HUD._offset_headDirection
member.summary: Most recently sampled head-forward direction in scene coordinates.

remarks.para: This is a direction vector of length 1, with no distance units. HEADHUDFOLLOW(true) initializes it from _playerHead.forward, and each head-motion step reads that direction again.

The desired world point is head position plus this direction multiplied by offset_HeadDistance, a distance in world units, normally metres. For example, a distance of 1 places that desired point one metre along the head’s current forward direction.
This field is sampling state, not an additional angle or configurable displacement. The running routine overwrites it from the head before using it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.UI_HUD._offset_headPlacement
member.summary: Most recently calculated world point that the head follower tries to reach.

remarks.para: The point is head world position plus head world forward direction multiplied by offset_HeadDistance. The position and distance are in world units, normally metres; the forward direction is a unit-length vector without distance units.
For example, with a head at (0, 1.6, 0), facing scene +Z, and a distance of 1, this desired point is (0, 1.6, 1). It is an absolute scene position, not a position relative to the head’s parent.

HEADHUDFOLLOW initializes this field, then the motion routine recomputes it each step. The visible follower may lag behind it by up to the smoothing offset; assigning this point directly is overwritten on the next step.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.UI_HUD._playerHead
member.summary: Cached head transform used to choose the head-follower’s world position and direction.

remarks.para: A transform describes an object’s position and orientation. Head following reads this head’s world position and forward direction, then chooses a point offset_HeadDistance world units ahead of it; world units normally mean metres.

OnLevelLoad explicitly replaces the cache with the player physics rig’s head. UIHudSetup and UpdateUI use the controller rig’s head only if the cache is missing. A valid old reference is therefore not automatically refreshed by UpdateUI.
Assigning this reference changes the source read by an already running follower on its next step, but does not start the follower. The HUD motion step skips its pose update when the head is missing.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.UI_HUD._resetLevel_timeToScale
member.summary: Duration, in game seconds, that the reset-popup routine uses to normalize its scale animation clock.

remarks.para: This internal duration starts at 0.5 seconds. Opening advances its clock by Unity’s reported game-time step; closing advances it six times as fast. With 0.5 seconds configured, the closing clock reaches the duration in roughly 0.5 / 6 game seconds, subject to update steps.

The curve is sampled with clock / duration, where clock is the current animation clock in seconds and duration is this value in seconds. It is separate from public timeToScale, which the inspected reset routine does not read.

Use a positive duration for the interpolation loop. Zero or a negative duration skips that loop; even for positive durations, the code caches the target at completion rather than explicitly writing a final scale sample. Game time and frame scheduling determine actual completion.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.UI_HUD._resetting
member.summary: Request/state flag set when a reset-popup routine starts and cleared after its closing branch hides the popup.

remarks.para: POPUPRELOADSCENE sets this true for both opening and closing requests, before creating and starting the new iterator. The reset iterator checks it at the start of a stage and ends when it is false.

After closing reaches its cached zero-scale target, it hides hud_RESETLEVEL, moves it to this component’s world pose, clears this flag, and turns head following off. The opening path keeps it true while the popup follows its target.

This is not proof that a scene reload is happening or that the popup is currently visible. OnEnable and OnDisable can stop coroutines without clearing it. Assigning true alone does not start the popup routine.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.UI_HUD._tar_resetLevel_scale
member.summary: Desired local scale set to full size when the reset popup opens and zero when it closes.

remarks.para: The routine sets this unitless vector to (1, 1, 1) for opening or (0, 0, 0) for closing. Local scale multiplies the popup’s size along its own X, Y and Z axes.

During animation it blends from _cur_resetLevel_scale to this vector using curve_scale’s clamped output. At the stage boundary it copies this vector into the cache; it does not independently measure that the visible transform has reached it. The opening/closing branch overwrites this target, so directly assigning it before a popup request does not preserve a custom target.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.UI_HUD.ammo_displayLocation
member.summary: Selected ammo mode read by the ammo-placement routine when choosing visibility and a target.

remarks.para: None (0) hides the ammo object; Belt (1) uses target_ammo_belt; Head (2) uses the right or left head target according to lowAmmoPopupRight; Inventory (3) uses target_ammo_inventory. Visible modes copy the target’s world position and rotation after physics updates.

SHOWAMMO writes this value and replaces and starts the placement routine. Changing the field alone affects the next step of an already running routine; it does not create one or immediately move the HUD. For example, SHOWAMMO(Inventory) starts following the inventory target, while assigning Inventory to an idle component only stores the choice.
CheckAmmoForHeldGuns preserves Inventory mode but requests None outside it. Inventory-open notifications choose Inventory and inventory-close notifications choose None.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.UI_HUD.clip_resetLevel_cancel
member.summary: Sound clip played when the reset-popup routine begins closing.

remarks.para: An AudioClip contains sound data; sfx_resetLevel is the AudioSource component that plays it. In the closing branch, the routine first prepares the scale target and stops and clears the progress countdown, then stops the source if it is already playing and calls PlayOneShot with this clip.

For example, use this clip for an audible cancel cue when that popup transition is requested. It is played at the branch start, without waiting for the scale animation or a scene reload to complete. Assign the clip and audio source before making the request.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.UI_HUD.clip_resetLevel_hold
member.summary: Sound clip played when the reset-popup routine begins opening.

remarks.para: An AudioClip contains sound data; sfx_resetLevel is the AudioSource component that plays it. In the opening branch, the routine first prepares the scale target and starts the progress countdown when needed, then stops the source if it is already playing and calls PlayOneShot with this clip.

For example, use this clip for an audible hold cue when that popup transition is requested. It is played at the branch start, without waiting for the scale animation or a scene reload to complete. Assign the clip and audio source before making the request.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.UI_HUD.curve_scale
member.summary: Curve that chooses the blend amount for the reset popup’s local-scale animation.

remarks.para: An AnimationCurve maps a horizontal input to a vertical output. Here the horizontal input is clock / duration: clock is _cur_resetLevel_timeToScale in seconds, and duration is _resetLevel_timeToScale in seconds. Input 0 is the start of a scaling stage and input 1 is its configured end.

The vertical output is a unitless blend amount. The routine clamps it between 0 and 1, then blends each scale axis from the cached starting scale toward the target. Output 0 keeps the cached start; output 1 selects the target. A curve output of 2 is clamped to 1 rather than making the popup twice as large.

Opening targets (1, 1, 1) and advances its clock by game-time steps; closing targets (0, 0, 0) and advances six times faster. Assign the curve before a popup request. Completion caches the target without an extra explicit final scale write, so the last sampled visible size need not equal the curve endpoint.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.UI_HUD.emptyNote
member.summary: Message DisplayAmmo writes when a stored ammo-group count is exactly zero.

remarks.para: The constructor default is "EMPTY". DisplayAmmo uses this string for each assigned light, medium or heavy text component whose group total is zero rounds. Nonzero totals are converted into number text instead.

For example, setting emptyNote to "NONE LEFT" changes the next zero-count refresh to that message. Assigning the string does not immediately update the labels; call UpdateUI or wait for an ammo-inventory update. It also does not hide the ammo module.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.UI_HUD.hud_AMMO
member.summary: Root object that the ammo-placement routine shows, hides and moves to the selected world target.

remarks.para: Start, Unity’s setup call before the first update, deactivates this object. The ammo routine activates it for Belt, Head and Inventory modes, copies the selected target’s world position and orientation, and repeats after physics updates. None deactivates it and copies this HUD component’s own pose once.

Assign the root before Start or SHOWAMMO. Its activation controls whether its graphics are displayed, while DisplayAmmo changes the assigned text components separately. For example, counts can refresh while the root remains hidden.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.UI_HUD.hud_RESETLEVEL
member.summary: Root object shown, scaled and positioned by the reset-popup routine.

remarks.para: Start, Unity’s setup call before the first update, initially deactivates this object. An opening popup request activates it, interpolates its unitless local scale toward (1, 1, 1), and follows target_resetLevel_head’s world position and rotation.

A closing request interpolates toward (0, 0, 0) with a clock that advances six times faster. At the closing-stage boundary it hides the root, moves it to this HUD component’s world pose, clears _resetting and turns head following off.

Assign the root before Start or a popup request. The routine’s cached scale is an interpolation reference rather than a readback of the visible scale; interrupted transitions can therefore resume from that cache. Showing this object does not itself reload the scene.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.UI_HUD.hud_ResetProgressBar
member.summary: Renderer whose material receives the reset countdown’s "_Float0" number.

remarks.para: A MeshRenderer is Unity’s component that draws a mesh using its material, which controls the visible surface. The progress routine obtains this renderer’s material and writes a unitless number starting at 1 and decreasing according to clamp(1 - elapsed / 2, 0, 1), where elapsed is accumulated game seconds and 2 is the duration in seconds.

For example, one accumulated second writes 0.5. The material must interpret "_Float0" to draw the intended bar. The routine ends once its clock reaches two seconds but does not explicitly force a final zero sample.
Assign this renderer before opening the reset popup. Accessing renderer.material uses that renderer’s material instance; this does not rewrite the shared material reference for every other renderer.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.UI_HUD.leftGun
member.summary: Cached WeaponSlot from qualifying left-hand inventory insertion/removal notifications.

remarks.para: A WeaponSlot identifies an inventory-compatible weapon object. The left hand handler looks up a WeaponSlot and Gun on the event’s object and requires the Gun’s ammoSocket reference, its ammunition-receiving component. A qualifying insertion stores the slot here; a qualifying removal clears it.

If those component checks fail, the helper returns without changing the cache. This field therefore records the last qualifying event, not a fresh scan of what the hand currently holds. CheckAmmoForHeldGuns uses its object to find the Gun and the cartridge group for stored-ammo comparisons.
Assigning a slot here changes what the next held-gun check examines; it does not put a weapon in the player’s hand or change its loaded ammunition.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.UI_HUD.lowAmmoHeavy
member.summary: Stored-round threshold for the heavy group’s low-ammo comparison.

remarks.para: The value counts rounds in the ammo inventory’s "heavy" group; its constructor default is 6. The comparison treats a group total less than or equal to this value as low. For example, a threshold of 6 includes exactly 6 rounds, but excludes 7. It does not count the cartridges already loaded into a held gun’s magazine.

The test reads this field when a held gun’s cartridge belongs to this group. Changing the field affects the next comparison. However, CheckAmmoForHeldGuns discards that test result in the inspected implementation, so changing the threshold does not by itself produce a warning popup.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.UI_HUD.lowAmmoPopupRight
member.summary: Selects the right head target when true or the left head target when false for Head ammo placement.

remarks.para: The running ammo routine reads this bool on each Head-mode step, chooses target_ammo_head_right or target_ammo_head_left, and copies that transform’s world position and rotation to hud_AMMO.

Changing it during Head placement switches target at the next physics step. It has no effect on Belt, Inventory or None placement and does not display the ammo HUD by itself. For example, select Head with SHOWAMMO before using this field to switch sides.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.UI_HUD.offset_HeadDistance
member.summary: Distance along the cached head’s forward direction used to choose the follower’s desired world point.

remarks.para: The constructor default is 1 world unit, normally 1 metre. Each head-follow step computes desired point = head world position + head forward direction × this distance. The position is in scene coordinates; forward is a unit-length direction, and this value supplies the distance.
For example, a head at (0, 1.6, 0) facing scene +Z and a distance of 1 gives desired point (0, 1.6, 1). The follower can lag behind the point by up to 0.2 metres because of motion smoothing.

Use a positive distance to place the desired point in front of the head. The code does not clamp this field; negative values put that point behind it. Changing the value affects the next step of an already running follower, but does not start head following.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.UI_HUD.rightGun
member.summary: Cached WeaponSlot from qualifying right-hand inventory insertion/removal notifications.

remarks.para: A WeaponSlot identifies an inventory-compatible weapon object. The right hand handler looks up a WeaponSlot and Gun on the event’s object and requires the Gun’s ammoSocket reference, its ammunition-receiving component. A qualifying insertion stores the slot here; a qualifying removal clears it.

If those component checks fail, the helper returns without changing the cache. This field therefore records the last qualifying event, not a fresh scan of what the hand currently holds. CheckAmmoForHeldGuns uses its object to find the Gun and the cartridge group for stored-ammo comparisons.
Assigning a slot here changes what the next held-gun check examines; it does not put a weapon in the player’s hand or change its loaded ammunition.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.UI_HUD.sfx_resetLevel
member.summary: AudioSource that plays the reset popup’s hold and cancel sound clips.

remarks.para: An AudioSource is Unity’s sound-playing component. Start, Unity’s setup call before the first update, routes this source to the game’s UI mixer group.

The opening and closing reset branches stop it if it is already playing, then play clip_resetLevel_hold or clip_resetLevel_cancel once. These cues begin during the transition setup and do not wait for scaling or scene reloading to finish.
Assign the source before Start or a popup request. Changing either clip or this reference affects a future sound request; it does not immediately play a sound.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.UI_HUD.showLowAmmoPopup
member.summary: Stored low-ammo-popup preference whose value does not control the inspected HUD display paths.

remarks.para: The complete UI_HUD setup, ammo-check, placement, reset and head-follow methods inspected for this documentation do not read this field. Their held-gun check calculates low-ammo results but discards them, then hides ammo outside Inventory mode.

Assigning true therefore does not make those paths open a popup. Use SHOWAMMO with Head, Belt or Inventory to explicitly start the corresponding display placement. This is a storage explanation scoped to the inspected methods, not a claim about every possible external reader.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.UI_HUD.target_HEADFOLLOWER
member.summary: Transform moved by the head-follow routine to provide a smoothed world pose for head-attached HUD targets.

remarks.para: A transform describes position and orientation. HEADHUDFOLLOW(true) places this target at the head position plus head forward direction times offset_HeadDistance, a distance in world units, normally metres. It sets the target’s world facing direction from the head toward the target, activates its object and starts motion smoothing.

Each physics step can keep it up to 0.2 metres from the desired point. HEADHUDFOLLOW(false) stops the routine, resets this target’s world position to (0, 0, 0) and its world rotation to the unrotated orientation, then deactivates its object.

Assign the target before starting following. It is the object moved by the routine; assigning it does not parent the ammo or reset targets to it. Any child-target relationship must be configured in the scene.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.UI_HUD.target_ammo_belt
member.summary: World-pose target copied to the ammo HUD in Belt mode.

remarks.para: A transform describes position and orientation. In Belt mode, the running ammo routine stores this target as its current placement, then copies its world position and rotation to hud_AMMO. It repeats after physics updates, without smoothing or copying local scale.

Assign the target before SHOWAMMO(Belt). Changing its world pose while the routine runs moves the ammo HUD at the next step. This field does not set the ammo text, activate the display by itself, or create a parent relationship; placement depends on the selected mode.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.UI_HUD.target_resetLevel_head
member.summary: World-pose target followed by the reset popup while its routine is active.

remarks.para: A transform describes position and orientation. The reset routine copies this target’s world position and rotation to hud_RESETLEVEL during scaling and while the popup remains open. It waits for a physics update between copies.

Assign this target before requesting the popup. Its name does not automatically attach it to the player head; the scene must give it the intended parent or another motion source. Local scaling of hud_RESETLEVEL is controlled separately by the reset curve.
Closing eventually hides the popup and moves it to this HUD component’s own world pose. Changing this target alone does not start the routine or reload a scene.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.UI_HUD.text_ammo_heavy
member.summary: Text component where DisplayAmmo writes the stored heavy ammo-group total.

remarks.para: TextMeshPro is Unity’s component for drawing text. DisplayAmmo reads the ammo inventory’s "heavy" group total in rounds and writes its integer text here, or emptyNote when the total is exactly zero. This is stored inventory ammunition, not the gun’s loaded-magazine count.

For example, a stored total of 12 writes "12". A missing text component is skipped; the other group labels still update. Assign this component before setup or a refresh. Changing the reference does not itself refresh text, and visibility follows hud_AMMO’s separate activation state.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.UI_HUD.timeToScale
member.summary: Stored public timing value, initially 1, separate from the internal duration actually read by the reset animation.

remarks.para: The name suggests seconds, and the constructor initializes it to 1. The complete UI_HUD setup, display, placement, head-follow and reset methods inspected here do not read this public field.

The reset routine instead reads _resetLevel_timeToScale, initially 0.5 game seconds, to normalize its scaling clock. Changing timeToScale alone therefore does not alter that routine’s duration. This missing-reader statement is limited to the inspected class methods; external code can still store or read the field.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.UI_HUD.uiRig
member.summary: Stored reference to the surrounding UI rig, separate from the rig’s reference used to initialize this HUD.

remarks.para: A UIRig groups the player’s UI components. Its own uiHud field lets UIRig.Start call this HUD’s UpdateUI and UIHudSetup in that order.

The complete UI_HUD setup, display and motion methods inspected here do not read this reverse uiRig reference. Assigning it does not automatically register the HUD, find its targets or start following. Set up the rig’s uiHud reference and the HUD’s individual targets for those operations.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.VRInputModule.ButtonState.eventData
member.summary: Gets or replaces the reported press/release state and pointer data that UI processing reads for this input button.

remarks.para: This is a MouseButtonEventData object. Its buttonState says which button report to process: Pressed, Released, PressedAndReleased or NotChanged. PressedAndReleased satisfies both press and release checks. Its buttonData is the PointerEventData record containing the pointer's hit target and the information needed to process presses, clicks and dragging.

MouseState.GetButtonState creates this object when a button is first tracked, then reuses the record. MouseState.SetButtonState updates its two fields, and the VR input update fills the left-button record from its raycast pointer. A frame means one game update. A reference saved from this property points to the shared object, so later updates can change the values you read from it.

For example, eventData.PressedThisFrame() tests whether the stored report includes a press. Setting this property only replaces the stored object reference; UI processing sends events later when it consumes the data. Keep a valid event-data object on a tracked record, because the update and processing methods expect it to exist.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.VRInputModule.MouseState.hasHitUIElement
member.summary: Stores whether the most recently sampled pointer raycast selected a valid object.

remarks.para: A raycast tests what a pointing line meets. GetMousePointerEventData asks Unity's EventSystem, the system that gathers pointer events, for raycast results and selects the first suitable result. It sets this flag according to whether that result has a valid GameObject, Unity's container for an object and its components. A result with no valid object sets it to false.

The producer does not inspect the hit object for a UI component before setting this flag. The flag alone therefore does not prove that a particular menu button is selected or that a click occurred. A valid hit can set it true without a new button press.

This is a saved result, refreshed when pointer data is sampled rather than whenever the pointer moves. After VRStandaloneInputModule finishes its mouse processing, it copies this value to its own public hasHitUIElement flag. Changing this stored value yourself changes the reported flag; it does not perform another raycast or send a click event.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.VRInputModule.MouseState.m_TrackedButtons
member.summary: Keeps the button records that the press and release checks scan and pointer processing reuses.

remarks.para: Each record pairs a button identity, such as Left, Right or Middle, with saved event data. That event data contains a label such as Pressed, Released, PressedAndReleased or NotChanged, plus the pointer details needed by event processing. The constructor creates an empty list.

GetButtonState looks for the requested button and returns its existing record. If no match exists, it creates a record and appends it, so asking for a new button expands the list. SetButtonState uses that record and replaces its saved press label and pointer-data reference. For example, setting the left button twice reuses the same matching record rather than deliberately adding two left-button records.

AnyPressesThisFrame and AnyReleasesThisFrame scan this list without removing records or clearing their labels. Old labels can remain until updated; initialize or refresh each button's event data before relying on the checks for a new frame. These checks require valid records and event-data objects, so inserting null entries or replacing the list with null breaks them.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.VRInputModule.kFakeTouchesId
member.summary: The value -4, reserved as the identifier for a simulated touch-style pointer.

remarks.para: This is a pointer-cache label, with no distance or time units. It keeps that possible record distinct from mouse-style IDs -1, -2 and -3. Supplying -4 to IsPointerOverGameObject only queries an existing record; it does not create a fake touch.

The inspected touch-data helper takes the finger ID supplied by its Touch input, and the mouse-data helper uses -1. The complete methods inspected in this module do not automatically create a -4 record or issue simulated-touch events merely because this constant exists. A caller using this reserved ID must provide the corresponding pointer data and processing.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.VRInputModule.kMouseLeftId
member.summary: The value -1, identifying the primary left-button mouse-style pointer record.

remarks.para: This pointer-cache identifier is -1. Pointer IDs distinguish records in m_PointerData; they are labels, with no distance or time units. They are different from the Left, Right and Middle button types, which have values 0, 1 and 2.

GetMousePointerEventData creates and refreshes only pointer ID -1 and its left-button entry. The right and middle constants name other mouse-style pointers, but declaring those constants does not create their records or generate their clicks. IsPointerOverGameObject returns false for an ID whose cached record is absent.

For example, IsPointerOverGameObject(-1) checks the primary simulated mouse pointer’s cached hover target. Passing 0 instead asks for a different pointer record, even though Left as a button type is 0.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.VRInputModule.kMouseMiddleId
member.summary: The value -3, identifying the middle-button mouse-style pointer record.

remarks.para: This pointer-cache identifier is -3. Pointer IDs distinguish records in m_PointerData; they are labels, with no distance or time units. They are different from the Left, Right and Middle button types, which have values 0, 1 and 2.

GetMousePointerEventData creates and refreshes only pointer ID -1 and its left-button entry. The right and middle constants name other mouse-style pointers, but declaring those constants does not create their records or generate their clicks. IsPointerOverGameObject returns false for an ID whose cached record is absent.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.VRInputModule.kMouseRightId
member.summary: The value -2, identifying the right-button mouse-style pointer record.

remarks.para: This pointer-cache identifier is -2. Pointer IDs distinguish records in m_PointerData; they are labels, with no distance or time units. They are different from the Left, Right and Middle button types, which have values 0, 1 and 2.

GetMousePointerEventData creates and refreshes only pointer ID -1 and its left-button entry. The right and middle constants name other mouse-style pointers, but declaring those constants does not create their records or generate their clicks. IsPointerOverGameObject returns false for an ID whose cached record is absent.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.VRInputModule.m_InputPressed
member.summary: The last press flag supplied to UpdateRaycastPosition for the primary simulated mouse button.

remarks.para: UpdateRaycastPosition copies its isPressed argument into this field. It does not read a physical controller trigger here, detect a change from the previous flag, or clear this value after use.

GetMousePointerEventData converts true to the left-button Pressed state and false to Released on every refresh. For example, leaving it true across two refreshes requests two Pressed states. A caller that wants a one-update press supplies true for that update and then false. PanelView.UpdateCursor supplies its queued press flag this way and clears the panel’s queued flag after forwarding it.

Changing this stored flag alone does not dispatch a UI click. Data collection and the active input module’s later event processing are separate steps. A false value is the supplied release signal, not proof that a particular physical hand button is currently released.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.VRInputModule.m_MouseState
member.summary: The shared collection of simulated mouse-button records and the latest usable-raycast-hit flag.

remarks.para: Created during this module’s construction. Each button record combines a button type, its current Pressed/Released-style state and a PointerEventData reference containing target and pointer details. GetButtonState returns an existing matching button record or creates one when needed.

GetMousePointerEventData refreshes the left button and hasHitUIElement, which says whether its first usable raycast result has a valid object. VRStandaloneInputModule reads that data, processes the left press/release, then hover/movement and dragging, and finally copies the hit flag to its own shared hit indicator. A hit flag is not proof that a button was clicked.

Successive refreshes return and mutate this same collection. ClearSelection removes cached pointers but retains the collection, so an old buttonData reference can survive until the next refresh reconnects it. For example, saving this reference does not preserve a snapshot of the previous frame’s button state.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.VRInputModule.m_PointerData
member.summary: The cache of PointerEventData records keyed by each pointer’s integer ID.

remarks.para: A dictionary maps an ID to the record holding that pointer’s hover, press, drag and hit information. It is created during module construction. GetPointerData returns an existing record or, when creation is requested, makes one and gives it the same pointer ID. Mouse-data collection requests -1; touch-data collection requests the finger ID supplied by the Touch input.

IsPointerOverGameObject reads this cache without creating records, then checks that record’s hover object. Removing a record uses its own pointer ID. ClearSelection first processes hover exits for the cached pointers, then clears the entire dictionary and deselects the EventSystem object.

A cached record is stored input history, not proof that a pointer is still physically active or that its hit is current. This module does not automatically mint all four negative constant IDs. For example, querying -4 returns false when no corresponding simulated-touch record exists.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.VRInputModule.m_RaycastNormal
member.summary: The latest supplied pointer-direction vector from .

remarks.para: The caller supplies the direction in world-space axes, the coordinate system of the whole scene. A direction has no distance or time unit; its three components describe which way to point. For example, (0, 0, 1) points along the scene’s positive Z axis. This method stores the components unchanged and does not make the vector length equal to 1 or rotate a local direction into world space.

GetMousePointerEventData copies it into the pointer record’s worldNormal field before running registered raycasters. Despite that destination field’s name, this is the supplied direction, not a surface direction measured from a successful hit. It remains stored until another update or field assignment replaces it, including across ClearSelection.

A raycaster is the component that tests pointer data against objects. It decides which fields it consumes; the inspected VRGraphicRaycaster uses the 2D position and does not read this stored 3D direction. Changing this field alone therefore does not guarantee a hit along the new direction.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.VRInputModule.m_RaycastOrigin
member.summary: The latest supplied world-space pointer origin, copied by into this module’s stored input.

remarks.para: World space means coordinates in the whole Unity scene, rather than coordinates relative to one menu or controller. Position components are scene-distance units, commonly set up as one unit per metre. UpdateRaycastPosition stores the supplied three components unchanged; it does not transform a local position into world space.

At the next GetMousePointerEventData refresh, this value is copied into the pointer record’s worldPosition field before registered raycasters run. For example, (0, 1.5, 0) represents an origin 1.5 scene units above the scene’s zero point. It is an origin value supplied by the caller, not necessarily a measured controller position or the eventual hit point.

The registered raycaster decides whether to use this field. The inspected VRGraphicRaycaster reads the pointer’s 2D position instead, so changing this origin alone does not guarantee moving the cursor or raycasting from that new 3D point. ClearSelection retains it; a new update or field assignment is needed to change the stored value.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.VoidLogic.ContinuousSoundPlayer.SLZ#Marrow#VoidLogic#IVoidLogicNode#PortMetadata
member.summary: Returns the sound node's fixed input descriptions: Start, Reset, Volume cap, Pitch, and Clip index.

remarks.para: A VoidLogic node is a logic component connected to other components through ports, which act like sockets for signals. The input descriptions are in connection-index order: 0 is Start, 1 is Reset, 2 is Volume cap, 3 is Pitch, and 4 is Clip index. There are no output descriptions.

Access this property through IVoidLogicNode, the common node interface through which the logic system accesses a node's descriptions. It describes the available sockets, rather than reporting their current signal values or which sound is playing. The description is shared by all ContinuousSoundPlayer instances and is created once when the class is first initialized. Actual saved connections are held separately in _previousConnections; reading this property does not connect anything or start a sound.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.VoidLogic.OneOffDriveEuler.SLZ#Marrow#VoidLogic#IVoidLogicNode#PortMetadata
member.summary: Returns the fixed descriptions for three angle inputs: X Euler, Y Euler, and Z Euler.

remarks.para: A VoidLogic port is a socket for a signal from another logic component. Input indices 0, 1, and 2 select X Euler, Y Euler, and Z Euler respectively. Euler angles describe a rotation with three angles, one for each axis; the input numbers are in degrees. This node declares no outputs.

The node negates the supplied angles and combines them into the target rotation for a ConfigurableJoint, a physics connection that can limit and drive how two objects move. For example, an X input of 30 contributes -30 degrees to that target's X angle. This is a requested joint rotation; the physical object's response depends on the joint's settings. When an input cannot supply a value, that axis starts with the joint object's current world rotation angle before the same negation.

Access the property through IVoidLogicNode, the common node interface through which the logic system accesses a node's descriptions. The descriptions are created once when the class is initialized and shared by all instances. Reading them does not move the joint or report current input values.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.VoidLogic.OneOffLineRendererSink.SLZ#Marrow#VoidLogic#IVoidLogicNode#PortMetadata
member.summary: Returns the description of the single Power input that switches the line's configured materials between on and off.

remarks.para: A VoidLogic port is a socket for a signal from another logic component. Power is input index 0; there are no output descriptions. Its value is a unitless number. While the component is active, a value above highThreshold switches to _onMat, the configured on material. Once on, a value below lowThreshold switches to _offMat, the configured off material. Between those thresholds it keeps its current choice. A material controls how a visible surface looks.

These decisions run only when the input differs from the last processed value by more than 0.001. For example, with highThreshold = 0.7 and lowThreshold = 0.3, values 0.8, 0.5, and 0.2 turn it on, keep it on, then turn it off. Reaching either threshold exactly does not trigger that threshold's switch.

Access this property through IVoidLogicNode, the common node interface through which the logic system accesses a node's descriptions. It returns descriptions created once for the class and shared by all instances. The current connection is saved separately in _previousConnection. Reading the descriptions does not change a material or read the live Power value.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.VoidLogic.OneOffSetEuler.SLZ#Marrow#VoidLogic#IVoidLogicNode#PortMetadata
member.summary: Returns the descriptions of the X Euler, Y Euler, and Z Euler inputs that set the target object's world rotation.

remarks.para: A VoidLogic port is a socket for a signal from another logic component. Indices 0, 1, and 2 are X Euler, Y Euler, and Z Euler respectively; there are no outputs. Euler angles describe a rotation with three angles. The numbers here are degrees relative to the world's axes. For example, inputs (0, 90, 0) request a quarter turn around the world's green Y axis.

Each actuation, when the logic system tells this node to apply its inputs, immediately writes the resulting world rotation to _target. Any input that cannot supply a value keeps that axis's current world angle. The result is also saved in targetRotation. With _setOnActuation disabled, Update additionally blends the current rotation halfway toward that saved rotation each frame; disabling the flag still allows the immediate assignment during actuation.

Access this property through IVoidLogicNode, the common node interface through which the logic system accesses a node's descriptions. The descriptions are created once when the class is initialized and shared by all instances. Reading them does not turn the object or report the current input angles.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.VoidLogic.OneOffThruster.SLZ#Marrow#VoidLogic#IVoidLogicNode#PortMetadata
member.summary: Returns the descriptions of six inputs that push and spin the target's Rigidbody.

remarks.para: A Rigidbody is the Unity component that gives an object simulated physical movement. A VoidLogic port is a socket for a signal from another logic component. Indices 0, 1, and 2 are X Force, Y Force, and Z Force; indices 3, 4, and 5 are X Torque, Y Torque, and Z Torque. Torque is a turning force. There are no outputs. Each actuation, when the logic system tells the node to apply its inputs, assembles these numbers into a push vector and a turning vector. An input that cannot supply a value contributes zero.

The force inputs use forceMode: Force means newtons, Acceleration means meters per second squared, Impulse means newton-seconds, and VelocityChange means a change in meters per second. With _relativeForce enabled, their axes follow the Rigidbody's orientation; otherwise they follow the world's axes. For example, Y Force = 10 with Force mode and _relativeForce disabled applies a 10-newton upward push.

The torque inputs always use ordinary Force mode, even when forceMode is set differently. Each is multiplied by 0.017453292 before applying torque in newton-meters. For example, X Torque of about 57.2958 applies about 1 newton-meter around X. With _relativeTorque enabled, the torque axes follow the Rigidbody's orientation; otherwise they use world axes. The resulting movement depends on the object's physical properties and the physics simulation.

Access this property through IVoidLogicNode, the common node interface through which the logic system accesses a node's descriptions. These are fixed descriptions created once for the class and shared by all instances. Reading them does not push the object or report current input values.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.VoidLogic.OneOffValueReaderSink.SLZ#Marrow#VoidLogic#IVoidLogicNode#PortMetadata
member.summary: Returns the description of the Power input whose number this node displays as text.

remarks.para: A VoidLogic port is a socket for a signal from another logic component. Power is input index 0, and the node declares no outputs. The display places labelText on one line and the input number, rounded to two decimal places, on the next. For example, labelText = Level and an input of 0.25 display Level above 0.25. The number keeps the meaning and units of the source signal; this node performs no unit conversion.

The text is refreshed when the logic system initializes the node. During Update, Unity's once-per-frame check, a valid input triggers a refresh only when its value differs by more than 0.001 from the value saved by the last Update that passed this test. Initialization refreshes the text without changing that saved comparison value. If a refresh runs without a valid connection, it displays labelText followed by END POINT on the next line.

Access this property through IVoidLogicNode, the common node interface through which the logic system accesses a node's descriptions. It returns fixed descriptions shared by all instances, created once when the class is initialized. Reading it does not refresh the text or return the live input number. This component is marked obsolete and replaced by TextAdapter.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.VoidLogic.OneShotSoundPlayer.SLZ#Marrow#VoidLogic#IVoidLogicNode#PortMetadata
member.summary: Returns the fixed descriptions of the Start, Reset, Volume cap, Pitch, and Clip index inputs for requesting and controlling one-shot sounds.

remarks.para: A VoidLogic port is a socket for a signal from another logic component. Input indices are 0 for Start, 1 for Reset, 2 for Volume cap, 3 for Pitch, and 4 for Clip index. There are no outputs. Start requests a sound; Reset clears queued requests and stops existing players. Update is the routine Unity calls once per game frame, one game update. If both trigger in the same Update, Reset takes priority.

StartEdgeDetector and ResetEdgeDetector decide when their respective signals trigger. These detectors can respond to a high signal repeatedly, a rise from low to high, a fall from high to low, or both kinds of change. Their thresholds define which numbers count as high and low. A Start request may be ignored, replace existing playback, wait in a queue, or play alongside other sounds according to ClipChooser.DispatchBehavior. A request does not prove a sound has successfully started.

Volume cap is a unitless multiplier clamped between 0 and 1, then multiplied by Volume, the node's configured loudness. For Volume = 0.8 and an input of 0.5, the audio-source volume is 0.4. Pitch is a unitless multiplier applied to playback pitch; the game also adjusts that pitch for slowed game time. Pitch controls how high or low the sound is. At normal game speed, 1 keeps normal pitch; positive values below 1 lower it and values above 1 raise it. These multipliers are refreshed when a Start triggers or tracked sounds are playing, provided Reset does not take priority.

Clip index supplies the selection number when ClipChooser.SelectBehavior is Select. It is clamped to the available array positions, then its fractional part is dropped. With three clip pairs, 0 chooses the first, 1 the second, and 2 the third. Other selection modes choose without that input.

Access this property through IVoidLogicNode, the common node interface through which the logic system accesses a node's descriptions. The descriptions are created once for the class and shared by all instances. They identify sockets; reading them does not request a sound or report live input values. The game marks this component's interface as unstable.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.VoidLogic.ParticleEmissionController.SLZ#Marrow#VoidLogic#IVoidLogicNode#PortMetadata
member.summary: Returns the description of the Emission Multiplier input that scales how quickly the configured particle systems create particles over time.

remarks.para: A VoidLogic port is a socket for a signal from another logic component. Emission Multiplier is input index 0; there are no outputs. The signal is a unitless multiplier clamped between 0 and 1. A valid connection supplies the signal; with no valid connection the controller uses 1.

Awake, Unity's initialization routine, saves each configured particle system's time-based emission rate multiplier. Each actuation, when the logic system tells the node to apply its input, sets the corresponding rate multiplier to the saved value times the input. For example, input 0.5 halves the saved time-based rate, while 1 restores it and 0 reduces that rate to zero.
