With a constant setup rate of 20 particles per second, those inputs correspond to 10, 20, and 0 particles per second. Emission curves can vary the rate over time. The baseline is the saved setup value, so this does not repeatedly halve the previous result.

This changes time-based emission without clearing existing particles. Bursts and emission based on distance traveled have separate settings. Actuation is skipped while the controller's _disable flag is set.

Access this property through IVoidLogicNode, the common node interface through which the logic system accesses a node's descriptions. It returns fixed descriptions created once for the class and shared by all instances. Reading it does not change a particle system or report the live input. The game marks this component's interface as unstable.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.WaveProfile.bulletsPerEnemy
member.summary: Stores a whole-number ammunition statistic for this wave; assigning it does not award ammunition for each enemy.

remarks.para: The default-round builder stores the result of CalcWaveBPE here. For a wave with enemies, that calculation is (L + 2 × H) / N, rounded toward zero: L is lightBulletAmount, the number of light ammunition rounds; H is heavyBulletAmount, the number of heavy rounds; and N is the number of entries in enemyProfilesList. The factor 2 counts each heavy round twice. Medium ammunition is omitted by this calculation. An empty enemy list produces 0.

For example, 40 light rounds, 40 heavy rounds and four enemy entries produce (40 + 2 × 40) / 4 = 30. This is a weighted rounds-per-enemy statistic, not 30 rounds automatically given on each kill. CopyWaveProfile copies this stored value without recalculating it; changes to ammunition or the enemy list can therefore leave it out of date.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.WaveProfile.enemyProfilesList
member.summary: Sets the ordered enemy spawn entries for the wave.

remarks.para: In the ordinary arena spawn loop, each list entry is a planned enemy spawn, so repeating the same profile plans another enemy of that type. The loop reads the next entry in list order when there is room below maxConcurrent, the allowed count of active enemies. For example, [crab, guard, guard] plans a crab followed by two guards. Empty means that this loop has no enemy entries to start.

Each entry is an EnemyProfile, a description passed to an enemy spawner. A HoiPoi capsule launch can be requested for that same entry instead of the ordinary spawner. Starting a spawn or capsule request does not by itself prove that the enemy has appeared. Objective mode uses a separate routine that requests maxConcurrent enemies, taking entries from this list first and falling back to a predefined enemy when the list is shorter.

CopyWaveProfile creates a new list containing the same profile objects. Difficulty helpers can append more entries before playback. The ordinary spawn loop reads the current wave list during its repeated checks, so configure the intended list before starting the wave.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.WaveProfile.friendlyProfileList
member.summary: Stores friendly profile entries whose count sets the friendly target at arena entry in CUSTOM and PROTECT modes.

remarks.para: For those two modes, ARENA_PlayerEnter passes this list’s current number of entries to the friendly spawning routine. For example, three entries request a target of three active friendlies. That target is captured when the routine starts; changing this list afterward does not change the captured count.

The inspected friendly routine chooses the first profile from StaticProfiles.friendlyProfiles for every friendly spawn. It does not choose the corresponding object from this wave’s list. Adding different profile objects here therefore changes the target count, rather than selecting different friendly types in that routine. Friendly spawns can take time, and the target count is not a guarantee of successful completed spawns.

A new WaveProfile starts with an empty list. UpdateCustomGroup fills it with repeated references to the predefined friendly profile. CopyWaveProfile shares this entire list with the source wave, so editing that shared list affects both profiles.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.WaveProfile.heavyBulletAmount
member.summary: Sets the number of heavy ammunition rounds added or requested when this wave’s loot is spawned.

remarks.para: This is a whole-number count of heavy ammunition rounds, not a number of ammo boxes or a reward for each enemy. In ordinary loot spawning, a positive value is added to the matching pickup if that pickup still exists and is active in the level. Otherwise the routine requests a new pickup, and its later spawn callback (code called after an object is created) sets that pickup’s ammoCount to the wave’s value. For example, 40 adds 40 rounds to an existing active pickup or fills a newly created pickup with 40 rounds.

Zero or a negative value skips this ammunition category’s request in the inspected loot routines. WEAPON mode requests a separate pickup for each positive category. Requesting a pickup is separate from its successful creation, and ammunition becomes available through the pickup rather than being immediately added to the player’s inventory.

Set the amount before requesting wave loot. The later callback reads the wave object again, so a change while a spawn is pending can change the new pickup’s amount. CopyWaveProfile copies the count. CreateDefaultRound sets each ammunition category to 40, and IncreaseWaveDifficulty raises any of the three counts below 40 to 40.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.WaveProfile.hoiPoiChance
member.summary: Controls how often an ordinary wave spawn is requested through a HoiPoi capsule launcher.

remarks.para: For each enemy entry that the ordinary spawn loop can start, it rolls a whole number from 1 through 10. A roll less than or equal to this value requests a capsule launch when a launcher exists; otherwise the loop uses an ordinary enemy spawner. Thus 0 gives no capsule requests, 2 gives a 20% chance, 5 gives 50%, and 10 gives 100% when a launcher is available. Values below 0 also never qualify, and values above 10 always qualify.

The constructor sets 2. UpdateCustomGroup sets 0 for its generated waves. The loop reads the value for each eligible entry, rather than storing one chance at wave startup. This chooses how to request that enemy; it does not guarantee a capsule or enemy has finished spawning. The separate objective enemy routine does not perform this chance test.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.WaveProfile.isProceduralWave
member.summary: Marks a wave that the arena created by copying an earlier wave and increasing its difficulty.

remarks.para: CreateNewWave copies an earlier profile, adjusts its enemy list and concurrency settings, sets this flag to true, and appends the new wave to the current round. A newly constructed profile starts false. The marker records how that profile was produced.

Setting this flag yourself does not perform those generation steps. The inspected ordinary and objective spawn routines choose enemies from their lists without branching on this flag; it does not switch those routines between fixed-list and random-enemy modes.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.WaveProfile.lightBulletAmount
member.summary: Sets the number of light ammunition rounds added or requested when this wave’s loot is spawned.

remarks.para: This is a whole-number count of light ammunition rounds, not a number of ammo boxes or a reward for each enemy. In ordinary loot spawning, a positive value is added to the matching pickup if that pickup still exists and is active in the level. Otherwise the routine requests a new pickup, and its later spawn callback (code called after an object is created) sets that pickup’s ammoCount to the wave’s value. For example, 40 adds 40 rounds to an existing active pickup or fills a newly created pickup with 40 rounds.

Zero or a negative value skips this ammunition category’s request in the inspected loot routines. WEAPON mode requests a separate pickup for each positive category. Requesting a pickup is separate from its successful creation, and ammunition becomes available through the pickup rather than being immediately added to the player’s inventory.

Set the amount before requesting wave loot. The later callback reads the wave object again, so a change while a spawn is pending can change the new pickup’s amount. CopyWaveProfile copies the count. CreateDefaultRound sets each ammunition category to 40, and IncreaseWaveDifficulty raises any of the three counts below 40 to 40.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.WaveProfile.lootItems
member.summary: Lists the item descriptions processed when the arena requests loot for this wave.

remarks.para: Each ArenaLootItem describes a spawnable item, meaning an asset the game can request as a new object. In ordinary loot spawning, the routine registers the listed assets and then visits the entries in list order. It requests each valid asset at the loot spawner’s world position, meaning its position in the level; invalid entries are skipped. Requests are spread across a coroutine, a routine that pauses and continues on later frames, so returning from SpawnWaveLoot does not mean all items have appeared.

WEAPON mode takes a separate path through Looter.GetAllLootItems, which can filter entries using their probability values, and requests the selected items at a drop location near the player. The two paths therefore need not produce the same items.

The WaveProfile constructor does not create this list: assign a list, including an empty list if no item loot is wanted, before calling these loot routines. Ammunition quantities are processed separately. CopyWaveProfile builds a new item list; its random-loot option can replace listed items with random choices of the corresponding weapon category.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.WaveProfile.maxConcurrent
member.summary: Limits ordinary wave spawning according to the arena’s current count of active enemies.

remarks.para: This is a whole-number enemy count, with a constructor default of 3. The ordinary spawn loop starts its next enemy entry only while activeEnemyCount is strictly below this value. With a limit of 3, a recorded count of 3 pauses new ordinary spawns; a count of 2 allows the next entry to start. A value of 0 or less prevents that loop from starting entries while the recorded count is nonnegative.

The loop reads the limit on each check. It does not remove existing enemies when you lower it, and its check uses the controller’s recorded active count, not a fresh search of every object. Spawn requests and delayed enemy registration can also affect what is present at a particular moment.

The separate objective routine uses this value as the number of enemy spawn requests in its batch, rather than testing the active count before each request. Difficulty and concurrency helpers may change this setting before playback.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.WaveProfile.medBulletAmount
member.summary: Sets the number of medium ammunition rounds added or requested when this wave’s loot is spawned.

remarks.para: This is a whole-number count of medium ammunition rounds, not a number of ammo boxes or a reward for each enemy. In ordinary loot spawning, a positive value is added to the matching pickup if that pickup still exists and is active in the level. Otherwise the routine requests a new pickup, and its later spawn callback (code called after an object is created) sets that pickup’s ammoCount to the wave’s value. For example, 40 adds 40 rounds to an existing active pickup or fills a newly created pickup with 40 rounds.

Zero or a negative value skips this ammunition category’s request in the inspected loot routines. WEAPON mode requests a separate pickup for each positive category. Requesting a pickup is separate from its successful creation, and ammunition becomes available through the pickup rather than being immediately added to the player’s inventory.

Set the amount before requesting wave loot. The later callback reads the wave object again, so a change while a spawn is pending can change the new pickup’s amount. CopyWaveProfile copies the count. CreateDefaultRound sets each ammunition category to 40, and IncreaseWaveDifficulty raises any of the three counts below 40 to 40.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.WaveProfile.showEnemies
member.summary: Stores the showEnemies flag; it does not enable or disable enemy spawning in the inspected arena playback routines.

remarks.para: This is a stored true/false value. The wave constructor leaves it false, and CopyWaveProfile does not carry it into the new profile.
The ordinary and objective enemy routines read the enemy list and concurrency count without testing this flag. A false value therefore does not suppress their enemy requests.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.WaveProfile.showFriendlies
member.summary: Stores the showFriendlies flag; it does not enable or disable friendly spawning in the inspected arena playback routines.

remarks.para: This is a stored true/false value. The wave constructor leaves it false, and CopyWaveProfile does not carry it into the new profile.

At arena entry, CUSTOM and PROTECT modes use the friendly list’s count, and the friendly routine spawns toward that captured count without testing this flag. A false value therefore does not suppress those friendly requests.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.WaveProfile.showWave
member.summary: Stores the showWave flag; it does not enable or disable the wave in the inspected arena playback routines.

remarks.para: This is a stored true/false value. The wave constructor leaves it false, and CopyWaveProfile does not carry it into the new profile.
StartNextWave selects the next wave by its position in the round’s wave list and starts it without testing this flag. A false value therefore does not exclude that wave from this playback path.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.WaveProfile.showWaveLootItems
member.summary: Stores the showWaveLootItems flag; it does not enable or disable wave loot spawning in the inspected arena playback routines.

remarks.para: This is a stored true/false value. The wave constructor leaves it false, and CopyWaveProfile does not carry it into the new profile.

SpawnWaveLoot chooses ordinary or WEAPON loot handling from the arena mode, and both routines process the wave’s loot and positive ammunition counts without testing this flag. A false value therefore does not suppress those loot requests.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.WeaponPack.OnPackGrabbed
member.summary: Stores the callback notified with this pack when OnWeaponGrabbed runs.

remarks.para: A callback is a method saved for another system to run later. OnWeaponGrabbed invokes this Action with one argument: this WeaponPack. It does not pass along the hand, grip, or a position.

OnSpawnWeapon connects OnWeaponGrabbed to every grip in allGrips. The callback can therefore run for different weapon grips and can run more than once. A direct call to OnWeaponGrabbed also notifies it without checking isSpawned.
If no callback is assigned, the notification is skipped. Assigning a callback here does not spawn an object or attach a hand; it only changes what runs when the notification occurs.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.WeaponPack.allGrips
member.summary: Stores the weapon's child grip components that receive this pack's hand-attachment notification handler.

remarks.para: A Grip is a component describing a place where a hand can attach to an object. WeaponSpawner fills this array from grips found in the spawned weapon's children when its completion callback runs.
OnSpawnWeapon subscribes OnWeaponGrabbed to every entry. The primary weaponGrip is a separate reference; changing that one field does not replace this array or its existing subscriptions.

Provide a nonnull array with valid entries before calling OnSpawnWeapon manually. An empty array adds no handlers. These are saved references, rather than a fresh search of the object each time. OnDespawnWeapon does not clear them; references may remain after bookkeeping says the pack is no longer spawned. Changing entries after setup does not move the handlers from old grips to new ones automatically.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.WeaponPack.gun
member.summary: Stores a configured or externally supplied Gun component reference for this pack.

remarks.para: A Gun component controls a firearm's behavior, such as firing and ammunition handling. This field is a saved component reference rather than a live query of spawnedWeaponObj.

The complete inspected WeaponPack methods and WeaponSpawner spawn-request, completion, selection, and despawn methods do not populate or use this field. That completion callback caches the weapon host, grips, root physics body, and pool component instead.
Assigning this field alone does not fire, load, or replace a weapon. It does not prove the pack's current asset is a firearm, and OnDespawnWeapon does not clear it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.WeaponPack.gunBody
member.summary: Stores the weapon root's physics body whose sliding and spinning motion is cleared during a matching reset.

remarks.para: A Rigidbody is Unity's physics component for a movable object, including its motion and response to forces. WeaponSpawner fills this with the Rigidbody directly on the spawned weapon GameObject, for either ranged or melee type. Its name does not restrict it to firearms, and it is not a search for every child body.
After ResetHostObj moves weaponHost to weaponSpawn, it sets this body's linear velocity to zero metres per second and angular velocity to zero radians per second if the reference exists.

These are saved references, rather than a fresh search of the object each time. OnDespawnWeapon does not clear them; references may remain after bookkeeping says the pack is no longer spawned. The reset moves the host Transform and clears the saved body separately, so these references should refer to the intended parts of the same weapon. Assigning another body does not automatically move or rebind the host.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.WeaponPack.isSpawned
member.summary: Records whether the pack's spawn bookkeeping has been marked active.

remarks.para: OnSpawnWeapon registers hosts, sets this true, and then adds grip handlers. OnDespawnWeapon unregisters hosts before setting it false. The WeaponSpawner completion and despawn paths perform the same ordered bookkeeping.

This is a saved flag, not a live check that a weapon and magazine both exist. A pending asset-spawn request does not set it in the request method, and it can already be true before all grip setup finishes.

WeaponSpawner.DespawnPack uses it as an early gate: false skips that pack's despawn work. Setting it directly does not create objects, populate references, register hosts, or remove objects. Keep it consistent with the setup/cleanup path you run.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.WeaponPack.magBody
member.summary: Supplies the magazine physics body whose sliding and spinning motion is cleared during a matching magazine-host reset.

remarks.para: A Rigidbody is Unity's physics component for a movable object, including its motion and response to forces. ResetHostObj first moves magHost's GameObject to magazineSpawn, then sets this body's linear velocity to zero metres per second and angular velocity to zero radians per second if it exists.

The complete inspected WeaponSpawner completion callback does not discover or fill this field. Provide the intended magazine body through scene setup or another creator; the body and host references should identify the intended parts of that magazine.

The host still moves when this body is absent. Assigning the field alone does not reset an object, insert a magazine, or change its current motion. OnDespawnWeapon leaves the saved reference unchanged.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.WeaponPack.magGrip
member.summary: Stores a configured or externally supplied grip reference for the separate magazine.

remarks.para: A Grip describes a place where a hand can attach to an object. This reference identifies a magazine grip; it does not report whether a hand is currently attached.

The complete inspected WeaponSpawner spawn-request and completion methods do not populate this field. OnSpawnWeapon subscribes its notification handler to allGrips instead, and does not separately subscribe magGrip.

Assigning this reference alone does not register a magazine host or add a pack-grab notification. OnDespawnWeapon does not clear it. If a magazine grip is deliberately included in allGrips, it follows that array's subscription setup.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.WeaponPack.magHost
member.summary: Supplies the optional magazine interaction host for reset registration and return-to-spawn handling.

remarks.para: An InteractableHost is the component that groups an object's hand interactions and tracks attachments. OnSpawnWeapon passes this host to WeaponResetVolume along with weaponHost. The reset lookup adds it only when it is valid and the weapon-host registration branch is taken.
ResetHostObj sends a matching magHost GameObject to magazineSpawn's world position and orientation, then clears magBody's motion if that body exists. It does not reload, insert, or rebind a magazine.

The inspected WeaponSpawner completion callback does not fill this reference, so supply it through scene setup or another creator when using a separate magazine. OnDespawnWeapon attempts to unregister it but does not clear the saved reference.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.WeaponPack.magSpawnable
member.summary: Stores the configured crate asset for a separate magazine.

remarks.para: A Spawnable describes an asset that a pool system can load and create. This configuration is separate from the weapon asset in weaponSpawnable.

The complete inspected WeaponSpawner spawn-request and completion methods do not populate or use this field. Configuring it alone does not add a separate magazine spawn or loading step to that path. OnSpawnWeapon only registers already supplied hosts and grip handlers.
If another system creates a magazine, it must supply the relevant object, host, and body references separately. Changing this value does not replace a magazine already in the scene.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.WeaponPack.magazine
member.summary: Stores a configured or externally supplied Magazine component reference.

remarks.para: A Magazine component describes the ammunition container's behavior. The saved reference does not mean that the container is currently inserted into a weapon.

The complete inspected WeaponPack methods and WeaponSpawner spawn-request and completion methods do not search for or fill this field. They also do not use it to load the gun. The magazine host and body used by ResetHostObj are separate fields.

Assigning it does not create an object or insert it into slotReciever. OnDespawnWeapon leaves this reference unchanged, so another system that provides it should keep it aligned with the current magazine object.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.WeaponPack.magazineSpawn
member.summary: Supplies the destination world position and orientation used when resetting the matching magazine host.

remarks.para: A Transform stores an object's position, orientation, and size. World position and orientation use the scene's shared coordinate system rather than its parent's coordinates. Position is measured in metres; orientation is a quaternion, Unity's four-number representation of rotation.

ResetHostObj reads this Transform when the supplied host matches magHost, copies its world position and orientation to the host GameObject, and does not copy its scale. Moving this point changes the next reset destination without moving the current magazine immediately.

Despite the field name, the complete inspected WeaponSpawner spawn-request and completion methods do not use it to create a separate magazine. Provide it before resetting magHost; assigning it alone does not spawn or load ammunition.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.WeaponPack.meleeType
member.summary: Stores the configured blade-or-blunt label for a melee pack.

remarks.para: BLADE has value 0 and BLUNT has value 1. This is a category label, not damage, mass, or a force value.

The complete inspected WeaponPack methods and WeaponSpawner spawn request, completion, selection, and despawn methods do not read it to change the weapon. The requested asset still comes from weaponSpawnable.

For example, changing this label from blade to blunt does not replace a spawned sword with a club in those paths. Keep the label appropriate for your configured asset; it does not automatically alter that asset's behavior.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.WeaponPack.secondaryPack
member.summary: Identifies another pack that the inspected WeaponSpawner path requests and despawns after this pack.

remarks.para: When this weapon's completion callback finishes its host and grip setup, it requests SpawnWeaponPack for this reference if one is assigned. The second request has its own completion callback, so it is not guaranteed to finish at the same time as the first.

During DespawnPack, the spawner requests this weapon's pool despawn and clears spawnedWeaponObj before processing the secondary pack, then unregisters this pack. The secondary pack uses its own asset, spawn Transform, references, and spawned flag.

This is a chain of pack references, not a command to attach the second object to the first. Assigning it after a weapon has already spawned does not immediately create the second weapon. OnSpawnWeapon and OnDespawnWeapon called alone do not traverse the chain.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.WeaponPack.slotReciever
member.summary: Stores a configured or externally supplied ammunition-socket component reference.

remarks.para: An AmmoSocket is the weapon component associated with receiving ammunition. This field points to that component; it is not a Boolean saying that a magazine is inserted.

The complete inspected WeaponPack methods and WeaponSpawner spawn-request and completion methods do not populate this reference or call it to insert a magazine. Setting it alone therefore does not load ammunition or establish a connection to magSpawnable or magazine.
Keep this saved reference aligned with the actual weapon if another system uses it. OnDespawnWeapon does not clear it or update it when a different asset is requested.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.WeaponPack.spawnedMagObj
member.summary: Stores a configured or externally supplied GameObject reference for a separate magazine.

remarks.para: This is an object reference, rather than a test that a magazine is inserted into the gun or that its ammunition is loaded. The magazine component, interaction host, grip, and body are separate saved references.

The complete inspected WeaponSpawner spawn-request and completion methods do not create or assign this separate magazine object. OnSpawnWeapon and OnDespawnWeapon do not create, destroy, or clear it either.
Changing this reference alone does not rebuild the other magazine references, move it to magazineSpawn, or register its host. A separate creator or scene setup must keep the references consistent.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.WeaponPack.spawnedWeaponObj
member.summary: Stores the GameObject received by the weapon spawn-completion callback.

remarks.para: WeaponSpawner assigns this when the requested weapon has been returned to its callback, then uses it to find the pool component, interaction host, child grips, and root physics body. A spawn request can be pending while this reference is still empty.

The request method checks this reference and skips another weapon request when it identifies an existing Unity object. The spawner's DespawnPack clears it after requesting the weapon's pool despawn; OnDespawnWeapon alone does not clear it.

This is the saved root object reference, not a promise that every companion magazine reference is populated or that the object is currently held. Assigning another object here does not rebuild the component caches or reset registrations automatically.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.WeaponPack.weaponGrip
member.summary: Stores the primary child grip found for a melee weapon by the inspected spawn-completion callback.

remarks.para: A Grip describes a place where a hand can attach. WeaponSpawner fills this reference from a child Grip only when weaponType is MELEE; allGrips is collected separately for every type.

This reference is not the complete grip list used by OnSpawnWeapon. Changing it does not move existing event subscriptions or re-parent its object, and it does not automatically replace a handling pose. Custom handling changes need to update the actual grip/object setup they intend to affect.
These are saved references, rather than a fresh search of the object each time. OnDespawnWeapon does not clear them; references may remain after bookkeeping says the pack is no longer spawned.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.WeaponPack.weaponHost
member.summary: Stores the weapon's interaction host used for reset registration, return-to-spawn, and detachment before pool despawn.

remarks.para: An InteractableHost is the component that groups an object's hand interactions and tracks attachments. WeaponSpawner tries to fill it from the spawned root object's component cache when its completion callback runs.

OnSpawnWeapon registers this host with WeaponResetVolume. ResetHostObj recognizes a matching host and returns its GameObject to weaponSpawn. The spawner's despawn path checks whether the host is attached and asks it to detach before returning the weapon to its pool.

These are saved references, rather than a fresh search of the object each time. OnDespawnWeapon does not clear them; references may remain after bookkeeping says the pack is no longer spawned. Replacing this reference alone does not unregister the old host, register the new one, or rebuild the other weapon references.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.WeaponPack.weaponPoolee
member.summary: Stores the weapon instance's pool component so WeaponSpawner can request its despawn.

remarks.para: A Poolee is a component connecting an object to the pool that reuses spawned instances. WeaponSpawner saves this reference when its completion callback finds that component on the returned weapon object.

DespawnPack uses it to find the weapon's scene object for a despawn effect and calls its Despawn method. This is the backing instance for an asset-spawned weapon too, rather than an alternative to the spawn system.

These are saved references, rather than a fresh search of the object each time. OnDespawnWeapon does not clear them; references may remain after bookkeeping says the pack is no longer spawned. Assigning it alone does not spawn, activate, or despawn the weapon. A missing pool component can leave this required reference unavailable for the inspected despawn path.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.WeaponPack.weaponSpawn
member.summary: Supplies the weapon's world position and orientation for spawning and for resetting its matching host.

remarks.para: A Transform stores an object's position, orientation, and size. World position and orientation use the scene's shared coordinate system rather than its parent's coordinates. Its position is measured in metres; its orientation is stored as a quaternion, Unity's four-number representation of rotation.

WeaponSpawner reads both values when requesting the asset spawn. ResetHostObj reads them again when returning weaponHost to this location. The method writes the host's Transform directly and does not copy this Transform's scale.

Moving this spawn point changes a later request or reset destination; it does not make an existing weapon follow it. For example, a spawn point on a shelf puts a new weapon there and provides the place to return a dropped weapon when reset. Provide the reference before either path runs.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.WeaponPack.weaponSpawnable
member.summary: Specifies the crate asset requested for this pack's weapon by WeaponSpawner.

remarks.para: A Spawnable describes an asset that the pool system can load and create. WeaponSpawner uses this value with weaponSpawn's world position and orientation, then saves the resulting GameObject only when its completion callback runs.

The spawner also uses this asset's crate identifier to map a weapon selection to its configured pack. Changing it after that lookup is built does not by itself rebuild the lookup or replace an already spawned object.
Assigning it or calling OnSpawnWeapon alone does not request a spawn. The request path skips creating another weapon when spawnedWeaponObj already identifies an existing object.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.WeaponPack.weaponType
member.summary: Labels the pack as ranged or melee; the inspected spawn-completion path uses the melee value to cache a primary grip.

remarks.para: RANGED has value 0 and MELEE has value 1. The constructor initially chooses MELEE, although saved scene settings can replace it.
After storing the spawned weapon and other common references, WeaponSpawner checks for MELEE and fills weaponGrip from a child Grip. It discovers allGrips and the root Rigidbody for either type.
The actual requested asset comes from weaponSpawnable. Changing this label alone does not exchange the asset, create a firearm, populate gun, or change the physical weapon currently present.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.WeaponSpawner.IsSpawningAllowed
member.summary: Stores the shared callback notified after a kiosk’s selection-permission flag is set.

remarks.para: A callback is a function called when notified. ToggleWeaponSpawning writes its instance’s isSpawningAllowed value first, then invokes this static callback with the supplied true-or-false value. It also invokes it when the value is unchanged.

All WeaponSpawner instances share this callback, and the payload does not identify which instance sent it. Subscribe a listener before calling ToggleWeaponSpawning; that method fails if this callback has no listener after already changing its flag.

For example, SpawnableDisplay subscribes while enabled and uses false to show its spawning-disabled message and true to hide that message. Remove a listener when it is no longer needed to avoid duplicate notifications.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.WeaponSpawner.OnCountUpdated
member.summary: Stores the shared callback that reports a spawner’s tracked-object count and configured limit.

remarks.para: A callback is a function called when notified. Its Vector2 payload contains two numbers: x is the number of objects in the sending spawner’s tracked dictionary, and y is its weaponLimit. Both are object counts, even though Vector2 stores them as floating-point numbers. For example, (3, 5) means 3 tracked objects with a selection limit of 5.

Completed weapon callbacks notify after finding a pooled-object component and updating the dictionary. DespawnCountUpdate notifies after removing a known object; DespawnAllWeapons notifies after clearing the dictionary. A completed callback can report the count even when the object was already present, so a notification does not always mean the number changed.

Subscribe once. The callback is static. All spawners share it, and the two-number payload does not identify its sender. For example, SpawnableDisplay subscribes while enabled and formats these values as count and limit text; unsubscribe a listener when it is no longer needed.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.WeaponSpawner.defSpawn
member.summary: Sets the world spawn position and orientation for selected crates that have no matching preset pack.

remarks.para: A Transform stores an object’s position and orientation. OnWeaponSelected reads this transform’s current world position and rotation for the general-crate request. World positions use Unity distance units, normally meters. Orientation determines which way the new object faces; it is not an angle in this field.

Preset packs instead use their own weaponSpawn transforms. This default point is also where rejected-selection sounds and some preset-cleanup sounds are played. The display’s spawn-point action can replace this reference while the spawner is enabled.
For example, move this transform to move future general-crate requests. It does not move existing spawned weapons.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.WeaponSpawner.defaultSpawnablePack
member.summary: Stores the startup crate selections requested when is true.

remarks.para: This SpawnablePack contains a list of crate references, asset identifiers to select rather than already spawned objects. SpawnDefaultSpawnablePack requests default ammo first and then sends each listed reference through OnWeaponSelected.

Each weapon selection uses the spawning flag and current tracked-count limit and can choose a matching preset pack from weaponPackMap. For example, list a pistol crate and a melee crate to request those selections when spawnDefAtStart enables startup spawning. Configure this pack and its list before that request path runs.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.WeaponSpawner.despawnClip
member.summary: Sets the sound played for tracked objects during DespawnAllWeapons cleanup.

remarks.para: The sound is played at each tracked pooled object’s world position after its despawn request and the explicit visual-effect request. Despawning removes an object from active play so it can be reused.
For example, assign a removal sound for the broader tracked-object reset. DespawnPack uses spawnClip for its explicit sound instead, and DespawnAllAmmo does not read this clip.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.WeaponSpawner.despawnFXSpawnable
member.summary: Stores an effect asset registered for pooled reuse during startup.

remarks.para: A spawnable identifies an asset that pooling can create and reuse. Start registers this configured effect, which prepares it for reuse without creating a visible effect at that moment.

The spawner’s pack and tracked-weapon cleanup methods request spawnFXSpawnable for their explicit effects instead. For example, assigning an effect here does not change those cleanup effects; configure spawnFXSpawnable to change them.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.WeaponSpawner.heavyAmmoPoolee
member.summary: Stores the pooled-object component returned by the last completed heavy-ammo spawn callback.

remarks.para: A Poolee manages an object that pooling can remove from active play and reuse. The heavy-ammo completion callback finds that component and stores it here after resetting the box’s motion and adding 40 to its pickup ammo count when present.

DespawnAllAmmo uses this reference to remove the cached heavy box and then clears it. A missing reference can mean that no request has finished or that the callback found no Poolee; it is not proof that no request is pending.

For example, inspect this after a heavy-ammo request completes to identify the cached box. It is a saved reference, not a continuously refreshed check that the box is still active; removal elsewhere can leave the reference until this spawner clears or replaces it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.WeaponSpawner.heavyAmmoSpawnTarg
member.summary: Sets the world position and orientation for heavy-ammo box requests.

remarks.para: SpawnDefaultAmmo reads this Unity object’s transform when requesting the heavy asset from StaticProfiles. A transform holds position and orientation. Position uses Unity distance units, normally meters; orientation determines which way the new box faces.

For example, move or rotate this target before requesting replacement ammo to change the next heavy box’s placement. Assign the target during setup. Moving it afterward does not move an already spawned box, and assigning it alone does not request ammo.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.WeaponSpawner.initSpawnDelay
member.summary: Stores an initial-delay setting that the default startup paths do not apply.

remarks.para: The field starts with a value of 3, intended as a delay in seconds. The actual CoSpawnDefaultPack routine uses a fixed wait of 2 game-clock seconds and does not read this field. A game-clock second follows game speed, so slower play takes longer in real-world time.

The loading-session startup path registers a level-load callback, a function run when that load action happens, without using this field or that coroutine wait. For example, assigning 10 here does not make either default-startup path wait 10 seconds.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.WeaponSpawner.inventorySlotRecievers
member.summary: Caches the inventory slot components whose stored items are dropped and removed during inventory cleanup.

remarks.para: An inventory slot receiver is a component that holds an item in an inventory slot. GetWeaponSlots replaces this array with a scene-wide search for active receivers. Inventory cleanup uses the saved array; if it is empty or its first entry is missing, cleanup refreshes it from a supplied player object’s children, or from the scene when no player is supplied.

For example, DespawnAllWeapons supplies no player and can therefore clean items from cached or scene-wide receivers, not only weapons spawned by this kiosk. Refresh this cache after replacing a rig. The initial array has six empty entries; those are placeholders, not six discovered slots.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.WeaponSpawner.isSpawningAllowed
member.summary: Stores whether this kiosk accepts OnWeaponSelected requests while below its tracked-count limit.

remarks.para: The flag initially starts true. OnWeaponSelected requires it to be true and the tracked dictionary count to be less than weaponLimit. False rejects those requests and plays the rejection sound.

Changing this field directly updates the gate without notifying IsSpawningAllowed listeners. ToggleWeaponSpawning also sends the permission notification. For example, a direct false assignment can reject selections while a subscribed display still shows its previous message.
This gate does not remove existing objects, cancel pending requests, or block the direct preset-pack, special-weapon, or ammo methods.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.WeaponSpawner.lightAmmoPoolee
member.summary: Stores the pooled-object component returned by the last completed light-ammo spawn callback.

remarks.para: A Poolee manages an object that pooling can remove from active play and reuse. The light-ammo completion callback finds that component and stores it here after resetting the box’s motion and adding 40 to its pickup ammo count when present.

DespawnAllAmmo uses this reference to remove the cached light box and then clears it. A missing reference can mean that no request has finished or that the callback found no Poolee; it is not proof that no request is pending.

For example, inspect this after a light-ammo request completes to identify the cached box. It is a saved reference, not a continuously refreshed check that the box is still active; removal elsewhere can leave the reference until this spawner clears or replaces it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.WeaponSpawner.lightAmmoSpawnTarg
member.summary: Sets the world position and orientation for light-ammo box requests.

remarks.para: SpawnDefaultAmmo reads this Unity object’s transform when requesting the light asset from StaticProfiles. A transform holds position and orientation. Position uses Unity distance units, normally meters; orientation determines which way the new box faces.

For example, move or rotate this target before requesting replacement ammo to change the next light box’s placement. Assign the target during setup. Moving it afterward does not move an already spawned box, and assigning it alone does not request ammo.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.WeaponSpawner.limitedSpawns
member.summary: Stores spawn-point references that this component’s spawn methods do not use.

remarks.para: Each Transform can hold a position and orientation, but this array does not select positions or enforce the weapon count in this implementation. Kiosk requests instead use defSpawn or a matching pack’s weaponSpawn; random special weapons use specialWepSpawnPoint.

For example, filling this array with five points does not create a five-weapon cap or make requests rotate through those points. The selection limit comes from weaponLimit and the tracked dictionary count.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.WeaponSpawner.medAmmoPoolee
member.summary: Stores the pooled-object component returned by the last completed medium-ammo spawn callback.

remarks.para: A Poolee manages an object that pooling can remove from active play and reuse. The medium-ammo completion callback finds that component and stores it here after resetting the box’s motion and adding 40 to its pickup ammo count when present.

DespawnAllAmmo uses this reference to remove the cached medium box and then clears it. A missing reference can mean that no request has finished or that the callback found no Poolee; it is not proof that no request is pending.

For example, inspect this after a medium-ammo request completes to identify the cached box. It is a saved reference, not a continuously refreshed check that the box is still active; removal elsewhere can leave the reference until this spawner clears or replaces it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.WeaponSpawner.medAmmoSpawnTarg
member.summary: Sets the world position and orientation for medium-ammo box requests.

remarks.para: SpawnDefaultAmmo reads this Unity object’s transform when requesting the medium asset from StaticProfiles. A transform holds position and orientation. Position uses Unity distance units, normally meters; orientation determines which way the new box faces.

For example, move or rotate this target before requesting replacement ammo to change the next medium box’s placement. Assign the target during setup. Moving it afterward does not move an already spawned box, and assigning it alone does not request ammo.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.WeaponSpawner.overLimitClip
member.summary: Sets the rejection sound for kiosk selections blocked by the count limit or permission flag.

remarks.para: OnWeaponSelected plays this clip at defSpawn’s current world position when the tracked count is at least weaponLimit or isSpawningAllowed is false. It is therefore also the disabled-spawning sound, not only a full-capacity sound.
For example, with a limit of 5, count 5 rejects another selection and plays this clip. Direct pack or special-weapon methods bypass this check and do not play this rejection sound.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.WeaponSpawner.pooleeDict
member.summary: Tracks completed spawned objects and their components for counting and cleanup.

remarks.para: A Poolee manages a reusable pooled object. Completed general-crate and preset-pack callbacks add the returned Unity object and its Poolee when that component is found. This dictionary’s entry count is what OnWeaponSelected compares with weaponLimit; pending requests do not reserve entries.

DespawnCountUpdate removes a known key. DespawnAllWeapons iterates the values to remove their objects from active play, then clears the dictionary. Ammo caches and random special weapons are not added by their request paths.

Field is private; treat as internal bookkeeping. For example, manually deleting a key can reduce the reported count while leaving its object active, and manually adding one does not create a weapon. Count updates are sent by the methods and callbacks, not automatically by assigning this field.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.WeaponSpawner.spawnClip
member.summary: Sets the sound requested with weapon creation and with preset-pack cleanup.

remarks.para: SpawnWeaponPack plays it at the pack’s weaponSpawn while making a request. The general-crate path in OnWeaponSelected plays it at defSpawn while requesting and again in the completed-spawn callback. That initial sound does not prove the object completed spawning.

DespawnPack also plays this clip at defSpawn during cleanup, despite the clip’s name. For example, choose a sound that fits both uses if a preset pack will be removed through that method. DespawnAllWeapons uses despawnClip for its tracked-object loop.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.WeaponSpawner.spawnDefAtStart
member.summary: Controls whether startup schedules the default ammo and crate-selection requests.

remarks.para: This flag initially starts true. Start always registers configured assets for pooled reuse and rebuilds the pack lookup. With this flag false, it returns after that setup; with true, it schedules SpawnDefaultSpawnablePack through a level-load callback while loading or through a fixed 2-game-second coroutine otherwise.

A callback is a function run when notified, and a coroutine is a routine that can pause across game updates. The eventual default method requests ammo before applying the weapon-selection permission and limit to its crate list.
For example, set this false before Start to prepare a kiosk without automatic loadout requests. Changing it afterward does not cancel a callback or coroutine already scheduled.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.WeaponSpawner.spawnFXSpawnable
member.summary: Sets the explicit effect requested for weapon spawn requests and weapon cleanup.

remarks.para: A spawnable identifies an asset that pooling can create and reuse. Start registers this effect for reuse. SpawnWeaponPack requests it at the pack’s weaponSpawn position; the general-crate selection path requests it at defSpawn with that point’s orientation.

DespawnPack and the tracked-object loop in DespawnAllWeapons also request this effect at the removed weapon’s position. Those paths use a neutral orientation, meaning no extra rotation. Their own object-level despawn effects are separate.

For example, changing this asset changes both the explicit creation feedback and these cleanup effects. A creation effect is requested alongside a weapon request without waiting for success, so it is not proof that a weapon exists.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.WeaponSpawner.specialWeaponsList
member.summary: Stores the spawnable assets eligible for random special-weapon requests.

remarks.para: SpawnRandSpecialWep chooses a zero-based list index at random, registers that entry for pooled reuse, and requests it at specialWepSpawnPoint’s world position and orientation. A spawnable identifies an asset, not an already created weapon.

For example, place three valid entries here to make each of indices 0, 1 and 2 eligible. The list must be nonempty. This direct method bypasses the permission and count gate and does not add its completed object to the tracked weapon dictionary.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.WeaponSpawner.specialWepSpawnPoint
member.summary: Sets the world position and orientation used by random special-weapon requests.

remarks.para: A Transform stores an object’s position and orientation. SpawnRandSpecialWep reads this transform when it makes the request. Position uses Unity distance units, normally meters; orientation determines which way the weapon faces.

For example, move or rotate this point to change future special-weapon placement. Assign it before calling the random-spawn method. Changing it does not move existing objects or add them to the tracked dictionary.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.WeaponSpawner.visDebug
member.summary: Controls a Console message when a preset pack already has a weapon object and another request is skipped.

remarks.para: Unity’s Console is a message log for developers. SpawnWeaponPack checks whether spawnedWeaponObj still refers to a usable object. If so, it skips creating another weapon and, with this flag true, logs a short message naming the pack.

For example, enable it to find repeated requests for an already populated pack. It does not draw spawn-point gizmos or change the permission, limit, or duplicate-request check; the duplicate request is skipped with the flag false too.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.WeaponSpawner.weaponLimit
member.summary: Sets the tracked-object threshold that blocks further kiosk crate selections.

remarks.para: This integer counts tracked objects, not seconds or a percentage. It initially starts at 5. OnWeaponSelected accepts a request only when pooleeDict.Count is strictly less than this value and isSpawningAllowed is true. With a limit of 5, count 4 can request another object and count 5 cannot. A zero or negative limit blocks ordinary selections even with an empty dictionary.

Only completed general-crate and preset-pack callbacks add their objects to that dictionary when a Poolee is found. A Poolee manages a reusable pooled object. Outstanding requests reserve no count, and a preset can request a secondary pack after completing, so the eventual count can exceed the threshold.

Direct SpawnPackByIndex, SpawnAllWeaponPacks, SpawnWeaponPack, random-special and ammo calls bypass the selection check. For example, this field is useful for kiosk capacity control, but does not impose a hard cap on every spawn method. Changing it directly sends no count notification.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.WeaponSpawner.weaponPackList
member.summary: Stores the preset packs registered, indexed, mapped, and cleaned up by this spawner.

remarks.para: Each WeaponPack supplies its weapon asset, its own spawn point, and an optional secondary pack. Start registers those assets and builds weaponPackMap from their weapon barcodes. SpawnPackByIndex uses this list’s current zero-based order; SpawnAllWeaponPacks and DespawnAllWeaponPacks iterate it.

For example, entry 0 is the first challenge loadout preset. Configure every pack and its weapon crate before startup. Reordering the list changes index selection immediately, but an existing barcode lookup still needs CreateSpawnDictionary to rebuild it.
SpawnAllWeaponPacks requires a nonempty list and skips the whole list if the first pack is marked spawned. Adding a pack to the list does not by itself spawn an object or notify the tracked count.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Bonelab.WeaponSpawner.weaponPackMap
member.summary: Maps selected crate barcodes to their configured presets.

remarks.para: A barcode is a crate asset’s identifier. CreateSpawnDictionary fills this map from weaponPackList at startup, keeping the first pack for a duplicate barcode. OnWeaponSelected consults it to choose the preset’s weapon spawn point and optional secondary weapon.
If a selected barcode is absent, the general-crate path uses defSpawn instead. OnWeaponSelected rebuilds the map only when the map reference is missing, not whenever the list changes.
For example, rebuild the map after changing preset crate assignments. Editing this map affects later lookup choices without creating, removing, or counting a weapon at that moment.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Combat.AttackReceiver.OnAttackReceived
member.summary: Unity event invoked whenever ReceiveAttack is called on this receiver.

remarks.para: Add listeners to make an attack notification perform a scene action, such as playing an effect or starting a configured mechanism. A listener is a callback, a routine called to respond to an action. This event sends no arguments, so it does not give listeners the attack’s damage, direction or hit position.

ReceiveAttack invokes this event directly without filtering the supplied attack or changing a health value itself. Each call invokes it again; there is no once-only flag or cooldown in this receiver. Keep the event assigned: a missing event is not silently skipped.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Combat.RigidbodyProjectile.BlastDamage
member.summary: The damage value placed into blast attacks for targets with an unobstructed path to the blast origin.

remarks.para: This is a game damage amount, not a distance or a physics force. A receiving component decides how to use it; for example, GenericAttackReceiver passes Attack.damage to its float event when the attack category matches. Unobstructed targets receive this full value anywhere inside the query radius; targets whose collider-bounds center is within 0.1 world units also receive it without a wall raycast.

For other targets the blast raycasts to the collider's bounds center using blockLayerMask. A blocked target farther than 0.5 world units is skipped. A blocked target between 0.1 and 0.5 units instead receives 1 - 2 × distance × BlastDamage. This is the actual arithmetic, and it is not clamped here. Illustratively, distance 0.25 and BlastDamage = 1 gives 0.5; the same distance with BlastDamage = 10 gives -4. How a particular receiver handles a negative damage value depends on that receiver.
Both collision and piercing-attack detonation construct an outgoing attack with this damage setting. Changing it affects subsequent blast calculations, not the size of blastSpawnable.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Combat.RigidbodyProjectile.BlastRadius
member.summary: The world-space radius used to search for objects that may receive the blast attack.

remarks.para: The sphere is centered on Attack.origin, which is the first collision contact point for collision detonation or the incoming attack's origin for piercing-attack detonation. Radius is a distance in world units, normally meters; an illustrative value of 2 searches a sphere 2 meters from that point. The projectile's transform scale does not multiply this query radius.

Increasing this can include more colliders, but attackLayerMask, the target's Rigidbody and TriggerRefProxy, blockLayerMask, and the query-buffer capacity still limit actual recipients. The normal buffer holds only six returned colliders. It does not resize the spawned visual effect or add a gradual damage falloff with distance.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Combat.RigidbodyProjectile.OnProjectileShot
member.summary: Shared, argument-free callback invoked after a piercing attack has made a projectile run its blast.

remarks.para: A callback is a routine called to report an action; here it reports the piercing-triggered blast. ReceiveAttack checks for the Piercing flag, calls BlowUp, then invokes this Action if it is assigned. Ordinary collision detonation does not invoke it, and OnEnable does not invoke it. The callback has no projectile, attacker, or position argument, so listeners cannot identify those from the callback alone.

Arena_GameController subscribes while enabled and removes its handler when disabled; the handler increments its projectilesShot counter. Subscribe with += and remove your handler with -= to preserve other listeners. Replacing this static Action affects listeners for all RigidbodyProjectile instances.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Combat.RigidbodyProjectile.Rb
member.summary: Returns the configured Rigidbody whose linear velocity is reset when this projectile is enabled after the level's first two seconds.

remarks.para: A Rigidbody is the Unity physics component that gives an object simulated movement. This getter returns the stored _rb reference directly; it does not search for a Rigidbody or create one. The component must already be assigned. For example, a launcher can use the returned Rigidbody to set the projectile's velocity after OnEnable has reset it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Combat.RigidbodyProjectile.Vec3EffectScale
member.summary: Stored vector that does not control the effect size in the audited projectile blast path.

remarks.para: A Vector3 holds three numbers, commonly one per X, Y, and Z axis. Despite this field's name, Awake, OnEnable, BlowUp, ReceiveAttack, OnCollisionEnter, the Rigidbody getter, and the constructor do not read or calculate it. BlowUp does not pass it to AssetSpawner.Spawn.

Changing it therefore has no effect through those audited RigidbodyProjectile methods. Configure the spawned asset's own presentation rather than treating this unconsumed field as a verified size multiplier. This description is limited to the audited projectile implementation.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Combat.RigidbodyProjectile._initialTime
member.summary: Records Time.time when the enable-time velocity and throw-sound reset runs.

remarks.para: Time.time is the game's elapsed, time-scaled clock in seconds. This field is written only in the OnEnable branch that runs once Time.timeSinceLevelLoad is at least 2 seconds; an earlier enable does not refresh it.

The audited RigidbodyProjectile methods do not read this timestamp to delay detonation, expire the projectile, or reject early collisions. Changing it does not change those methods' collision or piercing-attack conditions. It is a recorded value, not a verified fuse setting.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Combat.RigidbodyProjectile._rb
member.summary: The Rigidbody returned by Rb and used for the enable-time linear-velocity reset.

remarks.para: Assign the physics body that should carry the projectile's motion. When at least two seconds have elapsed since level loading, OnEnable writes zero to this body's velocity before playing the throw sound. Awake does not fill this reference automatically, and changing it does not transfer velocity or reconnect col to a different body.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Combat.RigidbodyProjectile.attackLayerMask
member.summary: Chooses which Unity layers the blast searches for possible attack targets.

remarks.para: A layer is a category assigned to a GameObject; a layer mask is a set of allowed categories. For example, including only a character layer makes the overlap query ignore colliders on other layers. This is a bit mask, not a single layer number.

The mask is passed to the BlastRadius overlap query, which explicitly includes trigger colliders. Returned colliders still need an attached Rigidbody and a TriggerRefProxy on that Rigidbody object, and wall-blocking checks can reject them. This mask does not decide which collisions detonate the projectile or which incoming attack categories can detonate it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Combat.RigidbodyProjectile.attackType
member.summary: Labels the outgoing blast attack so receiving components can choose how to react to it.

remarks.para: This is copied into Attack.attackType for both collision detonation and piercing-attack detonation. It is a flags value, so multiple categories can be combined. For example, GenericAttackReceiver runs its damage event only when its accepted categories overlap this value; a receiver accepting Fire will ignore an attack containing only Blunt.

This setting is separate from the condition for shooting this projectile to detonate it: ReceiveAttack always checks whether the incoming attack contains Piercing. Changing the outgoing category to Blunt does not make blunt incoming attacks detonate the projectile.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Combat.RigidbodyProjectile.blastSpawnable
member.summary: The asset-spawning description used to create the blast object when detonation occurs.

remarks.para: Awake registers this Spawnable with AssetSpawner. BlowUp requests a spawn at the projectile transform's current world position and world rotation, with no parent supplied. The damage sphere is calculated separately around Attack.origin, so the visual and damage centers can differ.

Choose the configured asset to request, such as the prefab that supplies the intended blast presentation. BlastRadius and BlastDamage are used by the attack calculation and are not passed as effect-size parameters in the audited spawn call. Asset registration alone does not spawn it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Combat.RigidbodyProjectile.blockLayerMask
member.summary: Chooses which Unity layers can obstruct the ray from the blast origin to a candidate target.

remarks.para: For a candidate farther than 0.1 world units from the blast origin, the blast casts a ray to the center of that collider's world-space bounds. A bounds center is the center of the box enclosing the collider, not necessarily the character's head or the nearest point on its surface. Only colliders on included layers count in this obstruction test.

A blocked target beyond 0.5 world units is skipped. A blocked target at most 0.5 units away uses the special damage calculation described by BlastDamage. This is a blast line-of-sight filter; assigning it does not alter Unity's ordinary collision rules or the OnEnable collision-ignore sphere.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Combat.RigidbodyProjectile.col
member.summary: The projectile collider enabled on activation and disabled before blast targeting begins.

remarks.para: A collider is the shape Unity uses for collision and overlap detection. Assign this reference, or let Awake obtain one from the same GameObject when it is missing. It selects one collider; the setup does not collect all colliders in the object's children.

OnEnable enables this collider before its nearby-overlap query. BlowUp disables it before gathering blast targets, which stops this selected shape participating while the blast is handled. Other collider components are not disabled by that assignment.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Combat.RigidbodyProjectile.hitClips
member.summary: The sound choices used whenever this projectile runs its blast.

remarks.para: BlowUp passes this array to Audio3dManager at the projectile transform's world position after requesting the blast asset. The manager picks one entry at random. Both collision detonation and piercing-attack detonation reach this request, even if the blast query finds no attack recipients.

The sound position comes from the projectile, while the damage-query center comes from Attack.origin; these can differ. Provide an assigned array; an empty array produces no selection, while null is not handled by the audited audio-array method.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Combat.RigidbodyProjectile.m_OverlappingColliders
member.summary: Reusable storage for the colliders found by the blast's sphere query.

remarks.para: Awake creates an array with six slots. BlowUp fills it with OverlapSphereNonAlloc and processes only the returned count. This avoids creating a new target array for each blast, but the query cannot return more targets than the array has slots; six colliders need not mean six different characters.

Entries beyond the returned count are not current blast targets and can contain old references. This buffer is separate from the new overlap array used by OnEnable for collision-ignore setup. It is generated query storage, not the configured list of intended victims.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Combat.RigidbodyProjectile.throwClips
member.summary: The sound choices used when activation performs the projectile's throw reset.

remarks.para: When the level has been loaded for at least 2 seconds, OnEnable passes this array to Audio3dManager at local position (0, 0, 0) under the projectile transform. The manager picks one array entry at random; it does not play all entries. This sound request accompanies activation/reset, not a detected hand-release event.

Provide an assigned array. An empty array makes the audited audio-array method return without selecting a sound; a null array is not handled there. Changing the array changes future requests, not a sound already playing.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Combat.RigidbodyProjectile.throwerProxy
member.summary: The attacker reference copied into attacks produced by this projectile's blast.

remarks.para: A TriggerRefProxy groups references for a character or other actor. Here it is copied into Attack.proxy to identify the source of the outgoing attack. It does not choose which nearby targets receive damage and is not automatically filled with the player or the object that shot the projectile.

OnEnable clears it when the level has been loaded for at least 2 seconds. A launcher that wants to preserve attacker attribution must assign the intended actor after that reset and before detonation. Both collision and piercing-attack detonation use this field rather than copying the incoming attack's proxy.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Combat.SpawnLauncher.firePoint
member.summary: Stores a transform reference that the launcher's current registration and wait sequence does not read.

remarks.para: A transform describes an object's position, rotation, and size. Although the original field name suggests a launch point, none of this class's declared methods or its complete asynchronous Spawn sequence uses the reference to place or aim an item.

Assigning a point in front of the launcher, or moving that point, therefore does not change the position or direction of an item through those paths: they never request an item spawn. This describes the inspected launcher implementation; it does not rule out separate code reading the stored reference.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Combat.SpawnLauncher.spawnable
member.summary: Chooses the crate that and startup ask the shared asset spawner to register.

remarks.para: A spawnable contains a reference to an item crate and spawning-policy data. A crate identifies an asset, such as the saved object template for a ball. Each newly started launcher sequence copies this value once and registers the referenced crate by its identifier. Registration can prepare a pool and start loading the asset; it does not request a launched copy of that asset.

This registration path reads the crate reference, rather than applying the spawnable's spawning-policy data. The sequence does not reread the field during its repeated waits. For example, changing from a ball crate to a box crate affects a later call to Spawn, but does not make an already running sequence register the box.
The crate reference must be assigned. A missing reference causes the registration call to fail; the launcher provides no fallback item or success result.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.ButtonToggle._endPosition
member.summary: Stores the world-space end marker position captured when the button first sets up.

remarks.para: Awake uses this position and _startPosition, the joint object’s initial world position, to measure the travel distance and place the joint’s connected anchor at their midpoint. Coordinates are world-space Unity distances, normally metres.

The press check reads endTransform’s current position again each awake frame, rather than this cache. Moving the marker later changes that check’s endpoint without rebuilding the original joint limits or travel denominator.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.ButtonToggle._hasBeenPressed
member.summary: Prevents the one-shot event from firing more than once during the current enabled period.

remarks.para: The first eligible press invokes onPressOneShot and sets this flag. Releasing the button does not clear it, so later presses can still invoke onPress without repeating onPressOneShot.
OnEnable clears the flag. CancelOneShot sets it to true to suppress that event. Changing this flag does not move the shaft or clear _isPressed.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.ButtonToggle._isPressed
member.summary: Remembers that the button has entered its pressed state until it returns almost to its starting position.

remarks.para: The check uses squared distance from the joint object to endTransform, divided by the squared start-to-end travel measured in Awake. It presses below 0.05 and releases above 0.95. Those correspond to endpoint distances below about 22.4% and above about 97.5% of the setup travel, not 5% and 95% of the ordinary distance.

Once pressed, the state remains true across intermediate positions. It clears when the release threshold is crossed, then onDepress runs. OnEnable also clears it. It does not mean the shaft is still touching the fully pressed marker.

Update skips all checks while the cached Rigidbody is sleeping, so a resting physics body does not produce repeated hold callbacks. Physics sleep means the body is temporarily excluded from movement updates while it is settled.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.ButtonToggle._jointHalfLimit
member.summary: Stores half the button’s setup travel distance, in metres, for configuring the joint.

remarks.para: Awake calculates _jointLimit × 0.5, installs it as the joint’s linear limit, and uses it when setting the joint’s target position. The connected anchor is at the midpoint between the start and end markers.
This does not determine the press thresholds directly; Update uses _jointSqrLimit instead. Editing the cache after Awake does not repeat the joint assignments.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.ButtonToggle._jointLimit
member.summary: Stores the full start-to-end travel distance used to calibrate the button, in metres.

remarks.para: Awake calculates the distance between the joint object’s initial position and endTransform. The physical joint receives half of this value as its linear limit because its connected anchor is placed at the midpoint.

Despite the field name, this cache is the full travel distance, not the value currently installed in joint.linearLimit. Changing it after setup does not reconfigure the joint or recompute the related caches.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.ButtonToggle._jointSqrLimit
member.summary: Stores the squared setup travel distance used to compare button positions without taking a square root each frame.

remarks.para: Awake calculates the squared world-space distance between the start and end positions, so this has units of square metres. Update divides the current squared endpoint distance by it to obtain a dimensionless ratio.

The check uses squared distance from the joint object to endTransform, divided by the squared start-to-end travel measured in Awake. It presses below 0.05 and releases above 0.95. Those correspond to endpoint distances below about 22.4% and above about 97.5% of the setup travel, not 5% and 95% of the ordinary distance.
Use a nonzero start-to-end separation when setting up the button. Changing this cache affects the threshold denominator without changing the physical joint limit.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.ButtonToggle._limitOffset
member.summary: Stores a limit-offset value that the inspected ButtonToggle setup and update methods do not use.

remarks.para: Awake, OnEnable, Update, CancelOneShot, and the constructor do not read or assign this field. Changing it therefore does not alter travel limits or press/release detection in those methods.

_jointLimit stores full setup travel in metres, _jointHalfLimit stores half that travel for joint setup, and _jointSqrLimit stores travel squared for press checks. A custom consumer could use this exposed value, but none was established in the inspected class.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.ButtonToggle._limitSqr
member.summary: Stores a squared-limit value that the inspected ButtonToggle setup and update methods do not use.

remarks.para: Awake, OnEnable, Update, CancelOneShot, and the constructor do not read or assign this field. Changing it therefore does not alter travel limits or press/release detection in those methods.

_jointLimit stores full setup travel in metres, _jointHalfLimit stores half that travel for joint setup, and _jointSqrLimit stores travel squared for press checks. A custom consumer could use this exposed value, but none was established in the inspected class.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.ButtonToggle._padding
member.summary: Stores a numeric margin field that the inspected ButtonToggle travel calculation does not apply.

remarks.para: The constructor initializes it to 0.00001, but Awake and Update do not read it. Awake installs _jointHalfLimit directly as the joint’s linear limit.
Changing this field alone does not add travel or change a press threshold in the inspected class methods. A meaning or unit for an external consumer was not established.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.ButtonToggle._rb
member.summary: Caches the Rigidbody on the joint’s GameObject, used to skip button checks while its physics body is settled.

remarks.para: A Rigidbody is the component that lets Unity move an object through physics. Awake finds it on the same GameObject as joint, and Update calls IsSleeping before reading positions.
This reference controls whether the button’s update logic runs; it is not found through buttonShaftCollider. A sleeping body produces no press, release, or hold check until it wakes.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.ButtonToggle._startPosition
member.summary: Stores the joint object’s initial world position as the button’s released end of travel.

remarks.para: Awake records joint.transform.position and measures its distance to endTransform. The midpoint becomes the connected anchor, and half of the distance becomes the joint’s linear limit.
This cache is a setup reference in world-space metres, not the moving shaft’s current position. Enabling the component again resets its press flags but does not recapture this position.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.ButtonToggle.buttonShaftCollider
member.summary: Chooses the collider whose collisions with ignoreColliders are disabled during button setup.

remarks.para: A collider is the surface that other physics objects can hit. Awake calls Physics.IgnoreCollision for this collider and each collider in ignoreColliders, allowing the moving button to avoid those specified parts.
This field does not select the Rigidbody used for travel detection; that body is taken from joint’s GameObject. Assigning another collider later does not repeat the collision-ignore setup.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.ButtonToggle.depressClips
member.summary: Supplies the sounds randomly selected when the button enters its release state.

remarks.para: Update passes this clip array to Audio3dManager when the release threshold is crossed. The helper chooses one clip at random and plays it at the ButtonToggle component’s world position, with requested volume 0.8 and pitch 1 before the helper’s time-scale adjustment.

Use an empty array for silence; a null array is not handled as an empty list by the inspected helper. Assigning clips does not press or release the button. Playback occurs once for the transition, not every held frame.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.ButtonToggle.endTransform
member.summary: Marks the depressed endpoint used to measure button travel and detect a press.

remarks.para: Place this marker apart from joint’s initial position before Awake. Setup measures their separation, places the connected anchor at their midpoint, and installs half that separation as the joint’s linear limit.

The check uses squared distance from the joint object to endTransform, divided by the squared start-to-end travel measured in Awake. It presses below 0.05 and releases above 0.95. Those correspond to endpoint distances below about 22.4% and above about 97.5% of the setup travel, not 5% and 95% of the ordinary distance.
Update reads the marker’s world position again while the body is awake. Moving it after setup changes the detection endpoint, but does not rebuild the cached travel distance or physical joint.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.ButtonToggle.ignoreColliders
member.summary: Lists the colliders that should not collide with the button shaft.

remarks.para: Awake disables collision between every entry and buttonShaftCollider. For example, this can keep a shaft from colliding with its surrounding housing while it slides, while preserving its collisions with other objects.
Use an empty array when no pairs need to be ignored; Awake iterates the array. Replacing the list later does not automatically enable old pairs or disable new pairs.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.ButtonToggle.joint
member.summary: Connects the moving button body to its support and supplies the Transform used to detect button travel.
