remarks.para: A ConfigurableJoint is a physics connection whose motion axes and drives control how its object moves. Configure it for the shaft’s intended sliding direction. Awake places its connected anchor at the start/end midpoint, sets its linear limit to half the measured travel, and sets its target position.

With a connected Rigidbody, the midpoint is converted into that body’s local coordinates; without one, the anchor is in world coordinates. Awake also finds the Rigidbody on this joint’s GameObject. Assigning a new joint after setup does not automatically redo that calibration.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.ButtonToggle.onDepress
member.summary: Runs once when a previously pressed button returns almost to its initial position.

remarks.para: While _isPressed is true, Update releases the button when squared endpoint distance divided by squared setup travel is greater than 0.95. It clears the pressed state, then invokes this parameterless UnityEvent, so listeners observe _isPressed as false. The threshold corresponds to an endpoint distance greater than about 97.5% of setup travel.
No release event is generated merely by enabling the component or by moving an already unpressed button. The Rigidbody must be awake for the check to run.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.ButtonToggle.onHold
member.summary: Runs on each processed frame while the button remains in its latched pressed state.

remarks.para: The first press frame can also invoke this parameterless UnityEvent. It keeps running while the shaft moves through intermediate positions after a press, stopping when the release threshold is crossed. The shaft does not need to remain at the depressed endpoint.

Update skips all checks while the cached Rigidbody is sleeping, so a resting physics body does not produce repeated hold callbacks. Physics sleep means the body is temporarily excluded from movement updates while it is settled.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.ButtonToggle.onPress
member.summary: Runs once when the button first crosses into the pressed state.

remarks.para: The check uses squared distance from the joint object to endTransform, divided by the squared start-to-end travel measured in Awake. It presses below 0.05 and releases above 0.95. Those correspond to endpoint distances below about 22.4% and above about 97.5% of the setup travel, not 5% and 95% of the ordinary distance.

After the state becomes pressed, Update invokes this parameterless UnityEvent, then may invoke onPressOneShot. It does not invoke onPress again until the button has crossed the release threshold and presses again.

Update skips all checks while the cached Rigidbody is sleeping, so a resting physics body does not produce repeated hold callbacks. Physics sleep means the body is temporarily excluded from movement updates while it is settled.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.ButtonToggle.onPressOneShot
member.summary: Runs on the first eligible press after the component is enabled, then stays suppressed until another enable.

remarks.para: This parameterless UnityEvent follows onPress when _hasBeenPressed is false. Update then sets that flag. Releasing the button does not clear it, so this is once per enabled period rather than once per ordinary press.

OnEnable clears the one-shot flag. CancelOneShot sets it ahead of time to prevent the event; it does not invoke it or reset the button’s pressed state. The ordinary onPress event still runs for later press transitions.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.ButtonToggle.pressClips
member.summary: Supplies the sounds randomly selected when the button enters its press state.

remarks.para: Update passes this clip array to Audio3dManager when the press threshold is crossed. The helper chooses one clip at random and plays it at the ButtonToggle component’s world position, with requested volume 0.8 and pitch 1 before the helper’s time-scale adjustment.

Use an empty array for silence; a null array is not handled as an empty list by the inspected helper. Assigning clips does not press or release the button. Playback occurs once for the transition, not every held frame.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.Key.code
member.summary: Codes carried by this key. A accepts it only when it carries every code that receiver requires.

remarks.para: The codes are independent switches that can be combined with the bitwise OR operator, written | in C#. For example, CODE_A | CODE_B gives the key both codes. That key passes the code check for a receiver requiring CODE_A, CODE_B, or CODE_A | CODE_B, but fails a receiver requiring CODE_C. Extra codes on the key are allowed; sharing just one of several required codes is insufficient.

The receiver checks this value when the key enters its interaction area. Passing the check lets its insertion process begin when the receiver is active and empty; the codes alone do not complete insertion or fire its unlock event. A receiver whose code value is zero has no required code switches, but it still requires a Key component on the entering object's InteractableHost GameObject.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.KeyReceiver.OnInserted
member.summary: Calls listeners with the Key after the automatic insertion animation has finished.

remarks.para: The receiver first plays insertClips and invokes onUnlock, then sets _State to INSERTED and _isActive to false before invoking this callback. The argument is the Key component obtained from _keyHost’s GameObject.
Use this callback to react when seating is complete, for example to show that the socket now contains a key. It also runs for consumed keys. A null callback is skipped.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.KeyReceiver.OnKeyRemoved
member.summary: Calls listeners with the Key when the receiver restores that key to independent physics.

remarks.para: Runs after the body is unpacked, the ejection sound is requested, onLock fires and the inserted-key grab listener is removed. The argument is the Key component on _keyHost’s GameObject.

This happens both when a removable inserted key is grabbed and when the ejection coroutine reaches the slot exit. It runs before _isActive is reset to true and before ejection’s final host cleanup. Therefore it differs from OnRemoved, which reports completion of animated ejection.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.KeyReceiver.OnRemoved
member.summary: Calls listeners after animated ejection finishes and the key’s host-exit cleanup has run.

remarks.para: CoEjectMagazine assigns outward Rigidbody velocity, restores interaction and invokes OnInteractableHostExit before calling this parameterless callback, a routine called to report completion. The optional Release callback runs after host exit and before OnRemoved. In the normal exit path, _State is EMPTY and the cached key and host references have been cleared by this point.
Simply grabbing a removable inserted key invokes OnKeyRemoved but does not invoke this callback. A null callback is skipped.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.KeyReceiver._ActivePerc
member.summary: Stores the smoothed strength of the hand’s alignment with the slot entrance.

remarks.para: During HOVERING, MoveTowardsStartInsertTarget calculates a target blend from the Key transform’s distance and orientation relative to startInsertTarget. It smooths this value and uses it to interpolate the hand-guided key pose toward the entrance pose. The value has no unit: 0 keeps the tracked pose and 1 uses the aligned entrance pose.
This is not elapsed animation time or progress along the start-to-end insertion path. It is reset to 0 when a candidate key is accepted and when ejection ends, then overwritten by guidance updates.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.KeyReceiver._ActivePercVel
member.summary: Stores the smoothing velocity used to ease the hand’s entrance-alignment blend.

remarks.para: MoveTowardsStartInsertTarget passes this field by reference to Mathf.SmoothDamp while updating _ActivePerc. It carries the current rate of change between updates, in blend units per second, so the hand’s guidance strength changes smoothly.
This is internal smoothing state, not key Rigidbody speed or a configurable insertion-speed limit. Guidance updates replace it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.KeyReceiver._CartridgeGrabbedTime
member.summary: Counts how many seconds the current post-removal pause has lasted.

remarks.para: While _WasMagazineGrabbed is true, OnInteractableHostStay adds Time.fixedDeltaTime to this value. Once the existing value exceeds 0.5 seconds, it re-runs host exit and entry handling, clears the pause flag and resets the timer, then adds one final fixed-update step before returning.
This is an elapsed-time counter, not the clock time when a grab happened. Key entry and exit also reset it to 0. The same pause flag can be set after an ejection marked by _IsHoverEject.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.KeyReceiver._HandTargetTransform
member.summary: Stores the world-space hand position and rotation calculated for entrance guidance.

remarks.para: MoveTowardsStartInsertTarget creates this pose while a key is held near startInsertTarget. OnPreRealtimeRig passes it to SkeletonHand.OverrideTransform with full override weight during HOVERING, moving the rendered hand toward the slot while accounting for its grip offset.
SimpleTransform contains a position and quaternion rotation; it is a saved pose, not a Unity Transform object. The position uses world units, normally meters. Each guidance update replaces it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.KeyReceiver._HandToInsertTarget
member.summary: Caches the Key transform’s position and rotation relative to the holding hand at initial alignment setup.

remarks.para: CalculateMagazineRig obtains the first held hand and computes the Key transform relative to that hand: position is measured from the hand’s origin along the hand’s rotated axes, and rotation describes how the key is turned relative to the hand. The position is in world-distance units, normally meters; SimpleTransform does not include scale.

The audited KeyReceiver methods and its insertion, ejection and fixed-update state machines write this calibration value but do not read it for guidance. Current guidance recomputes the hand-to-key relationship directly. Changing this cache has no demonstrated effect in those paths.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.KeyReceiver._InsertTargetToHand
member.summary: Caches the neutral grip-hand pose relative to the Key transform during initial alignment setup.

remarks.para: CalculateMagazineRig first expresses the grip’s handle pose in the Key transform’s coordinate frame, then combines it with HandPoseAnimator.GetHandInHandleNeutral for that grip’s selected hand pose. This describes where a neutral gripping hand would sit relative to the key, including both position and rotation.

The position uses the key’s rotated axes and world-distance units, normally meters; this SimpleTransform has no scale. The audited receiver methods and its three state machines write this cache but do not use it to calculate the current guidance pose.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.KeyReceiver._IsHoverEject
member.summary: Marks an ejection that should delay acceptance of the same nearby key afterward.

remarks.para: SetHoverEject sets this flag without starting removal. When _isActive allows entry handling, a matching key entering while the receiver is INSERTED also sets this flag and starts CoEjectMagazine. Normal completed insertion clears _isActive, so entry handling is disabled until removal restores it. At ejection completion the flag is cleared and _WasMagazineGrabbed is set, activating the half-second reentry pause in OnInteractableHostStay.
This is not a continuously checked hand-hover switch in the audited receiver code.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.KeyReceiver._State
member.summary: Selects which key-handling actions run during updates.

remarks.para: The enum values are EMPTY (0), SWITCHING (1), EJECTING (2), HOVERING (3), INSERTED (4) and SLIDING (5). HOVERING guides the held hand toward the entrance; SLIDING marks the automatic seating stage; realtime updates in this state apply the finger-pose override; INSERTED makes hasCartridge true when _key is valid.

The audited transitions use EMPTY, HOVERING, SLIDING and INSERTED. Animated ejection does not set the enum’s EJECTING value; it runs through its own coroutine, a sequence that continues over several frames. Writing the state alone does not pack or unpack the key, play sounds or fire events, so use the normal insertion and Release paths.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.KeyReceiver._WasMagazineGrabbed
member.summary: Enables the pause that prevents a recently removed key from being immediately accepted again.

remarks.para: Grabbing a removable inserted key sets this flag, changes _State to EMPTY and runs the unlock/removal helper. Ejection marked by _IsHoverEject also sets the flag after the key is expelled, even if no hand grabbed it.

OnInteractableHostStay uses _CartridgeGrabbedTime to wait slightly over half a second, then re-runs host exit and entry handling. It clears the pause flag, resets the elapsed-time counter and adds one final fixed-update step to the counter before returning. Key entry and exit also reset the flag and counter.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.KeyReceiver._isActive
member.summary: Allows the receiver to consider incoming hosts as key candidates.

remarks.para: The constructor starts this flag as true. Completed insertion sets it false, so later entry callbacks stop accepting candidates; removal restores it to true. It does not mean a key is present: a completely empty receiver can be active.
Changing it affects entry handling only. It does not cancel an insertion or ejection coroutine that is already running.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.KeyReceiver._key
member.summary: Stores the Key component accepted for the current approach, insertion or removal.

remarks.para: A Key supplies the code checked by the receiver and its transform supplies the alignment reference. This is assigned together with _keyHost when a matching key enters an empty receiver, before seating is complete.
hasCartridge also requires _State to be INSERTED. The host-exit path clears this reference when leaving HOVERING; simply restoring physics on a grabbed key does not immediately clear it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.KeyReceiver._keyHost
member.summary: Stores the accepted key’s interaction component, used for grips, hands and physics.

remarks.para: The receiver uses this host to find the held hand, detach it, disable or restore interaction, access its Rigidbody, and pack its entity body into the receiver. GetHost returns this same reference.

It is assigned when an accepted key enters an empty receiver and can remain assigned during guidance or removal. Changing it independently of _key can make the receiver manipulate a different object from the one whose alignment and code it measures.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.KeyReceiver._sphereCollider
member.summary: Caches the receiver’s SphereCollider and supplies the initial entrance-guidance distance scale.

remarks.para: Awake, Unity’s initialization routine, gets the SphereCollider on the receiver’s GameObject and sets _sqInsertDistance to its local radius squared, without applying transform scale. The base InteractionReciever receives trigger contacts and identifies nearby interaction hosts.

When a matching key is accepted, _sqInsertDistance is replaced using that key’s initial distance from startInsertTarget. Thus this collider’s radius is the initial distance setting, not a live value read on every guidance update. Add and configure a SphereCollider on the receiver’s GameObject before Unity initializes it. Awake fills this cached reference from that component.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.KeyReceiver._sqInsertDistance
member.summary: Stores the squared distance scale used to fade entrance guidance with distance.

remarks.para: Guidance divides the Key transform’s squared world distance from startInsertTarget by this value. A distance contribution of 1 - clamp01(distanceSquared / _sqInsertDistance) becomes stronger as the key approaches; facing alignment also limits the result. The unit is squared world-distance units, normally square meters.

Awake starts it as the SphereCollider radius squared. On key acceptance it becomes 0.25 × clamp(initialHostDistanceSquared, 0.005, 1). For example, an initial host distance of 0.2 meters produces 0.01 square meters, so the distance contribution reaches 0 at 0.1 meters from the entrance. This is an illustrative calculation, not a prefab default.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.KeyReceiver.cancelToken
member.summary: Stores the cancellation source for the receiver’s alternate fixed-update loop.

remarks.para: When an active receiver sees an unheld host enter, it cancels any previous source, creates a new one and starts AltFixedUpdateLoop with a token linked to object destruction. That loop checks when a hovering key is free of force pulling or other claims and can start automatic seating.

Host exit cancels and clears this source; OnDisable cancels it. Cancelling this source stops that alternate loop, not the separate insertion or ejection coroutines. The field is a CancellationTokenSource despite its name.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.KeyReceiver.code
member.summary: Specifies which code bits an entering Key must contain before this receiver accepts it.

remarks.para: The acceptance test is (key.code & receiver.code) == receiver.code. Every bit selected here must be present on the key; extra bits on the key are allowed. For example, a receiver requiring CODE_A accepts a key carrying CODE_A and CODE_B, while a receiver requiring both A and B rejects an A-only key.
The check occurs when the host enters. Changing code does not automatically eject an already inserted key. A code of 0 passes the bit test for any Key.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.KeyReceiver.ejectClips
member.summary: Provides the sounds from which one is randomly chosen when the key is unpacked during removal.

remarks.para: The sound is played at the receiver transform’s world position, not at a moving key position. It is requested before onLock and OnKeyRemoved, including removal by grabbing a removable inserted key.

Audio3dManager.PlayAtPoint chooses one clip randomly from a nonempty array. An empty array produces no sound; a null array is not checked safely by that helper. Use an empty array when no sound is wanted.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.KeyReceiver.endInsertTarget
member.summary: Defines the position and rotation of the Key alignment point when fully seated.

remarks.para: CoWaitLockMagazine reads this transform’s world pose when seating starts and converts it to the receiver’s coordinate frame. It animates toward that saved pose, then places the interaction host using its measured offset from the Key transform. Thus the target aligns the Key component’s transform, which need not be the host’s origin.

Ejection uses the same seated endpoint as its start and moves toward startInsertTarget. Arrange both markers to define the slot’s insertion direction. Editing the marker during an already running animation does not rebuild its saved endpoint.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.KeyReceiver.hasCartridge
member.summary: Reports whether a valid Key has finished insertion and the receiver is in INSERTED.

remarks.para: Returns true only when _key is neither null nor destroyed and _State is INSERTED. An accepted key that is still hovering or sliding does not count.

Animated ejection leaves the receiver’s state as INSERTED until its final removal stage, so this value can remain true while the key is visibly sliding out. Use OnRemoved to observe completion of that ejection.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.KeyReceiver.insertClips
member.summary: Provides the sounds from which one is randomly chosen when automatic seating finishes.

remarks.para: The sound is played at the receiver transform’s world position, not at a moving key position. It is requested just before onUnlock and OnInserted.

Audio3dManager.PlayAtPoint chooses one clip randomly from a nonempty array. An empty array produces no sound; a null array is not checked safely by that helper. Use an empty array when no sound is wanted.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.KeyReceiver.isKeyConsumed
member.summary: Keeps a seated key from being released by ordinary grabbing.

remarks.para: When false, completed seating attaches a grab listener and restores the host’s interaction. Grabbing the inserted key then unpacks it and fires onLock and OnKeyRemoved. When true, seating skips both that listener and interaction restoration, leaving the key held in the socket.

The key is kept rather than destroyed. Scripted Release checks only whether _key is valid and can still eject a consumed key. This option is read during seating completion; changing it afterward does not automatically rebuild grab listeners or interaction settings.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.KeyReceiver.marrowEntity
member.summary: Identifies the receiver’s physics assembly into which the key’s body is packed.

remarks.para: During seating, the receiver combines the key entity’s primary MarrowBody with this entity’s primary body. That lets the key remain part of the receiver assembly rather than falling away under its own physics. Removal unpacks it to restore an independent body.
Assign the receiver’s own MarrowEntity before insertion. This reference is required by MakeStatic, MakeDynamic and the corresponding coroutine operations.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.KeyReceiver.onLock
member.summary: Invokes configured UnityEvent actions when the key is removed from its packed socket state.

remarks.para: Use this to return the controlled mechanism to its locked state, for example to close access after its key is removed. It fires in OnMagazineUnlocked after unpacking and requesting the removal sound, before OnKeyRemoved.
It runs for both grabbing a removable key and completed animated ejection. It does not mean that the receiver has just fixed a key in place; insertion fires onUnlock.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.KeyReceiver.onUnlock
member.summary: Invokes configured UnityEvent actions after the key has finished seating.

remarks.para: Use this to unlock the mechanism controlled by the socket, for example to open access when the required key is inserted. OnMagazineLocked requests the insertion sound, then invokes this event before setting _State to INSERTED, setting _isActive false and calling OnInserted.

A listener invoked here can therefore still see the previous SLIDING state or hasCartridge false. OnInserted runs after those state changes if a listener needs the completed-state view. Removal fires onLock.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.KeyReceiver.startInsertTarget
member.summary: Defines the entrance position and orientation used to guide a key into the slot.

remarks.para: While hovering, the receiver compares the Key transform’s world distance and facing with this marker and moves the rendered holding hand toward an aligned entrance pose. Its position is also used to set the guidance distance scale when an accepted key first enters.

Animated ejection ends at this marker. The ejection coroutine saves its pose relative to the receiver when ejection starts, preserving the Key-to-host offset when positioning the physical object. Place this marker at the slot mouth and endInsertTarget at the fully seated alignment point.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.PowerPuncher._collisionCollector
member.summary: Supplies the impact reports that can discharge the puncher.

remarks.para: Assign the collector before Awake. Awake subscribes the puncher's collision handler, and OnDestroy removes that subscription. The collector first tests its own impactVelocityThresh against motion into the contact surface; the puncher then applies its charge, cooldown, direction, and speed checks.

PowerPuncher processes the collector's stored collisions during physics and rendered-frame updates when its own rigidbody exists and is awake. Replacing this reference after Awake does not move the existing event subscription to the new collector.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.PowerPuncher._cooldownStartTime
member.summary: Stores the scaled game-time timestamp of the last successful discharge, used to prevent another punch for 0.8 seconds.

remarks.para: This is a timestamp in seconds, not the remaining cooldown. The collision handler accepts the timing check when Time.time minus this value is at least 0.8. For example, a discharge at game time 10 can pass this check again at 10.8. Awake initializes it to zero, and each successful discharge overwrites it.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.PowerPuncher._fixedRan
member.summary: Tracks whether an eligible physics update has run since the last rendered-frame collision processing.

remarks.para: FixedUpdate sets this flag after checking that the puncher has a rigidbody and that it is awake. If the flag was already set, another physics step processes the collector's accumulated collisions first. Update processes any remaining haul while the flag is set, then clears it. This lets collisions be handled when several physics steps occur before one rendered frame.
This is recurring bookkeeping, not a one-time initialization flag. Changing it can skip a processing pass or request an extra one.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.PowerPuncher._host
member.summary: Stores the puncher's own interactable host, which supplies the rigidbody used to decide when collected collisions should be processed.

remarks.para: Awake gets the InteractableHost on the same GameObject. FixedUpdate and Update skip collision-haul processing if its physics body has no rigidbody or the rigidbody is sleeping, meaning Unity has stopped actively simulating it until something wakes it. This reference is a setup cache rather than the object currently being hit.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.PowerPuncher._triggerStartTime
member.summary: Stores when the current punch began charging, with zero marking an inactive charge.

remarks.para: The value is a timestamp in scaled game-time seconds. Attached-hand updates start it when the index trigger is greater than 0.3; elapsed time from this timestamp controls charge brightness, sound pitch, icon stages, and discharge strength. Charge reaches its strength cap after 1.6 seconds.

Awake, attachment, detachment, and releasing the trigger reset this value to zero. A successful discharge instead sets it to the current time, so holding the trigger continues charging a new punch. Changing the value changes how much elapsed charge the next update or impact sees; it is not a duration setting.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.PowerPuncher.blastParticles
member.summary: The particle system played once a punch successfully discharges.

remarks.para: Rejected impacts do not play it. Assign the particle system before use; the successful-discharge path calls Play directly. Its particle settings control the appearance of this feedback, while collision and charge calculations control the attack.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.PowerPuncher.body
member.summary: Selects the mesh objects whose materials glow as the punch charges.

remarks.para: Awake takes the material from each object's MeshRenderer and stores it in bodyMat. Every selected material receives the same charge color, using the first material's initial emission color as the fully charged color.
The array must contain at least one object, and each object must have a MeshRenderer. Changing this array after Awake does not rebuild the cached materials, so configure it before initialization.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.PowerPuncher.bodyEmissionColor
member.summary: The stored emission color that the body's charge glow approaches at full charge.

remarks.para: Awake copies this color from the first cached body material. Charge updates blend every body material from black toward this color using the 0-to-1 charge fraction. For example, a red stored color produces a red glow whose brightness grows while charging.

Changing this cache after Awake changes the endpoint used by later glow updates. It does not immediately recolor the body; the next emission update applies it. A shader must support emission for the written color to appear as a glow.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.PowerPuncher.bodyMat
member.summary: The cached material instances that receive the body's charge glow.

remarks.para: Awake creates an array matching body and fills it from each MeshRenderer's material. Later updates write emission colors to these instances rather than looking up the renderers again. Editing a referenced material can change the displayed body, but the next charge or fade update replaces its emission color.
Replacing body objects after initialization leaves this cache pointing at the old materials. The glow updater expects each cached material to exist.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.PowerPuncher.chargeParticles
member.summary: The particle systems started while a held hand presses the trigger enough to charge the puncher.

remarks.para: Charging begins above an index-trigger input of 0.3. The first charging update calls Play on every system and sets chargeParticlesPlaying, avoiding repeated Play calls while charging continues. Trigger release or hand detachment stops every system and clears that flag.
Assign an array whose entries are valid particle systems. An empty array provides no charging particles but still lets the bookkeeping flag change.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.PowerPuncher.chargeParticlesPlaying
member.summary: Records whether the puncher has started its charging particles and has not yet stopped them through its own release or detach handling.

remarks.para: This flag prevents repeated Play calls during charge. Release and detachment use it to decide whether to call Stop, then clear it. It is the puncher's bookkeeping rather than a live query of each particle system: stopping a system elsewhere does not update this flag.
Setting it to true does not start particles, and setting it to false does not stop them. Changing it can make the next charging update replay particles or make release skip its stop calls.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.PowerPuncher.forward
member.summary: Sets the puncher's accepted impact direction and the main direction of its added knockback.

remarks.para: The vector is relative to the PowerPuncher component's own rotation. With a length-1 vector of (0, 0, 1), punches are accepted toward its blue Z axis; (1, 0, 0) selects its red X axis. Rotating the component rotates this direction in the world.

The hit test compares this vector with the direction from triggerGrip.targetTransform's world position to the contact point. For a length-1 vector, their dot product must be greater than 0.76, allowing contacts less than about 40.5 degrees off the chosen direction. The code does not normalize forward itself: its length also changes this test and the shove magnitude. Use a length-1 vector when choosing a direction.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.PowerPuncher.icon
member.summary: The mesh object that displays charge stages and the short discharge animation while the puncher is held.

remarks.para: Awake caches its MeshRenderer material and hides the object. Hand attachment shows it; detachment hides it again. The material's texture is treated as six horizontal frames, with ordinary charge using frames 0 through 3 and PopAnim using frames 4 and 5.
Assign the object before Awake and give it a MeshRenderer. Swapping this object later changes which object is shown or hidden but does not rebuild iconMat.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.PowerPuncher.iconMat
member.summary: The cached icon material whose horizontal texture offset selects the charge or discharge picture.

remarks.para: Awake gets this instance from icon's MeshRenderer. Frame i uses a horizontal offset of i divided by 6: frame 0 uses 0, frame 3 uses 0.5, and frame 5 uses about 0.833. The texture and material must be arranged to display those six frames appropriately.
This code changes texture offset rather than tinting the icon. Later charge, release, detach, or discharge-animation updates can overwrite an offset you set manually.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.PowerPuncher.lastEmissionValue
member.summary: Remembers the last charge brightness so releasing the trigger can fade the body smoothly to black.

remarks.para: Attached-hand charging updates overwrite it with elapsed charge divided by 1.6 seconds, limited to 0 through 1. For example, after 0.8 seconds of charging it is 0.5, halfway between black and bodyEmissionColor.

On release, a 0.2-second eased animation starts from this saved value and fades to zero. The cache stores the latest charging value; that fade does not continuously update the cache. Changing it alone does not immediately change the materials or the attack strength.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.PowerPuncher.popAnimPlaying
member.summary: Marks the period when the icon is displaying its discharge animation.

remarks.para: PopAnim sets this flag before frame 4 and clears it after two 0.4-second waits. While it is true, charging skips its usual icon-stage changes, and the collision handler does not start another PopAnim sequence.
The flag does not itself start an animation or block a qualifying discharge. Setting it manually can suppress icon updates without showing the discharge frames.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.PowerPuncher.sfx
member.summary: Provides the charging-start, charging-loop, release, and successful-discharge sounds.

remarks.para: Starting charge calls Grab, releasing the trigger calls Release, successful discharge calls GravFire, and detaching the hand calls StopSound. During charging, the loop's pitch setting follows elapsed charge up to 1.6 seconds, plus 0.3, producing a rising pitch.
Assign this sound controller before use. Changing its audio clips changes the feedback; the puncher's timing and impact checks determine when those calls happen.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.PowerPuncher.triggerGrip
member.summary: Selects the grip whose held hand supplies the trigger input for charging the puncher.

remarks.para: Awake subscribes to this grip's attached updates and hand attach/detach events. A held hand's index-trigger input greater than 0.3 starts charging; releasing to 0.3 or below clears the charge. Attachment shows the icon, and detachment hides it and stops charge feedback.

The grip's targetTransform position is also the starting point for the impact-direction test. Assign this reference before Awake. Replacing it later does not transfer the existing event subscriptions to the new grip.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.MLAgents.AutoAgroBoid.attackProbability
member.summary: Unitless attack-decision threshold copied into a reported boid when the aggro callback runs.

remarks.para: The callback is a routine called to configure the reported boid. It copies this value into BehaviourBoid.attackProbability. In the boid’s Agroed attack-tick branch, a random value from 0 to 1 must be strictly below that threshold before the attack preparation can continue. For example, a threshold of 0.25 accepts a draw of 0.2 and rejects a draw of 0.3.

This is one condition of an attack decision, not a chance that each collision causes damage. A usable target, controller movement state, distance and obstruction checks also matter. The AutoAgroBoid callback copies the value directly; the Inspector’s 0–1 range is not a runtime clamp here.
Changing this setting affects later configuration callbacks. It does not continually overwrite boids that have already received their probability value.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.MLAgents.AutoAgroBoid.boid
member.summary: The most recent found while configuring an aggro notification.

remarks.para: SetAgro searches the reported Behaviour component’s object and children for BehaviourBoid and writes this cache before configuring its targets and settings. A boid is a game-controlled creature whose movement is handled by its behaviour and agent components.

This is one cached reference, not a collection of every boid configured by the spawner. Each later notification replaces it. Writing this cache does not choose which object the next notification reports or retarget the spawner’s event connection.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.MLAgents.AutoAgroBoid.boidSpawner
member.summary: The whose OnAutoAgro notifications this component listens to.

remarks.para: Awake is Unity’s initialization callback, a routine called to prepare the component. If this reference is missing, Awake looks for MLZoneSpawner_Child on the same GameObject. If neither is available, it logs the missing setup and returns; otherwise it subscribes SetAgro to OnAutoAgro.

A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action. The notification supplies the Behaviour to configure and a player target reference. This component reacts to that notification; it does not itself spawn boids or guarantee that every spawn emits it. Assign the intended source before Awake, since changing this field later does not move the already installed subscription.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.MLAgents.AutoAgroBoid.bumperUpdateRate
member.summary: Number of physics updates to wait between the configured boid bumper’s scheduled ray checks.

remarks.para: When setBumperRate is true, the aggro callback copies this integer into the boid’s child BoidBumper.fixedUpdateDelay. The bumper casts rays to refresh obstacle-hit information. After its counter resets, it waits this many FixedUpdate calls, then performs the cast step on the following call; FixedUpdate is Unity’s physics-update routine.

For an illustrative value of 2, it waits two physics updates and casts on the third. With an illustrative 0.02-second physics timestep, that is one scheduled cast step every 0.06 seconds of simulation time. A larger value means less frequent checks; after counter reset, a nonpositive value causes no waiting. This is a count of physics updates, not a rate in hertz.

The callback sets the delay but does not reset the bumper’s current counter. It requires a BoidBumper under the boid’s PuppetMaster, the component managing its physical body. Changing this AutoAgroBoid setting affects later callbacks rather than continuously updating already configured bumpers.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.MLAgents.AutoAgroBoid.findBall
member.summary: Requests the reported boid’s setup path to connect it to an associated BehaviourBoidBall.

remarks.para: The aggro callback copies this into the boid’s findBehaviourBall flag. The boid’s zone-setup response uses that flag to search up its parent hierarchy and through those ancestors’ children for BehaviourBoidBall, a component coordinating a group of boids. This is an associated hierarchy object, rather than any ball elsewhere in the scene.

That setup connects ball notifications to the boid’s agent and sensors, records the boid in the ball’s group, and assigns ball-related target references. It clears the boid’s request flag after successful linking. The true branch requires a suitable associated ball; the false branch follows the ordinary waypoint setup route.

Copying this option does not itself run the zone-setup response. Changing it later does not immediately make an already configured boid search, nor remove previously installed ball connections. It is a setup request, not a continuous “seek every ball” switch.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.MLAgents.AutoAgroBoid.setBumperRate
member.summary: Allows the aggro callback to replace the reported boid bumper’s physics-update delay with bumperUpdateRate.

remarks.para: When true, SetAgro finds BoidBumper under the boid’s PuppetMaster, which manages its physical body, and copies bumperUpdateRate into fixedUpdateDelay. That delay counts physics updates to wait before the following scheduled obstacle-ray check. For example, a copied value of 2 makes the bumper wait two physics updates before casting on the third.

When false, this callback leaves the bumper’s existing delay alone; it does not disable the bumper or restore a previous delay. Turning the option on affects later callbacks and does not immediately reconfigure previously processed boids. The true path requires the bumper reference it searches for.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.MLAgents.BehaviourBoid.MState
member.summary: Gets the stored mental state, or runs when assigned.

remarks.para: A mental state is this computer-controlled character's behavior mode. Reading this property returns the inherited mentalState value. Assigning it calls the state-switching method, including its sensor and AI setup; it does more than store an enum value. Assigning the current state again still reruns the setup.

Roam allows the boid sensor's goal-radius and proximity-radius setters, marks the inference agent actively managed, and sets a 1-second behavior-decision interval. Investigate does the same with a 0.2-second interval. An inference agent is the component that supplies observations to the learned AI; its activelyManaged flag allows the boid agent's observation routine to proceed, subject to other checks.

Roam requests a vision-sphere radius of (R + 1) / 2, where R is activeRange, the configured roaming distance value. Investigate uses the same equation with R equal to investigateRange, the configured investigation distance value. R and the radius use the sensor object's local Unity distance units, normally metres before object scaling. A requested radius greater than 0.5 enables the sphere; a radius of 0.5 units or less disables this round sensor area. For example, a roaming distance value of 9 requests a radius of 5 units.

Agroed blocks those boid-sensor radius setters, marks the agent actively managed, uses agroTickRate as the decision interval in seconds, requests a vision radius of 2 units, and calls the aggression-sound routine. When the ordinary sensors already have a target, it also copies that target's head physics body's position-and-rotation Transform to boidController.boidBall, the controller's follow reference. Selecting Agroed does not choose a new enemy by itself.

After successful setup, the switch stores the requested state and requests the next eligible AI tick, one round of behavior decisions, without waiting for the usual interval. It does not run an attack immediately. The intervals use time unaffected by the game's time-scale setting; the actual update schedule still determines when decisions run. Engaged and MindControlled receive only the stored-state and tick-request steps in this switching method.

Rest first runs SetAgentInactive, which selects start_state_list[start_state_ind] and runs that state's setup, before the outer switch stores Rest. The list holds starting-state choices and the index selects one. Rest can therefore retain that selected state's sensor and agent settings. Selecting Rest again through this helper on an ordinary BehaviourBoid can repeatedly enter the same Rest path. Use a valid list and index, and do not assume that reading Rest proves the inference agent has stopped. Setup failures can leave partial changes because the switch has no rollback.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.MLAgents.BehaviourBoidBall.MState
member.summary: Reports the stored mental state; assigning it runs and applies that mode’s settings.

remarks.para: A mental state is the ball’s behavior mode, such as Rest, Roam, Investigate or Agroed, meaning alerted to a target. Reading MState only returns the stored mentalState value. Setting MState calls this ball’s SwitchMentalState routine, rather than only writing an enum number. There is no same-value shortcut: assigning the current mode can repeat spawn-limit, radius, movement and sound setup.

For those four modes, the setter applies the corresponding boid count to the first encounter group’s maximum-alive limit and calls encounter startup. A boid is one of the small creatures associated with the ball. It selects the mode’s minimum/maximum goal and proximity radii, distance settings around the ball in world units normally metres, and resets their current values to the selected minima. Changed goal-radius callbacks, registered methods called by an event, run before changed proximity-radius callbacks and receive their new radius numbers. Connected boid sensors can block radius updates. The selected hover height is a target surface distance for the fourth physics thruster, a script that pushes the ball; it is not an instant position change. The radius transition settings are per-second blending factors for later radius updates, not a promised duration.

Roam sets the ordinary AI decision interval to 1 second, copies the configured roaming-choice frequency, enables the mover and applies its roaming navigation speed and turning rate. Investigate selects 0.2 seconds. Agroed selects health.cur_hp × agroTickRate seconds, where cur_hp is the health fraction, normally 1 at full health and 0.5 at half health, and agroTickRate is the full-health interval in seconds, and calls the aggression-sound routine. Lower health shortens this ordinary wait; intervals use time unaffected by game-time slowdown. Rest retains the current AI interval. The thruster destination-distance tolerance is 0 for Rest, Roam and Investigate, and 1 world unit, normally 1 metre, for Agroed. The three non-Rest presets also reset the vision sphere using sensors.visionFov as its local radius number; the call disables it at 0.5 or below and enables it above 0.5.

The stored mental state is updated after the selected setup and its radius callbacks finish. A callback reading MState during the transition therefore still sees the previous state, unless some callback or other code has changed it. The method then sets _forceAiTick, requesting that the next eligible AI decision pass skip its usual interval wait. Successful return means this setup reached its final writes; it does not prove that spawning, movement or audible playback has completed. Missing required setup or a throwing callback can interrupt the transition before those writes.

For example, ball.MState = Roam applies the Roam setup; reading ball.MState afterward returns Roam on the normal return path. Assigning Roam again repeats setup and can reset radii that have since changed. Engaged and MindControlled are recorded and request a forced AI pass, but this ball’s switch routine does not apply the four modes’ preset setup for them.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.MLAgents.BehaviourStationaryTurret._tempGroup
member.summary: Stores the turret body-part group most recently copied during collision handling, which selects the hand, foot, or ordinary-impact path.

remarks.para: A puppet muscle is a physics-controlled body part. Its group is a unitless category: Hips, Spine, Head, Arm, Hand, Leg, Foot, Tail, or Prop. When OnMuscleCollisionBehaviour reaches its group check, it copies the group from the turret's own collided muscle into this property. This is the turret part that was hit, rather than the other object's group.

A Hand collision takes the close-range hit path only while meleeAttackActive is true, meaning a close-range attack is active, and the other object has a Rigidbody—a Unity component that gives an object physical mass and motion. That path has further checks before damage can be applied. A Foot collision skips the ordinary stun and impact-sound path. For other groups, the ordinary path rejects squared relative speed below 0.4 (metres per second) squared, about 0.632 metres per second of relative speed. Relative speed measures how fast the colliding bodies move compared with each other. Equality passes this speed check; the health system's own thresholds then decide the stun or damage response.

The group is copied before those Hand, Foot, and speed checks. For example, a Foot collision can leave this property set to Foot even though that handler returns without applying ordinary impact effects. Earlier filters, such as a disabled behavior, a blocked collision interval, or a collision with one of the turret's own bodies, return before copying a group and leave the previous value here. Attack damage reported through OnMuscleHitBehaviour does not refresh it.

This property records the classification used by that collision handler. Writing it alone does not replay a collision or change a muscle's configured group. The next collision that reaches the group check overwrites it with that muscle's current group before selecting its response.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.FizzleOnRecycleDecorator.crateSpawner
member.summary: Selects the spawner whose recycling callbacks make this decorator request a despawn effect for the recycled entity.

remarks.para: Reset fills this reference from a CrateSpawner on the same GameObject; a GameObject is Unity's object in the scene. Awake then registers the decorator with that spawner, so assign it before Awake if you set up the component yourself.

Changing the field later does not unsubscribe from the old spawner or subscribe to the new one. A GameObject is Unity's object in the scene; a component is behavior or data attached to it, such as MarrowEntity. The spawner calls this component's OnRecycle(GameObject) callback to report a recycled object; a callback is a method the spawner invokes for an event. The MarrowEntity cache is the game's lookup table for finding that component on the GameObject. OnRecycle requests the effect only when that lookup succeeds. To change sources, unregister from the old CrateSpawner, change crateSpawner, then register with the new one; unregister from the current spawner to stop notifications.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.MobileEncounter.AllGroupsKilled
member.summary: A callback is code you assign for the encounter to call; this no-argument callback runs after each group's loop passes its death-count check.

remarks.para: Despite the name, the checked loop calls this once for each group reaching its IsAllDead condition, after CheckCompletion. It does not first test whether all configured groups have finished. The delegate has no arguments.

The base loop invokes this field without a null check. Assign a handler, even an empty one when you need no action, before a group can finish. CompleteEncounter called manually does not invoke this callback.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.MobileEncounter.OnComplete
member.summary: The encounter completion event invoked after marking complete and before requesting cancellation of group loops.

remarks.para: CompleteEncounter invokes it once per transition to _complete = true when the event is assigned. CheckCompletion can reach the same completion path automatically, and TerminateEncounter calls CompleteEncounter before resetting state, so termination can also fire it.

It does not guarantee every NPC has been despawned or every spawn task already finished. The cancellation sources are canceled after the event, and an empty unstarted source slot can fail during that later cancellation.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.MobileEncounter.OnGroupMemberSpawned
member.summary: A GameObject is the Unity scene object that holds attached components. This callback is user-supplied code the encounter calls with the spawned GameObject and the group that reported it.

remarks.para: Awake connects each group's OnGroupSpawned to this forwarding callback. The group sends its notification before finishing its AI-brain registration, so use the GameObject and supplied group directly instead of assuming every tracking counter has already advanced.

For example, a handler can tag or record the new object. The notification can occur before the group has verified that the object has both AIBrain and Poolee components. The base forwarding method has no null guard for this field, so assign a handler before spawning begins.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.MobileEncounter._complete
member.summary: Prevents StartEncounter from starting again after the completion path has run.

remarks.para: Completion sets this true before OnComplete and cancellation. TerminateEncounter clears it after CompleteEncounter returns. It is a state latch, not proof that all spawned NPCs were removed or all async work stopped. Editing it directly does not reset completeCount, a group's isComplete flag, or the spawn subscriptions.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.MobileEncounter._isEncounterActive
member.summary: Blocks another StartEncounter call while an encounter has been started and has not gone through completion or termination.

remarks.para: Starting sets this true; completing or terminating sets it false. StopEncounter and PauseEncounter do not clear it in the checked base implementation. The async loop does not read it, so setting it false does not stop a running loop and can allow another start while earlier work remains.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.MobileEncounter._isEncounterPaused
member.summary: Makes StartGroupEncounter skip the group's Setup call while this flag is true.

remarks.para: PauseEncounter sets it, starting clears it after group-start calls, and completion/termination clear it. The checked async loop does not read this flag, so changing it does not pause spawning or delay timers. This describes the base class and its loop; derived code can use the flag differently.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.MobileEncounter._spawnCTSs
member.summary: A cancellation source is a handle that requests its group's timed loop to stop; its token is the signal the loop checks between waits. This array stores each source at the matching spawnGroups index.

remarks.para: Awake allocates the array with empty slots. StartGroupEncounter cancels an older source when needed and replaces that slot with a new one. CompleteEncounter requests cancellation on every slot and assumes each contains a source, so sources for groups that have never started need particular care.

These tokens govern the encounter loop and its delays. They are not passed to the group's SpawnAsync or SpawnProfileAsync operation already being awaited. Replacing a field reference or stopping Unity coroutines does not cancel a source.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.MobileEncounter.completeCount
member.summary: Counts groups credited as complete and supplies the next group index in SERIES.

remarks.para: CheckCompletion increments it for an unfinished reported group. PARALLEL also counts unfinished nonhostile groups that it marks complete. Reaching spawnGroups.Length triggers encounter completion; SERIES otherwise starts the group at this count.

StartEncounter leaves the count unchanged, while TerminateEncounter resets it to zero. Writing it yourself changes both progression and completion decisions; it does not actually complete the corresponding groups.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.MobileEncounter.isWarmed
member.summary: No warmup behavior was verified for this flag in the base MobileEncounter class or its async encounter loop.

remarks.para: The checked Awake and Start methods prepare spawners, subscriptions, and profile resources without reading or setting this flag. Changing it is therefore not a verified way to preload the encounter or skip setup. This finding covers the base class and its complete loop, rather than all derived components or mods.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.MobileEncounter.onGroupComplete
member.summary: Holds optional callback code supplied by the caller; the encounter invokes it with a group after crediting that group as complete.

remarks.para: The single argument is the SpawnGroup credited complete. The callback is optional and runs after that group's CompleteGroup action, before the encounter decides whether to start the next series group or finish.

It is not called again by this branch for an already complete group. PARALLEL's additional bookkeeping that marks other nonhostile groups complete does not invoke this callback for each of those groups.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.MobileEncounter.spawnGroups
member.summary: Defines the groups the encounter prepares, starts, counts, targets, and manages.

remarks.para: Set up the array and each group's spawners before Awake, which sizes matching cancellation storage and subscribes to spawn callbacks. Start prepares profile resources and optional toggles. Null groups or spawners are not skipped by those setup paths.

PARALLEL starts all indices; SERIES uses completeCount as the next index, so array order defines series progression. Changing the array afterward does not rebuild cancellation storage or old subscriptions. Group settings control alive/dead limits, spawn totals, initial delay, and spawn interval.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.MobileEncounter.spawnOrder
member.summary: Selects whether all configured groups start together or progression starts one group at the current completion index.

remarks.para: PARALLEL starts every group; their own delays and alive/spawn limits can still postpone individual spawns. SERIES starts the group at completeCount and advances when CheckCompletion credits groups, normally after their total death count is reached.

This value is read by both start and completion handling. Changing it during an encounter affects later decisions but does not cancel, rearrange, or restart loops already running. Values other than the two defined enum choices do not enter either normal ordering branch.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.SFX.TriggeredAudio.audioClips
member.summary: Clip choices for ; each request selects one random entry.

remarks.para: The audio manager chooses one array index when PlayAudio() is called; it does not play every clip or move through them in a fixed order. For example, with three clips, each call requests one of those three. An empty array skips the playback request.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.SFX.TriggeredAudio.min_distance
member.summary: Sets the inner distance where moving closer stops making this positional sound louder.

remarks.para: This value is passed to Unity's AudioSource.minDistance without a conversion. It uses Unity world units: for example, 2 means the listener stops getting closer-louder inside two scene units from the sound. Outside that distance, Unity starts distance attenuation. This is not the maximum audible range; this component does not set the AudioSource's maximum distance or rolloff settings.
The constructor's code default is 1.0. A saved scene or prefab can supply another value; no scene or prefab settings were audited for this documentation.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.SFX.TriggeredAudio.pitch
member.summary: Sets the base pitch ratio for each sound request; at normal game speed, values above or below 1 make the clip play higher or lower and faster or slower.

remarks.para: The manager applies an extra time-speed factor before setting the audio player's pitch: effective pitch = pitch × (0.25 + 0.75 × Time.timeScale). Here pitch is this field's unitless ratio, Time.timeScale is the unitless game-time speed ratio (1 means normal speed), and the parenthesized factor is also unitless. For example, pitch 0.8 at timeScale 0.5 becomes 0.8 × 0.625 = 0.5. At normal timeScale 1, the factor is 1; at timeScale 0, it is 0.25.
The constructor's code default is 1.0. The TriggeredAudio code does not clamp this field before passing the adjusted value to Unity's AudioSource pitch setter.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.SFX.TriggeredAudio.volume
member.summary: Sets the volume value sent to the audio player for each sound request.

remarks.para: This is a unitless AudioSource volume level, not a distance or a decibel value. A value of 0 makes this source silent; 0.5 requests a halfway source-level setting, while mixer and listener settings can still change the final sound. Unity documents AudioSource volume on a 0-to-1 scale. TriggeredAudio passes the value through without a local clamp.
The constructor's code default is 1.0. Each request sends the value to the new or reused audio player's AudioSource; changing this field does not itself update a sound already requested.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.UI.SpawnablesPanelView.SpawnablesQuickMap
member.summary: Stores the ordered crate lists displayed for each category, package, or author row.

remarks.para: A dictionary pairs a string key with a value; here each row name maps to a list of spawnable crates, which are catalog entries for objects the gun can create. _selectedTag chooses which list supplies the item buttons.
GenerateCategoriesMapping clears and rebuilds this map for the selected tab. Editing the map directly does not rebuild navigation rows or refresh button text.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.UI.SpawnablesPanelView._activeTags
member.summary: Stores all navigation rows currently available in the browser, before they are divided into pages.

remarks.para: The first tab can replace this with the current tree branch’s available child categories plus All. Other tabs can contain tag, package-title, or author rows. Page display takes a slice of this list, and category selection uses a page number and button slot to find the full-list entry.
GenerateCategoriesMapping and FilterTagTree overwrite this list. Changing it directly does not refresh the buttons or item mapping.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.UI.SpawnablesPanelView._allTags
member.summary: Remembers the generated navigation tags for the current tab so tree filtering can hide unavailable categories.

remarks.para: GenerateCategoriesMapping replaces it with a copy of _activeTags. FilterTagTree keeps only tree-child names also found in this copy. It is not a complete list of every tag in every loaded package.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.UI.SpawnablesPanelView._currentPage
member.summary: Remembers which page of spawnable items the browser displays, with 0 meaning the first page.

remarks.para: Each page uses itemButtons.Length entries. With 6 buttons, page 1 begins at list index 6, meaning the seventh entry. Page controls update the text, buttons, and highlights as well as this stored index; assigning the index alone does not perform that refresh.
Selecting a tab resets it to 0. The navigation methods stop at the first or last page instead of wrapping.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.UI.SpawnablesPanelView._currentTagPage
member.summary: Remembers which page of category rows the browser displays, with 0 meaning the first page.

remarks.para: Each page uses treeButtons.Length entries. With 6 buttons, page 1 begins at list index 6, meaning the seventh entry. Page controls update the text, buttons, and highlights as well as this stored index; assigning the index alone does not perform that refresh.
Selecting a tab resets it to 0. The navigation methods stop at the first or last page instead of wrapping.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.UI.SpawnablesPanelView._numberOfPages
member.summary: Caches how many pages are needed for the current items list.

remarks.para: PopulateMenu divides the entry count by itemButtons.Length, the number of button slots per page, and rounds upward. For example, 13 entries with 6 slots give 3 pages; an empty list gives 0. The slots must be configured before calculating this.
The page controls read this count to stop at the last page and hide unnecessary arrows. Changing the count alone does not add entries or refresh the screen.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.UI.SpawnablesPanelView._numberOfTagPages
member.summary: Caches how many pages are needed for the current category rows list.

remarks.para: PopulateMenu divides the entry count by treeButtons.Length, the number of button slots per page, and rounds upward. For example, 13 entries with 6 slots give 3 pages. The slots must be configured before calculating this.

The page controls read this count to stop at the last page and hide unnecessary arrows. Changing the count alone does not add entries or refresh the screen. If _activeTags is empty, PopulateMenu returns before recalculating this cache, so the previous count can remain stored.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.UI.SpawnablesPanelView._selectedItem
member.summary: Remembers the button slot passed to the last item selection, starting at 0 on that page.

remarks.para: This is the slot within itemButtons, rather than the index across the entire category. Selecting the second button stores 1 even on a later page. _selectedItemIndex separately remembers the full-list index for the highlight. Assigning this field alone does not select a crate.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.UI.SpawnablesPanelView._selectedItemIndex
member.summary: Remembers the selected crate’s index across the full category list so its button can be highlighted on the correct page.

remarks.para: SelectItem calculates it as page × slots + buttonSlot. Here page is the 0-based item page number, slots is itemButtons.Length, and buttonSlot is the clicked button’s 0-based position. With 6 slots on page 1, slot 2 gives index 8, the ninth crate.
Selecting a tab, changing category, or going back in the tree sets it to -1 to clear the item highlight. That reset does not clear selectedObject or send a selection notification.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.UI.SpawnablesPanelView._selectedItemTag
member.summary: Remembers the category key that was active when the last item was selected.

remarks.para: SelectItem copies _selectedTag here before storing the new selected crate. Navigating to another category can change _selectedTag without changing this saved selection context. Assigning it does not update the item buttons or choose a crate.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.UI.SpawnablesPanelView._selectedTabIndex
member.summary: Remembers the selected top-level tab and controls how category lists are rebuilt.

remarks.para: The verified tab choices are 0 for the category tree, 1 for Developer Tools, 2 for Favorites, 3 for Pallets, and 4 for Authors. These are array indexes starting at 0.
SelectTab updates highlights, resets pages, changes headings, and rebuilds the lists before refreshing the display. Assigning this field directly only changes the stored choice.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.UI.SpawnablesPanelView._selectedTag
member.summary: Chooses which mapped crate list fills the item buttons.

remarks.para: Its string must be a key in SpawnablesQuickMap. Depending on the tab, that key can mean a category such as Ammo, a package title, an author, or All. Category navigation updates this key and resets the item page before refreshing.
Writing a new string alone does not update the display or select a crate. A missing map key cannot supply a valid list.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.UI.SpawnablesPanelView._selectedTagIndex
member.summary: Remembers the selected category row’s index across the full navigation list, for highlighting.

remarks.para: The index is categoryPage × slots + buttonSlot. categoryPage is the 0-based category page, slots is treeButtons.Length, and buttonSlot is the clicked slot starting at 0. With 5 slots on page 1, slot 2 gives full-list index 7.
HighlightProperSpawnItem shows its marker only on the page containing that index. Entering a branch or selecting a tab can reset the index to 0. It is not simply the visible button slot.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.UI.SpawnablesPanelView.ammoBarcodes
member.summary: Supplies the crate references that replace the browser’s Ammo category, in list order.

remarks.para: A crate reference identifies a catalog entry rather than an object already in the scene. GenerateCategoriesMapping resolves these references into a fresh Ammo list after sorting the other item lists, so this list controls both membership and order for Ammo.
The constructor supplies six ammunition references. Changing this list affects the next mapping rebuild; it does not immediately redraw the browser.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.UI.SpawnablesPanelView.capsuleButton
member.summary: Supplies the position-and-orientation component used to anchor the meow sound request.

remarks.para: MeowButton reads this button’s Transform and localPosition when meowClip is assigned. The local position is an offset in meters relative to a parent; the sound request uses the button itself as its parent and supplies that offset again. A missing button is not guarded when the clip exists.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.UI.SpawnablesPanelView.dummyBonelabPallet
member.summary: Represents the combined BONELAB package group when pallet rows are sorted by folder date.

remarks.para: CollectPalletDates finds the loaded pallet whose barcode is SLZ.BONELAB.Content and stores it here. Its cached date is set to the earliest possible date. GenerateCategoriesMapping associates the combined BONELAB row with this pallet, so it sorts after newer mod packages in newest-first order.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.UI.SpawnablesPanelView.favoriteButton
member.summary: Displays whether the selected crate’s barcode is in favorites through its special image.

remarks.para: SelectItem sets the special image after filling the item information; FavoriteItem toggles the same image before refreshing and saving. On first activation the image is disabled until an item supplies its favorite state.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.UI.SpawnablesPanelView.favoriteCrates
member.summary: Stores favorite barcode strings and their catalog crate values for the panel’s markers and saved list.

remarks.para: A dictionary pairs each barcode, a unique content identifier, with its crate entry. FavoriteItem toggles keys here; item and information buttons check key membership to decide whether to show a favorite marker. SaveFavorites exports the keys to player settings.

Activate reloads this dictionary from the active save each time the panel opens, replacing unsaved edits. A saved valid barcode can be present even when its crate lookup did not succeed, so a favorite key does not guarantee a usable crate value.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.UI.SpawnablesPanelView.firstActivation
member.summary: Requests first-time browser setup on the next activation.

remarks.para: The constructor sets it to true. While true, Activate initializes the folder-date cache, repairs tags, selects the first tab, and prepares the initial headings and page. Activate sets it false only after loading favorites and populating the menu.
true therefore means setup is still pending, not that first activation has already finished. Setting it true later requests that setup again and can alter the loaded crate tags again.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.UI.SpawnablesPanelView.itemButtons
member.summary: Provides the item grid’s button slots, determining how many crates fit on each page.

remarks.para: Page refresh assigns crate titles to these buttons, enables slots with entries, hides unused slots, and shows each favorite marker. Selection and highlight routines read their highlight images.
The array length is the page size. With 6 slots, page 0 shows entries 0–5 and page 1 shows entries 6–11. Configure the holder references and a nonzero length before populating the menu.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.UI.SpawnablesPanelView.itemPageText
member.summary: Displays the item page number and total when more than one page is available.

remarks.para: The stored page index starts at 0, but the displayed number starts at 1. With index 1 and three pages it reads "2 of 3". UpdatePageText clears this text and hides both arrows when fewer than two pages are needed.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.UI.SpawnablesPanelView.itemScrollDownButton
member.summary: Next item-page button whose visibility follows the available page range.

remarks.para: UpdatePageText hides both item arrows when fewer than two pages are needed. This arrow is shown only before the last page. The page-navigation routine also checks the boundary before changing pages.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.UI.SpawnablesPanelView.itemScrollUpButton
member.summary: Previous item-page button whose visibility follows the available page range.

remarks.para: UpdatePageText hides both item arrows when fewer than two pages are needed. This arrow is shown only after the first page. The page-navigation routine also checks the boundary before changing pages.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.UI.SpawnablesPanelView.labelText
member.summary: Displays the heading for Developer Tools, Favorites, Pallets, or Authors when those tabs are selected.

remarks.para: SelectTab changes both its text and its visibility. The category-tree tab hides this heading and shows the tree-path text instead; Pallets shows the heading alongside the NEW or ABC sort label. Assigning another text object changes where later tab updates write.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.UI.SpawnablesPanelView.otherStripTags
member.summary: Lists fallback category tags that the browser displays with the shorter label Other.

remarks.para: The constructor includes Weapon Other, Gun Other, Melee Other, Prop Other, and NPC Other. UpdateTagPageItems substitutes Other for these button labels, and FilterTagTree applies the same substitution at the current path end. The underlying category key remains the original tag.
Adding a name here changes its displayed label during the next refresh; it does not exclude that category’s crates.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.UI.SpawnablesPanelView.p
member.summary: Reads the active save’s player settings, including the saved favorite barcode list.

remarks.para: This getter asks the save manager for the active save on each call. It is not a separate cache owned by the panel. The active save must exist for the getter to return its settings.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.UI.SpawnablesPanelView.palletInstalledDates
member.summary: Caches pallet folder last-write dates for newest-first ordering of package rows.

remarks.para: The dates are collected during first activation, from runtime mod folders identified by pallet barcodes. They are timestamps, not durations in seconds, and are not guaranteed installation dates. Missing folders get an early fallback date; the combined BONELAB group uses the earliest date.
The date sorter reads this cache when sortSwap is false. Changing a cached date affects the next mapping sort, while merely switching sort mode does not recollect folder dates.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.UI.SpawnablesPanelView.palletStripTitles
member.summary: Lists built-in package titles whose crates are combined into the BONELAB package row.

remarks.para: The constructor lists BONELAB Content, Core, External, NoBuild, Test, and Brandons. GenerateCategoriesMapping compares the full titles and groups their crates together rather than making six separate pallet rows.
CleanupUserTags also uses this list to distinguish built-in packages from packages needing untagged fallback processing. These strings are matching rules, not a list of labels to draw directly.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.UI.SpawnablesPanelView.selectModeDelegate
member.summary: Contains listeners notified when the panel requests a spawn-gun mode.

remarks.para: A listener is a callback: a routine called to report an action. SelectMode forwards the requested UtilityModes value; SPAWNER is 0 and REMOVER is 1. It notifies even when the requested value matches a previous request.

SelectItem also sends SPAWNER before changing the selected crate or its information. A listener at that point sees the preceding selectedObject. The panel does not store a current mode here; the attached gun’s listener applies the request to the gun.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.UI.SpawnablesPanelView.selectSpawnableDelegate
member.summary: Contains listeners notified with the catalog crate chosen by an item selection.

remarks.para: A listener is a callback: a routine called to report an action. SelectItem stores selectedObject, fills the item information text, and updates the favorite marker before calling these listeners with that crate. It sends the SPAWNER-mode notification earlier in the same selection.

The argument describes content the gun can create; it is not a newly spawned scene object or a report that a spawn succeeded. The gun subscribes while its trigger grip is attached and uses the notification to change its selected crate and preview.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.UI.SpawnablesPanelView.selectedObject
member.summary: Remembers the catalog crate chosen by the panel’s last item selection.

remarks.para: A spawnable crate describes an object that can be created; it is not the object already placed in the scene. SelectItem writes this reference before filling the information text and notifying crate listeners. FavoriteItem uses its barcode to toggle favorites.

Changing category, changing page, or clearing an item highlight does not necessarily clear this reference. Writing it directly does not update information text, highlights, or the gun’s selection listener.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.UI.SpawnablesPanelView.sortSwap
member.summary: Chooses alphabetical or newest-first ordering of package rows in the Pallets tab.

remarks.para: true selects ABC and sorts package titles alphabetically. false selects NEW and sorts cached folder last-write timestamps from newest to oldest.
The crate lists inside each package still sort by crate title. Assigning this flag alone does not refresh the menu; SwapSortButton flips it and selects the Pallets tab to rebuild the rows.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.UI.SpawnablesPanelView.spawnGun
member.summary: Identifies the gun associated with this browser and allows its item and category buttons to be filled.

remarks.para: The gun assigns itself here when its trigger grip is attached. Both page-content writers return without filling buttons if this reference is missing.
Assigning this reference does not by itself subscribe the gun to selection notifications. The normal grip-attachment path also registers the gun’s mode and crate listeners.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.UI.SpawnablesPanelView.swapSortButton
member.summary: Sort-order control shown on the Pallets tab and hidden on the other standard tabs.

remarks.para: SwapSortButton flips the sort choice and selects the Pallets tab again, rebuilding package rows and resetting the pages. NEW means newest cached folder date first, and ABC means alphabetical package-title order.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.UI.SpawnablesPanelView.tabButtons
member.summary: Provides the top-level browser tab highlights in the order SelectTab expects.

remarks.para: The verified choices are indexes 0 for categories, 1 for Developer Tools, 2 for Favorites, 3 for Pallets, and 4 for Authors. SelectTab turns off all tab highlights, then enables the selected slot and rebuilds that tab’s lists.
The requested slot must exist and its holder must have a highlight image. Changing this array does not remap the hard-coded meanings of those indexes.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.UI.SpawnablesPanelView.tagTree
member.summary: Stores the category hierarchy and current branch that category navigation follows.

remarks.para: A tree is a set of categories with parent and child links, like folders and subfolders. Activate creates the tree if needed. CleanupUserTags adds unfamiliar categories beneath Other, SelectCategory can enter branches, and TreeBackButton moves to the parent.
FilterTagTree uses the current branch to choose navigation rows and build the path text. Replacing the tree alone does not redraw those rows.

member.name: P:Il2CppSLZ.UI.SpawnablesPanelView.treeBackButton
member.summary: Back control that is hidden at the category-tree root and shown inside a branch.
