It asks the shared asset spawner to register the configured crate, waits two seconds of game time, then keeps waiting in half-second steps. The launcher neither checks registration completion nor uses its stored fire-point transform.

The inspected implementation supplies no position, rotation, launch speed, or launch force to the shared spawner. For example, attaching this component to a cannon and assigning a ball crate and muzzle transform does not make the cannon fire. Calling Spawn again starts another registration-and-wait sequence, rather than firing a shot.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.ButtonToggle
member.summary: Turns a joint-driven physical button’s travel into press, release, hold, and enable-period one-shot callbacks.

remarks.para: Assign the sliding ConfigurableJoint, an end marker at the depressed position, and the desired sounds and callback listeners: functions configured to run when a button action occurs. Awake, Unity's initialization callback, measures the starting separation, centers the joint’s connected anchor, sets half-travel limits, and disables the listed shaft collision pairs.

A press is latched near the end marker and released only after the button returns nearly to its start, preventing repeated transitions around one threshold. onPress and onDepress run on transitions; onHold runs on processed pressed-state frames; onPressOneShot is limited to the first eligible press after enabling.

Update skips all checks while the cached Rigidbody is sleeping, so a resting physics body does not produce repeated hold callbacks. Physics sleep means the body is temporarily excluded from movement updates while it is settled.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.Key
member.summary: Marks a grabbable object as a coded key that a can recognize and insert.

remarks.para: Put this component on the same GameObject as the object's InteractableHost, which identifies the object to the grabbing system. The receiver looks for Key on that GameObject and compares the key's code switches with its own requirements. A Key component on a separate child object does not satisfy that lookup.

The receiver manages insertion and removal. When insertion finishes, it invokes its onUnlock event; when the key is released from the receiver, it invokes onLock. Connect those receiver events to the door or other scene object that should respond. This component supplies the key's identity and codes; the event connections determine what actually opens or closes.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.KeyReceiver
member.summary: Accepts a key carrying the required code bits, guides it into a socket and signals the controlled mechanism to unlock.

remarks.para: Assign a receiver MarrowEntity, SphereCollider, entrance marker and seated marker. The Key transform is the point aligned to those markers; its InteractableHost supplies the grip, held hand and physics body. Accepted keys first hover near the entrance, then an automatic animation detaches the hand, packs the key into the receiver and seats it.

Seating plays an insertion sound and fires onUnlock followed by OnInserted. A removable key can be grabbed, or Release can animate it outward. Removal restores separate physics and fires onLock and OnKeyRemoved; animated ejection additionally fires OnRemoved after cleanup. isKeyConsumed keeps ordinary grabbing disabled after seating but does not prevent scripted Release.

Several internal names retain magazine/cartridge terminology, but this class handles Key components. SetHoverEject marks a reentry delay after ejection; it does not itself detect a hovering hand or start removal.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.KeyReceiver.Code
member.summary: Compatibility flags used to decide whether a physical Key has the codes required by a KeyReceiver.

remarks.para: Set a Key’s code to the tags it carries and a KeyReceiver’s code to the tags it requires. Combine flags with the bitwise OR operator, written | in C#. The key must contain every required receiver flag, rather than just one matching flag.

For example, a receiver requiring CODE_A | CODE_B accepts a key carrying both A and B, including one that also carries C. A key with only A fails that check. A receiver value of 0 has no required bits, so the code comparison passes for any Key, though the receiver’s other state and insertion conditions still apply.

Passing the code check allows the insertion interaction to proceed; it does not instantly fire the unlock event. Unlock notification occurs later when the receiver completes its locking/insertion stage. KeyDecorator can replace a spawned key’s codes, so the spawned value can differ from its prefab setting.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.KeyReceiver._States
member.summary: Records the current stage of a KeyReceiver’s key approach, insertion, and removal handling.

remarks.para: The normal insertion route is EMPTY, then HOVERING while a matching key approaches the start target, then SLIDING during seating, and finally INSERTED. Movement and notifications are performed by the receiver callbacks (routines called to perform or report an action) and coroutines (sequences that continue over several frames); the enum value records their stage rather than starting those actions itself.

Some declared values are not used by the examined implementation, and ejection has its own coroutine instead of simply entering EJECTING. Check the relevant value’s description before using it to infer what the key is doing.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.KeycardReceiver.Code
member.summary: Independent permission flags carried by keycards and selected on objects to choose which cards grant access.

remarks.para: Combine flags with the bitwise OR operator, written | in C#. A receiver grants access when the inserted card and the receiver share at least one selected code. For example, a receiver set to CODE_A | CODE_B accepts a card carrying CODE_A alone, CODE_B alone, or both. A card carrying only CODE_C fails that check. The letters are separate permissions, not increasing clearance ranks.

The code check happens after the card slides into place. A matching card triggers the receiver's acceptance sound, unlocked light color, and onUnlock event; a card with no shared code triggers its rejection sound and locked light color. Physical insertion does not prove permission. A zero value selects no codes, so a card or receiver with zero cannot share a code and does not grant access.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.KeycardReceiver._States
member.summary: Identifies the receiver’s internal card-acquisition, alignment, sliding, and seated phases.

remarks.para: The inspected workflow uses EMPTY, HOVERING, SLIDING, and INSERTED. These phases control card-entry handling and the hand/alignment updates before the player rig applies the player’s skeleton pose. The insertion and ejection coroutines, sequences that continue over several frames, perform the card movement.

SWITCHING and EJECTING are declared labels without an assigned phase or dedicated update branch in the inspected receiver. Changing a state value alone does not acquire card references, start a coroutine, or run the lock/unlock callbacks: routines called to perform or report an action.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Interaction.PowerPuncher
member.summary: A held punch weapon that builds charge from trigger input and adds a directional attack and shove to qualifying collisions.

remarks.para: Hold its triggerGrip and press the index trigger above 0.3. Charge strength fills over 1.6 seconds of scaled game time, with a body glow, icon stages, charging particles, and rising sound pitch. An accepted collision can discharge before full charge, then another discharge is prevented for 0.8 seconds.

The contact must be in the configured forward direction, have a relative speed above 0.5 meters per second, and strike a collider with a valid rigidbody. Set up the grip, collision collector, sound controller, body meshes, icon mesh, and particle references before Awake; initialization caches materials and subscribes to the grip and collector events.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.MLAgents.AutoAgroBoid
member.summary: Configures a reported boid’s player targets and behaviour settings when its spawner delivers an aggro notification.

remarks.para: Awake is Unity’s initialization callback, a routine called to prepare the component. It subscribes to the assigned MLZoneSpawner_Child’s OnAutoAgro notification, falling back to that component on the same GameObject if needed. A callback is a routine called to perform or report an action; this one supplies a Behaviour and player target reference.

For each notification it finds the BehaviourBoid in the reported object’s children, caches it, optionally assigns nonempty betweenAgroWaypoints, and sets the player’s body as target references for the boid and its agent. It also sets the agent’s sensor radius values and blocks their automatic radius changes, then copies findBall and attackProbability. If setBumperRate is true, it finally copies bumperUpdateRate into the child bumper’s physics-update delay.

The reported boid needs its behaviour, agent/controller/sensor and player-body references configured. The waypoint array must be assigned, although it can be empty; the optional bumper path needs a child BoidBumper. These are notification-time changes, not continuous synchronization of every spawned boid. The component does not itself spawn a creature or force an immediate attack; normal boid decision checks still apply.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.MLAgents.BoidBullet.OnDespawnDelegate
member.summary: A callback, meaning a routine called to report an action, that receives the associated with a bullet when its lifetime counter expires.

remarks.para: BoidBullet.DespawnCounter is a coroutine: a sequence that continues over several frames. It checks whether currentTimeAlive has reached maxTimeAlive, both measured in game-time seconds. While below the limit it adds one physics step's duration, waits for the next physics update, and checks again. On reaching the limit it calls the registered routine with boidAgent, then ends. The argument identifies the boid whose lifetime expired, rather than the bullet component or the object it last collided with.

BoidGun registers its BoidDespawned routine before starting this counter. That routine requests the configured despawn visual effect when valid and then decreases the model manager's active-agent count. The checked notification and gun listener do not themselves remove the boid object. For your own bullet setup, register a listener before starting the counter; calling this delegate is a notification, so any additional cleanup must be performed by the routines you connect.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.FilteredDespawn
member.summary: Sends entrants accepted by its activatorTags filter through their Poolee despawn path after requesting the despawn effect.

remarks.para: A Zone detects entities entering an area. This component listens to its assigned Zone while enabled and stops listening while disabled. Its inherited activatorTags field is a MarrowQuery: it checks configured tag queries and can also check an entity's crate reference. Its all/any setting controls whether those checks combine with AND or OR, so configure it for the entrants you want this zone to remove.

Each MarrowEntity needs a non-null Poolee reference for this component's despawn path; the Poolee component tracks its pool state. The despawn effect is requested first, but this component does not wait for it to finish. For an in-pool Poolee with a registered non-null SpawnPolicy (a per-object rule for handling despawn), that policy receives the request and its mapping is removed. When the policy map has no entry and a matching pool is available, it calls Pool.Despawn. If Pool.Despawn finds the Poolee in the spawned list, it removes that entry and adds it to the pool's despawned list, where a later spawn can reuse it. Otherwise Pool.Despawn returns before sending despawn events, running the Poolee's registered cleanup methods, changing either list, or deactivating the object. Poolee.IsInPool does not establish spawned-list membership: it checks a stored flag or crate reference. A Poolee not currently in a pool follows a separate fallback: it sends its despawn event, runs the Poolee's registered cleanup methods, deactivates its Unity GameObject (the object in the scene), then logs an error.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.FizzleOnRecycleDecorator
member.summary: Requests the configured despawn visual and sound effects when its assigned CrateSpawner recycles an object that the MarrowEntity cache recognizes.

remarks.para: Reset is Unity's editor setup hook that finds the CrateSpawner on this GameObject, Unity's object in the scene; Awake is Unity's initialization callback and subscribes to that spawner's recycle listener list. A listener is a component the spawner calls when it recycles an object. A component is behavior or data attached to a GameObject. The spawner calls OnRecycle with each recycled GameObject; a callback is the method the spawner calls to report that event. The MarrowEntity cache is the game's lookup table for finding the MarrowEntity component attached to that object. If the lookup succeeds, this decorator requests the configured despawn visual and sound effects. A pool is the game's system for keeping spawned objects available for reuse; the spawner and pool handle recycling, while this listener only requests effects.

The decorator supplies an effect request; it does not remove the entity, and the visual and sound effects can finish after this listener returns. Recycling is handled by the spawner and pool. The cache lookup must succeed before an effect is requested. This class does not unregister when disabled, and CrateSpawner dispatches its registered recycle-listener list without checking enabled state, so a disabled but registered component can still receive OnRecycle. To stop notifications, call CrateSpawner.UnregisterSpawnEventListener(IRecycleListenable) on the current spawner. To change spawners, unregister from the old one, update crateSpawner, then register with the new one. Ordinary spawn and despawn notifications use a separate ISpawnListenable listener list and are distinct events from recycling.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.Marrow.Zones.MobileEncounter
member.summary: Coordinates timed NPC spawn groups in parallel or series, forwards spawn notifications, and tracks group completion toward an encounter completion event.

remarks.para: Awake switches configured spawners to manual mode and wires notifications; Start prepares profile assets and optional toggles. StartEncounter launches the group's async loops, which use initial delays, spawn intervals, alive/dead limits, and total death counts to control progression. A callback is code you assign for the encounter to call. The onGroupComplete, OnGroupMemberSpawned, and AllGroupsKilled fields hold these caller-supplied routines; the base code invokes them for credited group completions, spawn notifications, or each group's death-count check. The latter two are called without null checks, so assign them before those notifications can run.

CompleteEncounter marks completion, fires OnComplete, and then requests group-loop cancellation, requiring initialized sources in every slot. It does not kill or directly despawn all members. A Unity coroutine is a routine Unity resumes over later frames. StopEncounter stops these routines, but the group loops are separate and use _spawnCTSs for cancellation. The base PauseEncounter flag does not suspend that timed loop.

Use the entity start overload or MentalAllEncounter to provide a TriggerRefProxy for investigate/aggression modes. TerminateEncounter resets encounter bookkeeping and group tracking after completion, but does not itself remove physical NPCs or clear every group lifecycle flag.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.SFX.TriggeredAudio
member.summary: Stores settings for a positional sound effect; call to request one clip from at this component's position.

remarks.para: A Unity component is a script attached to a GameObject, the in-game object that has a position. This class does not add a trigger handler of its own; call PlayAudio() from another script or connect it to a trigger or event.

member.name: T:Il2CppSLZ.UI.SpawnablesPanelView
member.summary: Browser panel for choosing the catalog entry and utility mode that a spawn gun should use.

remarks.para: A spawnable crate is a catalog entry describing an object the game can create, rather than an object already placed in the scene. This panel organizes those entries into categories, Developer Tools, Favorites, Pallets, and Authors. A pallet is a package of game or mod content.

On first activation, the panel prepares the category tree, caches package dates, and calls CleanupUserTags. That routine edits tags on loaded crates only while Unity is playing (Application.isPlaying is true); otherwise it returns without editing them. Every activation reloads favorites and refreshes the pages. The panel also displays the chosen entry’s title, package, author, description, and tags.

Choosing an item first notifies mode listeners to use SPAWNER, then stores the chosen crate and updates its information and favorite marker, and finally notifies crate listeners. A listener is a callback: a routine called to report an action. The gun registers its listeners while its trigger grip is attached and updates its choice and preview when notified. Selecting a catalog entry is separate from successfully creating a scene object.
